One who, with zeal for the outward sign, commits a pārājika offense and reckons monastic seniority and the like, does not become a thief-in-disguise.

140. Tiracchānagatoti nāgo vā hotu supaṇṇamāṇavakādīnaṃ vā aññataro antamaso sakkaṃ devarājānaṃ upādāya yo koci amanussajātiyo, sabbova imasmiṃ atthe “tiracchānagato”ti veditabbo. So ca neva upasampādetabbo na pabbājetabbo, upasampannopi nāsetabbo.

140. Regarding 'one gone to the animal state': be it a nāga, or one among the supaṇṇas in the guise of a youth and so on, or any other non-human species, even including Sakka, the king of the devas—all of them indeed, in this context, should be understood as 'one gone to the animal state'. And such a one should neither be given the higher ordination nor the going-forth; even if he has received the higher ordination, he should be expelled.

141. Mātughātakādīsu pana yena manussitthibhūtā janikā mātā sayampi manussajātikeneva sabhā sañcicca jīvitā voropitā, ayaṃ ānantariyena mātughātakakammena mātughātako. Etassa pabbajjā ca upasampadā ca paṭikkhittā. Yena pana manussitthibhūtāpi ajanikā posāvanikā mātā vā cūḷamātā vā janikāpi vā na manussitthibhūtā mātā [M 0.0152] ghātitā, tassa pabbajjā na vāritā, na ca ānantariko hoti. Yena sayaṃ tiracchānabhūtena manussitthibhūtā mātā ghātitā, sopi ānantariko na hoti, tiracchānagatattā panassa pabbajjā [V 0.0146] paṭikkhittā. Pitughātakepi eseva nayo. Sacepi hi vesiyā putto hoti, “ayaṃ me pitā”ti na jānāti, yassa sambhavena nibbatto, so ce anena ghātito, pitughātakotveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati, ānantariyañca phusati.

141. Now, regarding matricides and so on: he by whom a birth mother, who is a human female, is intentionally deprived of life, while he himself is also of human birth, this one is a matricide by the matricidal act with immediate result. For this one, both the going-forth and the higher ordination are prohibited. But by whom a mother who is a human female but not the birth mother—such as a foster mother or a stepmother—is killed, or a birth mother who is not a human female is killed, for him the going-forth is not forbidden, and he does not commit an act with immediate result. He who, being an animal himself, kills a mother who is a human female, he too does not commit an act with immediate result; but because he has gone to the animal state, his going-forth is prohibited. In the case of a patricide also, this is the same method. For if one is the son of a prostitute and does not know, 'This is my father,' yet if that one by whose seed he was conceived is killed by him, he is indeed counted as a patricide and he incurs an act with immediate result.

Arahantaghātakopi manussaarahantavaseneva veditabbo. Manussajātiyañhi antamaso apabbajitampi khīṇāsavaṃ dārakaṃ vā dārikaṃ vā sañcicca jīvitā voropento arahantaghātakova hoti, ānantariyañca phusati, pabbajjā cassa vāritā. Amanussajātikaṃ pana arahantaṃ manussajātikaṃ vā avasesaṃ ariyapuggalaṃ ghātetvā ānantariko na hoti, pabbajjāpissa na vāritā, kammaṃ pana balavaṃ hoti. Tiracchāno manussaarahantampi ghātetvā ānantariko na hoti, kammaṃ pana bhāriyanti ayamettha vinicchayo.

A killer of an Arahant is also to be understood only in the sense of a human Arahant. For one who, in the human species, intentionally deprives of life even an unordained destroyer of the cankers, whether a young boy or a young girl, is indeed a killer of an Arahant, and he incurs an act with immediate result, and for him the going-forth is forbidden. But having killed a non-human Arahant, or a remaining noble person of the human species, one does not commit an act with immediate result, and for him the going-forth is not forbidden; but the kamma is powerful. An animal, having killed even a human Arahant, does not commit an act with immediate result; but the kamma is weighty. This is the decision in this matter.

Yo pana devadatto viya duṭṭhacittena vadhakacittena tathāgatassa jīvamānakasarīre khuddakamakkhikāya pivanamattampi lohitaṃ uppādeti, ayaṃ lohituppādako nāma. Etassa pabbajjā ca upasampadā ca vāritā. Yo pana rogavūpasamatthaṃ jīvako viya satthena phāletvā pūtimaṃsalohitaṃ haritvā phāsukaṃ karoti, bahuṃ so puññaṃ pasavatīti.

One who, like Devadatta, with a malevolent mind and a murderous mind, causes even as much blood as a small fly can drink to arise on the living body of the Tathāgata, is called a 'blood-causer' (lohituppādaka). For this person, both going forth and higher ordination are prohibited. But one who, like Jīvaka, for the purpose of alleviating disease, cuts open with a knife, and having removed putrid flesh and blood, brings about comfort, generates much merit.

Yo devadatto viya sāsanaṃ uddhammaṃ ubbinayaṃ katvā catunnaṃ kammānaṃ aññataravasena saṅghaṃ bhindati, ayaṃ saṅghabhedako nāma. Etassa pabbajjā ca upasampadā ca vāritā.

One who, like Devadatta, having rendered the Teaching as not-Dhamma and the Discipline as not-Vinaya, causes a schism in the Saṅgha by means of one of the four actions, is called a 'schismatic' (saṅghabhedaka). For this person, both going forth and higher ordination are prohibited.

Yo pana pakatattaṃ bhikkhuniṃ tiṇṇaṃ maggānaṃ aññatarasmiṃ dūseti, ayaṃ bhikkhunīdūsako nāma. Etassa pabbajjā ca upasampadā ca vāritā. Yo pana kāyasaṃsaggena sīlavināsaṃ pāpeti, tassa pabbajjā ca upasampadā ca na vāritā. Balakkārena odātavatthavasanaṃ katvā anicchamānaṃyeva dūsentopi bhikkhunīdūsakoyeva, balakkārena pana odātavatthavasanaṃ katvā icchamānaṃ dūsento bhikkhunīdūsako na hoti. Kasmā? Yasmā gihibhāve sampaṭicchi tamatteyeva sā abhikkhunī hoti. Sakiṃsīlavipannaṃ pacchā [M 0.0153] dūsento sikkhamānasāmaṇerīsu ca vippaṭipajjanto neva bhikkhunīdūsako hoti, pabbajjampi upasampadampi labhati. Iti ime ekādasa abhabbapuggalā veditabbā.

One who violates a bhikkhunī of normal virtue in one of the three passages is called a 'violator of bhikkhunīs' (bhikkhunīdūsaka). For him, going forth and higher ordination are prohibited. But for one who causes the destruction of virtue through bodily contact, going forth and higher ordination are not prohibited. Even one who, having forcibly made her wear white clothes, violates her against her will, is indeed a violator of bhikkhunīs. However, one who, having forcibly made her wear white clothes, violates her with her consent, is not a violator of bhikkhunīs. Why? Because at the very moment of consenting to the lay state, she is no longer a bhikkhunī. One who violates her after her virtue has once been destroyed, or who misconducts himself with female probationers or female novices, is not a violator of bhikkhunīs; he may obtain both going forth and higher ordination. Thus, these eleven incapable persons should be known.

142. Ūnavīsativassassa pana upasampadāyeva paṭikkhittā, na pabbajjā, tasmā paṭisandhiggahaṇato [V 0.0147] paṭṭhāya paripuṇṇavīsativasso upasampādetabbo. Gabbhavīsopi hi paripuṇṇavīsativassotveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Yathāha bhagavā –

142. However, for one who is under twenty years of age, only higher ordination is prohibited, not going forth. Therefore, one who is fully twenty years of age, counting from the taking of conception, should be given higher ordination. For indeed, one who is twenty years old including the time in the womb is counted as being fully twenty years of age. As the Blessed One has said—

“Yaṃ, bhikkhave, mātukucchismiṃ paṭhamaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ, paṭhamaṃ viññāṇaṃ pātubhūtaṃ, tadupādāya sāvassa jāti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gabbhavīsaṃ upasampādetu”nti (mahāva. 124).

“O monks, whatever first thought has arisen in the mother's womb, whatever first consciousness has manifested, taking that as the starting point, that is the birth of that being. I allow, O monks, to give higher ordination to one who is twenty years of age from conception.”

Tattha (pāci. aṭṭha. 404) yo dvādasa māse mātukucchismiṃ vasitvā mahāpavāraṇāya jāto, so tato paṭṭhāya yāva ekūnavīsatime vasse mahāpavāraṇā, taṃ atikkamitvā pāṭipade upasampādetabbo. Etenupāyena hāyanavaḍḍhanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Porāṇakattherā pana ekūnavīsativassaṃ sāmaṇeraṃ nikkhamanīyapuṇṇamāsiṃ atikkamma pāṭipadadivase upasampādenti. Kasmā? Ekasmiṃ vasse cha cātuddasikauposathā honti, iti vīsatiyā vassesu cattāro māsā parihāyanti, rājāno tatiye tatiye gasse vassaṃ ukkaḍḍhanti, iti aṭṭhārasavassesu cha māsā vaḍḍhanti, tato uposathavasena parihīne cattāro māse apanetvā dve māsā avasesā honti, te dve māse gahetvā vīsati vassāni paripuṇṇāni hontīti nikkaṅkhā hutvā nikkhamanīyapuṇṇamāsiṃ atikkamma pāṭipade upasampādenti.

Therein, one who, having dwelt in the mother's womb for twelve months, is born on the day of the Great Pavāraṇā, should be given higher ordination on the first day of the lunar month after passing the Great Pavāraṇā in his nineteenth year. By this method, the decrease and increase should be understood. The ancient elders, however, give higher ordination to a novice of nineteen years on the first day of the lunar month after passing the full moon of Nikkhamanīya. Why? In one year there are six cātuddasika uposathas; thus, in twenty years, four months are diminished. Kings intercalate a month every third year; thus, in eighteen years, six months are added. From that, after removing the four months diminished by way of the uposatha, two months remain. Taking those two months, twenty years become complete. Thus, being without doubt, they give higher ordination on the first day of the lunar month after passing the full moon of Nikkhamanīya.

Ettha pana yo pavāretvā vīsativasso bhavissati, taṃ sandhāya “ekūnavīsativassa”nti vuttaṃ. Tasmā yo mātukucchismiṃ dvādasa māse vasi, so ekavīsativasso hoti. Yo satta māse vasi, so sattamāsādhikavīsativasso. Chamāsajāto pana na jīvati, ūnavīsativassaṃ pana “paripuṇṇavīsativasso”ti saññāya upasampādentassa anāpatti, puggalo pana anupasampannova hoti. Sace pana so dasavassaccayena aññaṃ upasampādeti, tañce muñcitvā gaṇo pūrati, sūpasampanno. Sopi [M 0.0154] ca yāva na jānāti, tāvassa neva saggantarāyo na mokkhantarāyo, ñatvā pana puna upasampajjitabbaṃ.

Here, however, the phrase 'nineteen years of age' is stated with reference to one who will be twenty years of age after the Pavāraṇā. Therefore, one who dwelt for twelve months in the mother’s womb is twenty-one years of age. One who dwelt for seven months is twenty years and seven months of age. But one born at six months does not live. However, for one giving higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age from conception with the perception that 'he is fully twenty years of age,' there is no offense; but the person is indeed unordained. If, however, that person gives higher ordination to another after ten years have passed, and if the quorum is complete excluding him, the candidate is well-ordained. And as for that preceptor, as long as he does not know, for him there is neither an obstacle to heaven nor an obstacle to liberation; but upon knowing, he should be ordained again.

143. Iti imehi pabbajjādosehi virahitopi “na, bhikkhave, ananuññāto mātāpitūhi putto pabbājetabbo”ti (mahāva. 105) vacanato mātāpitūhi ananuññāto na pabbājetabbo. Tattha (mahāva. aṭṭha. 105) mātāpitūhīti janake sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sace dvepi atthi, dvepi āpucchitabbā. Sace pitā mato hoti mātā vā, yo jīvati, so āpucchi tabbo, pabbajitāpi āpucchitabbāva. Āpucchantena sayaṃ vā gantvā āpucchitabbaṃ, añño vā [V 0.0148] pesetabbo. So eva vā pesetabbo “gaccha mātāpitaro āpucchitvā ehī”ti. Sace “anuññātomhī”ti vadati, saddahantena pabbājetabbo. Pitā sayaṃ pabbajito puttampi pabbājetukāmo hoti, mātaraṃ āpucchitvā pabbājetu. Mātā vā dhītaraṃ pabbājetukāmā pitaraṃ āpucchitvāva pabbājetu. Pitā puttadārena anatthiko palāyi, mātā “imaṃ pabbajethā”ti puttaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ deti, “pitāssa kuhi”nti vutte “cittakeḷiṃ kīḷituṃ palāto”ti vadati, taṃ pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. Mātā kenaci purisena saddhiṃ palātā hoti, pitā pana “pabbājethā”ti vadati, etthāpi eseva nayo. Pitā vippavuttho hoti, mātā puttaṃ “pabbājethā”ti anujānāti, “pitāssa kuhi”nti vutte “kiṃ tumhākaṃ pitarā, ahaṃ jānissāmī”ti vadati, pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭatīti kurundiyaṃ vuttaṃ.

143. Thus, even if one is free from these faults that are obstacles to going forth, one who is not permitted by his parents should not be given the going forth, according to the saying: “Bhikkhus, a son not permitted by his parents should not be given the going forth.” Therefore, one who is not permitted by his parents should not be given the going forth. Therein, the term 'mātāpitūhi' (by parents) is said with reference to the biological parents. If both are present, both should be asked. If the father or the mother has died, the one who is living should be asked. Even parents who have gone forth must indeed be asked. When asking, one should either go oneself to ask, or another should be sent. Or that very person should be sent with the instruction: “Go, ask your parents and come back.” If he says, “I have been permitted,” he should be given the going forth by one who believes him. If a father, having gone forth himself, wishes to give the going forth to his son, he should give the going forth only after asking the mother. Or if a mother wishes to give the going forth to her daughter, she should give the going forth only after asking the father. If the father, having no desire for his son and wife, has run away, and the mother gives the son to the bhikkhus, saying, “Give him the going forth,” when asked, “Where is his father?” she says, “He has run away for amusement,” it is allowable to give him the going forth. If the mother has run away with some man, but the father says, “Give him the going forth,” here too, this is the rule. If the father is away and the mother permits the son, saying, “Give him the going forth,” when asked, “Where is his father?” she says, “What is his father to you? I will take responsibility,” it is allowable to give him the going forth, so it is said in the Kurundī.

Mātāpitaro matā, dārako cūḷamātādīnaṃ santike saṃvaddho, tasmiṃ pabbājiyamāne ñātakā kalahaṃ vā karonti khiyyanti vā, tasmā vivādupacchedanatthaṃ āpucchitvā pabbājetabbo, anāpucchitvā pabbājentassa pana āpatti natthi. Daharakāle gahetvā posakā mātāpitaro nāma honti, tesupi eseva nayo. Putto attānaṃ nissāya jīvati, na mātāpitaro. Sacepi rājā hoti, āpucchitvāva pabbājetabbo. Mātāpitūhi anuññāto pabbajitvā puna vibbhamati, sacepi satakkhattuṃ pabbajitvā vibbhamati, āgatāgatakāle punappunaṃ āpucchitvāva pabbājetabbo. Sacepi evaṃ vadanti “ayaṃ vibbhamitvā gehaṃ āgato, amhākaṃ kammaṃ na karoti, pabbajitvā tumhākaṃ vattaṃ na pūreti, natthi imassa āpucchanakiccaṃ[M 0.0155], āgatāgataṃ naṃ pabbājeyyāthā”ti, evaṃ nissaṭṭhaṃ puna anāpucchāpi pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati.

If the mother and father are dead and the child is raised in the care of a stepmother and others, when he is being given the going forth, the relatives may quarrel or complain. Therefore, in order to cut off disputes, he should be given the going forth after asking permission. However, for one who gives the going forth without asking permission, there is no offense. Those who, having taken a child in his youth, raise him are called mother and father; for them also, this is the same rule. A son lives depending on himself; he does not live depending on his mother and father. Even if he is a king, he should be given the going forth only after asking permission. If one who was permitted by his mother and father, having gone forth, disrobes again—even if, having gone forth a hundred times, he disrobes—each time he comes, he should be given the going forth again and again only after asking permission. But if they say thus: 'This one, having disrobed, has come home. He does not do our work. Having gone forth, he does not fulfill your duties. For this one, there is no duty of asking permission; you may give him the going forth each time he comes,' it is permissible to give the going forth again to one thus given up, even without asking permission.

Yopi daharakāleyeva “ayaṃ tumhākaṃ dinno, yadā icchatha, tadā pabbājeyyāthā”ti evaṃ dinno hoti, sopi āgatāgato puna anāpucchitvāva pabbājetabbo. Yaṃ pana daharakāleyeva “imaṃ, bhante, pabbājeyyāthā”ti anujānitvā pacchā vuḍḍhippattakāle nānujānanti, ayaṃ na anāpucchā pabbājetabbo. Eko mātāpitūhi saddhiṃ bhaṇḍitvā “pabbājetha ma”nti āgacchati, “āpucchitvā ehī”ti ca vutto “nāhaṃ gacchāmi, sace maṃ na pabbājetha, vihāraṃ vā jhāpemi, satthena vā tumhe paharāmi, tumhākaṃ ñātakānaṃ vā upaṭṭhākānaṃ vā ārāmacchedanādīhi anatthaṃ uppādemi, rukkhā vā patitvā marāmi, coramajjhaṃ vā pavisāmi, desantaraṃ vā gacchāmī”ti vadati, taṃ tasseva rakkhaṇatthāya pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace panassa mātāpitaro āgantvā “kasmā amhākaṃ puttaṃ pabbājayitthā”ti vadanti, tesaṃ tamatthaṃ ārocetvā [V 0.0149] “rakkhaṇatthāya naṃ pabbājayimha, paññāyatha tumhe puttenā”ti vattabbā. “Rukkhā patissāmī”ti abhiruhitvā pana hatthapāde muñcantaṃ pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

A person who from a young age is given with the words, 'This boy is given to you; when you wish, then you may ordain him,' and is thus given—he too, whenever he comes, may be ordained again without asking permission. But as for one for whom permission was given in childhood with the words, 'Venerable sir, please ordain this one,' but for whom permission is not given later when he reaches maturity—he should not be ordained without asking permission. A person who quarrels with his parents and comes saying, 'Ordain me,' and when told, 'Ask permission and come back,' replies, 'I will not go. If you do not ordain me, I will burn down the monastery, or I will strike you with a weapon, or I will cause harm to your relatives or supporters by such things as cutting down the park's trees, or I will fall from a tree and die, or I will enter among thieves, or I will go to another region'—it is allowable to ordain him for his own protection. If his parents come and say, 'Why did you ordain our son?', the matter should be explained to them, saying, 'We ordained him for his protection. You should come to an understanding with your son.' Even if he climbs a tree saying, 'I will fall,' and lets go of his hands and feet, it is still allowable to ordain him.

Eko videsaṃ gantvā pabbajjaṃ yācati, āpucchitvā ce gato, pabbājetabbo. No ce, daharabhikkhuṃ pesetvā āpucchāpetvā pabbājetabbo. Atidūrañce hoti, pabbājetvāpi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ pesetvā dassetuṃ vaṭṭati. Kurundiyaṃ pana vuttaṃ “sace dūraṃ hoti, maggo ca mahākantāro, ‘gantvā āpucchissāmī’ti pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti. Sace pana mātāpitūnaṃ bahū puttā honti, evañca vadanti “bhante, etesaṃ dārakānaṃ yaṃ icchatha, taṃ pabbājeyyāthā”ti, dārake vīmaṃsitvā yaṃ icchati, so pabbājetabbo. Sacepi sakalena kulena vā gāmena vā anuññāto hoti “bhante, imasmiṃ kule vā gāme vā yaṃ icchatha, taṃ pabbājeyyāthā”ti, yaṃ icchati, so pabbājetabboti.

If one, having gone to another region, requests ordination, he should be ordained if he has gone after taking leave. If not, a junior monk should be sent to have permission asked for, and then he should be ordained. If the distance is too great, it is permissible to ordain him and then send him with monks to be presented. However, in the Kurundi it is said: “If the distance is great and the road is a vast wilderness, it is permissible to ordain him with the thought, ‘I will go and take leave.’” But if parents have many sons and say, “Venerable sir, you may ordain whichever of these children you wish,” the children should be examined, and the one who is desired should be ordained. And if he is given permission by an entire family or village, saying, “Venerable sir, you may ordain whomever you wish from this family or village,” the one who is desired should be ordained.

144. Evaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 34) pabbajjādosavirahitaṃ mātāpitūhi anuññātaṃ pabbājentenapi ca sace acchinnakeso hoti, ekasīmāyañca aññepi bhikkhū [M 0.0156] atthi, kesacchedanatthāya bhaṇḍukammaṃ āpucchitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ āpucchanavidhi (mahāva. aṭṭha. 98) – sīmāpariyāpanne bhikkhū sannipātetvā pabbajjāpekkhaṃ tattha netvā “saṅghaṃ, bhante, imassa dārakassa bhaṇḍukammaṃ āpucchāmī”ti tikkhattuṃ vā dvikkhattuṃ vā sakiṃ vā vattabbaṃ. Ettha ca “imassa dārakassa bhaṇḍukammaṃ āpucchāmī”tipi “imassa samaṇakaraṇaṃ āpucchāmī”tipi “ayaṃ samaṇo hotukāmo”tipi “ayaṃ pabbajitukāmo”tipi vattuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Sace sabhāgaṭṭhānaṃ hoti, dasa vā vīsati vā tiṃsaṃ vā bhikkhū vasantīti paricchedo paññāyati, tesaṃ ṭhitokāsaṃ vā nisinnokāsaṃ vā gantvāpi purimanayeneva āpucchitabbaṃ. Pabbajjāpekkhaṃ vināva daharabhikkhū vā sāmaṇere vā pesetvāpi “eko, bhante, pabbajjāpekkho atthi, tassa bhaṇḍukammaṃ āpucchāmā”tiādinā nayena āpucchāpetuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace keci bhikkhū senāsanaṃ vā gumbādīni vā pavisitvā niddāyanti vā samaṇadhammaṃ vā karonti, āpucchakā ca pariyesantāpi adisvā “sabbe āpucchitā amhehī”ti saññino honti, pabbajjā nāma lahukakammaṃ, tasmā pabbajito supabbajito, pabbājentassapi anāpatti.

144. Thus, by one who is ordaining a person free from the faults for ordination and permitted by his parents, if that person has uncut hair, and if other monks are also present within a single boundary, the act of bhaṇḍukamma must be requested for the purpose of cutting the hair. In that regard, this is the procedure for requesting: Having assembled the monks included within the boundary and having led the one who desires ordination there, it should be said three times, or twice, or once: 'Venerable sirs, I request from the Saṅgha the bhaṇḍukamma for this boy.' And here, it is indeed proper to say: 'I request the bhaṇḍukamma of this boy,' or 'I request the making of a recluse for this one,' or 'This one desires to become a recluse,' or 'This one desires to go forth.' If it is a suitable place, and it is known that a number of monks—ten, or twenty, or thirty—are residing there, even having gone to the place where they are standing or the place where they are sitting, the request should be made in the same way as before. Even without the one who desires ordination, it is proper to have the request made by sending a junior monk or a novice, by the method beginning with: 'Venerable sirs, there is one who desires ordination; we request the bhaṇḍukamma for him.' If some monks, having entered their lodgings or thickets and so on, are sleeping or are practicing the recluse's duties, and the requesters, even while searching, do not see them and are of the perception, 'All the monks have been requested by us,' the act of ordination is a light act. Therefore, the one ordained is well-ordained, and for the one who ordains, there is no offense.

Sace pana vihāro mahā hoti anekabhikkhusahassāvāso, sabbe bhikkhū sannipātāpetumpi dukkaraṃ, pageva paṭipāṭiyā āpucchituṃ, khaṇḍasīmāya vā ṭhatvā nadīsamuddādīni vā gantvā pabbājetabbo. Yo pana navamuṇḍo vā hoti vibbhantako vā nigaṇṭhādīsu [V 0.0150] aññataro vā dvaṅgulakeso vā ūnadvaṅgulakeso vā, tassa kesacchedanakiccaṃ natthi, tasmā bhaṇḍukammaṃ anāpucchitvāpi tādisaṃ pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. Dvaṅgulātirittakeso pana yo hoti antamaso ekasikhāmattadharopi, so bhaṇḍukammaṃ āpucchitvāva pabbājetabbo.

If, however, the monastery is large, being a residence for many thousands of monks, it is difficult even to assemble all the monks; what then is to be said of asking them in succession? He should be ordained either having stood in a fragment boundary or having gone to a river, sea, or the like. But as for one who is newly shaven, or has newly left the order, or is one among the Nigaṇṭhas and others, or has hair two fingers long, or has hair less than two fingers long, for him there is no duty of cutting the hair. Therefore, it is allowable to ordain such a person even without requesting the bhaṇḍukamma. But as for one whose hair exceeds two fingers in length, even if he wears only a single topknot, he should be ordained only after having requested the bhaṇḍukamma.

145. Evaṃ āpucchitvā pabbājentena ca paripuṇṇapattacīvarova pabbājetabbo. Sace tassa natthi, yācitakenapi pattacīvarena pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati, sabhāgaṭṭhāne vissāsena gahetvāpi pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace (mahāva. aṭṭha. 118) pana apakkaṃ pattaṃ cīvarūpagāni ca vatthāni gahetvā āgato hoti, yāva patto paccati, cīvarāni ca karīyanti, tāva vihāre vasantassa anāmaṭṭhapiṇḍapātaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭati, thālakesu bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Purebhattaṃ sāmaṇerabhāgasamako [M 0.0157] āmisabhāgo dātuṃ vaṭṭati, senāsanaggāho pana salākabhattauddesabhattanimantanādīni ca na vaṭṭanti. Pacchābhattampi sāmaṇerabhāgasamo telataṇḍulamadhuphāṇitādibhesajjabhāgo vaṭṭati. Sace gilāno hoti, bhesajjamassa kātuṃ vaṭṭati, sāmaṇerassa viya sabbaṃ paṭijagganakammaṃ. Upasampadāpekkhaṃ pana yācitakena pattacīvarena upasampādetuṃ na vaṭṭati. “Na, bhikkhave, yācitakena pattacīvarena upasampādetabbo, yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 118) vuttaṃ. Tasmā so paripuṇṇapattacīvaroyeva upasampādetabbo. Sace tassa natthi, ācariyupajjhāyā cassa dātukāmā honti, aññe vā bhikkhū nirapekkhehi nissajjitvā adhiṭṭhānupagaṃ pattacīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ. Yācitakena pana pattena vā cīvarena vā upasampādentasseva āpatti hoti, kammaṃ pana na kuppati.

145. Having taken leave in this way, one who is giving the going forth should give it only to a person who has a complete bowl and robes. If he lacks these, it is proper to give the going forth even with a borrowed bowl and robes; it is also proper to give the going forth by taking them from a common place with familiarity. If, however, he arrives with an unfired bowl and cloths suitable for robes, he may be given untouched almsfood as long as he stays in the monastery until the bowl is fired and the robes are made. He may eat from plates. Before the meal, he may be given a food portion equal to that of a novice. However, the taking of a lodging is not proper for him, nor are ticket-food, designated food, invitations, and so on. After the meal, a share of medicines such as oil, rice, honey, and molasses, equal to a novice’s share, is proper. If he is sick, it is proper to prepare medicine for him; all acts of care should be performed as for a novice. But it is not proper to confer higher ordination on one seeking it with a borrowed bowl and robes. It is said, “Monks, one should not be given higher ordination with a borrowed bowl and robes. Whoever should confer higher ordination commits an offense of wrong-doing.” Therefore, he should be given higher ordination only when he has a complete bowl and robes. If he lacks these, and his preceptor or teacher are willing to give them, or other monks are, a bowl and robes suitable for determination should be given, having been relinquished by those without attachment. However, the offense is only for the one who confers higher ordination with a borrowed bowl or robes; the formal act itself is not invalidated.

146. Paripuṇṇapattacīvaraṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 34) pabbājentenapi sace okāso hoti, sayaṃ pabbājetabbo. Sace uddesaparipucchādīhi byāvaṭo hoti, okāsaṃ na labhati, eko daharabhikkhu vattabbo “etaṃ pabbājehī”ti. Avuttopi ce daharabhikkhu upajjhāyaṃ uddissa pabbājeti, vaṭṭati. Sace daharabhikkhu natthi, sāmaṇeropi vattabbo “etaṃ khaṇḍasīmaṃ netvā pabbājetvā kāsāyāni acchādetvā ehī”ti. Saraṇāni pana sayaṃ dātabbāni. Evaṃ bhikkhunāva pabbājito hoti. Purisañhi bhikkhuto añño pabbājetuṃ na labhati, mātugāmaṃ bhikkhunīto añño, sāmaṇero pana sāmaṇerī vā āṇattiyā kāsāyāni dātuṃ labhanti, kesoropanaṃ yena kenaci kataṃ sukataṃ.

146. When giving the going forth to one who has a complete bowl and robes, if there is an opportunity, one should give the going forth oneself. If one is occupied with recitation, questioning, and other such duties and does not get the opportunity, a junior monk should be told, "Give this one the going forth." Even if not instructed, if the junior monk, intending it for the preceptor, gives the going forth, it is allowable. If there is no junior monk, a novice may be told, "Take this one to the broken boundary, give him the going forth, clothe him in the ochre robes, and then return." However, the refuges must be given by oneself. In this way, he is given the going forth by a monk. For a man, no one other than a monk is allowed to give him the going forth; for a woman, no one other than a nun. But a novice or a female novice may, by instruction, give the ochre robes. The shaving of the head, done by anyone, is well done.

Sace pana bhabbarūpo hoti sahetuko ñāto yasassī kulaputto, okāsaṃ katvāpi sayameva pabbājetabbo, “mattikāmuṭṭhiṃ gahetvā nahāyitvā āgacchāhī”ti ca na pana vissajjetabbo[V 0.0151]. Pabbajitukāmānañhi paṭhamaṃ balavaussāho hoti, pacchā pana kāsāyāni ca kesaharaṇasatthakañca disvā utrasanti, ettoyeva palāyanti, tasmā sayameva nahānatitthaṃ netvā sace nātidaharo, “nahāhī”ti vattabbo, kesā panassa sayameva mattikaṃ gahetvā dhovitabbā[M 0.0158]. Daharakumārako pana sayaṃ udakaṃ otaritvā gomayamattikāhi ghaṃsitvā nahāpetabbo. Sacepissa kacchu vā piḷakā vā honti, yathā mātā puttaṃ na jigucchati, evamevaṃ ajigucchantena sādhukaṃ hatthapādato ca sīsato ca paṭṭhāya ghaṃsitvā ghaṃsitvā nahāpetabbo. Kasmā? Ettakena hi upakārena kulaputtā ācariyupajjhāyesu ca sāsane ca balavasinehā tibbagāravā anivattidhammā honti, uppannaṃ anabhiratiṃ vinodetvā therabhāvaṃ pāpuṇanti, kataññukatavedino honti.

If, however, he is a suitable person, endowed with the causal basis, well-known, of great repute, and a son of good family, one should give him the going forth oneself, even by making an opportunity. He should not be sent away with the words, 'Take a handful of clay, bathe, and then come.' For those desiring to go forth, the initial enthusiasm is strong, but later, upon seeing the ochre robes and the razor for removing hair, they become frightened and flee from that very point. Therefore, one should take him to the bathing place oneself. If he is not too young, he should be told, 'Bathe.' But his hair should be washed by oneself, having taken clay. A young boy, however, should be bathed by oneself, having entered the water and scrubbed him with cow-dung and clay. If he has scabies or boils, without disgust—just as a mother would not be disgusted with her son—he should be thoroughly bathed, having scrubbed and scrubbed him, starting from the hands, feet, and head. Why? For by such assistance, sons of good family develop strong affection and keen reverence for their teachers and preceptors and for the Dispensation. They become unwavering in nature, and having dispelled any discontent that arises, they attain the state of an elder and become grateful and appreciative.

Evaṃ nahāpanakāle pana kesamassuṃ oropanakāle vā “tvaṃ ñāto yasassī, idāni mayaṃ taṃ nissāya paccayehi na kilamissāmā”ti na vattabbo, aññāpi aniyyānikakathā na vattabbā, atha khvassa “āvuso, suṭṭhu upadhārehi, satiṃ upaṭṭhāpehī”ti vatvā tacapañcakakammaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Ācikkhantena ca vaṇṇasaṇṭhānagandhāsayokāsavasena asucijegucchapaṭikkūlabhāvaṃ nijjīvanissattabhāvaṃ vā pākaṭaṃ karontena ācikkhitabbaṃ. Sace hi so pubbe madditasaṅkhāro hoti bhāvitabhāvano kaṇṭakavedhāpekkho viya paripakkagaṇḍo sūriyuggamanāpekkhaṃ viya ca pariṇatapadumaṃ, athassa āraddhamatte kammaṭṭhānaṃ manasikāre indāsani viya pabbate kilesapabbate cuṇṇayamānaṃyeva ñāṇaṃ pavattati, khuraggeyeva arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti. Ye hi keci khuragge arahattaṃ pattā, sabbe te evarūpaṃ savanaṃ labhitvā kalyāṇamittena ācariyena dinnanayaṃ nissāya, no anissāya. Tasmāssa āditova evarūpī kathā kathetabbāti.

At the time of bathing or when shaving the hair and beard, one should not say, "You are well-known and famous; now, through you, we will not be troubled in obtaining requisites." Nor should any other talk that does not lead to liberation be spoken. Instead, one should say, "Friend, pay close attention, establish your mindfulness," and then the meditation subject of the five skin-parts should be taught. While teaching, one should make clear its state of being impure, disgusting, and repulsive, or its state of being lifeless and not a being, in terms of color, shape, smell, abode, and location. For if that person has previously contemplated the formations and has developed meditation, like a ripe boil awaiting lancing, and like a mature lotus bud awaiting the sunrise, then as soon as he begins to apply his mind to the meditation subject, knowledge arises, pulverizing the mountains of defilements just as Indra's thunderbolt pulverizes mountains. He attains Arahantship at the very edge of the razor. Indeed, all those who have attained Arahantship at the edge of the razor have done so by receiving such instruction and relying on the method given by a teacher who is a good friend; not without relying on it. Therefore, from the very beginning, one should speak to him in this manner.

Kesesu pana oropitesu haliddicuṇṇena vā gandhacuṇṇena vā sīsañca sarīrañca ubbaṭṭetvā gihigandhaṃ apanetvā kāsāyāni tikkhattuṃ vā dvikkhattuṃ vā sakiṃ vā paṭiggāhāpetabbo. Athāpissa hatthe adatvā ācariyo vā upajjhāyo vā sayameva acchādeti, vaṭṭati. Sace aññaṃ daharaṃ vā sāmaṇeraṃ vā upāsakaṃ vā āṇāpeti “āvuso, etāni kāsāyāni gahetvā etaṃ acchādehī”ti, taññeva vā āṇāpeti “etāni gahetvā acchādehī”ti, sabbaṃ taṃ vaṭṭati, sabbaṃ tena bhikkhunāva dinnaṃ hoti. Yaṃ pana nivāsanaṃ vā pārupanaṃ [M 0.0159] vā anāṇattiyā nivāseti vā pārupati vā, taṃ apanetvā puna dātabbaṃ. Bhikkhunā [V 0.0152] hi sahatthena vā āṇattiyā vā dinnameva kāsāyaṃ vaṭṭati, adinnaṃ na vaṭṭati. Sacepi tasseva santakaṃ hoti, ko pana vādo upajjhāyamūlake.

When the hair has been shaved off, having rubbed the head and body with turmeric powder or fragrant powder and having removed the householder's scent, the ochre robes should be made to be accepted three times, two times, or once. Alternatively, without placing them in his hand, the teacher or preceptor himself may clothe him; this is allowable. If he instructs another—a younger monk, a novice, or a lay follower—saying, 'Friend, take these ochre robes and clothe him,' or if he instructs that very person, the candidate, 'Take these and clothe yourself,' all that is allowable. Everything is considered to have been given by that very monk. However, whatever lower robe or upper robe he puts on or wears without instruction, that must be removed and given again. For, only an ochre robe given by a monk's own hand or by his instruction is allowable; what is not given is not allowable. Even if it is the candidate's own property, what then is to be said of robes belonging to the preceptor?

147. Evaṃ pana dinnāni kāsāyāni acchādāpetvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ kārāpetvā ye tattha sannipatitā bhikkhū, tesaṃ pāde vandāpetvā atha saraṇagahaṇatthaṃ ukkuṭikaṃ nisīdāpetvā añjaliṃ paggaṇhāpetvā “evaṃ vadehī”ti vattabbo, “yamahaṃ vadāmi, taṃ vadehī”ti vattabbo. Athassa upajjhāyena vā ācariyena vā “buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”tiādinā nayena saraṇāni dātabbāni yathāvuttapaṭipāṭiyāva, na uppaṭipāṭiyā. Sace hi ekapadampi ekakkharampi uppaṭipāṭiyā deti, buddhaṃ saraṇaṃyeva vā tikkhattuṃ datvā puna itaresu ekekaṃ tikkhattuṃ deti, adinnāni honti saraṇāni.

147. Thus, having caused him to be clothed with the given ochre robes and having caused him to arrange the upper robe over one shoulder, and having caused him to pay homage at the feet of whatever monks are assembled there, then for the purpose of taking the refuges, having caused him to sit in the squatting posture and having caused him to raise his joined palms, he should be told, 'Say thus,' and he should be told, 'Say what I say.' Then, the refuges should be given by the preceptor or the teacher according to the method beginning, 'I go to the Buddha for refuge,' only in the sequence as stated, not out of sequence. For if he gives even one word or even one syllable out of sequence, or if, having given 'I go to the Buddha for refuge' three times, he then gives each of the others three times, the refuges are considered not given.

Imañca pana saraṇagamanupasampadaṃ paṭikkhipitvā anuññātaupasampadā ekatosuddhiyā vaṭṭati, sāmaṇerapabbajjā pana ubhatosuddhiyāva vaṭṭati, no ekatosuddhiyā. Tasmā upasampadāya sace ācariyo ñattidosañceva kammavācādosañca vajjetvā kammaṃ karoti, sukataṃ hoti. Pabbajjāya pana imāni tīṇi saraṇāni bu-kāra dha-kārādīnaṃ byañjanānaṃ ṭhānakaraṇasampadaṃ ahāpentena ācariyenapi antevāsikenapi vattabbāni. Sace ācariyo vattuṃ sakkoti, antevāsiko na sakkoti, antevāsiko vā sakkoti, ācariyo na sakkoti, ubhopi vā na sakkonti, na vaṭṭati. Sace pana ubhopi sakkonti, vaṭṭati. Imāni ca pana dadamānena “buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”ti evaṃ ekasambandhāni anunāsikantāni vā katvā dātabbāni, “buddhama saraṇama gacchāmī”ti evaṃ vicchinditvā makārantāni vā katvā dātabbāni. Andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “nāmaṃ sāvetvā ‘ahaṃ, bhante, buddharakkhito yāvajīvaṃ buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ ekaṭṭhakathāyampi natthi, pāḷiyampi na vuttaṃ, tesaṃ rucimattameva, tasmā na gahetabbaṃ. Na hi tathā avadantassa saraṇaṃ kuppati. Ettāvatā ca sāmaṇerabhūmiyaṃ patiṭṭhito hoti.

Moreover, having rejected this ordination by going for refuge, the permitted higher ordination is valid through purity on one side, whereas the novice ordination is valid only through purity on both sides, not on one side alone. Therefore, in the higher ordination, if the teacher performs the formal act having avoided faults in the motion and faults in the proclamation, it is well-done. In the novice ordination, however, these three refuges must be spoken by both the teacher and the pupil, without failing in the perfection of articulation for consonants such as 'bu' and 'dha'. If the teacher is able to speak but the pupil is not, or the pupil is able but the teacher is not, or both are unable, it is not valid. But if both are able, it is valid. And when giving these refuges, they should be given either as a single connected phrase with nasal endings, thus: 'buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi'; or, having separated them, with 'm' endings, thus: 'buddhama saraṇama gacchāmi'. In the Andhaka commentary it is said, 'Having announced the name, one should say: "Venerable sir, I, Buddharakkhito, for as long as life lasts, go to the Buddha for refuge."' But this is not found in any other commentary, nor is it stated in the Pāli Canon; it is merely their own preference, therefore it should not be accepted. For the refuge of one who does not speak in that way is not invalidated. And with just this much, one becomes established in the state of a novice.

148. Sace panesa gatimā hoti paṇḍitajātiko, athassa tasmiṃyeva ṭhāne sikkhāpadāni uddisitabbāni. Kathaṃ? Yathā bhagavatā uddiṭṭhāni. Vuttañhetaṃ –

148. If, however, this novice is capable and of an intelligent nature, then the training rules should be recited to him right there in that very place. How? Just as they were taught by the Blessed One. For this has been said:

“Anujānāmi[M 0.0160], bhikkhave, sāmaṇerānaṃ dasa sikkhāpadāni, tesu ca sāmaṇerehi sikkhituṃ. Pāṇātipātā veramaṇi, adinnādānā veramaṇi, abrahmacariyā veramaṇi, musāvādā [V 0.0153] veramaṇi, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇi, vikālabhojanā veramaṇi, naccagītavādita visūkadassanā veramaṇi, mālāgandha vilepana dhāraṇa maṇḍana vibhūsanaṭṭhānā veramaṇi, uccāsayanamahāsayanā veramaṇi, jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇā veramaṇī”ti (mahāva. 106).

“I allow, monks, ten training rules for novices, and I allow for novices to train in them: Abstaining from the destruction of life; abstaining from taking what is not given; abstaining from unchaste conduct; abstaining from false speech; abstaining from fermented and distilled intoxicants which are a cause for heedlessness; abstaining from eating at the wrong time; abstaining from dancing, singing, instrumental music, and watching entertainments; abstaining from wearing garlands, using scents and unguents, and from occasions for adornment and beautification; abstaining from high and large beds; abstaining from accepting gold and silver.”

Andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “ahaṃ, bhante, itthannāmo yāvajīvaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇisikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmī”ti evaṃ saraṇadānaṃ viya sikkhāpadadānampi vuttaṃ, taṃ neva pāḷiyaṃ, na aṭṭhakathāsu atthi, tasmā yathāpāḷiyāva uddisitabbāni. Pabbajjā hi saraṇagamaneheva siddhā, sikkhāpadāni pana kevalaṃ sikkhāpadapūraṇatthaṃ jānitabbāni, tasmā pāḷiyā āgatanayeneva uggahetuṃ asakkontassa yāya kāyaci bhāsāya atthavasenapi ācikkhituṃ vaṭṭati. Yāva pana attanā sikkhitabbasikkhāpadāni na jānāti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇaṭṭhānanisajjādīsu pānabhojanādividhimhi ca na kusalo hoti, tāva bhojanasālaṃ vā salākabhājanaṭṭhānaṃ vā aññaṃ vā tathārūpaṭṭhānaṃ na pesetabbo, santikāvacaroyeva kātabbo, bāladārako viya paṭipajjitabbo, sabbamassa kappiyākappiyaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ, nivāsanapārupanādīsu abhisamācārikesu vinetabbo. Tenapi –

In the Andhakaṭṭhakathā, however, the giving of the training rules is also mentioned, similar to the giving of the refuges, as follows: 'Venerable sir, I, so-and-so by name, undertake for as long as life lasts the training rule of abstinence from the destruction of life.' But this is found neither in the Pāli nor in the commentaries; therefore, they should be recited only according to the Pāli. For the going forth is accomplished by the goings for refuge alone, whereas the training rules are to be known merely for the purpose of fulfilling them. Therefore, for one who is unable to learn them by the method that has come down in the Pāli, it is proper to explain them in any language whatsoever by way of their meaning. However, as long as one does not know the training rules that are to be trained in, and is not skilled in the procedures concerning the wearing of the saṅghāṭi, bowl, and robes, standing, sitting, and so on, and in the method of drinking and eating, for so long they should not be sent to a dining hall, or a place where tickets for food are distributed, or another such place. They should be made to stay nearby and should be looked after like a young child. All that is allowable and unallowable should be explained to them, and they should be trained in the observances of proper conduct concerning dressing, wearing the robe, and so on. That novice, in turn—

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ sāmaṇeraṃ nāsetuṃ. Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, abrahmacārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, majjapāyī hoti, buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, bhikkhunīdūsako hotī”ti (mahāva. 108) –

“I allow, monks, to expel a novice endowed with ten factors. He destroys life, takes what is not given, engages in unchaste conduct, speaks falsely, drinks intoxicants, speaks in dispraise of the Buddha, speaks in dispraise of the Dhamma, speaks in dispraise of the Saṅgha, holds wrong view, and corrupts a bhikkhunī.”

Evaṃ vuttāni dasa nāsanaṅgāni ārakā parivajjetvā ābhisamācārikaṃ paripūrentena dasavidhe sīle sādhukaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ.

Avoiding from afar these ten factors of expulsion thus stated, and fulfilling the customary practices, one should train well in the tenfold virtue.

149. Yo [M 0.0161] pana (mahāva. aṭṭha. 108) pāṇātipātādīsu dasasu nāsanaṅgesu ekampi kammaṃ karoti, so liṅganāsanāya nāsetabbo. Tīsu hi nāsanāsu liṅganāsanāyeva idhādhippetā. Yathā ca bhikkhūnaṃ pāṇātipātādīsu tā tā āpattiyo honti, na tathā sāmaṇerānaṃ. Sāmaṇero hi kuntha kipillikampi māretvā maṅgulaṇḍakampi bhinditvā nāsetabbataṃyeva pāpuṇāti, tāvadevassa saraṇagamanāni ca upajjhāyaggahaṇañca senāsanaggāho ca paṭippassambhanti, saṅghalābhaṃ na labhati, liṅgamattameva ekaṃ avasiṭṭhaṃ hoti. So sace ākiṇṇadosova [V 0.0154] hoti, āyatiṃ saṃvare na tiṭṭhati, nikkaḍḍhitabbo. Atha sahasā virajjhitvā “duṭṭhu mayā kata”nti puna saṃvare ṭhātukāmo hoti, liṅganāsanakiccaṃ natthi, yathānivatthapārutasseva saraṇāni dātabbāni, upajjhāyo dātabbo. Sikkhāpadāni pana saraṇagamaneneva ijjhanti. Sāmaṇerānañhi saraṇagamanaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ upasampadakammavācāsadisaṃ, tasmā bhikkhūnaṃ viya catupārisuddhisīlaṃ imināpi dasa sīlāni samādinnāneva honti, evaṃ santepi daḷhīkaraṇatthaṃ āyatiṃ saṃvare patiṭṭhāpanatthaṃ puna dātabbāni. Sace purimikāya puna saraṇāni gahitāni, pacchimikāya vassāvāsikaṃ lacchati. Sace pacchimikāya gahitāni, saṅghena apaloketvā lābho dātabbo. Adinnādāne tiṇasalākamattenapi vatthunā, abrahmacariye tīsu maggesu yattha katthaci vippaṭipattiyā, musāvāde hasādhippāyatāyapi musā bhaṇite assamaṇo hoti, nāsetabbataṃ āpajjati, majjapāne pana bhikkhuno ajānitvāpi bījato paṭṭhāya majjaṃ pivantassa pācittiyaṃ. Sāmaṇero jānitvā pivantova sīlabhedaṃ āpajjati, na ajānitvā. Yāni panassa itarāni pañca sikkhāpadāni, etesu bhinnesu na nāsetabbo, daṇḍakammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Sikkhāpade pana puna dinnepi adinnepi vaṭṭati, daṇḍakammena pana pīḷetvā āyatiṃ saṃvare ṭhapanatthāya dātabbameva.

149. Whatever novice commits even one of these ten factors of expulsion, beginning with taking life, he should be expelled by the expulsion of his insignia. For here, among the three expulsions, only the expulsion of insignia is intended. And just as for monks there are various offenses in matters beginning with taking life, it is not so for novices. For a novice, by killing even a woodlouse or an ant, or by breaking even a bedbug's egg, attains only the state of being liable for expulsion. At that very moment, for that novice, the goings for refuge, the taking of a preceptor, and the acceptance of a dwelling cease; he does not obtain gain from the Sangha, and only the mere insignia remains. If that novice is indeed full of faults and does not stand in future restraint, he should be driven out. But if, having transgressed suddenly, he thinks, 'A wrong thing was done by me,' and again wishes to stand in restraint, there is no need for the act of expelling the insignia. The refuges should be given to him just as he is, dressed and robed, and a preceptor should be given. The training rules, however, are fulfilled by the going for refuge alone. For the novices' going for refuge is similar to the monks' formal act of ordination; therefore, like the monks' fourfold purity of virtue, by this act also the ten precepts are indeed undertaken. Even so, for the sake of strengthening and for the sake of establishing him in future restraint, they should be given again. If the refuges are taken again in the first period of the rains-residence, he will obtain the rains-residence allowance in the latter period. If they are taken in the latter period, gain should be given after informing the Sangha. In taking what is not given, with an object the size of even a blade of grass or a splinter of bamboo; in unchastity, by misconduct in any of the three passages; in false speech, when a lie is spoken even with the intention of jesting—he is not a novice and becomes liable for expulsion. But in the case of drinking intoxicants, for a monk who drinks an intoxicant, even unknowingly, from when it is a seed onwards, there is a pācittiya offense. A novice attains a breach of virtue only if he drinks knowingly, not if he drinks unknowingly. As for his other five training rules, when these are broken, he should not be expelled; a disciplinary action should be carried out. But regarding the training rules, it is allowable whether they are given again or not given; however, having disciplined him with a disciplinary action, they should indeed be given for the sake of establishing him in future restraint.

Avaṇṇabhāsane pana “arahaṃ sammāsambuddho”tiādīnaṃ paṭipakkhavasena buddhassa vā “svākkhāto”tiādīnaṃ paṭipakkhavasena dhammassa vā “suppaṭipanno”tiādīnaṃ paṭipakkhavasena saṅghassa vā avaṇṇaṃ bhāsanto ratanattayaṃ nindanto garahanto ācariyupajjhāyādīhi “mā evaṃ avacā”ti avaṇṇabhāsane ādīnavaṃ dassetvā nivāretabbo. “Sace yāvatatiyaṃ vuccamāno [M 0.0162] na oramati, kaṇṭakanāsanāya nāsetabbo”ti kurundiyaṃ vuttaṃ. Mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “sace evaṃ vuccamāno taṃ laddhiṃ nissajjati, daṇḍakammaṃ kāretvā accayaṃ desāpetabbo. Sace na nissajjati, tatheva ādāya paggayha tiṭṭhati, liṅganāsanāya nāsetabbo”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ yuttaṃ. Ayameva hi nāsanā idhādhippetāti. Micchādiṭṭhikepi eseva nayo. Sassatucchedānañhi aññataradiṭṭhiko sace ācariyādīhi ovadiyamāno nissajjati, daṇḍakammaṃ kāretvā accayaṃ desāpetabbo, apaṭinissajjantova nāsetabbo. Bhikkhunīdūsako cettha kāmaṃ abrahmacāriggahaṇena gahitova, abrahmacāriṃ pana āyatiṃ saṃvare ṭhātukāmaṃ saraṇāni datvā upasampādetuṃ vaṭṭati. Bhikkhunīdūsako āyatiṃ saṃvare ṭhātukāmopi pabbajjampi na labhati, pageva upasampadanti etamatthaṃ dassetuṃ “bhikkhunīdūsako”ti idaṃ visuṃ dasamaṃ aṅgaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

However, regarding speaking dispraise, if one speaks dispraise of the Buddha by way of opposition to 'Arahant, Perfectly Self-Enlightened One,' and so on; or of the Dhamma by way of opposition to 'well-expounded,' and so on; or of the Sangha by way of opposition to 'well-practiced,' and so on, thus censuring and disparaging the Triple Gem, he should be restrained by teachers, preceptors, and others by showing him the danger in speaking dispraise, saying, 'Do not speak thus.' It is stated in the Kurundī: 'If, being spoken to up to a third time, he does not desist, he should be expelled by the expulsion of the thorn.' But in the Mahā-aṭṭhakathā, it is said: 'If, being spoken to thus, he abandons that view, he should be made to undergo disciplinary action and confess his offense. If he does not abandon it, but stands holding and maintaining it just as it is, he should be expelled by the expulsion of the insignia.' That is appropriate. For this very expulsion is intended here. This same method applies also in the case of one with wrong view. For if one holding either an eternalist or an annihilationist view, when admonished by teachers and others, abandons it, he should be made to undergo disciplinary action and confess his offense; only if he does not abandon it should he be expelled. And here, a defiler of bhikkhunīs is indeed included by the inclusion of 'unchaste one.' However, it is allowable to give the refuges and grant full ordination to an unchaste person who wishes to maintain restraint in the future. A defiler of bhikkhunīs, even if he wishes to maintain restraint in the future, does not obtain even the going forth, let alone full ordination. It should be understood that to show this meaning, this tenth factor, 'defiler of bhikkhunīs,' is stated separately.

150. “Anujānāmi[V 0.0155], bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa sāmaṇerassa daṇḍakammaṃ kātuṃ. Bhikkhūnaṃ alābhāya parisakkati, bhikkhūnaṃ anatthāya parisakkati, bhikkhūnaṃ avāsāya parisakkati, bhikkhū akkosati, paribhāsati, bhikkhū bhikkhūhi bhedetī”ti (mahāva. 107) “vacanato pana imāni pañca aṅgāni, sikkhāpadesu ca pacchimāni vikālabhojanādīni pañcāti dasa daṇḍakammavatthūni. Kiṃpanettha daṇḍakammaṃ kattabba”nti? “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yattha vā vasati, yattha vā paṭikkamati, tattha āvaraṇaṃ kātu”nti (mahāva. 107) vacanato yattha (mahāva. aṭṭha. 107) vasati vā pavisati vā, tattha āvaraṇaṃ kātabbaṃ “mā idha pavisā”ti. Ubhayenapi attano pariveṇañca vassaggena pattasenāsanañca vuttaṃ. Tasmā na sabbo saṅghārāmo āvaraṇaṃ kātabbo, karonto ca dukkaṭaṃ āpajjati “na, bhikkhave, sabbo saṅghārāmo āvaraṇaṃ kātabbo, yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti vuttattā. Na ca mukhadvāriko āhāro āvaraṇaṃ kātabbo, karonto ca dukkaṭaṃ āpajjati “na, bhikkhave, mukhadvāriko āhāro āvaraṇaṃ kātabbo, yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti vuttattā. Tasmā “ajja mā khāda mā bhuñjā”ti vadatopi “āhārampi nivāressāmī”ti pattacīvaraṃ anto nikkhipatopi sabbapayogesu dukkaṭaṃ. Anācārassa pana dubbacasāmaṇerassa daṇḍakammaṃ katvā yāguṃ vā bhattaṃ vā pattacīvaraṃ vā dassetvā “ettake [M 0.0163] nāma daṇḍakamme āhaṭe idaṃ lacchasī”ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Bhagavatā hi āvaraṇameva daṇḍakammaṃ vuttaṃ. Dhammasaṅgāhakattherehi pana “aparādhānurūpaṃ udakadāruvālikādīnaṃ āharāpanampi kātabba”nti vuttaṃ, tasmā tampi kātabbaṃ, tañca kho “oramissati viramissatī”ti anukampāya, na “nassissati vibbhamissatī”tiādinayappavattena pāpajjhāsayena. “Daṇḍakammaṃ karomī”ti ca uṇhapāsāṇe vā nipajjāpetuṃ pāsāṇiṭṭhakādīni vā sīse nikkhipāpetuṃ udakaṃ vā pavesetuṃ na vaṭṭati.

150. “I allow, Bhikkhus, that a disciplinary action be carried out for a novice endowed with five factors: he strives for the bhikkhus' lack of gain, he strives for the harm of the bhikkhus, he strives for the non-residence of the bhikkhus, he abuses and reviles the bhikkhus, and he divides bhikkhus from bhikkhus.” From this statement, these five factors, and in the training rules the latter five beginning with eating at the wrong time, are the ten grounds for disciplinary action. What disciplinary action, then, should be carried out? “I allow, Bhikkhus, that wherever he dwells or wherever he resorts, a barrier should be made there.” According to this statement, wherever he dwells or enters, a barrier should be made there, saying, “Do not enter here.” By both are meant his own precinct and the lodging obtained by seniority of the rains-residence. Therefore, the entire monastery should not be barred, and one who does so incurs an offense of wrongdoing, for it has been said: “Bhikkhus, the entire monastery should not be barred; whoever does so incurs an offense of wrongdoing.” Nor should food that enters by the mouth be barred, and one who does so incurs an offense of wrongdoing, for it has been said: “Bhikkhus, food that enters by the mouth should not be barred; whoever does so incurs an offense of wrongdoing.” Therefore, for one who says, “Today, do not chew or eat,” or for one who, intending to withhold food, puts away the bowl and robe, in all such applications, there is an offense of wrongdoing. However, for a misbehaving and disobedient novice, after imposing a disciplinary action, it is permissible to show him gruel, food, or a bowl and robe and say, “When such and such a disciplinary task has been carried out, you will receive this.” For by the Blessed One only barring was stated as a disciplinary action. But the Elders who compiled the Dhamma said, “According to the offense, causing him to bring water, firewood, sand, and so on, should also be done.” Therefore, that too should be done. And that should be done out of compassion, with the thought, “He will desist, he will cease,” not with an evil intention proceeding in the manner of “he will perish, he will disrobe,” and so on. And, thinking, “I am imposing a disciplinary action,” it is not permissible to make him lie on hot stones, or have him place stones, bricks, and so on, on his head, or make him enter water.

Upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchāpi daṇḍakammaṃ na kāretabbaṃ “na, bhikkhave, upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchā āvaraṇaṃ kātabbaṃ, yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 108) vacanato. Ettha pana “tumhākaṃ sāmaṇerassa ayaṃ nāma aparādho, daṇḍakammamassa karothā”ti tikkhattuṃ vutte sace so upajjhāyo daṇḍakammaṃ na karoti, sayaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sacepi ādito upajjhāyo vadati “mayhaṃ sāmaṇerānaṃ dose sati tumhe daṇḍakammaṃ karothā”ti, kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Yathā ca sāmaṇerānaṃ, evaṃ saddhivihārikantevāsikānampi daṇḍakammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, aññesaṃ pana parisā na apalāḷetabbā, apalāḷento dukkaṭaṃ āpajjati “na, bhikkhave, aññassa parisā apalāḷetabbā, yo apalāḷeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 108) vacanato[V 0.0156]. Tasmā “tumhākaṃ pattaṃ dema, cīvaraṃ demā”ti attano upaṭṭhānakaraṇatthaṃ saṅgaṇhitvā sāmaṇerā vā hontu upasampannā vā, antamaso dussīlabhikkhussapi parassa parisabhūte bhinditvā gaṇhituṃ na vaṭṭati, ādīnavaṃ pana vattuṃ vaṭṭati “tayā nahāyituṃ āgatena gūthamakkhanaṃ viya kataṃ dussīlaṃ nissāya viharantenā”ti. Sace so sayameva jānitvā upajjhaṃ vā nissayaṃ vā yācati, dātuṃ vaṭṭati.

One should not have a disciplinary action carried out without asking the preceptor, because of the text: “Bhikkhus, a prohibition should not be made without asking the preceptor. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrongdoing.” Here, however, if it is said three times, “This novice of yours has this particular offense; perform disciplinary action for him,” and if that preceptor does not perform the disciplinary action, it is allowable to do it oneself. And if from the beginning the preceptor says, “When my novices have a fault, you should perform the disciplinary action,” it is certainly allowable to do so. And just as for novices, so too for co-residents and pupils, it is allowable to perform disciplinary action. But the assembly of others should not be enticed away; one who entices away commits an offense of wrongdoing, because of the text: “Bhikkhus, the assembly of another should not be enticed away. Whoever should entice it away, commits an offense of wrongdoing.” Therefore, for the purpose of making them one's own attendants by saying, “We will give you a bowl, we will give you a robe,” it is not allowable to break up and take those who are another's assembly—whether they be novices or fully ordained bhikkhus, even down to the assembly of an immoral bhikkhu. But it is allowable to speak of the danger, thus: “By you, dwelling in dependence on an immoral person, it is as if one who has come to bathe has smeared themselves with excrement.” If that person, having understood for himself, requests a preceptor or dependence, it is allowable to give it.

Iti pāḷimuttakavinayavinicchayasaṅgahe

Thus in the Pāḷimuttakavinayavinicchayasaṅgaha.

Pabbajjāvinicchayakathā samattā.

The Discourse on the Determination of the Going Forth is concluded.

23. Nissayavinicchayakathā

23. The Discourse on the Determination of Dependence

151. Nissayoti [M 0.0164][V 0.0157] ettha pana ayaṃ nissayo nāma kena dātabbo, kena na dātabbo, kassa dātabbo, kassa na dātabbo, kathaṃ gahito hoti, kathaṃ paṭippassambhati, nissāya kena vasitabbaṃ, kena ca na vasitabbanti? Tattha kena dātabbo, kena na dātabboti ettha tāva “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena dasavassena vā atirekadasavassena vā upasampādetuṃ, nissayaṃ dātu”nti (mahāva. 76, 82) ca vacanato yo byatto hoti paṭibalo upasampadāya dasavasso vā atirekadasavasso vā, tena dātabbo, itarena na dātabbo. Sace deti, dukkaṭaṃ āpajjati.

151. Regarding dependence, in this context: By whom should it be given? By whom should it not be given? To whom should it be given? To whom should it not be given? How is it undertaken? How does it cease? Under whose dependence should one live? And under whose dependence should one not live? Here, regarding 'by whom should it be given, and by whom should it not be given,' first, according to the statement, 'I allow, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who is competent, capable, and of ten years' standing or more than ten years' standing to confer ordination and to give dependence,' it should be given by a bhikkhu who is competent, capable, and is of ten years' standing or more than ten years' standing from his higher ordination. It should not be given by another. If one gives it, one incurs an offense of wrongdoing.

Ettha (pāci. aṭṭha. 145-147) ca “byatto”ti iminā parisupaṭṭhāpakabahussuto veditabbo. Parisupaṭṭhāpakena hi sabbantimena paricchedena parisaṃ abhivinaye vinetuṃ dve vibhaṅgā paguṇā vācuggatā kātabbā, asakkontena tīhi janehi saddhiṃ parivattanakkhamā kātabbā, kammākammañca khandhakavattañca uggahetabbaṃ, parisāya pana abhidhamme vinayanatthaṃ sace majjhimabhāṇako hoti, mūlapaṇṇāsako uggahetabbo, dīghabhāṇakena mahāvaggo, saṃyuttabhāṇakena heṭṭhimā vā tayo vaggā mahāvaggo vā, aṅguttarabhāṇakena heṭṭhā vā upari vā upaḍḍhanikāyo uggahetabbo, asakkontena tikanipātato paṭṭhāya uggahetumpi vaṭṭati. Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana “ekaṃ gaṇhantena catukkanipātaṃ vā pañcakanipātaṃ vā uggahetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Jātakabhāṇakena sāṭṭhakathaṃ jātakaṃ uggahetabbaṃ, tato oraṃ na vaṭṭati. “Dhammapadampi saha vatthunā uggahetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti mahāpaccariyaṃ vuttaṃ. Tato tato samuccayaṃ katvā mūlapaṇṇāsakamattaṃ vaṭṭati, “na vaṭṭatī”ti kurundaṭṭhakathāyaṃ paṭikkhittaṃ, itarāsu vicāraṇāyeva natthi. Abhidhamme kiñci gahetabbanti na vuttaṃ. Yassa pana sāṭṭhakathampi vinayapiṭakaṃ abhidhammapiṭakañca paguṇaṃ, suttante ca vuttappakāro gantho natthi, parisaṃ upaṭṭhāpetuṃ na labhati. Yena pana suttantato ca vinayato ca vuttappamāṇo gantho uggahito, ayaṃ parisupaṭṭhāko bahussutova hoti, disāpāmokkho yenakāmaṃgamo parisaṃ upaṭṭhāpetuṃ labhati, ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe “byatto”ti adhippeto.

Here (Pāci. Aṭṭha. 145-147), by the term 'byatto' (competent), one who is learned and attends to an assembly should be understood. For, at the very minimum, one who attends to an assembly must, in order to discipline the assembly in the Abhivinaya, make the two Vibhaṅgas proficient and learn them by heart. If unable, one should be capable of recitation in rotation with three others. The Kammākamma and the duties of the Khandhakas must also be learned. Furthermore, for the purpose of disciplining the assembly in the Abhidhamma, if one is a reciter of the Majjhima Nikāya, the Mūlapaṇṇāsaka should be learned. A Dīgha reciter should learn the Mahāvagga; a Saṃyutta reciter, either the lower three Vaggas or the Mahāvagga; and an Aṅguttara reciter, either the lower or upper half of the Nikāya. If unable, it is permissible to learn starting from the Tikanipāta. In the Mahāpaccarī, however, it is said: 'For one learning a single Nipāta, it is permissible to learn either the Catukkanipāta or the Pañcakanipāta.' A Jātaka reciter must learn the Jātaka with its commentary; less than that is not permissible. In the Mahāpaccarī it is also said: 'It is permissible to learn the Dhammapada together with its stories.' The proposition that it is permissible to compile selections from various texts to the extent of the Mūlapaṇṇāsaka is rejected in the Kurundaṭṭhakathā with the words, 'It is not permissible.' In the other commentaries, there is no investigation of this matter. It is not said that anything from the Abhidhamma should be learned. However, a monk for whom the Vinaya Piṭaka and the Abhidhamma Piṭaka with their commentaries are proficient, but who lacks the type of textual knowledge in the Suttanta as described, is not permitted to attend to an assembly. But the one who has learned the prescribed amount from the Suttanta and the Vinaya is indeed one who attends to assemblies and is learned. Such a person becomes a leading teacher of the region and, being one who can go wherever they wish, is permitted to attend to an assembly. This is the person intended by the term 'byatto' in this context.

Yo [M 0.0165][V 0.0158] pana antevāsino vā saddhivihārikassa vā gilānassa sakkoti upaṭṭhānādīni kātuṃ, ayaṃ idha “paṭibalo”ti adhippeto. Yaṃ pana vuttaṃ –

The monk who is able to perform duties such as attending to a sick pupil or co-resident is here intended by the term 'capable.' And it has been said:

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Na asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Monks, a monk endowed with five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He is not endowed with the aggregate of moral discipline of one beyond training, not endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, not endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, not endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, not endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Attanā na asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe sīlakkhandhe samādapetā. Attanā na asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe samādhikkhandhe samādapetā. Attanā na asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe paññākkhandhe samādapetā. Attanā na asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe vimuttikkhandhe samādapetā. Attanā na asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhe samādapetā. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Furthermore, monks, a monk endowed with another five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He himself is not endowed with the aggregate of moral discipline of one beyond training, nor does he establish another in the aggregate of moral discipline of one beyond training. He himself is not endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, nor does he establish another in the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training. He himself is not endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, nor does he establish another in the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training. He himself is not endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, nor does he establish another in the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training. He himself is not endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training, nor does he establish another in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Assaddho hoti, ahiriko hoti, anottappī hoti, kusīto hoti, muṭṭhassati hoti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ[M 0.0166], na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Furthermore, monks, a monk endowed with another five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He is without faith, he is shameless, he is without fear of wrongdoing, he is lazy, and he is of lapsed mindfulness. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre [V 0.0159] ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti, appassuto hoti, duppañño hoti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Furthermore, monks, a monk endowed with another five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He is corrupt in higher morality, corrupt in higher conduct, corrupt in higher view, is of little learning, and is of little wisdom. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Na paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ vā upaṭṭhāpetuṃ vā, anabhirataṃ vūpakāsetuṃ vā vūpakāsāpetuṃ vā, uppannaṃ kukkuccaṃ dhammato vinodetuṃ, āpattiṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā vuṭṭhānaṃ na jānāti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Furthermore, monks, a monk endowed with another five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He is not able to attend on or have another attend on a sick resident pupil or co-resident; he is not able to appease or have another appease discontent; he is not able to dispel arisen remorse according to the Dhamma; he does not know an offense; he does not know the rehabilitation from an offense. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Na paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā ābhisamācārikāya sikkhāya sikkhāpetuṃ, ādibrahmacariyakāya sikkhāya vinetuṃ, abhidhamme vinetuṃ, abhivinaye vinetuṃ, uppannaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ dhammato vivecetuṃ. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not give the higher ordination, nor give dependence, nor have a novice attend on him. He is not capable of training a resident pupil or a co-resident in the training concerning excellent conduct, of disciplining them in the training that is the beginning of the holy life, of disciplining them in the Abhidhamma, of disciplining them in the Abhivinaya, or of dispelling an arisen wrong view in accordance with the Dhamma. Indeed, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not give the higher ordination, nor give dependence, nor have a novice attend on him.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo[M 0.0167]. Āpattiṃ na jānāti, anāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena na svāgatāni honti na suvibhattāni na suppavattīni na suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not give the higher ordination, nor give dependence, nor have a novice attend on him. He does not know an offense, he does not know what is not an offense, he does not know a light offense, he does not know a heavy offense; and for him, both Pātimokkhas have not been well-mastered in detail, are not well-analyzed, are not well-practiced, and are not well-adjudicated according to the rules and their detailed explanations. Indeed, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not give the higher ordination, nor give dependence, nor have a novice attend on him.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Āpattiṃ na jānāti, anāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ūnadasavasso hoti[V 0.0160]. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo”tiādi (mahāva. 84). Tampi –

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not give the higher ordination, nor give dependence, nor have a novice attend on him. He does not know an offense, he does not know what is not an offense, he does not know a light offense, he does not know a heavy offense, and he is of less than ten years' standing. Indeed, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not give the higher ordination, nor give dependence, nor have a novice attend on him.” And so on.

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena dasavassena vā atirekadasavassena vā upasampādetuṃ, nissayaṃ dātu”nti (mahāva. 76, 82) ca evaṃ saṅkhepato vuttasseva upajjhāyācariyalakkhaṇassa vitthāradassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ.

“I allow, bhikkhus, a competent and able bhikkhu of ten years' standing or more than ten years' standing to give the higher ordination and to give dependence.” This was said for the purpose of showing in detail the characteristics of preceptors and teachers which were thus stated only concisely.

Tattha (mahāva. aṭṭha. 84) kiñci ayuttavasena paṭikkhittaṃ, kiñci āpattiaṅgavasena. Tathā hi “na asekkhena sīlakkhandhenā”ti ca “attanā na asekkhenā”ti ca “assaddho”ti ca ādīsu tīsu pañcakesu ayuttavasena paṭikkhepo kato, na āpattiaṅgavasena. Yo hi asekkhehi sīlakkhandhādīhi asamannāgato pare ca tattha samādapetuṃ asakkonto assaddhiyādidosayuttova hutvā parisaṃ pariharati, tassa parisā sīlādīhi pariyāyatiyeva na vaḍḍhati, tasmā “tena na upasampādetabba”ntiādi ayuttavasena vuttaṃ, na āpattiaṅgavasena. Na hi khīṇāsavasseva upajjhācariyabhāvo bhagavatā anuññāto, yadi tasseva anuññāto abhavissa, “sace upajjhāyassa anabhirati uppannā hotī”tiādiṃ na vadeyya, yasmā pana khīṇāsavassa parisā sīlādīhi na parihāyati, tasmā “pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabba”ntiādi vuttaṃ.

Therein, some things are rejected on account of unsuitability, and some on account of being factors of an offense. For instance, in the three sets of five, such as “not with the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training,” “not being oneself beyond training,” and “one who is faithless,” the rejection is made on account of unsuitability, not on account of being a factor of an offense. For, a person who is not endowed with the aggregates of virtue, etc., of one beyond training and is unable to establish others therein, and who, being endowed with faults such as lack of faith, leads an assembly—that person's assembly only declines in virtue, etc., and does not grow. Therefore, it was said, “The higher ordination should not be given by that person,” etc., on account of unsuitability, not on account of being a factor of an offense. Indeed, the state of being a preceptor or teacher was not permitted by the Blessed One exclusively to one whose taints are destroyed. If it had been permitted only to such a one, He would not have said, “If dissatisfaction arises in the preceptor,” etc. However, because the assembly of one whose taints are destroyed does not decline in virtue, etc., it was said, “Bhikkhus, the higher ordination should be given by a bhikkhu endowed with five factors,” etc.

Adhisīle [M 0.0168] sīlavipannotiādīsu pārājikañca saṅghādisesañca āpanno adhisīle sīlavipanno nāma. Itare pañcāpattikkhandhe āpanno ajjhācāre ācāravipanno nāma. Sammādiṭṭhiṃ pahāya antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno nāma. Yattakaṃ sutaṃ parisaṃ pariharantassa icchitabbaṃ, tena virahitattā appassuto. Yaṃ tena jānitabbaṃ āpattādi, tassa ajānanato duppañño. Imasmiṃ pañcake purimāni tīṇi padāni ayuttavasena vuttāni, pacchimāni dve āpattiaṅgavasena.

In such phrases as ‘corrupt in virtue regarding higher virtue’: one who has committed a pārājika or a saṅghādisesa offense is called ‘corrupt in virtue regarding higher virtue.’ One who has committed offenses in the other five groups of offenses is called ‘corrupt in conduct regarding higher conduct.’ One who, having abandoned right view, is endowed with a view that grasps at extremes is called ‘corrupt in view regarding higher view.’ Because of being devoid of as much learning as is desirable for one who leads an assembly, one is of little learning. Because of not knowing what should be known by him, such as what is an offense, one is of little wisdom. In this pentad, the former three terms are stated on account of unsuitability; the latter two are stated on account of being factors of an offense.

Āpattiṃ na jānātīti “idaṃ nāma mayā kata”nti vutte “imaṃ nāma āpattiṃ ayaṃ āpanno”ti na jānāti. Vuṭṭhānaṃ na jānātīti “vuṭṭhānagāminito vā desanāgāminito vā āpattito evaṃ nāma vuṭṭhānaṃ hotī”ti na jānāti. Imasmiñhi pañcake purimāni dve padāni ayuttavasena vuttāni, pacchimāni tīṇi āpattiaṅgavasena.

‘He does not know an offense’ means: when it is said, ‘Such and such was done by me,’ he does not know, ‘This one has committed such and such an offense.’ ‘He does not know the rehabilitation’ means: he does not know, ‘From an offense that is rehabilitation-leading or from an offense that is confession-leading, rehabilitation occurs in such and such a way.’ Indeed, in this pentad, the former two terms are stated on account of unsuitability; the latter three are stated on account of being factors of an offense.

Ābhisamācārikāya [V 0.0161] sikkhāyāti khandhakavatte vinetuṃ na paṭibalo hotīti attho. Ādibrahmacariyakāyāti sekkhapaṇṇattiyaṃ vinetuṃ na paṭibaloti attho. Abhidhammeti nāmarūpaparicchede vinetuṃ na paṭibaloti attho. Abhivinayeti sakale vinayapiṭake vinetuṃ na paṭibaloti attho. Vinetuṃ na paṭibaloti ca sabbattha sikkhāpetuṃ na sakkotīti attho. Dhammato vivecetunti dhammena kāraṇena vissajjāpetuṃ. Imasmiṃ pañcake sabbapadesu āpatti.

‘In the training concerning excellent conduct’ means: he is not capable of training in the Khandhaka duties. ‘In the training that is the beginning of the holy life’ means: he is not capable of training in the rules for trainees. ‘In the Abhidhamma’ means: he is not capable of training in the discrimination of name-and-form. ‘In the Abhivinaya’ means: he is not capable of training in the entire Vinaya Piṭaka. And ‘is not capable of training’ means, in all cases: he is not able to instruct. ‘To dispel in accordance with the Dhamma’ means: to cause to be dismissed by a reason in accordance with the Dhamma. In this pentad, an offense is incurred in all cases.

“Āpattiṃ na jānātī”tiādipañcakasmiṃ vitthārenāti ubhatovibhaṅgena saddhiṃ. Na svāgatānīti na suṭṭhu āgatāni. Suvibhattānīti suṭṭhu vibhattāni padapaccābhaṭṭhasaṅkaradosaraatāni. Suppavattīnīti paguṇāni vācuggatāni suvinicchitāni. Suttasoti khandhakaparivārato āharitabbasuttavasena suṭṭhu vinicchitāni. Anubyañjanasoti akkharapadapāripūriyā ca suvinicchitāni akhaṇḍāni aviparītakkharāni. Etena aṭṭhakathā dīpitā. Aṭṭhakathāto hi esa vinicchayo hotīti. Imasmiṃ pañcakepi sabbapadesu āpatti. Ūnadasavassapariyosānapañcakepi eseva nayo. Iti ādito tayo pañcakā, catutthe tīṇi padāni, pañcame dve padānīti sabbepi cattāro pañcakā ayuttavasena vuttā, catutthe pañcake dve [M 0.0169] padāni, pañcame tīṇi, chaṭṭhasattamaṭṭhamā tayo pañcakāti sabbepi cattāro pañcakā āpattiaṅgavasena vuttā.

In the set of five beginning with “He does not know an offense,” the phrase “in detail” means together with both Vibhaṅgas. ‘Not well-mastered’ means not properly mastered. ‘Well-analyzed’ means well-analyzed, free from the faults of misrecitation and confusion of words. ‘Well-recited’ means fluent, memorized, and well-determined. ‘By way of the suttas’ means well-determined by way of the suttas to be brought from the Khandhaka and Parivāra. ‘By way of the details’ means well-determined through the completeness of letters and words, being unbroken and with uncorrupted letters. By this, the commentary is explained, for this determination is indeed from the commentary. In this set of five also, there is an offense in all cases. In the set of five ending with “less than ten years’ standing” also, this is the same method. Thus, the first three sets of five, three terms in the fourth, and two terms in the fifth—all these four sets of five are stated on account of unsuitability. Two terms in the fourth set of five, three in the fifth, and the sixth, seventh, and eighth sets of five—all these four sets of five are stated on account of being factors of an offense.

Sukkapakkhe pana vuttavipariyāyena “pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hotī”tiādinā (mahāva. 84) aṭṭha pañcakā āgatāyeva. Tattha sabbattheva anāpatti.

However, in the positive aspect, in the reverse manner of what was said, it is stated: “O bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with five qualities should give the full ordination, give dependence, and have a novice attend on him. He is endowed with the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training,” and so forth—thus, eight sets of five have indeed been presented. There, in all these cases, there is no offense.

152. Kassa dātabbo, kassa na dātabboti ettha pana yo lajjī hoti, tassa dātabbo. Itarassa na dātabbo “na, bhikkhave, alajjīnaṃ nissayo dātabbo, yo dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 120) vacanato.
