Evaṃ sannipatitesu bhikkhūsu chandārahānaṃ chande āhaṭe tesu tesu maggesu nadītitthagāmadvārādīsu ca āgantukabhikkhūnaṃ sīghaṃ sīghaṃ hatthapāsanayanatthañceva bahisīmakaraṇatthañca ārāmike ceva samaṇuddese ca [M 0.0187] ṭhapetvā bherisaññaṃ vā saṅkhasaññaṃ vā katvā nimittakittanānantaraṃ vuttāya “suṇātu me bhante saṅgho”tiādikāya kammavācāya sīmā bandhitabbā. Kammavācāpariyosāneyeva nimittāni bahikatvā heṭṭhā pathavīsandhārakaṃ udakapariyantaṃ katvā sīmā gatā hoti.

Thus, when the monks have assembled and the consents of those eligible to give consent have been brought, having stationed monastery attendants and novices on those various roads, and at river-fords, village-gates, and so on, for the purpose of very quickly bringing arriving monks into hand's reach and for the purpose of keeping them outside the boundary, and having made a signal with a drum or a conch, immediately after the announcement of the boundary-markers, the boundary should be established by the formal act beginning with, 'Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha listen to me.' Just at the conclusion of the formal act, having made the boundary-markers external, and having made it so that below it has the earth as its support and water as its limit, the boundary is established.

163. Imaṃ pana samānasaṃvāsakasīmaṃ sammannantehi pabbajjūpasampadādīnaṃ saṅghakammānaṃ sukhakaraṇatthaṃ paṭhamaṃ khaṇḍasīmā bandhitabbā. Taṃ pana bandhantehi vattaṃ jānitabbaṃ. Sace hi bodhicetiyabhattasālādīni [V 0.0178] sabbavatthūni patiṭṭhāpetvā katavihāre bandhanti, vihāramajjhe bahūnaṃ samosaraṇaṭṭhāne abandhitvā vihārapaccante vivittokāse bandhitabbā. Akatavihāre bandhantehi bodhicetiyādīnaṃ sabbavatthūnaṃ ṭhānaṃ sallakkhetvā yathā patiṭṭhitesu vatthūsu vihārapaccante vivittokāse hoti, evaṃ bandhitabbā. Sā heṭṭhimaparicchedena sace ekavīsati bhikkhū gaṇhāti, vaṭṭati, tato oraṃ na vaṭṭati, paraṃ bhikkhusahassaṃ gaṇhantīpi vaṭṭati. Taṃ bandhantehi sīmamāḷakassa samantā nimittupagā pāsāṇā ṭhapetabbā, na khaṇḍasīmāya ṭhitehi mahāsīmā bandhitabbā, na mahāsīmāya ṭhitehi khaṇḍasīmā, khaṇḍasīmāyameva pana ṭhatvā khaṇḍasīmā bandhitabbā.

163. When designating this boundary for common-communion, a partial boundary (khaṇḍasīmā) should first be established for the ease of performing Saṅgha acts such as the going forth and higher ordination. When establishing it, the procedure should be known. If they are establishing it in a constructed monastery where all structures such as Bodhi trees, cetiyas, and dining halls have been established, it should be established in a secluded place at the edge of the monastery, not in the gathering place of many in the middle of the monastery. When establishing it in an unconstructed monastery, after marking out the locations for all structures such as Bodhi trees and cetiyas, it should be established in such a way that when these structures are established, it will be in a secluded place at the edge of the monastery. This boundary, by its lowest limit, if it holds twenty-one monks, is allowable; less than that is not allowable; beyond that, even one holding a thousand monks is allowable. When establishing it, stones serving as markers should be placed all around the sīmā enclosure. A great boundary (mahāsīmā) should not be established by those standing within a partial boundary, nor a partial boundary by those standing within a great boundary; however, a partial boundary should be established only by standing within that same partial boundary.

Tatrāyaṃ bandhanavidhi – samantā “eso pāsāṇo nimitta”nti evaṃ nimittāni kittetvā kammavācāya sīmā sammannitabbā. Atha tassā eva daḷhīkammatthaṃ avippavāsakammavācā kātabbā. Evañhi “sīmaṃ samūhanissāmā”ti āgatā samūhanituṃ na sakkhissanti. Sīmaṃ sammannitvā bahi sīmantarikapāsāṇā ṭhapetabbā. Sīmantarikā pacchimakoṭiyā ekaratanappamāṇā vaṭṭati. “Vidatthippamāṇāpi vaṭṭatī”ti kurundiyaṃ, “caturaṅgulappamāṇāpi vaṭṭatī”ti mahāpaccariyaṃ vuttaṃ. Sace pana vihāro mahā hoti, dvepi tissopi tatuttarimpi khaṇḍasīmāyo bandhitabbā.

Herein is the method of establishing the boundary. Having announced the markers all around, saying, 'This stone is a marker,' the boundary should be designated by a formal act (kammavācā). Then, for the sake of making it firm, a formal act of non-separation should be performed. For thus, those who have come saying, 'We will remove the boundary,' will not be able to remove it. Having designated the boundary, boundary-interval stones should be placed outside. The boundary-interval, at a minimum, is allowable at a distance of one ratana. In the Kurundī it is said, 'Even a distance of one span (vidatthi) is allowable,' and in the Mahāpaccarī it is said, 'Even a distance of four finger-breadths is allowable.' However, if the monastery is large, two, three, or even more partial boundaries should be established.

Evaṃ khaṇḍasīmaṃ sammannitvā mahāsīmasammutikāle khaṇḍasīmato nikkhamitvā mahāsīmāyaṃ ṭhatvā samantā anupariyāyantehi sīmantarikapāsāṇā kittetabbā, tato avasesanimittāni kittetvā hatthapāsaṃ avijahantehi kammavācāya samānasaṃvāsakasīmaṃ sammannitvā tassā daḷhīkammatthaṃ avippavāsakammavācāpi kātabbā. Evañhi “sīmaṃ samūhanissāmā”ti āgatā samūhanituṃ na sakkhissanti. Sace pana khaṇḍasīmāya [M 0.0188] nimittāni kittetvā tato sīmantarikāya nimittāni kittetvā mahāsīmāya nimittāni kittenti, evaṃ tīsu ṭhānesu nimittāni kittetvā yaṃ sīmaṃ icchanti, taṃ paṭhamaṃ bandhituṃ vaṭṭati. Evaṃ santepi yathāvuttanayena khaṇḍasīmatova paṭṭhāya bandhitabbā. Evaṃ baddhāsu pana sīmāsu khaṇḍasīmāya ṭhitā bhikkhū mahāsīmāya kammaṃ karontānaṃ na kopenti, mahāsīmāya vā ṭhitā khaṇḍasīmāya karontānaṃ, sīmantarikāya pana ṭhitā ubhinnampi na kopenti. Gāmakhette ṭhatvā kammaṃ karontānaṃ pana sīmantarikāya ṭhitā kopenti. Sīmantarikā hi gāmakhettaṃ bhajati.

Having thus established a partial boundary, at the time of establishing a great boundary, they should step out from the partial boundary and stand within the great boundary. Then, while walking around the perimeter, they should designate the boundary stones of the boundary-interval. Thereafter, having designated the remaining signs of the great boundary, without straying beyond a hand's reach, they should establish a boundary for common-communion by means of a formal act. To strengthen this, a formal act of non-separation should also be performed. For in this way, those who come saying, 'We will remove the boundary,' will not be able to remove it. But if, after designating the marks of the partial boundary, they then designate the marks of the boundary-interval, and then designate the marks of the great boundary—having thus designated the marks in these three places—they may first establish whichever boundary they desire. Even so, they should begin establishing from the partial boundary in the manner stated. When the boundaries are thus established, the monks standing in the partial boundary do not invalidate the formal acts of those performing a formal act in the great boundary, nor do those standing in the great boundary invalidate the acts of those performing an act in the partial boundary. Those standing in the boundary-interval, however, invalidate neither. But those standing in the boundary-interval do invalidate the formal acts of those performing a formal act while standing in a village area, for the boundary-interval belongs to the village area.

Sīmā [V 0.0179] ca nāmesā na kevalā pathavītaleyeva baddhā baddhā nāma hoti, atha kho piṭṭhipāsāṇepi kuṭigehepi leṇepi pāsādepi pabbatamatthakepi baddhā baddhāyeva hoti. Tattha piṭṭhipāsāṇe bandhantehi pāsāṇapiṭṭhiyaṃ rājiṃ vā koṭṭetvā udukkhalaṃ vā khaṇitvā nimittaṃ na kātabbaṃ, nimittupagapāsāṇe ṭhapetvā nimittāni kittetabbāni. Kammavācāpariyosāne sīmā pathavīsandhārakaṃ udakapariyantaṃ katvā otarati. Nimittapāsāṇā yathāṭhāne na tiṭṭhanti, tasmā samantato rāji vā upaṭṭhāpetabbā, catūsu vā koṇesu pāsāṇā vijjhitabbā, “ayaṃ sīmāparicchedo”ti vatvā akkharāni vā chinditabbāni. Keci usūyakā “sīmaṃ jhāpessāmā”ti aggiṃ denti, pāsāṇāva jhāyanti, na sīmā.

This boundary is not considered established only when established on the surface of the earth; rather, it is indeed established when established on a flat stone, in a hut-dwelling, in a cave, in a mansion, or on a mountain peak. When establishing the boundary on a flat stone, a mark should not be made by carving a line or digging a small pit on the surface of the stone; instead, stones suitable for marks should be placed and the marks declared. At the conclusion of the formal act, the boundary descends, making the earth its support and water its limit. The marker stones do not remain in their proper place; therefore, a line should be made all around, or stones should be pierced at the four corners, or letters should be carved after saying, 'This is the boundary demarcation.' Some envious people, thinking, 'We will burn the boundary,' apply fire, but only the stones burn, not the boundary.

Kuṭigehepi bhittiṃ akittetvā ekavīsatiyā bhikkhūnaṃ okāsaṭṭhānaṃ antokaritvā pāsāṇanimittāni ṭhapetvā sīmā sammannitabbā, antokuṭṭameva sīmā hoti. Sace antokuṭṭe ekavīsatiyā bhikkhūnaṃ okāso natthi, pamukhe nimittapāsāṇe ṭhapetvā sammannitabbā. Sace evampi nappahoti, bahi nibbodakapatanaṭṭhānepi nimittāni ṭhapetvā sammannitabbā. Evaṃ sammatāya pana sabbaṃ kuṭigehaṃ sīmaṭṭhameva hoti.

In a hut-dwelling also, without declaring the wall, having included a space for twenty-one monks inside and having placed stone markers, the boundary should be agreed upon; the boundary is only within the wall. If there is no space for twenty-one monks within the wall, marker stones should be placed at the entrance and it should be agreed upon. If even this is not sufficient, markers should be placed even at the outside place where water drips down, and it should be agreed upon. When it has been agreed upon in this way, the entire hut-dwelling is indeed within the boundary.

Catubhittiyaleṇepi bandhantehi kuṭṭaṃ akittetvā pāsāṇāva kittetabbā, anto okāse asati pamukhepi nimittāni ṭhapetabbāni, evaṃ leṇassa anto ca bahi ca sīmā hoti.

When establishing a boundary in a four-walled cave also, without declaring the wall, only the stones should be declared. If there is no space inside, markers should be placed at the entrance also. Thus, the boundary is both inside and outside the cave.

Uparipāsādepi [M 0.0189] bhittiṃ akittetvā antopāsāṇe ṭhapetvā sīmā sammannitabbā. Sace nappahoti, pamukhepi pāsāṇe ṭhapetvā sammannitabbā. Evaṃ sammatā uparipāsādeyeva hoti, heṭṭhā na otarati. Sace pana bahūsu thambhesu tulānaṃ upari katapāsādassa heṭṭhimatale kuṭṭo yathā nimittānaṃ anto hoti, evaṃ uṭṭhahitvā tulārukkhehi ekasambandho ṭhito, heṭṭhāpi otarati, ekathambhapāsādassa pana uparitale baddhā sīmā. Sace thambhamatthake ekavīsatiyā bhikkhūnaṃ okāso hoti, heṭṭhā otarati. Sace pāsādabhittito niggatesu niyyūhakādīsu pāsāṇe ṭhapetvā sīmaṃ bandhanti, pāsādabhitti antosīmāya hoti. Heṭṭhā panassā otaraṇānotaraṇaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

Even on an upper palace, without declaring the wall, the boundary should be agreed upon by placing stones inside. If that is not sufficient, it should be agreed upon by placing stones at the entrance as well. A boundary agreed upon in this way is only on the upper palace; it does not descend below. However, if, for a palace built upon many pillars above the beams, the wall in the lower story is such that it is inside the marks, having risen up and standing connected as one with the beam-pillars, it descends below as well. As for a boundary established on the upper story of a single-pillared palace, if there is space for twenty-one monks on the top of the pillar, it descends below. If they establish the boundary by placing stones on projecting features like eaves, etc., extending from the palace wall, the palace wall is within the boundary. But whether it descends below or not should be understood in the way already explained.

Heṭṭhāpāsāde kittentehipi bhitti ca rukkhatthambhā ca na kittetabbā, bhittilagge pana pāsāṇatthambhe kittetuṃ vaṭṭati. Evaṃ kittitā sīmā heṭṭhāpāsādassa pariyantathambhānaṃ antoyeva hoti. Sace pana heṭṭhāpāsādassa kuṭṭo uparimatalena sambaddho hoti, uparipāsādampi [V 0.0180] abhiruhati. Sace pāsādassa bahi nibbodakapatanaṭṭhāne nimittāni karonti, sabbo pāsādo sīmaṭṭho hoti.

When declaring marks in a lower palace, neither the wall nor the wooden pillars should be declared. But it is permissible to declare stone pillars attached to the wall. A boundary declared in this way is only within the perimeter pillars of the lower palace. However, if the wall of the lower palace is connected to the upper story, it ascends to the upper palace as well. If they make marks outside the palace at the place where the water-drips fall, the entire palace is situated within the boundary.

Pabbatamatthake talaṃ hoti ekavīsatiyā bhikkhūnaṃ okāsārahaṃ, tattha piṭṭhipāsāṇe viya sīmaṃ bandhanti, heṭṭhāpabbatepi teneva paricchedena sīmā otarati. Tālamūlakapabbatepi upari sīmā baddhā heṭṭhā otarateva. Yo pana vitānasaṇṭhāno hoti, upari ekavīsatiyā bhikkhūnaṃ okāso atthi, heṭṭhā natthi, tassupari baddhā sīmā heṭṭhā na otarati. Evaṃ mudiṅgasaṇṭhāno vā hotu paṇavasaṇṭhāno vā, yassa heṭṭhā vā majjhe vā sīmappamāṇaṃ natthi, tassa upari baddhā sīmā heṭṭhā na otarati. Yassa pana dve kūṭāni āsanne ṭhitāni, ekassapi upari sīmappamāṇaṃ nappahoti, tassa kūṭantaraṃ cinitvā vā pūretvā vā ekābaddhaṃ katvā upari sīmā sammannitabbā. Eko sappaphaṇasadiso pabbato, tassa upari sīmappamāṇassa atthitāya sīmaṃ bandhanti, tassa ce heṭṭhā ākāsapabbhāraṃ hoti, sīmā na otarati. Sace panassa vemajjhe sīmappamāṇo susirapāsāṇo hoti, otarati, so ca pāsāṇo sīmaṭṭhoyeva hoti. Athāpissa heṭṭhāleṇassa kuṭṭo aggakoṭiṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati[M 0.0190], otarati, heṭṭhā ca upari ca sīmāyeva hoti. Sace pana heṭṭhā uparimassa sīmāparicchedassa pārato antoleṇaṃ hoti, bahi sīmā na otarati. Athāpi uparimassa sīmāparicchedassa orato bahi leṇaṃ hoti, anto sīmā na otarati. Athāpi upari sīmāparicchedo khuddako, heṭṭhā leṇaṃ mahantaṃ sīmāparicchedamatikkamitvā ṭhitaṃ, sīmā upariyeva hoti, heṭṭhā na otarati. Yadi pana leṇaṃ khuddakaṃ sabbapacchimasīmāparimāṇaṃ, upari sīmā mahatī naṃ ajjhottharitvā ṭhitā, sīmā otarati. Atha leṇaṃ atikhuddakaṃ sīmappamāṇaṃ na hoti, sīmā upariyeva hoti, heṭṭhā na otarati. Sace tato upaḍḍhaṃ bhijjitvā patati, sīmappamāṇaṃ cepi hoti, bahi patitaṃ asīmā. Apatitaṃ pana yadi sīmappamāṇaṃ, sīmā hotiyeva.

On the summit of a mountain, if there is a level area suitable for twenty-one monks, they may establish a boundary there as if on a flat stone, and the boundary descends to the mountain below by that same demarcation. Also on a mountain like the root of a palm tree, a boundary established above certainly descends below. However, as for a mountain that has the shape of a canopy, where there is space above for twenty-one monks but none below, a boundary established on its top does not descend below. Likewise, whether it has the shape of a mudiṅga drum or a paṇava drum, if it does not have the measure for a boundary either below or in the middle, a boundary established on its top does not descend below. But if a mountain has two peaks situated nearby, and on top of even one there is not sufficient measure for a boundary, the space between the peaks should be built up or filled to make it a single connected area, and a boundary should be established on top. If there is a mountain similar to a cobra's hood, and due to there being the measure for a boundary on its top, they establish a boundary, and if below it there is an open precipice, the boundary does not descend. But if in its middle there is a hollow stone of the measure for a boundary, it descends, and that stone is indeed included in the boundary. Furthermore, if the wall of a cave below reaches and touches the very edge, it descends, and it is indeed the boundary both below and above. But if below, beyond the demarcation of the boundary above, there is an inner cave, the boundary does not descend to the outside. Furthermore, if from within the demarcation of the boundary above, there is a cave to the outside, the boundary does not descend inside. Furthermore, if the demarcation of the boundary above is small, and the cave below is large and is situated so as to surpass the boundary demarcation, the boundary is only above; it does not descend below. But if the cave is small, being of the minimum measure for a boundary, and the boundary above is large and is situated so as to encompass it, the boundary descends. Then, if the cave is very small and is not of the measure for a boundary, the boundary is only above; it does not descend below. If half of that boundary breaks off and falls, even if it is of the measure for a boundary, the fallen part is not a boundary. But as for the part that has not fallen, if it is of the measure for a boundary, it is indeed a boundary.

Khaṇḍasīmā ca nīcavatthukā hoti, taṃ pūretvā uccavatthukaṃ karonti, sīmāyeva. Sīmāya gehaṃ karonti, sīmaṭṭhakameva hoti. Sīmāya pokkharaṇiṃ khaṇanti, sīmāyeva. Ogho sīmāmaṇḍalaṃ ottharitvā gacchati, sīmāmāḷake aṭṭaṃ bandhitvā kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sīmāya heṭṭhā umaṅganadī hoti, iddhimā bhikkhu tattha nisīdati. Sace sā nadī paṭhamaṃ gatā, sīmā pacchā baddhā, kammaṃ na kopeti. Atha paṭhamaṃ sīmā baddhā, pacchā nadī gatā, kammaṃ kopeti, heṭṭhāpathavītale ṭhito pana kopetiyeva.

A khaṇḍasīmā may also have a low site; if they fill it and make it a high site, it is still a boundary. If they make a building within the boundary, it is just a boundary structure. If they dig a pond within the boundary, it is still a boundary. If a flood sweeps over the boundary circle, it is permissible to perform an act after constructing a platform on the boundary terrace. If there is an underground river below the boundary where a bhikkhu with psychic power is sitting, and if that river was there first and the boundary was established afterwards, the act is not invalidated. But if the boundary was established first and the river came to be afterwards, it invalidates the act. However, one standing on the ground level below certainly invalidates it.

Sīmāmāḷake [V 0.0181] vaṭarukkho hoti, tassa sākhā vā tato niggatapāroho vā mahāsīmāya pathavītalaṃ vā tatthajātarukkhādīni vā āhacca tiṭṭhati, mahāsīmaṃ vā sodhetvā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ, te vā sākhāpārohā chinditvā bahiṭṭhakā kātabbā. Anāhacca ṭhitasākhādīsu āruḷhabhikkhū hatthapāsaṃ ānetabbā. Evaṃ mahāsīmāya jātarukkhassa sākhā vā pāroho vā vuttanayeneva sīmāmāḷake patiṭṭhāti, vuttanayeneva sīmaṃ sodhetvā vā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ, te vā sākhāpārohā chinditvā bahiṭṭhakā kātabbā. Sace māḷake kamme kariyamāne koci bhikkhu māḷakassa anto pavisitvā vehāsaṃ ṭhitasākhāya nisīdati, pādā vāssa bhūmigatā honti, nivāsanapārupanaṃ vā bhūmiṃ phusati, kammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Pāde pana nivāsanapārupanañca ukkhipāpetvā kātuṃ kammaṃ vaṭṭati, idañca [M 0.0191] lakkhaṇaṃ purimanayepi veditabbaṃ. Ayaṃ pana viseso – tatra ukkhipāpetvā kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, hatthapāsameva ānetabbo. Sace antosīmato pabbato abbhuggacchati, tatraṭṭho bhikkhu hatthapāsaṃ ānetabbo. Iddhiyā antopabbataṃ paviṭṭhepi eseva nayo. Bajjhamānā eva hi sīmā pamāṇarahitaṃ padesaṃ na otarati, baddhāya sīmāya jātaṃ yaṃ kiñci yattha katthaci ekasambandhena gataṃ sīmāsaṅkhyameva gacchatīti.

On the boundary terrace, there is a banyan tree. If its branch or an aerial root extending from it touches the ground of the great boundary, or trees and so forth that have grown there, then either the great boundary should be cleared and the act performed, or those branches and aerial roots should be cut and made to be external. Monks who have climbed on branches and so forth that are situated without touching the ground should be brought to within arm's reach. Similarly, if a branch or an aerial root of a tree that has grown in the great boundary is established on the boundary terrace, then in the same way as stated, either the boundary should be cleared and the act performed, or those branches and aerial roots should be cut and made to be external. If, while an act is being performed on the terrace, some monk, having entered inside the terrace, sits on a branch situated in the open air, and his feet reach the ground or his lower or upper robe touches the ground, it is not allowable to perform the act. However, having caused his feet and his lower and upper robes to be lifted up, it is allowable to perform the act. And this characteristic should be understood in the previous case as well. This, however, is the difference: there, it is not allowable to perform the act after having caused them to be lifted up; he should only be brought to within arm's reach. If a mountain rises up from within the boundary, a monk standing there should be brought to within arm's reach. Even when one has entered into the mountain by psychic power, this is the same method. For a boundary, when it is being established, does not extend to a place beyond its measure. It should be understood that whatever has arisen within an established boundary, whatever it may be, having gone to any place whatsoever by a single connection, is reckoned only as the boundary.

Tiyojanaparamaṃ pana sīmaṃ sammannantena majjhe ṭhatvā yathā catūsupi disāsu diyaḍḍhadiyaḍḍhayojanaṃ hoti, evaṃ sammannitabbā. Sace pana majjhe ṭhatvā ekekadisato tiyojanaṃ karonti, chayojanaṃ hotīti na vaṭṭati. Caturassaṃ vā tikoṇaṃ vā sammannantena yathā koṇato koṇaṃ tiyojanaṃ hoti, evaṃ sammannitabbā. Sace hi yena kenaci pariyantena kesaggamattampi tiyojanaṃ atikkāmeti, āpattiñca āpajjati, sīmā ca asīmā hoti.

However, by one establishing a boundary of three yojanas at most, having stood in the middle, it should be established in such a way that it is one and a half yojanas in each of the four directions. If, however, having stood in the middle, they make it three yojanas from each direction, it becomes six yojanas; therefore, it is not permissible. By one establishing a square or a triangular boundary, it should be established in such a way that from corner to corner it is three yojanas. Indeed, if by any edge whatsoever one causes it to exceed three yojanas even by a hair's breadth, one both incurs an offense and the boundary becomes a non-boundary.

164. “Na, bhikkhave, nadīpārasīmā sammannitabbā, yo sammanneyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 140) vacanato nadīpārasīmā na sammannitabbā. Yatra pana dhuvanāvā vā dhuvasetu vā abhimukhatittheyeva atthi, evarūpaṃ nadīpārasīmaṃ sammannituṃ vaṭṭati. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yatthassa dhuvanāvā vā dhuvasetu vā, evarūpaṃ nadīpārasīmaṃ sammannitu”nti hi vuttaṃ. Sace dhuvanāvā vā dhuvasetu vā abhimukhatitthe natthi, īsakaṃ uddhaṃ abhiruhitvā adho vā orohitvā atthi, evampi vaṭṭati. Karavikatissatthero pana “gāvutamattabbhantarepi vaṭṭatī”ti āha.

164. “O monks, a river-spanning boundary should not be established. Whoever should establish one, there is an offense of wrong-doing.” According to this saying, a river-spanning boundary should not be established. But where there is a permanent boat or a permanent bridge right at the facing landing-place, it is proper to establish such a river-spanning boundary. For it was said: “I allow, O monks, to establish such a river-spanning boundary where there might be a permanent boat or a permanent bridge.” If there is no permanent boat or permanent bridge at the facing landing-place, but there is one a little upstream, having gone up, or downstream, having gone down, even so it is proper. The Elder Karavikatissa, however, said: “It is proper even within the measure of a gāvuta.”

Imañca pana nadīpārasīmaṃ sammannantena ekasmiñca tīre ṭhatvā uparisote nadītīre nimittaṃ kittetvā tato paṭṭhāya attānaṃ parikkhipantena yattakaṃ paricchedaṃ icchati, tassa pariyosāne [V 0.0182] adhosotepi nadītīre nimittaṃ kittetvā paratīre sammukhaṭṭhāne nadītīre nimittaṃ kittetabbaṃ. Tato paṭṭhāya yattakaṃ paricchedaṃ icchati, tassa vasena yāva uparisote paṭhamaṃ kittitanimittassa sammukhā nadītīre nimittaṃ, tāva kittetvā paccāharitvā paṭhamakittitanimittena saddhiṃ ghaṭetabbaṃ. Atha sabbanimittānaṃ anto ṭhite bhikkhū hatthapāsagate katvā kammavācāya [M 0.0192] sīmā sammannitabbā. Nadiyā ṭhitā anāgatāpi kammaṃ na kopenti, sammutipariyosāne ṭhapetvā nadiṃ nimittānaṃ anto paratīre ca orimatīre ca ekasīmā hoti, nadī pana baddhasīmāsaṅkhyaṃ na gacchati. Visuṃ nadīsīmā eva hi sā.

However, when establishing this river-spanning boundary, one should stand on one bank and announce a sign on the river bank upstream. Starting from there and enclosing the area on one's own side for the desired extent, at the end of that extent, one should also announce a sign on the river bank downstream. Then, a sign should be announced on the river bank on the opposite bank, in a place directly opposite. Starting from there, according to the desired extent, one should announce signs up to the point on the river bank directly opposite the first announced sign upstream. Then, having brought it back, it should be connected with the first announced sign. Then, having brought all monks standing inside the signs within hand-reach, the boundary should be established by means of the Kammavācā. Monks standing in the river, even if they do not come, do not invalidate the act. At the conclusion of the establishment, excluding the river, the area within the signs on both the far bank and the near bank becomes a single boundary. The river, however, is not included in the reckoning of a bound sīmā, for it is indeed a separate river-sīmā.

Sace antonadiyaṃ dīpako hoti, taṃ antosīmāya kātukāmena purimanayeneva attanā ṭhitatīre nimittāni kittetvā dīpakassa orimante ca pārimante ca nimittaṃ kittetabbaṃ. Atha paratīre nadiyā orimatīre nimittassa sammukhaṭṭhāne nimittaṃ kittetvā tato paṭṭhāya purimanayeneva yāva uparisote paṭhamaṃ kittitanimittassa sammukhā nimittaṃ, tāva kittetabbaṃ. Atha dīpakassa pārimante ca orimante ca nimittaṃ kittetvā paccāharitvā paṭhamaṃ kittitanimittena saddhiṃ ghaṭetabbaṃ. Atha dvīsu tīresu dīpakesu ca bhikkhū sabbe hatthapāsagate katvā kammavācāya sīmā sammannitabbā, nadiyaṃ ṭhitā anāgacchantāpi kammaṃ na kopenti, sammutipariyosāne ṭhapetvā nadiṃ nimittānaṃ anto tīradvayañca dīpako ca ekasīmā hoti, nadī pana nadīsīmāyeva.

If there is a small island in the middle of the river, one who wishes to include it within the sīmā should, following the previous method, announce signs on the bank where one stands; a sign should also be announced on the near edge and the far edge of the island. Then, on the far bank of the river, a sign should be announced in a place opposite the sign on the near bank. Starting from there and following the previous method, signs should be announced upstream as far as the point opposite the first announced sign. Then, having announced signs on the far edge and the near edge of the island, one should bring it back and connect it with the first announced sign. Then, having brought all the bhikkhus on both banks and on the island within hand-reach, the sīmā should be consecrated by means of the Kammavācā. Bhikkhus standing in the river, even if not coming, do not invalidate the act. At the conclusion of the consecration, excluding the river, the area within the signs, comprising the two banks and the island, becomes a single sīmā. The river, however, is a river-sīmā.

Sace pana dīpako vihārasīmāparicchedato uddhaṃ vā adho vā adhikataro hoti, atha vihārasīmāparicchedanimittassa ujukameva sammukhībhūte dīpakassa orimante nimittaṃ kittetvā tato paṭṭhāya dīpakasikharaṃ parikkhipantena puna dīpakassa orimante nimittasammukhe pārimante nimittaṃ kittetabbaṃ. Tato paraṃ purimanayeneva paratīre sammukhanimittamādiṃ katvā paratīre nimittāni ca dīpakassa pārimantaorimante nimittāni ca kittetvā paṭhamakittitanimittena saddhiṃ ghaṭanā kātabbā. Evaṃ kittetvā sammatā sīmā pabbatasaṇṭhānā hoti. Sace pana dīpako vihārasīmāparicchedato uddhampi adhopi adhikataro hoti, purimanayeneva dīpakassa ubhopi sikharāni parikkhipitvā nimittāni kittentena nimittaghaṭanā kātabbā. Evaṃ kittetvā sammatā sīmā mudiṅgasaṇṭhānā hoti. Sace dīpako vihārasīmāparicchedassa anto khuddako hoti, sabbapaṭhamena nayena dīpake nimittāni kittetabbāni. Evaṃ kittetvā sammatā sīmā paṇavasaṇṭhānā hoti. Evaṃ tāva sīmābandhanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

If, however, the island extends beyond the monastery boundary demarcation, either upstream or downstream, then, having announced a sign on the near side of the island directly opposite the sign of the monastery boundary demarcation, and starting from there, one should encircle the island's tip. Then, on the far side, a sign should be announced opposite the sign on the near side of the island. After that, following the previous method, making the opposite sign on the far bank the starting point, and having announced the signs on the far bank as well as the signs on the far and near sides of the island, a connection should be made with the first announced sign. A sīmā thus announced and consecrated has the shape of a mountain. If, however, the island extends beyond the monastery boundary demarcation both upstream and downstream, then, following the previous method, having encircled both extremities of the island and announced the signs, the connection of the signs should be made. A sīmā thus announced and consecrated has the shape of a mudiṅga drum. If the island is small and within the monastery boundary demarcation, the signs should be announced on the island by the very first method. A sīmā thus announced and consecrated has the shape of a paṇava drum. Thus should the binding of a sīmā be understood.

165. Evaṃ [V 0.0183] baddhā pana sīmā kadā asīmā hotīti? Yadā saṅgho sīmaṃ samūhanati, tadā asīmā hoti. Kathaṃ panesā samūhanitabbāti? “Sīmaṃ[M 0.0193], bhikkhave, sammannantena paṭhamaṃ samānasaṃvāsasīmā sammannitabbā, pacchā ticīvarena avippavāso sammannitabbo. Sīmaṃ, bhikkhave, samūhanantena paṭhamaṃ ticīvarena avippavāso samūhantabbo, pacchā samānasaṃvāsasīmā samūhantabbā”ti vacanato paṭhamaṃ avippavāso samūhanitabbo, pacchā sīmā samūhanitabbāti. Kathaṃ? Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

165. But when does a sīmā thus bound become a non-sīmā? When the Saṅgha removes the sīmā, then it becomes a non-sīmā. How then should this sīmā be removed? 'Bhikkhus, by one consecrating a sīmā, the sīmā for common residence should first be consecrated; afterwards, the non-separation from the three robes should be consecrated. Bhikkhus, by one removing a sīmā, the non-separation from the three robes should first be removed; afterwards, the sīmā for common residence should be removed.' According to this, first the non-separation should be removed, then the sīmā should be removed. How? A competent and able bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yo so saṅghena ticīvarena avippavāso sammato, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho taṃ ticīvarena avippavāsaṃ samūhaneyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. That non-separation from the three robes which was consecrated by the Saṅgha—if the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should remove that non-separation from the three robes. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yo so saṅghena ticīvarena avippavāso sammato, saṅgho taṃ ticīrena avippavāsaṃ samūhanati. Yassāyasmato khamati etassa ticīvarena avippavāsassa samugghāto, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. That non-separation from the three robes which was consecrated by the Saṅgha—the Saṅgha removes that non-separation from the three robes. If any venerable one approves of the removal of this non-separation from the three robes, he should remain silent. If any does not approve, he should speak.

“Samūhato so saṅghena ticīvarena avippavāso, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti (mahāva. 145) –

This non-separation from the three robes has been removed by the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I take it.

Evaṃ tāva avippavāso samūhanitabbo.

Thus, first, the non-separation should be removed.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yā sā saṅghena sīmā sammatā samānasaṃvāsā ekūposathā, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho taṃ sīmaṃ samūhaneyya samānasaṃvāsaṃ ekūposathaṃ, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. That sīmā which was consecrated by the Saṅgha for common residence and a single Uposatha—if the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should remove that sīmā for common residence and a single Uposatha. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yā sā saṅghena sīmā sammatā samānasaṃvāsā ekūposathā, saṅgho taṃ sīmaṃ samūhanati samānasaṃvāsaṃ ekūposathaṃ. Yassāyasmato khamati etissā sīmāya samānasaṃvāsāya ekūposathāya samugghāto, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. That sīmā which was consecrated by the Saṅgha for common residence and a single Uposatha—the Saṅgha removes that sīmā for common residence and a single Uposatha. If any venerable one approves of the removal of this sīmā for common residence and a single Uposatha, he should remain silent. If any does not approve, he should speak.

“Samūhatā [M 0.0194] sā sīmā saṅghena samānasaṃvāsā ekūposathā, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti (mahāva. 146) –

This sīmā for common residence and a single Uposatha has been removed by the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I take it.

Evaṃ [V 0.0184] sīmā samūhanitabbā.

Thus the sīmā should be removed.

Samūhanantena pana bhikkhunā vattaṃ jānitabbaṃ. Tatridaṃ vattaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 144) – khaṇḍasīmāya ṭhatvā avippavāsasīmā na samūhantabbā, tathā avippavāsasīmāya ṭhatvā khaṇḍasīmāpi. Khaṇḍasīmāya pana ṭhitena khaṇḍasīmāva samūhanitabbā, tathā itarāya ṭhitena itarā. Sīmaṃ nāma dvīhi kāraṇehi samūhananti pakatiyā khuddakaṃ puna āvāsavaḍḍhanatthāya mahatiṃ vā kātuṃ, pakatiyā mahatiṃ puna aññesaṃ vihārokāsadānatthāya khuddakaṃ vā kātuṃ. Tattha sace khaṇḍasīmañca avippavāsasīmañca jānanti, samūhanituñceva bandhituñca sakkhissanti. Khaṇḍasīmaṃ pana jānantā avippavāsaṃ ajānantāpi samūhanituñceva bandhituñca sakkhissanti. Khaṇḍasīmaṃ ajānantā avippavāsaṃyeva jānantā cetiyaṅgaṇabodhiyaṅgaṇaupaosathāgārādīsu nirāsaṅkaṭṭhānesu ṭhatvā appeva nāma samūhanituṃ sakkhissanti, paṭibandhituṃ pana na sakkhissanteva. Sace bandheyyuṃ, sīmāsambhedaṃ katvā vihāraṃ avihāraṃ kareyyuṃ, tasmā na samūhanitabbā. Ye pana ubhopi na jānanti, te neva samūhanituṃ, na bandhituṃ sakkhissanti. Ayañhi sīmā nāma kammavācāya vā asīmā hoti sāsanantaradhānena vā, na ca sakkā sīmaṃ ajānantehi kammavācā kātuṃ, tasmā na samūhanitabbā, sādhukaṃ pana ñatvāyeva samūhanitabbā ceva bandhitabbā cāti. Ayaṃ tāva baddhasīmāya vinicchayo.

However, a bhikkhu who wishes to abolish a boundary should know the procedure. Herein, this is the procedure: one should not abolish the boundary of non-separation while standing within a limited boundary, nor abolish a limited boundary while standing within the boundary of non-separation. When standing within a limited boundary, only the limited boundary should be abolished. Similarly, when standing within the other, only that other should be abolished. A boundary is abolished for two reasons: either to make a naturally small one larger for the purpose of expanding the residence, or to make a naturally large one smaller to provide space for a monastery for other bhikkhus. In this regard, if they know both the limited boundary and the boundary of non-separation, they will be able to both abolish and establish it. However, those knowing the limited boundary, even if not knowing the boundary of non-separation, will be able to both abolish and establish it. Those not knowing the limited boundary but knowing only the boundary of non-separation, standing in places free of doubt—such as shrine courtyards, Bodhi-tree courtyards, or Uposatha halls—might indeed be able to abolish it, but they will certainly not be able to re-establish it. If they were to establish it, they would cause a confusion of boundaries, making the monastery a non-monastery. Therefore, it should not be abolished. Those who know neither boundary will be able neither to abolish nor to establish it. For this boundary becomes a non-boundary either through the formal act of the Saṅgha or through the disappearance of the Dispensation, and it is not possible for those who do not know the boundary to perform the formal act of the Saṅgha; therefore, it should not be abolished. Only after having understood it well should it be both abolished and established. This, for now, is the analysis regarding an established boundary.

166. Abaddhasīmā pana gāmasīmā sattabbhantarasīmā udakukkhepasīmāti tividhā. Tattha yāvatā ekaṃ gāmakhettaṃ, ayaṃ gāmasīmā nāma, gāmaggahaṇena cettha (mahāva. aṭṭha. 147) nagarampi nigamampi gahitameva hoti. Tattha yattake padese tassa tassa gāmassa gāmabhojakā baliṃ labhanti, so padeso appo vā hotu mahanto vā, gāmasīmātveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Nagaranigamasīmāsupi eseva nayo. Yampi ekasmiṃyeva gāmakhette ekaṃ padesaṃ “ayaṃ visuṃgāmo hotū”ti paricchinditvā rājā kassaci deti, sopi visuṃgāmasīmā hotiyeva, tasmā sā ca itarā ca pakatigāmanagaranigamasīmā [M 0.0195] baddhasīmāsadisāyeva honti, kevalaṃ pana ticīvaravippavāsaparihāraṃ na labhanti.

166. An unestablished boundary, however, is of three kinds: a village boundary, a seven-abbhantara boundary, and a water-splash boundary. Among these, whatever is the extent of a single village-field, this is called a village boundary. And in this context, by the term 'village', a city and a market-town are indeed included. Therein, whatever region the village headmen of that particular village receive tax, that region, whether it be small or large, is reckoned as a village boundary. This same method applies to the boundaries of cities and market-towns. And also, if a king, having demarcated a certain portion within a single village-field, saying, 'Let this be a separate village,' gives it to someone, that portion also indeed becomes a separate village boundary. Therefore, both that boundary and the other ordinary village, city, and market-town boundaries are indeed similar to an established boundary; however, they do not afford the protection against the offense of dwelling apart from the three robes.

Agāmake pana araññe samantā sattabbhantarā sattabbhantarasīmā nāma. Tattha agāmakaṃ nāma araññaṃ viñjhāṭavīādīsu vā samuddamajjhe vā macchabandhānaṃ agamanapathe dīpakesu labbhati. Samantā sattabbhantarāti majjhe ṭhitānaṃ sabbadisāsu sattabbhantarā vinibbedhena cuddasa honti. Tattha ekaṃ abbhantaraṃ aṭṭhavīsatihatthappamāṇaṃ hoti. Ayañca sīmā parisavasena vaḍḍhati[V 0.0185], tasmā samantā parisapariyantato paṭṭhāya abbhantaraparicchedo kātabbo. Sace pana dve saṅghā visuṃ uposathaṃ karonti, dvinnaṃ sattabbhantarānaṃ antare aññamekaṃ abbhantaraṃ upacāratthāya ṭhapetabbaṃ.

However, in a forest without a village, the seven abbhantaras all around are called the seven-abbhantara boundary. Therein, a forest called 'without a village' is found in places like the Vindhya forest-tract, or in the middle of the ocean, or on small islands in the middle of the ocean that are on a path from which fishermen cannot return in a single day. 'Seven abbhantaras all around' means that from the place of the bhikkhus standing in the middle, there are seven abbhantaras in all directions; by diameter, there are fourteen. Therein, one abbhantara has the measure of twenty-eight cubits. And since this boundary increases according to the assembly, the demarcation of the abbhantaras should be made starting from the periphery of the assembly all around. If, however, two Saṅghas perform the Uposatha separately, another single abbhantara should be established between the two seven-abbhantara boundaries for the purpose of an approach-area.

167. Yā panesā “sabbā, bhikkhave, nadī asīmā, sabbo samuddo asīmo, sabbo jātassaro asīmo”ti (mahāva. 147) evaṃ nadīādīnaṃ baddhasīmabhāvaṃ paṭikkhipitvā puna “nadiyā vā, bhikkhave, samudde vā jātassare vā yaṃ majjhimassa purisassa samantā udakukkhepā, ayaṃ tattha samānasaṃvāsā ekūposathā”ti (mahāva. 147) vuttā, ayaṃ udakukkhepasīmā nāma. Tattha nadī nadīnimitte vuttalakkhaṇāva, samuddopi pākaṭoyeva. Yo pana yena kenaci khaṇitvā akato sayaṃjāto sobbho samantato āgatena udakena pūrito tiṭṭhati, yattha nadiyaṃ vuttappakāre vassakāle udakaṃ santiṭṭhati, ayaṃ jātassaro nāma. Yopi nadiṃ vā samuddaṃ vā bhinditvā nikkhantaudakena khato sobbho etaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ pāpuṇāti, ayampi jātassaroyeva. Etesu nadīādīsu yaṃ ṭhānaṃ thāmamajjhimassa purisassa samantato udakukkhepena paricchinnaṃ, ayaṃ udakukkhepasīmā nāma.

167. Furthermore, as for that boundary which was spoken of after first rejecting the state of rivers and so on being an established boundary by stating, 'Bhikkhus, every river is a non-boundary, every ocean is a non-boundary, every natural lake is a non-boundary,' and then stating again, 'Bhikkhus, in a river, or in an ocean, or in a natural lake, whatever place is demarcated all around by a splash of water by a man of medium strength, this is for common communion and for a single Uposatha there'—this is called the water-splash boundary. Therein, a river has the characteristic already stated in the section on the river-boundary marker; the ocean also is the well-known one. But whatever pit, not dug by anyone whatsoever but self-arisen, stands filled with water that has come from all around, wherein water remains during the rainy season in the manner stated for a river—this is called a natural lake. And also whatever pit, formed by water that has come out after breaking through a river or an ocean, attains this characteristic, this too is indeed a natural lake. Among these—rivers and so on—whatever place is demarcated all around by a splash of water by a man of medium strength, this is called the water-splash boundary.

Kathaṃ pana udakukkhepo kātabboti? Yathā akkhadhuttā dāruguḷaṃ khipanti, evaṃ udakaṃ vā vālukaṃ vā hatthena gahetvā thāmamajjhimena purisena sabbathāmena khipitabbaṃ. Yattha evaṃ khittaṃ udakaṃ vā vālukā vā patati, ayameko udakukkhepo, tassa antohatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā ṭhito kammaṃ kopeti. Yāva parisā vaḍḍhati, tāva sīmāpi vaḍḍhati, parisapariyantato udakukkhepoyeva pamāṇaṃ, ayaṃ pana etesaṃ nadīādīnaṃ [M 0.0196] antoyeva labbhati, na bahi. Tasmā nadiyā vā jātassare vā yattakaṃ padesaṃ pakativassakāle catūsu māsesu udakaṃ ottharati, samudde yasmiṃ padese pakativīciyo osaritvā saṇṭhahanti, tato paṭṭhāya kappiyabhūmi, tattha ṭhatvā uposathādikammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, dubbuṭṭhikāle vā gimhe vā nadījātassaresu sukkhesupi sā eva kappiyabhūmi. Sace pana sukkhe jātassare vāpiṃ vā khaṇanti, vappaṃ vā karonti, taṃ ṭhānaṃ gāmakhettaṃ hoti. Yā panesā “kappiyabhūmī”ti vuttā, tato bahi udakukkhepasīmā na gacchati, anto gacchati, tasmā tesaṃ anto parisapariyantato paṭṭhāya samantā udakukkhepaparicchedo kātabbo, ayamettha saṅkhepo.

How then should the water-casting be done? Just as gamblers with dice throw a wooden die, so should water or sand be taken in the hand and thrown with all his strength by a man of moderate strength. Wherever the water or sand thus thrown falls, that is one water-casting. A bhikkhu standing within that water-casting, but beyond the hand's reach of the assembly, invalidates the act. As far as the assembly extends, so far does the boundary also extend; from the limit of the assembly, the water-casting is the measure. However, this boundary is established only within these rivers and the like, not outside. Therefore, in a river or a natural lake, whatever area the water covers during the four months of the normal rainy season, and in the ocean, in whatever area the normal waves recede and settle—starting from that point is allowable ground. There, it is allowable to perform the Uposatha and other acts. Even in a time of drought or in the summer, when rivers and natural lakes are dry, that very same area is allowable ground. But if, in a dry natural lake, they dig a pond or do cultivation, that place becomes village-land. And as for that land which is called 'allowable ground,' the water-casting boundary does not extend outside of it; it extends only within. Therefore, within them, starting from the limit of the assembly, the demarcation by water-casting should be done all around. This is the summary here.

Ayaṃ pana vitthāro – sace nadī nātidīghā hoti, pabhavato paṭṭhāya yāva mukhadvārā sabbattha saṅgho nisīdati, udakukkhepasīmāya kammaṃ natthi, sakalāpi nadī etesaṃyeva bhikkhūnaṃ pahoti[V 0.0186]. Yaṃ pana mahāsumattherena vuttaṃ “yojanaṃ pavattamānāyeva nadī, tatrāpi upari aḍḍhayojanaṃ pahāya heṭṭhā aḍḍhayojane kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti, taṃ mahāpadumatthereneva paṭikkhittaṃ. Bhagavatā hi “timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādetvā yattha katthaci uttarantiyā bhikkhuniyā antaravāsako temiyatī”ti (pāci. 692) idaṃ nadiyā pamāṇaṃ vuttaṃ, na yojanaṃ vā aḍḍhayojanaṃ vā, tasmā yā imassa suttassa vasena pubbe vuttalakkhaṇā nadī, tassā pabhavato paṭṭhāya saṅghakammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace panettha bahū bhikkhū visuṃ visuṃ kammaṃ karonti, sabbehi attano ca aññesañca udakukkhepaparicchedassa antarā añño udakukkhepo sīmantarikatthāya ṭhapetabbo, tato adhikaṃ vaṭṭatiyeva, ūnaṃ pana na vaṭṭatīti vuttaṃ. Jātassarasamuddepi eseva nayo.

Now, this is the detailed explanation: If the river is not excessively long, the Saṅgha can sit along its entire length from its source to its mouth, and there is no act concerning a water-casting boundary. The entire river suffices for these very bhikkhus. However, that which was stated by the great elder Mahāsuma—'Even for a river that flows for just a yojana, it is permissible to perform the act in the half yojana downstream, having abandoned the half yojana upstream'—was refuted by the great elder Mahāpaduma himself. For by the Blessed One this measure of a river was stated: 'Wherever a bhikkhunī crosses, having covered the three circles, her inner robe gets wet,' and a yojana or half a yojana was not stated. Therefore, for whatever river has the characteristics previously stated according to this sutta, it is permissible to perform a Saṅgha act starting from its source. If, however, many bhikkhus perform separate acts therein, another water-casting must be established by all for the purpose of a boundary-interval, between their own water-casting boundary and that of others. More than that is indeed permissible, but less is not permissible, it is said. This very same method applies also to natural lakes and the ocean.

Nadiyā pana “kammaṃ karissāmā”ti gatehi sace nadī paripuṇṇā hoti samatittikā, udakasāṭikaṃ nivāsetvā antonadiyaṃyeva kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Sace na sakkonti, nāvāyapi ṭhatvā kātabbaṃ. Gacchantiyā pana nāvāya kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Kasmā? Udakukkhepamattameva hi sīmā. Taṃ nāvā sīghameva atikkamati, evaṃ sati aññissā sīmāya ñatti, aññissā anusāvanā hoti, tasmā nāvaṃ arittena vā ṭhapetvā pāsāṇe [M 0.0197] vā lambetvā antonadiyaṃ jātarukkhe vā bandhitvā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Antonadiyaṃ baddhaaṭṭakepi antonadiyaṃ jātarukkhepi ṭhitehi kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace pana rukkhassa sākhā vā tato nikkhantapāroho vā bahinadītīre vihārasīmāya vā gāmasīmāya vā patiṭṭhito, sīmaṃ vā sodhetvā sākhaṃ vā chinditvā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Bahinadītīre jātarukkhassa antonadiyaṃ paviṭṭhasākhāya vā pārohe vā nāvaṃ bandhitvā kammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, karontehi sīmā vā sodhetabbā, chinditvā vāssa bahipatiṭṭhitabhāvo nāsetabbo. Nadītīre pana khāṇukaṃ koṭṭetvā tattha baddhanāvāya na vaṭṭatiyeva. Nadiyaṃ setuṃ karonti, sace antonadiyaṃyeva setu ca setupādā ca honti, setumhi ṭhitehi kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace pana setu vā setupādā vā bahitīre patiṭṭhitā, kammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, sīmaṃ sodhetvā kātabbaṃ. Atha setupādā anto, setu pana ubhinnampi tīrānaṃ upariākāse ṭhito, vaṭṭati.

When going to perform a formal act in a river, if the river is full and level with the bank, one should put on a bathing cloth and perform the act within the river itself. If they are unable to do so, they may perform it while standing on a boat. However, it is not allowable to perform the act while the boat is moving. Why? Because the boundary is only the extent of the water-casting. The boat quickly passes beyond that, and this being so, the motion would be in one boundary and the announcements in another. Therefore, the act should be performed by holding the boat steady with an oar, or by securing it to a rock, or by tying it to a tree growing naturally within the river. It is allowable for those standing on a platform built within the river or on a tree growing naturally within the river to perform the act. But if a branch of a tree or a shoot extending from it is established on the outer riverbank, within a monastery boundary or a village boundary, then the boundary must be cleared or the branch cut before the act is performed. It is not allowable to perform the act having tied a boat to a branch or a shoot that has entered into the river from a tree growing naturally on the outer riverbank. Those performing the act must either clear the boundary or, by cutting it, destroy its state of being established outside. However, if a stake is driven into the riverbank and a boat is tied there, it is certainly not allowable. If they make a bridge in the river, and if both the bridge and its supports are entirely within the river, it is allowable for those standing on the bridge to perform the act. But if the bridge or its supports are established on the outer bank, it is not allowable to perform the act; it must be performed after clearing the boundary. But if the bridge supports are within the river, and the bridge itself is established in the space above both banks, it is allowable.

Antonadiyaṃ pāsāṇo vā dīpako vā hoti, tattha yattakaṃ padesaṃ pubbe vuttappakāre pakativassakāle vassānassa catūsu māsesu udakaṃ ottharati, so nadīsaṅkhyameva gacchati. Ativuṭṭhikāle oghena otthatokāso na gahetabbo. So hi gāmasīmāsaṅkhyameva gacchati. Nadito mātikaṃ nīharantā nadiyaṃ āvaraṇaṃ karonti, taṃ ce ottharitvā vā vinibbijjhitvā vā udakaṃ gacchati, sabbattha pavattanaṭṭhāne kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace pana āvaraṇena vā koṭṭakabandhanena [V 0.0187] vā sotaṃ pacchindati, udakaṃ nappavattati, appavattanaṭṭhāne kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, āvaraṇamattakepi kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Sace koci āvaraṇappadeso pubbe vuttapāsāṇadīpakappadeso viya udakena ajjhottharīyati, tattha vaṭṭati. So hi nadīsaṅkhyameva gacchati. Nadiṃ vināsetvā taḷākaṃ karonti, heṭṭhā pāḷibaddhā udakaṃ āgantvā taḷākaṃ pūretvā tiṭṭhati, ettha kammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, upari pavattanaṭṭhāne heṭṭhā ca chaḍḍitodakaṃ nadiṃ otaritvā sandanaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya vaṭṭati. Deve avassante hemantagimhesu vā sukkhanadiyāpi vaṭṭati, nadito nīhaṭamātikāya na vaṭṭati. Sace sā kālantarena bhijjitvā nadī hoti, vaṭṭati. Kāci nadī uppatitvā gāmanigamasīmaṃ ottharitvā pavattati, nadīyeva hoti, kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace pana vihārasīmaṃ ottharati, vihārasīmātveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

If there is a rock or an island within the river, the extent of land there that water covers during the four months of the rainy season in a normal rainy season, as previously stated, is reckoned as a river. In times of excessive rain, the area covered by a flood should not be taken, for that is reckoned as a village boundary. If those drawing off a channel from the river make a barrier in the river, and if the water flows by either overflowing or breaking through it, it is permissible to perform the act in any place where the water flows. But if the current is cut off by a barrier or a dam, and the water does not flow, it is not permissible to perform the act in a place where there is no flow; it is not permissible to perform it even on the barrier itself. If any part of the barrier is submerged by water like the previously mentioned rock or island, it is permissible there, for that is reckoned as a river. If they destroy a river and make a pond, and water, having been dammed below, comes, fills the pond, and remains there, it is not permissible to perform the act there. It is permissible in the place where it flows from above, and also below, from the point where the discharged water descends into the river and flows onward. Even when it does not rain, in winter or summer, it is permissible in a dry river, but it is not permissible in a channel drawn off from the river. If that channel in time breaks and becomes a river, it is permissible. If some river overflows, spreads across a village or town boundary, and flows, it is still a river, and it is permissible to perform the act. But if it overflows into a monastery boundary, it is reckoned as a monastery boundary.

Samuddepi [M 0.0198] kammaṃ karontehi yaṃ padesaṃ uddhaṃ vaḍḍhanaudakaṃ vā pakativīci vā vegena āgantvā ottharati, tattha kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Yasmiṃ pana padese pakativīciyo osaritvā saṇṭhahanti, so udakantato paṭṭhāya anto samuddo nāma, tattha ṭhitehi kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Sace ūmivego bādhati, nāvāya vā aṭṭake vā ṭhatvā kātabbaṃ. Tesu vinicchayo nadiyaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Samudde piṭṭhipāsāṇo hoti, taṃ kadāci ūmiyo āgantvā ottharanti, kadāci na ottharanti, tattha kammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. So hi gāmasīmāsaṅkhyameva gacchati. Sace pana vīcīsu āgatāsupi anāgatāsupi pakatiudakeneva ottharīyati, vaṭṭati. Dīpako vā pabbato vā hoti, so ce dūre hoti macchabandhānaṃ agamanapathe, araññasīmāsaṅkhyameva gacchati. Tesaṃ gamanapariyantassa orato pana gāmasīmāsaṅkhyaṃ gacchati, tattha gāmasīmaṃ asodhetvā kammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Samuddo gāmasīmaṃ vā nigamasīmaṃ vā ottharitvā tiṭṭhati, samuddova hoti, tattha kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace pana vihārasīmaṃ ottharati, vihārasīmātveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

Also in the sea, it is not permissible for monks performing an act to do so in a place that rising water or natural waves, coming with force, would cover. But in a place where the natural waves, having receded, settle, that place, beginning from the water's edge, is called 'within the sea'. There, an act should be performed by those standing. If the force of the waves is oppressive, it should be done while standing on a boat or on a platform. The ruling concerning these should be understood according to the method stated for a river. In the sea, there may be a flat rock. Sometimes waves, having come, cover it; sometimes they do not cover it. It is not permissible to perform an act there, for it is reckoned only as a village boundary. But if, whether waves have come or have not come, it is covered by the normal water level alone, it is permissible. There may be an islet or a mountain. If it is far, on a path from which fishermen cannot return in a day, it is reckoned only as a wilderness boundary. But within the limit of their journey from which they can return in a day, it is reckoned as a village boundary. There, it is not permissible to perform an act without having purified the village boundary. If the sea, having covered a village boundary or a town boundary, remains, it is just the sea. There, it is permissible to perform an act. But if it covers a monastery boundary, it is reckoned only as a monastery boundary.

Jātassare kammaṃ karontehi yattha pubbe vuttappakāre vassakāle vasse pacchinnamatte pivituṃ vā hatthapāde vā dhovituṃ udakaṃ na hoti, sukkhati, ayaṃ na jātassaro, gāmakhettasaṅkhyameva gacchati, tattha kammaṃ na kātabbaṃ. Yattha pana vuttappakāre vassakāle udakaṃ santiṭṭhati, ayameva jātassaro. Tassa yattake padese vassānaṃ cātumāse udakaṃ tiṭṭhati, tattha kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace gambhīraṃ udakaṃ, aṭṭakaṃ bandhitvā tattha ṭhitehipi jātassarassa antojātarukkhamhi baddhaaṭṭakepi kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Piṭṭhipāsāṇadīpakesu panettha nadiyaṃ vuttasadisova vinicchayo. Samavassadevakāle pahonakajātassaro pana cepi dubbuṭṭhikakāle vā [V 0.0188] gimhahemantesu vā sukkhati, nirudako hoti, tattha saṅghakammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Yaṃ andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ “sabbo jātassaro sukkho anodako gāmakhettaṃyeva bhajatī”ti, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Sace panettha udakatthāya āvāṭaṃ vā pokkharaṇīādīni vā khaṇanti, taṃ ṭhānaṃ ajātassaro hoti, gāmasīmāsaṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Lābutipusakādivappe katepi eseva nayo. Sace pana naṃ pūretvā thalaṃ vā karonti, ekasmiṃ [M 0.0199] disābhāge pāḷiṃ bandhitvā sabbameva naṃ mahātaḷākaṃ vā karonti, sabbopi ajātassaro hoti, gāmasīmāsaṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Loṇīpi jātassarasaṅkhyameva gacchati. Vassike cattāro māse udakaṭṭhānokāse kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti. Ayaṃ abaddhasīmāya vinicchayo.

For monks performing an act in a natural lake: if, in a certain natural lake, as previously described, just as the rain of the rainy season has ceased, there is no water to drink or to wash hands and feet, and it dries up, this is not a natural lake; it is reckoned only as a village-field. An act should not be performed there. But where, as described, water remains during the rainy season, this indeed is a natural lake. In whatever area of it water stands during the four months of the rains, it is permissible to perform an act there. If the water is deep, it is permissible to perform the act even for those standing on a platform that has been built, or on a platform built on a tree that has grown within the natural lake. Regarding flat rocks and islets therein, the determination is the same as that stated for a river. Furthermore, if a natural lake that is suitable during a time of regular rainfall dries up and becomes waterless during a time of drought or during the summer and winter seasons, it is permissible to perform a Saṅgha act there. The statement made in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā, 'Every natural lake that is dry and without water is reckoned only as a village-field,' should not be accepted. If, however, they dig a pit or ponds and so forth therein for the sake of water, that place becomes a non-natural lake; it is reckoned as a village boundary. This is the same principle even when the sowing of gourds, cucumbers, and so forth is done. But if they fill it and make it dry land, or if, having built a dike on one side, they make the whole of it into a great reservoir, the entire lake becomes a non-natural lake; it is reckoned as a village boundary. A salt marsh is also reckoned as a natural lake. During the four rainy months, it is permissible to perform an act in the place where water stands. This is the determination regarding an unconsecrated sīmā.

Iti pāḷimuttakavinayavinicchayasaṅgahe

Thus, in the Compendium of Vinaya Determinations Not Found in the Pāḷi Canon,

Sīmāvinicchayakathā samattā.

The Discourse on the Determination of Sīmā is concluded.

25. Uposathapavāraṇāvinicchayakathā

25. The Discourse on the Determination of Uposatha and Pavāraṇā

168. Uposathapavāraṇāti [V 0.0189] ettha (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) divasavasena tayo uposathā cātuddasiko pannarasiko sāmaggīuposathoti. Tattha hemantagimhavassānānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ utūnaṃ tatiyasattamapakkhesu dve dve katvā cha cātuddasikā, sesā pannarasikāti evaṃ ekasaṃvacchare catuvīsati uposathā. Idaṃ tāva pakaticārittaṃ. Tathārūpapaccaye sati aññasmimpi cātuddase uposathaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Purimavassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ pana pubbakattikapuṇṇamā, tesaṃyeva sace bhaṇḍanakārakehi upaddutā pavāraṇaṃ paccukkaḍḍhanti, atha kattikamāsassa kāḷapakkhacātuddaso vā pacchimakattikapuṇṇamā vā pacchimavassaṃvuṭṭhānañca pacchimakattikapuṇṇamā eva vāti ime tayo pavāraṇādivasāpi honti. Idampi pakaticārittameva. Tathārūpapaccaye sati dvinnaṃ kattikapuṇṇamānaṃ purimesu cātuddasesupi pavāraṇaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Yadā pana kosambakakkhandhake (mahāva. 451 ādayo) āgatanayena bhinne bhikkhusaṅghe osārite tasmiṃ bhikkhusmiṃ saṅgho tassa vatthussa vūpasamāya saṅghasāmaggiṃ karoti, tadā tāvadeva uposatho kātabbo. “Pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabba”nti vacanato ṭhapetvā cātuddasapannarase aññopi yo koci divaso uposathadivaso nāma hoti, vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ pana kattikamāsabbhantare ayameva sāmaggīpavāraṇādivaso nāma hoti. Iti imesu tīsu divasesu uposatho kātabbo. Karontena pana sace cātuddasiko hoti, “ajjuposatho cātuddaso”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace sāmaggīuposatho hoti, “ajjuposatho [M 0.0200] sāmaggī”ti vattabbaṃ. Pannarasiyaṃ pana pāḷiyaṃ āgatanayeneva “ajjuposatho pannaraso”ti vattabbaṃ.

168. Regarding Uposatha and Pavāraṇā: Here, by way of days, three Uposathas are spoken of: the fourteenth-day, the fifteenth-day, and the Uposatha of harmony. Among them, in the third and seventh fortnights of the three seasons—winter, summer, and the rains—making two each, six are fourteenth-day Uposathas. The remaining eighteen are fifteenth-day Uposathas. Thus, in one year, there are twenty-four Uposathas. This, for a start, is the regular practice. When a suitable cause arises, it is also proper to perform the Uposatha on another fourteenth day. For those who have completed the earlier rains-residence, however, the earlier Kattika full moon is the Pavāraṇā day. If those very monks, being harassed by quarrelsome monks, should postpone the Pavāraṇā, then either the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kattika or the later Kattika full moon becomes the day. And for those who have completed the later rains-residence, it is the later Kattika full moon itself. Thus, these three are also Pavāraṇā days. This too is the regular practice. When a suitable cause arises, it is also proper to perform the Pavāraṇā on the fourteenth days preceding the two Kattika full moons. However, when, according to the method that comes in the Kosambaka Khandhaka, the community of monks is divided, and when that monk has been reinstated, the Saṅgha performs an act of community harmony for the settling of that issue, then on that very day the Uposatha must be performed. According to the saying, 'The Pātimokkha should be recited,' setting aside the fourteenth and fifteenth days, any other day whatsoever is also called an Uposatha day. For those who have completed the rains-residence, however, within the month of Kattika, this very day is called the day of harmony Pavāraṇā. Thus, on these three kinds of days, the Uposatha should be performed. However, by the one performing it, if it is a fourteenth-day Uposatha, it should be said, 'Today is the fourteenth-day Uposatha.' If it is a harmony Uposatha, it should be said, 'Today is the harmony Uposatha.' On the fifteenth day, however, according to the method that comes in the Pāḷi, it should be said, 'Today is the fifteenth-day Uposatha.'

169. Saṅghe uposatho (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā), gaṇe uposatho, puggale uposathoti evaṃ kārakavasena aparepi tayo uposathā vuttā, kattabbākāravasena pana suttuddeso pārisuddhiuposatho adhiṭṭhānuposathoti aparepi tayo uposathā. Tattha suttuddeso nāma “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho”tiādinā nayena vutto pātimokkhuddeso. Ye panitare dve uposathā, tesu pārisuddhiuposatho tāva aññesañca santike aññamaññañca ārocanavasena duvidho. Tattha yvāyaṃ aññesaṃ santike karīyati, sopi pavāritānañca appavāritānañca santike karaṇavasena duvidho. Tattha mahāpavāraṇāya pavāritānaṃ santike pacchimikāya upagatena vā anupagatena vā chinnavassena vā cātumāsiniyaṃ pana pavāritānaṃ santike anupagatena vā chinnavassena [V 0.0190] vā kāyasāmaggiṃ datvā “parisuddho ahaṃ bhante, parisuddhoti maṃ dhārethā”ti tikkhattuṃ vatvā kātabbo. Ṭhapetvā pana pavāraṇādivasaṃ aññasmiṃ kāle āvāsikehi uddiṭṭhamatte pātimokkhe avuṭṭhitāya vā ekaccāya vuṭṭhitāya vā sabbāya vā vuṭṭhitāya parisāya ye aññe samasamā vā thokatarā vā āgacchanti, tehi tesaṃ santike vuttanayeneva pārisuddhi ārocetabbā.

169. The Uposatha of the Saṅgha, the Uposatha of a group, and the Uposatha of an individual—thus, by way of the agent, three other Uposathas are spoken of. But by way of the manner of performance, three other Uposathas are also spoken of: the Suttuddesa Uposatha, the Pārisuddhi Uposatha, and the Adhiṭṭhāna Uposatha. Among these, the Suttuddesa is the recitation of the Pātimokkha spoken of in the manner beginning with, 'May the Saṅgha hear me, venerable sirs.' As for the other two Uposathas, among them the Pārisuddhi Uposatha is, first of all, twofold by way of announcing: in the presence of others, and to one another. Among these, that which is performed in the presence of others is also twofold by way of performance: in the presence of those who have performed Pavāraṇā and those who have not performed Pavāraṇā. Here, in the presence of those who have performed the Great Pavāraṇā, it is to be performed by one who has entered the later rains-residence, or not entered, or has a broken rains-residence; and in the presence of those who have performed the Cātumāsinī Pavāraṇā, by one who has not entered the rains-residence, or has a broken rains-residence, by giving one's physical presence and saying three times, 'I am pure, venerable sirs; regard me as pure.' However, setting aside the Pavāraṇā day, at another time, when the Pātimokkha has just been recited by the resident bhikkhus, if other bhikkhus who are equal in number or fewer arrive—whether the assembly has not yet dispersed, or a part has dispersed, or the entire assembly has dispersed—they should announce their purity in the presence of those residents in the very manner already stated.

Yo panāyaṃ aññamaññaṃ ārocanavasena karīyati, so ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā karaṇavasena ca aṭṭhapetvā karaṇavasena ca duvidho. Tattha yasmiṃ āvāse tayo bhikkhū viharanti, tesu uposathadivase sannipatitesu ekena bhikkhunā “suṇantu me āyasmantā, ajjuposatho cātuddaso”ti vā “pannaraso”ti vā vatvā “yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, mayaṃ aññamaññaṃ pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kareyyāmā”ti ñattiyā ṭhapitāya therena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā “parisuddho ahaṃ, āvuso, parisuddhoti maṃ dhārethā”ti tikkhattuṃ vattabbaṃ. Itarehi “bhante”ti vatvā evameva vattabbaṃ. Evaṃ ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā kātabbo. Yatra pana dve bhikkhū viharanti, tatra ñattiṃ aṭṭhapetvā vuttanayeneva pārisuddhi ārocetabbāti ayaṃ pārisuddhiuposatho.

However, this Purity Uposatha which is performed by way of mutual announcement is twofold: by way of performing it having established a motion, and by way of performing it without having established a motion. Among these, in a residence where three bhikkhus dwell, when they have assembled on the Uposatha day, one bhikkhu should say, 'May the venerable sirs hear me. Today is the Uposatha, the fourteenth,' or 'the fifteenth.' Then, when the motion has been established by saying, 'If it is the proper time for the venerable sirs, we should perform the Purity Uposatha mutually,' the senior bhikkhu, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat on his heels, and having raised his folded hands, should say three times: 'I am pure, friends; may you hold me as pure.' The other bhikkhus, having said, 'Venerable sir,' should say it in just the same way. Thus, it should be done having established a motion. But where two bhikkhus dwell, there, without having established a motion, the purity should be announced in the way just stated. This is the Purity Uposatha.

Sace [M 0.0201] pana ekova bhikkhu hoti, sabbaṃ pubbakaraṇīyaṃ katvā aññesaṃ anāgamanaṃ ñatvā “ajja me uposatho cātuddaso”ti vā “pannaraso”ti vā vatvā “adhiṭṭhāmī”ti vattabbaṃ. Ayaṃ adhiṭṭhānuposathoti evaṃ kattabbākāravasena tayo uposathā veditabbā. Ettāvatā nava uposathā dīpitā honti. Tesu divasavasena pannarasiko, kārakavasena saṅghuposatho, kattabbākāravasena suttuddesoti evaṃ tilakkhaṇasampanne uposathe pavattamāne uposathaṃ akatvā tadahuposathe aññaṃ abhikkhukaṃ nānāsaṃvāsakehi vā sabhikkhukaṃ āvāsaṃ vā anāvāsaṃ vā vāsatthāya aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā gacchantassa dukkaṭaṃ hoti.

But if there is only one bhikkhu, having completed all the preliminary duties and having known the non-arrival of other bhikkhus, he should say, 'Today for me is the Uposatha, the fourteenth,' or 'the fifteenth,' and then he should say, 'I determine.' This is the Determination Uposatha. Thus, the three Uposathas should be known by way of the manner of performance. By this much, nine Uposathas have been shown. Among these are: by way of the day, the fifteenth-day Uposatha; by way of the agent, the Saṅgha Uposatha; and by way of the manner of performance, the Suttuddesa. Thus, when an Uposatha endowed with these three characteristics is proceeding, for one who, without having performed the Uposatha on that Uposatha day, goes for the purpose of dwelling to another residence or non-residence that is without bhikkhus, or to a residence or non-residence that has bhikkhus of a different communion—except with the Saṅgha, except for a danger—there is a dukkaṭa offense.

170. Uposathakaraṇatthaṃ sannipatite saṅghe bahi uposathaṃ katvā āgatena sannipātaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā kāyasāmaggiṃ adentena chando dātabbo. Yopi gilāno vā hoti kiccapasuto vā, tenapi pārisuddhiṃ dentena chandopi dātabbo. Kathaṃ? Ekassa bhikkhuno santike “chandaṃ dammi, chandaṃ me hara, chandaṃ me ārocehī”ti ayamattho kāyena vā vācāya vā ubhayena vā viññāpetabbo, evaṃ dinno hoti chando. Akatuposathena gilānena vā kiccapasutena vā pārisuddhi dātabbā. Kathaṃ? Ekassa bhikkhuno santike “pārisuddhiṃ dammi, pārisuddhiṃ me hara[V 0.0191], pārisuddhiṃ me ārocehī”ti ayamattho kāyena vā vācāya vā ubhayena vā viññāpetabbo, evaṃ dinnā hoti pārisuddhi. Taṃ pana dentena chandopi dātabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe pārisuddhiṃ dentena chandampi dātuṃ, santi saṅghassa karaṇīya”nti (mahāva. 165). Tattha pārisuddhidānaṃ saṅghassapi attanopi uposathakaraṇaṃ sampādeti, na avasesaṃ saṅghakiccaṃ, chandadānaṃ saṅghasseva uposathakaraṇañca sesakiccañca sampādeti, attano panassa uposatho akatoyeva hoti, tasmā pārisuddhiṃ dentena chandopi dātabbo. Pubbe vuttaṃ pana suddhikacchandaṃ vā pārisuddhiṃ vā imaṃ vā chandapārisuddhiṃ ekena bahūnampi āharituṃ vaṭṭati. Sace pana so antarāmagge aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ passitvā yesaṃ tena chando vā pārisuddhi vā gahitā, tesañca attano ca chandapārisuddhiṃ deti, tasseva āgacchati. Itarā [M 0.0202] pana biḷālasaṅkhalikā chandapārisuddhi nāma hoti, sā na āgacchati, tasmā sayameva sannipātaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā ārocetabbaṃ. Sace pana sañcicca nāroceti, dukkaṭaṃ āpajjati, chandapārisuddhi pana tasmiṃ hatthapāsaṃ upagatamatteyeva āgatā hoti.

170. When the Saṅgha has gathered to perform the Uposatha, a bhikkhu who, having performed the Uposatha outside, comes to the assembly place without joining the physical concord, should give his consent. And whatever bhikkhu is sick or occupied with duties, by him also, when giving his declaration of purity, consent should also be given. How? In the presence of one bhikkhu, this meaning should be made known by body, or by speech, or by both: 'I give my consent; convey my consent; announce my consent.' Thus, consent is given. By one who has not performed the Uposatha—whether sick or occupied with duties—a declaration of purity should be given. How? In the presence of one bhikkhu, this meaning should be made known by body, or by speech, or by both: 'I give my declaration of purity; convey my declaration of purity; announce my declaration of purity.' Thus, the declaration of purity is given. However, when giving it, consent should also be given. For this was stated by the Blessed One: 'Bhikkhus, I allow that on the Uposatha day, one giving a declaration of purity may also give consent, if there is business for the Saṅgha to attend to.' In this matter, the giving of a declaration of purity accomplishes the performance of the Uposatha for both the Saṅgha and for oneself, but not the remaining business of the Saṅgha. The giving of consent accomplishes the performance of the Uposatha and the remaining business for the Saṅgha only, but for oneself, the Uposatha remains unperformed. Therefore, when giving a declaration of purity, consent should also be given. But it was previously stated that it is proper for one bhikkhu to convey for many either mere consent, or a declaration of purity, or this consent-and-purity. However, if on the way he sees another bhikkhu and gives to him the consent-and-purity of those from whom he had taken consent or purity, and his own as well, it is conveyed for himself only. But the consent-and-purity of the others is called 'cat's chain' consent-and-purity; it is not conveyed. Therefore, one should go to the assembly place oneself and announce it. If, however, he intentionally does not announce it, he incurs a dukkaṭa offense. But the consent-and-purity is considered conveyed as soon as he comes within arm's reach.

171. Pārivāsiyena pana chandadānena yaṃ kiñci saṅghakammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Tattha (pāci. aṭṭha. 1167) catubbidhaṃ pārivāsiyaṃ parisapārivāsiyaṃ rattipārivāsiyaṃ chandapārivāsiyaṃ ajjhāsayapārivāsiyanti. Tesu parisapārivāsiyaṃ nāma bhikkhū kenacideva karaṇīyena sannipatitā honti, atha megho vā uṭṭheti, ussāraṇā vā karīyati, manussā vā ajjhottharantā āgacchanti, bhikkhū “anokāsā mayaṃ, aññattha gacchāmā”ti chandaṃ avissajjetvāva uṭṭhahanti. Idaṃ parisapārivāsiyaṃ. Kiñcāpi parisapārivāsiyaṃ, chandassa pana avissaṭṭhattā kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati.

171. However, it is not allowable to perform any Saṅgha act with a giving of consent that has become provisional. Therein, there are four types of provisionality: provisionality due to the assembly, provisionality due to the night, provisionality due to consent, and provisionality due to intention. Among these, provisionality due to the assembly refers to when bhikkhus have gathered for some business, but then a storm arises, or a dispersal is announced, or people come crowding in, and the bhikkhus rise to leave without having relinquished their consent, thinking, 'We have no opportunity; let us go elsewhere.' This is provisionality due to the assembly. Although it is provisionality due to the assembly, since consent was not relinquished, it is allowable to perform the act.

Puna bhikkhū “uposathādīni karissāmā”ti rattiṃ sannipatitvā “yāva sabbe sannipatanti, tāva dhammaṃ suṇissāmā”ti ekaṃ ajjhesanti, tasmiṃ dhammakathaṃ kathenteyeva aruṇo uggacchati. Sace “cātuddasikaṃ uposathaṃ karissāmā”ti nisinnā, pannarasoti kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace pannarasikaṃ kātuṃ nisinnā, pāṭipade anuposathe uposathaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, aññaṃ pana saṅghakiccaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Idaṃ rattipārivāsiyaṃ nāma.

Again, bhikkhus, intending to perform the Uposatha, etc., gather at night and, thinking, 'Until everyone gathers, we will listen to the Dhamma,' they ask one bhikkhu. While he is giving a Dhamma talk, dawn breaks. If they sat intending to perform the fourteenth-day Uposatha, it is permissible to perform it as a fifteenth-day Uposatha. If they sat intending to perform the fifteenth-day Uposatha, it is not permissible to perform the Uposatha on the first day of the new half-month, which is not an Uposatha day, but it is permissible to perform other Saṅgha business. This is called provisionality due to the night.

Puna bhikkhū “kiñcideva abbhānādisaṅghakammaṃ karissāmā”ti nisinnā honti, tatreko nakkhattapāṭhako bhikkhu evaṃ vadati “ajja nakkhattaṃ dāruṇaṃ, mā imaṃ karothā”ti. Te tassa [V 0.0192] vacanena chandaṃ vissajjetvā tattheva nisinnā honti. Athañño āgantvā “nakkhattaṃ patimānentaṃ, attho bālaṃ upaccagā”ti (jā. 1.1.49) vatvā “kiṃ nakkhattena, karothā”ti vadati. Idaṃ chandapārivāsiyañceva ajjhāsayapārivāsiyañca. Etasmiṃ pārivāsiye puna chandapārisuddhiṃ anānetvā kammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati.

Again, bhikkhus sit intending to perform some Saṅgha action such as rehabilitation, etc. Then one bhikkhu who knows the constellations says, 'Today the constellation is inauspicious; do not perform this.' They then relinquish their consent based on his words and remain seated. Later, another arrives and says, 'Purpose passes by the fool who waits for the constellations,' and urges, 'What does the constellation matter? Proceed.' This is both provisionality due to consent and provisionality due to intention. In such a provisionality, the act cannot be performed without again obtaining consent-and-purity.

172. Sace koci bhikkhu gilāno na sakkoti chandapārisuddhiṃ dātuṃ, so mañcena vā pīṭhena vā saṅghamajjhaṃ ānetabbo. Sace gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti “sace kho mayaṃ gilānaṃ ṭhānā cāvessāma, ābādho vā abhivaḍḍhissati, kālakiriyā vā bhavissatī”ti, na [M 0.0203] so bhikkhu ṭhānā cāvetabbo, saṅghena tattha gantvā uposatho kātabbo. Sace bahū tādisā gilānā honti, saṅghena paṭipāṭiyā ṭhatvā sabbe hatthapāse kātabbā. Sace dūre honti, saṅgho nappahoti, taṃ divasaṃ uposatho na kātabbo. Na tveva vaggena saṅghena uposatho kātabbo, kareyya ce, dukkaṭaṃ.

172. If some bhikkhu is ill and unable to give his consent-and-purity, he should be brought into the midst of the Saṅgha on a bed or a seat. If the bhikkhus attending the sick one think, 'If we move the sick one from his place, his illness will worsen, or he will die,' then that bhikkhu should not be moved from his place. The Saṅgha should go there and perform the Uposatha. If there are many such sick bhikkhus, the Saṅgha should stand in order and bring all of them within hand's reach. If they are far away and the Saṅgha is not sufficient, the Uposatha should not be performed on that day. The Uposatha should certainly not be performed by a divided Saṅgha; if it were performed, it would be an offense of wrong-doing.

Sace (mahāva. aṭṭha. 149) ekasmiṃ vihāre catūsu bhikkhūsu vasantesu ekassa chandapārisuddhiṃ āharitvā tayo pārisuddhiuposathaṃ karonti, tīsu vā vasantesu ekassa chandapārisuddhiṃ āharitvā dve pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti, adhammena vaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ hoti. Sace pana cattāropi sannipatitvā pārisuddhiuposathaṃ karonti, tayo vā dve vā pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti, adhammena samaggaṃ nāma hoti. Sace catūsu janesu ekassa pārisuddhiṃ āharitvā tayo pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti, tīsu vā janesu ekassa pārisuddhiṃ āharitvā dve pārisuddhiuposathaṃ karonti, dhammena vaggaṃ nāma hoti. Sace pana cattāro ekattha vasantā sabbe sannipatitvā pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti, tayo pārisuddhiuposathaṃ karonti, dve aññamaññaṃ pārisuddhiuposathaṃ karonti, dhammena samaggaṃ nāma hoti.

If, in one monastery where four bhikkhus reside, the consent and purity of one is brought and the other three perform the Uposatha of purity, or if, where three reside, the consent and purity of one is brought and the other two recite the Pātimokkha, the Uposatha act is unlawfully divided. If, however, all four gather and perform the Uposatha of purity, or if three or two recite the Pātimokkha, it is called unlawfully harmonious. If, among four persons, the declaration of purity of one is brought and the other three recite the Pātimokkha, or if, among three persons, the declaration of purity of one is brought and the other two perform the Uposatha of purity, it is called lawfully divided. If, however, four residing in one place all gather and recite the Pātimokkha; or three perform the Uposatha of purity; or two mutually perform the Uposatha of purity, it is called lawfully harmonious.

173. Pavāraṇākammesu (mahāva. aṭṭha. 212) pana sace ekasmiṃ vihāre pañcasu bhikkhūsu vasantesu ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā cattāro gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, catūsu vā tīsu vā vasantesu ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā tayo vā dve vā saṅghañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, sabbametaṃ adhammena vaggaṃ pavāraṇākammaṃ. Sace pana sabbepi pañca janā ekato sannipatitvā gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, cattāro vā tayo vā dve vā vasantā ekato sannipatitvā saṅghañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, sabbametaṃ adhammena samaggaṃ pavāraṇākammaṃ. Sace pañcasu janesu ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā cattāro saṅghañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, catūsu vā tīsu [V 0.0193] vā ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā tayo vā dve vā gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, sabbametaṃ dhammena vaggaṃ pavāraṇākammaṃ. Sace pana sabbepi pañca janā ekato sannipatitvā saṅghañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, cattāro vā tayo vā ekato sannipatitvā gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, dve aññamaññaṃ [M 0.0204] pavārenti, ekako vasanto adhiṭṭhānapavāraṇaṃ karoti, sabbametaṃ dhammena samaggaṃ nāma pavāraṇākammanti.

173. Regarding Pavāraṇā proceedings, if among five bhikkhus residing in one monastery, having brought the pavāraṇā of one, four bhikkhus perform pavāraṇā having established a group motion; or if among four or three residing, having brought the pavāraṇā of one, three or two perform pavāraṇā having established a Sangha motion, all this is an unlawful, divided Pavāraṇā proceeding.
