However, if all five persons assemble together and perform pavāraṇā having established a group motion; or if four, three, or two residing bhikkhus assemble together and perform pavāraṇā having established a Sangha motion, all this is an unlawful, harmonious Pavāraṇā proceeding. If among five persons, having brought the pavāraṇā of one, four perform pavāraṇā having established a Sangha motion; or if among four or three, having brought the pavāraṇā of one, three or two perform pavāraṇā having established a group motion, all this is a lawful, divided Pavāraṇā proceeding. However, if all five persons assemble together and perform pavāraṇā having established a Sangha motion; or if four or three assemble together and perform pavāraṇā having established a group motion; or if two perform pavāraṇā mutually; or if a bhikkhu residing alone performs the determination-pavāraṇā, all this is called a lawful, harmonious Pavāraṇā proceeding.

Ettha sace cātuddasikā hoti, “ajja me pavāraṇā cātuddasī”ti, sace pannarasikā, “ajja me pavāraṇā pannarasī”ti evaṃ adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Pavāraṇaṃ dentena pana “pavāraṇaṃ dammi, pavāraṇaṃ me hara, mamatthāya pavārehī”ti kāyena vā vācāya vā kāyavācāhi vā ayamattho viññāpetabbo. Evaṃ dinnāya (mahāva. aṭṭha. 213) pavāraṇāya pavāraṇāhārakena saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ pavāretabbaṃ “tisso, bhante, bhikkhu saṅghaṃ pavāreti diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā, vadatu taṃ, bhante, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāya, passanto paṭikarissati. Dutiyampi, bhante…pe… tatiyampi, bhante, tisso bhikkhu saṅghaṃ pavāreti…pe… paṭikarissatī”ti. Sace pana vuḍḍhataro hoti, “āyasmā, bhante, tisso”ti vattabbaṃ. Evañhi tena tassatthāya pavāritaṃ hoti. Pavāraṇaṃ dentena pana chandopi dātabbo, chandadānaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Idhāpi chandadānaṃ avasesakammatthāya. Tasmā sace pavāraṇaṃ dento chandaṃ deti, vuttanayena āhaṭāya pavāraṇāya tena ca bhikkhunā saṅghena ca pavāritameva hoti. Atha pavāraṇameva deti, na chandaṃ, tassa ca pavāraṇāya ārocitāya saṅghena ca pavārite sabbesaṃ suppavāritaṃ hoti, aññaṃ pana kammaṃ kuppati. Sace chandameva deti, na pavāraṇaṃ, saṅghassa pavāraṇā ca sesakammāni ca na kuppanti, tena pana bhikkhunā appavāritaṃ hoti, pavāraṇādivase pana bahisīmāya pavāraṇaṃ adhiṭṭhahitvā āgatenapi chando dātabbo tena saṅghassa pavāraṇākammaṃ na kuppati.

Here, if it is the fourteenth day, one should resolve, 'Today is my Pavāraṇā, the fourteenth.' If it is the fifteenth, one should resolve thus, 'Today is my Pavāraṇā, the fifteenth.' However, one giving the Pavāraṇā should convey this meaning by body, or by speech, or by both body and speech, saying, 'I give Pavāraṇā, take my Pavāraṇā, perform Pavāraṇā on my behalf.' When the Pavāraṇā has been given in this way, the one who brings the Pavāraṇā should approach the Sangha and perform the Pavāraṇā thus: 'Venerable Sirs, the monk Tissa invites the Sangha by what is seen, or by what is heard, or by what is suspected. Let the Sangha, venerable sirs, speak to him out of compassion. Seeing it, he will make amends. For the second time, venerable sirs… For the third time, venerable sirs, the monk Tissa invites the Sangha… he will make amends.' However, if he is senior, it should be said, 'Venerable Sirs, the venerable Tissa.' For thus has the Pavāraṇā been performed by him on his behalf. However, one giving the Pavāraṇā should also give consent; the giving of consent is to be understood in the manner stated before. Here too, the giving of consent is for the purpose of the remaining formal acts. Therefore, if one giving Pavāraṇā also gives consent, when the Pavāraṇā is brought in the stated manner, Pavāraṇā is indeed performed by that monk and by the Sangha. But if one gives only Pavāraṇā and not consent, when his Pavāraṇā has been announced and the Sangha has performed Pavāraṇā, it is a well-performed Pavāraṇā for all, but another formal act is invalidated. If one gives only consent and not Pavāraṇā, the Sangha’s Pavāraṇā and remaining formal acts are not invalidated, but that monk has not performed Pavāraṇā. However, on the day of Pavāraṇā, even by one who has resolved on Pavāraṇā outside the boundary and returned, consent should be given; by that, the Sangha’s Pavāraṇā formal act is not invalidated.

Sace purimikāya pañca bhikkhū vassaṃ upagatā, pacchimikāyapi pañca, purimehi ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārite pacchimehi tesaṃ santike pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo, na ekasmiṃ uposathagge dve ñattiyo ṭhapetabbā. Sacepi pacchimikāya upagatā cattāro tayo dve eko vā hoti, eseva nayo. Atha purimikāya cattāro, pacchimikāyapi cattāro tayo dve eko vā, eseva nayo. Athāpi purimikāya tayo, pacchimikāyapi tayo dve eko vā, eseva nayo. Idañhettha lakkhaṇaṃ.

If five bhikkhus have entered upon the rains-residence of the first period, and five have also entered upon it in the later period, then when those of the first period have performed the Pavāraṇā after establishing the motion, those of the later period should perform the Pārisuddhi-uposatha in their presence; two motions should not be established in one Uposatha hall. Even if in the later period there are four, three, two, or one who have entered upon the rains-residence, this is the same method. Now, if there are four in the first period, and in the later period also there are four, three, two, or one, this is the same method. Furthermore, if there are three in the first period, and in the later period also there are three, two, or one, this is the same method. This is the guiding principle here.

Sace [M 0.0205][V 0.0194] purimikāya upagatehi pacchimikāya upagatā thokatarā ceva honti samasamā ca, saṅghapavāraṇāya ca gaṇaṃ pūrenti, saṅghapavāraṇāvasena ñatti ṭhapetabbā. Sace pana pacchimikāya eko hoti, tena saddhiṃ te cattāro honti, catunnaṃ saṅghañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavāretuṃ na vaṭṭati. Gaṇañattiyā pana so gaṇapūrako hoti, tasmā gaṇavasena ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā purimehi pavāretabbaṃ, itarena tesaṃ santike pārisuddhiuposatho kātabboti. Purimikāya dve, pacchimikāya dve vā eko vā eseva nayo. Purimikāya eko pacchimikāya ekoti ekena ekassa santike pavāretabbaṃ, ekena pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo. Sace purimehi vassūpagatehi pacchā vassūpagatā ekenapi adhikatarā honti, paṭhamaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitvā pacchā thokatarehi tesaṃ santike pavāretabbaṃ.

If those who entered upon the rains-residence in the later period are fewer than or equal in number to those of the first period, and they complete the quorum for the Saṅgha-pavāraṇā, the motion should be established by way of Saṅgha-pavāraṇā. But if there are three in the first period and one in the later period, they are four together with him; it is not allowable for the four to perform Pavāraṇā after establishing a Saṅgha-motion. For a group-motion, however, that one is a quorum-filler; therefore, after establishing the motion by way of a group, those of the first period should perform the Pavāraṇā, and the other one should perform the Pārisuddhi-uposatha in their presence. This is the same method if there are two in the first period, and in the later period two or one. If there is one in the first period and one in the later period, one should perform Pavāraṇā in the presence of the other, and the other should perform the Pārisuddhi-uposatha. If those who entered upon the later rains-residence are more numerous, even by one, than those who entered upon the first, first the Pātimokkha should be recited, and afterwards the fewer ones should perform the Pavāraṇā in their presence.

Kattikāya cātumāsinipavāraṇāya pana sace paṭhamavassūpagatehi mahāpavāraṇāya pavāritehi pacchā upagatā adhikatarā vā samasamā vā honti, pavāraṇāñattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavāretabbaṃ. Tehi pavārite pacchā itarehi pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo. Atha mahāpavāraṇāyaṃ pavāritā bahū honti, pacchā vassūpagatā thokā vā eko vā, pātimokkhe uddiṭṭhe pacchā tesaṃ santike tena pavāretabbaṃ. Kiṃ panetaṃ pātimokkhaṃ sakalameva uddisitabbaṃ, udāhu ekadesampīti? Ekadesampi uddisituṃ vaṭṭati. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā –

But regarding the four-month Pavāraṇā in Kattika, if those who undertook the later rains-residence are more numerous than, or equal in number to, those who undertook the first rains-residence and have performed the Great Pavāraṇā, then having established the motion for Pavāraṇā, the Pavāraṇā should be performed. After they have performed the Pavāraṇā, the others should perform the Pārisuddhi-uposatha. But if those who have performed the Great Pavāraṇā are many, and those who undertook the later rains-residence are few or just one, then after the Pātimokkha has been recited, the Pavāraṇā should be performed by him in their presence. Should this Pātimokkha be recited in its entirety, or even a part? It is permissible to recite even a part. For this has been said by the Blessed One:

“Pañcime, bhikkhave, pātimokkhuddesā, nidānaṃ uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ, ayaṃ paṭhamo pātimokkhuddeso. Nidānaṃ uddisitvā cattāri pārājikāni uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ, ayaṃ dutiyo pātimokkhuddeso. Nidānaṃ uddisitvā cattāri pārājikāni uddisitvā terasa saṅghādisese uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ, ayaṃ tatiyo pātimokkhuddeso. Nidānaṃ uddisitvā cattāri pārājikāni uddisitvā terasa saṅghādisese uddisitvā dve aniyate uddisitvā avasesaṃ bhutena sāvetabbaṃ, ayaṃ catuttho pātimokkhuddeso. Vitthāreneva pañcamo”ti (māhāva. 150).

“Monks, these are five recitations of the Pātimokkha. Having recited the preamble, the remainder should be announced by the word ‘heard’; this is the first recitation of the Pātimokkha. Having recited the preamble and the four Pārājikas, the remainder should be announced by the word ‘heard’; this is the second recitation of the Pātimokkha. Having recited the preamble, the four Pārājikas, and the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, the remainder should be announced by the word ‘heard’; this is the third recitation of the Pātimokkha. Having recited the preamble, the four Pārājikas, the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, and the two Aniyatas, the remainder should be announced by the word ‘heard’; this is the fourth recitation of the Pātimokkha. The fifth is the recitation in full.”

Tattha (mahāva. aṭṭha. 150) [M 0.0206] nidānaṃ uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbanti “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho…pe… āvikatā hissa phāsu hotī”ti imaṃ nidānaṃ uddisitvā “uddiṭṭhaṃ kho āyasmanto nidānaṃ, tatthāyasmante pucchāmi kaccittha parisuddhā. Dutiyampi pucchāmi…pe… evametaṃ dhārayāmi. Sutā kho panāyasmantehi cattāro pārājikā dhammā [V 0.0195] …pe… avivadamānehi sikkhitabba”nti evaṃ avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ. Etena nayena sesāpi cattāro pātimokkhuddesā veditabbā.

Therein, regarding the phrase “having recited the preamble, the remainder should be announced by the word ‘heard’”: having recited this preamble, “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me… for one who has made it manifest, it is comfortable,” the remainder should be announced by the word ‘heard’ in this way: “Venerable sirs, the preamble has been recited. Therein I ask the venerable ones: Are you pure in this matter? A second time I ask… Thus do I bear this in mind. The four Pārājika rules have been heard by you, venerable sirs… one should train without disputing.” By this method, the other four recitations of the Pātimokkha should also be understood.

174. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sati antarāye saṃkhittena pātimokkhaṃ uddisituṃ. Na, bhikkhave, asati antarāye saṃkhittena pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ, yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 150) vacanato pana vinā antarāyā saṃkhittena pātimokkhaṃ na uddisitabbaṃ. Tatrime antarāyā – rājantarāyo corantarāyo agyantarāyo udakantarāyo manussantarāyo amanussantarāyo vāḷantarāyo sarīsapantarāyo jīvitantarāyo brahmacariyantarāyoti.

174. “I allow, O monks, the Pātimokkha to be recited in brief when there is an obstruction. O monks, the Pātimokkha should not be recited in brief when there is no obstruction; whoever should recite it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.” Therefore, according to this statement, the Pātimokkha should not be recited in brief without an obstruction. Therein, these are the obstructions: a royal obstruction, a thief obstruction, a fire obstruction, a water obstruction, a human obstruction, a non-human obstruction, an obstruction from beasts of prey, an obstruction from creeping creatures, an obstruction to life, and an obstruction to the holy life.

Tattha sace bhikkhūsu uposathaṃ karissāmāti nisinnesu rājā āgacchati, ayaṃ rājantarāyo. Corā āgacchanti, ayaṃ corantarāyo. Davaḍāho āgacchati, āvāse vā aggi uṭṭhāti, ayaṃ agyantarāyo. Megho vā uṭṭheti, ogho vā āgacchati, ayaṃ udakantarāyo. Bahū manussā āgacchanti, ayaṃ manussantarāyo. Bhikkhuṃ yakkho gaṇhāti, ayaṃ amanussantarāyo. Byagghādayo caṇḍamigā āgacchanti, ayaṃ vāḷantarāyo. Bhikkhuṃ sappādayo ḍaṃsanti, ayaṃ sarīsapantarāyo. Bhikkhu gilāno vā hoti, kālaṃ vā karoti, verino vā taṃ māretukāmā gaṇhanti, ayaṃ jīvitantarāyo. Manussā ekaṃ vā bahū vā bhikkhū brahmacariyā cāvetukāmā gaṇhanti, ayaṃ brahmacariyantarāyo. Evarūpesu antarāyesu saṃkhittena pātimokkho uddisitabbo, paṭhamo vā uddeso uddisitabbo. Ādimhi dve tayo cattāro vā. Ettha dutiyādīsu uddesesu yasmiṃ apariyosite antarāyo hoti, sopi suteneva sāvetabbo. Nidānuddese pana aniṭṭhite sutena sāvetabbaṃ nāma natthi.

Therein, if while the monks are seated intending to perform the Uposatha, a king arrives—this is a royal obstruction. Thieves arrive—this is a thief obstruction. A forest fire arrives, or a fire breaks out in the dwelling—this is a fire obstruction. A storm cloud arises, or a flood comes—this is a water obstruction. Many humans arrive—this is a human obstruction. A yakkha seizes a monk—this is a non-human obstruction. Fierce beasts of prey, such as tigers, arrive—this is an obstruction from beasts of prey. Creeping creatures, such as snakes, bite a monk—this is an obstruction from creeping creatures. A monk is ill, or he dies, or enemies, wishing to kill him, seize him—this is an obstruction to life. Humans, wishing to make one or many monks fall away from the holy life, seize them—this is an obstruction to the holy life. In such obstructions, the Pātimokkha should be recited in brief, or the first section should be recited. Or at the beginning, two, three, or four sections should be recited. Herein, among the sections from the second onwards, if an obstruction arises before a section is completed, that section also should be announced with the word ‘heard’. However, if the Introductory Section is unfinished, there is no such thing as announcing with the word ‘heard’.

Pavāraṇākammepi [M 0.0207] sati antarāye dvevācikaṃ ekavācikaṃ samānavassikaṃ vā pavāretuṃ vaṭṭati. Ettha (mahāva. aṭṭha. 234) ñattiṃ ṭhapentenapi “yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho dvevācikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti vattabbaṃ. Ekavācike “ekavācikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti, samānavassikepi “samānavassikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti vattabbaṃ. Ettha ca bahūpi samānavassā ekato pavāretuṃ labhanti. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ajja pavāraṇā pannarasī, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho pavāreyyā”ti imāya pana sabbasaṅgāhikāya ñattiyā ṭhapitāya tevācikaṃ dvevācikaṃ ekavācikañca pavāretuṃ vaṭṭati, samānavassikaṃ na vaṭṭati. “Tevācikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti vutte pana tevācikameva vaṭṭati, aññaṃ na vaṭṭati. “Dvevācikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti vutte dvevācikaṃ tevācikañca [V 0.0196] vaṭṭati, ekavācikañca samānavassikañca na vaṭṭati. “Ekavācikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti vutte pana ekavācikadvevācikatevācikāni vaṭṭanti, samānavassikameva na vaṭṭati. “Samānavassika”nti vutte sabbaṃ vaṭṭati.

If there is an obstacle even during the Pavāraṇā ceremony, it is permissible to perform the Pavāraṇā with two recitations, with one recitation, or for those of the same rains-residence. Here, when presenting the motion, it should be said: 'If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā with two recitations.' In the case of one recitation, it should be said: '...should perform the Pavāraṇā with one recitation,' and in the case of the Pavāraṇā for those of the same rains-residence: '...should perform the Pavāraṇā for those of the same rains-residence.' And here, even many bhikkhus of the same rains-residence may perform the Pavāraṇā together. However, when this all-inclusive motion is presented—'Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. Today is the fifteenth, the Pavāraṇā day. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā'—it is permissible to perform the Pavāraṇā with three recitations, two recitations, and one recitation; the Pavāraṇā for those of the same rains-residence is not permissible. However, when it is said, '...should perform the Pavāraṇā with three recitations,' only the Pavāraṇā with three recitations is permissible; another is not permissible. When it is said, '...should perform the Pavāraṇā with two recitations,' the Pavāraṇā with two recitations and with three recitations are permissible; the Pavāraṇā with one recitation and for those of the same rains-residence are not permissible. However, when it is said, '...should perform the Pavāraṇā with one recitation,' the Pavāraṇā with one, two, and three recitations are permissible; only the Pavāraṇā for those of the same rains-residence is not permissible. When 'samānavassika' is said, all are permissible.

175. Kena pana pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbanti? “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, therādhikaṃ pātimokkha”nti (mahāva. 154) vacanato therena vā pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ, “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yo tattha bhikkhu byatto paṭibalo, tassādheyyaṃ pātimokkha”nti (mahāva. 155) vacanato navakatarena vā. Ettha (mahāva. aṭṭha. 155) ca kiñcāpi navakatarassapi byattassa pātimokkhaṃ anuññātaṃ, atha kho ettha ayaṃ adhippāyo – sace therassa pañca vā cattāro vā tayo vā pātimokkhuddesā nāgacchanti, dve pana akhaṇḍā suvisadā vācuggatā honti, therāyattaṃva pātimokkhaṃ. Sace pana ettakampi visadaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti, byattassa bhikkhuno āyatthaṃ hoti, tasmā sayaṃ vā uddisitabbaṃ, añño vā ajjhesitabbo. “Na, bhikkhave, saṅghamajjhe anajjhiṭṭhena pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ, yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 154) vacanato anajjhiṭṭhena pātimokkhaṃ na uddisitabbaṃ. Na kevalaṃ pātimokkhaṃyeva, dhammopi na bhāsitabbo “na, bhikkhave, saṅghamajjhe anajjhiṭṭhena dhammo bhāsitabbo, yo bhāseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 150) vacanato.

175. But by whom, indeed, should the Pātimokkha be recited? According to the statement, “I allow, O bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha that is under the authority of the senior bhikkhu” (Mahāvagga 154), the Pātimokkha should be recited by a senior bhikkhu; or, according to the statement, “I allow, O bhikkhus, for whichever bhikkhu there is who is skilled and capable, the Pātimokkha that is under his authority” (Mahāvagga 155), it should be recited by a junior bhikkhu. And here (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 155), although the Pātimokkha is permitted even for a skilled junior bhikkhu, yet this is the intention here: if the senior bhikkhu does not know five, or four, or three recitations of the Pātimokkha, but two recitations are unbroken, very clear, and committed to memory, the Pātimokkha is indeed dependent on the senior bhikkhu. But if he is not able to make even this much clear, it becomes dependent on a skilled bhikkhu. Therefore, either he himself should recite it, or another should be requested. According to the statement, “O bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should not be recited in the midst of the Saṅgha by one who has not been requested. Whoever should recite it, incurs an offense of wrong-doing” (Mahāvagga 154), the Pātimokkha should not be recited by one who has not been requested. Not only the Pātimokkha, but the Dhamma also should not be spoken, according to the statement: “O bhikkhus, the Dhamma should not be spoken in the midst of the Saṅgha by one who has not been requested. Whoever should speak it, incurs an offense of wrong-doing” (Mahāvagga 150).

Ajjhesanā [M 0.0208] cettha saṅghena sammatadhammajjhesakāyattā vā saṅghatthe rāyattā vā, tasmā dhammajjhesake asati saṅghattheraṃ āpucchitvā vā tena yācito vā bhāsituṃ labhati. Saṅghattherenapi sace vihāre bahū dhammakathikā honti, vārapaṭipāṭiyā vattabbo. “Tvaṃ dhammaṃ bhaṇa, dhammadānaṃ dehī”ti vā vuttena tīhipi vidhīhi dhammo bhāsitabbo, “osārehī”ti vutto pana osāretumeva labhati, “kathehī”ti vutto kathetumeva, “sarabhaññaṃ bhaṇāhī”ti vutto sarabhaññameva. Saṅghattheropi ca uccatare āsane nisinno yācituṃ na labhati. Sace upajjhāyo ceva saddhivihāriko ca hoti, upajjhāyo ca naṃ uccāsane nisinno “bhaṇā”ti vadati, sajjhāyaṃ adhiṭṭhahitvā bhaṇitabbaṃ. Sace panettha daharabhikkhū honti, “tesaṃ bhaṇāmī”ti bhaṇitabbaṃ. Sace vihāre saṅghatthero attanoyeva nissitake bhaṇāpeti, aññe madhurabhāṇakepi nājjhesati, so aññehi vattabbo – “bhante, asukaṃ nāma bhaṇāpemā”ti. Sace “bhaṇāpethā”ti vadati, tuṇhī vā hoti, bhaṇāpetuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace pana paṭibāhati, na bhaṇāpetabbaṃ. Yadi pana anāgateyeva saṅghatthere dhammassavanaṃ āraddhaṃ, puna āgate ṭhapetvā āpucchanakiccaṃ [V 0.0197] natthi. Osāretvā pana kathentena āpucchitvā aṭṭhapetvāyeva vā kathetabbaṃ. Kathentassa puna āgatepi eseva nayo.

Here, the request is dependent on the bhikkhu appointed by the Saṅgha to make the request for a Dhamma talk, or it is dependent on the Saṅghathera. Therefore, in the absence of the one who requests the Dhamma talk, one may speak after having asked permission of the Saṅghathera, or having been requested by him. The Saṅghathera, too, if there are many Dhamma-speakers in the monastery, should have them speak in sequential turns. One who has been told, 'You speak the Dhamma,' or 'Give the gift of the Dhamma,' should speak the Dhamma according to the three methods. However, one who is told, 'Recite the Pāli text,' may only recite the Pāli text; one who is told, 'Explain the meaning,' may only explain the meaning; one who is told, 'Recite the Sarabhañña,' may only recite the Sarabhañña. And the Saṅghathera, while sitting on a higher seat, is not permitted to make a request. If there is both a preceptor and his co-resident, and the preceptor, while sitting on a high seat, says to him, 'Speak,' it should be recited after having undertaken it as a recitation. If there are junior bhikkhus in this assembly, it should be spoken with the thought, 'I will speak for them.' If the Saṅghathera in the monastery has only his own dependents speak and does not request other eloquent speakers, he should be addressed by others: 'Venerable sir, let us have so-and-so speak.' If he says, 'You may have him speak,' or if he remains silent, it is proper to have him speak. But if he refuses, one should not have him speak. However, if the hearing of the Dhamma has already begun before the Saṅghathera arrives, then when he arrives, there is no need to pause and ask for permission. However, when one who has recited the Pāli text then explains the meaning, it should be explained either after asking permission or without pausing. This same principle applies even if he arrives while one is explaining the meaning.

Upanisinnakathāyampi saṅghattherova sāmī, tasmā tena sayaṃ vā kathetabbaṃ, añño vā bhikkhu “kathehī”ti vattabbo, no ca kho uccatare āsanne nisinnena, manussānaṃ pana “bhaṇāhī”ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Manussā attano jānanakaṃ bhikkhuṃ pucchanti, tena theraṃ āpucchitvāpi kathetabbaṃ. Sace saṅghatthero “bhante, ime pañhaṃ pucchantī”ti puṭṭho “kathehī”ti vā bhaṇati, tuṇhī vā hoti, kathetuṃ vaṭṭati. Antaraghare anumodanādīsupi eseva nayo. Sace saṅghatthero “vihāre vā antaraghare vā maṃ anāpucchitvāpi katheyyāsī”ti anujānāti, laddhakappiyaṃ hoti, sabbattha vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Sajjhāyaṃ karontenāpi thero āpucchitabboyeva. Ekaṃ āpucchitvā sajjhāyantassa aparo āgacchati, puna āpucchanakiccaṃ natthi. Sacepi “vissamissāmī”ti ṭhapitassa āgacchati, puna ārabhantena āpucchitabbaṃ. Saṅghatthere anāgateyeva āraddhaṃ sajjhāyantassāpi [M 0.0209] eseva nayo. Ekena saṅghattherena “maṃ anāpucchāpi yathāsukhaṃ sajjhāyāhī”ti anuññāte yathāsukhaṃ sajjhāyituṃ vaṭṭati, aññasmiṃ pana āgate taṃ āpucchitvāva sajjhāyitabbaṃ.

Even when giving a discourse to those sitting nearby, the elder of the Saṅgha is the sole authority. Therefore, he himself should speak, or another monk should be told, 'Speak!' However, this should not be said by one sitting on a higher seat. To laypeople, however, it is proper to say, 'Speak!' Laypeople ask a monk whom they know. That monk should speak after having consulted the elder. If the elder of the Saṅgha, having been asked, 'Venerable sir, these people are asking a question,' either says, 'Speak!' or is silent, it is proper to speak. The same rule applies to giving a blessing and so forth inside a house. If the elder of the Saṅgha gives permission, saying, 'You may speak in the monastery or inside a house even without consulting me,' it becomes allowable, and it is proper to speak in all such cases. Even when making a recitation, the elder must indeed be consulted. If, after consulting one elder, another arrives while one is reciting, there is no need to consult again. But if one has stopped, thinking, 'I will take a break,' and another elder arrives, one must consult when beginning again. This same rule also applies to one who has started reciting before the elder of the Saṅgha has arrived. If one has been given permission by an elder of the Saṅgha, saying, 'You may recite as you please even without consulting me,' it is proper to recite as you please. However, if another elder arrives, one should recite only after consulting him.

Yasmiṃ pana vihāre sabbeva bhikkhū bālā honti abyattā na jānanti pātimokkhaṃ uddisituṃ, tattha kiṃ kātabbanti? Tehi bhikkhūhi eko bhikkhu sāmantā āvāsā sajjukaṃ pāhetabbo “gacchāvuso, saṃkhittena vā vitthārena vā pātimokkhaṃ pariyāpuṇitvā āgacchāhī”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, tehi bhikkhūhi sabbeheva yattha tādisā bhikkhū honti, so āvāso uposathakaraṇatthāya anvaḍḍhamāsaṃ gantabbo, agacchantānaṃ dukkaṭaṃ. Idañca utuvasseyeva, vassāne pana purimikāya pātimokkhuddesakena vinā na vassaṃ upagacchitabbaṃ. Sace so vassūpagatānaṃ pakkamati vā vibbhamati vā kālaṃ vā karoti, aññasmiṃ satiyeva pacchimikāya vasituṃ vaṭṭati, asati aññattha gantabbaṃ, agacchantānaṃ dukkaṭaṃ. Sace pana pacchimikāya pakkamati vā vibbhamati vā kālaṃ vā karoti, māsadvayaṃ vasitabbaṃ.

But in a monastery where all the bhikkhus are ignorant and unskilled, and do not know how to recite the Pātimokkha, what is to be done? Those bhikkhus should promptly send one bhikkhu to a nearby residence with the instruction: “Go, friend, learn the Pātimokkha, whether in brief or in detail, and then return.” If this can be achieved, it is good. If not, all those bhikkhus should go every half-month to a residence where there are such bhikkhus, for the purpose of performing the Uposatha. For those not going, there is a dukkaṭa offense. And this applies only during the non-rainy seasons. But during the rains, one should not enter the rains-residence for the first period without a Pātimokkha-reciter. If, after they have entered the rains-residence, that reciter departs, or disrobes, or dies, it is permissible to reside for the latter period only if another reciter is present. If one is not present, they must go elsewhere; for those not going, there is a dukkaṭa offense. But if he departs, or disrobes, or dies during the latter period, they must reside for two months.

Yattha pana te bālā bhikkhū viharanti abyattā, sace tattha koci bhikkhu āgacchati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito byatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo, tehi bhikkhūhi so bhikkhu saṅgahetabbo anuggahetabbo upalāpetabbo[V 0.0198], upaṭṭhāpetabbo cuṇṇena mattikāya dantakaṭṭhena mukhodakena. No ce saṅgaheyyuṃ anuggaheyyuṃ upalāpeyyuṃ, upaṭṭhāpeyyuṃ cuṇṇena mattikāya dantakaṭṭhena mukhodakena, sabbesaṃ dukkaṭaṃ. Idha neva therā, na daharā muccanti, sabbehi vārena upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Attano vāre anupaṭṭhahantassa āpatti. Tena pana mahātherānaṃ pariveṇasammajjanadantakaṭṭhadānādīni na sāditabbāni, evampi sati mahātherehi sāyaṃpātaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ āgantabbaṃ, tena pana tesaṃ āgamanaṃ ñatvā paṭhamataraṃ mahātherānaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ gantabbaṃ. Sacassa saddhiñcarā bhikkhū upaṭṭhākā atthi, “mayhaṃ upaṭṭhākā atthi, tumhe appossukkā viharathā”ti vattabbaṃ. Athāpissa saddhiñcarā natthi, tasmiṃyeva vihāre eko vā dve vā vattasampannā vadanti “mayaṃ therassa kattabbaṃ karissāma, avasesā phāsu viharantū”ti, sabbesaṃ anāpatti.

Where ignorant and unskilled monks reside, if a monk arrives there who is very learned, versed in the scriptures, a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the Mātikā, wise, skilled, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of the training, those monks should support him, assist him, conciliate him, and attend to him with bath powder, clay, a tooth-stick, and water for the face. If they do not support, assist, conciliate, or attend to him with bath powder, clay, a tooth-stick, and water for the face, it is a dukkaṭa offense for all. Here, neither the elders nor the young are exempt; all must attend to him in turn. For one who does not attend in his own turn, there is an offense. However, that person should not accept from the great elders services such as sweeping the monastic compound, giving a tooth-stick, and so on. Even so, the great elders should come in the evening and morning to attend to him. Knowing of their arrival, he should go first to attend to the great elders. If he has attendant monks accompanying him, he should say, “I have attendants; you may dwell without concern.” Or if he has no accompanying attendants, and in that very monastery one or two monks accomplished in their duties say, “We will do what should be done for the elder; let the others dwell at ease,” there is no offense for anyone.

176. “Yassa [M 0.0210] siyā āpatti, so āvikareyyā”ti(mahāva. 134) ādivacanato na sāpattikena uposatho kātabbo, tasmā tadahuposathe āpattiṃ sarantena desetabbā. Desentena ca ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evaṃ vattabbo “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno, taṃ paṭidesemī”ti. Sace navakataro hoti, “ahaṃ, bhante”ti vattabbaṃ. “Taṃ paṭidesemī”ti idaṃ pana attano attano anurūpavasena “taṃ tuyhamūle, taṃ tumhamūle paṭidesemī”ti vuttepi suvuttameva hoti. Paṭiggāhakenapi attano attano anurūpavasena “passatha, bhante, taṃ āpattiṃ, passasi, āvuso, taṃ āpatti”nti vā vattabbaṃ, puna desakena “āma, āvuso, passāmi, āma, bhante, passāmī”ti vā vattabbaṃ. Puna paṭiggāhakena “āyatiṃ, bhante, saṃvareyyātha, āyatiṃ, āvuso, saṃvareyyāsī”ti vā vattabbaṃ. Evaṃ vutte desakena “sādhu suṭṭhu āvuso saṃvarissāmi, sādhu suṭṭhu, bhante, saṃvarissāmī”ti vā vattabbaṃ. Sace āpattiyā vematiko hoti, ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evaṃ vattabbo “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmāya āpattiyā vematiko, yadā nibbematiko bhavissāmi, tadā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmī”ti vatvā uposatho kātabbo, pātimokkhaṃ sotabbaṃ, na tveva tappaccayā uposathassa antarāyo kātabbo. “Na, bhikkhave, sabhāgā āpatti desetabbā, yo deseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na, bhikkhave, sabhāgā āpatti paṭiggahetabbā, yo paṭiggaṇheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 169) vacanato yaṃ dvepi janā vikālabhojanādinā sabhāgavatthunā āpattiṃ āpajjanti, evarūpā vatthusabhāgā āpatti neva desetabbā, na ca paṭiggahetabbā. Vikālabhojanapaccayā [V 0.0199] āpannaṃ pana āpattisabhāgaṃ anatirittabhojanapaccayā āpannassa santike desetuṃ vaṭṭati.

176. “‘A monk who may have an offense should reveal it’ (Mahāvagga 134)—because of this saying, the Uposatha should not be performed by one who has an offense. Therefore, on that Uposatha day, an offense, upon being remembered, should be confessed. One who is confessing should approach a certain monk, arrange the upper robe over one shoulder, sit down in a squatting position, raise the joined palms, and speak thus: ‘Friend, I have fallen into an offense of such-and-such a name; I confess that offense.’ If he is more junior, it should be said, ‘I, venerable sir.’ This phrase, ‘I confess it,’ is also well-spoken when adapted according to one's own suitability, such as, ‘I confess it in your presence.’ The receiver should also, according to his own suitability, say, ‘Do you see that offense, venerable sir?’ or ‘Do you see that offense, friend?’ Then the confessor should say, ‘Yes, friend, I see,’ or ‘Yes, venerable sir, I see.’ Then the receiver should say, ‘In the future, venerable sir, you should restrain yourself,’ or ‘In the future, friend, you should restrain yourself.’ When this is said, the confessor should say, ‘Good, friend, I will restrain myself well,’ or ‘Good, venerable sir, I will restrain myself well.’ If one is doubtful about an offense, one should approach a certain monk, arrange the upper robe over one shoulder, sit down in a squatting position, raise the joined palms, and speak thus: ‘Friend, I am doubtful about an offense of such-and-such a name. When I become free from doubt, then I will make amends for that offense.’ Having said this, the Uposatha should be performed and the Pātimokkha should be listened to. But on account of that, an obstacle to the Uposatha should certainly not be made. ‘Monks, a common offense should not be confessed. Whoever should confess it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, a common offense should not be received. Whoever should receive it, commits an offense of wrong-doing’ (Mahāvagga 169). Because of this saying, when two persons fall into an offense through a common matter, such as eating at the wrong time, such an offense with a common basis should neither be confessed nor received. However, it is allowable to confess an offense of a similar class that was incurred on account of eating at the wrong time in the presence of one who has incurred an offense on account of eating non-leftover food.

Sace pana sabbo saṅgho vikālabhojanādinā sabhāgavatthunā lahukāpattiṃ āpajjati, tattha kiṃ kātabbanti? Tehi bhikkhūhi eko bhikkhu sāmantā āvāsā sajjukaṃ pāhetabbo “gacchāvuso, taṃ āpattiṃ [M 0.0211] paṭikaritvā āgaccha, mayaṃ te santike āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmā”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo – “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ sabbo saṅgho sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno, yadā aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ suddhaṃ anāpattikaṃ passissati, tadā tassa santike taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissatī”ti (mahāva. 171) vatvā uposatho kātabbo. Sace pana vematiko hoti, “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ sabbo saṅgho sabhāgāya āpattiyā vematiko, yadā nibbematiko bhavissati, tadā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissatī”ti (mahāva. 171) vatvā uposatho kātabbo. Sace panettha koci “taṃ sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ desetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti maññamāno ekassa santike deseti, desitā sudesitāva. Aññaṃ pana desanāpaccayā desako paṭiggahaṇapaccayā paṭiggāhako cāti ubhopi dukkaṭaṃ āpajjanti, taṃ nānāvatthukaṃ hoti, tasmā aññamaññaṃ desetabbaṃ. Ettāvatā te nirāpattikā honti, tesaṃ santike sesehi sabhāgāpattiyo desetabbā vā ārocetabbā vā. Sace te evaṃ akatvā uposathaṃ karonti, “pārisuddhiṃ āyasmanto ārocethā”tiādinā nayena sāpattikassa uposathakaraṇe paññattaṃ dukkaṭaṃ āpajjanti.

But if the entire Saṅgha commits a light offense due to a shared ground, such as eating at the wrong time, what should be done? Those monks should promptly send one monk to a neighboring residence with the message: “Go, friend, expiate that offense and return. We will expiate the offense in your presence.” If this can be arranged, it is good. If not, a competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha: “Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. This entire Saṅgha has committed a shared offense. When it sees another monk who is pure and free from offense, it will then expiate that offense in his presence.” Having said this, the Uposatha should be performed. If there is uncertainty, he should say: “Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. This entire Saṅgha is uncertain about the shared offense. When it becomes free of doubt, it will then expiate that offense.” Having said this, the Uposatha should be performed. If someone here, thinking, “It is proper to confess that shared offense,” confesses it in the presence of one monk, the confession is well-made. However, both the one who confesses, on account of the confession, and the one who accepts, on account of the acceptance, incur another offense of wrong-doing. Since that offense has a different ground, it should be confessed to each other. To this extent, they become free of offense. In their presence, the shared offenses should be confessed or announced by the remaining monks. If they perform the Uposatha without doing this, they incur the offense of wrong-doing prescribed for performing the Uposatha while still having an offense, according to the rule beginning with: “Venerable ones, announce your purity.”

Sace koci bhikkhu pātimokkhe uddissamāne āpattiṃ sarati, tena bhikkhunā sāmanto bhikkhu evaṃ vattabbo “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno, ito vuṭṭhahitvā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmī”ti. Sāmanto ca bhikkhu sabhāgoyeva vattabbo. Visabhāgassa hi vuccamāne bhaṇḍanakalahasaṅghabhedādīnipi honti, tasmā tassa avatvā “ito vuṭṭhahitvā paṭikarissāmī”ti ābhogaṃ katvā uposatho kātabbo. Sace pana koci pātimokkhe uddissamāne āpattiyā vematiko hoti, tenapi sabhāgoyeva sāmanto bhikkhu evaṃ vattabbo “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmāya āpattiyā vematiko, yadā nibbematiko bhavissāmi, tadā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmī”ti. Evañca vatvā uposatho kātabbo, pātimokkhaṃ sotabbaṃ, na tveva tappaccayā uposathassa antarāyo kātabbo.

If any bhikkhu, while the Pātimokkha is being recited, remembers an offense, that bhikkhu should say to a neighboring bhikkhu: “Friend, I have committed such-and-such an offense; after rising from here, I will remedy that offense.” And the neighboring bhikkhu should be of the same category. For if it is said to one of a different category, arguments, quarrels, schisms in the Sangha, and so on, may arise. Therefore, without speaking to him, having made the resolution, “After rising from here, I will remedy it,” the Uposatha should be performed. If, however, any bhikkhu, while the Pātimokkha is being recited, is uncertain about an offense, he should likewise say to a neighboring bhikkhu of the same category: “Friend, I am uncertain about such-and-such an offense; when I am no longer uncertain, then I will remedy that offense.” And having spoken thus, the Uposatha should be performed, and the Pātimokkha should be listened to; on that account, an obstacle to the Uposatha should certainly not be made.

177. “Anujānāmi[M 0.0212][V 0.0200], bhikkhave, uposathāgāraṃ sammajjitu”nti(mahāva. 159) ādivacanato –

177. From the statement beginning, “Monks, I allow the sweeping of the Uposatha hall”—

“Sammajjanī padīpo ca, udakaṃ āsanena ca;

Uposathassa etāni, pubbakaraṇanti vuccatī”ti. (mahāva. aṭṭha. 168) –

“Broom and lamp, and water with a seat—these are called the preliminaries to the Uposatha.”

Evaṃ vuttaṃ catubbidhaṃ pubbakaraṇaṃ katvāva uposatho kātabbo. Kena pana taṃ kātabbanti? “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, therena bhikkhunā navaṃ bhikkhuṃ āṇāpetuṃ, na, bhikkhave, therena āṇattena agilānena na sammajjitabbaṃ, yo na sammajjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”tiādivacanato yo therena āṇatto, tena kātabbaṃ. Āṇāpentena ca kiñci kammaṃ karonto vā sadākālameva eko vā bhāranittharaṇako vā sarabhāṇakadhammakathikādīsu aññataro vā na uposathāgārasammajjanatthaṃ āṇāpetabbo, avasesā pana vārena āṇāpetabbā. Sace āṇatto sammuñjaniṃ tāvakālikampi na labhati, sākhābhaṅgaṃ kappiyaṃ kāretvā sammajjitabbaṃ, tampi alabhantassa laddhakappiyaṃ hoti.

Thus it is said, the Uposatha should be performed only after having done the fourfold preliminary duties. By whom, then, should they be done? 'Monks, I allow a senior bhikkhu to instruct a junior bhikkhu. Monks, a non-ill bhikkhu instructed by a senior should not fail to sweep. Whoever does not sweep commits an offense of wrong-doing.' On account of such words, it should be done by the one who has been instructed by a senior. And when instructing, one should not instruct for the purpose of sweeping the Uposatha hall a bhikkhu who is doing some work, or one who is always early, or one who dwells alone, or one who carries out the burdens of the Sangha, or one among those such as a melodious reciter or a Dhamma-preacher. But the remaining bhikkhus should be instructed in turn. If the instructed bhikkhu cannot obtain even a temporary broom, he should have a broken branch made allowable and then sweep. For one who does not obtain that either, what is obtained is allowable.

Āsanapaññāpanatthaṃ āṇattena ca sace uposathāgāre āsanāni natthi, saṅghikāvāsato āharitvā paññapetvā puna āharitabbāni, āsanesu asati kaṭasārakepi taṭṭikāyopi paññāpetuṃ vaṭṭati, taṭṭikāsupi asati sākhābhaṅgāni kappiyaṃ kāretvā paññapetabbāni, kappiyakārakaṃ alabhantassa laddhakappiyaṃ hoti.

And by one instructed for the purpose of preparing seats, if there are no seats in the Uposatha hall, they should be brought from the Sangha's dwelling, arranged, and then returned. If there are no seats, it is permissible to arrange even coarse mats or woven matting. If woven matting is also unavailable, broken branches should be had made allowable and then arranged. For one who cannot find a person to make it allowable, what is obtained is allowable.

Padīpakaraṇatthaṃ āṇāpentena pana “asukasmiṃ nāma okāse telaṃ vā vaṭṭi vā kapallikā vā atthi, taṃ gahetvā karohī”ti vattabbo. Sace telādīni natthi, pariyesitabbāni, pariyesitvā alabhantassa laddhakappiyaṃ hoti. Apica kapāle aggipi jāletabbo.

However, for the purpose of lighting a lamp, one who is instructing should say: 'In such and such a place there is oil, or a wick, or a lamp-bowl. Take them and light it.' If oil and the like are not available, they should be sought. If, after searching, they are not obtained, what is obtained is allowable. Moreover, a fire may also be kindled on a potsherd.

“Chandapārisuddhiutukkhānaṃ, bhikkhugaṇanāca ovādo;

Uposathassa etāni, pubbakiccanti vuccatī”ti. (mahāva. 168) –

The conveying of consent, the conveying of purity, the announcement of the season, the counting of the bhikkhus, and the admonition; these are called the preliminary duties of the Uposatha.

Evaṃ [V 0.0201] vuttaṃ pana catubbidhampi pubbakiccaṃ pubbakaraṇato pacchā kātabbaṃ. Tampi hi akatvā uposatho na kātabbo.

However, thus it is said that even the fourfold preliminary duties should be performed after the preliminary work. For without doing them, the Uposatha should not be performed.

178. Yadi [M 0.0213] saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho uposathaṃ kareyyā”ti (mahāva. 143) vacanato yadā saṅghassa uposathakammaṃ pattakallaṃ hoti, tadā taṃ kātabbaṃ, pattakallañca nāmetaṃ catūhi aṅgehi saṅgahitaṃ. Tenāhu aṭṭhakathācariyā –

178. “If it is fitting for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Uposatha.” According to this, when the Uposatha act is fitting for the Saṅgha, then it should be done. And this, which is called ‘fitting,’ is comprised of four factors. Therefore, the commentary teachers said:

“Uposatho yāvatikā ca bhikkhū kammappattā,

Sabhāgāpattiyo ca na vijjanti;

Vajjanīyā ca puggalā tasmiṃ na honti,

Pattakallanti vuccatī”ti. (mahāva. aṭṭha. 168);

“The Uposatha day is present, and as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act are present; and offenses of a shared basis do not exist; and persons to be excluded are not present therein—this is called ‘fitting.’”

Tattha uposathoti tīsu uposathadivasesu aññataradivaso. Tasmiñhi sati idaṃ saṅghassa uposathakammaṃ pattakallaṃ nāma hoti, nāsati. Yathāha “na ca, bhikkhave, anuposathe uposatho kātabbo”ti (mahāva. 183).

Therein, ‘Uposatha’ means any one of the three Uposatha days. For when that day is present, this Uposatha act of the Saṅgha is called ‘fitting’; when it is absent, it is not. As it is said: “And, monks, the Uposatha should not be performed on a non-Uposatha day.”

Yāvatikā ca bhikkhū kammappattāti yattakā bhikkhū tassa uposathakammassa pattā yuttā anurūpā sabbantimena paricchedena cattāro pakatattā, te ca kho hatthapāsaṃ avijahitvā ekasīmāyaṃ ṭhitā. Tesu hi catūsu bhikkhūsu ekasīmāyaṃ hatthapāsaṃ avijahitvā ṭhitesveva taṃ saṅghassa uposathakammaṃ pattakallaṃ nāma hoti, na itarathā. Yathāha “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitu”nti (mahāva. 168).

‘And as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act’ means as many bhikkhus as are worthy, suitable, and appropriate for that Uposatha act—at the very least, four bhikkhus of proper standing. And they are remaining within a single boundary without leaving hand’s reach. For only when those four bhikkhus are remaining within a single boundary without leaving hand’s reach is that Uposatha act of the Saṅgha called ‘fitting,’ not otherwise. As it is said: “I allow, monks, the Pātimokkha to be recited for four.”

Sabhāgāpattiyo ca na vijjantīti ettha yaṃ sabbo saṅgho vikālabhojanādinā sabhāgavatthunā lahukāpattiṃ āpajjati, evarūpā vatthusabhāgā sabhāgāti vuccati. Etāsu avijjamānāsupi sabhāgāsu vijjamānāsupi pattakallaṃ hotiyeva.

Herein, regarding ‘and offenses of a shared basis do not exist’: whatever light offense the entire Saṅgha commits due to a shared basis, such as eating at an unseasonable time, such a shared basis is called ‘shared.’ Even if these shared offenses are absent, or even if they are present, it is indeed fitting.

Vajjanīyā ca puggalā tasmiṃ na hontīti “na, bhikkhave, sagahaṭṭhāya parisāya pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabba”nti (mahāva. 154) vacanato gahaṭṭho ca, “na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā nisinnaparisāya pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabba”ntiādinā (mahāva. 183) nayena vuttā bhikkhunī, sikkhamānā, sāmaṇero, sāmaṇerī, sikkhāpaccakkhātako, antimavatthuajjhāpannako[V 0.0202], āpattiyā adassane ukkhittako, āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittako, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittako, paṇḍako, theyyasaṃvāsako, titthiyapakkantako, tiracchānagato, mātughātako[M 0.0214], pitughātako, arahantaghātako, bhikkhunīdūsako, saṅghabhedako, lohituppādako, ubhatobyañjanakoti ime vīsati cāti ekavīsati puggalā vajjanīyā nāma. Te hatthapāsato bahikaraṇavasena vajjetabbā. Etesu hi tividhe ukkhittake sati uposathaṃ karonto saṅgho pācittiyaṃ āpajjati, sesesu dukkaṭaṃ, ettha ca tiracchānagatoti yassa upasampadā paṭikkhittā. Titthiyā gahaṭṭheneva saṅgahitā. Etepi hi vajjanīyā. Evaṃ pattakallaṃ imehi catūhi aṅgehi saṅgahitanti veditabbaṃ. Idañca sabbaṃ pavāraṇākammepi yojetvā dassetabbaṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, pātimokkhuddesakena sañcicca na sāvetabbaṃ, yo na sāveyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pātimokkhuddesakena vāyamituṃ ‘kathaṃ sāveyya’nti, vāyamantassa anāpattī”ti (mahāva. 154) vacanato pātimokkhuddesakena parisaṃ sāvetuṃ vāyamitabbanti.

‘And persons to be excluded are not present therein’—because it is said: ‘Monks, the Pātimokkha should not be recited in an assembly that includes a householder.’ This refers to a householder; and, as stated in the manner beginning ‘Monks, the Pātimokkha should not be recited in an assembly where a bhikkhunī is seated,’ a bhikkhunī, a probationer, a male novice, a female novice, one who has renounced the training, one who has committed a terminal offense, one suspended for not seeing an offense, one suspended for not making amends for an offense, one suspended for not renouncing an evil view, a paṇḍaka, one in clandestine communion, one who has gone over to another sect, one in the animal state, a matricide, a patricide, a murderer of an arahant, a defiler of a bhikkhunī, a schismatic, one who has shed a Buddha’s blood, and one with indeterminate sex—these twenty-one individuals are called ‘persons to be excluded.’ They should be excluded by being kept outside of hand’s reach. For if the Saṅgha performs the Uposatha while any of the three types of suspended individuals are present, it incurs a pācittiya offense; for the others, a dukkaṭa offense. Here, ‘one in the animal state’ refers to one for whom higher ordination has been rejected. Heretics are included under the term ‘householder.’ For these too are to be excluded. Thus, it should be understood that the ‘fitness of the occasion’ is comprised of these four factors. All this should also be applied and shown in the Pavāraṇā ceremony. Because it is said: ‘Monks, the reciter of the Pātimokkha should not intentionally fail to make it heard. Whoever does not make it heard, incurs a dukkaṭa offense. I allow, monks, the reciter of the Pātimokkha to make an effort, thinking, “How can I make it heard?” There is no offense for one who makes such an effort,’ therefore, the reciter of the Pātimokkha should strive to make it heard by the assembly.

Iti pāḷimuttakavinayavinicchayasaṅgahe

Thus in the Compendium of Vinaya Decisions Independent of the Canon.

Uposathapavāraṇāvinicchayakathā samattā.

The Discussion on Decisions Regarding Uposatha and Pavāraṇā is concluded.

26. Vassūpanāyikavinicchayakathā

26. A Discussion on the Determination of the Rains-residence

179. Vassūpanāyikāti [V 0.0203] ettha purimikā pacchimikāti duve vassūpanāyikā. Tattha (mahāva. aṭṭha. 184 ādayo) āsāḷhīpuṇṇamāya anantare pāṭipadadivase purimikā upagantabbā, pacchimikā pana āsāḷhīpuṇṇamato aparāya puṇṇamāya anantare pāṭipadadivase. Upagacchantena ca vihāraṃ paṭijaggitvā pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā sabbaṃ cetiyavandanādisāmīcikammaṃ niṭṭhāpetvā “imasmiṃ vihāre imaṃ temāsaṃ vassaṃ upemī”ti sakiṃ vā dvattikkhattuṃ vā vācaṃ nicchāretvā vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ. Sacepi “idha vasissāmī”ti ālayo atthi, asatiyā pana vassaṃ na upeti, gahitasenāsanaṃ suggahitaṃ, chinnavasso na hoti, pavāretuṃ labhatiyeva. Vināpi hi vacībhedaṃ ālayakaraṇamattenapi vassaṃ upagatameva hoti. “Idha vassaṃ vasissāmī”ti cittuppādoyevettha ālayo nāma.

179. Here, regarding the undertaking of the Rains-residence, there are two undertakings of the Rains-residence: the earlier and the later. Among these, the earlier should be undertaken on the day of the first of the waning moon immediately following the full moon of Āsāḷhī; the later, however, on the day of the first of the waning moon immediately following the next full moon after the Āsāḷhī full moon. One who is undertaking the Rains-residence, having prepared the monastery, having set out drinking water and water for use, and having completed all proper duties such as paying homage to the cetiya, should undertake the Rains-residence by uttering the words, 'I undertake the Rains-residence for these three months in this monastery,' once, or two or three times. Even if there is the attachment of mind, 'I will dwell here,' but due to forgetfulness one does not formally undertake the Rains-residence, the lodging taken is well-taken, one does not have a broken Rains-residence, and one is indeed entitled to perform the Pavāraṇā. For indeed, even without a verbal utterance, merely by the act of forming an attachment of mind, the Rains-residence is considered undertaken. Here, 'attachment' (ālaya) is simply the arising of the thought, 'I will dwell here for the Rains-residence.'

“Na[M 0.0215], bhikkhave, tadahuvassūpanāyikāya vassaṃ anupagantukāmena sañcicca āvāso atikkamitabbo, yo atikkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 186) vacanato vassūpanāyikadivase vassaṃ anupagantukāmo vihārasīmaṃ atikkamati, vihāragaṇanāya dukkaṭaṃ. Sace hi taṃ divasaṃ vihārasatassa upacāraṃ okkamitvā atikkamati, sataṃ āpattiyo. Sace pana vihāraṃ atikkamitvā aññassa vihārassa upacāraṃ anokkamitvāva nivattati, ekāva āpatti. Kenaci antarāyena purimikaṃ anupagatena pacchimikā upagantabbā.

“Monks, a dwelling should not be intentionally passed beyond by one who does not wish to undertake the Rains-residence on the very day of undertaking the Rains-residence. Whoever should pass beyond it, there is an offence of wrong-doing.” According to this, if on the day of undertaking the Rains-residence one who does not wish to undertake the Rains-residence crosses the monastery boundary, there is an offence of wrong-doing for each monastery. For if on that day one encroaches upon and passes beyond the vicinity of a hundred monasteries, there are a hundred offences. If, however, having passed beyond a monastery, one turns back without having encroached upon the vicinity of another monastery, there is only one offence. If, due to some obstacle, one has not undertaken the earlier Rains-residence, the later one should be undertaken.

“Na, bhikkhave, asenāsanikena vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ, yo upagaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 204) vacanato yassa pañcannaṃ chadanānaṃ aññatarena channaṃ yojitadvārabandhanaṃ senāsanaṃ natthi, tena na upagantabbaṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, chavakuṭikāya vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ, yo upagaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti(mahāva. 204) ādivacanato chavakuṭikāyaṃ chatte cāṭiyañca upagantuṃ na vaṭṭati. Tattha chavakuṭikā nāma ṭaṅkitamañcādibhedā kuṭi. Tattheva upagantuṃ na vaṭṭati, susāne pana aññaṃ kuṭikaṃ katvā upagantuṃ vaṭṭati, chattepi catūsu thambhesu chattaṃ ṭhapetvā āvaraṇaṃ katvā dvāraṃ yojetvā upagantuṃ vaṭṭati, chattakuṭi nāmesā [V 0.0204] hoti. Cāṭiyāpi mahantena kapallena chatte vuttanayena kuṭikaṃ katvā upagantuṃ vaṭṭati.

“Monks, one without a lodging should not undertake the Rains-residence. Whoever should undertake it, there is an offence of wrong-doing.” According to this, one for whom there is no lodging covered by one of the five kinds of roofing and having a fitted door-frame should not undertake the Rains-residence. “Monks, one should not undertake the Rains-residence in a bedstead-hut. Whoever should undertake it, there is an offence of wrong-doing.” According to this and similar statements, it is not allowable to undertake the Rains-residence in a bedstead-hut, under a canopy, or in a large pot. Here, a 'bedstead-hut' is a hut distinguished by things such as a bedstead with legs. It is not allowable to undertake the Rains-residence in that very place; however, it is allowable to make another small hut in a charnel ground and undertake the Rains-residence. Also, regarding a canopy, it is allowable to set up a canopy on four posts, make an enclosure, attach a door, and undertake the Rains-residence; this is called a 'canopy-hut'. Regarding a large pot, it is also allowable to make a small hut with a large potsherd in the manner described for a canopy and undertake the Rains-residence.

“Na, bhikkhave, rukkhasusire vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ, yo upagaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 204) vacanato suddhe rukkhasusire upagantuṃ na vaṭṭati, mahantassa pana rukkhasusirassa anto padaracchadanaṃ kuṭikaṃ katvā pavisanadvāraṃ yojetvā upagantuṃ vaṭṭati, rukkhaṃ chinditvā khāṇukamatthake padaracchadanaṃ kuṭikaṃ katvāpi vaṭṭatiyeva. “Na, bhikkhave, rukkhaviṭabhiyā”ti(mahāva. 204) ādivacanato suddhe viṭabhimatte upagantuṃ na vaṭṭati, mahāviṭape pana aṭṭakaṃ bandhitvā tattha padaracchadanaṃ kuṭikaṃ katvā dvāraṃ yojetvā upagantabbaṃ.

“Monks, one should not undertake the Rains-residence in a tree hollow. Whoever should undertake it, there is an offence of wrong-doing.” According to this, it is not allowable to undertake the Rains-residence in a bare tree hollow. However, in the case of a large tree hollow, it is allowable to undertake the Rains-residence after constructing a small hut with a plank roof inside it and fitting an entrance door. Even if a tree is cut down and a small hut with a plank roof is built on the stump, it is indeed allowable. “Monks, [one should not undertake the Rains-residence] in the fork of a tree.” According to this and similar statements, it is not allowable to undertake the Rains-residence in a mere tree fork. However, in the case of a large tree fork, one should build a platform, construct a small hut with a plank roof on it, fit a door, and undertake the Rains-residence.

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vaje vassaṃ upagantu”ntiādivacanato vaje satthe nāvāyañca upagantuṃ vaṭṭati. Tattha vajoti gopālakānaṃ nivāsaṭṭhānaṃ. Vaje vuṭṭhite vajena saddhiṃ gatassa vassacchede anāpatti “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yena vajo, tena gantu”nti (mahāva. 203) vuttattā. Satthe [M 0.0216] vassaṃ upagacchantena pana vassūpanāyikadivase upāsakā vattabbā “kuṭikā laddhuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti. Sace karitvā denti, tattha pavisitvā “idha vassaṃ upemī”ti tikkhattuṃ vattabbaṃ. No ce denti, sālāsaṅkhepena ṭhitasakaṭassa heṭṭhā upagantabbaṃ. Tampi alabhantena ālayo kātabbo, satthe pana vassaṃ upagantuṃ na vaṭṭati. Ālayo nāma “idha vassaṃ vasissāmī”ti cittuppādamattaṃ. Sace maggappaṭipanneyeva satthe pavāraṇādivaso hoti, tattheva pavāretabbaṃ. Atha sattho antovasseyeva bhikkhunā patthitaṭṭhānaṃ patvā atikkamati, patthitaṭṭhāne vasitvā tattha bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ pavāretabbaṃ. Athāpi sattho antovasseyeva antarā ekasmiṃ gāme tiṭṭhati vā vippakirati vā, tasmiṃyeva gāme bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ vasitvā pavāretabbaṃ, appavāretvā tato paraṃ gantuṃ na vaṭṭati. Nāvāya vassaṃ upagacchantenapi kuṭiyaṃyeva upagantabbaṃ, pariyesitvā alabhantena ālayo kātabbo. Sace antotemāsaṃ nāvā samuddeyeva hoti, tattheva pavāretabbaṃ. Atha nāvā kūlaṃ labhati, ayañca parato gantukāmo hoti, gantuṃ na vaṭṭati, nāvāya laddhagāmeyeva vasitvā bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ pavāretabbaṃ. Sacepi nāvā anutīrameva aññattha gacchati, bhikkhu ca paṭhamaṃ laddhagāmeyeva vasitukāmo, nāvā gacchatu, bhikkhunā tattheva vasitvā bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ pavāretabbaṃ. Iti vaje satthe nāvāyanti tīsu ṭhānesu natthi vassacchede āpatti, pavāretuñca labhati.

“I allow, monks, to undertake the Rains-residence in a cattle station.” According to this and similar statements, it is allowable to undertake the Rains-residence in a cattle station, in a caravan, or on a ship. Here, “cattle station” means a dwelling place of cowherds. If one has undertaken the Rains-residence in a cattle station and then goes with the cattle station, there is no offence of breaking the Rains-residence, because it is said, “I allow, monks, to go where the cattle station goes.” However, one who undertakes the Rains-residence in a caravan should, on the day of undertaking the Rains-residence, tell the lay followers, “It is allowable to obtain a small hut.” If they make one and give it, one should enter it and say three times, “I undertake the Rains-residence here.” If they do not give one, one should undertake the Rains-residence beneath a cart that stands in place of a hall. If even that is not obtained, one should form the intention. However, it is not allowable to undertake the Rains-residence in a caravan together with bhikkhus. Here, “intention” means merely the arising of the thought, “I will dwell here during the rains.” If the day of Pavāraṇā occurs while the caravan is still on the road, one should perform the Pavāraṇā right there. But if the caravan passes the destination desired by the bhikkhu within the Rains-residence period, one should dwell at the desired destination and perform the Pavāraṇā with the bhikkhus there. Or if the caravan stops or disperses in a village along the way within the Rains-residence period, one should dwell in that village with the bhikkhus and perform the Pavāraṇā. It is not allowable to proceed further without performing the Pavāraṇā. Similarly, one who undertakes the Rains-residence on a ship should undertake it in a hut. If one cannot find one after searching, one should form the intention. If the ship remains at sea within the three months, the Pavāraṇā should be performed right there. But if the ship reaches shore, and one wishes to go elsewhere, it is not allowable to go. Instead, one should dwell in the village reached by the ship and perform the Pavāraṇā with the bhikkhus. Even if the ship continues to sail elsewhere along the coast, but the bhikkhu wishes to dwell in the village reached first, the ship may depart, and the bhikkhu should dwell there and perform the Pavāraṇā with the bhikkhus. Thus, in these three places—a cattle station, a caravan, or a ship—there is no offence of breaking the Rains-residence, and one is also able to perform the Pavāraṇā.

“Na, bhikkhave, vassaṃ upagantvā purimaṃ vā temāsaṃ pacchimaṃ vā temāsaṃ avasitvā cārikā [V 0.0205] pakkamitabbā, yo pakkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 186) vacanato purimikāya vassaṃ upagatena purimaṃ temāsaṃ, pacchimikāya upagatena pacchimaṃ temāsaṃ avasitvā cārikā na pakkamitabbā, vassaṃ upagantvā pana aruṇaṃ anuṭṭhāpetvāpi tadaheva sattāhakaraṇīyena pakkamantassapi antosattāhe nivattantassa anāpatti, ko pana vādo dvīhatīhaṃ vasitvā sattāhakaraṇīyena pakkamantassa antosattāhe nivattantassa.

“Monks, having undertaken the Rains-residence, one should not depart on a journey without having completed either the first three months or the last three months. Whoever departs incurs an offence of wrong-doing.” According to this statement, one who has undertaken the Rains-residence in the earlier period should not depart on a journey without having completed the first three months, and one who has undertaken it in the later period should not depart without having completed the last three months. However, for one who, having undertaken the Rains-residence, departs on that very day on a seven-day business even without letting the dawn arise and returns within seven days, there is no offence; what then is to be said of one who, having stayed for two or three days, departs on a seven-day business and returns within seven days?

180. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sattannaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena pahite gantuṃ, na tveva appahite. Bhikkhussa bhikkhuniyā sikkhamānāya sāmaṇerassa [M 0.0217] sāmaṇeriyā upāsakassa upāsikāyā”ti (mahāva. 187) vacanato pañcannaṃ sahadhammikānaṃ aññatarena saṅghagaṇapuggale uddissa attano vā atthāya vihāraṃ aḍḍhayogaṃ pāsādaṃ hammiyaṃ guhaṃ pariveṇaṃ koṭṭhakaṃ upaṭṭhānasālaṃ aggisālaṃ kappiyakuṭiṃ vaccakuṭiṃ caṅkamaṃ caṅkamanasālaṃ udapānaṃ udapānasālaṃ jantāgharaṃ jantāgharasālaṃ pokkharaṇiṃ maṇḍapaṃ ārāmaṃ ārāmavatthuṃ vā kāretvā “āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ dhammañca sotuṃ bhikkhū ca passitu”nti evaṃ niddisitvā pesite gantabbaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena, na tveva appahite. Upāsako vā upāsikā vā tatheva saṅghagaṇapuggale uddissa vihārādīsu aññataraṃ kāretvā attano vā atthāya nivesanasayanigharādīsu aññataraṃ kārāpetvā aññaṃ vā kiccakaraṇīyaṃ niddisitvā gilāno vā hutvā bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya “āgacchantu bhadantā, icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ dhammañca sotuṃ bhikkhū ca passitu”nti, gantabbaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena, na tveva appahite.

180. “I allow, bhikkhus, to go when sent by any of seven persons for a purpose lasting seven days, but not if unsent. These are: a bhikkhu, a bhikkhunī, a female probationer, a male novice, a female novice, a lay follower, or a laywoman.” According to this, when any one of five co-religionists—designating the Sangha, a group, or an individual, or for one's own sake—has caused to be built a monastery, a half-gabled house, a multi-storied building, a mansion, a cave, an enclosure, a gatehouse, a service hall, a fire hall, a suitable hut, a toilet, a walkway, a hall for the walkway, a well, a hall over a well, a steam-bath house, a hall for the steam-bath house, a pond, a pavilion, a park, or a park ground, and sends word saying, “Let the bhikkhus come, I wish to give alms, hear the Dhamma, and see the bhikkhus,” then one may go for a purpose lasting seven days, but not if unsent. Similarly, if a male lay follower or a female lay follower, having caused to be built any of these for the sake of the Sangha, a group, or an individual, or having caused to be built a dwelling, a sleeping-place, a house, or the like for their own sake, or having specified some other business, or being ill, sends a messenger to the bhikkhus saying, “Let the venerables come, I wish to give alms, hear the Dhamma, and see the bhikkhus,” then one may go for a purpose lasting seven days, but not if unsent.

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sattannaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena appahitepi gantuṃ, pageva pahite. Bhikkhussa bhikkhuniyā sikkhamānāya sāmaṇerassa sāmaṇeriyā mātuyā ca pitussa cā”ti (mahāva. 198) vacanato “gilānānaṃ etesaṃ bhikkhuādīnaṃ sahadhammikānaṃ mātāpitūnañca gilānānaṃyeva gilānabhattaṃ vā gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ vā bhesajjaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, pucchissāmi vā upaṭṭhahissāmi vā”ti iminā kāraṇena appahitepi gantabbaṃ, pageva pahite. Andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “ye mātāpitūnaṃ upaṭṭhākā ñātakā vā aññātakā vā, tesampi appahite gantuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ neva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ, na pāḷiyaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmā na gahetabbaṃ.

“I allow, bhikkhus, to go even uninvited for a purpose lasting seven days, how much more so if invited, for a bhikkhu, a bhikkhunī, a female probationer, a male novice, a female novice, and for one's mother and father.” According to this statement, it is allowable to go even if uninvited—and how much more so if invited—for this reason: ‘I will seek food for the sick, or food for a sick-attendant, or medicine; or I will inquire after, or I will attend to, these sick co-religionists, namely bhikkhus and so forth, and one's sick mother and father.’ However, in the Andhaka commentary, it is said: “For those who attend to one's mother and father, whether relatives or non-relatives, it is also proper to go uninvited.” This is stated neither in the commentary nor in the Pāḷi; therefore, it should not be accepted.

Sace pana bhikkhuno bhātā vā añño vā ñātako gilāno hoti, so ce bhikkhussa santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya “ahaṃ gilāno, āgacchatu bhadanto, icchāmi bhadantassa āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena, na tveva appahite. Sace ekasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ [V 0.0206] vasanto bhikkhubhattiko gilāno hoti, so ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya “ahaṃ gilāno, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena, na tveva appahite.

If, however, a bhikkhu’s brother or another relative is sick, and if that person sends a messenger to the bhikkhu saying, “I am sick, venerable sir, please come; I wish for your coming,” it is allowable to go for a purpose lasting seven days, but certainly not if uninvited. If the brother of a bhikkhu, living together with bhikkhus in one monastery, is sick, and if he sends a messenger to the bhikkhus saying, “I am sick, bhikkhus, please come; I wish for your coming,” it is allowable to go for a purpose lasting seven days, but certainly not if uninvited.

Sace [M 0.0218] bhikkhussa bhikkhuniyā sikkhamānāya sāmaṇerassa sāmaṇeriyā anabhirati vā kukkuccaṃ vā diṭṭhigataṃ vā uppannaṃ hoti, gantabbaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena appahitepi “anabhiratiṃ vūpakāsessāmi vā vūpakāsāpessāmi vā kumkuccaṃ vinodessāmi vā vinodāpessāmi vā diṭṭhigataṃ vivecessāmi vā vivecāpessāmi vā dhammakathaṃ vā karissāmī”ti, pageva pahite. Sace koci bhikkhu garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti parivāsāraho mūlāyapaṭikassanāraho mānattāraho abbhānāraho vā, appahitepi gantabbaṃ “parivāsadānādīsu ussukkaṃ āpajjissāmi, anussāvessāmi, gaṇapūrako vā bhavissāmī”ti, pageva pahite. Bhikkhuniyāpi mānattārahāya mūlāyapaṭikassanārahāya abbhānārahāya vā eseva nayo. Sace sāmaṇero upasampajjitukāmo hoti, vassaṃ vā pucchitukāmo, sikkhamānā vā upasampajjitukāmā hoti, sikkhā vāssā kupitā, sāmaṇerī vā sikkhā samādiyitukāmā hoti, vassaṃ vā pucchitukāmā, appahitepi gantabbaṃ, pageva pahite.

If a bhikkhu, bhikkhunī, female probationer, male novice, or female novice develops discontent, remorse, or a wrong view, one should go for a purpose lasting seven days even if not invited, thinking, “I will allay their discontent, or have it allayed; I will dispel their remorse, or have it dispelled; I will resolve their wrong view, or have it resolved; or I will give a Dhamma talk”—how much more so if invited. If any bhikkhu has fallen into a grave offense and is deserving of probation, deserving of reinstatement to the beginning, deserving of penance, or deserving of rehabilitation, one should go even if not invited, thinking, “I will apply myself to the granting of probation and so forth, I will announce it, or I will be one who completes the quorum”—how much more so if invited. The same principle applies for a bhikkhunī deserving of penance, deserving of reinstatement to the beginning, or deserving of rehabilitation. If a male novice wishes to receive full ordination, or to ask about the rains-residence period; if a female probationer wishes to receive full ordination, or her training has been disrupted; if a female novice wishes to undertake the training, or to ask about the rains-residence period—one should go even if not invited, how much more so if invited.

Sace bhikkhussa bhikkhuniyā vā saṅgho kammaṃ kātukāmo hoti, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, appahitepi gantabbaṃ, pageva pahite “kiṃ nu kho saṅgho kammaṃ na kareyya, lahukāya vā pariṇāmeyyā”ti. Sacepi kataṃyeva hoti kammaṃ, appahitepi gantabbaṃ “kiṃ nu kho sammā vatteyya, lomaṃ pāteyya, netthāraṃ vatteyya, saṅgho taṃ kammaṃ paṭippassambheyyā”ti.

If the Saṅgha wishes to perform an act against a bhikkhu or bhikkhunī—whether an act of rebuke, an act of subordination, an act of banishment, an act of reconciliation, or an act of suspension—one should go even if not invited, how much more so if invited, thinking, “How might it be that the Saṅgha would not perform the act, or would incline towards a lighter one?” Even if the act has already been performed, one should go even if not invited, thinking, “How might it be that he would conduct himself rightly, would humble himself, would act in a way that leads to restoration, and that the Saṅgha would revoke that act?”

181. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghakaraṇīyena gantu”nti (mahāva. 199) vacanato senāsanapaṭibaddhasaṅghakaraṇīyenapi gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Ettha (mahāva. aṭṭha. 199) hi yaṃ kiñci uposathāgārādīsu senāsanesu cetiyachattavedikādīsu vā kattabbaṃ, antamaso bhikkhuno puggalikasenāsanampi sabbaṃ saṅghakaraṇīyamevāti adhippetaṃ, tasmā tassa nipphādanatthaṃ dabbasambhārādīni vā āharituṃ vaḍḍhakīpabhutīnaṃ bhattavetanādīni vā dātuṃ gantabbaṃ. Apicettha ayampi pāḷimuttakanayo veditabbo – dhammassavanatthāya animantitena gantuṃ na vaṭṭati, sace ekasmiṃ mahāvāse paṭhamaṃyeva katikā katā hoti “asukadivasaṃ [M 0.0219] nāma sannipatitabba”nti, nimantitoyeva nāma hoti, gantuṃ vaṭṭati. “Bhaṇḍakaṃ dhovissāmī”ti gantuṃ na vaṭṭati. Sace pana [V 0.0207] ācariyupajjhāyā pahiṇanti, vaṭṭati. Nātidūre vihāro hoti, “tattha gantvā ajjeva āgamissāmī”ti sampāpuṇituṃ na sakkoti, vaṭṭati. Uddesaparipucchādīnaṃ atthāyapi gantuṃ na labhati, “ācariyaṃ pana passissāmī”ti gantuṃ labhati. Sace naṃ ācariyo “ajja mā gacchā”ti vadati, vaṭṭati, upaṭṭhākakulaṃ vā ñātikulaṃ vā dassanāya gantuṃ na labhati.

181. “I allow, bhikkhus, to go for Saṅgha business.” (Mahāvagga 199) According to this statement, it is permissible to go even for Saṅgha business related to lodging. Here, whatever needs to be done in the Uposatha hall and other lodgings, or at shrines, canopies, platforms, etc.—even a bhikkhu’s personal lodging—all is considered Saṅgha business. Therefore, one may go to fetch materials or to pay food and wages to carpenters and others for completing such tasks. Moreover, this non-canonical principle should be understood: it is not permissible to go uninvited for the purpose of hearing the Dhamma. But if, in a large monastery, an agreement was made from the start stating, “We will assemble on such-and-such a day,” then it counts as an invitation, and it is permissible to go. One should not go thinking, “I will wash the robe.” But if one's teachers and preceptors send one, it is permissible. If the monastery is not too far, and one thinks, “I will go there and return today,” but cannot manage to do so, it is permissible. One is not allowed to go for the purpose of recitation or questioning, etc., but one is allowed to go thinking, “I will see my teacher.” If the teacher tells him, “Do not go today,” it is permissible (to obey). One is not allowed to go to visit a supporting family or relatives.

Sace bhikkhūsu vassūpagatesu gāmo corehi vuṭṭhāti, tattha kiṃ kātabbanti? Yena gāmo, tena gantabbaṃ. Sace gāmo dvidhā bhijjati, yattha bahutarā manussā, tattha gantabbaṃ. Sace bahutarā assaddhā honti appasannā, yattha saddhā pasannā, tattha gantabbaṃ. Ettha ca sace gāmo avidūragato hoti, tattha piṇḍāya caritvā vihārameva āgantvā vasitabbaṃ. Sace dūraṃ gato, sattāhavārena aruṇo uṭṭhāpetabbo, na sakkā ce hoti, tattheva sabhāgaṭṭhāne vasitabbaṃ. Sace manussā yathāpavattāni salākabhattādīni denti, “na mayaṃ tasmiṃ vihāre vasimhā”ti vattabbā. “Mayaṃ vihārassa vā pāsādassa vā na dema, tumhākaṃ dema, yattha katthaci vasitvā bhuñjathā”ti vutte pana yathāsukhaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ, tesaṃyeva taṃ pāpuṇāti. “Tumhākaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne pāpuṇāpetvā bhuñjathā”ti vutte pana yattha vasanti, tattha netvā vassaggena pāpuṇāpetvā bhuñjitabbaṃ. Sace pavāritakāle vassāvāsikaṃ denti, yadi sattāhavārena aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpayiṃsu, gahetabbaṃ. Chinnavassehi pana “na mayaṃ tattha vasimha, chinnavassā maya”nti vattabbaṃ. Yadi “yesaṃ amhākaṃ senāsanaṃ pāpitaṃ, te gaṇhantū”ti vadanti, gahetabbaṃ. Yaṃ pana “vihāre upanikkhittakaṃ mā vinassī”ti idha āhaṭaṃ cīvarādivebhaṅgiyabhaṇḍaṃ, taṃ tattheva gantvā apaloketvā bhājetabbaṃ. “Ito ayyānaṃ cattāro paccaye dethā”ti kappiyakārakānaṃ dinne khettavatthuādike tatruppādepi eseva nayo. Saṅghikañhi vebhaṅgiyabhaṇḍaṃ antovihāre vā bahisīmāya vā hotu, bahisīmāya ṭhitānaṃ apaloketvā bhājetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Ubhayattha ṭhitampi pana antosīmāya ṭhitānaṃ apaloketvā bhājetuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

If, when the bhikkhus have entered the rains residence, the village is displaced by robbers, what should be done? One should go to where the village people are. If the village splits into two, one should go where the majority of people are. If the majority are faithless and lacking confidence, one should go where the faithful and confident are. And here, if the village is not far away, one should go for alms there and then return to the monastery to stay. If it is far away, one must ensure that dawn rises at the original residence within a seven-day period. If that is not possible, one should stay right there in a suitable place. If the people give the customary shares of food such as ticket-food, they should be told, “We did not stay in that monastery.” But if they say, “We are not giving this to the monastery or the residence, but to you—wherever you stay, eat it,” then one may eat it as one pleases, and it belongs only to those bhikkhus. If they say, “Have it delivered to your dwelling place and eat it,” then one should have it brought to where they are staying, and after it is received as the share for the rains-residence, eat it. If they give the rains-residence requisites at the time of Pavāraṇā, and if one has caused dawn to rise within a seven-day period, it may be accepted. But those whose rains-residence is broken should say, “We did not stay there; our rains-residence is broken.” If they say, “Let those to whom our lodging was assigned accept it,” it may be accepted. As for any divisible goods, such as robes, that were brought here with the thought, ‘Let the property deposited in the monastery not be lost,’ one must go back to that very monastery, seek consent, and then divide them. This same principle applies also to the produce of fields, land, and so on, that were given to stewards with the instruction, “Give the four requisites to the venerables from this.” For divisible property belonging to the Sangha, whether it is inside the monastery or outside the boundary, it is not allowable to divide it after seeking consent from those staying outside the boundary. But even if it is situated in both places, it is indeed allowable to divide it after seeking consent from those staying within the boundary.

Sace [M 0.0220] pana vassūpagatā bhikkhū vāḷehi ubbāḷhā honti, gaṇhantipi paripātentipi, sarīsapehi vā ubbāḷhā honti, ḍaṃsantipi paripātentipi, corehi vā ubbāḷhā honti, vilumpantipi ākoṭentipi, pisācehi vā ubbāḷhā honti, āvisantipi hanantipi, “eseva antarāyo”ti pakkamitabbaṃ, natthi vassacchede āpatti. Sace gāmo agginā vā daḍḍho hoti, udakena vā vuḷho. Bhikkhū piṇḍakena kilamanti, “eseva antarāyo”ti pakkamitabbaṃ, vassacchede anāpatti. Senāsanaṃ agginā vā daḍḍhaṃ hoti, udakena vā vuḷhaṃ, bhikkhū senāsanena kilamanti, “eseva antarāyo”ti pakkamitabbaṃ, vassacchede anāpatti. Sace [V 0.0208] vassūpagatā bhikkhū na labhanti lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ, “eseva antarāyo”ti pakkamitabbaṃ. Sace labhanti lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ, na labhanti sappāyāni bhojanāni, “eseva antarāyo”ti pakkamitabbaṃ. Sacepi labhanti lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ, labhanti sappāyāni bhojanāni, na labhanti sappāyāni bhesajjāni, “eseva antarāyo”ti pakkamitabbaṃ. Sace labhanti lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ, labhanti sappāyāni bhojanāni, labhanti sappāyāni bhesajjāni, na labhanti patirūpaṃ upaṭṭhākaṃ, “eseva antarāyo”ti pakkamitabbaṃ, sabbattha vassacchede anāpatti.

If, however, bhikkhus who have entered the rains-residence are harassed by wild beasts, which seize or pursue them; or are harassed by reptiles, which bite or pursue them; or are harassed by thieves, which plunder or strike them; or are harassed by demons, which possess or kill them—they should depart, thinking, ‘This itself is a danger.’ There is no offense for breaking the rains. If an alms-round village is burned by fire or swept away by water, and the bhikkhus are troubled by lack of alms-food, they should depart, thinking, ‘This itself is a danger.’ There is no offense for breaking the rains. If a lodging is burned by fire or swept away by water, and the bhikkhus are troubled by lack of a lodging, they should depart, thinking, ‘This itself is a danger.’ There is no offense for breaking the rains. If bhikkhus who have entered the rains-residence do not obtain a sufficient quantity of coarse or fine food, they should depart, thinking, ‘This itself is a danger.’ If they obtain a sufficient quantity of coarse or fine food but do not obtain suitable food, they should depart, thinking, ‘This itself is a danger.’ Even if they obtain a sufficient quantity of coarse or fine food and suitable food but do not obtain suitable medicines, they should depart, thinking, ‘This itself is a danger.’ If they obtain a sufficient quantity of coarse or fine food, suitable food, and suitable medicines but do not obtain a suitable attendant, they should depart, thinking, ‘This itself is a danger.’ In all these cases, there is no offense for breaking the rains.

Sace pana vassūpagataṃ bhikkhuṃ itthī nimanteti “ehi, bhante, hiraññaṃ vā te demi, suvaṇṇaṃ vā khettaṃ vā vatthuṃ vā gāvuṃ vā gāviṃ vā dāsaṃ vā dāsiṃ vā te demi, dhītaraṃ vā te demi bhariyatthāya, ahaṃ vā te bhariyā homi, aññaṃ vā te bhariyaṃ ānemī”ti, tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti “lahuparivattaṃ kho cittaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, siyāpime brahmacariyassa antarāyo”ti, pakkamitabbaṃ, natthi vassacchede āpatti. Vuttanayeneva vesī vā nimanteti, thullakumārī vā nimanteti, paṇḍako vā nimanteti, ñātakā vā nimantenti, rājāno vā nimantenti, corā vā nimantenti, dhuttā vā nimantenti, eseva nayo. Sace vassūpagato bhikkhu passati asāmikaṃ nidhiṃ, tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti “lahuparivattaṃ kho cittaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, siyāpi me brahmacariyassa antarāyo”ti, pakkamitabbaṃ, anāpatti vassacchede.

If, however, a woman invites a bhikkhu who has entered the rains residence, saying, “Come, venerable sir, I will give you silver or gold, or a field, or a site, or a bull, or a cow, or a male slave, or a female slave, or I will give you my daughter as a wife, or I myself will be your wife, or I will bring another wife for you,” and if the bhikkhu thinks, ‘The Blessed One has said that the mind is indeed quick to change—this might be an obstacle to my holy life,’ he should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains residence. The same method applies if a prostitute invites him, or a widow invites him, or a eunuch invites him, or relatives invite him, or kings invite him, or thieves invite him, or rogues invite him. If a bhikkhu who has entered the rains residence sees ownerless treasure, and if he thinks, ‘The Blessed One has said that the mind is indeed quick to change—this might be an obstacle to my holy life,’ he should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains residence.
