Sace [M 0.0221] vassūpagato bhikkhu passati sambahule bhikkhū saṅghabhedāya parakkamante, suṇāti vā “sambahulā bhikkhū saṅghabhedāya parakkamantī”ti, tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti “garuko kho saṅghabhedo vutto bhagavatā, mā mayi sammukhībhūte saṅgho bhijjī”ti, pakkamitabbaṃ, anāpatti vassacchede. Sace vassūpagato bhikkhu suṇāti “asukasmiṃ kira āvāse sambahulā bhikkhū saṅghabhedāya parakkamantī”ti, tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti “te ca kho me bhikkhū mittā, tyāhaṃ vakkhāmi ‘garuko kho, āvuso, saṅghabhedo vutto bhagavatā, mā āyasmantānaṃ saṅghabhedo ruccitthā’ti, karissanti me vacanaṃ sussūsissanti, sotaṃ odahissantī”ti, pakkamitabbaṃ, anāpatti vassacchede, bhinne pana saṅghe gantvā karaṇīyaṃ natthi.

If a monk who has entered the rains residence sees many monks striving for a schism in the Sangha, or hears that “many monks are striving for a schism in the Sangha,” and if that monk thinks, “A schism in the Sangha has indeed been declared serious by the Blessed One; may the Sangha not split while I am present,” he should depart—there is no offense for breaking the rains residence. If a monk who has entered the rains residence hears, “In such and such a dwelling, many monks are said to be striving for a schism in the Sangha,” and if that monk thinks, “Those monks are my friends; I will say to them, ‘Friends, a schism in the Sangha has indeed been declared serious by the Blessed One; may a schism in the Sangha not be agreeable to you venerable ones.’ They will heed my words, they will wish to hear, and they will pay attention,” he should depart—there is no offense for breaking the rains residence. But if the Sangha has already split, there is nothing to be done by going.

Sace [V 0.0209] pana koci bhikkhu “imaṃ temāsaṃ idha vassaṃ vasathā”ti vutte paṭissuṇitvā visaṃvādeti, dukkaṭaṃ. Na kevalaṃ tasseva paṭissavassa visaṃvāde dukkaṭaṃ, “imaṃ temāsaṃ bhikkhaṃ gaṇhatha, ubhopi mayaṃ idha vassaṃ vasissāma, ekato uddisāpessāmā”ti evamādināpi tassa tassa paṭissavassa visaṃvāde dukkaṭaṃ. Tañca kho paṭhamaṃ suddhacittassa pacchā visaṃvādanapaccayā, paṭhamampi asuddhacittassa pana paṭissave pācittiyaṃ. Visaṃvāde dukkaṭanti pācittiyena saddhiṃ dukkaṭaṃ yujjati.

If a monk, when told, “Spend the rains residence here for these three months,” agrees and then reneges, it is a dukkaṭa offense. Not only is there a dukkaṭa offense in reneging on that agreement, but also in reneging on any such agreement, as when saying, “Take alms for these three months, both of us will spend the rains residence here, we will have the recitation done together,” and so on—in each case of reneging on such an agreement, it is a dukkaṭa offense. And that is for one who, having a pure mind at first, reneges later. But for one whose mind is impure even at first, at the time of agreeing, there is a pācittiya offense. For the reneging, there is a dukkaṭa offense; thus, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred along with the pācittiya offense.

182. Vassūpagatehi (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318) antovasse nibaddhavattaṃ ṭhapetvā vassūpagatā bhikkhū “sammuñjaniyo bandhathā”ti vattabbā. Sulabhā ce daṇḍakā ceva salākāyo ca honti, ekakena cha pañca muṭṭhisammuñjaniyo dve tisso yaṭṭhisammuñjaniyo vā bandhitabbā. Dullabhā honti, dve tisso muṭṭhisammuñjaniyo ekā yaṭṭhisammuñjanī bandhitabbā. Sāmaṇerehi pañca pañca ukkā vā koṭṭetabbā, vasanaṭṭhānesu kasāvaparibhaṇḍaṃ kātabbaṃ. Vattaṃ karontehi ca na uddisitabbaṃ na uddisāpetabbaṃ, na sajjhāyo kātabbo, na pabbājetabbaṃ na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na dhammassavanaṃ kātabbaṃ. Sabbeva hi ete papañcā, nippapañcā hutvā samaṇadhammameva karissāmāti vā sabbe terasa dhutaṅgāni samādiyantu, seyyaṃ akappetvā ṭhānacaṅkamehi vītināmentu, mūgabbataṃ gaṇhantu, sattāhakaraṇīyena gatāpi [M 0.0222] bhājanīyabhaṇḍaṃ labhantūti vā evarūpaṃ adhammikavattaṃ na kātabbaṃ. Evaṃ pana kātabbaṃ – pariyattidhammo nāma tividhampi saddhammaṃ patiṭṭhāpeti, tasmā sakkaccaṃ uddisatha uddisāpetha, sajjhāyaṃ karotha, padhānaghare vasantānaṃ saṅghaṭṭanaṃ akatvā antovihāre nisīditvā uddisatha uddisāpetha, sajjhāyaṃ karotha, dhammassavanaṃ samiddhaṃ karotha, pabbājentā sodhetvā pabbājetha, sodhetvā upasampādetha, sodhetvā nissayaṃ detha. Ekopi hi kulaputto pabbajjañca upasampadañca labhitvā sakalaṃ sāsanaṃ patiṭṭhāpeti, attano thāmena yattakāni sakkotha, tattakāni dhutaṅgāni samādiyatha, antovassaṃ nāmetaṃ sakaladivasaṃ rattiyā ca paṭhamayāmapacchimayāmesu appamattehi bhavitabbaṃ, vīriyaṃ ārabhitabbaṃ. Porāṇakamahātherāpi sabbapalibodhe chinditvā antovasse ekacāriyavattaṃ pūrayiṃsu, bhasse mattaṃ jānitvā dasavatthukathaṃ dasaasubhadasānussatiaṭṭhatiṃsārammaṇakathaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, āgantukānaṃ vattaṃ kātuṃ, sattāhakaraṇīyena gatānaṃ apaloketvā dātuṃ vaṭṭatīti evarūpaṃ vattaṃ kātabbaṃ.

182. Those who have entered the rains residence (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭha. 318), having established a fixed duty during the rains, should be told, “Bind the brooms.” If sticks and splints are easily available, each one should bind five or six hand-brooms or two or three brooms with handles. If they are hard to obtain, two or three hand-brooms and one broom with a handle should be bound. Novices should each prepare five torches, and in the dwelling places, requisites should be dyed with an astringent solution. While performing the duties, one should not study, nor cause others to study; recitation should not be done; the going forth should not be given; the higher ordination should not be given; dependence should not be given; nor should one listen to the Dhamma. Such an unrighteous practice should not be done, such as: 'For all these are proliferations. Being free from proliferation, we will practice only the ascetic's duty.' Or: 'Let all undertake the thirteen ascetic practices. Without preparing a bed, let them pass the time standing and walking. Let them take up the vow of silence. Even those who have gone on a seven-day errand should receive the distributable goods.' Rather, it should be done in this way: The Dhamma of learning establishes the threefold good Dhamma. Therefore, carefully study, cause others to study, and do recitation. Without causing disturbance to those dwelling in the meditation hall, sit inside the monastery and study, cause others to study, and do recitation. Make listening to the Dhamma abundant. When giving the going forth, investigate and then give the going forth. Investigate and then give the higher ordination. Investigate and then give dependence. For even one son of good family, having received the going forth and higher ordination, establishes the entire Dispensation. According to your own strength, undertake as many ascetic practices as you are able. During this rains-residence, one should be diligent the entire day and during the first and last watches of the night; energy should be aroused. The great elders of old, too, having cut off all impediments, fulfilled the solitary practice during the rains-residence. Knowing the measure in speech, it is proper to give a talk on the ten topics, the ten kinds of foulness, the ten recollections, and the thirty-eight meditation subjects. It is proper to perform the duties for newcomers. It is proper to give a share, after having informed the Sangha, to those who have gone on a seven-day errand. Such a practice should be undertaken.

Apica bhikkhū ovaditabbā “viggāhikapisuṇapharusavacanāni mā vadatha, divase divase sīlāni āvajjentā caturārakkhaṃ ahāpentā manasikārabahulā viharathā”ti. Dantakaṭṭhakhādanavattaṃ [V 0.0210] ācikkhitabbaṃ, cetiyaṃ vā bodhiṃ vā vandantena gandhamālaṃ vā pūjentena pattaṃ vā thavikāya pakkhipantena na kathetabbaṃ, bhikkhācāravattaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ, antogāme manussehi saddhiṃ paccayasaññuttakathā vā visabhāgakathā vā na kathetabbā, rakkhitindriyehi bhavitabbaṃ, khandhakavattañca sekhiyavattañca pūretabbanti evarūpā bahukāpi niyyānikakathā ācikkhitabbāti.

Furthermore, the bhikkhus should be admonished thus: 'Do not speak contentious, slanderous, or harsh words. Dwell reflecting daily on the moral precepts, not neglecting the four protections, and being abundant in the application of mind.' The duty of chewing tooth-wood should be explained. One should not speak while paying homage to a cetiya or a Bodhi tree, while offering fragrances or garlands, or while putting the bowl into its bag. The duty of the alms-round should be explained. Inside a village, one should not engage in talk connected with requisites or unsuitable talk with people. One should be restrained in the senses. The duties of the Khandhakas and the Sekhiya duties should be fulfilled. Thus, many such teachings leading to liberation should also be explained.

Iti pāḷimuttakavinayavinicchayasaṅgahe

Thus in the Collection of Vinaya Decisions Independent of the Pāḷi Canon,

Vassūpanāyikavinicchayakathā samattā.

The Discussion on the Determination of Entering the Rains-Residence is concluded.

27. Upajjhāyādivattavinicchayakathā

27. The Discussion on the Determination of Duties Regarding Preceptors and Others

183. Vattanti [M 0.0223][V 0.0211] ettha pana vattaṃ nāmetaṃ upajjhāyavattaṃ ācariyavattaṃ āgantukavattaṃ āvāsikavattaṃ gamikavattaṃ bhattaggavattaṃ piṇḍacārikavattaṃ āraññikavattaṃ senāsanavattaṃ jantāgharavattaṃ vaccakuṭivattanti bahuvidhaṃ. Tattha upajjhāyavattaṃ tāva evaṃ veditabbaṃ – saddhivihārikena kālasseva uṭṭhāya upāhanā omuñcitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā upajjhāyassa dantakaṭṭhaṃ dātabbaṃ, mukhodakaṃ dātabbaṃ. Tattha dantakaṭṭhaṃ dentena mahantaṃ majjhimaṃ khuddakanti tīṇi dantakaṭṭhāni upanetvā ito yaṃ tīṇi divasāni gaṇhāti, catutthadivasato paṭṭhāya tādisameva dātabbaṃ. Sace aniyamaṃ katvā yaṃ vā taṃ vā gaṇhāti, atha yādisaṃ labhati, tādisaṃ dātabbaṃ. Mukhodakaṃ dentenapi sītañca uṇhañca udakaṃ upanetvā tato yaṃ tīṇi divasāni vaḷañjeti. Catutthadivasato paṭṭhāya tādisameva mukhadhovanodakaṃ dātabbaṃ. Sace duvidhampi vaḷañjeti, duvidhampi upanetabbaṃ. Udakaṃ mukhadhovanaṭṭhāne ṭhapetvā vaccakuṭito paṭṭhāya sammajjitabbaṃ. There vaccakuṭigate pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ, evaṃ pariveṇaṃ asuññaṃ hoti. There vaccakuṭito anikkhanteyeva āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Sarīrakiccaṃ katvā āgantvā tasmiṃ nisinnassa sace yāgu hoti, bhājanaṃ dhovitvā yāgu upanāmetabbā, yāguṃ pivitassa udakaṃ datvā bhājanaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Upajjhāyamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti kenaci kacavarena saṃkiṇṇo, so deso sammajjitabbo. Sace pana añño kacavaro natthi, udakaphusitāneva honti, hatthena pamajjitabbo.

183. Here, however, the duties are of many kinds, namely: the duty toward the preceptor, the duty toward the teacher, the duty toward a visiting monk, the duty toward a resident monk, the duty toward a traveling monk, the duty at the meal hall, the duty of an alms-goer, the duty of a forest-dweller, the duty regarding lodgings, the duty regarding the hot-bath room, and the duty regarding the toilet. Among these, the duty toward the preceptor should be understood thus: A student should rise early in the morning, remove his sandals, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, and offer the preceptor a tooth-cleaner and water for washing the face. Regarding the tooth-cleaner: having brought three tooth-cleaners—large, medium, and small—whichever he takes for three days, starting from the fourth day, the same kind should be given. If he takes one indiscriminately, then whatever kind is available should be given. Regarding the water for washing the face: having brought both cold and hot water, whichever he uses for three days, starting from the fourth day, the same kind of water for washing the face should be given. If he uses both kinds, both kinds should be brought. Having placed the water in the place for washing the face, the area should be swept starting from the toilet. When the elder has gone to the toilet, the precinct should be swept; in this way, the precinct is not left unattended. Before he has even come out from the toilet, a seat should be prepared. After he has attended to his bodily needs, returned, and sat down, if there is rice-gruel, the bowl should be washed and the rice-gruel offered. After he has drunk the rice-gruel, water should be given, the bowl received, and holding it low, it should be washed well without making a clattering sound, and put away. When the preceptor rises, the seat should be removed. If that area is messy, scattered with any rubbish, it should be swept. If, however, there is no other rubbish and there are only water splashes, they should be wiped with the hand.

Sace upajjhāyo gāmaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, kāyabandhanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo dātabbā, dhovitvā patto saudako dātabbo. Sace upajjhāyo pacchāsamaṇaṃ ākaṅkhati, timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentena parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ bandhitvā saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo pārupitvā gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā dhovitvā pattaṃ gahetvā upajjhāyassa pacchāsamaṇena hotabbaṃ, nātidūre gantabbaṃ, nāccāsanne gantabbaṃ. Ettha pana sace upajjhāyaṃ nivattitvā olokentaṃ ekena vā dvīhi vā padavītihārehi sampāpuṇāti, ettāvatā nātidūre nāccāsanne gato hotīti veditabbaṃ. Sace [M 0.0224] upajjhāyena bhikkhācāre yāguyā vā bhatte vā laddhe patto uṇho vā bhāriko vā hoti, attano [V 0.0212] pattaṃ tassa datvā so patto gahetabbo, na upajjhāyassa bhaṇamānassa antarantarā kathā opātetabbā. Ito paṭṭhāya pana yattha yattha na-kārena paṭisedho karīyati, sabbattha dukkaṭāpatti veditabbā. Upajjhāyo āpattisāmantā bhaṇamāno nivāretabbo. Nivārentena ca “bhante, īdisaṃ nāma vattuṃ vaṭṭati, āpatti na hotī”ti evaṃ pucchantena viya vāretabbo, “vāressāmī”ti pana katvā “mahallaka, mā evaṃ bhaṇā”ti na vattabbo.

If the preceptor wishes to enter the village, the lower robe for wearing on alms-round should be given, the lower robe for wearing in the monastery should be received, the belt should be given, the upper robes, having been folded, should be given, and the bowl, having been washed, should be given with water. If the preceptor desires an attendant monk, one should cover the three circles, wear the lower robe evenly all around, fasten the belt, wear the upper robes folded, fasten the clasp, wash the bowl, take it, and become the preceptor’s attendant monk. One should not go too far away nor too close. Here, if the preceptor turns back and looks, and one reaches him within one or two steps, it should be understood that one has gone neither too far nor too close. If during the alms-round the preceptor receives gruel or food and the bowl becomes hot or heavy, one should give one’s own bowl to him and take that bowl. One should not interrupt the preceptor while he is speaking. From this point on, wherever a prohibition is made by the particle 'na', an offense of wrong-doing should be understood in every case. A preceptor who is speaking in a way that borders on an offense should be stopped. And when stopping him, he should be stopped as if asking, 'Venerable sir, is it proper to say such a thing? Does an offense not occur?' But one should not, having resolved, 'I will stop him,' say, 'Elder, do not speak thus.'

Sace āsanne gāmo hoti, vihāre vā gilāno bhikkhu hoti, gāmato paṭhamataraṃ āgantabbaṃ. Sace dūre gāmo hoti, upajjhāyena saddhiṃ āgacchantopi natthi, teneva saddhiṃ gāmato nikkhamitvā cīvarena pattaṃ veṭhetvā antarāmaggato paṭhamataraṃ āgantabbaṃ. Evaṃ paṭhamataraṃ āgatena āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Sace cīvaraṃ sedaggahitaṃ hoti, muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbaṃ, na ca uṇhe cīvaraṃ nidahitabbaṃ, cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharantena ca caturaṅgulaṃ kaṇṇaṃ ussāretvā cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ. Kiṃkāraṇā? Mā majjhe bhaṅgo ahosīti. Samaṃ katvā saṅgharitassa hi majjhe bhaṅgo hoti, tato niccaṃ bhijjamānaṃ dubbalaṃ hoti, taṃ nivāraṇatthametaṃ vuttaṃ. Tasmā yathā ajja bhaṅgaṭṭhāneyeva sve na bhijjissati, tathā divase divase caturaṅgulaṃ ussāretvā saṅgharitabbaṃ, obhoge kāyabandhanaṃ kātabbaṃ.

If the village is nearby, or if a monk is sick in the monastery, one should return from the village earlier. If the village is far away, and there is no one coming with the preceptor, having departed from the village together with him and having wrapped the bowl with the robe, one should come back earlier from on the way. Having returned earlier, a seat should be prepared; foot-water, a footstool, and a foot-rubbing tile should be placed nearby. Having gone out to meet him, the bowl and robe should be received. A fresh under-robe should be given, and the worn under-robe should be received. If the robe is damp with sweat, it should be aired in the sun for a moment, but the robe should not be left in the sun for a long time. The robe should be folded. And when folding the robe, one should fold it having shifted the edge by four finger-widths. For what reason? So that a crease may not form in the middle. For of a robe folded evenly, a crease occurs in the middle; from being constantly creased there, it becomes weak. This was said to prevent that. Therefore, so that it will not be creased tomorrow in the very same place it was creased today, it should be folded each day by shifting it four finger-widths. The waistband should be placed in the fold.

Sace piṇḍapāto hoti, upajjhāyo ca bhuñjitukāmo hoti, udakaṃ datvā piṇḍapāto upanāmetabbo, upajjhāyo pānīyena pucchitabbo. Pucchantena ca tikkhattuṃ “pānīyaṃ, bhante, āharīyatū”ti pānīyena pucchitabbo. Sace kālo atthi, upajjhāye bhutte sayaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Sace upakaṭṭho kālo, pānīyaṃ upajjhāyassa santike ṭhapetvā sayampi bhuñjitabbaṃ. Bhuttāvissa udakaṃ datvā pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā vodakaṃ katvā muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbo, na ca uṇhe patto nidahitabbo, pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena [M 0.0225] ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo, na ca taṭṭikacammakhaṇḍādīhi anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Sace pana kāḷavaṇṇakatā vā sudhābaddhā vā bhūmi hoti nirajamattikā, tathārūpāya bhūmiyā ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭati, dhotavālikāyapi ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭati, paṃsurajasakkharādīsu na vaṭṭati. Tatra pana paṇṇaṃ vā ādhārakaṃ vā ṭhapetvā tatra nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā [V 0.0213] pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Idañca cīvaravaṃsādīnaṃ heṭṭhā hatthaṃ pavesetvā abhimukhena hatthena saṇikaṃ nikkhipanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Ante pana gahetvā bhogena cīvaravaṃsādīnaṃ upari khipantassa bhittiyaṃ bhogo paṭihaññati, tasmā tathā na kātabbaṃ. Upajjhāyamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

If there is almsfood and the preceptor wishes to eat, after giving water, the almsfood should be offered. The preceptor should be asked about drinking water. When asking, one should inquire three times: "Venerable sir, may drinking water be brought?" If there is time, after the preceptor has eaten, one should eat oneself. If the time is close to midday, having placed drinking water near the preceptor, one should also eat. After he has eaten, water should be given, the bowl received, lowered, and carefully washed without scraping it. After making it free of water, it should be dried in the sun for a moment, but the bowl should not be left in the heat. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting away the bowl, one should take the bowl with one hand, and with the other hand feel underneath the bed or underneath the seat, and then place the bowl down. The bowl should not be placed on the ground without a covering such as a mat or a piece of leather. If, however, the ground is colored black, plastered, or is earth free of dust, it is permissible to place it on such ground. It is also permissible to place it on washed sand, but not on soil, dust, gravel, or the like. In such a place, however, one should first place a leaf or a bowl-stand, and place the bowl on that. When putting away the robe, one should take the robe with one hand, and with the other hand wipe the robe-rack or robe-cord, then making a fold with the far end towards this side, place the robe down. And this is said for the purpose of placing it gently: inserting the hand underneath the robe-rack or the like, one should place it with the hand facing forward. But for one who, taking it by the end, throws the fold over the robe-rack or the like, the fold may strike the wall; therefore, it should not be done in that way. When the preceptor has risen, the seat should be removed. The foot-water, footstool, and foot-wiping cloth should be put away. If that place is dirty, that place should be swept.

Sace upajjhāyo nahāyitukāmo hoti, nahānaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace sītena attho hoti, sītaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace uṇhena attho hoti, uṇhaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ.

If the preceptor wishes to bathe, bathing water should be prepared. If cold water is needed, cold water should be prepared. If hot water is needed, hot water should be prepared.

Sace upajjhāyo jantāgharaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, cuṇṇaṃ sannetabbaṃ, mattikā temetabbā. Jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya upajjhāyassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito gantvā jantāgharapīṭhaṃ datvā cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā ekamante niddhūmaṭṭhāne ṭhapetabbaṃ, cuṇṇaṃ dātabbaṃ, mattikā dātabbā. Sace ussahati, jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ, pavisantena mattikāya mukhaṃ makkhetvā purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Na there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ, na navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā, jantāghare upajjhāyassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Jantāghare parikammaṃ nāma aṅgāramattikāuṇhodakadānādikaṃ sabbakiccaṃ. Jantāgharā nikkhamantena jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharā nikkhamitabbaṃ.

If the preceptor wishes to enter the steam-room, powder should be mixed with water, and clay should be moistened. Taking the steam-room seat, one should follow closely behind the preceptor, give the steam-room seat, receive his robe, and place it aside in a smokeless place. The powder should be given, and the clay should be given. If one is able, one should enter the steam-room. When entering, one should smear the face with clay, cover oneself front and back with a bathing cloth, and then enter the steam-room. One should not sit encroaching upon the senior monks, nor should junior monks be obstructed from their seats. In the steam-room, service should be rendered to the preceptor. Service in the steam-room means all duties such as providing embers, clay, hot water, and so on. When leaving the steam-room, one should take the steam-room seat, cover oneself front and back with a bathing cloth, and then leave the steam-room.

Udakepi upajjhāyassa aṅgapaccaṅgaghaṃsanādikaṃ parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ, nahātena paṭhamataraṃ uttaritvā attano gattaṃ vodakaṃ katvā nivāsetvā upajjhāyassa gattato udakaṃ pamajjitabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saṅghāṭi dātabbā[M 0.0226], jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, upajjhāyo pānīyena pucchitabbo. Jantāghare hi uṇhasantāpena pipāsā hoti. Sace uddisāpetukāmo hoti, uddisitabbo. Sace paripucchitukāmo hoti, paripucchitabbo.

Even in the water, service should be rendered to the preceptor, such as rubbing his major and minor limbs. Having bathed, one should come out before him, make one's own body free of water, put on one's lower robe, and then wipe the water from the preceptor's body. The lower robe should be given; the outer robe should be given. Taking the steam-room seat, one should return before him and prepare a seat. Foot-water, a footstool, and a foot-wiper should be placed nearby. The preceptor should be asked if he requires drinking water. For in the steam-room, thirst arises from the oppressive heat. If he wishes to have the Pāḷi recited, it should be recited. If he wishes to have the commentary explained, it should be explained.

Yasmiṃ vihāre upajjhāyo viharati, sace so vihāro uklāpo hoti, sace ussahati, kenaci gelaññena anabhibhūto hoti, sodhetabbo. Agilānena hi saddhivihārikena saṭṭhivassenapi sabbaṃ upajjhāyavattaṃ kātabbaṃ, anādarena akarontassa vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ, na-kārapaṭisaṃyuttesu pana padesu gilānassapi paṭikkhittakiriyaṃ karontassa dukkaṭameva. Vihāraṃ sodhentena paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ nīharitvā [V 0.0214] ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, bhisibimbohanaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, mañco nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ apaṭighaṃsantena asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapīṭhaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo, pīṭhaṃ nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ apaṭighaṃsantena asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapīṭhaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, mañcapaṭipādakā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbā, kheḷamallako nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo, apassenaphalakaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Bhūmattharaṇaṃ yathāpaññattaṃ sallakkhetvā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace vihāre santānakaṃ hoti, ullokā paṭhamaṃ ohāretabbaṃ, ālokasandhikaṇṇabhāgā pamajjitabbā. Sace gerukaparikammakatā bhitti kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace kāḷavaṇṇakatā bhūmi kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace akatā hoti bhūmi, udakena paripphositvā paripphositvā sammajjitabbā “mā vihāro rajena uhaññī”ti, saṅkāraṃ vicinitvā ekamantaṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

In the dwelling where the preceptor resides, if that dwelling is dirty, and if he is able—not overcome by any illness—it should be cleaned. Indeed, by a co-resident pupil who is not ill, even one who is sixty years of age, all duties toward the preceptor must be performed. If one neglects to do so out of disrespect, there is an offense of wrong-doing for the breach of duty. However, in matters connected with prohibitions, even for one who is ill, performing a forbidden action incurs an offense of wrong-doing. When cleaning the dwelling, first the bowl and robe should be taken out and placed to one side; the sitting mat and covering should be taken out and placed to one side; the cushion and pillow should be taken out and placed to one side. The bed should be lowered and taken out carefully, without scraping or bumping the door-leaf and door-post, and placed to one side. The stool should be lowered and taken out carefully, without scraping or bumping the door-leaf and door-post, and placed to one side. The legs of the bed should be taken out and placed to one side; the spittoon should be taken out and placed to one side; the leaning board should be taken out and placed to one side. Having noted how the floor covering was laid out, it should be taken out and placed to one side. If there are cobwebs in the dwelling, they should be removed, starting from the ceiling. The window joints and corner portions should be wiped. If a wall finished with red ochre is moldy, a rag should be moistened, wrung out, and used to wipe it. If a floor finished with a black color is moldy, a rag should be moistened, wrung out, and used to wipe it. If the floor is unfinished, it should be sprinkled with water again and again and swept, with the thought, “May the dwelling not be filled with dust.” The rubbish should be gathered and discarded to one side.

Bhūmattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā abhiharitvā yathā paṭhamaṃ paññattaṃ ahosi, tatheva paññapetabbaṃ. Etadatthameva hi “yathāpaññattaṃ sallakkhetvā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Sace pana paṭhamaṃ ajānantena kenaci paññattaṃ ahosi, samantato bhittiṃ dvaṅgulamattena vā tivaṅgulamattena vā mocetvā paññapetabbaṃ. Idañhettha paññāpanavattaṃ [M 0.0227] – sace kaṭasārako hoti atimahanto ca, chinditvā koṭiṃ nivattetvā bandhitvā paññapetabbo. Sace koṭiṃ nivattetvā bandhituṃ na jānāti, na chinditabbo. Mañcapaṭipādakā otāpetvā pamajjitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbā, mañco otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ apaṭighaṃsantena asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapīṭhaṃ atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbo, pīṭhaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ apaṭighaṃsantena asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapīṭhaṃ atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, bhisibimbohanaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, kheḷamallako otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbo, apassenaphalakaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbaṃ. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo, na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ, orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ.

Having aired the ground covering, cleaned it, shaken it out, and brought it back, it should be arranged just as it was originally arranged. For this very purpose, it was said, 'After observing how it was arranged, it should be taken out and set aside.' However, if it was initially arranged by someone unaware, it should be arranged leaving a space of two or three finger-widths from the wall all around. This is the procedure for arranging it: if the mat is a kaṭasāra and is too large, it should be cut, the edge turned back, tied, and then arranged. If one does not know how to turn back and tie the edge, it should not be cut. The bed legs should be aired, wiped, and placed back in their original positions. The bed should be aired, cleaned, shaken out, lowered carefully without scraping or bumping, carried past the door-leaf and door-post, and arranged as originally arranged. The stool should be aired, cleaned, shaken out, lowered carefully without scraping or bumping, carried past the door-leaf and door-post, and arranged as originally arranged. The cushion and pillow should be aired, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and arranged as originally arranged. The sitting mat and covering should be aired, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and arranged as originally arranged. The spittoon should be aired, wiped, brought back, and placed in its original position. The leaning board should be aired, wiped, brought back, and placed in its original position. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting away the bowl, one should hold the bowl with one hand, feel under the bed or under the stool with the other hand, and then place the bowl. The bowl should not be placed on the ground without a covering. When putting away the robe, one should hold the robe with one hand, wipe the robe-pole or robe-rope with the other hand, and place the robe with its end on the far side and its fold on the near side.

Sace [V 0.0215] puratthimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, puratthimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace pacchimā, uttarā, dakkhiṇā sarajā vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace sītakālo hoti, divā vātapānā vivaritabbā, rattiṃ thaketabbā. Sace uṇhakālo hoti, divā thaketabbā, rattiṃ vivaritabbā.

If dusty winds blow from the east, the eastern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the west, north, or south, the southern windows should be closed. If it is the cold season, the windows should be opened during the day and closed at night. If it is the hot season, they should be closed during the day and opened at night.

Sace uklāpaṃ hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo, upaṭṭhānasālā sammajjitabbā, aggisālā sammajjitabbā, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhapetabbaṃ, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ.

If it is untidy, the monastic cell should be swept, the storeroom should be swept, the service hall should be swept, the fire-hall should be swept, the latrine should be swept, drinking water and water for use should be set up, and water should be poured into the rinsing pot.

Sace upajjhāyassa anabhirati uppannā hoti, saddhivihārikena aññattha netabbo, añño vā bhikkhu vattabbo “theraṃ gahetvā aññattha gacchā”ti, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace upajjhāyassa kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, saddhivihārikena vinodetabbaṃ, aññena vā vinodāpetabbaṃ dhammakathā [M 0.0228] vāssa kātabbā. Sace upajjhāyassa diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti, saddhivihārikena vissajjetabbaṃ, añño vā vattabbo “theraṃ diṭṭhigataṃ vissajjāpehī”ti, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace upajjhāyo garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti parivāsāraho, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ, parivāsadānatthaṃ so so bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā yācitabbo. Sace attanā paṭibalo hoti, attanāva dātabbo. No ce paṭibalo hoti, aññena dāpetabbo. Sace upajjhāyo mūlāyapaṭikassanāraho hoti mānattāraho abbhānāraho vā, vuttanayeneva ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ. Sace saṅgho upajjhāyassa kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ “kena nu kho upāyena saṅgho upajjhāyassa kammaṃ na kareyya, lahukāya vā pariṇāmeyyā”ti. Saddhivihārikena hi “upajjhāyassa ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kattukāmo saṅgho”ti ñatvā ekamekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā “mā, bhante, amhākaṃ upajjhāyassa kammaṃ karitthā”ti yācitabbā. Sace karontiyeva, “tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā lahukakammaṃ karothā”ti yācitabbā. Sace karontiyeva, atha upajjhāyo “sammā vattatha, bhante”ti yācitabbo. Iti taṃ sammā vattāpetvā “paṭippassambhetha, bhante, kamma”nti bhikkhū yācitabbā.

If dissatisfaction arises in the preceptor, the co-resident should lead him elsewhere, or another monk should be told, “Take the elder and go elsewhere,” or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If remorse arises in the preceptor, the co-resident should dispel it, or have it dispelled by another, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If a wrong view arises in the preceptor, the co-resident should make him abandon it, or another monk should be told, “Make the elder abandon the wrong view,” or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If the preceptor has committed a grave offense deserving of probation, the co-resident should make an effort for the sake of granting probation; he should approach this and that monk and request it. If he himself is able, he himself should grant it. If he is not able, he should have it granted by another. If the preceptor deserves to be sent back to the beginning, deserves mānatta, or deserves rehabilitation, an effort should be made in the way already stated. If the Saṅgha wishes to carry out an act against the preceptor—be it an act of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—the co-resident should make an effort, thinking: “By what means indeed might the Saṅgha not carry out the act against the preceptor, or change it to a lighter one?” Indeed, the co-resident, having known, “The Saṅgha wishes to carry out an act of suspension against the preceptor,” should approach each and every monk and request: “Venerable Sirs, do not carry out the act against our preceptor.” If they still carry it out, they should be requested: “Carry out a lighter act, such as an act of censure or subordination.” If they still carry it out, then the preceptor should be requested: “Venerable Sir, please conduct yourself properly.” Thus, having made him conduct himself properly, the monks should be requested: “Venerable Sirs, please revoke the act.”

Sace upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ dhovitabbaṃ hoti, saddhivihārikena dhovitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ “kinti nu kho upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ dhoviyethā”ti. Sace upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ kātabbaṃ [V 0.0216] hoti, rajanaṃ vā pacitabbaṃ, cīvaraṃ vā rajetabbaṃ hoti, saddhivihārikena sabbaṃ kātabbaṃ, ussakkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ “kinti nu kho upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ rajiyethā”ti. Cīvaraṃ rajantena sādhukaṃ saṃparivattetvā rajetabbaṃ, na ca acchinne theve pakkamitabbaṃ.

If the preceptor's robe is to be washed, it should be washed by the co-resident, or an effort should be made, thinking, 'How indeed might the preceptor's robe be washed?' If the preceptor's robe is to be made, or dye is to be prepared, or the robe is to be dyed, all this should be done by the co-resident, or an effort should be made, thinking, 'How indeed might the preceptor's robe be dyed?' When dyeing the robe, it should be dyed having carefully turned it over. And one should not depart while the dye is still dripping.

Na upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchā ekaccassa patto dātabbo, na ekaccassa patto paṭiggahetabbo, na ekaccassa cīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ, na ekaccassa cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, na ekaccassa parikkhāro dātabbo, na ekaccassa parikkhāro paṭiggahetabbo, na ekaccassa kesā chedetabbā, na ekaccena kesā chedāpetabbā[M 0.0229], na ekaccassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ, na ekaccena parikammaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ, na ekaccassa veyyāvacco kātabbo, na ekaccena veyyāvacco kārāpetabbo, na ekaccassa pacchāsamaṇena hotabbaṃ, na ekacco pacchāsamaṇo ādātabbo, na ekaccassa piṇḍapāto nīharitabbo, na ekaccena piṇḍapāto nīharāpetabbo, na upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchā gāmo pavisitabbo, piṇḍāya vā aññena vā karaṇīyena pavisitukāmena āpucchitvāva pavisitabbo. Sace upajjhāyo kālasseva vuṭṭhāya dūraṃ bhikkhācāraṃ gantukāmo hoti, “daharā piṇḍāya pavisantū”ti vatvā gantabbaṃ. Avatvā gate pariveṇaṃ gantvā upajjhāyaṃ apassantena gāmaṃ pavisituṃ vaṭṭati. Sace gāmaṃ pavisantopi passati, diṭṭhaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya āpucchituṃyeva vaṭṭati. Na upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchā vāsatthāya vā asubhadassanatthāya vā susānaṃ gantabbaṃ, na disā pakkamitabbā, pakkamitukāmena pana kammaṃ ācikkhitvā yāvatatiyaṃ yācitabbo. Sace anujānāti, sādhu, no ce anujānāti, taṃ nissāya vasato cassa uddeso vā paripucchā vā kammaṭṭhānaṃ vā na sampajjati, upajjhāyo bālo hoti abyatto, kevalaṃ attano santike vasāpetukāmatāya eva gantuṃ na deti, evarūpe nivārentepi gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace upajjhāyo gilāno hoti, yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbo, vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabbaṃ, na katthaci gantabbaṃ. Sace añño bhikkhu upaṭṭhāko atthi, bhesajjaṃ pariyesitvā tassa hatthe datvā “bhante, ayaṃ upaṭṭhahissatī”ti vatvā gantabbaṃ. Idaṃ tāva upajjhāyavattaṃ.

Without asking the preceptor, a bowl should not be given to another, nor a bowl received from another; a robe should not be given to another, nor a robe received from another; requisites should not be given to another, nor requisites received from another; hair should not be cut for another, nor should one have one's hair cut by another; service should not be done for another, nor should one have service done by another; duties should not be done for another, nor should one have duties done by another; one should not be an attendant for another, nor accept another as an attendant; alms-food should not be carried back for another, nor should one have alms-food carried back by another. A village should not be entered without asking the preceptor. When wishing to enter for alms or for some other business, one should enter only after asking. If the preceptor rises early wishing to go far for alms, he should go after saying, "Let the young ones enter for alms." If he goes without saying so, it is allowable for one who has gone to the residence and not seen the preceptor to enter the village. If one sees him even while entering the village, it is proper to ask from the very place where he is seen. Without asking the preceptor, one should not go to a cemetery for the purpose of dwelling or for seeing the repulsive. One should not depart to another region. But one who wishes to depart, having explained the reason, should request up to a third time. If he gives permission, it is good. If he does not give permission, and if for one staying in dependence on him, instruction, questioning, or a meditation subject is not accomplished, and the preceptor is foolish and incompetent, and he does not allow one to go merely out of a desire to have one stay near him—in such a case, it is allowable to go even if he prevents it. If the preceptor is sick, he should be attended on for life; one should wait for his recovery; one should not go anywhere. If there is another monk as an attendant, having searched for medicine and given it into his hand, one may go after saying, "Venerable, this one will attend." This, for now, is the duty to the preceptor.

184. Idameva ca antevāsikena ācariyassa kattabbattā ācariyavattanti vuccati. Nāmamattameva hettha nānaṃ. Tattha yāva cīvararajanaṃ, tāva vatte akariyamāne upajjhāyassa ācariyassa ca parihāni hoti, tasmā taṃ akarontassa nissayamuttakassapi amuttakassapi āpattiyeva, ekaccassa pattadānato paṭṭhāya amuttanissayasseva āpatti. Upajjhāye ācariye vā vattaṃ sādiyante saddhivihārikā antevāsikā ca bahukāpi hontu, sabbesaṃ āpatti. Sace [V 0.0217] upajjhāyo ācariyo vā “mayhaṃ upaṭṭhāko atthi, tumhe attano sajjhāyamanasikārādīsu yogaṃ karothā”ti vadati, saddhivihārikādīnaṃ anāpatti. Upajjhāyo vā ācariyo vā sace sādiyanaṃ vā asādiyanaṃ vā na [M 0.0230] jānāti, bālo hoti, saddhivihārikādayo bahū, tesu eko vattasampanno bhikkhu “upajjhāyassa vā ācariyassa vā kiccaṃ ahaṃ karissāmi, tumhe appossukkā viharathā”ti evañce attano bhāraṃ katvā itare vissajjeti, tassa bhārakaraṇato paṭṭhāya tesaṃ anāpatti. Ettha antevāsikesu pana nissayantevāsikena yāva ācariyaṃ nissāya vasati, tāva sabbaṃ ācariyavattaṃ kātabbaṃ. Pabbajjaupasampadadhammantevāsikehi pana nissayamuttakehipi ādito paṭṭhāya yāva cīvararajanaṃ, tāva vattaṃ kātabbaṃ. Anāpucchitvā pattadānādimhi pana etesaṃ anāpatti.

184. Furthermore, this is called the 'duties toward a teacher' (ācariyavatta) because it is what should be done by a pupil toward a teacher. Here, only the name differs. In this regard, if the duties up to robe-dyeing are not performed, both the preceptor and the teacher suffer a loss. Therefore, for one who does not perform them, there is indeed an offense, whether one is released from dependence or not. According to some, for one who is not released from dependence, there is an offense beginning from the giving of the bowl. If the preceptor or teacher delights in the performance of duties, even if there are many co-residents and pupils, there is an offense for all of them. If the preceptor or teacher says, 'I have an attendant; you should apply yourselves to your own recitation, reflection, and so on,' there is no offense for the co-residents and others. If the preceptor or teacher does not know whether the service is delighted in or not, he is a fool. If there are many co-residents and others, and one monk among them who is accomplished in the duties takes it upon himself as his own responsibility and releases the others, saying, 'I will perform the duties for the preceptor or the teacher; you may dwell without concern,' then from the moment he takes on this responsibility, there is no offense for the others. Here, among the pupils, a pupil under dependence must perform all the duties toward a teacher for as long as he dwells depending on the teacher. However, pupils by way of going forth, higher ordination, and the Dhamma, even if released from dependence, must perform the duties from the beginning up to the dyeing of robes. But for these pupils, there is no offense in giving the bowl and so on without asking.

Etesu pabbajjantevāsiko ca upasampadantevāsiko ca ācariyassa yāvajīvaṃ bhārā. Nissayantevāsiko ca dhammantevāsiko ca yāva samīpe vasanti, tāva ācariyupajjhāyehipi antevāsikasaddhivihārikā saṅgahetabbā anuggahetabbā uddesena paripucchāya ovādena anusāsaniyā. Sace antevāsikasaddhivihārikānaṃ patto vā cīvaraṃ vā añño vā koci parikkhāro natthi, attano atirekapattacīvaraṃ atirekaparikkhāro vā atthi, dātabbaṃ. No ce, dhammiyena nayena pariyesanatthāya ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ. Sace antevāsikasaddhivihārikā gilānā honti, upajjhāyavatte vuttanayena dantakaṭṭhadānaṃ ādiṃ katvā ācamanakumbhiyā udakasiñcanapariyosānaṃ sabbaṃ vattaṃ kātabbameva, akarontānaṃ āpatti. Tasmā ācariyupajjhāyehipi antevāsikasaddhivihārikesu sammā vattitabbaṃ. Ācariyupajjhāyādīsu hi yo yo na sammā vattati, tassa tassa āpatti. Upajjhāyādivattakathā.

Among these pupils, the pupil for the going forth and the pupil for the higher ordination are lifelong responsibilities of the teacher. The pupil who lives in dependence and the pupil who studies the Dhamma, for as long as they live in the teacher's presence, should be supported and assisted by the teachers and preceptors by means of recitation, questioning, admonition, and repeated instruction. If the pupils or co-residents have no bowl, robe, or any other requisite, and one has an extra bowl, robe, or extra requisite, it should be given. If not, effort should be made to seek it by a righteous method. If the pupils or co-residents are sick, all duties—beginning with the giving of a tooth-stick and ending with the pouring of water in the rinsing pot—must be performed according to the method described in the duties towards a preceptor. For those not doing so, there is an offense. Therefore, teachers and preceptors should also act properly towards their pupils and co-residents. Indeed, for whatever bhikkhu does not act properly towards teachers, preceptors, and so on, for that very bhikkhu there is an offense. The discourse on the duties towards preceptors and so on is finished.

185. Idāni āgantukavattādīni veditabbāni. Āgantukena bhikkhunā upacārasīmāsamīpaṃ gantvā upāhanā omuñcitvā nīcaṃ katvā papphoṭetvā upāhanadaṇḍakena gahetvā chattaṃ upanāmetvā sīsaṃ vivaritvā sīse cīvaraṃ khandhe karitvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena ārāmo pavisitabbo, ārāmaṃ pavisantena sallakkhetabbaṃ “kattha āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatantī”ti. Yattha āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti upaṭṭhānasālāya vā maṇḍape vā rukkhamūle vā, tattha gantvā ekamantaṃ patto nikkhipitabbo, ekamantaṃ cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, patirūpaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā nisīditabbaṃ, pānīyaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, paribhojanīyaṃ pucchitabbaṃ “katamaṃ pānīyaṃ, katamaṃ paribhojanīya”nti. Sace [M 0.0231] pānīyena attho hoti, pānīyaṃ gahetvā pātabbaṃ. Sace paribhojanīyena attho hoti, paribhojanīyaṃ gahetvā pādā dhovitabbā. Pāde dhovantena ekena [V 0.0218] hatthena udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ, ekena hatthena pādā dhovitabbā, na teneva hatthena udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ, na teneva hatthena pādā dhovitabbā, upāhanapuñchanacoḷakaṃ puñchitvā upāhanā puñchitabbā, upāhanā puñchantena paṭhamaṃ sukkhena coḷakena puñchitabbā, pacchā allena, upāhanapuñchanacoḷakaṃ dhovitvā ekamantaṃ pattharitabbaṃ.

185. Now, the duties for incoming monks, and so forth, should be known. An incoming monk, having gone near the monastery precincts, should take off his sandals, place them low, shake them, take them with a small sandal-hooking staff, lower his umbrella, uncover his head, place the robe from his head onto his shoulder, and should enter the monastery properly and unhurriedly. Upon entering the monastery, he should observe: “Where do the resident monks assemble?” Wherever the resident monks assemble—whether in an attendance hall, a pavilion, or at the foot of a tree—he should go there, place his bowl to one side, place his robe to one side, take a suitable seat, and sit down. He should ask about the drinking water and ask about the water for use, saying: “Which is drinking water, and which is water for use?” If there is a need for drinking water, he should take it and drink. If there is a need for water for use, he should take it and wash his feet. When washing the feet, water should be poured with one hand, and the feet should be washed with the other. Water should not be poured with that same hand, nor should the feet be washed with that same hand. Having asked for the sandal-wiping cloth, the sandals should be wiped. When wiping the sandals, they should first be wiped with a dry cloth, and afterwards with a wet one. The sandal-wiping cloth should be washed and spread out in a place to one side.

Sace āvāsiko bhikkhu vuḍḍho hoti, abhivādetabbo. Sace navako hoti, abhivādāpetabbo. Senāsanaṃ pucchitabbaṃ “katamaṃ me senāsanaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti, ajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ vā anajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ vā pucchitabbaṃ, “gocaragāmo āsanne, udāhu dūre, kālasseva piṇḍāya caritabbaṃ, udāhu divā”ti evaṃ bhikkhācāro pucchitabbo, agocaro pucchitabbo, gocaro pucchitabbo. Agocaro nāma micchādiṭṭhikānaṃ gāmo paricchinnabhikkho vā gāmo, yattha ekassa vā dvinnaṃ vā bhikkhā dīyati, sekkhasammahāni kulāni pucchitabbāni, vaccaṭṭhānaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, passāvaṭṭhānaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, “kiṃ imissā pokkharaṇiyā pānīyaṃyeva pivanti, nahānādiparibhogampi karontī”ti evaṃ pānīyañceva paribhojanīyañca pucchitabbaṃ, kattaradaṇḍo pucchitabbo, saṅghassa katikasaṇṭhānaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, kesuci ṭhānesu vāḷamigā vā amanussā vā honti, tasmā “kaṃ kālaṃ pavisitabbaṃ, kaṃ kālaṃ nikkhamitabba”nti pucchitabbaṃ. Sace vihāro anajjhāvuṭṭho hoti, kavāṭaṃ ākoṭetvā muhuttaṃ āgametvā ghaṭikaṃ ugghāṭetvā kavāṭaṃ paṇāmetvā bahi ṭhitena nilloketabbo.

If the resident monk is senior, he should be venerated. If he is junior, he should be made to pay respect. The lodging should be asked about: “Which lodging is for me?” Whether it has been previously occupied or not should be asked about. The alms-round should be asked about thus: “Is the alms-resort village near, or is it far? Should one go for alms early, or during the day?” The unsuitable alms-resort should be asked about; the suitable alms-resort should be asked about. An unsuitable alms-resort, namely, is a village of those with wrong views or a village with limited alms, where alms are given to only one or two monks. Families designated for learners should be asked about. The place for defecation should be asked about. The place for urination should be asked about. Both the drinking water and the water for use should be asked about thus: “Do they only drink the water from this pond, or do they also use it for bathing and other purposes?” The walking stick should be asked about. The Saṅgha’s established agreement should be asked about. In some places, there are beasts of prey or non-human beings; therefore, it should be asked: “At what time should one enter, and at what time should one leave?” If the monastery has not been occupied, one should knock on the door, wait a moment, open the bolt, push aside the door, and look inside while standing outside.

Sace so vihāro uklāpo hoti, mañce vā mañco āropito hoti, pīṭhe vā pīṭhaṃ āropitaṃ hoti, senāsanaṃ upari puñjīkataṃ hoti, sace sakkoti, sabbo vihāro sodhetabbo, asakkontena attano vasanokāso jaggitabbo. Sabbaṃ sodhetuṃ sakkontena pana upajjhāyavatte vuttanayena bhūmattharaṇamañcapīṭhādīni bahi nīharitvā vihāraṃ sodhetvā puna atiharitvā yathāṭhāne paññapetabbāni.

If that monastery is untidy, if a bed is placed on a bed, or a stool on a stool, or the lodging is piled up, if one is able, the entire monastery should be cleaned. If unable, one's own living space should be tended to. However, by one who is able to clean everything, following the method described in the section on the duties towards a preceptor, the floor coverings, beds, stools, and so on, should be taken outside, the monastery cleaned, then brought back in again, and arranged in their proper places.

Sace [M 0.0232] puratthimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, puratthimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace pacchimā, uttarā, dakkhiṇā sarajā vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace sītakālo hoti, divā vātapānā vivaritabbā, rattiṃ thaketabbā. Sace uṇhakālo hoti, divā thaketabbā, rattiṃ vivaritabbā.

If dusty winds blow from the east, the eastern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the west, north, or south, the southern windows should be closed. If it is the cold season, the windows should be opened during the day and closed at night. If it is the hot season, the windows should be closed during the day and opened at night.

Sace uklāpaṃ hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo, upaṭṭhānasālā sammajjitabbā[V 0.0219], aggisālā sammajjitabbā, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ. Idaṃ āgantukavattaṃ.

If it is untidy, the monastery compound should be swept, the storeroom should be swept, the service hall should be swept, the fire-hall should be swept, and the toilet should be swept. Drinking water and water for general use should be set up, and water should be poured into the rinsing pot. These are the duties for a newcomer.

186. Āvāsikavatte āvāsikena bhikkhunā āgantukaṃ bhikkhuṃ vuḍḍhataraṃ disvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, pānīyena pucchitabbo, pucchantena pana sakiṃ ānītaṃ pānīyaṃ sabbaṃ pivati, “puna ānemī”ti pucchitabboyeva. Bījanenapi bījitabbo, bījantena sakiṃ pādapiṭṭhiyaṃ bījitvā sakiṃ majjhe, sakiṃ sīse bījitabbo, “alaṃ hotū”ti vuttena mandataraṃ bījitabbaṃ, puna “ala”nti vuttena tato mandataraṃ bījitabbaṃ, tatiyavāraṃ vuttena bījanī ṭhapetabbā, pādāpissa dhovitabbā. Sace attano telaṃ atthi, telena makkhetabbā. No ce atthi, tassa santakena makkhetabbā. Sace ussahati, upāhanā puñchitabbā. Upāhanā puñchantena paṭhamaṃ sukkhena coḷena puñchitabbā, pacchā allena, upāhanapuñchanacoḷakaṃ dhovitvā ekamantaṃ vissajjetabbaṃ.

186. In the duties of a resident, a resident monk, upon seeing a visiting monk who is senior, should prepare a seat. Foot-water, a footstool, and a foot-wiper should be placed nearby. Having gone out to meet him, his bowl and robe should be received. He should be asked concerning drinking water. If he drinks all the water that was brought, he should be asked, 'Shall I bring more?' He should also be fanned with a fan. When fanning, having fanned once on the top of the feet, he should fan once at the middle of the body and once at the head. When it is said, 'Let that be enough,' one should fan more gently. When 'enough' is said again, one should fan even more gently than that. When it is said for the third time, the fan should be put down. His feet should also be washed. If one has one's own oil, they should be anointed with oil. If not, they should be anointed with the visitor's own. If one is able, the sandals should be wiped. When wiping the sandals, they should first be wiped with a dry cloth, and afterwards with a damp one. The cloth for wiping the sandals should be washed and spread out in a secluded place.

Āgantuko bhikkhu abhivādetabbo, senāsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ “etaṃ senāsanaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti. Ajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ vā anajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ vā ācikkhitabbaṃ, gocaro ācikkhitabbo, agocaro ācikkhitabbo, sekkhasammatāni kulāni ācikkhitabbāni, vaccaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ, passāvaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ, pānīyaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ, paribhojanīyaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ, kattaradaṇḍo ācikkhitabbo, saṅghassa katikasaṇṭhānaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ “imaṃ kālaṃ pavisitabbaṃ, imaṃ kālaṃ nikkhamitabba”nti.

A visiting bhikkhu should be venerated, and a lodging should be prepared, saying, “This lodging is for you.” Whether it is occupied or unoccupied should be pointed out. The suitable alms-resort should be pointed out; the unsuitable alms-resort should be pointed out. Families designated for learners should be pointed out. The place for defecation should be pointed out. The place for urination should be pointed out. Drinking water should be pointed out. Water for use should be pointed out. The walking stick should be pointed out. The Saṅgha's established agreement should be explained: “One should enter at this time; one should depart at this time.”

Sace āgantuko navako hoti, nisinnakeneva ācikkhitabbaṃ “atra pattaṃ nikkhipāhi, atra cīvaraṃ nikkhipāhi, idaṃ āsanaṃ, nisīdāhī”ti. Pānīyaṃ [M 0.0233] ācikkhitabbaṃ, paribhojanīyaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ, upāhanapuñchanacoḷakaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ, āgantuko bhikkhu abhivādāpetabbo, senāsanādīnipi nisinneneva ācikkhitabbāni. Vuḍḍhatare pana āgate āsanaṃ paññapetabbanti evamādi sabbaṃ cīvarakammaṃ vā navakammaṃ vā ṭhapetvāpi kātabbaṃ. Cetiyaṅgaṇaṃ sammajjantena sammuñjaniṃ nikkhipitvā tassa vattaṃ kātuṃ ārabhitabbaṃ. Paṇḍito hi āgantuko “sammajjāhi tāva cetiyaṅgaṇa”nti vakkhati. Gilānassa bhesajjaṃ karontena pana sace nātiāturo gilāno hoti, bhesajjaṃ akatvā vattameva [V 0.0220] kātabbaṃ, mahāgilānassa pana bhesajjameva kātabbaṃ. Paṇḍito hi āgantuko “karohi tāva bhesajja”nti vakkhati. Idaṃ āvāsikavattaṃ.

If the visiting bhikkhu is a junior, he should be instructed while seated: “Place the bowl here, place the robe here, this is the seat, sit down.” Drinking water should be pointed out, water for use should be pointed out, and the sandal-wiping cloth should be pointed out. The visiting bhikkhu should be made to pay respect; the lodging and other things should also be pointed out while seated. But when a more senior bhikkhu arrives, all duties, such as preparing a seat and so forth, should be done, even setting aside robe-work or new construction work. One who is sweeping the cetiya-courtyard should put down the broom and begin to perform the duties towards him. For a wise visiting bhikkhu will say, “First, sweep the cetiya-courtyard.” But by one preparing medicine for a sick person, if the sick person is not gravely ill, the duty itself should be done without preparing the medicine. For one who is gravely ill, however, the medicine itself should be prepared. For a wise visiting bhikkhu will say, “First, prepare the medicine.” These are the duties of a resident bhikkhu.

187. Gamikavatte gamikena bhikkhunā mañcapīṭhādidārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍampi rajanabhājanādi sabbaṃ aggisālāyaṃ vā aññasmiṃ vā guttaṭṭhāne paṭisāmetvā dvāravātapānaṃ thaketvā senāsanaṃ āpucchitvā pakkamitabbaṃ. Sace bhikkhu na hoti, sāmaṇero āpucchitabbo. Sace sāmaṇero na hoti, ārāmiko āpucchitabbo. Sace na hoti bhikkhu vā sāmaṇero vā ārāmiko vā, catūsu pāsāṇesu mañcaṃ paññapetvā mañce mañcaṃ āropetvā pīṭhe pīṭhaṃ āropetvā senāsanaṃ upari puñjaṃ karitvā dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ paṭisāmetvā dvāravātapānaṃ thaketvā pakkamitabbaṃ. Sace vihāro ovassati, sace ussahati, sabbo chādetabbo, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ “kinti nu kho vihāro chādiyethā”ti, evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, yo deso anovassako hoti, tattha catūsu pāsāṇesu mañcaṃ paññapetvā mañce mañcaṃ āropetvā pīṭhe pīṭhaṃ āropetvā senāsanaṃ upari puñjaṃ karitvā dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ paṭisāmetvā dvāravātapānaṃ thaketvā pakkamitabbaṃ. Sace vihāro ovassati, sace ussahati, senāsanaṃ gāmaṃ atiharitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ “kinti nu kho senāsanaṃ gāmaṃ atihariyethā”ti, evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, ajjhokāse catūsu pāsāṇesu mañcaṃ paññapetvā mañce mañcaṃ āropetvā pīṭhe pīṭhaṃ āropetvā senāsanaṃ upari puñjaṃ karitvā dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ paṭisāmetvā [M 0.0234] tiṇena vā paṇṇena vā paṭicchādetvā pakkamitabbaṃ “appeva nāma aṅgānipi seseyyu”nti. Idaṃ gamikavattaṃ.

187. Regarding the duties for a traveling monk: a monk who is going on a journey should put away all wooden articles such as beds and stools, and also clay articles and all things such as dye pots, in the fire hall or in another secure place. Having closed the doors and windows and having taken leave of the lodging, he should depart. If there is no monk, he should take leave of a novice. If there is no novice, he should take leave of a monastery attendant. If there is no monk, novice, or monastery attendant, he should place a bed on four stones, place a bed upon the bed, place a stool upon the stool, make a pile of the lodging items on top, put away the wooden and clay articles, close the doors and windows, and then depart. If the monastery is rained on, and if he is able, the entire monastery should be covered, or an effort should be made, thinking, “How, indeed, might the monastery be covered?” If he should accomplish this, that is good. If he should not accomplish this, in a place that is not rained on, he should place a bed on four stones, place a bed upon the bed, place a stool upon the stool, make a pile of the lodging items on top, put away the wooden and clay articles, close the doors and windows, and then depart. If the monastery is rained on, and if he is able, the lodging items should be carried to the village, or an effort should be made, thinking, “How, indeed, might the lodging items be carried to the village?” If he should accomplish this, that is good. If he should not accomplish this, in an open space, he should place a bed on four stones, place a bed upon the bed, place a stool upon the stool, make a pile of the lodging items on top, put away the wooden and clay articles, and having covered them with grass or with leaves, he should depart, thinking, “Indeed, may even the components remain.” This is the duty for a traveling monk.

188. Bhattaggavatte sace ārāme kālo ārocito hoti, timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentena parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ bandhitvā saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo pārupitvā gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā dhovitvā pattaṃ gahetvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena gāmo pavisitabbo.

188. Regarding the duties in the alms-hall: if the time has been announced in the monastery, one should cover the three circles, put on the lower robe evenly all around, fasten the waistband, put on the outer robes making them doubled, fasten the knot, wash and take the bowl, and enter the village carefully without hurrying.

Na okkamma therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ purato gantabbaṃ. Suppaṭicchannena, susaṃvutena, okkhittacakkhunā, appasaddena antaraghare gantabbaṃ, na ukkhittakāya, na ujjagghikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ, na kāyappacālakaṃ, na bāhuppacālakaṃ, na sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ, na khambhakatena, na oguṇṭhitena, na ukkuṭikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ.

One should not overtake the elder monks to walk in front of them. One should go among the houses well-covered, well-restrained, with downcast eyes, and making little noise. One should not go among the houses with an uplifted body or with boisterous laughter. One should not go among the houses swaying the body or swinging the arms. One should not go among the houses with arms akimbo, with the head covered, or squatting.

Suppaṭicchannena[V 0.0221], susaṃvutena, okkhittacakkhunā, appasaddena antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ, na ukkhittakāya, na ujjagghikāya antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ, na kāyappacālakaṃ, na bāhuppacālakaṃ, na sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ, na khambhakatena, na oguṇṭhitena, na pallatthikāya antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ, na there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ. Sace mahātherassa nisinnāsanena samakaṃ āsanaṃ hoti, bahūsu āsanesu sati ekaṃ dve āsanāni ṭhapetvā nisīditabbaṃ. Bhikkhū gaṇetvā paññattāsanesu anisīditvā mahātherena “nisīdā”ti vuttena nisīditabbaṃ. No ce mahāthero vadati, “idaṃ, bhante, āsanaṃ ucca”nti vattabbaṃ. “Nisīdā”ti vuttena nisīditabbaṃ. Sace pana evaṃ āpucchitepi na vadati, nisīdantassa anāpatti, mahātherasseva āpatti. Navako hi evarūpe āsane anāpucchā nisīdanto āpajjati, thero āpucchite ananujānanto. Na navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā, na saṅghāṭikaṃ ottharitvā antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ.

One should sit inside a house well-covered, well-restrained, with downcast eyes, and making little noise. One should not sit inside a house with an uplifted body or with boisterous laughter. One should not sit inside a house swaying the body, swinging the arms, or shaking the head. One should not sit inside a house with arms akimbo, with the head covered, or with legs crossed. One should not sit pressing upon the elder monks. If there is a seat level with that of a great elder, and there are many seats, one should leave one or two seats aside and then sit. Having counted the monks, one should not sit on the prepared seats, but should sit only when told 'Sit' by the great elder. If the great elder does not speak, one should say, 'Venerable sir, this seat is high.' When told, 'Sit,' one should sit. But if, even when asked thus, he does not speak, there is no offense for the one who sits; the offense is for the great elder alone. For a junior monk who sits on such a seat without asking commits an offense, while an elder who does not give permission when asked also commits an offense. Junior monks should not be refused a seat. One should not sit inside a house having spread out the outer robe.

Pattadhovanodake dīyamāne ubhohi hatthehi pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā udakaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, dakkhiṇodakaṃ pana purato ādhārake pattaṃ ṭhapetvā gahetabbaṃ, nīcaṃ katvā udakasaddaṃ akarontena apaṭighaṃsantena patto dhovitabbo. Sace udakapaṭiggāhako hoti, nīcaṃ katvā udakapaṭiggāhake udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ “mā udakapaṭiggāhako udakena osiñci[M 0.0235], mā sāmantā bhikkhū udakena osiñciṃsu, mā saṅghāṭi udakena osiñcī”ti. Sace udakapaṭiggāhako na hoti, nīcaṃ katvā chamāya udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ “mā sāmantā bhikkhū udakena osiñciṃsu, mā saṅghāṭi udakena osiñcī”ti.

When water for washing the bowl is being offered, one should take hold of the bowl with both hands and receive the water. The water of dedication, however, should be received after placing the bowl on a stand in front. The bowl should be washed while holding it low, without making the sound of water, and without scraping it. If there is a water-receptacle, holding the bowl low, water should be poured into the water-receptacle with the thought: 'May the water-receptacle not be splashed by the water, may the nearby monks not be splashed by the water, may the outer robe not be splashed by the water.' If there is no water-receptacle, holding the bowl low, water should be poured onto the ground with the thought: 'May the nearby monks not be splashed by the water, may the outer robe not be splashed by the water.'

Odane dīyamāne ubhohi hatthehi pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā odano paṭiggahetabbo. Yathā sūpassa okāso hoti, evaṃ mattāya odano gaṇhitabbo. Sace hoti sappi vā telaṃ vā uttaribhaṅgaṃ vā, therena vattabbo “sabbesaṃ samakaṃ sampādehī”ti. Idañca na kevalaṃ sappiādīsu, odanepi vattabbaṃ. Sappiādīsu pana yaṃ appaṃ hoti ekassa vā dvinnaṃ vā anurūpaṃ, taṃ sabbesaṃ samakaṃ sampādehīti vutte manussānaṃ vihesā hoti, tasmā tādisaṃ sakiṃ vā dvikkhattuṃ vā gahetvā sesaṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Sakkaccaṃ piṇḍapāto paṭiggahetabbo, pattasaññinā piṇḍapāto paṭiggahetabbo, samasūpako samatitthiko piṇḍapāto paṭiggahetabbo, na tāva therena bhuñjitabbaṃ, yāva na sabbesaṃ odano sampatto hoti. Idañca yaṃ paricchinnabhikkhukaṃ bhattaggaṃ, yattha manussā sabbesaṃ pāpetvā vanditukāmā honti, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ[V 0.0222]. Yaṃ pana mahābhattaggaṃ hoti, yattha ekasmiṃ padese bhuñjanti, ekasmiṃ padese udakaṃ dīyati, tattha yathāsukhaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ.

When rice is being offered, the bowl should be accepted with both hands, and then the rice should be accepted. Rice should be taken in such a measure that there is space for curry. If there is ghee, oil, or an additional dish, the elder should say, 'Provide it equally to all.' This should be said not only about ghee and the like, but also about the rice. However, concerning ghee and the like, if the amount is small and suitable for only one or two, then saying, 'Provide it equally to all,' would be a vexation to the people. Therefore, such items should be taken once or twice, and the rest should not be taken. Almsfood should be received respectfully. Almsfood should be received while being mindful of the bowl. Almsfood should be received with an equal amount of curry, and level with the brim. The elder should not eat until the rice has been served to all. This is said with reference to a meal-hall with a limited number of monks, where people wish to serve all and then pay respects. But in a large meal-hall, where they eat in one area and water is given in another, one may eat as one pleases.

Sakkaccaṃ piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo, pattasaññinā piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo, sapadāno piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo, samasūpako piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo, na thūpakato omadditvā piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo, na sūpaṃ vā byañjanaṃ vā odanena paṭicchādetabbaṃ bhiyyokamyataṃ upādāya, na sūpaṃ vā odanaṃ vā agilānena attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjitabbaṃ, na ujjhānasaññinā paresaṃ patto oloketabbo, nātimahanto kabaḷo kātabbo, parimaṇḍalaṃ ālopo kātabbo, na anāhaṭe kabaḷe mukhadvāraṃ vivaritabbaṃ, na bhuñjamānena sabbo hattho mukhe pakkhipitabbo, na sakabaḷena mukhena byāharitabbaṃ, na piṇḍukkhepakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ, na kabaḷāvacchekaṃ, na avagaṇḍakārakaṃ, na hatthaniddhunakaṃ, na sitthāvakārakaṃ, na jivhānicchārakaṃ, na capucapukārakaṃ, na surusurukārakaṃ, na hatthanillehakaṃ, na pattanillehakaṃ, na oṭṭhanillehakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ.

Almsfood should be eaten respectfully. Almsfood should be eaten with attention to the bowl. Almsfood should be eaten in sequence. Almsfood should be eaten with an equal amount of soup. Almsfood should not be eaten by pressing down from the top of the heap. Soup or sauce should not be covered with rice out of a desire for more. Soup or rice should not be requested for oneself when not ill. One should not look at another's bowl with thoughts of fault-finding. A morsel that is too large should not be made. A round morsel should be made. The mouth should not be opened before the morsel is brought to it. While eating, the whole hand should not be put into the mouth. One should not speak with a mouthful. One should not eat by tossing up morsels, nor by cutting off from a morsel, nor by making the cheeks bulge, nor by shaking the hand, nor by scattering rice grains, nor by sticking out the tongue, nor by making a smacking sound, nor by making a slurping sound, nor by licking the hand, nor by licking the bowl, nor by licking the lips.

Na [M 0.0236] sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālako paṭiggahetabbo, na tāva therena hatthadhovanaudakaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, yāva na sabbe bhuttāvino honti. Sace manussā “dhovatha, bhante, pattañca hatthe cā”ti vadanti, bhikkhū vā “tumhe udakaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadanti, vaṭṭati. Udake dīyamāne ubhohi hatthehi pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā udakaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, nīcaṃ katvā udakasaddaṃ akarontena apaṭighaṃsantena patto dhovitabbo. Sace udakapaṭiggāhako hoti, nīcaṃ katvā udakapaṭiggāhake udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ “mā udakapaṭiggāhako udakena osiñci, mā sāmantā bhikkhū udakena osiñciṃsu, mā saṅghāṭi udakena osiñcī”ti. Sace udakapaṭiggāhako na hoti, nīcaṃ katvā chamāya udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ “mā sāmantā bhikkhū udakena osiñciṃsu, mā saṅghāṭi udakena osiñcī”ti, na sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

A drinking water vessel should not be accepted with a hand soiled with food. Water for washing hands should not be accepted by an elder until all have finished eating. If laypeople say, 'Venerable sirs, wash your bowl and hands,' or if monks say, 'You may take the water,' it is allowable. When water is being given, the bowl should be accepted with both hands, and then the water should be accepted. The bowl should be washed by holding it low, without making the sound of water, and without striking it. If there is a water-receptacle, the water should be poured low into the water-receptacle, reflecting thus: 'May the water-receptacle not be splashed by the water, may the surrounding monks not be splashed by the water, may the outer robe not be splashed by the water.' If there is no water-receptacle, the water should be poured low onto the ground, reflecting thus: 'May the surrounding monks not be splashed by the water, may the outer robe not be splashed by the water.' Bowl-washing water containing rice grains should not be discarded inside the house.

Bhattaggato uṭṭhāya nivattantesu navakehi bhikkhūhi paṭhamataraṃ nivattitabbaṃ, pacchā therehi. Sambādhesu hi gharesu mahātherānaṃ nikkhamanokāso na hoti, tasmā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Evaṃ nivattantehi pana navakehi gehadvāre ṭhatvā theresu nikkhamantesu paṭipāṭiyā gantabbaṃ. Sace pana mahātherā dhure nisinnā honti, navakā antogehe, therāsanato paṭṭhāya paṭipāṭiyā eva nikkhamitabbaṃ[V 0.0223], kāyena kāyaṃ asaṅghaṭṭentena yathā antarena manussā gantuṃ sakkonti, evaṃ viraḷāya pāḷiyā gantabbaṃ.

Having risen from the meal-hall, when the monks are returning, the junior monks should return first, and the elders afterward. For in crowded houses, there is no opportunity for the great elders to exit; therefore, it was said thus. When returning thus, the junior monks should stand at the house door and, as the elders exit, proceed in order. If, however, the great elders are seated at the front and the junior monks are inside the house, they should exit in succession only, starting from the elders' seats, without body touching body, proceeding in a sparse line such that people are able to pass in between.

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, therena bhikkhunā bhattagge anumoditu”nti (cūḷava. 362) vacanato saṅghattherena bhattagge anumoditabbaṃ. Taṃ ekameva ohāya sesehi na gantabbaṃ.

As it is stated, 'Monks, I allow an elder monk to give the anumodanā in the meal-hall' (Cūḷavagga 362), the anumodanā in the meal-hall should be given by the elder of the Sangha. The others should not depart, leaving him behind alone.

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhattagge catūhi pañcahi therānutherehi bhikkhūhi āgametu”nti (cūḷava. 362) vacanato saṅghattherena anumodanatthāya nisinne heṭṭhā paṭipāṭiyā catūhi nisīditabbaṃ, anuthere nisinne mahātherena ca heṭṭhā ca tīhi nisīditabbaṃ, pañcame nisinne upari catūhi nisīditabbaṃ, saṅghattherena heṭṭhā daharabhikkhusmiṃ ajjhiṭṭhepi saṅghattherato paṭṭhāya [M 0.0237] catūhi nisīditabbameva. Sace pana anumodako bhikkhu “gacchatha, bhante, āgametabbakiccaṃ natthī”ti vadati, gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Mahātherena “gacchāma, āvuso”ti vutte “gacchathā”ti vadati, evampi vaṭṭati, “bahigāme āgamissāmā”ti ābhogaṃ katvāpi bahigāmaṃ gantvā attano nissitake “tumhe tassa āgamanaṃ āgamethā”ti vatvāpi gantuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Sace pana manussā attano rucitena ekena anumodanaṃ kārenti, neva tassa anumodato āpatti, na mahātherassa bhāro hoti. Upanisinnakathāyameva hi manussesu kathāpentesu thero āpucchitabbo. Mahātherena ca anumodanāya ajjhiṭṭhova āgametabboti idamettha lakkhaṇaṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sati karaṇīye ānantarikaṃ bhikkhuṃ āpucchitvā gantu”nti (cūḷava. 362) vacanato pana vaccādipīḷitena anantaraṃ bhikkhuṃ āpucchitvā gantabbanti. Idaṃ bhattaggavattaṃ.

Because it is said: “Monks, I allow that in the dining hall, four or five senior and junior monks should wait” (Cūḷavagga 362), when the Saṅghatthera is seated to give the anumodanā, four monks should sit below him in order. When a junior monk is seated, the most senior monk and three others should sit below. When a fifth monk is seated, four should sit above him. Even if a junior monk below the Saṅghatthera is requested, four monks, starting from the Saṅghatthera, must still sit. However, if the monk giving the anumodanā says, “Venerable sirs, you may go; there is no need to wait,” it is permissible to go. When the most senior monk says, “Friend, let us go,” and the other replies, “You may go,” this is also permissible. And having decided, “We will wait outside the village,” and having gone outside the village and told one’s own dependents, “You wait for his arrival,” it is indeed permissible to go. However, if laypeople have the anumodanā given by a monk of their own choosing, there is no offense for the one giving the anumodanā, nor is it a burden for the most senior monk. For it is only in the case of a talk given while sitting near, when laypeople request a monk to speak, that the senior monk should be asked for permission. And the most senior monk should wait only for the one who has been requested to give the anumodanā—this is the guideline here. Because it is said: “Monks, I allow that when there is something to be done, one may go after taking leave of the nearest monk” (Cūḷavagga 362), one who is afflicted by the need to defecate and so forth should go after taking leave of the adjacent monk. This is the practice concerning the dining hall.

189. Piṇḍacārikavatte pana piṇḍacārikena bhikkhunā “idāni gāmaṃ pavisissāmī”ti timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentena parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ bandhitvā saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo pārupitvā gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā dhovitvā pattaṃ gahetvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena gāmo pavisitabbo. Suppaṭicchannena antaraghare gantabbantiādi sabbaṃ bhattaggavatte vuttanayeneva idhāpi veditabbaṃ.

189. Now, regarding the practice of going for alms: a monk going for alms, thinking, “Now I will enter the village,” should enter the village carefully and without hurrying, having covered the three circles, having worn the lower robe evenly, having tied the waistband, having put on the outer robes folded double, having fastened the toggle, and having washed and taken the bowl. “One should go inside the house well-covered,” and so on—all this should be understood here also in the same way as stated in the section on the dining hall practice.

Nivesanaṃ pavisantena sallakkhetabbaṃ “iminā pavisissāmi, iminā nikkhamissāmī”ti, nātisahasā pavisitabbaṃ, nātidūre nāccāsanne ṭhātabbaṃ, nāticiraṃ ṭhātabbaṃ, nātilahukaṃ nivattitabbaṃ, ṭhitena sallakkhetabbaṃ “bhikkhaṃ dātukāmā vā adātukāmā vā”ti[V 0.0224]. Sace kammaṃ vā nikkhipati, āsanā vā vuṭṭhāti, kaṭacchuṃ vā parāmasati, bhājanaṃ vā parāmasati, ṭhapeti vā, “dātukāmassā”ti ṭhātabbaṃ. Bhikkhāya dīyamānāya vāmena hatthena saṅghāṭiṃ uccāretvā dakkhiṇena hatthena pattaṃ paṇāmetvā ubhohi hatthehi pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā bhikkhā paṭiggahetabbā, itthī vā hotu puriso vā, bhikkhādānasamaye mukhaṃ na oloketabbaṃ, sallakkhetabbaṃ “sūpaṃ dātukāmā vā adātukāmā vā”ti. Sace kaṭacchuṃ vā parāmasati, bhājanaṃ vā parāmasati, ṭhapeti vā, “dātukāmassā”ti ṭhātabbaṃ. Bhikkhāya dinnāya saṅghāṭiyā pattaṃ paṭicchādetvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena nivattitabbaṃ.

When entering a dwelling, one should note, “I will enter by this door and exit by that one.” One should not enter too hastily. One should not stand too far away or too close. One should not stand for too long. One should not turn back too quickly. While standing, one should observe, “Do they wish to give alms or not?” If they put down their work, or rise from their seat, or touch a ladle, or touch a vessel, or ask one to wait, one should stand, thinking, “They wish to give.” When alms are being given, having lifted the outer robe with the left hand and extended the bowl with the right hand, the alms should be received by taking the bowl with both hands. Whether it be a woman or a man, one should not look at their face at the time of giving alms. One should observe, “Do they wish to give curry or not?” If they touch a ladle, or touch a vessel, or ask one to wait, one should stand, thinking, “They wish to give.” When the alms have been given, having covered the bowl with the outer robe, one should depart carefully and without hurrying.

Yo [M 0.0238] paṭhamaṃ gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati, tena āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, avakkārapāti dhovitvā upaṭṭhāpetabbā, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Yo pacchā gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati, sace hoti bhuttāvaseso, sace ākaṅkhati, bhuñjitabbaṃ. No ce ākaṅkhati, appaharite vā chaḍḍetabbaṃ, appāṇake vā udake opilāpetabbaṃ, tena āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ, avakkārapāti dhovitvā paṭisāmetabbā, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ, bhattaggaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Yo passati pānīyaghaṭaṃ vā paribhojanīyaghaṭaṃ vā vaccaghaṭaṃ vā rittaṃ tucchaṃ, tena upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sacassa hoti avisayhaṃ, hatthavikārena dutiyaṃ āmantetvā hatthavilaṅghakena upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ, na ca tappaccayā vācā bhinditabbāti. Idaṃ piṇḍacārikavattaṃ.

The monk who returns first from the alms-round in the village should prepare a seat; he should place water for the feet, a footstool, and a foot-scraper. The bowl for leftovers should be washed and set out; drinking water and water for use should be set up. The monk who returns later from the alms-round in the village, if there are leftovers from what has been eaten and if he wishes, should eat them. If he does not wish, they should be discarded in a place without greenery or submerged in water that is free of living beings. He should then clear away the seat; he should put away the water for the feet, the footstool, and the foot-scraper. The bowl for leftovers should be washed and put away; the drinking water and water for use should be put away. The dining hall should be swept. Whoever sees a drinking water pot, a pot for water for use, or a toilet pot that is empty should fill it. If it is too heavy for him, he should call a second person with a hand gesture, and it should be set up with assistance. But on account of this, speech should not be broken. This is the practice for one who goes for alms.

190.
