Āraññikavatte āraññikena bhikkhunā kālasseva uṭṭhāya pattaṃ thavikāya pakkhipitvā aṃse laggetvā cīvaraṃ khandhe karitvā upāhanā ārohitvā dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ paṭisāmetvā dvāravātapānaṃ thaketvā vasanaṭṭhānato nikkhamitabbaṃ. “Idāni gāmaṃ pavisissāmā”ti upāhanā omuñcitvā nīcaṃ katvā papphoṭetvā thavikāya pakkhipitvā aṃse laggetvā timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentena parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ bandhitvā saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo pārupitvā gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā dhovitvā pattaṃ gahetvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena gāmo pavisitabbo. Suppaṭicchannena antaraghare gantabbantiādi sabbaṃ gamanavidhānaṃ idhāpi bhattaggavatte vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

190. Regarding the practice for a forest-dweller: a forest-dwelling monk, having risen early, should place his bowl in its bag, hang it on his shoulder, place his robe over his shoulder, put on his sandals, put away the wooden and clay utensils, close the door and window, and then depart from his dwelling. When about to enter the village, thinking, “Now we will enter the village,” he should remove his sandals, hold them low, shake them out, place them in the bag, and hang it on his shoulder. Covering the three circles of the body, having worn the lower robe evenly all around, having fastened the waistband, having put on the outer robes folded double, having fastened the toggle, having washed and taken the bowl, the village should be entered carefully and without hurrying. The entire procedure for movement, such as, “One should go into the houses well-covered,” and so on, should be understood here also in the same way as it was stated in the practice concerning the dining hall.

Nivesanaṃ pavisantena sallakkhetabbaṃ “iminā pavisissāmi, iminā nikkhamissāmī”tiādi sabbaṃ bhikkhācāravidhānaṃ piṇḍacārikavatte vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Āraññikena [V 0.0225] bhikkhunā pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace bhājanāni nappahonti, pānīyameva paribhojanīyampi katvā upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Bhājanaṃ alabhantena veḷunāḷikāyapi upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Tampi alabhantassa yathā samīpe udakaāvāṭo hoti, evaṃ kātabbaṃ. Aggi upaṭṭhāpetabbo, araṇisahitaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ, araṇisahite sati aggiṃ akātumpi vaṭṭati. Yathā ca āraññikassa, evaṃ kantārappaṭipannassapi araṇisahitaṃ icchitabbaṃ. Gaṇavāsino pana tena vināpi vaṭṭati. Kattaradaṇḍo [M 0.0239] upaṭṭhāpetabbo, nakkhattapadāni uggahetabbāni sakalāni vā ekadesāni vā, disākusalena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ āraññikavattaṃ.

When entering a dwelling, one should note, “I will enter by this door, I will leave by this door.” And so on, the entire procedure for going for alms should be understood in the very manner described in the duties of an alms-farer. A forest-dwelling monk should prepare drinking water and water for use. If vessels are not sufficient, drinking water itself should also be made into water for use and prepared. If a vessel is not obtained, it should be prepared even in a bamboo tube. For one who does not obtain even that, it should be arranged so that a water well is nearby. A fire should be prepared; a fire-drill set should be prepared. If a fire-drill set is available, it is permissible even not to make a fire. Just as for a forest-dweller, so too for one traveling through a wilderness, a fire-drill set is desirable. For those living in a group, however, it is permissible even without it. A staff should be prepared. The positions of the constellations should be learned, either all of them or in part. One should be skilled in the directions. This is the duty of a forest-dweller.

191. Senāsanavatte yasmiṃ vihāre viharati, sace so vihāro uklāpo hoti, sace ussahati, sodhetabbo. Vihāraṃ sodhentena paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, bhisibimbohanaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, mañco nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ apaṭighaṃsantena asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapīṭhaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo, pīṭhaṃ nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ apaṭighaṃsantena asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapīṭhaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, mañcapaṭipādakā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbā, kheḷamallako nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo, apassenaphalakaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, bhūmattharaṇaṃ yathāpaññattaṃ sallakkhetvā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace vihāre santānakaṃ hoti, ullokā paṭhamaṃ ohāretabbaṃ, ālokasandhikaṇṇabhāgā pamajjitabbā. Sace gerukaparikammakatā bhitti kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace kāḷavaṇṇakatā bhūmi kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace akatā hoti bhūmi, udakena paripphositvā paripphositvā sammajjitabbā “mā vihāro rajena uhaññī”ti, saṅkāraṃ vicinitvā ekamantaṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

191. In the duty concerning lodgings, if the monastery where one resides is dirty, and if one is able, it should be cleaned. When cleaning the monastery, the bowl and robes should first be taken out and placed to one side. The sitting mat and ground-covering should be taken out and placed to one side. The mattress and pillow should be taken out and placed to one side. The bed, having been lowered, should be taken out carefully, without scraping it or knocking it against the door-leaf and door-post, and placed to one side. The bench, having been lowered, should be taken out carefully, without scraping it or knocking it against the door-leaf and door-post, and placed to one side. The legs of the bed should be taken out and placed to one side. The spittoon should be taken out and placed to one side. The leaning-board should be taken out and placed to one side. The floor covering, having noted how it was laid out, should be taken out and placed to one side. If there are cobwebs in the monastery, they should first be removed from the ceiling. The window-joints and corners should be wiped. If a wall prepared with red ochre is stained, a cloth should be wetted, wrung out, and used to wipe it. If a floor made black is stained, a cloth should be wetted, wrung out, and used to wipe it. If the floor is an unprepared one, it should be sprinkled repeatedly with water and swept, with the thought, ‘Let the monastery not be affected by dust.’ The sweepings should be gathered and discarded to one side.

Na bhikkhusāmantā senāsanaṃ papphoṭetabbaṃ, na vihārasāmantā senāsanaṃ papphoṭetabbaṃ, na pānīyasāmantā senāsanaṃ papphoṭetabbaṃ, na paribhojanīyasāmantā senāsanaṃ papphoṭetabbaṃ, na paṭivāte aṅgaṇe senāsanaṃ papphoṭetabbaṃ, adhovāte senāsanaṃ papphoṭetabbaṃ.

Bedding should not be shaken out near a bhikkhu, nor near a dwelling, nor near drinking water, nor near water for use, nor in a courtyard upwind; bedding should be shaken out downwind.

Bhūmattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, mañcapaṭipādakā ekamantaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā abhiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbā, mañco ekamantaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā [V 0.0226] nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ apaṭighaṃsantena asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapīṭhaṃ atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbo, pīṭhaṃ ekamantaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ apaṭighaṃsantena asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapīṭhaṃ atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ[M 0.0240], bhisibimbohanaṃ ekamantaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, kheḷamallako ekamantaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbo, apassenaphalakaṃ ekamantaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbaṃ. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo, na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ, orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ.

The ground covering should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and laid out as it was before. The bed legs should be aired in the sun to one side, wiped, brought back, and placed in their proper place. The bed should be aired in the sun to one side, cleaned, shaken out, lowered, and brought back carefully without scraping or knocking against the door-leaf and door-post, and laid out as it was before. The chair should be aired in the sun to one side, cleaned, shaken out, lowered, and brought back carefully without scraping or knocking against the door-leaf and door-post, and laid out as it was before. The mattress and cushion should be aired in the sun to one side, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and laid out as it was before. The sitting mat and ground-covering should be aired in the sun, shaken out, brought back, and laid out as it was before. The spittoon should be aired in the sun to one side, wiped, brought back, and placed in its proper place. The leaning board should be aired in the sun to one side, wiped, and placed in its proper place. The bowl and robes should be put away. When putting down the bowl, one should take the bowl with one hand, feel underneath the bed or underneath the chair with the other hand, and then put the bowl down. The bowl should not be put down on the bare ground. When putting away a robe, one should take the robe with one hand, wipe the robe-rail or the robe-rope with the other hand, and making a fold on the near side with the end on the far side, put the robe away.

Sace puratthimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, puratthimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace pacchimā, uttarā, dakkhiṇā sarajā vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace sītakālo hoti, divā vātapānā vivaritabbā, rattiṃ thaketabbā. Sace uṇhakālo hoti, divā vātapānā thaketabbā, rattiṃ vivaritabbā.

If dusty winds blow from the east, the eastern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the west, north, or south, the southern windows should be closed. If it is the cold season, the windows should be opened during the day and closed at night. If it is the hot season, the windows should be closed during the day and opened at night.

Sace uklāpaṃ hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo, upaṭṭhānasālā sammajjitabbā, aggisālā sammajjitabbā, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā. Sace pānīyaṃ na hoti, pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace paribhojanīyaṃ na hoti, paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ.

If the precinct is dirty, the precinct should be swept; the chamber should be swept; the service hall should be swept; the fire-hall should be swept; the toilet should be swept. If there is no drinking water, drinking water should be prepared. If there is no water for use, water for use should be prepared. If there is no water in the rinsing pot, water should be poured into the rinsing pot.

Sace vuḍḍhena saddhiṃ ekavihāre viharati, na vuḍḍhaṃ anāpucchā uddeso dātabbo, na paripucchā dātabbā, na sajjhāyo kātabbo, na dhammo bhāsitabbo, na padīpo kātabbo, na padīpo vijjhāpetabbo, na vātapānā vivaritabbā, na vātapānā thaketabbā. Dvāraṃ nāma yasmā mahāvaḷañjaṃ, tasmā tattha āpucchanakiccaṃ natthi, sesāni pana uddesadānādīni āpucchitvāva kātabbāni, devasikampi āpucchituṃ vaṭṭati. Athāpi “bhante, āpucchitameva hotū”ti vutte vuḍḍhataro “sādhū”ti sampaṭicchati, sayameva vā “tvaṃ yathāsukhaṃ viharāhī”ti vadati, evampi vaṭṭati. Sabhāgassa vissāsenapi vaṭṭatiyeva. Sace vuḍḍhena saddhiṃ ekacaṅkame caṅkamati, yena vuḍḍho, tena parivattetabbaṃ, na ca vuḍḍho saṅghāṭikaṇṇena ghaṭṭetabbo. Idaṃ senāsanavattaṃ.

If one dwells in the same dwelling with an elder, one should not give a recitation without asking the elder, nor ask questions, nor engage in chanting, nor speak the Dhamma, nor light a lamp, nor extinguish a lamp, nor open the windows, nor close the windows. As for the door, because it is for public use, there is no need to ask permission regarding it. However, the other things, such as giving recitations, should be done only after asking permission. It is also proper to ask permission daily. Or if, when one has said, 'Venerable sir, may it be that I have asked permission?' the elder accepts, saying, 'Good,' or if he himself says, 'You may dwell as you please,' this is also proper. With a senior of the same group, it is also proper through familiarity. If one walks on the same promenade with an elder, one should turn towards the elder, and the elder should not be touched by the corner of one's outer robe. This is the duty concerning lodgings.

192. Jantāgharavatte [M 0.0241] yo paṭhamaṃ jantāgharaṃ gacchati, sace chārikā ussannā hoti, chārikā [V 0.0227] chaḍḍetabbā. Sace uklāpaṃ hoti, jantāgharaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ, paribhaṇḍaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo, jantāgharasālā sammajjitabbā, cuṇṇaṃ sannetabbaṃ, mattikā temetabbā, udakadoṇiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ. Jantāgharaṃ pavisantena mattikāya mukhaṃ makkhetvā purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ, na there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ, na navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā. Sace ussahati, jantāghare therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Jantāgharā nikkhamantena jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharā nikkhamitabbaṃ. Sace ussahati, udakepi therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ, na therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ purato nahāyitabbaṃ, na uparito nahāyitabbaṃ, nahātena uttarantena otarantānaṃ maggo dātabbo. Yo pacchā jantāgharā nikkhamati, sace jantāgharaṃ cikkhallaṃ hoti, dhovitabbaṃ, mattikādoṇiṃ dhovitvā jantāgharapīṭhaṃ paṭisāmetvā aggiṃ vijjhāpetvā dvāraṃ thaketvā pakkamitabbaṃ. Idaṃ jantāgharavattaṃ.

192. In the conduct for the steam-room: the one who goes to the steam-room first, if the ashes have piled up, should dispose of the ashes. If it is dirty, the steam-room should be swept, the equipment should be swept, the precinct should be swept, the storeroom should be swept, and the hall of the steam-room should be swept. The bathing powder should be kneaded, the clay should be moistened, and water should be poured into the water trough. When entering the steam-room, one should smear one’s face with clay, cover oneself in front and in back, and then enter the steam-room. One should not sit crowding the senior bhikkhus, nor should junior bhikkhus be kept from their seats. If one is able, one should attend on the senior bhikkhus in the steam-room. When leaving the steam-room, one should take the steam-room stool, cover oneself in front and in back, and then leave the steam-room. If one is able, one should also attend on the senior bhikkhus in the bathing place. One should not bathe in front of the senior bhikkhus, nor upstream from them. When getting out after bathing, one should give way to those getting in. The one who leaves the steam-room last, if the steam-room is muddy, should wash it. Having washed the clay trough, put away the steam-room stool, extinguished the fire, and closed the door, one should depart. This is the conduct for the steam-room.

193. Vaccakuṭivatte yo vaccakuṭiṃ gacchati, bahi ṭhitena ukkāsitabbaṃ, anto nisinnenapi ukkāsitabbaṃ, cīvaravaṃse vā cīvararajjuyā vā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā sādhukaṃ ataramānena vaccakuṭi pavisitabbā, nātisahasā pavisitabbā, na ubbhajitvā pavisitabbā, vaccapādukāya ṭhitena ubbhajitabbaṃ, na nitthunantena vacco kātabbo, na dantakaṭṭhaṃ khādantena vacco kātabbo, na bahiddhā vaccadoṇikāya vacco kātabbo, na bahiddhā passāvadoṇikāya passāvo kātabbo, na passāvadoṇikāya kheḷo kātabbo, phālitena vā kharena vā gaṇṭhikena vā kaṇṭakena vā susirena vā pūtinā vā kaṭṭhena na avalekhitabbaṃ, avalekhanakaṭṭhaṃ pana aggahetvā paviṭṭhassa āpatti natthi, na avalekhanakaṭṭhaṃ vaccakūpamhi pātetabbaṃ, vaccapādukāya ṭhitena paṭicchādetabbaṃ, nātisahasā nikkhamitabbaṃ, na ubbhajitvā nikkhamitabbaṃ, ācamanapādukāya ṭhitena ubbhajitabbaṃ, na capucapukārakaṃ ācametabbaṃ, na ācamanasarāvake udakaṃ sesetabbaṃ. Idañca sabbasādhāraṇaṭṭhānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tatra hi aññe aññe āgacchanti, tasmā udakaṃ na sesetabbaṃ. Yaṃ pana saṅghikepi vihāre ekadese nibaddhagamanatthāya [M 0.0242] kataṃ ṭhānaṃ hoti puggalikaṭṭhānaṃ vā, tasmiṃ vaṭṭati. Virecanaṃ pivitvā punappunaṃ pavisantassapi vaṭṭatiyeva. Ācamanapādukāya ṭhitena paṭicchādetabbaṃ.

193. Regarding the duties of the latrine: A bhikkhu who goes to the latrine should clear his throat while standing outside; the one sitting inside should also clear his throat. Having placed his robe on the robe-pole or on the robe-line, the latrine should be entered properly and without hurrying. It should not be entered very hastily. It should not be entered with the lower robe hitched up. Standing on the latrine-clogs, the lower robe should be hitched up. One should not pass excrement while groaning. One should not pass excrement while chewing a tooth-stick. Excrement should not be passed outside the latrine-receptacle. Urine should not be passed outside the urine-trough. Spittle should not be put in the urine-trough. One should not wipe with a stick that is split, rough, knotted, thorny, hollow, or decayed. However, for one who has entered without taking a wiping-stick, there is no offense. The wiping-stick should not be dropped in the latrine-pit. Standing on the latrine-clogs, one should cover the waste. One should not exit very hastily. One should not exit with the lower robe hitched up. Standing on the washing-clogs, the lower robe should be hitched up. One should not wash making a 'capu-capu' sound. Water should not be left remaining in the washing-bowl. And this was said in reference to a place common to all. For there, other bhikkhus come; therefore, water should not be left remaining. But as for a place made for one's own regular use in a certain part of a monastery, even a communal one, or a private place, in that place it is allowable. It is indeed allowable also for one who, having drunk a purgative, enters again and again. Standing on the washing-clogs, one should cover oneself.

Sace vaccakuṭi uhatā hoti bahi vaccamakkhitā, udakaṃ āharitvā dhovitabbā. Udakaṃ atthi, bhājanaṃ natthi, asantaṃ nāma hoti. Bhājanaṃ atthi, udakaṃ natthi, etampi asantaṃ[V 0.0228]. Ubhayasmiṃ asati asantameva, kaṭṭhena vā kenaci vā puñchitvā gantabbaṃ. Sace avalekhanapiṭako pūrito hoti, avalekhanakaṭṭhaṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ. Sace kacavaraṃ atthi, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā, paribhaṇḍaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo. Sace ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ.

If the latrine is smeared with excrement, or if excrement is smeared outside, water should be fetched and it should be washed. If there is water but no vessel, it is considered as not being available. If there is a vessel but no water, this too is considered as not being available. If both are unavailable, it is indeed unavailable; one should wipe it with a stick or with something and leave. If the basket for wiping sticks is full, the wiping sticks should be discarded. If there is rubbish, the latrine should be swept, the equipment should be swept, the precinct should be swept, and the storeroom should be swept. If there is no water in the rinsing pot, water should be poured into the rinsing pot.

“Na, bhikkhave, vaccaṃ katvā sati udake nācametabbaṃ, yo nācameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 373) vacanato udake sati udakakiccaṃ akarontassa āpatti. Sace udakaṃ atthi, paṭicchannaṭṭhānaṃ pana natthi, bhājanena nīharitvā ācamitabbaṃ. Bhājane asati pattena nīharitabbaṃ, pattepi asati asantaṃ nāma hoti. “Idaṃ ativivaṭaṃ, purato aññaṃ udakaṃ bhavissatī”ti gatassa udakaṃ alabhantasseva bhikkhācāravelā hoti, kaṭṭhena vā kenaci vā puñchitvā gantabbaṃ, bhuñjitumpi anumoditumpi vaṭṭati. “Na, bhikkhave, vaccakuṭiyā yathāvuḍḍhaṃ vacco kātabbo, yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āgatapaṭipāṭiyā vaccaṃ kātu”nti (cuḷava. 373) vacanato vaccakuṭiṃ pavisantena āgatapaṭipāṭiyā pavisitabbaṃ. Vaccakuṭiyaṃ passāvaṭṭhāne nahānatittheti tīsupi āgatapaṭipāṭiyeva pamāṇaṃ. Idaṃ vaccakuṭivattaṃ.

Because it is said: 'Monks, having defecated, when water is available, one must not fail to cleanse oneself. Whoever should not cleanse himself, commits an offense of wrong-doing' (Cūḷavagga 373), there is an offense for one who does not perform the duty concerning water when water is available. If water is available but there is no concealed place, one should take it out with a vessel and cleanse oneself. If there is no vessel, one should take it out with a bowl; if there is no bowl either, it is considered as not being available. For one who goes on thinking, 'This place is too exposed; there will be other water ahead,' and the time for the alms-round arrives without his having found water, he should wipe himself with a stick or with something and go on; it is permissible to eat and to give thanks. Because it is said: 'Monks, in the toilet, one should not defecate according to seniority. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, to defecate according to the order of arrival' (Cūḷavagga 373), one entering the toilet should enter according to the order of arrival. In the toilet, in the place for urination, and at the bathing place—in these three places, the order of arrival is indeed the standard. This is the duty concerning the toilet.

Iti pāḷimuttakavinayavinicchayasaṅgahe

Thus, in the Compilation of Vinaya Decisions Not Found in the Pāḷi Canon,

Upajjhāyādivattavinicchayakathā samattā.

The Discussion on the Decision Concerning the Duties toward a Preceptor and Others is concluded.

28. Catupaccayabhājanīyavinicchayakathā

28. 28. The Discussion on the Decision Concerning the Distribution of the Four Requisites

194. Catupaccayabhājananti [M 0.0243][V 0.0229] cīvarādīnaṃ catunnaṃ paccayānaṃ bhājanaṃ. Tattha cīvarabhājane tāva cīvarapaṭiggāhako veditabbo, cīvaranidahako veditabbo, bhaṇḍāgāriko veditabbo, bhaṇḍāgāraṃ veditabbaṃ, cīvarabhājako veditabbo, cīvarabhājanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

194. 'Distribution of the four requisites' means the distribution of the four requisites, such as robes. Therein, regarding the distribution of robes, first: the robe-receiver should be known, the robe-storer should be known, the storekeeper should be known, the storehouse should be known, the robe-distributor should be known, and the distribution of robes should be known.

Tattha (mahāva. aṭṭha. 340-342) “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarapaṭiggāhakaṃ sammannituṃ, yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na bhayāgatiṃ gaccheyya, gahitāgahitañca jāneyyā”ti (mahāva. 342) vacanato imehi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato cīvarapaṭiggāhako sammannitabbo. Tattha pacchā āgatānampi attano ñātakādīnaṃ paṭhamataraṃ paṭiggaṇhanto vā ekaccasmiṃ pemaṃ dassetvā gaṇhanto vā lobhapakatitāya attano pariṇāmento vā chandāgatiṃ gacchati nāma. Paṭhamataraṃ āgatassapi kodhavasena pacchā gaṇhanto vā duggatamanussesu avamaññaṃ katvā gaṇhanto vā “kiṃ vo ghare ṭhapanokāso natthi, tumhākaṃ santakaṃ gahetvā gacchathā”ti evaṃ saṅghassa lābhantarāyaṃ karonto vā dosāgatiṃ gacchati nāma. Yo pana muṭṭhassati asampajāno, ayaṃ mohāgatiṃ gacchati nāma. Pacchā āgatānampi issarānaṃ bhayena paṭhamataraṃ paṭiggaṇhanto vā “cīvarapaṭiggāhakaṭṭhānaṃ nāmetaṃ bhāriya”nti santasanto vā bhayāgatiṃ gacchati nāma. “Mayā idañcidañca gahitaṃ, idañcidañca na gahita”nti evaṃ jānanto gahitāgahitaṃ jānāti nāma. Tasmā yo chandāgatiādivasena na gacchati, ñātakaaññātakaaḍḍhaduggatesu visesaṃ akatvā āgatapaṭipāṭiyā gaṇhāti, sīlācārapaṭipattiyutto hoti satimā medhāvī bahussuto, sakkoti dāyakānaṃ vissaṭṭhāya vācāya parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehi anumodanaṃ karonto pasādaṃ janetuṃ, evarūpo sammannitabbo.

Herein (Mahāvagga, Aṭṭha. 340-342), it is said: “I allow, O monks, a monk endowed with five qualities to be appointed as a robe-receiver: one who would not proceed through favoritism, would not proceed through ill will, would not proceed through delusion, would not proceed through fear, and who would know what has been received and what has not been received” (Mahāvagga 342). According to this statement, a robe-receiver endowed with these five qualities should be appointed. Herein, one who receives first from his own relatives and others even though they arrived later, or who receives while showing affection for a certain person, or who appropriates robes for himself due to a greedy nature—such a one is said to proceed through favoritism. One who, out of anger, receives later from those who arrived earlier, or who receives while showing contempt for the poor, or who says, “Is there no place in your house to store these? Take what belongs to you and go,” thereby obstructing the Sangha's gain—such a one is said to proceed through ill will. One who is of lapsed mindfulness and lacks clear comprehension—such a one is said to proceed through delusion. One who, out of fear of powerful people, receives first from those who arrive later, or who is fearful, thinking, “This position of robe-receiver is burdensome”—such a one is said to proceed through fear. One who knows, “This has been received by me, and this has not been received”—such a one is said to know what has been received and what has not been received. Therefore, one who does not proceed due to favoritism or the like; who does not discriminate between relatives, strangers, the wealthy, or the destitute but receives in the order of arrival; who is endowed with virtue and good conduct, is mindful, wise, and learned; and is capable of generating confidence in donors by expressing gratitude with clear and well-articulated phrases—such a one should be appointed.

Evañca pana sammannitabbo. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo, yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

And he should be appointed in this way. First, a monk should be asked; having been asked, the Sangha should be informed by a monk who is competent and able—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarapaṭiggāhakaṃ sammanneyya, esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it seems fit to the Sangha, the Sangha should appoint the monk named so-and-so as the robe-receiver. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu [M 0.0244][V 0.0230] me, bhante, saṅgho, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarapaṭiggāhakaṃ sammannati, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno cīvarapaṭiggāhakassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The Sangha appoints the monk named so-and-so as the robe-receiver. If the appointment of the monk named so-and-so as robe-receiver is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent. If it is not agreeable to anyone, let him speak.

“Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu cīvarapaṭiggāhako, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti (mahāva. 342) –

“The monk named so-and-so has been appointed by the Sangha as the robe-receiver. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.”

Iti imāya kammavācāya vā apalokanena vā antovihāre sabbasaṅghamajjhepi khaṇḍasīmāyampi sammannituṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Evaṃ sammatena ca vihārapaccante vā padhānaghare vā na acchitabbaṃ. Yattha pana āgatāgatā manussā sukhaṃ passanti, tādise dhuravihāraṭṭhāne bījaniṃ passe ṭhapetvā sunivatthena supārutena nisīditabbaṃ.

Thus, by this formal act or by announcement, it is indeed proper to appoint a monk within the monastery, in the midst of the entire Sangha, or even within a broken boundary. And one who has been thus appointed should not stay in the outskirts of the monastery or in a meditation hall. But in a place such as a prominent monastery where people who come and go may see him easily, he should sit, having placed a fan nearby, with his lower robe well-worn and his upper robe well-draped.

195. Cīvaranidahakopi “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvaranidahakaṃ sammannituṃ, yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na bhayāgatiṃ gaccheyya, nihitānihitañca jāneyyā”ti vacanato pañcaṅgasamannāgato bhikkhu –

195. Also the robe-storer: 'I allow, monks, a monk endowed with five factors to be appointed as a robe-storer: one who does not proceed through favoritism, does not proceed through ill will, does not proceed through delusion, does not proceed through fear, and knows what is stored and what is not stored.' According to this saying, a monk endowed with five factors—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvaranidahakaṃ sammanneyya, esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it seems fit to the Sangha, the Sangha should appoint the monk named so-and-so as the robe-storer. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me bhante saṅgho, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvaranidahakaṃ sammannati, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno cīvaranidahakassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The Sangha appoints the monk named so-and-so as the robe-storer. If the appointment of the monk named so-and-so as robe-storer is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent. He to whom it is not agreeable, let him speak.

“Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu cīvaranidahako, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti (mahāva. 342) –

The monk named so-and-so has been appointed by the Sangha as the robe-storer. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I understand this.

Iti imāya kammavācāya vā apalokanena vā vuttanayeneva sammannitabbo.

Thus, he should be appointed only by the stated procedure, either by this formal act or by announcement.

196. Bhaṇḍāgārikopi [M 0.0245] “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ bhaṇḍāgārikaṃ [V 0.0231] sammannituṃ, yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na bhayāgatiṃ gaccheyya, guttāguttañca jāneyyā”ti (mahāva. 343) vacanato pañcaṅgasamannāgato bhikkhu “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ bhaṇḍāgārikaṃ sammanneyyā”tiādinā (mahāva. 343) nayena kammavācāya vā apalokanena vā sammannitabbo.

196. Regarding the storekeeper also: “I allow, monks, a monk endowed with five qualities to be appointed as storekeeper: one who would not go astray through desire, would not go astray through ill will, would not go astray through delusion, and would not go astray through fear, and who would know what is secured and what is unsecured.” According to this statement, a monk endowed with these five qualities should be appointed by a formal act or by announcement, following the procedure beginning: “Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should appoint the monk named so-and-so as storekeeper.”

Ettha (mahāva. aṭṭha. 343) ca yattha chadanādīsu koci doso natthi, taṃ guttaṃ. Yattha pana chadanatiṇaṃ vā chadaniṭṭhakā vā yattha katthaci patitā, yena ovassati vā, mūsikādīnaṃ vā paveso hoti, bhittiādīsu vā katthaci chiddaṃ hoti, upacikā vā uṭṭhahanti, taṃ sabbaṃ aguttaṃ nāma. Taṃ sallakkhetvā bhaṇḍāgārikena paṭisaṅkharitabbaṃ. Sītasamaye dvārañca vātapānañca supihitaṃ kātabbaṃ. Sītena hi cīvarāni kaṇṇakitāni honti. Uṇhasamaye antarantarā vātappavesanatthaṃ vivaritabbaṃ. Evaṃ karonto hi guttāguttaṃ jānāti nāma.

And here, a place where there is no defect in the roofing and so forth is secured. But a place where the roofing thatch or roofing tiles have fallen anywhere, through which rain leaks in, or there is an entrance for rats and so forth, or there is a hole anywhere in the walls and so forth, or termites arise—all that is called unsecured. Having noted this, it should be repaired by the storekeeper. In the cold season, the door and the window should be kept well closed, for due to the cold, robes become moldy. In the hot season, they should be opened from time to time to let in air. Indeed, one who acts thus is called one who knows what is secured and unsecured.

197. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhaṇḍāgāraṃ sammannituṃ, yaṃ saṅgho ākaṅkhati vihāraṃ vā aḍḍhayogaṃ vā pāsādaṃ vā hammiyaṃ vā guhaṃ vā”ti (mahāva. 343) vacanato bhaṇḍāgāraṃ sammannitvā ṭhapetabbaṃ. Ettha ca yo ārāmamajjhe ārāmikasāmaṇerādīhi avivitto sabbesaṃ samosaraṇaṭṭhāne vihāro vā aḍḍhayogo vā hoti, so sammannitabbo. Paccantasenāsanaṃ pana na sammannitabbaṃ. Imaṃ pana bhaṇḍāgāraṃ khaṇḍasīmaṃ gantvā khaṇḍasīmāya nisinnehi sammannituṃ na vaṭṭati. Vihāramajjheyeva “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ vihāraṃ bhaṇḍāgāraṃ sammanneyyā”tiādinā (mahāva. 343) nayena kammavācāya vā apalokanena vā sammannitabbaṃ.

197. “I allow, monks, the appointment of a storehouse, whichever the Sangha desires—a dwelling, a half-gabled dwelling, a long-storied building, a flat-roofed building, or a cave.” According to this statement, a storehouse should be established by appointment. And here, whichever dwelling or half-gabled dwelling is in the middle of the monastery, not secluded from monastery attendants, novices, and so on, and is in a gathering place for all—that should be appointed. But a remote lodging should not be appointed. Moreover, it is not proper for this storehouse to be appointed by those who have gone to a separate boundary and are sitting within that separate boundary. It should be appointed right in the middle of the dwelling, either by a formal act or by an announcement, according to the procedure beginning: “Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should appoint the dwelling named so-and-so as a storehouse.”

Cīvarapaṭiggāhakādīhi pana tīhipi attano vattaṃ jānitabbaṃ. Tattha cīvarapaṭiggāhakena tāva yaṃ yaṃ manussā “kālacīvara”nti vā “akālacīvara”nti vā “accekacīvara”nti vā “vassikasāṭika”nti vā “nisīdana”nti vā “paccattharaṇa”nti vā “mukhapuñchanacoḷa”nti vā denti, taṃ sabbaṃ ekarāsiṃ [M 0.0246] katvā missetvā na gaṇhitabbaṃ, visuṃ visuṃ katvāva gaṇhitvā cīvaranidahakassa tatheva ācikkhitvā dātabbaṃ. Cīvaranidahakenapi bhaṇḍāgārikassa dadamānena “idaṃ kālacīvaraṃ…pe… idaṃ mukhapuñchanacoḷa”nti ācikkhitvāva dātabbaṃ. Bhaṇḍāgārikenapi tatheva visuṃ visuṃ saññāṇaṃ katvā ṭhapetabbaṃ. Tato [V 0.0232] saṅghena “kālacīvaraṃ āharā”ti vutte kālacīvarameva dātabbaṃ…pe… “mukhapuñchanacoḷaṃ āharā”ti vutte tadeva dātabbaṃ. Iti bhagavatā cīvarapaṭiggāhako anuññāto, cīvaranidahako anuññāto, bhaṇḍāgāriko anuññāto, bhaṇḍāgāraṃ anuññātaṃ, na bāhulikatāya, na asantuṭṭhitāya, apica kho saṅghānuggahāya. Sace hi āhaṭāhaṭaṃ gahetvā bhikkhū bhājeyyuṃ, neva āhaṭaṃ, na anāhaṭaṃ, na dinnaṃ, na adinnaṃ, na laddhaṃ, na aladdhaṃ jāneyyuṃ, āhaṭāhaṭaṃ therāsane vā dadeyyuṃ, khaṇḍākhaṇḍaṃ vā chinditvā gaṇheyyuṃ, evaṃ sati ayuttaparibhogo ca hoti, na ca sabbesaṃ saṅgaho kato hoti. Bhaṇḍāgāre pana cīvaraṃ ṭhapetvā ussannakāle ekekassa bhikkhuno ticīvaraṃ vā dve dve vā ekekaṃ vā cīvaraṃ dassanti, laddhāladdhaṃ jānissanti, aladdhabhāvaṃ ñatvā saṅgahaṃ kātuṃ maññissantīti.

Moreover, the three—the robe-receiver and the others—should each know their own duties. In this regard, first, the robe-receiver should not gather all the things that people give—whether they are called “seasonal robes,” “out-of-season robes,” “emergency robes,” “rains-bathing cloths,” “sitting cloths,” “spreads,” or “face-wiping cloths”—into a single pile and mix them together. Instead, he should collect them separately and, after informing the robe-storer accordingly, hand them over. Similarly, the robe-storer, when giving them to the storekeeper, should declare, “This is a seasonal robe… this is a face-wiping cloth,” and then hand them over. The storekeeper, in turn, should store them separately, marking them accordingly. Then, when the Sangha says, “Bring the seasonal robe,” only the seasonal robe should be given… or when they say, “Bring the face-wiping cloth,” only that should be given. Thus, the Blessed One has allowed the robe-receiver, the robe-storer, the storekeeper, and the storehouse—not for the sake of abundance, nor for discontent, but for the support of the Sangha. For if the monks were to take and distribute robes as soon as they were brought, they would not know what had been brought or not brought, what had been given or not given, or what had been received or not received. They might place newly brought items on the elder's seat or cut them into pieces and take them. In such a case, improper use would occur, and not everyone would be properly provided for. But by storing the robes in the storehouse and distributing them at a time of abundance—giving each monk either a set of three robes, two robes, or one robe—they will know what has been received and what has not. Recognizing what has not been received, they will consider how to provide for them.

198. Cīvarabhājakovi “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarabhājakaṃ sammannituṃ, yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na bhayāgatiṃ gaccheyya, bhājitābhājitañca jāneyyā”ti (mahāva. 343) vacanato pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatoyeva “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarabhājakaṃ sammanneyyā”ti(mahāva. 343) ādinā nayena kammavācāya vā apalokanena vā sammannitvā ṭhapetabbo.

198. Regarding the distributor of robes also: “I allow, monks, a monk endowed with five qualities to be appointed as a distributor of robes: one who would not go astray through desire, would not go astray through ill will, would not go astray through delusion, would not go astray through fear, and who would know what has been distributed and what has not been distributed.” Because of this statement, only one endowed with these five qualities should be appointed and established by the procedure beginning with, “Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should appoint the monk named so-and-so as the distributor of robes,” either by a formal act or by an announcement.

Ettha sabhāgānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ apāpuṇantampi mahagghacīvaraṃ dento chandāgatiṃ gacchati nāma. Aññesaṃ vuḍḍhatarānaṃ pāpuṇantampi mahagghacīvaraṃ adatvā appagghaṃ dento dosāgatiṃ gacchati nāma. Mohamūḷho cīvaradānavattaṃ ajānanto mohāgatiṃ gacchati nāma. Mukharānaṃ navakānampi bhayena apāpuṇantaṃ eva mahagghaṃ cīvaraṃ dento bhayāgatiṃ gacchati nāma. Yo evaṃ na [M 0.0247] gacchati, sabbesaṃ tulābhūto pamāṇabhūto majjhatto, so sammannitabbo. Tenapi cīvaraṃ bhājentena paṭhamaṃ “idaṃ thūlaṃ, idaṃ saṇhaṃ, idaṃ ghanaṃ, idaṃ tanukaṃ, idaṃ paribhuttaṃ, idaṃ aparibhuttaṃ, idaṃ dīghato ettakaṃ, puthulato ettaka”nti evaṃ vatthāni vicinitvā “idaṃ ettakaṃ agghati, idaṃ ettaka”nti evaṃ agghaparicchedaṃ katvā sace sabbesaṃ ekekameva dasadasaagghanakaṃ pāpuṇāti, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce pāpuṇāti, yaṃ nava vā aṭṭha vā agghati, taṃ aññena ekaagghanakena ca dviagghanakena ca saddhiṃ bandhitvā etena upāyena same paṭivīse ṭhapetvā kuso pātetabbo. Sace ekekassa dīyamāne cīvare divaso nappahoti, dasa dasa bhikkhū gaṇetvā dasa dasa cīvarapaṭivīse ekato bandhitvā bhaṇḍikaṃ katvā eko cīvarapaṭivīso ṭhapetabbo[V 0.0233]. Evaṃ ṭhapitesu cīvarapaṭivīsesu kuso pātetabbo. Tehipi bhikkhūhi puna kusapātaṃ katvā bhājetabbaṃ.

Herein, a bhikkhu who gives a valuable robe to bhikkhus of a similar disposition, even when it is not due to them, is said to be following the wrong path of desire. He who, not giving a valuable robe to other, more senior bhikkhus, even when it is due to them, but instead gives a robe of little value, is said to be following the wrong path of aversion. One who, being bewildered by delusion, does not know the proper procedure for giving robes, is said to be following the wrong path of delusion. He who, out of fear, gives a valuable robe even to junior bhikkhus who are sharp-tongued, when it is not due to them, is said to be following the wrong path of fear. A bhikkhu who does not act in this way, who is for all like a balance, a standard, and impartial—he should be appointed. That appointed bhikkhu, when distributing robes, should first examine the cloths thus: ‘This cloth is coarse, this is fine, this is thick, this is thin, this is used, this is unused, it is this long, and this wide.’ Then, having determined their value thus: ‘This is worth this much, and this is worth that much,’ if a robe worth ten kahāpaṇas reaches each and every one, this is good. If it does not, then a cloth that is worth nine or eight should be bundled together with another worth one or two, and by this method, having arranged them into equal shares, a ticket should be cast. If, when giving the robes to each one, the day is not sufficient, then having counted bhikkhus in groups of ten, ten robe-portions should be bundled together, made into a packet, and set aside as one share of robes. Among the robe-shares thus set aside, a ticket should be cast. Those bhikkhus should then, having cast the ticket again, distribute it among themselves.

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerānaṃ upaḍḍhapaṭivīsaṃ dātu”nti (mahāva. 343) vacanato ye sāmaṇerā attissarā bhikkhusaṅghassa kattabbakammaṃ na karonti, uddesaparipucchāsu yuttā ācariyupajjhāyānaṃyeva vattapaṭivattaṃ karonti, aññesaṃ na karonti, etesaṃyeva upaḍḍhabhāgo dātabbo. Ye pana purebhattañca pacchābhattañca bhikkhusaṅghasseva kattabbakiccaṃ karonti, tesaṃ samako dātabbo. Idañca piṭṭhisamaye uppannena bhaṇḍāgāre ṭhapitena akālacīvareneva kathitaṃ, kālacīvaraṃ pana samakaṃyeva dātabbaṃ. Tatruppādavassāvāsikaṃ sammuñjanībandhanādi saṅghassa phātikammaṃ katvā gahetabbaṃ. Etañhettha sabbesaṃ vattaṃ. Bhaṇḍāgāracīvarepi sace sāmaṇerā āgantvā “bhante, mayaṃ yāguṃ pacāma, bhattaṃ pacāma, khajjakaṃ pacāma, appaharitaṃ karoma, dantakaṭṭhaṃ āharāma, raṅgachalliṃ kappiyaṃ katvā dema, kiṃ amhehi na kataṃ nāmā”ti ukkuṭṭhiṃ karonti, samabhāgova dātabbo. Etaṃyeva virajjhitvā karonti, yesañca karaṇabhāvo na paññāyati, te sandhāya vuttaṃ “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerānaṃ upaḍḍhapaṭivīsaṃ dātu”nti. Kurundiyaṃ pana “sace sāmaṇerā ‘kasmā mayaṃ, bhante, saṅghakammaṃ na karoma, karissāmā’ti yācanti, samapaṭivīso dātabbo”ti vuttaṃ.

Because it was said, “I allow, O monks, to give novices half a share,” those novices who are self-willed, do not perform the work that should be done for the community of monks, are engaged in recitation and questioning, and perform the major and minor duties only for their teachers and preceptors and not for others—to these only, half a share should be given. But as for those who perform the duties that should be done for the community of monks both before and after the meal, to them an equal share should be given. And this was stated only with reference to an unseasonal robe that has arisen outside the Kathina season and has been placed in the storeroom; a seasonal robe, however, should be given equally. The rains-residence robe that has arisen there should be taken after performing a service for the Sangha, such as binding brooms and so forth. This, in this matter, is the duty for all novices. Also regarding the storeroom robe, if novices come and make an outcry, saying, “Venerable sirs, we cook gruel, we cook rice, we cook snacks, we clear away the green growth, we bring tooth-wood, we make the bark for dye suitable and give it. What, indeed, has not been done by us?”—an equal share should be given. It was said with reference to those who do this deficiently, and for whom the fact of their doing is not apparent: “I allow, O monks, to give novices half a share.” But in the Kurundī it is said: “If novices request, saying, ‘Venerable sirs, why should we not do the Sangha's work? We will do it,’ an equal share should be given.”

Sace [M 0.0248] koci bhikkhu sakaṃ bhāgaṃ gahetvā satthaṃ labhitvā nadiṃ vā kantāraṃ vā uttaritvā disāpakkamitukāmo hoti, tassa “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uttarantassa sakaṃ bhāgaṃ dātu”nti (mahāva. 343) vacanato cīvaresu bhaṇḍāgārato bahi nīhaṭesu ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā bhikkhusaṅghe sannipatite cīvarabhājakena “imassa bhikkhuno koṭṭhāsena ettakena bhavitabba”nti takketvā nayaggāhena samabhāgena cīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ. Tulāya tulitamiva hi samasamaṃ dātuṃ na sakkā, tasmā ūnaṃ vā hotu adhikaṃ vā, evaṃ takkena nayena dinnaṃ sudinnaṃ. Neva ūnakaṃ puna dātabbaṃ, nātirittaṃ paṭiggaṇhitabbaṃ. Sace dasa bhikkhū honti, sāṭakāpi daseva, tesu eko dvādasa agghati, sesā dasagghanakā. Sabbesu dasagghanakavasena kuse pātite yassa bhikkhuno dvādasagghanako kuso pātito, tena yattakaṃ tasmiṃ paṭivīse adhikaṃ, tattakaṃ agghanakaṃ yaṃ kiñci attano santakaṃ kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ datvā so atirekabhāgo gahetabbo. Sace sabbesaṃ pañca pañca vatthāni pattāni, sesānipi atthi, ekekaṃ pana na pāpuṇāti, chinditvā dātabbāni.

If any monk, having obtained a caravan, wishes to depart to another region after crossing a river or a wilderness, then in accordance with the saying, “I allow, O monks, that his own share be given to one who is crossing over,” when the robes have been brought out from the storeroom, after the bell has been struck and the community of monks has assembled, the robe-distributor should give the robe with an equal share by a reasoned method, having estimated, “This monk should receive such and such a portion.” Indeed, it is not possible to give exactly equally, as if weighed with a scale; therefore, whether it is less or more, what is given thus by this reasoned method is well-given. A deficiency should not be given again, nor should an excess be taken back. If there are ten monks and also ten robes, and among them one is worth twelve while the others are worth ten each, when lots are cast for all on the basis of a value of ten each, the monk for whom the lot worth twelve is cast must give an allowable requisite of his own equal in value to the excess in that share; then that excess portion may be taken. If all have received five cloths each, and there are still remaining cloths, but not enough for one more each, they should be cut and distributed.

Chindantena [V 0.0234] ca aḍḍhamaṇḍalādīnaṃ vā upāhanatthavikādīnaṃ vā pahonakāni khaṇḍāni katvā dātabbāni. Heṭṭhimaparicchedena caturaṅgulavitthārampi anuvātappahonakāyāmaṃ khaṇḍaṃ katvā dātuṃ vaṭṭati, aparibhogaṃ pana na kātabbaṃ. Sacepi ekassa bhikkhuno koṭṭhāse ekaṃ vā dve vā vatthāni nappahonti, tattha aññaṃ sāmaṇakaṃ parikkhāraṃ ṭhapetvā yo tena tussati, tassa taṃ bhāgaṃ katvā pacchā kusapāto kātabbo. Sace dasa dasa bhikkhū gaṇetvā vaggaṃ karontānaṃ eko vaggo na pūrati, aṭṭha vā nava vā honti, tesaṃ aṭṭha vā nava vā koṭṭhāsā “tumhe ime gahetvā visuṃ bhājethā”ti dātabbā. Evaṃ datvā pacchā kusapāto kātabbo.

And by cutting, pieces suitable for half-circles and the like, or for sandal-bags and the like, should be made and given. At a minimum, it is proper to make and give a piece with a width of four finger-breadths and a length suitable for a border; however, it should not be made unusable. If in one portion one or two cloths are lacking, another requisite suitable for a monk should be placed there. That portion is then to be assigned to whichever bhikkhu is satisfied with it, after which the casting of lots should be done. If, when forming groups by counting ten bhikkhus at a time, one group is not complete—there being eight or nine—those eight or nine portions should be given to them, saying, 'You, take these and divide them separately among yourselves.' Having given thus, the casting of lots should be done afterwards.

199. Idāni “aṭṭhimā, bhikkhave, mātikā cīvarassa uppādāya, sīmāya deti, katikāya deti, bhikkhāpaññattiyā deti, saṅghassa deti, ubhatosaṅghassa deti, vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa deti, ādissa deti, puggalassa detī”ti (mahāva. 379) cīvarānaṃ paṭilābhakhettadassanatthaṃ yā tā aṭṭha mātikā vuttā, tāsaṃ vasena vinicchayo veditabbo.

199. Now, 'Bhikkhus, these are the eight mātikās for the arising of robes: it is given on account of a boundary; it is given by agreement; it is given on account of an established alms-round; it is given to the Saṅgha; it is given to the double Saṅgha; it is given to the Saṅgha that has completed the rains-residence; it is given by dedication; it is given to an individual.' For the purpose of showing the field for the acquisition of robes, these eight mātikās have been stated; the analysis should be understood according to them.

Tattha [M 0.0249] “sīmāya dammī”ti evaṃ sīmaṃ parāmasitvā dento sīmāya deti nāma. Evaṃ sīmāya dinnaṃ yāvatikā bhikkhū antosīmāgatā, tehi bhājetabbaṃ. Sīmā ca nāmesā khaṇḍasīmā upacārasīmā samānasaṃvāsasīmā avippavāsasīmā lābhasīmā gāmasīmā nigamasīmā nagarasīmā abbhantarasīmā udakukkhepasīmā janapadasīmā raṭṭhasīmā rajjasīmā dīpasīmā cakkavāḷasīmāti pannarasavidhā hoti. Tattha khaṇḍasīmā sīmākathāyaṃ vuttāva. Upacārasīmā nāma parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepena, aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānena paricchinnā hoti. Apica bhikkhūnaṃ dhuvasannipātaṭṭhānato pariyante ṭhitabhojanasālato vā nibaddhavasanaāvāsato vā thāmamajjhimassa purisassa dvinnaṃ leḍḍupātānaṃ anto upacārasīmāti veditabbā. Sā pana āvāsesu vaḍḍhantesu vaḍḍhati, parihāyantesu parihāyati. Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana “bhikkhūsupi vaḍḍhantesu vaḍḍhatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tasmā sace vihāre sannipatitabhikkhūhi saddhiṃ ekābaddhā hutvā yojanasatampi pūretvā nisīdanti, yojanasatampi upacārasīmāva hoti, sabbesaṃ lābho pāpuṇāti. Samānasaṃvāsaavippavāsasīmādvayampi vuttameva. Lābhasīmā nāma neva sammāsambuddhena anuññātā, na dhammasaṅgāhakattherehi ṭhapitā, apica kho rājarājamahāmattā vihāraṃ kāretvā gāvutaṃ vā aḍḍhayojanaṃ vā yojanaṃ vā samantato paricchinditvā “ayaṃ amhākaṃ vihārassa lābhasīmā”ti nāmalikhitake thambhe nikhaṇitvā “yaṃ etthantare uppajjati, sabbaṃ amhākaṃ vihārassa demā”ti sīmā ṭhapenti, ayaṃ lābhasīmā nāma. Gāmanigamanagaraabbhantaraudakukkhepasīmāpi vuttā eva.

Therein, one who gives while referring to the boundary, saying, 'I give to the Saṅgha in the boundary,' is called one who gives to the Saṅgha in the boundary. What is thus given by means of the boundary should be shared by however many bhikkhus have come within the boundary. And this boundary is of fifteen kinds: a sectional boundary, an adjacent boundary, a shared-communion boundary, a non-separation boundary, a gains boundary, a village boundary, a market-town boundary, a city boundary, an inner boundary, a water-throwing boundary, a district boundary, a province boundary, a kingdom boundary, an island boundary, and a world-system boundary. Among these, the sectional boundary has already been spoken of in the discourse on boundaries. The adjacent boundary is defined by the enclosure of an enclosed monastery, and for an unenclosed one, by a place suitable for an enclosure. Furthermore, the area within two stone-throws of a man of average strength—from the bhikkhus' regular assembly place, or from the dining hall situated at the edge, or from their fixed dwelling place—should be known as the adjacent boundary. That boundary, however, expands when the dwellings increase and contracts when they diminish. In the Mahāpaccariya, however, it is said: 'It also expands when the bhikkhus increase.' Therefore, if, together with the bhikkhus assembled in the monastery, they sit as a single continuous group, filling even a hundred yojanas, then even a hundred yojanas becomes the adjacent boundary, and the gain reaches all of them. The pair of boundaries, the shared-communion boundary and the non-separation boundary, have also already been spoken of. The gains boundary was neither authorized by the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One nor established by the Elders who compiled the Dhamma. Rather, kings and royal ministers, having had a monastery built, demarcate a gāvuta, or half a yojana, or a yojana all around, and having erected pillars with inscriptions saying, 'This is the gains boundary of our monastery,' they establish the boundary, saying, 'Whatever revenue arises within this area, we give it all to our monastery.' This is called the gains boundary. The village, market-town, city, inner, and water-throwing boundaries have also been spoken of.

Janapadasīmā [V 0.0235] nāma kāsikosalaraṭṭhādīnaṃ anto bahū janapadā honti, tattha ekeko janapadaparicchedo janapadasīmā. Raṭṭhasīmā nāma kāsikosalādiraṭṭhaparicchedo. Rajjasīmā nāma “coḷabhogo keraḷabhogo”ti evaṃ ekekassa rañño āṇāpavattiṭṭhānaṃ. Dīpasīmā nāma samuddantena paricchinnamahādīpā ca antaradīpā ca. Cakkavāḷasīmā cakkavāḷapabbateneva paricchinnā. Evametāsu sīmāsu khaṇḍasīmāya kenaci kammena sannipatitaṃ saṅghaṃ disvā “ettheva sīmāya saṅghassa demī”ti vutte yāvatikā bhikkhū antokhaṇḍasīmāgatā, tehi bhājetabbaṃ. Tesaṃyeva hi taṃ pāpuṇāti, aññesaṃ sīmantarikāya vā upacārasīmāya [M 0.0250] vā ṭhitānampi na pāpuṇāti. Khaṇḍasīmāya ṭhite pana rukkhe vā pabbate vā ṭhitassa heṭṭhā vā pathavīvemajjhagatassa pāpuṇātiyeva. “Imissā upacārasīmāya saṅghassa dammī”ti dinnaṃ pana khaṇḍasīmāsīmantarikāsu ṭhitānampi pāpuṇāti. “Samānasaṃvāsasīmāya dammī”ti dinnaṃ pana khaṇḍasīmāsīmantarikāsu ṭhitānaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Avippavāsasīmālābhasīmāsu dinnaṃ tāsu sīmāsu antogatānaṃ pāpuṇāti. Gāmasīmādīsu dinnaṃ tāsaṃ sīmānaṃ abbhantare baddhasīmāya ṭhitānampi pāpuṇāti. Abbhantarasīmāudakukkhepasīmāsu dinnaṃ tattha antogatānaṃyeva pāpuṇāti. Janapadaraṭṭharajjadīpacakkavāḷasīmāsupi gāmasīmādīsu vuttasadisoyeva vinicchayo.

The district boundary (janapadasīmā) is so-called: within provinces such as Kāsi and Kosala, there are many districts; there, the demarcation of each district is a district boundary. The province boundary (raṭṭhasīmā) is the demarcation of provinces such as Kāsi and Kosala. The kingdom boundary (rajjasīmā) is the place where the authority of each king extends, such as “the domain of the Colas, the domain of the Keralas.” The island boundary (dīpasīmā) refers to the great islands and smaller islands enclosed by the ocean. The world-system boundary (cakkavāḷasīmā) is enclosed by the Cakkavāḷa mountain itself. Thus, among these boundaries, if, having seen a Saṅgha assembled for some formal act within a sectional boundary (khaṇḍasīmā), one says, “I give to the Saṅgha here within this boundary,” it should be distributed by however many bhikkhus have arrived within the sectional boundary. For it reaches only them; it does not reach others standing in the intermediate boundary (sīmantarikā) or the adjacent boundary (upacārasīmā). However, for one standing within the sectional boundary—whether on a tree, a mountain, or below in the middle of the earth—it certainly reaches them. But if something is given with the words, “I give to the Saṅgha in this adjacent boundary,” it reaches even those standing in the sectional and intermediate boundaries. If something is given with the words, “I give in the shared-communion boundary (samānasaṃvāsasīmā),” it does not reach those standing in the sectional and intermediate boundaries. What is given in the non-separation (avippavāsasīmā) and gains (lābhasīmā) boundaries reaches those who are within those boundaries. What is given in village boundaries (gāmasīmā) and others reaches even those standing in a consecrated boundary (baddhasīmā) inside those boundaries. What is given in the inner boundary (abbhantarasīmā) and the water-throwing boundary (udakukkhepasīmā) reaches only those who are within them. In the district, province, kingdom, island, and world-system boundaries, the ruling is the same as that stated for village boundaries and others.

Sace pana jambudīpe ṭhito “tambavaṇṇidīpe saṅghassa dammī”ti vadati, tambapaṇṇidīpato ekopi āgantvā sabbesaṃ gaṇhituṃ labhati. Sacepi tatreva eko sabhāgabhikkhu sabhāgānaṃ bhāgaṃ gaṇhāti, na vāretabbo. Evaṃ tāva yo sīmaṃ parāmasitvā deti, tassa dāne vinicchayo veditabbo. Yo pana “asukasīmāya”nti vattuṃ na jānāti, kevalaṃ “sīmā”ti vacanamattameva jānanto vihāraṃ āgantvā “sīmāya dammī”ti vā “sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghassa dammī”ti vā bhaṇati, so pucchitabbo “sīmā nāma bahuvidhā, katarasīmaṃ sandhāya bhaṇasī”ti. Sace vadati “ahaṃ ‘asukasīmā’ti na jānāmi, sīmaṭṭhakasaṅgho bhājetvā gaṇhatū”ti, katarasīmāya bhājetabbaṃ? Mahāsīvatthero kirāha “avippavāsasīmāyā”ti. Tato naṃ āhaṃsu “avippavāsasīmā nāma tiyojanāpi hoti, evaṃ sante tiyojane ṭhitā lābhaṃ gaṇhissanti, tiyojane ṭhatvā āgantukavattaṃ pūretvā ārāmaṃ pavisitabbaṃ bhavissati, gamiko tiyojanaṃ gantvā senāsanaṃ āpucchissati, nissayappaṭipannassa tiyojanātikkame nissayo paṭippassambhissati, pārivāsikena tiyojanaṃ atikkamitvā aruṇaṃ uṭṭhapetabbaṃ bhavissati, bhikkhuniyā tiyojane ṭhatvā ārāmappavesanaṃ āpucchitabbaṃ bhavissati, sabbampetaṃ upacārasīmāparicchedavaseneva kātuṃ vaṭṭati, tasmā upacārasīmāya bhājetabba”nti.

If, however, a person standing in Jambudīpa says, 'I give to the Saṅgha in Tambapaṇṇidīpa,' even one monk coming from Tambapaṇṇidīpa is able to receive the share for all. Even if, right there, one monk of the same affiliation takes the share for those of his affiliation, he should not be prevented. Thus, this is how the decision should be understood regarding the gift of one who gives by specifying the boundary. But as for one who does not know how to say, 'in such-and-such a boundary,' and, knowing only the mere word 'boundary,' comes to the monastery and says, 'I give to the boundary,' or 'I give to the Saṅgha established in the boundary,' he should be asked, 'Boundaries are of many kinds; which boundary do you refer to?' If he says, 'I do not know "such-and-such a boundary"; let the Saṅgha established in the boundary divide and take it,' in which boundary should it be divided? The Elder Mahāsīva reportedly said, 'It should be divided in the non-separation boundary.' Then they said to him, 'A non-separation boundary can be as much as three yojanas. In that case, monks standing within three yojanas would receive the gain. One would have to fulfill the duties for an incoming monk while standing within the three yojanas before entering the monastery. A traveling monk would have to ask leave of his lodging after having gone three yojanas. For a monk who has undertaken dependence, the dependence would be terminated upon exceeding three yojanas. A monk on probation would have to let dawn arise after having crossed three yojanas. A bhikkhunī would have to ask permission to enter the monastery while standing within the three yojanas. All this is fittingly done only by defining an access boundary. Therefore, it should be divided within the access boundary.'

200. Katikāya [V 0.0236] detīti ettha pana katikā nāma samānalābhakatikā. Tatrevaṃ katikā kātabbā, ekasmiṃ vihāre sannipatitehi bhikkhūhi yaṃ vihāraṃ saṅgaṇhitukāmā samānalābhaṃ kātuṃ icchanti[M 0.0251], tassa nāmaṃ gahetvā “asuko nāma vihāro porāṇako”ti vā “buddhādhivuttho”ti vā “appalābho”ti vā ya kiñci kāraṇaṃ vatvā “taṃ vihāraṃ iminā vihārena saddhiṃ ekalābhaṃ kātuṃ saṅghassa ruccatī”ti tikkhattuṃ sāvetabbaṃ. Ettāvatā tasmiṃ vihāre nisinnopi idha nisinnova hoti. Tasmiṃ vihārepi saṅghena evameva kātabbaṃ. Ettāvatā idha nisinnopi tasmiṃ nisinnova hoti. Ekasmiṃ vihāre lābhe bhājiyamāne itarasmiṃ ṭhitassa bhāgaṃ gahetuṃ vaṭṭati. Evaṃ ekena vihārena saddhiṃ bahūpi āvāsā ekalābhā kātabbā. Evañca kate ekasmiṃ āvāse dinne sabbattha dinnaṃ hoti.

200. In the context of “one gives by agreement,” “agreement” here means an agreement for equal gains. In that case, the agreement should be made thus: when monks assembled in one monastery wish to support a certain monastery and make it have equal gains, they should take its name and, stating some reason whatsoever—such as, “The monastery named so-and-so is ancient,” or “It was dwelt in by the Buddha,” or “It has few gains”—announce three times: “It is agreeable to the Saṅgha to make that monastery have equal gains with this monastery.” By this much, one sitting in that monastery is as one sitting here. In that other monastery also, it should be done by the Saṅgha in just the same way. By this much, one sitting here is as one sitting there. When gains are being distributed in one monastery, it is allowable for one staying in the other to take a share. Thus, even many residences may be made to have equal gains with one monastery. And when this is done, what is given in one residence is given everywhere.

201. Bhikkhāpaññatti nāma attano pariccāgapaññāpanaṭṭhānaṃ, yattha saṅghassa dhuvakārā karīyanti. Ettha ca yasmiṃ vihāre imassa cīvaradāyakassa santakaṃ saṅghassa pākavaṭṭaṃ vā vattati, yasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhū attano bhāraṃ katvā sadā gehe bhojeti, yattha vā tena āvāso kārito, salākabhattādīni vā nibaddhāni, ime dhuvakārā nāma. Yena pana sakalopi vihāro patiṭṭhāpito, tattha vattabbameva natthi, tasmā sace so “yattha mayhaṃ dhuvakārā karīyanti, tattha dammī”ti vā “tattha dethā”ti vā bhaṇati, bahūsu cepi ṭhānesu dhuvakārā honti, sabbattha dinnameva hoti. Sace pana ekasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhū bahutarā honti, tehi vattabbaṃ “tumhākaṃ dhuvakāre ekattha bhikkhū bahū, ekattha appakā”ti. Sace “bhikkhugaṇanāya gaṇhathā”ti bhaṇati, tathā bhājetvā gaṇhituṃ vaṭṭati. Ettha ca vatthabhesajjādi appakampi sukhena bhājīyati. Yadi pana mañco vā pīṭhaṃ vā ekameva hoti, taṃ pucchitvā yassa vihārassa, ekavihārepi vā yassa senāsanassa so vicāreti, tattha dātabbaṃ. Sacepi “asukabhikkhu gaṇhatū”ti vadati, vaṭṭati. Atha “mayhaṃ dhuvakāre dethā”ti vatvā avicāretvā gacchati, saṅghassapi vicāretuṃ vaṭṭati. Evaṃ pana vicāretabbaṃ, “saṅghattherassa vasanaṭṭhāne dethā”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace tattha senāsanaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ hoti, yattha nappahoti, tattha dātabbaṃ. Sace eko bhikkhu “mayhaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne senāsanaparibhogabhaṇḍaṃ natthī”ti vadati, tattha dātabbaṃ.

201. What is called Bhikkhāpaññatti is the place for making known one's own donation, where permanent services for the Saṅgha are performed. And here, in whichever monastery the duty of providing cooked food for the Saṅgha, belonging to this robe-donor, is ongoing; in whichever monastery he, having made it his own responsibility, always feeds the monks in his house; or where a dwelling has been built by him; or where regular offerings like ticket-meals are established—these are called 'permanent services.' However, for one by whom an entire monastery has been established, there is nothing to be said. Therefore, if he says, 'I give it where my permanent services are performed,' or 'Give it there,' even if there are permanent services in many places, it is indeed given in all those places. But if in one monastery the monks are more numerous, they should say, 'With regard to your permanent services, in one place there are many monks, in another, few.' If he says, 'Take it according to the count of monks,' then it is proper to divide and take it accordingly. And here, even a small amount of cloth, medicine, and so on, is easily divided. But if there is only one bed or bench, after asking him, it should be given to whichever monastery—or even in a single monastery, to whichever lodging—he decides upon. Even if he says, 'Let such-and-such a monk take it,' it is proper. Then, if he says, 'Give it to my place of permanent service,' and departs without deciding, it is also proper for the Saṅgha to decide. However, the deliberation should be thus: it should be said, 'Give it to the dwelling place of the Elder of the Saṅgha.' If the lodging there is complete, it should be given where it is not sufficient. If one monk says, 'In my dwelling place, there are no furnishings for the use of a lodging,' it should be given there.

202. Saṅghassa detīti ettha pana sace vihāraṃ pavisitvā “imāni cīvarāni saṅghassa dammī”ti deti, upacārasīmāya ṭhitena saṅghena ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā [M 0.0252] kālaṃ ghosetvā bhājetabbāni, sīmaṭṭhakassa asampattassapi bhāgaṃ gaṇhanto na vāretabbo. Vihāro mahā hoti, therāsanato [V 0.0237] paṭṭhāya vatthesu dīyamānesu alasajātikā mahātherā pacchā āgacchanti, “bhante, vīsativassānaṃ dīyati, tumhākaṃ ṭhitikā atikkantā”ti na vattabbā, ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvā tesaṃ datvā pacchā ṭhitibhāya dātabbaṃ. “Asukavihāre kira bahu cīvaraṃ uppanna”nti sutvā yojanantarikavihāratopi bhikkhū āgacchanti, sampattasampattānaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya dātabbaṃ, asampattānampi upacārasīmaṃ paviṭṭhānaṃ antevāsikādīsu gaṇhantesu dātabbameva. “Bahiupacārasīmāya ṭhitānaṃ dethā”ti vadanti, na dātabbaṃ. Sace pana upacārasīmaṃ okkantehi ekābaddhā hutvā attano vihāradvāre vā antovihāreyeva vā honti, parisavasena vaḍḍhitā nāma sīmā hoti, tasmā dātabbaṃ. Saṅghanavakassa dinnepi pacchā āgatānaṃ dātabbameva. Dutiyabhāge pana therāsanaṃ āruḷhe āgatānaṃ paṭhamabhāgo na pāpuṇāti, dutiyabhāgato vassaggena dātabbaṃ.

202. Regarding 'gives to the Saṅgha': in this case, if one enters the monastery and gives, saying, 'These robes I give to the Saṅgha,' they should be distributed by the Saṅgha standing within the precincts after striking the bell and announcing the time. One who takes the share of a person who is within the boundary but has not yet arrived should not be prevented. If the monastery is large, and while robes are being distributed starting from the elder's seat, some senior monks of an indolent nature arrive late, it should not be said, 'Venerable Sirs, it is being given to those of twenty vassas; your sequence has passed.' Their sequence should be set aside and given to them, and afterwards, the distribution should proceed according to the sequence. Having heard, 'It is said that many robes have arisen in such-and-such a monastery,' monks come even from a monastery a yojana away. It should be given to those who have arrived, starting from the place where they are standing. Even for those who have not arrived, if they have entered the precincts, when their pupils and others take a share, it should certainly be given. If they say, 'Give to those standing outside the precincts,' it should not be given. However, if, having become contiguous with those who have entered the precincts, they are at their own monastery gate or just inside the monastery, the boundary is considered to be extended by way of the assembly; therefore, it should be given. Even after it has been given to the most junior monk of the Saṅgha, it should certainly be given to those who arrive later. But regarding the second portion, for those who arrive after the distribution has reached the elder's seat, the first portion does not accrue to them; from the second portion, it should be given according to seniority by vassa.

Ekasmiṃ vihāre dasa bhikkhū honti, dasa vatthāni “saṅghassa demā”ti denti, pāṭekkaṃ bhājetabbāni. Sace “sabbāneva amhākaṃ pāpuṇantī”ti gahetvā gacchanti, duppāpitāni ceva duggahitāni ca, gatagataṭṭhāne saṅghikāneva honti. Ekaṃ pana uddharitvā “idaṃ tumhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti saṅghattherassa pāpetvā “sesāni amhākaṃ pāpuṇantī”ti gahetuṃ vaṭṭati. Ekameva vatthaṃ “saṅghassa demā”ti āharanti, abhājetvāva “amhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti gaṇhanti, duppāpitañceva duggahitañca. Satthakena vā haliddiādinā vā lekhaṃ katvā ekakoṭṭhāsaṃ “idaṃ ṭhānaṃ tumhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti saṅghattherassa pāpetvā “sesaṃ amhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti gahetuṃ vaṭṭati. Yaṃ pana vatthasseva pupphaṃ vā vali vā, tena paricchedaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Sace ekaṃ tantaṃ uddharitvā “idaṃ ṭhānaṃ tumhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti therassa datvā “sesaṃ amhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti gaṇhanti, vaṭṭati. Khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ chinditvā bhājiyamānaṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

In one monastery, there are ten monks, and they give ten robes, saying, 'We give these to the Saṅgha.' They should be divided individually. If they take them all, thinking, 'All of these accrue to us,' then they are improperly caused to be received and improperly taken, and wherever they have gone, they remain property of the Saṅgha. However, if they set one aside and cause it to accrue to the senior monk of the Saṅgha, saying, 'This one accrues to you,' then it is allowable to take the rest, thinking, 'The remaining ones accrue to us.' If they bring just one robe, saying, 'We give this to the Saṅgha,' and take it without dividing it, thinking, 'This accrues to us,' then it is improperly caused to be received and improperly taken. If, having made a mark with a small knife or with turmeric and so on, they cause one portion to accrue to the senior monk of the Saṅgha, saying, 'This place accrues to you,' then it is allowable to take the rest, thinking, 'The remainder accrues to us.' But as for a flower-pattern or a fold of the robe itself, it is not allowable to make a division with that. If they pull out one thread, give it to the elder, saying, 'This place accrues to you,' and take the rest, thinking, 'The remainder accrues to us,' it is allowable. Being divided after cutting it piece by piece is indeed allowable.

Ekabhikkhuke vihāre saṅghassa cīvaresu uppannesu sace pubbe vuttanayeneva so bhikkhu “sabbāni mayhaṃ pāpuṇantī”ti gaṇhāti, suggahitāni[M 0.0253], ṭhitikā pana na tiṭṭhati. Sace ekekaṃ uddharitvā “idaṃ mayhaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti gaṇhāti, ṭhitikā tiṭṭhati. Tattha aṭṭhitāya ṭhitikāya puna aññasmiṃ cīvare uppanne sace eko bhikkhu āgacchati, majjhe chinditvā dvīhipi gahetabbaṃ. Ṭhitāya ṭhitikāya puna aññasmiṃ cīvare uppanne sace navakataro āgacchati, ṭhitikā heṭṭhā orohati. Sace vuḍḍhataro āgacchati, ṭhitikā uddhaṃ ārohati. Atha añño natthi, puna attano pāpetvā gahetabbaṃ. “Saṅghassa demā”ti vā “bhikkhusaṅghassa demā”ti vā yena kenaci ākārena saṅghaṃ āmasitvā dinnaṃ pana paṃsukūlikānaṃ na vaṭṭati “gahapaticīvaraṃ [V 0.0238] paṭikkhipāmi, paṃsukūlikaṅgaṃ samādiyāmī”ti vuttattā, na pana akappiyattā. Bhikkhusaṅghena apaloketvā dinnampi na gahetabbaṃ. Yaṃ pana bhikkhu attano santakaṃ deti, taṃ bhikkhudattiyaṃ nāma vaṭṭati, paṃsukūlaṃ pana na hoti. Evaṃ santepi dhutaṅgaṃ na bhijjati. “Bhikkhūnaṃ dema, therānaṃ demā”ti vutte pana paṃsukūlikānampi vaṭṭati, “idaṃ vatthaṃ saṅghassa dema, iminā upāhanatthavikapattatthavikaāyogaaṃsabaddhakādīni karontū”ti dinnampi vaṭṭati. Pattatthavikādīnaṃ atthāya dinnāni bahūnipi honti, cīvaratthāyapi pahonti, tato cīvaraṃ katvā pārupituṃ vaṭṭati. Sace pana saṅgho bhājitātirittāni vatthāni chinditvā upāhanatthavikādīnaṃ atthāya bhājeti, tato gahetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Sāmikehi vicāritameva hi vaṭṭati, na itaraṃ. Paṃsukūlikaṃ “saṅghassa dhammakaraṇapaṭādīnaṃ atthāya demā”ti vuttepi gahetuṃ vaṭṭati, parikkhāro nāma paṃsukūlikānampi icchitabbo. Yaṃ tattha atirekaṃ hoti, taṃ cīvarepi upanetuṃ vaṭṭati. Suttaṃ saṅghassa denti, paṃsukūlikehipi gahetabbaṃ. Ayaṃ tāva vihāraṃ pavisitvā “imāni cīvarāni saṅghassa dammī”ti dinnesu vinicchayo. Sace pana bahiupacārasīmāya addhānamaggappaṭipanne bhikkhū disvā “saṅghassa dammī”ti saṅghattherassa vā saṅghanavakassa vā āroceti, sacepi yojanaṃ pharitvā parisā ṭhitā hoti, ekābaddhā ce, sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Ye pana dvādasahi hatthehi parisaṃ asampattā, tesaṃ na pāpuṇāti.

In a monastery with a single bhikkhu, when robes for the Saṅgha have arisen, if that bhikkhu takes them in the manner previously stated, saying, 'All these accrue to me,' they are well-taken, but the sequence does not stand. If, having selected them one by one, he takes them, saying, 'This accrues to me,' the sequence stands. Therein, when the sequence is not standing and another robe arises, if one bhikkhu arrives, it should be divided in the middle and taken by both. When the sequence is standing and another robe arises, if a more junior bhikkhu arrives, the sequence descends. If a more senior bhikkhu arrives, the sequence ascends. Then, if there is no other bhikkhu, it should be taken again after causing it to accrue to oneself. However, what is given after addressing the Saṅgha in any way, by saying, 'We give to the Saṅgha,' or 'We give to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha,' is not allowable for rag-robe wearers because of the statement, 'I reject a householder's robe, I undertake the rag-robe-wearer's practice,' but not because of it being unsuitable. Even what is given by the Bhikkhu Saṅgha after a formal announcement should not be taken. But what a bhikkhu gives that is his own property, that, called a 'gift from a bhikkhu', is allowable; however, it is not a rag-robe. Even so, the ascetic practice is not broken. But when it is said, 'We give to the bhikkhus,' or 'We give to the elders,' it is allowable even for rag-robe wearers. What is given with the words, 'We give this cloth to the Saṅgha, with this let them make cases for sandals, cases for bowls, waistbands, shoulder straps, and so on,' is also allowable. Many cloths may be given for the purpose of bowl cases and so on, and they may also be sufficient for robes; it is allowable to make a robe from that and wear it. However, if the Saṅgha, having cut up cloths remaining after distribution, distributes them for the purpose of sandal cases and so on, it is not allowable to take from that. Indeed, only what has been arranged by the owners is allowable, not the other. Even when it is said regarding a rag-robe cloth, 'We give this to the Saṅgha for the purpose of water-strainer cloths and so on,' it is allowable to take it, for a requisite is indeed to be desired even by rag-robe wearers. Whatever is surplus there, it is allowable to apply that to a robe as well. They give thread to the Saṅgha; it should also be taken by rag-robe wearers. This, for now, is the ruling concerning what is given upon entering a monastery with the words, 'I give these robes to the Saṅgha.' However, if a person, having seen bhikkhus who have set out on a long road outside the monastery precincts, announces to the elder of the Saṅgha or to the junior of the Saṅgha, 'I give to the Saṅgha,' then even if the assembly is standing, covering a yojana, if it is a single, connected group, it accrues to all. But for those who have not reached the assembly by twelve cubits, it does not accrue to them.

203. Ubhatosaṅghassa detīti ettha “ubhatosaṅghassa dammī”ti vuttepi “dvidhā saṅghassa dammī”ti, “dvinnaṃ saṅghānaṃ dammī”ti, “bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunīsaṅghassa [M 0.0254] ca dammī”ti vuttepi ubhatosaṅghassa dinnameva hoti. Tattha sace bahukāpi bhikkhū honti, ekā bhikkhunī hoti, upaḍḍhaṃ dātabbaṃ, dve bhāge same katvā eko bhāgo dātabboti attho. Sace bahukāpi bhikkhuniyo honti, eko bhikkhu hoti, upaḍḍhaṃ dātabbaṃ. “Ubhatosaṅghassa ca tuyhañca dammī”ti vutte sace dasa dasa bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca honti, ekavīsati paṭivīse katvā eko puggalassa dātabbo, dasa bhikkhusaṅghassa, dasa bhikkhunīsaṅghassa. Yena puggaliko laddho, so saṅghatopi attano vassaggena gahetuṃ labhati. Kasmā? Ubhatosaṅghaggahaṇena gahitattā. “Ubhatosaṅghassa ca cetiyassa ca dammī”ti vuttepi eseva nayo. Idha pana cetiyassa saṅghato pāpuṇanakoṭṭhāso nāma natthi, ekapuggalassa pattakoṭṭhāsasamova koṭṭhāso hoti. “Ubhatosaṅghassa ca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vutte pana dvāvīsati koṭṭhāse katvā dasa bhikkhūnaṃ, dasa bhikkhunīnaṃ, eko puggalassa, eko cetiyassa dātabbo. Tattha puggalo saṅghatopi attano vassaggena gahetuṃ labhati, cetiyassa ekoyeva.

203. Here, regarding 'gives to both Saṅghas,' even if it is said, 'I give to both Saṅghas,' or 'I give to the Saṅgha in two divisions,' or 'I give to two Saṅghas,' or 'I give to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha and to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha,' it is indeed given to both Saṅghas. In that case, if there are many bhikkhus and one bhikkhunī, half should be given; meaning, having made two equal shares, one share is to be given. If there are many bhikkhunīs and one bhikkhu, half should be given. When it is said, 'I give to both Saṅghas and to you,' if there are ten bhikkhus and ten bhikkhunīs, having made twenty-one shares, one is to be given to the individual, ten to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha, and ten to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha. The one who has received the individual share is able to take also from the Saṅgha's portion according to his seniority in the rains. Why? Because he is included by the term 'both Saṅghas.' When it is said, 'I give to both Saṅghas and to the shrine,' this same method applies. Here, however, for the shrine, there is no share that accrues from the Saṅgha; its share is equal to the share obtained by a single individual. But when it is said, 'I give to both Saṅghas, to you, and to the shrine,' having made twenty-two shares, ten are to be given to the bhikkhus, ten to the bhikkhunīs, one to the individual, and one to the shrine. In that case, the individual is able to take also from the Saṅgha's portion according to his seniority in the rains; for the shrine, there is only one share.

“Bhikkhusaṅghassa [V 0.0239] ca bhikkhunīnañca dammī”ti vutte pana na majjhe bhinditvā dātabbaṃ, bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca gaṇetvā dātabbaṃ. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañcā”ti vutte pana puggalo visuṃ na labhati, pāpuṇanaṭṭhānato ekameva labhati. Kasmā? Bhikkhusaṅghaggahaṇena gahitattā. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vuttepi cetiyassa ekapuggalapaṭivīso labbhati, puggalassa visuṃ na labbhati, tasmā ekaṃ cetiyassa datvā avasesaṃ bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca gaṇetvā bhājetabbaṃ.

However, when it is said, 'I give to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha and to the bhikkhunīs,' it should not be given by splitting it in the middle, but should be given after counting the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs. When it is said, 'I give to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha and to the bhikkhunīs and to you,' the individual does not receive a separate share; from the place of accrual, he receives only one share. Why? Because he is included by the term 'Bhikkhu Saṅgha.' Even when it is said, 'I give to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha and to the bhikkhunīs, to you, and to the shrine,' the shrine receives a share for one individual, but the individual does not receive a separate share. Therefore, after giving one share to the shrine, the remainder should be divided after counting the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs.

“Bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca dammī”ti vuttepi majjhe bhinditvā na dātabbaṃ, puggalagaṇanāya eva vibhajitabbaṃ. “Bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañca, bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca cetiyassa ca, bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti evaṃ vuttepi cetiyassa ekapaṭivīso labbhati, puggalassa visuṃ natthi, bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca gaṇetvā eva bhājetabbaṃ. Yathā ca bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ādiṃ katvā nayo nīto, evaṃ bhikkhunīsaṅghaṃ ādiṃ katvāpi netabbo.

Even when it is said, 'I give to the bhikkhus and to the bhikkhunīs,' it should not be given by splitting it in the middle; it should be divided only by the count of individuals. Even when it is said thus: 'I give to the bhikkhus and to the bhikkhunīs and to you'; 'to the bhikkhus and to the bhikkhunīs and to the shrine'; or 'to the bhikkhus and to the bhikkhunīs and to you and to the shrine,' the shrine receives a share for one person, but there is no separate share for the individual. It should be divided only after counting the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs. And just as the method has been set forth beginning with the Bhikkhu Saṅgha, so too should it be set forth beginning with the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha.

“Bhikkhusaṅghassa [M 0.0255] ca tuyhañcā”ti vutte puggalassa visuṃ na labbhati, vassaggeneva gahetabbaṃ. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca cetiyassa cā”ti vutte pana cetiyassa visuṃ paṭivīso labbhati. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vuttepi cetiyasseva visuṃ labbhati, na puggalassa. “Bhikkhūnañca tuyhañcā”ti vuttepi visuṃ na labbhati, “bhikkhūnañca cetiyassa cā”ti vutte pana cetiyassa labbhati. “Bhikkhūnañca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vuttepi cetiyasseva visuṃ labbhati, na puggalassa. Bhikkhunīsaṅghaṃ ādiṃ katvāpi evameva yojetabbaṃ.

When it is said, 'For the Bhikkhu Saṅgha and for you,' a separate portion is not obtained for the individual; it should be taken only according to seniority in the rains. However, when it is said, 'For the Bhikkhu Saṅgha and for the shrine,' a separate share is obtained for the shrine. Even when it is said, 'For the Bhikkhu Saṅgha, for you, and for the shrine,' only the shrine receives separately, not the individual. Even when it is said, 'For the bhikkhus and for you,' a separate portion is not obtained. However, when it is said, 'For the bhikkhus and for the shrine,' the shrine receives a share. Even when it is said, 'For the bhikkhus, for you, and for the shrine,' only the shrine receives separately, not the individual. The same should be applied by taking the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha as the beginning.

Pubbe buddhappamukhassa ubhatosaṅghassa dānaṃ denti, bhagavā majjhe nisīdati, dakkhiṇato bhikkhū, vāmato bhikkhuniyo nisīdanti, bhagavā ubhinnaṃ saṅghatthero, tadā bhagavā attanā laddhapaccaye attanāpi paribhuñjati, bhikkhūnampi dāpeti.
