Etarahi pana paṇḍitamanussā sadhātukaṃ paṭimaṃ vā cetiyaṃ vā ṭhapetvā buddhappamukhassa ubhatosaṅghassa dānaṃ denti, paṭimāya vā cetiyassa vā purato ādhārake pattaṃ ṭhapetvā dakkhiṇodakaṃ datvā “buddhānaṃ demā”ti, tattha paṭhamaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ denti, vihāraṃ vā āharitvā “idaṃ cetiyassa demā”ti piṇḍapātañca mālāgandhādīni ca denti, tattha kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti? Mālāgandhādīni tāva cetiye āropetabbāni, vatthehi paṭākā, telena padīpā kātabbā. Piṇḍapātamadhuphāṇitādīni pana [V 0.0240] yo nibaddhacetiyajaggako hoti pabbajito vā gahaṭṭho vā, tassa dātabbāni. Nibaddhajaggake asati āhaṭabhattaṃ ṭhapetvā vattaṃ katvā paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati, upakaṭṭhe kāle bhuñjitvā pacchāpi vattaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Mālāgandhādīsu ca yaṃ kiñci “idaṃ haritvā cetiye pūjaṃ karothā”ti vutte dūrampi haritvā pūjetabbaṃ, “bhikkhusaṅghassa harā”ti vuttepi haritabbaṃ. Sace pana “ahaṃ piṇḍāya carāmi, āsanasālāya bhikkhū atthi, te harissantī”ti vutte “bhante, tuyhameva dammī”ti vadati, bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Atha pana “bhikkhusaṅghassa dassāmī”ti harantassa gacchato antarāva kālo upakaṭṭho hoti, attano pāpetvā bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati.

In the past, they gave alms to the two-fold Saṅgha headed by the Buddha. The Blessed One would sit in the middle, the bhikkhus to the right, and the bhikkhunīs to the left. The Blessed One was the Elder of both Saṅghas. At that time, the Blessed One would himself partake of the requisites he had received and would also have them given to the bhikkhus. But now, wise people establish an image or a stupa with relics and give alms to the two-fold Saṅgha headed by the Buddha. Placing a bowl on a stand in front of the image or stupa, they pour the water of dedication and say, 'We give to the Buddhas.' Therein, they first give hard and soft food. Or, having brought it to the monastery, they give almsfood, flowers, perfumes, and so forth, saying, 'We give this to the stupa.' Therein, how should one act? As for flowers, perfumes, and so forth, they should first be placed on the stupa. Banners should be made from cloths, and lamps should be made with oil. As for almsfood, honey, molasses, and so forth, they should be given to whoever is the regular caretaker of the stupa, be it one who has gone forth or a householder. If there is no regular caretaker, it is proper to set aside the brought food, perform the caretaking duties, and then partake. If the time is near, it is indeed proper to eat first and perform the duties afterwards. And regarding flowers, perfumes, and so forth, if anything is given with the words, 'Take this and make an offering at the stupa,' it should be taken and offered, even to a distant place. Even if it is said, 'Take it to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus,' it should be taken. But if, when one says, 'I am going on alms round; there are bhikkhus in the assembly hall, they will take it,' the donor says, 'Venerable sir, I give it only to you,' it is proper to eat it. Furthermore, if for one who is going, taking it with the intention, 'I will give this to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus,' the time for the meal becomes near while on the way, it is proper to take it for oneself and eat it.

204. Vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa detīti ettha pana sace vihāraṃ pavisitvā “imāni cīvarāni vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa dammī”ti deti, yattakā bhikkhū tasmiṃ āvāse vassacchedaṃ akatvā purimavassaṃvuṭṭhā, tehi bhājetabbaṃ, aññesaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Disāpakkantassapi sati gāhake yāva kathinassubbhārā [M 0.0256] dātabbaṃ. “Anatthate pana kathine antohemante evañca vatvā dinnaṃ pacchimavassaṃvuṭṭhānampi pāpuṇātī”ti lakkhaṇaññū vadanti. Aṭṭhakathāsu panetaṃ na vicāritaṃ. Sace pana bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhito “vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa dammī”ti vadati, sampattānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Atha “asukavihāre vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassā”ti vadati, tatra vassaṃvuṭṭhānameva yāva kathinassubbhārā pāpuṇāti. Sace pana gimhānaṃ paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya evaṃ vadati, tatra sammukhībhūtānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Kasmā? Piṭṭhisamaye uppannattā. Antovasseyeva “vassaṃ vasantānaṃ dammī”ti vutte chinnavassā na labhanti, vassaṃ vasantāva labhanti. Cīvaramāse pana “vassaṃ vasantānaṃ dammī”ti vutte pacchimikāya vassūpagatānaṃyeva pāpuṇāti, purimikāya vassūpagatānañca chinnavassānañca na pāpuṇāti.

204. Now, regarding the phrase 'he gives to the Sangha that has completed the rains-residence': if, having entered the monastery, he gives, saying, 'I give these robes to the Sangha that has completed the rains-residence,' it should be divided by however many bhikkhus in that residence completed the earlier rains-residence without having broken it; it does not accrue to others. For one who has departed to another region, it should also be given, as long as there is a recipient, until the withdrawal of the Kathina. Those who know the characteristics say: 'However, if the Kathina has not been spread, and the gift is given in the winter season having spoken thus, it also accrues to those who have completed the later rains-residence.' However, this is not discussed in the commentaries. If, however, standing in the outer boundary of the precincts, he says, 'I give to the Sangha that has completed the rains-residence,' it accrues to all who are present. But if he says, 'To the Sangha that has completed the rains-residence in such-and-such a monastery,' it accrues only to those who have completed the rains-residence there, until the withdrawal of the Kathina. If, however, starting from the first day of the hot season, he speaks thus, it accrues to all who are present. Why? Because it arose outside the proper season. If, only within the rains-residence, it is said, 'I give to those observing the rains-residence,' those whose rains-residence is broken do not receive it; only those observing the rains-residence receive it. However, in the robe-month, if it is said, 'I give to those observing the rains-residence,' it accrues only to those who undertook the later rains-residence; it does not accrue to those who undertook the earlier rains-residence nor to those whose rains-residence is broken.

Cīvaramāsato paṭṭhāya yāva hemantassa pacchimo divaso, tāva “vassāvāsikaṃ demā”ti vutte kathinaṃ atthataṃ vā hotu anatthataṃ vā, atītavassaṃvuṭṭhānameva pāpuṇāti. Gimhānaṃ paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya vutte pana mātikā āropetabbā “atītapassāvāsassa pañca māsā atikkantā, anāgato cātumāsaccayena bhavissati, kataravassāvāsassa desī”ti. Sace “atītavassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ dammī”ti vadati, taṃ antovassaṃvuṭṭhānameva pāpuṇāti, disāpakkantānampi sabhāgā gaṇhituṃ labhanti. Sace “anāgate vassāvāsikaṃ dammī”ti vadati, taṃ ṭhapetvā vassūpanāyikadivase gahetabbaṃ. Atha “agutto vihāro, corabhayaṃ atthi, na sakkā ṭhapetuṃ gaṇhitvā vā āhiṇḍitu”nti vutte “sampattānaṃ dammī”ti vadati, bhājetvā gahetabbaṃ. Sace vadati [V 0.0241] “ito me, bhante, tatiye vasse vassāvāsikaṃ na dinnaṃ, taṃ dammī”ti, tasmiṃ antovasse vuṭṭhabhikkhūnaṃ pāpuṇāti. Sace te disā pakkantā, añño vissāsiko gaṇhāti, dātabbaṃ. Athekoyeva avasiṭṭho, sesā kālakatā, sabbaṃ ekasseva pāpuṇāti. Sace ekopi natthi, saṅghikaṃ hoti, sammukhībhūtehi bhājetabbaṃ.

Starting from the robe-season month until the last day of winter, if it is said, “We give the rains-residence robe,” whether the Kathina has been spread or not, it accrues only to those who completed the previous rains-residence. However, if this is said starting from the first day of the hot season, a formal question should be raised: “Five months have passed since the previous rains-residence, and the future one will occur after the passing of four months. To the residents of which rains-residence do you give?” If one says, “I give to those who have completed the previous rains-residence,” it accrues only to those who resided during that rains-residence; fellow residents are entitled to receive the share even of those who have departed to other regions. If one says, “I give the rains-residence robe for the future rains-residence,” it should be set aside and received on the day of entering the rains-residence. Then, if it is said, “The monastery is unguarded, there is danger from thieves, it is not possible to set it aside or to wander about after receiving it,” and the donor says, “I give to those who are present,” it should be received after being distributed. If one says, “Venerable sir, by me, in the third year from this one, the rains-residence robe was not given; I give it now,” it accrues to the bhikkhus who completed the rains-residence within that year. If those bhikkhus have departed to other regions and another trustworthy bhikkhu receives it, it should be given. Then, if only one remains and the others have passed away, everything accrues to that one alone. If there is not even one, it becomes the property of the Sangha and should be distributed by those who are present.

205. Ādissa detīti ettha pana yāguyā vā bhatte vā khādanīye vā cīvare vā senāsane vā bhesajje vā ādisitvā paricchinditvā dento ādissa deti nāma. Tatrāyaṃ vinicchayo – bhikkhū ajjatanāya vā [M 0.0257] svātanāya vā yāguyā nimantetvā tesaṃ gharaṃ paviṭṭhānaṃ yāguṃ deti, yāguṃ datvā pītāya yāguyā “imāni cīvarāni yehi mayhaṃ yāgu pītā, tesaṃ dammī”ti deti, yehi nimantitehi yāgu pītā, tesaṃyeva pāpuṇāti. Yehi pana bhikkhācāravattena gharadvārena gacchantehi vā gharaṃ paviṭṭhehi vā yāgu laddhā, yesaṃ vā āsanasālato pattaṃ āharitvā manussehi nītā, yesaṃ vā therehi pesitā, tesaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Sace pana nimantihabhikkhūhi saddhiṃ aññepi bahū āgantvā antogehañca bahigehañca pūretvā nisinnā, dāyako ca evaṃ vadati “nimantitā vā hontu animantitā vā, yesaṃ mayā yāgu dinnā, sabbesaṃ imāni vatthāni hontū”ti, sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Yehi pana therānaṃ hatthato yāgu laddhā, tesaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Atha so “yehi mayhaṃ yāgu pītā, sabbesaṃ hotū”ti vadati, sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Bhattakhādanīyesupi eseva nayo. Cīvare pana pubbepi tena vassaṃ vāsetvā bhikkhūnaṃ cīvaraṃ dinnapubbaṃ hoti, so ce bhikkhū bhojetvā vadati “yesaṃ mayā pubbe cīvaraṃ dinnaṃ, tesaṃyeva imaṃ cīvaraṃ vā suttaṃ vā sappimadhuphāṇitādīni vā hontū”ti, sabbaṃ tesaṃyeva pāpuṇāti. Senāsanepi “yo mayā kārite vihāre vā pariveṇe vā vasati, tassidaṃ hotū”ti vutte tasseva hoti. Bhesajjepi “mayaṃ kālena kālaṃ therānaṃ sappiādīni bhesajjāni dema, yehi tāni laddhāni, tesaṃyevidaṃ hotū”ti vutte tesaṃyeva hoti.

205. Now, regarding the phrase 'gives by specifying': Here, when one gives congee, or rice, or solid food, or robes, or lodging, or medicine, after specifying and defining, it is called 'giving by specifying.' In this regard, the decision is as follows: If bhikkhus are invited for congee today or tomorrow, and upon entering the house, one gives them congee, and after the congee has been drunk, one says, 'I give these robes to those by whom my congee was drunk,' then it accrues only to those who were invited and drank the congee. However, it does not accrue to those bhikkhus who obtained the congee by going on an alms round and either passing by the house door or entering the house, nor to those whose bowls were brought from the assembly hall by people, nor to those for whom it was sent by the elders. But if, along with the invited bhikkhus, many others also come and, filling both the inside and outside of the house, sit down, and the donor says, 'Whether invited or uninvited, let these cloths belong to all those to whom I have given congee,' then it accrues to all of them. Yet, it does not accrue to those who received the congee from the hands of the elders. But if the donor says, 'Let it belong to all those by whom my congee was drunk,' then it accrues to all of them. The same principle applies to rice and solid food. Regarding robes, if one has previously had bhikkhus spend the rains-residence with him and given them robes, and then, after feeding the bhikkhus, one says, 'Let these robes, or thread, or ghee, honey, molasses, and so forth, belong only to those to whom I previously gave robes,' then everything accrues only to them. Regarding lodging, if it is said, 'Let this belong to whoever stays in the monastery or dwelling I had built,' then it belongs to that person alone. Regarding medicine, if it is said, 'From time to time, we give ghee and other medicines to the elders; let this belong only to those who received them,' then it belongs only to them.

206. Puggalassa detīti ettha pana “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī”ti evaṃ parammukhā vā, pādamūle ṭhapetvā “idaṃ, bhante, tumhākaṃ dammī”ti evaṃ sammukhā vā deti, taṃ tasseva hoti. Sace pana “idaṃ tumhākañca tumhākaṃ antevāsikānañca dammī”ti evaṃ vadati, therassa ca antevāsikānañca pāpuṇāti. Uddesaṃ gahetuṃ āgato gahetvā gacchanto ca atthi, tassapi pāpuṇāti. “Tumhehi saddhiṃ nibaddhacārikabhikkhūnaṃ dammī”ti vutte uddesantevāsikānaṃ vattaṃ katvā [V 0.0242] uddesaparipucchādīni gahetvā vicarantānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Ayaṃ “puggalassa detī”ti imasmiṃ pade vinicchayo.

206. Here, regarding 'gives to an individual': if one gives either in absence, saying, 'I give this robe to so-and-so,' or in presence, having placed it at the feet and saying, 'Venerable sir, I give this to you,' it belongs to that very person. However, if one says, 'I give this to you and to your pupils,' it reaches the elder and the pupils. It also reaches the pupil who has come to receive instruction and the one who is departing after having received it. When it is said, 'I give to the monks who regularly travel with you,' it reaches all those who are wandering about, having performed the duties of an instruction-pupil and having learned the text, inquiries, and so forth. This is the determination in the phrase 'gives to an individual.'

Sace koci bhikkhu ekova vassaṃ vasati, tattha manussā “saṅghassa demā”ti cīvarāni denti, tattha kiṃ kātabbanti? “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tasseva [M 0.0258] tāni cīvarāni yāva kathinassa ubbhārā”ti (mahāva. 363) vacanato sace (mahāva. aṭṭha. 363) gaṇapūrake bhikkhū labhitvā kathinaṃ atthataṃ hoti, pañca māse, no ce atthataṃ hoti, ekaṃ cīvaramāsaṃ aññattha gahetvā nītānipi tasseva tāni cīvarāni, na tesaṃ añño koci issaro. Yaṃ yañhi “saṅghassa demā”ti vā “saṅghaṃ uddissa demā”ti vā “vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa demā”ti vā “vassāvāsikaṃ demā”ti vā denti, sacepi matakacīvaraṃ avibhajitvā taṃ vihāraṃ pavisati, taṃ sabbaṃ tasseva bhikkhuno hoti. Yampi so vassāvāsatthāya vaḍḍhiṃ payojetvā ṭhapitaupanikkhepato vā tatruppādato vā vassāvāsikaṃ gaṇhāti, sabbaṃ suggahitameva hoti. Idañhettha lakkhaṇaṃ – yena tenākārena saṅghassa uppannavatthaṃ atthatakathinassa pañca māse, anatthatakathinassa ekaṃ cīvaramāsaṃ pāpuṇāti. Sace pana koci bhikkhu vassānato aññasmiṃ utukāle ekako vasati, tattha manussā “saṅghassa demā”ti cīvarāni denti, tena bhikkhunā adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ “mayhimāni cīvarānī”ti. Adhiṭṭhahantena pana vattaṃ jānitabbaṃ. Tena hi bhikkhunā ghaṇṭiṃ vā paharitvā kālaṃ vā ghosetvā thokaṃ āgametvā sace ghaṇṭisaññāya vā kālasaññāya vā bhikkhū āgacchanti, tehi saddhiṃ bhājetabbāni. Tehi ce bhikkhūhi tasmiṃ cīvare bhājiyamāne apātite kuse añño bhikkhu āgacchati, samako dātabbo bhāgo, pātite kuse añño bhikkhu āgacchati, na akāmā dātabbo bhāgo. Ekakoṭṭhāsepi hi kusadaṇḍake pātitamatte sacepi bhikkhusahassaṃ hoti, gahitameva nāma cīvaraṃ, tasmā na akāmā bhāgo dātabbo. Sace pana attano ruciyā dātukāmā honti, dentu. Anubhāgepi eseva nayo.

If a certain monk resides alone for the rains-residence, and the people there give robes, saying, “We give to the Sangha,” what is to be done in that case? Because it is said, “I allow, monks, that those robes are for him alone until the lifting of the Kathina,” if, having obtained monks who complete the quorum, the Kathina is spread, it is allowable for him to keep them for five months. If the Kathina is not spread, it is allowable for him to keep them for one robe-month. Even if they are taken and carried elsewhere, those robes are for him alone; no one else is their master. For whatever is given, saying, “We give to the Sangha,” or “We give, having designated it for the Sangha,” or “We give to the Sangha that has completed the rains-residence,” or “We give the rains-residence offering,” and even if a robe of a deceased monk enters that monastery without having been divided, all of it belongs to that monk alone. And whatever rains-residence robe he receives, whether from a deposit set aside with interest or from what is produced there, all of it is properly received. And this is the principle here: in whatever manner cloth has arisen for the Sangha, it accrues to one who has spread the Kathina for five months, and to one who has not spread the Kathina for one robe-month. If, however, a certain monk resides alone in a season other than the rains-period, and the people there give robes, saying, “We give to the Sangha,” it should be determined by that monk, “These robes are for me.” But one who is determining should know the proper conduct. Therefore, that monk, having either struck a bell or announced the time, should wait a little. If monks arrive by the signal of the bell or the signal of the time, the robes should be divided with them. And if, while that robe is being divided by those monks, another monk arrives before the lot-sticks are cast, an equal share should be given. If another monk arrives after the lot-sticks have been cast, a share should not be given if one is unwilling. For, at the very moment the lot-stick is cast for even a single portion, even if there are a thousand monks, the robe is considered taken; therefore, a share should not be given if one is unwilling. If, however, they are desirous of giving out of their own inclination, let them give. This same method applies also to a subsequent share.

Atha ghaṇṭisaññāya vā kālasaññāya vā aññe bhikkhū na āgacchanti, “mayhimāni cīvarāni pāpuṇantī”ti adhiṭṭhātabbāni. Evaṃ adhiṭṭhite sabbāni tasseva honti, ṭhitikā pana na tiṭṭhati. Sace ekekaṃ uddharitvā “ayaṃ paṭhamabhāgo mayhaṃ pāpuṇāti, ayaṃ dutiyabhāgo”ti evaṃ gaṇhāti, gahitāni ca suggahitāni honti, ṭhitikā ca tiṭṭhati, evaṃ pāpetvā gaṇhantenapi adhiṭṭhitameva hoti. Sace pana ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā vā appaharitvā vā kālampi ghosetvā vā aghosetvā vā “ahamevettha[M 0.0259], mayhameva imāni cīvarānī”ti gaṇhāti[V 0.0243], duggahitāni honti. Atha “añño koci idha natthi, mayhaṃ etāni pāpuṇantī”ti gaṇhāti, suggahitāni. Atha anadhiṭṭhahitvāva tāni cīvarāni gahetvā aññaṃ vihāraṃ uddissa gacchati “tattha bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhājessāmī”ti, tāni cīvarāni gatagataṭṭhāne saṅghikāneva honti. Bhikkhūhi diṭṭhamattamevettha pamāṇaṃ. Tasmā sace keci paṭipathaṃ āgacchantā “kuhiṃ, āvuso, gacchasī”ti pucchitvā tamatthaṃ sutvā “kiṃ, āvuso, mayaṃ saṅgho na homā”ti tattheva bhājetvā gaṇhanti, suggahitāni. Sacepi esa maggā okkamitvā kañci vihāraṃ vā āsanasālaṃ vā piṇḍāya caranto ekagehameva vā pavisati, tatra ca naṃ bhikkhū disvā tamatthaṃ pucchitvā bhājetvā gaṇhanti, suggahitāneva.

Furthermore, if other bhikkhus do not come by the signal of the bell or the signal of the time, the robes should be determined thus: 'These robes accrue to me.' When thus determined, all of them belong to him alone, but the established seniority does not stand. If, having taken them out one by one, he takes them thus, 'This first share accrues to me, this is the second share,' then they are well-taken, and the established seniority stands. Even when taking them after having caused them to accrue in this way, it is indeed considered determined. But if, having struck the bell or not, or having announced the time or not, he takes them, thinking, 'I alone am here; these robes are mine alone,' they are improperly taken. Alternatively, if he takes them, thinking, 'There is no one else here; these accrue to me,' they are well-taken. Or if, without having determined them, he takes those robes and goes intending for another monastery, thinking, 'There I will divide them with the bhikkhus,' those robes, in every place he goes, belong to the Sangha. Here, the mere sight by the bhikkhus is the measure. Therefore, if some bhikkhus, coming along the path, ask, 'Friend, where are you going?' and, having heard the matter, divide and take them right there, saying, 'What, friend, are we not the Sangha?' they are well-taken. And even if this bhikkhu deviates from the path and, while going for alms, enters some monastery, or a rest hall, or even a single house, and the bhikkhus there see him, ask about the matter, and then divide and take them, they are indeed well-taken.

“Na, bhikkhave, aññatra vassaṃvuṭṭhena aññatra cīvarabhāgo sāditabbo, yo sādiyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 364) vacanato aññatra vassaṃvuṭṭho aññatra bhāgaṃ gaṇhāti, dukkaṭaṃ. Ettha pana kiñcāpi lahukā āpatti, atha kho gahitāni cīvarāni gahitaṭṭhāne dātabbāni. Sacepi naṭṭhāni vā jiṇṇāni vā honti, tasseva gīvā. “Dehī”ti vutte adento dhuranikkhepe bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbo.

'Monks, one who has completed the rains-residence in one place should not accept a share of robes from another place. Whoever should accept it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.' According to this statement, if a monk who has completed the rains-residence in one place takes a share in another, it is an offense of wrong-doing. Here, although it is a light offense, the robes that were taken must be given back at the place where they were taken. Even if they are lost or worn out, it is his responsibility. If, when told, 'Give it back,' he does not give, he should be made to pay the value of the goods for abandoning his duty.

Eko bhikkhu dvīsu āvāsesu vassaṃ vasati “evaṃ me bahu cīvaraṃ uppajjissatī”ti, ekaṃ puggalapaṭivīsaṃyeva labhati. Tasmā sace ekekasmiṃ vihāre ekāhamekāhaṃ vā sattāhaṃ vā vasati, ekekasmiṃ vihāre yaṃ eko puggalo labhati, tato tato upaḍḍhaṃ upaḍḍhaṃ dātabbaṃ. Evañhi ekapuggalapaṭivīso dinno hoti. Sace pana ekasmiṃ vihāre vasanto itarasmiṃ sattāhavārena aruṇameva uṭṭhāpeti, bahutaraṃ vasitavihārato tassa paṭivīso dātabbo. Evampi ekapuggalapaṭivīsoyeva dinno hoti. Idañca nānālābhehi nānūpacārehi ekasīmāvihārehi kathitaṃ, nānāsīmāvihāre pana senāsanaggāho paṭippassambhati. Tasmā tattha cīvarapaṭivīso na pāpuṇāti, sesaṃ pana āmisabhesajjādi sabbaṃ sabbattha antosīmāgatassa pāpuṇāti.

A certain monk resides for the Rains in two residences, thinking, 'Thus, much robe-cloth will arise for me'; he receives only one individual's portion. Therefore, if he resides in each monastery for one day each or for one week each, from the portion that one individual receives in each monastery, half and half should be given. For thus a single individual's portion is given. If, however, while residing in one monastery, he only causes the dawn to arise in the other on a weekly turn, his portion should be given from the monastery where he resided more. Even so, only a single individual's portion is given. And this is stated with reference to monasteries within a single boundary that have different gains and different precincts. In the case of monasteries with different boundaries, however, the taking of a lodging ceases. Therefore, the portion of robes is not obtained there. But the remainder—all such things as material requisites and medicine—is obtained everywhere by one who has come within the boundary.

207. “Bhikkhussa, bhikkhave, kālakate saṅgho sāmī pattacīvare, apica gilānupaṭṭhākā bahūpakārā, anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghena ticīvarañca [M 0.0260] pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dātuṃ, yaṃ tattha lahubhaṇḍaṃ lahuparikkhāraṃ, taṃ sammukhībhūtena saṅghena bhājetuṃ, yaṃ tattha garubhaṇḍaṃ garuparikkhāraṃ, taṃ āgatānāgatacātuddisassa saṅghassa avissajjikaṃ avebhaṅgika”nti (mahāva. 369) vacanato bhikkhusmiṃ kālakate apaloketvā vā –

207. 'O monks, when a monk has passed away, the Saṅgha is the owner of his bowl and robes. And moreover, the attendants of the sick are of great help. I allow, O monks, for the Saṅgha to give the three robes and the bowl to the attendants of the sick. Whatever light goods and light requisites are there, I allow them to be divided by the Saṅgha that is present. Whatever heavy goods and heavy requisites are there, belongs to the Saṅgha of the four directions, of those who have arrived and those who have not yet arrived; it is not to be given away and not to be distributed.' According to this statement, when a monk has passed away, having made a formal announcement, or—

“Suṇātu [V 0.0244] me, bhante, saṅgho, itthannāmo bhikkhu kālakato, idaṃ tassa ticīvarañca patto ca, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ ticīvarañca pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The bhikkhu named so-and-so has passed away. This is his triple robe and bowl. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give this triple robe and bowl to the attendants of the sick. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, itthannāmo bhikkhu kālakato, idaṃ tassa ticīvarañca patto ca, saṅgho imaṃ ticīvarañca pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati imassa ticīvarassa ca pattassa ca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The bhikkhu named so-and-so has passed away. This is his triple robe and bowl. The Saṅgha gives this triple robe and bowl to the attendants of the sick. To whichever venerable one the giving of this triple robe and bowl to the attendants of the sick is agreeable, let him be silent. Whomever it is not agreeable to, let him speak.

“Dinnaṃ idaṃ saṅghena ticīvarañca patto ca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti (mahāva. 367) –

This triple robe and bowl have been given by the Saṅgha to the attendants of the sick. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent; thus I hold it.

Evaṃ kammavācaṃ vā sāvetvā gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ pattacīvaraṃ datvā sesaṃ lahuparikkhāraṃ sammukhībhūtena saṅghena bhājetvā gahetabbaṃ.

Thus, having recited the formal act and given the bowl and robes to the attendants of the sick, the remaining light requisites should be divided and taken by the Saṅgha that is present.

208. Gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ lābhe pana ayaṃ vinicchayo – sace sakale bhikkhusaṅghe upaṭṭhahante kālaṃ karoti, sabbepi sāmikā. Atha ekaccehi vāre kate ekaccehi akateyeva kālaṃ karoti, tatra ekacce ācariyā vadanti “sabbepi attano vāre sampatte kareyyuṃ, tasmā sabbepi sāmino”ti. Ekacce vadanti “yehi jaggito, te eva labhanti, itare na labhantī”ti. Sāmaṇerepi kālakate sace cīvaraṃ atthi, gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dātabbaṃ. No ce atthi, yaṃ atthi, taṃ dātabbaṃ. Aññasmiṃ parikkhāre sati cīvarabhāgaṃ katvā dātabbaṃ. Bhikkhu ca sāmaṇero ca sace samaṃ upaṭṭhahiṃsu, samako bhāgo dātabbo. Atha sāmaṇerova upaṭṭhahati, bhikkhussa saṃvidahanamattameva hoti, sāmaṇerassa jeṭṭhakoṭṭhāso dātabbo. Sace sāmaṇero [M 0.0261] bhikkhunā ānītaudakena yāguṃ pacitvā paṭiggahāpanamattameva karoti, bhikkhu upaṭṭhahati, bhikkhussa jeṭṭhabhāgo dātabbo. Bahū bhikkhū sabbe samaggā hutvā upaṭṭhahanti, sabbesaṃ samako bhāgo dātabbo. Yo panettha visesena upaṭṭhahati, tassa viseso kātabbo.

208. Regarding the gain for those who attend to the sick, this is the decision: if he dies while the entire community of monks is attending, all are owners. But if he dies when some have done their turn and some have not yet done so, in that case, some teachers say, 'All would attend when their turn arrives; therefore, all are owners.' Others say, 'Those by whom he was attended to, they alone receive; the others do not.' When a novice also dies, if there is a robe, it should be given to those who attended the sick. If there is not, whatever there is, that should be given. If there are other requisites, having made a robe-share, it should be given. If a monk and a novice attended equally, an equal share should be given. But if only the novice attends, and for the monk there is only the arranging, the larger portion should be given to the novice. If the novice, having cooked gruel with water brought by a monk, merely offers it, while the monk attends, the larger portion should be given to the monk. If many monks, all being in harmony, attend, an equal share should be given to all of them. But whoever among them attends with special effort, a special portion should be made for him.

Yena pana ekadivasampi gilānupaṭṭhākavasena yāgubhattaṃ vā pacitvā dinnaṃ, nhānaṃ vā paṭisāditaṃ, sopi gilānupaṭṭhākova. Yo pana samīpaṃ anāgantvā bhesajjataṇḍulādīni peseti, ayaṃ gilānupaṭṭhāko na hoti. Yo pariyesitvā gāhetvā āgacchati, ayaṃ gilānupaṭṭhākova[V 0.0245]. Eko vattasīsena jaggati, eko paccāsāya, matakāle ubhopi paccāsīsanti, ubhinnampi dātabbaṃ. Eko upaṭṭhahitvā gilānassa vā kammena attano vā kammena katthaci gato “puna āgantvā jaggissāmī”ti, etassapi dātabbaṃ. Eko ciraṃ upaṭṭhahitvā “idāni na sakkomī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā gacchati, sacepi taṃ divasameva gilāno kālaṃ karoti, upaṭṭhākabhāgo na dātabbo. Gilānupaṭṭhāko nāma gihī vā hotu pabbajito vā antamaso mātugāmopi, sabbe bhāgaṃ labhanti. Sace tassa bhikkhuno pattacīvaramattameva hoti, aññaṃ natthi, sabbaṃ gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃyeva dātabbaṃ. Sacepi sahassaṃ agghati, aññaṃ pana bahumpi parikkhāraṃ te na labhanti, saṅghasseva hoti. Avasesaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ bahu ceva mahagghañca, ticīvaraṃ appagghaṃ, tato gahetvā ticīvaraparikkhāro dātabbo, sabbañcetaṃ saṅghikatova labbhati. Sace pana so jīvamānoyeva sabbaṃ attano parikkhāraṃ nissajjitvā kassaci adāsi, koci vā vissāsaṃ aggahesi, yassa dinnaṃ, yena ca gahitaṃ, tasseva hoti, tassa ruciyā eva gilānupaṭṭhākā labhanti. Aññesaṃ adatvā dūre ṭhapitaparikkhārāpi tattha tattha saṅghasseva honti. Dvinnaṃ santakaṃ hoti avibhattaṃ, ekasmiṃ kālakate itaro sāmī. Bahūnampi santake eseva nayo. Sabbesu matesu saṅghikaṃ hoti. Sacepi avibhajitvā saddhivihārikādīnaṃ denti, adinnameva hoti, vibhajitvā dinnaṃ pana sudinnaṃ. Taṃ tesu matesupi saddhivihārikādīnaṃyeva hoti, na saṅghassa.

Furthermore, one who, in the capacity of an attendant to the sick, has cooked and given rice-gruel or food, or has prepared a bath, even for a single day, is also indeed an attendant of the sick. However, one who does not come near but sends medicines, rice, and so forth, is not an attendant of the sick. One who, having searched for and procured them, comes, is indeed an attendant of the sick. One attends based on duty; another attends with expectation. At the time of death, both will have expectations, and it should be given to both. If one, having attended, has gone somewhere on an errand for the sick person or on one's own errand, thinking, 'I will return and attend again,' it should be given to this one also. But if one who, after attending for a long time, lays down the burden, saying, 'Now I am not able,' and departs—even if the sick person dies on that very day, the attendant's share should not be given. An attendant of the sick, whether a householder, one who has gone forth, or even a woman—all receive a share. If that bhikkhu has only a bowl and robes and nothing else, all of it should be given to the attendants of the sick. Even if it is worth a thousand, it should be given. However, as for other requisites, even if they are many, those attendants do not receive them; they belong only to the Sangha. If the remaining goods are both many and of great value, and the triple robe is of little value, then having taken from those goods, the requisites for the triple robe should be given; and all this is obtained from what is Sanghika property. However, if the sick person, while still alive, relinquished all his own requisites and gave them to someone, or someone took them based on intimacy, it belongs only to the one to whom it was given and by whom it was taken. The attendants of the sick receive only according to that person's wish. Requisites not given to others but placed in distant places belong only to the Sangha of those respective places. If there is undivided property belonging to two, when one dies, the other is the owner. This same principle applies to property belonging to many. When all have died, it becomes Sanghika property. Even if they give it to their co-resident pupils and others without dividing it, it is not considered given. But what is given after dividing is well-given. That property, even when they (the givers) have died, belongs only to the co-resident pupils and others, not to the Sangha.

Sace [M 0.0262] vassaṃvuṭṭho bhikkhu anuppanne vā uppanne vā cīvare abhājite vā pakkamati, ummattako khittacitto vedanāṭṭo ukkhittako vā hoti, sante patirūpe gāhake bhāgo dātabbo. Sace pana vibbhamati vā kālaṃ vā karoti sāmaṇero vā paṭijānāti, sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako, antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannako, paṇḍako, theyyasaṃvāsako, titthiyapakkantako, tiracchānagato, mātughātako, pitughātako, arahantaghātako, bhikkhunīdūsako, saṅghabhedako, lohituppādako, ubhatobyañjanako vā paṭijānāti, saṅgho sāmī, bhāgo na dātabbo.

If a bhikkhu who has completed the rains-residence departs—whether the robe-cloth has not yet arisen, or has arisen but is undivided—and he is insane, mentally deranged, afflicted with pain, or is one who has been suspended, a share should be given if there is a suitable recipient. But if he disrobes, or dies, or if he admits to being a novice, one who has renounced the training, one who has committed a terminal offense, a paṇḍaka, one who lives in communion by theft, one who has gone over to another sect, an animal, a matricide, a patricide, a murderer of an Arahant, a defiler of a bhikkhunī, a schismatic, one who has shed the Buddha's blood, or an ubhatobyañjanaka, the Saṅgha is the owner; the share should not be given.

Sace vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anuppanne cīvare saṅgho bhijjati, kosambakabhikkhū viya dve koṭṭhāsā honti, tattha manussā ekasmiṃ pakkhe dakkhiṇodakañca gandhādīni ca denti, ekasmiṃ cīvarāni denti “saṅghassa demā”ti, yattha vā udakaṃ dinnaṃ, yasmiṃyeva pakkhe cīvarāni denti “saṅghassa demā”ti, saṅghasseva tāni cīvarāni, dvinnampi koṭṭhāsānaṃ pāpuṇanti, ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā dvīhipi pakkhehi ekato bhājetabbāni. Sace pana manussā ekasmiṃ pakkhe dakkhiṇodakaṃ gandhādīni ca denti, ekasmiṃ pakkhe cīvarāni denti “pakkhassa [V 0.0246] demā”ti, pakkhasseva tāni cīvarāni. Evañhi dinne yassa koṭṭhāsassa udakaṃ dinnaṃ, tassa udakameva hoti. Yassa cīvaraṃ dinnaṃ, tasseva cīvaraṃ. Yasmiṃ padese dakkhiṇodakaṃ pamāṇaṃ hoti, tattha eko pakkho dakkhiṇodakassa laddhattā cīvarāni labhati, eko cīvarānameva laddhattāti ubhohi ekato hutvā yathāvuḍḍhaṃ bhājetabbaṃ. “Idaṃ kira parasamudde lakkhaṇa”nti mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Sace yasmiṃ pakkhe udakaṃ dinnaṃ, tasmiṃyeva pakkhe cīvarāni denti “pakkhassa demā”ti, pakkhasseva tāni cīvarāni, itaro pakkho anissaroyeva. Sace pana vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ uppanne cīvare abhājite saṅgho bhijjati, sabbesaṃ samakaṃ bhājetabbaṃ.

If, for the monks who have completed the rains-residence, the Sangha splits before robe-cloth has arisen—becoming two factions like the monks of Kosambī—and people give water for dedication and perfumes, etc., to one faction, while giving robe-cloth to another faction, saying, 'We give this to the Sangha,' then regardless of where the water was given, the robe-cloth given to whichever faction with the words 'We give this to the Sangha' belongs to the Sangha itself. Both factions are entitled to it, and after striking the bell, it should be distributed by both factions together. However, if people give water for dedication and perfumes, etc., to one faction, while giving robe-cloth to the other faction, saying, 'We give this to the faction,' then that robe-cloth belongs only to that faction. For when given in this way, the water belongs only to the faction to which it was given, and the robe-cloth belongs only to the faction to which it was given. In a region where the water of dedication is the standard, one faction receives the robes on account of having received the water of dedication, and the other on account of having received the robes themselves; therefore, both should come together and distribute them according to seniority. It is said in the Great Commentary: 'This, it seems, is the custom in the land beyond the sea.' If water is given to one faction and robe-cloth is given to that same faction with the words, 'We give this to the faction,' then that robe-cloth belongs only to that faction, and the other faction has no authority over it. But if the Sangha splits after the monks have completed the rains-residence and robe-cloth has arisen but is still undivided, it should be shared equally among all.

Sace sambahulesu bhikkhūsu addhānamaggappaṭipannesu keci bhikkhū paṃsukūlatthāya susānaṃ okkamanti, keci anāgamentā pakkamanti, anāgamentānaṃ na akāmā bhāgo dātabbo, āgamentānaṃ pana akāmāpi dātabbo bhāgo. Yadi pana manussā “idhāgatā eva gaṇhantū”ti denti, saññāṇaṃ vā katvā gacchanti “sampattā gaṇhantū”ti, sampattānaṃ sabbesampi pāpuṇāti[M 0.0263]. Sace chaḍḍetvā gatā, yena gahitaṃ, so eva sāmī. Sace keci bhikkhū paṭhamaṃ susānaṃ okkamanti, keci pacchā, tattha paṭhamaṃ okkantā paṃsukūlaṃ labhanti, pacchā okkantā na labhanti. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pacchā okkantānaṃ na akāmā bhāgaṃ dātu”nti (mahāva. 341) vacanato pacchā okkantānaṃ akāmā bhāgo na dātabbo. Sace pana sabbepi samaṃ okkantā, keci labhanti, keci na labhanti. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sadisānaṃ okkantānaṃ akāmāpi bhāgaṃ dātu”nti (mahāva. 341) vacanato samaṃ okkantānaṃ akāmāpi bhāgo dātabbo. Sace pana “laddhaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ sabbe bhājetvā gaṇhissāmā”ti bahimeva katikaṃ katvā susānaṃ okkantā keci labhanti, keci na labhanti, “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, katikaṃ katvā okkantānaṃ akāmā bhāgaṃ dātu”nti (mahāva. 341) vacanato katikaṃ katvā okkantānampi akāmā bhāgo dātabbo. Ayaṃ tāva cīvarabhājanīyakathā.

If, among many monks journeying on a long road, some monks enter a charnel ground for rag-robes while others depart without waiting, a share is not to be given to those who do not wait if the finders are unwilling; but to those who wait, a share must be given even if the finders are unwilling. If, however, people give saying, 'Let only those who have come here take it,' or if they leave after making a sign saying, 'Let those who have arrived take it,' it belongs to all who have arrived. If they have abandoned it and gone, whoever takes it is the owner. If some monks enter the charnel ground first and others later, those who entered first obtain the rag-robe; those who entered later do not. According to the saying, 'I allow, monks, that a share not be given to those who enter later if the finders are unwilling,' a share is not to be given to those who entered later if the finders are unwilling. If, however, all enter at the same time, and some obtain it while others do not, according to the saying, 'I allow, monks, that a share be given to those who entered together, even if the finders are unwilling,' a share must be given to those who entered at the same time, even if the finders are unwilling. If, however, they enter the charnel ground after making an agreement beforehand, saying, 'We will all divide and take whatever rag-robe is obtained,' and some obtain it while others do not, according to the saying, 'I allow, monks, that a share be given to those who entered after making an agreement, even if the finders are unwilling,' a share must be given to those who entered after making an agreement, even if the finders are unwilling. This, for now, is the discussion on the apportionment of robes.

209. Piṇḍapātabhājane pana “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghabhattaṃ uddesabhattaṃ nimantanaṃ salākabhattaṃ pakkhikaṃ uposathikaṃ pāṭipadika”nti (cūḷava. 325) evaṃ anuññātesu saṅghabhattādīsu ayaṃ vinicchayo (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 325) –

209. Now, regarding the apportionment of alms-food, in the case of Saṅgha-meals and so on, which were allowed thus: 'I allow, monks, a Saṅgha-meal, a designated meal, an invitation meal, a ticket meal, a fortnightly meal, an Uposatha meal, and a meal on the first day of the fortnight,' this is the decision:

Saṅghabhattaṃ nāma sakalassa saṅghassa dātabbaṃ bhattaṃ. Tasmā saṅghabhatte ṭhitikā nāma natthi, tatoyeva [V 0.0247] ca “amhākaṃ ajja dasa dvādasa divasā bhuñjantānaṃ, idāni aññato bhikkhū ānethā”ti na evaṃ tattha vattabbaṃ, “purimadivasesu amhehi na laddhaṃ, idāni taṃ amhākaṃ gāhethā”ti evampi vattuṃ na labhati. Tañhi āgatāgatānaṃ pāpuṇātiyeva.

A meal called Saṅghabhatta is a meal to be given to the entire Saṅgha. Therefore, in a Saṅghabhatta, there is no such thing as a rotation. For this very reason, one should not say there, “We have been eating for ten or twelve days now; bring monks from elsewhere.” Nor is it permissible to say, “We did not receive it on previous days; now let us receive it.” For that meal indeed reaches whoever comes.

Uddesabhattādīsu pana ayaṃ nayo – raññā vā rājamahāmattena vā “saṅghato uddisitvā ettake bhikkhū ānethā”ti pahite kālaṃ ghosetvā ṭhitikā pucchitabbā. Sace atthi, tato paṭṭhāya gāhetabbaṃ. No ce, therāsanato paṭṭhāya gāhetabbaṃ. Uddesakena piṇḍapātikānampi na atikkāmetabbaṃ. Te pana dhutaṅgaṃ rakkhantā sayameva atikkamissanti. Evaṃ gāhiyamāne alasajātikā mahātherā pacchā āgacchanti, “bhante, vīsativassānaṃ gāhīyati, tumhākaṃ ṭhitikā atikkantā”ti na vattabbā, ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvā tesaṃ gāhetvā pacchā ṭhitikāya gāhetabbaṃ. “Asukavihāre [M 0.0264] bahu uddesabhattaṃ uppanna”nti sutvā yojanantarikavihāratopi bhikkhū āgacchanti, sampattasampattānaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya gāhetabbaṃ, asampattānampi upacārasīmaṃ paviṭṭhānaṃ antevāsikādīsu gaṇhantesu gāhetabbameva. “Bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitānaṃ gāhethā”ti vadanti, na gāhetabbaṃ. Sace upacārasīmaṃ okkantehi ekābaddhā hutvā attano vihāradvāre vā antovihāreyeva vā honti, parisavasena vaḍḍhitā nāma sīmā hoti, tasmā gāhetabbaṃ. Saṅghanavakassa dinnepi pacchā āgatānaṃ gāhetabbameva. Dutiyabhāge pana therāsanaṃ āruḷhe puna āgatānaṃ paṭhamabhāgo na pāpuṇāti, dutiyabhāgato vassaggena gāhetabbaṃ.

However, in the case of designated meals and the like, this is the method: When a king or a great minister of the king sends an instruction, saying, “Having designated from the Saṅgha, bring this many monks,” one should announce the time and then ask about the rotation. If there is a rotation, the distribution should begin from that point. If not, it should begin from the senior elder’s seat. The designator should not bypass even the alms-food-goers. But those monks, protecting their ascetic practice, will bypass it of their own accord. When the distribution is being made in this way, if senior elders of a sluggish nature arrive later, it should not be said, “Venerable sirs, it is being given to those of twenty years’ standing; your rotation has passed.” Setting aside the rotation, they should be given their share, and afterwards, the distribution should proceed according to the rotation. Upon hearing, “Much designated food has arisen in such-and-such monastery,” monks may come even from a monastery a yojana away. The distribution should begin from the place where those who have arrived are standing. Even for those who have not yet arrived at the assembly but have entered the vicinity-boundary, they should indeed be included when their resident pupils and others are receiving their share. If some say, “Give also to those standing outside the vicinity-boundary,” it should not be given. If, being connected as one group with those who have entered the vicinity-boundary, they are at their own monastery gate or even inside the monastery, the boundary is said to be extended by the power of the assembly; therefore, it should be given. Even after a share has been given to the most junior monk of the Saṅgha, it must indeed be given to those who arrive later. However, in the second portion, after the senior elder’s seat has been taken, the first portion does not reach those who arrive again; from the second portion, it should be given according to seniority by rains-residence.

Ekasmiṃ vihāre ekaṃ bhattuddesaṭṭhānaṃ paricchinditvā gāvutappamāṇāyapi upacārasīmāya yattha katthaci ārocitaṃ uddesabhattaṃ tasmiṃyeva bhattuddesaṭṭhāne gāhetabbaṃ. Eko ekassa bhikkhuno pahiṇati “sve saṅghato uddisitvā dasa bhikkhū pahiṇathā”ti, tena so attho bhattuddesakassa ārocetabbo. Sace taṃ divasaṃ pamussati, dutiyadivase pātova ārocetabbo, atha pamussitvāva piṇḍāya pavisanto sarati, yāva upacārasīmaṃ nātikkamati, tāva yā bhojanasālāya pakatiṭhitikā, tassāyeva vasena gāhetabbaṃ. Sacepi upacārasīmaṃ atikkanto, bhikkhū ca upacārasīmaṭṭhakehi ekābaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ dvādasahatthantaraṃ avijahitvā gacchanti, pakatiṭhitikāya vasena gāhetabbaṃ. Bhikkhūnaṃ pana tādise ekābaddhe asati bahiupacārasīmāya yasmiṃ ṭhāne sarati, tattha navaṃ ṭhitikaṃ katvā gāhetabbaṃ. Antogāme āsanasālāya sarantena āsanasālāya ṭhitikāya gāhetabbaṃ. Yattha katthaci saritvā gāhetabbameva, agāhetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Na hi etaṃ dutiyadivase labbhatīti.

In a monastery, having designated a single place for meal-designation, even within a proximity boundary of a gāvuta's extent, a designated meal that is announced anywhere should be accepted at that very place for meal-designation. If a person sends to a monk, saying, “Tomorrow, having designated from the Saṅgha, send ten monks,” that matter should be announced by that monk to the meal-designator. If he forgets on that day, it should be announced early in the morning on the second day. But if, having forgotten, he remembers while entering for alms-food, as long as he has not crossed the proximity boundary, it should be accepted according to the regular turn in the dining hall. And if he has crossed the proximity boundary, but the monks are connected with those at the proximity boundary, proceeding without leaving a twelve-cubit interval between one another, it should be accepted according to the regular turn. However, if there is no such connection of the monks, outside the proximity boundary, wherever he remembers, it should be accepted by making a new turn there. If one remembers while inside the village at the rest-house, it should be accepted according to the turn of the rest-house. Having remembered anywhere whatsoever, it must indeed be accepted; it is not allowable not to accept. For this designated meal is not obtained on the second day.

Sace [V 0.0248] sakavihārato aññaṃ vihāraṃ gacchante bhikkhū disvā koci uddesabhattaṃ uddisāpeti, yāva antoupacāre vā upacārasīmaṭṭhakehi saddhiṃ vuttanayena ekābaddhā vā honti, tāva sakavihāre ṭhitikāvasena gāhetabbaṃ. Bahiupacāre ṭhitānaṃ dinnaṃ pana “saṅghato, bhante, ettake [M 0.0265] nāma bhikkhū uddisathā”ti vutte sampattasampattānaṃ gāhetabbaṃ. Tattha dvādasahatthantaraṃ avijahitvā ekābaddhanayena dūre ṭhitāpi sampattāyevāti veditabbā. Sace yaṃ vihāraṃ gacchanti, tattha paviṭṭhānaṃ ārocenti, tassa vihārassa ṭhitikāvasena gāhetabbaṃ. Sacepi gāmadvāre vā vīthiyaṃ vā catukke vā antaraghare vā bhikkhū disvā koci saṅghuddesaṃ āroceti, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāne antoupacāragatānaṃ gāhetabbaṃ.

If, seeing monks going from their own monastery to another monastery, someone has a designated meal assigned, it should be taken according to the standing-order of their own monastery for as long as they are within the inner precinct or are connected in a single group with the boundary markers of the precinct in the aforesaid manner. But when it is given to those standing outside the precinct, upon it being said, 'Venerable sirs, please designate so many monks from the Saṅgha,' it should be taken by whichever monks have arrived. Therein, even those standing at a distance are to be known as having indeed arrived, by the method of being connected without leaving an interval of twelve cubits. If one announces it to those who have entered the monastery to which they are going, it should be taken according to the standing-order of that monastery. And if, seeing monks at a village gate, on a street, at a crossroads, or inside a house, someone announces a designation for the Saṅgha, in each respective place, it should be taken by those who have entered the inner precinct.

Gharūpacāro cettha ekagharaṃ ekūpacāraṃ, ekagharaṃ nānūpacāraṃ, nānāgharaṃ ekūpacāraṃ, nānāgharaṃ nānūpacāranti imesaṃ vasena veditabbo. Tattha yaṃ ekakulassa gharaṃ ekavaḷañjaṃ hoti, taṃ suppapātaparicchedassa anto ekūpacāraṃ nāma, tatthuppanno uddesalābho ekasmiṃ upacāre bhikkhācāravattenapi ṭhitānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Etaṃ ekagharaṃ ekūpacāraṃ nāma. Yaṃ pana ekagharaṃ dvinnaṃ bhariyānaṃ sukhavihāratthāya majjhe bhittiṃ uṭṭhapetvā nānādvāravaḷañjaṃ kataṃ, tatthuppanno uddesalābho bhittiantarikassa na pāpuṇāti, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāne nisinnasseva pāpuṇāti. Etaṃ ekagharaṃ nānūpacāraṃ nāma. Yasmiṃ pana ghare bahū bhikkhū nimantetvā antogehato paṭṭhāya ekābaddhe katvā paṭivissakagharānipi pūretvā nisīdāpenti, tattha uppanno uddesalābho sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Yampi nānākulassa nivesanaṃ majjhe bhittiṃ akatvā ekadvāreneva vaḷañjanti, tatrāpi eseva nayo. Etaṃ nānāgharaṃ ekūpacāraṃ nāma. Yo pana nānānivesanesu nisinnānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ uddesalābho uppajjati, kiñcāpi bhitticchiddena bhikkhū dissanti, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ nivesane nisinnānaṃyeva pāpuṇāti. Etaṃ nānāgharaṃ nānūpacāraṃ nāma.

Herein, the house-precinct should be understood by way of these: one house, one precinct; one house, various precincts; various houses, one precinct; various houses, various precincts. Therein, whatever house of a single family is used with a single entrance, that is called 'one precinct' within a well-defined boundary. A designated gain that has arisen there reaches all those who are standing, even according to the practice of the alms-round, in that one precinct. This is called 'one house, one precinct'. But as for whatever single house is made to be used with separate doorways by having erected a wall in the middle for the comfortable living of two wives, a designated gain that has arisen there does not reach a monk separated by the wall; it reaches only the one who is sitting in that particular place. This is called 'one house, various precincts'. But in whatever house, having invited many monks, they cause them to be seated beginning from the inner house, having made it a single continuous space and having filled even the neighboring houses, a designated gain that has arisen there reaches all of them. Also, whatever dwelling of various families they use with only one entrance, without making a wall in the middle, there also this is the same principle. This is called 'various houses, one precinct'. But whatever designated gain arises for monks sitting in various dwellings, although the monks are seen through a hole in the wall, it reaches only those who are sitting in that particular dwelling. This is called 'various houses, various precincts'.

Yo pana gāmadvāravīthicatukkesu aññatarasmiṃ ṭhāne uddesabhattaṃ labhitvā aññasmiṃ bhikkhusmiṃ asati attanova pāpuṇāpetvā dutiyadivasepi tasmiṃyeva ṭhāne aññaṃ labhati, tena yaṃ aññaṃ navakaṃ vā vuḍḍhaṃ vā bhikkhuṃ passati, tassa gāhetabbaṃ. Sace koci natthi, attanova pāpetvā bhuñjitabbaṃ. Sace āsanasālāya nisīditvā kālaṃ paṭimānentesu bhikkhūsu koci āgantvā “saṅghuddesapattaṃ detha, uddesapattaṃ detha, saṅghato uddisitvā pattaṃ detha, saṅghikaṃ pattaṃ dethā”ti vā vadati, uddesapattaṃ ṭhitikāya gāhetvā dātabbaṃ. “Saṅghuddesabhikkhuṃ detha, saṅghato uddisitvā bhikkhuṃ detha, saṅghikaṃ bhikkhuṃ dethā”ti vuttepi eseva nayo.

Now, if a monk obtains a designated meal at any of the village gates, streets, or crossroads, and there is no other monk present, he may take it for himself. If on the second day he obtains another in that very same place, he should ensure it is received by whatever other monk he sees, whether junior or senior. If there is no one, he should take it for himself and eat it. If, while monks are sitting in the assembly hall waiting for the time, someone comes and says, 'Give the bowl designated by the Saṅgha, give the designated bowl, give a bowl designated from the Saṅgha, give the Saṅgha's bowl,' the designated bowl should be assigned according to the established turn and then given. When it is said, 'Give the monk designated by the Saṅgha, give a monk designated from the Saṅgha, give the Saṅgha's monk,' this is the same method.

Uddesako [M 0.0266][V 0.0249] panettha pesalo lajjī medhāvī icchitabbo, tena tikkhattuṃ ṭhitikaṃ pucchitvā sace koci ṭhitikaṃ jānanto natthi, therāsanato gāhetabbaṃ. Sace pana “ahaṃ jānāmi, dasavassena laddha”nti koci bhaṇati, “atthāvuso, dasavassā bhikkhū”ti pucchitabbaṃ. Sace tassa sutvāva “dasavassamha dasavassamhā”ti bahū āgacchanti, “tuyhaṃ pāpuṇāti, tuyhaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti agatvā “sabbe appasaddā hothā”ti vatvā paṭipāṭiyā ṭhapetabbā, ṭhapetvā “kati bhikkhū icchathā”ti upāsako pucchitabbo, “ettake nāma, bhante”ti vutte “tuyhaṃ pāpuṇāti, tuyhaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti avatvā sabbanavakassa vassaggañca utu ca divasabhāgo ca chāyā ca pucchitabbā. Sace chāyāyapi pucchiyamānāya añño vuḍḍhataro āgacchati, tassa dātabbaṃ. Atha chāyaṃ pucchitvā “tuyhaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti vutte vuḍḍhataro āgacchati, na labhati. Kathāpapañcena hi nisinnassapi niddāyantassapi gāhitaṃ suggāhitaṃ, atikkantaṃ suatikkantaṃ. Bhājanīyabhaṇḍañhi nāmetaṃ sampattasseva pāpuṇāti, tattha sampattabhāvo upacārena paricchinditabbo. Āsanasālāya ca antoparikkhepo upacāro, tasmiṃ ṭhitassa lābho pāpuṇāti.

The assigner herein should be a person who is virtuous, modest, and wise; he is to be sought. He should ask three times whose turn it is. If no one knows whose turn it is, it should be determined starting from the elder's seat. If, however, some monk says, 'I know, the turn has fallen to a ten-vassa monk,' he should be asked, 'Friend, are there monks of ten vassas?' If, just upon hearing this, many monks come forward saying, 'We are of ten vassas, we are of ten vassas,' then without saying, 'It is yours, it is yours,' he should say, 'All of you, be silent,' and they should be arranged in order. Having arranged them, the lay supporter should be asked, 'How many monks do you desire?' When it is said, 'Venerable sir, we desire this many monks,' then without saying, 'It is yours, it is yours,' the most junior of all should be asked about his count of vassas, the season, the part of the day, and the shadow at the time of ordination. If, even while the shadow is being asked about, another, more senior monk arrives, it should be given to him. But if, after the shadow has been asked about and it has been said, 'It is yours,' a more senior monk arrives, he does not receive it. For in the case of one sitting engaged in a proliferation of talk or dozing, the acceptance of the gain by another is a valid acceptance, and his being passed over is a valid passing over. For this, which is called a divisible requisite, reaches only the one who has arrived. Therein, the state of having arrived should be determined by the precinct. And for an assembly hall, the inner enclosure is the precinct; the gain reaches one standing within it.

Koci āsanasālato aṭṭha uddesapatte āharāpetvā satta patte paṇītabhojanānaṃ, ekaṃ udakassa pūretvā āsanasālaṃ pahiṇati, gahetvā āgatā kiñci avatvā bhikkhūnaṃ hatthesu patiṭṭhapetvā pakkamanti, yena yaṃ laddhaṃ, tasseva taṃ hoti. Yena pana udakaṃ laddhaṃ, tassa atikkantampi ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ uddesabhattaṃ gāhetabbaṃ, tañca lūkhaṃ vā labhatu paṇītaṃ vā ticīvaraparivāraṃ vā, tasseva taṃ hoti. Īdiso hissa puññaviseso, udakaṃ pana yasmā āmisaṃ na hoti, tasmā aññaṃ uddesabhattaṃ labhati. Sace pana te gahetvā āgatā “idaṃ kira, bhante, sabbaṃ bhājetvā bhuñjathā”ti vatvā gacchanti, sabbehi bhājetvā bhuñjitvā udakaṃ pātabbaṃ. “Saṅghato uddisitvā aṭṭha mahāthere detha, majjhime detha, navake detha, paripuṇṇavasse sāmaṇere detha, majjhimabhāṇakādayo detha, mayhaṃ ñātibhikkhū dethā”ti vadantassa pana “upāsaka, tvaṃ evaṃ vadasi, ṭhitikāya pana tesaṃ na pāpuṇātī”ti vatvā ṭhitikāvaseneva dātabbā. Daharasāmaṇerehi pana uddesabhattesu laddhesu sace dāyakānaṃ ghare [M 0.0267] maṅgalaṃ hoti, “tumhākaṃ ācariyupajjhāye pesethā”ti vattabbaṃ. Yasmiṃ pana uddesabhatte paṭhamabhāgo sāmaṇerānaṃ pāpuṇāti, anubhāgo mahātherānaṃ, na tattha sāmaṇerā “mayaṃ paṭhamabhāgaṃ labhimhā”ti purato gantuṃ labhanti, yathāpaṭipāṭiyā eva gantabbaṃ. “Saṅghato uddisitvā tumhe ethā”ti vutte “mayhaṃ aññadāpi jānissasi, ṭhitikā pana evaṃ gacchatī”ti ṭhitikāvaseneva [V 0.0250] gāhetabbaṃ. Atha “saṅghuddesapattaṃ dethā”ti vatvā aggāhiteyeva patte yassa kassaci pattaṃ gahetvā pūretvā āharati, āhaṭampi ṭhitikāya eva gāhetabbaṃ.

A certain person has eight designated bowls brought from a rest house, fills seven bowls with fine food and one with water, and sends them to the rest house. Those who have brought them, without saying anything, place them in the hands of the bhikkhus and depart. Whatever is received by a certain bhikkhu, that belongs to him alone. However, for the bhikkhu who has received the water, another designated meal should be accepted on his behalf, setting aside even a turn that has passed. And whether he receives that designated meal as coarse or fine, or with the three robes as an accessory, it belongs to him alone. Truly, such is his special merit. But since water is not material food, he receives another designated meal. If, however, those who have brought them say, 'Venerable sirs, please divide all this and partake of it,' and then depart, it should be divided and partaken of by all, and the water should be drunk. If a person says, 'Having designated from the Saṅgha, give to the eight great elders, give to the middle ones, give to the new ones, give to the novices who have completed the rains-residence, give to the reciters of the Majjhima Nikāya and so on, give to my bhikkhu-relatives,' he should be told, 'Lay supporter, you speak thus, but according to the turn, it does not reach them,' and it should be given only according to the turn. When young novices have received designated meals, if there is an auspicious occasion at the donors’ house, they should be told, 'Send your teachers and preceptors.' In a designated meal where the first portion reaches the novices and a subsequent portion reaches the great elders, the novices do not get to go in front thinking, 'We received the first portion'; they should go only in the proper order of seniority. When it is said, 'Having designated from the Saṅgha, you come,' he should accept it only according to the turn, saying, 'You will know of me on another occasion, but the turn proceeds thus.' Then, if a person says, 'Give the Saṅgha's designated bowl,' and before a bowl is specified, he takes the bowl of some bhikkhu, fills it, and brings it, even what has been brought should be accepted only according to the turn.

Eko “saṅghuddesapattaṃ āharā”ti pesito “bhante, ekaṃ pattaṃ detha, nimantanabhattaṃ āharissāmī”ti vadati, so ce “uddesabhattagharato ayaṃ āgato”ti ñatvā bhikkhūhi “nanu tvaṃ asukagharato āgato”ti vutto “āma, bhante, na nimantanabhattaṃ, uddesabhatta”nti bhaṇati, ṭhitikāya gāhetabbaṃ. Yo pana “ekaṃ pattaṃ āharā”ti vutte “kinti vatvā āharāmī”ti vatvā “yathā te ruccatī”ti vutto āgacchati, ayaṃ vissaṭṭhadūto nāma. Uddesapattaṃ vā paṭipāṭipattaṃ vā puggalikapattaṃ vā yaṃ icchati, taṃ etassa dātabbaṃ. Eko bālo abyatto “uddesapattaṃ āharā”ti pesito vattuṃ na jānāti, tuṇhībhūto tiṭṭhati, so “kassa santikaṃ āgatosī”ti vā “kassa pattaṃ harissasī”ti vā na vattabbo. Evañhi vutto pucchāsabhāgena “tumhākaṃ santikaṃ āgatomhī”ti vā “tumhākaṃ pattaṃ harissāmī”ti vā vadeyya. Tato taṃ bhikkhuṃ aññe bhikkhū jigucchantā na olokeyyuṃ, “kuhiṃ gacchasi, kiṃ karonto āhiṇḍasī”ti pana vattabbo. Tassa “uddesapattatthāya āgatomhī”ti vadantassa gāhetvā patto dātabbo.

A certain one, sent with the instruction, 'Bring a bowl designated for the Saṅgha,' says, 'Venerable sirs, give one bowl; I will bring the invitation meal.' If the bhikkhus, knowing, 'This one has come from the house providing the designated meal,' say to him, 'Have you not come from such-and-such a house?' and he replies, 'Yes, venerable sirs, it is not an invitation meal but a designated meal,' it should be accepted according to the turn. But if one, when told, 'Bring one bowl,' says, 'Saying what shall I bring it?' and is told, 'As you please,' and then comes, this one is called a messenger with free rein. Whatever bowl he wishes—whether a designated bowl, a bowl in order, or a personal bowl—should be given to him. A certain one who is foolish and inexperienced, sent with the instruction, 'Bring a designated bowl,' does not know what to say and stands silent. He should not be asked, 'To whose presence have you come?' or 'Whose bowl will you carry?' For if spoken to in this way, he might say in response to the question, 'I have come to your presence,' or 'I will carry your bowl.' Then other bhikkhus, being disgusted with that bhikkhu, would not look at him. Instead, he should be asked, 'Where are you going? What are you doing, wandering about?' When he says, 'I have come for the designated bowl,' a bowl should be procured from the one whose turn it is and given to him.

Ekā kūṭaṭṭhitikā nāma hoti. Rañño vā rājamahāmattassa vā gehe atipaṇītāni aṭṭha uddesabhattāni niccaṃ dīyanti, tāni ekacārikabhattāni katvā bhikkhū visuṃ ṭhitikāya paribhuñjanti. Ekacce bhikkhū “sve dāni amhākaṃ pāpuṇissantī”ti attano ṭhitikaṃ sallakkhetvā gatā. Tesu anāgatesuyeva aññe āgantukā bhikkhū āgantvā āsanasālāya nisīdanti. Taṅkhaṇaññeva rājapurisā āgantvā “paṇītabhattapatte dethā”ti vadanti, āgantukā ṭhitikaṃ ajānantā gāhenti, taṅkhaṇaññeva ca ṭhitikaṃ jānanakabhikkhū āgantvā “kiṃ gāhethā”ti vadanti[M 0.0268]. Rājagehe paṇītabhattanti. Kativassato paṭṭhāyāti. Ettakavassato nāmāti. “Mā gāhethā”ti nivāretvā ṭhitikāya gāhetabbaṃ. Gāhite āgatehipi, pattadānakāle āgatehipi, dinnakāle āgatehipi, rājagehato patte pūretvā āhaṭakāle āgatehipi, rājā “ajja bhikkhūyeva āgacchantū”ti pesetvā bhikkhūnaṃyeva hatthe piṇḍapātaṃ deti, evaṃ dinnaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ gahetvā āgatakāle āgatehipi ṭhitikaṃ jānanakabhikkhūhi “mā bhuñjitthā”ti vāretvā ṭhitikāyameva gāhetabbaṃ.

There is a case called the deceptive allocation by turn. In the house of a king or a royal minister, eight portions of the finest designated food are always given. These are made into individual meals, and the bhikkhus partake of them separately according to the allocation by turn. Some bhikkhus, noting that their turn is tomorrow, depart. Before they have returned, other visiting bhikkhus arrive and sit in the rest hall. At that moment, the king's men arrive and say, 'Give the bowls for the fine food.' The visiting bhikkhus, not knowing the allocation by turn, accept them. At that very moment, the bhikkhus who know the allocation by turn arrive and ask, 'What are you accepting?' 'The fine food from the king's house.' 'From what seniority in Rains-residences are you accepting this?' 'From such-and-such a seniority.' Having prevented them by saying, 'Do not accept it,' it should be accepted according to the allocation by turn. This intervention should be made by the bhikkhus who know the turn, even if they arrive after the bowls have been accepted, at the time of giving the bowls, after they have been given, or when the bowls are brought back filled from the king's house. Furthermore, if the king sends a message saying, 'Today let the bhikkhus themselves come,' and gives almsfood directly into the bhikkhus' hands, and the bhikkhus who know the turn arrive as the others are returning with the almsfood, they should prevent them, saying, 'Do not eat,' and it should be accepted only according to the allocation by turn.

Atha ne rājā bhojetvā pattepi nesaṃ pūretvā deti, yaṃ āhaṭaṃ, taṃ ṭhitikāya gāhetabbaṃ[V 0.0251]. Sace pana “mā tucchahatthā gacchantū”ti thokameva pattesu pakkhittaṃ hoti, taṃ na gāhetabbaṃ. “Atha bhuñjitvā tucchapattāva āgacchanti, yaṃ tehi bhuttaṃ, taṃ nesaṃ gīvā hotī”ti mahāsumatthero āha. Mahāpadumatthero panāha “gīvākiccaṃ ettha natthi, ṭhitikaṃ pana ajānantehi yāva jānanakā āgacchanti, tāva nisīditabbaṃ siyā, evaṃ santepi bhikkhūhi bhuttaṃ subhuttaṃ, idāni pattaṭṭhānena gāhetabba”nti.

Now, if the king, having fed them, also fills their bowls and gives it to them, whatever food is brought back, that should be received according to the allocation by turn. But if, with the thought, 'Let them not go empty-handed,' only a little is placed in their bowls, that should not be accepted. The Elder Mahāsuma said: 'Now, if having eaten, they return with empty bowls, what they have eaten becomes their liability.' The Elder Mahāpaduma, however, said: 'There is no matter of liability here. However, those who do not know the allocation by turn should wait until those who know it arrive. Even so, what has been eaten by the bhikkhus is well-eaten; now, when their turn for the bowl arrives, it should not be accepted.'

Eko ticīvaraparivāro satagghanako piṇḍapāto avassikassa bhikkhuno patto, vihāre ca “evarūpo piṇḍapāto avassikassa patto”ti likhitvā ṭhapesuṃ. Atha saṭṭhivassaccayena añño tathārūpo piṇḍapāto uppanno, ayaṃ kiṃ avassikaṭhitikāya gāhetabbo, udāhu saṭṭhivassaṭhitikāyāti? Saṭṭhivassaṭhitikāyāti vuttaṃ. Ayañhi bhikkhuṭhitikaṃ gahetvāyeva vaḍḍhitoti. Eko uddesabhattaṃ bhuñjitvā sāmaṇero jāto, puna taṃ bhattaṃ sāmaṇeraṭhitikāya pattaṃ gaṇhituṃ labhati. Ayaṃ kira antarābhaṭṭhako nāma. Yo pana paripuṇṇavasso sāmaṇero “sve uddesabhattaṃ labhissatī”ti ajjeva upasampajjati, atikkantā tassa ṭhitikā. Ekassa bhikkhuno uddesabhattaṃ pattaṃ, patto cassa na tuccho hoti, so aññassa samīpe nisinnassa pattaṃ dāpeti, taṃ ce theyyāya haranti, gīvā hoti. Sace pana so bhikkhu “mayhaṃ pattaṃ dammī”ti sayameva deti, assa gīvā na hoti. Athāpi tena bhattena anatthiko hutvā “alaṃ mayhaṃ, tavetaṃ [M 0.0269] bhattaṃ dammi, pattaṃ pesetvā āharāpehī”ti aññaṃ vadati, yaṃ tato āharīyati, sabbaṃ pattasāmikassa hoti. Pattaṃ ce theyyāya haranti, suhaṭo, bhattassa dinnattā gīvā na hoti.

An alms-food offering worth one hundred, accompanied by a set of three robes, was due to a resident monk. And in the monastery, they wrote and placed a notice: 'An alms-food offering of this kind is due to the resident monk.' Then, after sixty years had passed, another similar alms-food offering arose. Should this be taken according to the resident monk's fixed allocation or according to the sixty-year fixed allocation? It was said: 'According to the sixty-year fixed allocation.' For this one has grown old having taken the monk's position. One, having eaten a designated meal, became a novice. Again, he is able to receive that meal which is due according to the novice's fixed allocation. This, it is said, is called an 'intervening meal.' However, if a novice who is of full age, thinking, 'Tomorrow I will receive the designated meal,' takes higher ordination today, his turn has passed. A designated meal is due to a certain monk, and his bowl is not empty. He has another monk sitting nearby give the bowl; if they then steal it by theft, he is liable for replacement. But if that monk gives it himself, saying, 'I give my bowl,' he is not liable for replacement. Furthermore, if, having no need for that meal, he tells another, 'Enough for me. I give this meal to you. Send the bowl and have the food brought back,' whatever is brought from there belongs to the owner of the bowl. If they steal the bowl by theft, it is a successful theft; because the meal had been given, he is not liable for replacement.

Vihāre dasa bhikkhū honti, tesu nava piṇḍapātikā, eko sādiyanako, “dasa uddesapatte dethā”ti vutte piṇḍapātikā gahetuṃ na icchanti. Itaro bhikkhu “sabbāni mayhaṃ pāpuṇantī”ti gaṇhāti, ṭhitikā na hoti. Ekekaṃ ce pāpetvā gaṇhāti, ṭhitikā tiṭṭhati. Evaṃ gāhetvā dasahipi pattehi āharāpetvā “bhante, mayhaṃ saṅgahaṃ karothā”ti nava patte piṇḍapātikānaṃ deti, bhikkhudattiyaṃ nāmetaṃ, gahetuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace so upāsako “bhante, gharaṃ āgantabba”nti vadati, so ca bhikkhu te bhikkhū “etha, bhante, mayhaṃ sahāyā hothā”ti tassa gharaṃ gacchati, yaṃ tattha labhati, sabbaṃ tasseva hoti, itare tena dinnaṃ labhanti. Atha nesaṃ ghareyeva nisīdāpetvā dakkhiṇodakaṃ datvā yāgukhajjakādīni denti “bhante, yaṃ manussā denti, taṃ gaṇhathā”ti, tassa bhikkhuno vacaneneva itaresaṃ vaṭṭati. Bhuttāvīnaṃ patte pūretvā gaṇhitvā gamanatthāya denti, sabbaṃ tasseva bhikkhuno hoti, tena dinnaṃ itaresaṃ vaṭṭati. Yadi pana [V 0.0252] te vihāreyeva tena bhikkhunā “bhante, mayhaṃ bhikkhaṃ gaṇhatha, manussānaṃ vacanaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttā gacchanti, tattha yaṃ bhuñjanti ceva nīharanti ca, sabbaṃ taṃ tesaṃyeva santakaṃ. Athāpi “mayhaṃ bhikkhaṃ gaṇhathā”ti avuttā “manussānaṃ vacanaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti gacchanti, tatra ce ekassa madhurena sarena anumodanaṃ karontassa sutvā therānañca upasame pasīditvā bahuṃ samaṇaparikkhāraṃ denti, ayaṃ theresu pasādena uppanno akatabhāgo nāma, tasmā sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti.

In a monastery, there are ten monks. Among them, nine are alms-food-eaters, and one is a monk who consents to designated food. When it is said, 'Give ten bowls for designated food,' the alms-food-eaters do not wish to take them. The other monk takes them, thinking, 'All will come to me'; a regular turn is not established. If he receives them after having them brought one by one, a regular turn is established. Having caused them to be accepted in this way, and having caused the ten bowls to be brought, he says, 'Venerable sirs, do me a favor,' and gives nine bowls to the alms-food-eaters. This is called a gift of food from a monk; it is allowable to take it. If that lay supporter says, 'Venerable sir, you should come to the house,' and that monk goes to that person's house after saying to those monks, 'Come, venerable sirs, be my companions,' whatever he receives there all belongs to him alone; the others receive what is given by him. Then, if, having seated them in the house itself and having given the water of dedication, the donors give gruel, hard food, and so on, saying, 'Venerable sirs, take what the people give,' it is allowable for the others only by the word of that monk. Having filled the bowls of those who have eaten, they take them and give them for the purpose of their departure; all of it belongs to that monk alone. What is given by him is allowable for the others. If, however, those monks, having been told by that monk in the monastery itself, 'Venerable sirs, take my alms; it is allowable to act on the word of the people,' go, then whatever they both eat and take away there belongs to them alone. Furthermore, if, without being told, 'Take my alms,' they go, thinking, 'It is allowable to act on the word of the people,' and if there, having heard one giving a blessing with a sweet voice, and having become pleased with the tranquility of the elder monks, the donors give many monastic requisites—this, having arisen from confidence in the elder monks, is called the unallotted portion. Therefore, it belongs to all.

Eko saṅghato uddisāpetvā ṭhitikāya gāhitapattaṃ haritvā paṇītassa khādanīyabhojanīyassa pūretvā āharitvā “imaṃ, bhante, sabbo saṅgho paribhuñjatū”ti deti, sabbehi bhājetvā paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Pattasāmikassa pana atikkantampi ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ uddesabhattaṃ dātabbaṃ. Atha paṭhamaṃyeva “sabbaṃ saṅghikapattaṃ dethā”ti vadati, ekassa lajjibhikkhuno santako patto dātabbo. Āharitvā ca “sabbo saṅgho [M 0.0270] paribhuñjatū”ti vutte bhājetvā paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Eko pātiyā bhattaṃ āharitvā “saṅghuddesaṃ dammī”ti vadati, ekekaṃ ālopaṃ adatvā ṭhitikāya ekassa yāpanamattaṃ katvā dātabbaṃ. Atha so bhattaṃ āharitvā kiñci vattuṃ ajānanto tuṇhībhūto acchati, “kassa te ānītaṃ, kassa dātukāmosī”ti na vattabbaṃ. Pucchāsabhāgena hi “tumhākaṃ ānītaṃ, tumhākaṃ dātukāmomhī”ti vadeyya, tato taṃ bhikkhuṃ aññe bhikkhū jigucchantā gīvaṃ parivattetvā oloketabbampi na maññeyyuṃ. Sace pana “kuhiṃ yāsi, kiṃ karonto āhiṇḍasī”ti vutte “uddesabhattaṃ gahetvā āgatomhī”ti vadati, ekena lajjibhikkhunā ṭhitikāya gāhetabbaṃ. Sace ābhataṃ bahu hoti, sabbesaṃ pahoti, ṭhitikākiccaṃ natthi. Therāsanato paṭṭhāya pattaṃ pūretvā dātabbaṃ.

A man has a bowl designated by the Saṅgha, takes it according to the turn, carries it away, fills it with excellent hard and soft food, brings it back, and gives it, saying, “Venerable sirs, may the entire Saṅgha partake of this.” It should be divided by all and partaken of. However, for the owner of the bowl, even if his turn has passed, setting that aside, another designated meal should be given. Now, if at the very beginning he says, “Give the bowl for the entire Saṅgha,” the bowl belonging to one conscientious monk should be given. And having brought it, when it is said, “May the entire Saṅgha partake,” it should be divided and partaken of. A man brings almsfood in a vessel and says, “I give this as a designation for the Saṅgha.” Then, without giving individual mouthfuls, a sustenance-amount should be given to one person according to the turn. Now, if that man brings the almsfood and, not knowing what to say, remains silent, it should not be said, “For whom have you brought it? To whom do you wish to give it?” For, being prompted by the question, he might say, “I have brought it for you; I wish to give it to you.” Because of that, other monks, being disgusted with that monk, might turn their necks and not even consider him worthy of being looked at. But if, when asked, “Where are you going? What are you doing, wandering about?” he says, “I have come, having taken a designated meal,” it should be received by one conscientious monk according to the turn. If the almsfood that is brought is much and is sufficient for all, there is no need for the turn-taking duty. Starting from the elder’s seat, the bowl should be filled and given.

“Saṅghuddesapattaṃ dethā”ti vutte “kiṃ āharissasī”ti avatvā pakatiṭhitikāya eva gāhetabbaṃ. Yo pana pāyāso vā rasapiṇḍapāto vā niccaṃ labbhati, evarūpānaṃ paṇītabhojanānaṃ āveṇikā ṭhitikā kātabbā, tathā saparivārāya yāguyā mahagghānaṃ phalānaṃ paṇītānañca khajjakānaṃ. Pakatibhattayāguphalakhajjakānaṃ ekāva ṭhitikā kātabbā. “Sappiṃ āharissāmī”ti vutte sabbasappīnaṃ ekāva ṭhitikā vaṭṭati, tathā sabbatelānaṃ. “Madhuṃ āharissāmī”ti vutte pana madhuno ekāva ṭhitikā vaṭṭati, tathā phāṇitassa laṭṭhimadhukādīnañca bhesajjānaṃ. Sace pana gandhamālaṃ saṅghuddesaṃ denti, piṇḍapātikassa vaṭṭati, na [V 0.0253] vaṭṭatīti? Āmisasseva paṭikkhittattā vaṭṭati. “Saṅghaṃ uddissa dinnattā pana na gahetabba”nti vadanti.

When it is said, 'Give the bowl designated for the Sangha,' it should be accepted by the regular procedure only, without asking, 'What will you bring?' Furthermore, for whatever pāyāsa or almsfood rich in flavor is regularly received, a special procedure should be made for such choice foods; likewise, for gruel with its accompaniments, for costly fruits, and for choice hard foods. For ordinary rice, gruel, fruits, and hard foods, only a single procedure should be made. When it is said, 'I will bring ghee,' only a single procedure is allowable for all kinds of ghee; likewise for all kinds of oil. But when it is said, 'I will bring honey,' only a single procedure is allowable for honey; likewise for molasses and for medicines such as licorice and so forth. But if they give perfumes and garlands designated for the Sangha, is it allowable for one who undertakes the alms-goer's practice, or is it not? It is allowable because only material food has been rejected. But some say, 'Because it was given having been designated for the Sangha, it should not be accepted.'

Uddesabhattakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on the designated meal is concluded.

210. Nimantanaṃ puggalikaṃ ce, sayameva issaro. Saṅghikaṃ pana uddesabhatte vuttanayeneva gāhetabbaṃ. Sace panettha dūto byatto hoti, “bhante, rājagehe bhikkhusaṅghassa bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti avatvā “bhikkhaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadati, piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati. Atha dūto abyatto “bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadati, bhattuddesako byatto “bhatta”nti avatvā “bhante[M 0.0271], tumhe yātha, tumhe yāthā”ti vadati, evampi piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati, “tumhākaṃ, bhante, paṭipāṭiyā bhattaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti vutte pana na vaṭṭati. Sace nimantituṃ āgatamanusso āsanasālaṃ pavisitvā “aṭṭha bhikkhū dethā”ti vā “aṭṭha patte dethā”ti vā vadati, evampi piṇḍapātikānaṃ vaṭṭati, “tumhe ca tumhe ca gacchathā”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace “aṭṭha bhikkhū detha, bhattaṃ gaṇhatha, aṭṭha patte detha, bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vā vadati, paṭipāṭiyā gāhetabbaṃ. Gāhentena pana vicchinditvā “bhatta”nti avadantena “tumhe ca tumhe ca gacchathā”ti vutte piṇḍapātikānaṃ vaṭṭati. “Bhante, tumhākaṃ pattaṃ detha, tumhe ethā”ti vutte pana “sādhu upāsakā”ti gantabbaṃ. “Saṅghato uddisitvā tumhe ethā”ti vuttepi ṭhitikāya gāhetabbaṃ.

210. If an invitation meal is personal, one is master of it oneself. But if it is for the Sangha, it should be accepted only in the manner stated for the designated meal. If the messenger here is articulate and, without saying, 'Venerable sirs, at the royal palace, accept the meal for the community of bhikkhus,' says, 'Accept alms,' it is permissible even for the alms-round-farers. If the messenger is inarticulate and says, 'Accept a meal,' while the meal-designator is articulate and, without saying 'meal,' says, 'Venerable sirs, you go, you go,' even then it is permissible for the alms-round-farers. But if it is said, 'Venerable sirs, the meal will reach you by turn,' then it is not permissible. If a person who has come to invite enters the seating hall and says, 'Give eight bhikkhus,' or 'Give eight bowls,' even then it is permissible for the alms-round-farers; it should be said, 'You and you, go.' If he says, 'Give eight bhikkhus, accept a meal,' or 'Give eight bowls, accept a meal,' it should be accepted by turn. However, when arranging the acceptance, if one interrupts and, without saying 'meal,' says, 'You and you, go,' it is permissible for the alms-round-farers. But if it is said, 'Venerable sirs, give your bowl, you come,' then one should go, saying, 'Good, lay supporter.' Even if it is said, 'Having been designated from the Sangha, you come,' it should be accepted according to the established procedure.

Nimantanabhattagharato pana pattatthāya āgatassa uddesabhatte vuttanayeneva ṭhitikāya patto dātabbo. Eko “saṅghato paṭipāṭiyā patta”nti avatvā kevalaṃ “ekaṃ pattaṃ dethā”ti vatvā aggāhiteyeva patte yassa kassaci pattaṃ gahetvā pūretvā āharati, taṃ pattasāmikasseva hoti. Uddesabhatte viya ṭhitikāya na gāhetabbaṃ. Idhāpi yo āgantvā tuṇhībhūto tiṭṭhati, so “kassa santikaṃ āgatosī”ti vā “kassa pattaṃ harissasī”ti vā na vattabbo. Pucchāsabhāgena hi “tumhākaṃ santikaṃ āgato, tumhākaṃ pattaṃ harissāmī”ti vadeyya, tato so bhikkhu bhikkhūhi jigucchanīyo assa. “Kuhiṃ gacchasi, kiṃ karonto āhiṇḍasī”ti pana vutte “tassa pattatthāya āgatomhī”ti vadantassa paṭipāṭibhattaṭṭhitikāya gahetvā patto dātabbo. “Bhattaharaṇapattaṃ dethā”ti vuttepi paṭipāṭibhattaṭṭhitikāya eva dātabbo. Sace āharitvā “sabbo saṅgho bhuñjatū”ti vadati, bhājetvā bhuñjitabbaṃ. Pattasāmikassa atikkantampi ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ paṭipāṭibhattaṃ gāhetabbaṃ.

But from the house of an invitation meal, for one who has come for a bowl, the bowl should be given according to the procedure stated for the designated meal. If a certain person, without saying, 'A bowl from the Sangha by turn,' but merely saying, 'Give one bowl,' takes anyone's bowl before it has been accepted, has it filled, and brings it, that food belongs only to the owner of the bowl. It should not be caused to be accepted according to the procedure, as in the case of the designated meal. Here also, if a person comes and stands silent, he should not be asked, 'To whose presence have you come?' or 'Whose bowl will you carry?' For, in response to the question, he might say, 'I have come to your presence, I will carry your bowl,' and for that reason that bhikkhu would be one to be reproached by the bhikkhus. But when asked, 'Where are you going? What are you doing, wandering about?' to that person who says, 'I have come for his bowl,' a bowl should be given, having been accepted according to the procedure for the meal received in turn. Even when it is said, 'Give a bowl for carrying food,' it should be given only according to the procedure for the meal received in turn. If, having brought it, he says, 'Let the entire Sangha eat,' it should be divided and eaten. For the owner of the bowl, even if his turn has passed, setting that aside, another meal-in-turn should be accepted for him.

Eko [V 0.0254] pātiyā bhattaṃ āharitvā “saṅghassa dammī”ti vadati, ālopabhattaṭṭhitikato paṭṭhāya ālopasaṅkhepena bhājetabbaṃ. Sace pana tuṇhībhūto acchati, “kassa te ābhataṃ, kassa dātukāmosī”ti [M 0.0272] na vattabbo.
