Sace pana “kuhiṃ gacchasi, kiṃ karonto āhiṇḍasī”ti vutte pana “saṅghassa me bhattaṃ ābhataṃ, therānaṃ me bhattaṃ ābhata”nti vadati, gahetvā ālopabhattaṭṭhitikāya bhājetabbaṃ. Sace pana evaṃ ābhataṃ bhattaṃ bahu hoti, sakalasaṅghassa pahoti, abhihaṭabhikkhā nāma, piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati, ṭhitikāpucchanakiccaṃ natthi, therāsanato paṭṭhāya pattaṃ pūretvā dātabbaṃ.

If a person brings food in a bowl and says, 'I give this to the Sangha,' it should be distributed by giving one lump at a time, starting from the procedure for food-by-the-lump. But if he remains silent, he should not be asked, 'For whom have you brought this? To whom do you wish to give it?' But if, when asked, 'Where are you going? What are you doing, wandering about?' he replies, 'I have brought food for the Sangha,' or 'I have brought food for the elders,' it should be accepted and distributed according to the procedure for food-by-the-lump. But if the food brought in this manner is abundant and is sufficient for the entire Sangha, it is called 'brought-almsfood,' and it is allowable even for those who go on almsround. There is no duty to ask about the procedure; starting from the elder's seat, it should be given, having filled the bowl.

Upāsako saṅghattherassa vā ganthadhutaṅgavasena abhiññātassa vā bhattuddesakassa vā pahiṇati “amhākaṃ bhattagahaṇatthāya aṭṭha bhikkhū gahetvā āgacchathā”ti, sacepi ñātiupaṭṭhākehi pesitaṃ hoti, ime tayo janā pucchituṃ na labhanti, āruḷhāyeva mātikaṃ. Saṅghato aṭṭha bhikkhū uddisāpetvā attanavamehi gantabbaṃ. Kasmā? Bhikkhusaṅghassa hi ete bhikkhū nissāya lābho uppajjatīti. Ganthadhutaṅgādīhi pana anabhiññāto āvāsikabhikkhu āpucchituṃ labhati, tasmā tena “kiṃ saṅghato gaṇhāmi, udāhu ye jānāmi, tehi saddhiṃ āgacchāmī”ti mātikaṃ āropetvā yathā dāyakā vadanti, tathā paṭipajjitabbaṃ. “Tumhākaṃ nissitake vā ye vā jānātha, te gahetvā ethā”ti vutte pana ye icchanti, tehi saddhiṃ gantuṃ labhati. Sace “aṭṭha bhikkhū pahiṇathā”ti pesenti, saṅghatova pesetabbā. Attanā sace aññasmiṃ gāme sakkā hoti bhikkhā labhituṃ, añño gāmo gantabbo. Na sakkā ce hoti labhituṃ, soyeva gāmo piṇḍāya pavisitabbo.

A lay follower sends a message to the Sangha's elder, or to one well-known on account of scriptural learning and ascetic practices, or to the meal-designator, saying, 'Taking eight bhikkhus, please come for the purpose of receiving our meal.' Even if the message is sent by relatives or attendants, these three persons do not get to ask questions; they are already placed on the register. Having caused eight bhikkhus to be appointed from the Sangha, one should go as the ninth. Why? Because it is in dependence on these bhikkhus that gain arises for the community of bhikkhus. But a resident bhikkhu who is not well-known for such things as scriptural learning and ascetic practices gets to ask. Therefore, he should raise the matter for the procedure, asking, 'Shall I take them from the Sangha, or shall I come with those whom I know?' and he should act according to what the donors say. But if it is said, 'Taking your dependents or those whom you know, please come,' then he gets to go with whomever he wishes. If they send a message saying, 'Please send eight bhikkhus,' they must be sent from the Sangha itself. If it is possible for oneself to obtain almsfood in another village, another village should be gone to. If it is not possible to obtain it, that very village should be entered for alms.

Nimantitabhikkhū āsanasālāya nisinnā honti, tatra ce manussā “patte dethā”ti āgacchanti, animantitehi na dātabbā, “ete nimantitā bhikkhū”ti vattabbaṃ, “tumhepi dethā”ti vutte pana dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Ussavādīsu manussā sayameva pariveṇāni ca padhānagharāni ca gantvā tipiṭake ca dhammakathike ca bhikkhusatenapi saddhiṃ nimantenti, tadā tehi ye jānanti, te gahetvā gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Kasmā? Na hi mahābhikkhusaṅghena atthikā manussā pariveṇapadhānagharāni gacchanti, sannipātaṭṭhānatova yathāsatti yathābalaṃ bhikkhū gaṇhitvā gacchantīti.

The invited bhikkhus are seated in the rest-house. If people come there saying, 'Give bowls,' the uninvited bhikkhus should not give them. It should be said, 'These are invited bhikkhus.' But if it is said, 'You also, give,' then it is permissible to give. On festival days and so on, people themselves go to the monasteries and meditation halls and invite masters of the Tipiṭaka and Dhamma-preachers, together with even a hundred bhikkhus. Then, it is proper for those bhikkhus to take those whom they know and go. Why? For people who need monks do not go to the monasteries and meditation halls with a great community of bhikkhus; rather, from the assembly place itself, they take bhikkhus according to their ability and strength and go.

Sace [M 0.0273] pana saṅghatthero vā ganthadhutaṅgavasena abhiññāto vā bhattuddesako vā aññatra vā vassaṃ vasitvā katthaci vā gantvā puna sakaṭṭhānaṃ āgacchati, manussā ca āgantukassa sakkāraṃ [V 0.0255] karonti, ekavāraṃ ye jānanti, te gahetvā gantabbaṃ. Paṭibaddhakālato paṭṭhāya dutiyavāre āraddhe saṅghatoyeva gahetvā gantabbaṃ. Abhinavaāgantukāva hutvā “ñātī vā upaṭṭhāke vā passissāmī”ti gacchanti, tatra ce tesaṃ ñātī ca upaṭṭhākā ca sakkāraṃ karonti, ettha pana ye jānanti, te gahetvā gantumpi vaṭṭati. Yo pana atilābhī hoti, sakaṭṭhānañca āgantukaṭṭhānañca ekasadisaṃ, sabbattha manussā saṅghabhattaṃ sajjetvāva nisīdanti, tena saṅghatova gahetvā gantabbanti ayaṃ nimantane viseso. Avaseso sabbapañho uddesabhatte vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Kurundiyaṃ pana “aṭṭha mahāthere dethāti vutte aṭṭha mahātherāva dātabbā”ti vuttaṃ. Esa nayo majjhimādīsu. Sace pana avisesetvā “aṭṭha bhikkhū dethā”ti vadati, saṅghato dātabbāti.

If, however, the Elder of the Saṅgha, or one well-known by way of scriptural learning and ascetic practices, or the meal-designator, having spent the rains-residence elsewhere or having gone somewhere, returns to his own place, and people make offerings to the newcomer, for the first time it is proper for him to take those whom he knows and go. Beginning from the fixed time, when a second occasion arises, he should take bhikkhus from the Saṅgha itself and go. If new arrivals go thinking, 'We will see our relatives or supporters,' and their relatives and supporters there make offerings to them, in this case also, it is proper for them to take those whom they know and go. But as for a bhikkhu who has abundant gains, for whom his own place and the place he has come to are alike, and everywhere people wait, having prepared a meal for the Saṅgha—that bhikkhu should take bhikkhus only from the Saṅgha and go. This is the distinction in the matter of invitation. All remaining questions should be understood according to the method stated for the designated meal. But in the Kurundī commentary, it is said: 'When it is said, "Give the eight Great Elders," only the eight Great Elders should be given.' This is the method for the middle-rank bhikkhus and so on. If, however, one says without specifying, 'Give eight bhikkhus,' they should be given from the Saṅgha.

Nimantanabhattakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Chapter on Invited Meals is concluded.

211. Salākabhattaṃ pana “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, salākāya vā paṭṭikāya vā upanibandhitvā opuñjitvā bhattaṃ uddisitu”nti (cūḷava. 326) vacanato rukkhasāramayāya salākāya vā veḷuvilīvatālapaṇṇādimayāya paṭṭikāya vā “asukassa nāma salākabhatta”nti evaṃ akkharāni upanibandhitvā pacchiyaṃ vā cīvarabhoge vā katvā sabbasalākāyo opuñjitvā punappunaṃ heṭṭhupariyavasena āloḷetvā pañcaṅgasamannāgatena bhattuddesakena sace ṭhitikā atthi, ṭhitikato paṭṭhāya, no ce atthi, therāsanato paṭṭhāya salākā dātabbā. Pacchā āgatānampi ekābaddhavasena dūre ṭhitānampi uddesabhatte vuttanayeneva dātabbā.

211. Regarding the ticket-meal, because of the saying, “I allow, O monks, to designate a meal by writing on a ticket or a slip and shaking them down,” one should write the letters, “The ticket-meal of so-and-so,” on a ticket made of heartwood or on a slip made of materials such as bamboo strips, rattan, or palm leaves. Having placed them in a basket or in a fold of a robe, having shaken down all the tickets, and having mixed them up again and again by turning them upside down and right side up, the tickets should be given out by a meal-distributor who is endowed with the five factors. If there is a fixed order of seniority, they should be given starting from that fixed order; if there is not, they should be given starting from the elder’s seat. To those who arrive later, and also to those standing at a distance but within the continuous boundary of the assembly, they should be given in the very same way as stated for the designated meal.

Sace vihārassa samantato bahū gocaragāmā, bhikkhū pana na bahū, gāmavasenapi salākā pāpuṇanti. “Tumhākaṃ asukagāme salākabhattaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti gāmavaseneva gāhetabbaṃ. Evaṃ gāhentena sacepi ekamekasmiṃ gāme nānappakārāni saṭṭhi salākabhattāni, sabbāni gahitāneva honti. Tassa pattagāmasamīpe aññānipi dve tīṇi salākabhattāni [M 0.0274] honti, tāni tasseva dātabbāni. Na hi sakkā tesaṃ kāraṇā aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ pahiṇitunti.

If there are many alms-villages all around a monastery, but the monks are not many, the tickets may be assigned by village. When it is said, “The ticket-meal in such-and-such a village is assigned to you,” it should be accepted by village. When they are assigned in this way, even if in a single village there are sixty ticket-meals of various kinds, all are considered to have been accepted. If near the village that has been assigned to a monk there are also two or three other ticket-meals, those should be given to that very monk. For it is not possible to send another monk on account of those.

Sace ekaccesu gāmesu bahūni salākabhattāni sallakkhetvā sattannampi aṭṭhannampi bhikkhūnaṃ dātabbāni. Dentena pana catunnaṃ pañcannaṃ bhattānaṃ salākāyo ekato bandhitvā dātabbā. Sace taṃ gāmaṃ atikkamitvā añño gāmo hoti, tasmiñca ekameva salākabhattaṃ, taṃ pana pātova denti, tampi etesu bhikkhūsu ekassa niggahena datvā “pātova taṃ gahetvā pacchā [V 0.0256] orimagāme itarāni bhattāni gaṇhāhī”ti vattabbo. Sace orimagāme salākabhattesu aggahitesveva gahitasaññāya gacchati, parabhāgagāme salākabhattaṃ gahetvā puna vihāraṃ āgantvā itarāni gahetvā orimagāmo gantabbo. Na hi bahisīmāya saṅghalābho gāhetuṃ labbhatīti ayaṃ nayo kurundiyaṃ vutto. Sace pana bhikkhū bahū honti, gāmavasena salākā na pāpuṇanti, vīthivasena vā vīthiyaṃ ekagehavasena vā ekakulavasena vā gāhetabbaṃ. Vīthiādīsu ca yattha bahūni bhattāni, tattha gāme vuttanayeneva bahūnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ gāhetabbāni, salākāsu asati uddisitvāpi gāhetabbāni.

If, having noted many ticket-meals in some villages, they should be given to seven or eight monks. But by one who is giving, the tickets for four or five meals should be tied together and given. If, having passed beyond that village, there is another village, and in it there is only one ticket-meal, and they give that early in the morning, that too should be given to one of these monks by special assignment, and he should be told: 'Take that early in the morning, and afterwards, take the other meals in the near village.' If, while the ticket-meals in the near village have not yet been received, one goes with the perception that they have been received, then after receiving the ticket-meal in the further village, one should return to the monastery, receive the other meals, and then go to the near village. For indeed, a gain of the Sangha is not to be received outside the boundary—this method is stated in the Kurundi. But if there are many monks, and the tickets do not suffice on a village-by-village basis, they should be received by way of street, or in a street by way of a single row of houses, or by way of a single family. And in streets and so on, wherever there are many meals, they should be received for many monks in that village by the method already stated. When there are no tickets, they may also be received by designation.

212. Salākadāyakena pana vattaṃ jānitabbaṃ. Tena hi kālasseva vuṭṭhāya pattacīvaraṃ gahetvā bhojanasālaṃ gantvā asammaṭṭhaṭṭhānaṃ sammajjitvā pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā “idāni bhikkhūhi vattaṃ kataṃ bhavissatī”ti kālaṃ sallakkhetvā ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā bhikkhūsu sannipatitesu paṭhamameva vāragāme salākabhattaṃ gāhetabbaṃ, “tuyhaṃ asukasmiṃ nāma vāragāme salākā pāpuṇāti, tatra gacchā”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace abhirekagāvute gāmo hoti, taṃ divasaṃ gacchantā kilamanti, “sve tuyhaṃ vāragāme pāpuṇātī”ti ajjeva gāhetabbaṃ. Yo vāragāmaṃ pesiyamāno na gacchati, aññaṃ salākaṃ maggati, na dātabbā. Saddhānañhi manussānaṃ puññahāni ca saṅghassa ca lābhacchedo hoti, tasmā tassa dutiyepi tatiyepi divase aññā salākā na dātabbā, “attano pattaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā bhuñjāhī”ti vattabbo, tīṇi pana divasāni agacchantassa vāragāmato orimavāragāme salākā gāhetabbā. Tañce na gaṇhāti, tato paṭṭhāya tassa aññaṃ salākaṃ dātuṃ na vaṭṭati, daṇḍakammaṃ daḷhaṃ kātabbaṃ[M 0.0275]. Saṭṭhito vā paṇṇāsato vā na parihāpetabbaṃ. Vāragāme gāhetvā vihāravāro gāhetabbo, “tuyhaṃ vihāravāro pāpuṇātī”ti vattabbaṃ. Vihāravārikassa dve tisso yāgusalākāyo tisso catasso bhattasalākāyo ca dātabbā, nibaddhaṃ katvā pana na dātabbā. Yāgubhattadāyakā hi “amhākaṃ yāgubhattaṃ vihāragopakāvabhuñjantī”ti aññathattaṃ āpajjeyyuṃ, tasmā aññesu kulesu dātabbā.

212. The duty of the distributor of tickets should be known. He should rise early in the morning, take his bowl and robe, go to the meal hall, sweep any unswept area, set out drinking water and water for use, and then, noting the time—'Now the monks will have performed their duties'—he should strike the bell. When the monks have assembled, he should first distribute the tickets for the meal in the village whose turn it is, saying, 'Your ticket has arrived for such-and-such village whose turn it is; go there.' If the village is more than a gāvuta away and those going on that day would become weary, he should give the ticket this very day, saying, 'Your ticket will arrive for the village whose turn it is tomorrow.' If a monk who is sent to the village whose turn it is does not go and asks for another ticket, it should not be given. For there would be a loss of merit for the faithful people and a loss of gain for the Saṅgha. Therefore, on the second or third day, other tickets should not be given to him; he should be told, 'Go to your own designated place and eat.' However, for one who does not go for three days, a ticket for a nearer village whose turn it is should be given. If he does not accept it, from then on it is not allowable to give that monk another ticket; a strict penalty must be imposed. It should not be reduced below sixty or fifty. After distributing the tickets for the village whose turn it is, the turn for monastery duty should be assigned, saying, 'Your turn for monastery duty has arrived.' The one on monastery duty should be given two or three tickets for gruel and three or four tickets for meals. However, they should not be given as a fixed arrangement. For the donors of gruel and meals might have a change of mind, thinking, 'Only the monastery guardians are eating our gruel and meals.' Therefore, tickets should be given for meals from other families.

Sace vihāravārikānaṃ sabhāgā āharitvā denti, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce, vāraṃ gahetvā tesaṃ yāgubhattaṃ āharāpetabbaṃ, tāva nesaṃ salākā phātikammameva bhavanti. Vassaggena pattaṭṭhāne pana aññampi paṇītabhattasalākaṃ gaṇhituṃ labhantiyeva. Atirekauttaribhaṅgassa ekacārikabhattassa visuṃ ṭhitikaṃ katvā salākā dātabbā. Sace yena salākā laddhā, so taṃ divasaṃ taṃ bhattaṃ na labhati, puna divase gāhetabbaṃ. Bhattaññeva labhati, na uttaribhaṅgaṃ, evampi [V 0.0257] puna gāhetabbaṃ. Khīrabhattasalākāyapi eseva nayo. Sace pana khīrameva labhati, na bhattaṃ, khīralābhato paṭṭhāya puna na gāhetabbaṃ. Dve tīṇi ekacārikabhattāni ekasseva pāpuṇanti, dubbhikkhasamaye saṅghanavakena laddhakāle vijaṭetvā visuṃ gāhetabbāni. Pākatikasalākabhattaṃ aladdhassapi punadivase gāhetabbaṃ.

If the counterparts of the monastery attendants bring and give, this is good. If not, having assigned a turn, gruel and food should be caused to be brought for them; for that long, their tickets are indeed a matter of profit. However, at the place reached by seniority of rains-residence, they may indeed receive another ticket for excellent food as well. For a one-person meal with extra side-dishes, having made a separate arrangement, tickets should be given. If a monk by whom a ticket has been obtained does not get that food on that day, it should be obtained on another day. He gets only the food, not the side-dish; even so, it should be obtained again. In the case of a ticket for milk-rice also, this is the same method. But if he gets only milk, not the food, starting from the receipt of the milk, it should not be obtained again. Should two or three portions of food sufficient for one person fall to just one person, if it is a time of famine, at the time of receiving, they should be separated by the junior-most monk of the Sangha and obtained separately. Even for one who has not received the regular ticket-food, it should be obtained on the next day.

Sace khuddako vihāro hoti, sabbe bhikkhū ekasambhogā, ucchusalākaṃ gāhentena yassa kassaci sammukhībhūtassa pāpetvā mahātherādīnaṃ divā tacchetvā dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Rasasalākaṃ pāpetvā pacchābhattampi parissāvetvā phāṇitaṃ vā kāretvā piṇḍapātikādīnampi dātabbaṃ, āgantukānaṃ āgatānāgatabhāvaṃ ñatvā gāhetabbā. Mahāāvāse ṭhitikaṃ katvā gāhetabbā. Takkasalākampi sabhāgaṭṭhāne pāpetvā vā dhūmāpetvā pacāpetvā vā therānaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Mahāāvāse vuttanayeneva paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Phalasalākapūvasalākabhesajjagandhamālāsalākāyopi visuṃ ṭhitikāya gāhetabbā. Bhesajjādisalākāyo cettha kiñcāpi piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭanti, salākavasena pana gāhitattā na sāditabbā. Aggabhikkhāmattaṃ salākabhattaṃ denti, ṭhitikaṃ [M 0.0276] pucchitvā gāhetabbaṃ. Asatiyā ṭhitikāya therāsanato paṭṭhāya gāhetabbaṃ. Sace tādisāni bhattāni bahūni honti, ekekassa bhikkhuno dve tīṇi dātabbāni. No ce, ekekameva datvā paṭipāṭiyā gatāya puna therāsanato paṭṭhāya dātabbaṃ. Atha antarāva upacchijjati, ṭhitikā sallakkhetabbā. Yadi pana tādisaṃ bhattaṃ nibaddhameva hoti, yassa pāpuṇāti, so vattabbo “laddhā vā aladdhā vā svepi gaṇheyyāsī”ti. Ekaṃ anibaddhaṃ hoti, labhanadivase pana yāvadatthaṃ labhati. Alabhanadivasā bahutarā honti, taṃ yassa pāpuṇāti, so alabhitvā “sve gaṇheyyāsī”ti vattabbo.

If the monastery is small and all monks have meals in common, it is permissible for one who takes the sugar-cane ticket to have it delivered to any monk who is present, and after peeling it during the day, to give it to the great elders and others. Regarding the juice-ticket, having had it delivered, it should be given even to alms-round-goers and others, even after the meal, having had the juice strained or made into molasses. For newcomers, the tickets should be taken after ascertaining whether they have arrived or not. In a large monastery, they should be taken after establishing a roster. It is also permissible to have the buttermilk ticket delivered to a common place, or having had it flavored or cooked, to give it to the elders. In a large monastery, one should proceed according to the method already stated. Fruit tickets, cake tickets, medicine tickets, perfume tickets, and garland tickets should also be taken separately according to a roster. Herein, although medicine tickets and the like are permissible even for alms-round-goers, since they are received by means of a ticket, they should not be accepted. If they give a ticket-meal amounting only to the first portion of alms-food, it should be taken after inquiring about the roster. If there is no roster, it should be taken starting from the elders' seats. If there are many such meals, two or three tickets should be given to each monk. If not, having given only one each, when the turn has passed in order, it should be given again starting from the elders' seats. Then, if it is interrupted in the middle, the roster should be noted. However, if such a meal is indeed regular, whoever is due should be told, 'Whether you have received it or not, you may take it tomorrow as well.' A certain ticket-meal may be irregular; however, on the day of receiving, one receives as much as is wanted. The days of not receiving are more numerous; whoever is due that ticket, not having received it, should be told, 'You may take it tomorrow.'

Yo salākāsu gahitāsu pacchā āgacchati, tassa atikkantāva salākā na upaṭṭhāpetvā dātabbā. Salākaṃ nāma ghaṇṭiṃ paharaṇato paṭṭhāya āgantvā hatthaṃ pasārentova labhati, aññassa āgantvā samīpe ṭhitassapi atikkantā atikkantāva hoti. Sace panassa añño gaṇhanto atthi, sayaṃ anāgatopi labhati, sabhāgaṭṭhāne “asuko anāgato”ti ñatvā “ayaṃ tassa salākā”ti ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace “anāgatassa na dātabbā”ti katikaṃ karonti, adhammikā hoti. Antoupacāre ṭhitassa hi bhājanīyabhaṇḍaṃ pāpuṇāti. Sace pana “anāgatassa dethā”ti mahāsaddaṃ karonti, daṇḍakammaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ, “āgantvā gaṇhantū”ti vattabbaṃ. Cha pañcasalākā naṭṭhā honti, bhattuddesako dāyakānaṃ nāmaṃ na sarati, so ce naṭṭhasalākā mahātherassa vā attano vā pāpetvā bhikkhū vadeyya “mayā asukagāme [V 0.0258] salākabhattaṃ mayhaṃ pāpitaṃ, tumhe tattha laddhasalākabhattaṃ bhuñjeyyāthā”ti, vaṭṭati, vihāre apāpitaṃ pana āsanasālāya taṃ bhattaṃ labhitvā tattheva pāpetvā bhuñjituṃ na vaṭṭati. “Ajja paṭṭhāya mayhaṃ salākabhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vutte tatra āsanasālāya gāhetuṃ na vaṭṭati, vihāraṃ ānetvā gāhetabbaṃ. “Sve paṭṭhāyā”ti vutte pana bhattuddesakassa ācikkhitabbaṃ “sve paṭṭhāya asukakulaṃ nāma salākabhattaṃ deti, salākaggāhaṇakāle sareyyāsī”ti. Dubbhikkhe salākabhattaṃ pacchinditvā subhikkhe jāte kañci bhikkhuṃ disvā “ajja paṭṭhāya amhākaṃ salākabhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti puna paṭṭhapenti, antogāme [M 0.0277] agāhetvā vihāraṃ ānetvā gāhetabbaṃ. Idañhi salākabhattaṃ nāma uddesabhattasadisaṃ na hoti, vihārameva sandhāya dīyati, tasmā bahiupacāre gāhetuṃ na vaṭṭati, “sve paṭṭhāyā”ti vutte pana vihāre gāhetabbameva.

A monk who comes later, after the tickets have been taken, should not be presented with and given a ticket that has already passed. A ticket is obtained by one who comes and extends his hand from the moment the bell is struck; even for another who comes and stands nearby, if it has passed, it has indeed passed. However, if there is another to take it for him, he obtains it even if he himself has not arrived. In a common place, knowing that 'so-and-so has not arrived,' it is permissible to set aside a ticket, saying, 'This is his ticket.' If they make an agreement, 'It should not be given to one who has not arrived,' that agreement is unrighteous. For what is to be shared reaches one who is within the precinct. But if they make a loud noise, saying, 'Give to those who have not arrived,' a penalty should be imposed, and it should be said, 'Let them come and take it.' If five or six tickets are lost, and the meal-distributor does not remember the donors' names, should he, having assigned the lost tickets to the great elder or to himself, say to the monks, 'A ticket-meal in such-and-such a village has been assigned to me; you may eat the ticket-meal obtained there,' it is permissible. However, if it was not assigned at the monastery, it is not permissible to obtain that meal in the dining hall and, having had it assigned there, to eat it. If it is said, 'From today, take my ticket-meal,' it is not permissible to take it there in the dining hall; it must be brought to the monastery and taken. But if it is said, 'Starting tomorrow,' the meal-distributor should be informed thus: 'Starting tomorrow, such-and-such a family will give a ticket-meal; you should remember this at the time of taking the tickets.' If, during a famine, a ticket-meal was discontinued, and when there is abundance, seeing some monk, they re-establish it, saying, 'From today, take our ticket-meal,' it should not be taken within the village but should be brought to the monastery and taken. For this ticket-meal is not like an assigned meal; it is given with reference to the monastery itself. Therefore, it is not permissible to take it outside the precinct. But if it is said, 'Starting tomorrow,' it must be taken in the monastery.

Gamiko bhikkhu yaṃ disābhāgaṃ gantukāmo, tattha aññena vāragāmasalākā laddhā hoti, taṃ gahetvā itaraṃ bhikkhuṃ “mayhaṃ pattasalākaṃ tvaṃ gaṇhāhī”ti vatvā gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Tena pana upacārasīmaṃ anatikkanteyeva tasmiṃ tassa salākā gāhetabbā. Chaḍḍitavihāre vasitvā manussā “bodhicetiyādīni jaggitvā bhuñjantū”ti salākabhattaṃ paṭṭhapenti, bhikkhū sabhāgaṭṭhānesu vasitvā kālasseva gantvā tattha vattaṃ karitvā taṃ bhattaṃ bhuñjanti, vaṭṭati. Sace tesu svātanāya attano pāpetvā gatesu āgantuko bhikkhu chaḍḍitavihāre vasitvā kālasseva vattaṃ katvā ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā salākabhattaṃ attano pāpetvā āsanasālaṃ gacchati, sova tassa bhattassa issaro. Yo pana bhikkhūsu vattaṃ karontesuyeva bhūmiyaṃ dve tayo sammuñjanīpahāre datvā ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā “dhuragāme salākabhattaṃ mayhaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti gacchati, tassa taṃ corikāya gahitattā na pāpuṇāti, vattaṃ katvā pāpetvā pacchāgatabhikkhūnaṃyeva hoti.

A monk who is a traveler wishes to go to a certain region. If a ticket for a turn-village in that place has been obtained by another monk, it is permissible for the traveler to depart, having taken that ticket and having said to a different monk, 'You take the ticket that has fallen to me.' However, the ticket of that departing monk must be taken by the resident monk before he has passed beyond the precinct boundary. Laypeople, having stayed in an abandoned monastery, may establish a ticket-meal, thinking, 'Let them eat after looking after the Bodhi tree, cetiyas, and so forth.' It is permissible for monks, having resided in suitable places, to go early in the morning, perform the duties there, and eat that meal. If, when those monks have gone after having had their own share assigned for the next day, a visiting monk, having resided in the abandoned monastery, performs his duties early, strikes the bell, has the ticket-meal assigned to himself, and goes to the dining hall, he alone is the owner of that meal. But as for the monk who, while the other monks are still performing their duties, gives two or three sweeps on the ground with a broom, strikes the bell, and departs, saying, 'The ticket-meal in the regular-alms-village is due to me,' it does not belong to him, as it was taken by theft. It belongs only to the monks who came later, who performed the duties and had it assigned.

Eko gāmo atidūre hoti, bhikkhū niccaṃ gantuṃ na icchanti, manussā “mayaṃ puññena paribāhirā homā”ti vadanti, ye tassa gāmassa āsannavihāre sabhāgabhikkhū, te vattabbā “imesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anāgatadivase tumhe bhuñjathā”ti, salākā pana devasikaṃ pāpetabbā. Tā ca kho pana ghaṇṭipaharaṇamattena vā pacchicālanamattena vā pāpitā na honti, pacchiṃ pana gahetvā salākā pīṭhake ākiritabbā, pacchi pana mukhavaṭṭiyaṃ na gahetabbā. Sace hi tattha ahi vā vicchiko vā bhaveyya, dukkhaṃ uppādeyya, tasmā heṭṭhā gahetvā pacchiṃ parammukhaṃ katvā salākā ākiritabbā “sacepi sappo bhavissati, ettova palāyissatī”ti. Evaṃ salākā ākiritvā gāmādivasena pubbe vuttanayeneva gāhetabbā.

A certain village is very far away, and monks do not wish to go constantly. The people say, 'We are excluded from merit.' The like-minded monks who are in the nearby monastery of that village should be told, 'On the days these monks do not come, you should eat.' However, the lots should be caused to reach daily. But they are not caused to reach merely by striking the bell or merely by shaking the basket. Instead, having taken the basket, the lots should be scattered on a seat. The basket should not be held at the rim of its opening. For if there were a snake or a scorpion there, it would cause suffering. Therefore, holding the basket from below and turning it away, the lots should be scattered, with the thought, 'Even if there is a snake, it will flee just from this.' Having scattered the lots in this way, they should be taken as stated previously, according to the village and so forth.

Apica [M 0.0278][V 0.0259] ekaṃ mahātherassa pāpetvā “avasesā mayhaṃ pāpuṇantī”ti attano pāpetvā vattaṃ katvā cetiyaṃ vanditvā vitakkamāḷake ṭhitehi bhikkhūhi “pāpitā, āvuso, salākā”ti vutte “āma, bhante, tumhe gatagatagāme salākabhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vattabbaṃ. Evañhi pāpitāpi supāpitāva honti. Bhikkhū sabbarattiṃ dhammassavanatthaṃ aññaṃ vihāraṃ gacchantā “mayaṃ tattha dānaṃ aggahetvāva amhākaṃ gocaragāme piṇḍāya caritvā āgamissāmā”ti salākā aggahetvāva gatā vihāre therassa pattaṃ salākabhattaṃ bhuñjituṃ āgacchanti, vaṭṭati. Atha mahātheropi “ahaṃ idha kiṃ karomī”ti tehiyeva saddhiṃ gacchati, tehi gatavihāre abhuñjitvāva gocaragāmaṃ anuppattehi “detha, bhante, patte, salākayāguādīni āharissāmā”ti vutte pattā na dātabbā. Kasmā, bhante, na dethāti. Vihāraṭṭhakaṃ bhattaṃ vihāre vutthānaṃ pāpuṇāti, mayaṃ aññavihāre vutthāti. “Detha, bhante, na mayaṃ vihāre pālikāya dema, tumhākaṃ dema, gaṇhatha amhākaṃ bhikkha”nti vutte pana vaṭṭati.

Furthermore, having assigned one ticket to the great elder, and having assigned the remainder to oneself with the thought, 'The remaining tickets will accrue to me,' and having performed his duties and paid homage to the cetiya, when standing in the discussion hall, if he is asked by the monks, 'Sirs, have the tickets been distributed?' he should reply, 'Yes, venerable sirs, you may take the ticket-food in whatever village you go to.' For in this way, even though distributed, they are well-distributed. If monks, going to another monastery for the entire night to listen to the Dhamma, depart without taking tickets, thinking, 'We will not take the offering there; we will go for alms in our own resort-village and then return,' and they come to eat the ticket-food that has accrued to the elder in the monastery, it is allowable. Then, if the great elder also thinks, 'What shall I do here?' and goes together with them, and if, without having eaten at the monastery they went to, they arrive back at their resort-village and the laypeople say, 'Venerable sirs, give us the bowls; we will bring ticket-gruel and other things,' the bowls should not be given. If they ask, 'Venerable sirs, why do you not give them?' the reply should be, 'The food belonging to the monastery accrues to those who have resided in the monastery, whereas we have resided in another monastery.' However, if they say, 'Venerable sirs, please give them. We are not giving to the monastery's keeper; we are giving to you. Please accept our alms,' then it is allowable.

Salākabhattakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on ticket-food is concluded.

213. Pakkhikādīsu pana yaṃ abhilakkhitesu cātuddasī pañcadasī pañcamī aṭṭhamīti imesu pakkhesu kammappasutehi uposathaṃ kātuṃ satikaraṇatthāya dīyati, taṃ pakkhikaṃ nāma. Taṃ salākabhattagatikameva hoti, gāhetvā bhuñjitabbaṃ. Sace salākabhattampi pakkhikabhattampi bahuṃ sabbesaṃ vinivijjhitvā gacchati, dvepi bhattāni visuṃ visuṃ gāhetabbāni. Sace bhikkhusaṅgho mahā, pakkhikaṃ gāhetvā tassa ṭhitikāya salākabhattaṃ gāhetabbaṃ, salākabhattaṃ vā gāhāpetvā tassa ṭhitikāya pakkhikaṃ gāhetabbaṃ. Yesaṃ na pāpuṇāti, te piṇḍāya carissanti. Sace dvepi bhattāni bahūni, bhikkhū mandā, salākabhattaṃ nāma devasikaṃ labbhati, tasmā taṃ ṭhapetvā “pakkhikaṃ, āvuso, bhuñjathā”ti pakkhikameva dātabbaṃ. Pakkhikaṃ paṇītaṃ denti, visuṃ ṭhitikā kātabbā, “sve pakkho”ti ajja pakkhikaṃ na gāhetabbaṃ. Sace pana dāyakā vadanti “svepi amhākaṃ ghare lūkhabhattaṃ bhavissati, ajjeva pakkhikabhattaṃ uddisathā”ti, evaṃ vaṭṭati.

213. Furthermore, regarding fortnightly food and so on, whatever food is given by those diligent in good deeds on these specified fortnights—the fourteenth, the fifteenth, the fifth, and the eighth—for the purpose of establishing mindfulness to observe the Uposatha, that is called fortnightly food. It has the same procedure as ticket-food; having been received, it should be eaten. If both ticket-food and fortnightly food are abundant and reach all without being divided, both foods should be received separately. If the community of monks is large, having received the fortnightly food, the ticket-food should be received according to its turn; or, having had the ticket-food received, the fortnightly food should be received according to its turn. Those whom it does not reach will go for alms-food. If both foods are abundant but the monks are few, since ticket-food is received daily, that should be set aside, and only the fortnightly food should be given, with the words, 'Venerable sirs, eat the fortnightly food.' If they give excellent fortnightly food, a separate turn should be arranged. Thinking, 'Tomorrow is the fortnight day,' the fortnightly food should not be received today. However, if the donors say, 'Tomorrow, too, there will be coarse food in our house; please designate the fortnightly food today,' in such a case, it is allowable.

Uposathikaṃ [M 0.0279] nāma anvaḍḍhamāse uposathadivase uposathaṅgāni samādiyitvā yaṃ attanā bhuñjati, tadeva dīyati. Pāṭipadikaṃ nāma “uposathe bahū saddhā pasannā bhikkhūnaṃ sakkāraṃ karonti, pāṭipade pana bhikkhū kilamanti, pāṭipade dinnaṃ dubbhikkhadānasadisaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti, uposathakammena vā parisuddhasīlānaṃ dutiyadivase dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ hotī”ti sallakkhetvā pāṭipade [V 0.0260] dīyamānakadānaṃ. Tampi ubhayaṃ salākabhattagatikameva. Iti imāni sattapi bhattāni piṇḍapātikānaṃ na vaṭṭanti, dhutaṅgabhedaṃ karontiyeva.

Uposatha food is so called because, on the Uposatha day every fortnight, having undertaken the Uposatha precepts, one gives the very same food that one eats oneself. Pāṭipadika food is the name for a gift given on the day following the Uposatha, after reflecting thus: 'On the Uposatha day, many faithful and devoted people make offerings to the monks, but on the following day, the monks are weary. A gift given on the following day is of great fruit, like a gift given in a time of famine. Or, a gift given on the second day to those of purified virtue through the Uposatha observance is of great fruit.' Both of these also have the same procedure as ticket-food. Thus, these seven kinds of food are not allowable for those who undertake the alms-food-eater's ascetic practice; they indeed cause a breach of the ascetic practice.

214. Aparānipi cīvarakkhandhake (mahāva. 350) visākhāya varaṃ yācitvā dinnāni āgantukabhattaṃ gamikabhattaṃ gilānabhattaṃ gilānupaṭṭhākabhattanti cattāri bhattāni pāḷiyaṃ āgatāneva. Tattha āgantukānaṃ dinnaṃ bhattaṃ āgantukabhattaṃ. Esa nayo sesesu. Sace panettha āgantukabhattānipi āgantukāpi bahū honti, sabbesaṃ ekekaṃ gāhetabbaṃ. Bhattesu appahontesu ṭhitikāya gāhetabbaṃ. Eko āgantuko paṭhamameva āgantvā sabbaṃ āgantukabhattaṃ attano gāhetvā nisīdati, sabbaṃ tasseva hoti. Pacchā āgatehi āgantukehi tena dinnāni paribhuñjitabbāni. Tenapi ekaṃ attano gahetvā sesāni dātabbāni. Ayaṃ uḷāratā. Sace pana paṭhamaṃ āgantvāpi attano aggahetvā tuṇhībhūto nisīdati, pacchā āgatehi saddhiṃ paṭipāṭiyā gaṇhitabbaṃ. Sace niccaṃ āgantukā āgacchanti, āgatadivaseyeva bhuñjitabbaṃ. Antarantarā ce āgacchanti, dve tīṇi divasāni bhuñjitabbaṃ. Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana “satta divasāni bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Āvāsiko katthaci gantvā āgato, tenapi āgantukabhattaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Sace pana taṃ vihāre nibandhāpitaṃ hoti, vihāre gāhetabbaṃ. Atha vihāro dūre hoti, āsanasālāya nibandhāpitaṃ, āsanasālāya gāhetabbaṃ. Sace pana dāyakā “āgantukesu asati āvāsikāpi bhuñjantū”ti vadanti, vaṭṭati, avutte pana na vaṭṭati.

214. Furthermore, in the Cīvarakkhandhaka (Mahāvagga 350), four meals given by Visākhā after requesting a boon are indeed mentioned in the Pāḷi: the meal for incoming bhikkhus, the meal for travelling bhikkhus, the meal for the sick, and the meal for attendants of the sick. Therein, the meal given to incoming bhikkhus is the meal for incoming bhikkhus. This is the principle for the remaining cases. If, in this case, both the meals for incoming bhikkhus and the incoming bhikkhus themselves are many, one portion should be taken for each. If the meals are insufficient, they should be taken according to the established procedure. If one incoming bhikkhu, having arrived first, takes all the meal for incoming bhikkhus for himself and sits down, all of it belongs to him. The incoming bhikkhus who arrive later should consume what is given by him. He, too, having taken one portion for himself, should give the remaining portions. This is magnanimity. But if, having arrived first, he sits down silently without taking a portion for himself, it should be taken in order together with those who arrive later. If incoming bhikkhus arrive regularly, it should be eaten on the very day of arrival. If they arrive intermittently, it may be eaten for two or three days. In the Mahāpaccariya, however, it is said: “It is allowable to eat for seven days.” A resident bhikkhu who has gone somewhere and returned may also eat the meal for incoming bhikkhus. But if it has been established for the monastery, it should be taken at the monastery. If the monastery is far away and it has been established for the rest-house, it should be taken at the rest-house. But if the donors say, “When there are no incoming bhikkhus, the resident bhikkhus may also eat,” it is allowable; but if this is not said, it is not allowable.

Gamikabhattepi ayameva kathāmaggo. Ayaṃ pana viseso – āgantuko āgantukabhattameva labhati, gamiko āgantukabhattampi gamikabhattampi. Āvāsikopi pakkamitukāmo gamiko hoti, gamikabhattaṃ [M 0.0280] labhati. Yathā pana āgantukabhattaṃ, evamidaṃ dve tīṇi vā satta vā divasāni na labhati. “Gamissāmī”ti bhuttopi taṃ divasaṃ kenaci kāraṇena na gato, punadivasepi bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati saussāhattā. “Gamissāmī”ti bhuttassa corā vā panthaṃ rundhanti, udakaṃ vā devo vā vassati, sattho vā na gacchati, saussāhena bhuñjitabbaṃ. “Ete upaddave olokentena dve tayo divase bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti mahāpaccariyaṃ vuttaṃ. “Gamissāmi gamissāmī”ti pana lesaṃ oḍḍetvā bhuñjituṃ na labhati.

For the meal for travelling bhikkhus, this very same procedure applies. Here, however, is the distinction: an incoming bhikkhu receives only the meal for incoming bhikkhus, while a travelling bhikkhu receives both the meal for incoming bhikkhus and the meal for travelling bhikkhus. Even a resident bhikkhu who wishes to depart becomes a travelling bhikkhu and receives the meal for travelling bhikkhus. But unlike the meal for incoming bhikkhus, this is not received for two, three, or seven days. If one has eaten, thinking, 'I will go,' but does not go that day for some reason, it is allowable to eat again the next day, due to the earnest intention. If one has eaten, thinking, 'I will go,' but thieves block the path, or the water rises, or it rains, or the caravan does not proceed, one should eat with earnest intention. The Mahāpaccariya states: 'Considering these obstacles, it is allowable to eat for two or three days.' However, one is not permitted to eat by raising the pretense, saying, 'I will go, I will go.'

Gilānabhattampi sace sabbesaṃ gilānānaṃ pahoti, taṃ sabbesaṃ dātabbaṃ. No ce, ṭhitikaṃ katvā gāhetabbaṃ. Eko gilāno arogarūpo sakkoti antogāmaṃ gantuṃ, eko na sakkoti, ayaṃ mahāgilāno nāma, etassa gilānabhattaṃ dātabbaṃ. Dve mahāgilānā, eko lābhī abhiññāto [V 0.0261] bahuṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ labhati, eko anātho appalābhatāya antogāmaṃ pavisati, etassa gilānabhattaṃ dātabbaṃ. Gilānabhatte divasaparicchedo natthi, yāva rogo na vūpasammati, sappāyabhojanaṃ abhuñjanto na yāpeti, tāva bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yadā pana missakayāguṃ vā missakabhattaṃ vā bhuttassapi rogo na kuppati, tato paṭṭhāya na bhuñjitabbaṃ.

Regarding the meal for the sick, if it is sufficient for all the sick, it should be given to all. If not, it should be taken after making an allocation. If one sick bhikkhu is well enough to go into the village, but another is not, the latter is called 'gravely sick'—to him the meal for the sick should be given. If there are two gravely sick bhikkhus, and one is well-known and obtains much hard and soft food, while the other is without support and enters the village due to lack of gains—to him the meal for the sick should be given. For the meal for the sick, there is no time limit; as long as the illness does not subside and the patient cannot sustain himself without consuming suitable food, it should be eaten. But when, even after eating mixed gruel or a mixed meal, the illness is not aggravated, from then on it should not be eaten.

Gilānupaṭṭhākabhattampi yaṃ sabbesaṃ pahoti, taṃ sabbesaṃ dātabbaṃ. No ce pahoti, ṭhitikaṃ katvā gāhetabbaṃ. Idampi dvīsu gilānesu mahāgilānupaṭṭhākassa gāhetabbaṃ, dvīsu mahāgilānesu anāthagilānupaṭṭhākassa. Yaṃ kulaṃ gilānabhattampi deti gilānupaṭṭhākabhattampi, tattha yassa gilānassa gilānabhattaṃ pāpuṇāti, tadupaṭṭhākassapi tattheva gāhetabbaṃ. Gilānupaṭṭhākabhattepi divasaparicchedo natthi, yāva gilāno labhati, tāvassa upaṭṭhākopi labhatīti. Imāni cattāri bhattāni sace evaṃ dinnāni honti “āgantukagamikagilānagilānupaṭṭhākā mama bhikkhaṃ gaṇhantū”ti, piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati. Sace pana “āgantukādīnaṃ catunnaṃ bhattaṃ nibandhāpemi, mama bhattaṃ gaṇhantū”ti evaṃ dinnāni honti, piṇḍapātikānaṃ na vaṭṭati.

As for the meal for attendants of the sick, if it is sufficient for all, it should be given to all. If it is not sufficient, it should be taken after making a fixed arrangement. This too, between two sick bhikkhus, should be taken by the attendant of the gravely sick one; between two gravely sick bhikkhus, by the attendant of the sick one who is without support. In whatever family gives both the meal for the sick and the meal for attendants of the sick, there, for whichever sick bhikkhu the meal for the sick is obtained, for his attendant also it should be taken from that very place. In the case of the meal for attendants of the sick, there is no daily limit; for as long as the sick bhikkhu receives it, for so long his attendant also receives it. If these four kinds of meals are given thus: “Let incoming bhikkhus, travelling bhikkhus, the sick, and attendants of the sick receive my almsfood,” it is permissible even for those who go for alms. But if they are given thus: “I establish a meal for the four, beginning with incoming bhikkhus; let them receive my meal,” it is not permissible for those who go for alms.

215. Aparānipi dhurabhattaṃ kuṭibhattaṃ vārakabhattanti tīṇi bhattāni. Tattha dhurabhattanti niccabhattaṃ vuccati, taṃ duvidhaṃ saṅghikañca puggalikañca. Tattha yaṃ “saṅghassa dhurabhattaṃ demā”ti nibandhāpitaṃ, taṃ salākabhattagatikaṃ. “Mama [M 0.0281] nibaddhabhikkhaṃ gaṇhantū”ti vatvā dinnaṃ pana piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati. Puggalikepi “tumhākaṃ dhurabhattaṃ dammī”ti vutte piṇḍapātiko ce, na vaṭṭati, “mama nibaddhabhikkhaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vutte pana vaṭṭati, sāditabbaṃ. Sace pacchā katipāhe vītivatte “dhurabhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadati, mūle suṭṭhu sampaṭicchitattā vaṭṭati.

215. There are also three other meals: the regular meal, the lodging meal, and the meal taken in turn. Therein, 'regular meal' is called a constant meal. It is of two kinds: for the Sangha and for an individual. Therein, that which is established with the words, “We give a regular meal to the Sangha,” is of the nature of a ticket-meal. But that which is given after saying, “Let them receive my constant almsfood,” is permissible even for those who go for alms. In the case of an individual meal also, if it is said, “I give you a regular meal,” it is not permissible if one is a bhikkhu who goes for alms. But if it is said, “Receive my constant almsfood,” it is permissible; it should be consented to. If later, after a few days have passed, one says, “Receive the regular meal,” it is permissible because it was well accepted at the beginning.

Kuṭibhattaṃ nāma yaṃ saṅghassa āvāsaṃ kāretvā “amhākaṃ senāsanavāsino amhākaṃyeva bhattaṃ gaṇhantū”ti evaṃ nibandhāpitaṃ, taṃ salākabhattagatikameva hoti, gāhetvā bhuñjitabbaṃ. “Amhākaṃ senāsanavāsino amhākaṃyeva bhikkhaṃ gaṇhantū”ti vutte pana piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati. Yaṃ pana puggale pasīditvā tassa āvāsaṃ katvā “tumhākaṃ demā”ti dinnaṃ, taṃ tasseva hoti, tasmiṃ katthaci gate nissitakehi bhuñjitabbaṃ.

The meal called kuṭibhatta is that which, after a dwelling is constructed for the Sangha, is stipulated thus: “Let the residents of our dwelling take only our meal.” That is indeed like a ticket-meal; it should be taken and eaten. However, when it is said, “Let the residents of our dwelling take only our alms,” it is permissible even for alms-round-goers. But as for that which is given after, having had faith in a particular person, a dwelling is made for him with the words, “We give this to you,” it belongs solely to that person. When he has gone somewhere, it should be eaten by his dependents.

Vārakabhattaṃ nāma dubbhikkhasamaye “vārena bhikkhū jaggissāmā”ti dhuragehato paṭṭhāya dinnaṃ, tampi bhikkhāvacanena dinnaṃ piṇḍapātikānaṃ vaṭṭati, “vārakabhatta”nti vutte pana salākabhattagatikaṃ hoti. Sace taṇḍulādīni pesenti “sāmaṇerā pacitvā dentū”ti, piṇḍapātikānaṃ [V 0.0262] vaṭṭati. Iti imāni ca tīṇi, āgantukabhattādīni ca cattārīti satta, tāni saṅghabhattādīhi saha cuddasa bhattāni honti.

The meal called vārakabhatta is that which is given during a time of famine, starting from the house with a standing commitment, with the thought, “We will look after the monks by turns.” That too, when given with the word ‘alms,’ is permissible for alms-round-goers. However, when it is called ‘vārakabhatta,’ it is like a ticket-meal. If they send rice and other things with the instruction, “Let the novices cook and give it,” it is permissible for alms-round-goers. Thus, these three, and the four beginning with the guest-meal, make seven. Together with the Sangha-meal and others, they become fourteen meals.

216. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana vihārabhattaṃ aṭṭhakabhattaṃ catukkabhattaṃ guḷhakabhattanti aññānipi cattāri bhattāni vuttāni. Tattha vihārabhattaṃ nāma vihāre tatruppādabhattaṃ, taṃ saṅghabhattena saṅgahitaṃ. Taṃ pana tissamahāvihāracittalapabbatādīsu paṭisambhidāppattehi khīṇāsavehi yathā piṇḍapātikānampi sakkā honti paribhuñjituṃ, tathā paṭiggahitattā tādisesu ṭhānesu piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati. “Aṭṭhannaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dema, catunnaṃ demā”ti evaṃ dinnaṃ pana aṭṭhakabhattañceva catukkabhattañca, tampi bhikkhāvacanena dinnaṃ piṇḍapātikānaṃ vaṭṭati. Mahābhisaṅkhārena atirasakapūvena pattaṃ thaketvā dinnaṃ guḷhakabhattaṃ nāma. Imāni tīṇi salākabhattagatikāneva. Aparampi guḷhakabhattaṃ nāma atthi, idhekacce manussā mahādhammassavanañca vihārapūjañca kāretvā “sakalasaṅghassa dātuṃ na sakkoma, dve tīṇi bhikkhusatāni amhākaṃ bhikkhaṃ gaṇhantū”ti bhikkhuparicchedajānanatthaṃ guḷhake denti, idaṃ piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati.

216. However, in the commentary, four other meals are mentioned: the monastery meal (vihārabhatta), the meal for eight (aṭṭhakabhatta), the meal for four (catukkabhatta), and the hidden meal (gūḷhabhatta). Among these, the monastery meal is food produced there in the monastery; it is included under the Sangha-meal. However, concerning that monastery meal, in places such as Tissa Mahāvihāra and Cittalapabbata, because it is received by Arahants who have attained the analytical knowledges in such a way that it is possible even for alms-round-goers to partake, it is permissible for alms-round-goers in such places. Furthermore, that which is given with the words, “We give to eight monks; we give to four,” is the meal for eight and the meal for four. That too, being given with the term 'alms-food', is permissible for alms-round-goers. That which is given with great preparation, after covering the bowl with an extremely delicious cake, is called the hidden meal. These three are indeed of the nature of ticket-meals. There is also another meal called the jaggery-lump meal: here, some people, after having arranged for a great Dhamma-hearing and a monastery-offering, think, “We are not able to give to the entire Saṅgha; let two or three hundred monks accept our alms-food.” For the purpose of determining the number of monks, they give out jaggery-lumps. This is also permissible for alms-round-goers.

Piṇḍapātabhājanīyaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on the Distribution of Alms-food is concluded.

217. Gilānapaccayabhājanīyaṃ [M 0.0282] pana evaṃ veditabbaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 325 pakkhikabhattādikathā) – sappiādīsu bhesajjesu rājarājamahāmattā sappissa tāva kumbhasatampi kumbhasahassampi vihāraṃ pesenti, ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā therāsanato paṭṭhāya gahitabhājanaṃ pūretvā dātabbaṃ, piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati. Sace alasajātikā mahātherā pacchā āgacchanti, “bhante, vīsativassānaṃ dīyati, tumhākaṃ ṭhitikā atikkantā”ti na vattabbā, ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvā tesaṃ datvā pacchā ṭhitikāya dātabbaṃ. “Asukavihāre bahu sappi uppanna”nti sutvā yojanantaravihāratopi bhikkhū āgacchanti, sampattasampattānampi ṭhitaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya dātabbaṃ. Asampattānampi upacārasīmaṃ paviṭṭhānaṃ antevāsikādīsu gaṇhantesu dātabbameva. “Bahiupacārasīmāya ṭhitānaṃ dethā”ti vadanti, na dātabbaṃ. Sace pana upacārasīmaṃ okkantehi ekābaddhā hutvā attano vihāradvāre antovihāreyeva vā honti, parisavasena vaḍḍhitā nāma sīmā hoti, tasmā dātabbā. Saṅghanavakassa dinnepi pacchā āgatānaṃ dātabbameva. Dutiyabhāge pana therāsanaṃ āruḷhe āgatānaṃ paṭhamabhāgo na pāpuṇāti, dutiyabhāgato vassaggena dātabbaṃ. Antoupacārasīmaṃ pavisitvā yattha katthaci dinnaṃ hoti, sabbaṃ sannipātaṭṭhāneyeva bhājetabbaṃ.

217. Regarding the distribution of requisites for the sick, it should be understood as follows: Among medicines such as ghee, kings and great ministers may send even a hundred or a thousand jars of ghee to the monastery. After striking the bell, starting from the Elder's seat, the received vessels should be filled and given. It is permissible even for alms-round-goers. If great elders who are of a slow nature arrive later, they should not be told, “Venerable Sirs, it is being given to those of twenty years’ standing; your turn in seniority has passed.” Setting aside the regular order of seniority, it should be given to them first, and afterwards, it should be given according to the order of seniority. Upon hearing, “Much ghee has become available at such-and-such monastery,” if bhikkhus come even from a monastery a yojana away, it should be given to all who arrive, starting from the place where they stand. Even for those who have not yet arrived at the assembly, but have entered the vicinity-boundary, it should certainly be given when their pupils and others receive it on their behalf. If they say, “Give to those standing outside the vicinity-boundary,” it should not be given. However, if they form a continuous group with those who have entered the vicinity-boundary, and are at their own monastery gate or inside the monastery, the boundary is considered to be extended by the power of the assembly; therefore, it should be given. Even when it has been given to the most junior in the Sangha, it should certainly be given to those who arrive later. But regarding the second portion, for those who arrive after it has been brought to the Elder's seat, the first portion is not available; it should be given from the second portion according to seniority by rains-residence. Having entered within the vicinity-boundary, wherever a donation may be given, all of it should be distributed only at the place of assembly.

Yasmiṃ [V 0.0263] vihāre dasa bhikkhū, daseva ca sappikumbhā dīyanti, ekekakumbhavasena bhājetabbaṃ. Eko sappikumbho hoti, dasabhikkhūhi bhājetvā gahetabbaṃ. Sace “yathāṭhitaṃyeva amhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti gaṇhanti, duggahitaṃ, taṃ gatagataṭṭhāne saṅghikameva hoti. Kumbhaṃ pana āvajjetvā thālake thokaṃ sappiṃ katvā “idaṃ mahātherassa pāpuṇāti, avasesaṃ amhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti vatvā tampi kumbheyeva ākiritvā yathicchitaṃ gahetvā gantabbaṃ. Sace thinaṃ sappi hoti, lekhaṃ katvā “lekhato parabhāgo mahātherassa pāpuṇāti, avasesaṃ amhāka”nti gahitampi suggahitaṃ. Vuttaparicchedato ūnādhikesu bhikkhūsu sappikumbhesu ca eteneva upāyena bhājetabbaṃ. Sace paneko bhikkhu, eko kumbho hoti, ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā “ayaṃ mayhaṃ pāpuṇātī”tipi gahetuṃ vaṭṭati. “Ayaṃ paṭhamabhāgo mayhaṃ pāpuṇāti, ayaṃ dutiyabhāgo”ti evaṃ thokaṃ thokampi pāpetuṃ vaṭṭati. Esa nayo navanītādīsupi[M 0.0283]. Yasmiṃ pana vippasannatilatelādimhi lekhā na santiṭṭhati, taṃ uddharitvā bhājetabbaṃ. Siṅgiveramaricādibhesajjampi avasesapattathālakādisamaṇaparikkhāropi sabbo vuttānurūpeneva nayena suṭṭhu sallakkhetvā bhājetabboti. Ayaṃ gilānapaccayabhājanīyakathā.

In a monastery where there are ten monks and ten pots of ghee are given, they should be distributed, one pot per monk. If there is one pot of ghee, it should be divided among the ten monks to be taken. If they take it thinking, 'Let it accrue to us just as it is,' it is improperly taken; that remains Sangha property wherever it is taken. However, having tilted the pot and put a little ghee into a dish, saying, 'This accrues to the senior elder; the remainder accrues to us,' and having said this, that portion should also be poured back into the pot, and they may take it as they wish and depart. If the ghee is solid, having made a line, it is properly taken even if taken thus: 'The portion beyond the line accrues to the senior elder; the remainder accrues to us.' When there are fewer or more monks and pots of ghee than the stated amount, they should be distributed by this same method. But if there is one monk and one pot, it is permissible to strike a bell and take it, saying, 'This accrues to me.' It is also permissible to make it accrue little by little, saying, 'This first portion accrues to me, this second portion.' This is also the method for fresh butter and so on. However, in the case of clear sesame oil and the like, in which a line does not hold, it should be ladled out and distributed. Medicine such as ginger and pepper, and remaining monastic requisites such as bowls and dishes—all should be distributed according to the method described, having carefully considered it. This is the discussion on the distribution of requisites for the sick.

218. Idāni senāsanaggāhe vinicchayo veditabbo (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318) – ayaṃ senāsanaggāho nāma duvidho hoti utukāle ca vassāvāse ca. Tattha utukāle tāva keci āgantukā bhikkhū purebhattaṃ āgacchanti, keci pacchābhattaṃ paṭhamayāmaṃ majjhimayāmaṃ pacchimayāmaṃ vā. Ye yadā āgacchanti, tesaṃ tadāva bhikkhū uṭṭhāpetvā senāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, akālo nāma natthi. Senāsanapaññāpakena pana paṇḍitena bhavitabbaṃ, ekaṃ vā dve vā mañcaṭṭhānāni ṭhapetabbāni. Sace vikāle eko vā dve vā therā āgacchanti, te vattabbā “bhante, ādito paṭṭhāya vuṭṭhāpiyamāne sabbepi bhikkhū ubbhaṇḍikā bhavissanti, tumhe amhākaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne vasathā”ti.

218. Now, the ruling regarding the taking of lodgings should be understood. This taking of lodgings is of two kinds: during the seasons and during the rains-residence. In this regard, concerning the seasons, some visiting monks arrive before the meal, some after the meal, or in the first, middle, or last watch of the night. Whenever they arrive, lodging should be given to them at that very time by having the resident monks get up; there is no such thing as an improper time. However, the one who allots lodgings should be wise; one or two bed-places should be set aside. If one or two elders arrive at an improper time, they should be told, 'Venerable sirs, if monks are made to get up starting from the first one, all the monks will have to pack up their belongings. You may stay in our dwelling place.'

Bahūsu pana āgatesu vuṭṭhāpetvā paṭipāṭiyā dātabbaṃ. Sace ekekaṃ pariveṇaṃ pahoti, ekekaṃ pariveṇaṃ dātabbaṃ. Tattha aggisālādīghasālāmaṇḍalamāḷādayo sabbepi tasseva pāpuṇanti. Evaṃ appahonte pāsādaggena dātabbaṃ, pāsādesu appahontesu ovarakaggena dātabbaṃ, ovarakesu appahontesu seyyaggena dātabbaṃ, seyyaggesu appahontesu mañcaṭṭhānena dātabbaṃ, mañcaṭṭhāne appahonte ekapīṭhakaṭṭhānavasena dātabbaṃ, bhikkhuno pana ṭhitokāsamattaṃ na gāhetabbaṃ. Etañhi senāsanaṃ nāma na hoti. Pīṭhakaṭṭhāne pana appahonte ekaṃ mañcaṭṭhānaṃ vā ekaṃ pīṭhaṭṭhānaṃ vā “vārena vārena, bhante, vissamathā”ti tiṇṇaṃ janānaṃ dātabbaṃ. Na hi sakkā [V 0.0264] sītasamaye sabbarattiṃ ajjhokāseva vasituṃ. Mahātherena paṭhamayāmaṃ vissamitvā nikkhamitvā dutiyattherassa vattabbaṃ “āvuso idha pavisāhī”ti. Sace mahāthero niddāgaruko hoti, kālaṃ na jānāti, ukkāsitvā dvāraṃ ākoṭetvā “bhante kālo jāto, sītaṃ anudahatī”ti vattabbaṃ. Tena nikkhamitvā okāso dātabbo, adātuṃ na labhati. Dutiyattherenapi majjhimayāmaṃ vissamitvā [M 0.0284] purimanayeneva itarassa dātabbaṃ. Niddāgaruko vuttanayeneva vuṭṭhāpetabbo. Evaṃ ekarattiṃ ekamañcaṭṭhānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ dātabbaṃ. Jambudīpe pana ekacce bhikkhū “senāsanaṃ nāma mañcaṭṭhānaṃ vā pīṭhaṭṭhānaṃ vā kiñcideva kassaci sappāyaṃ hoti, kassaci asappāya”nti āgantukā hontu vā mā vā, devasikaṃ senāsanaṃ gāhenti. Ayaṃ utukāle senāsanaggāho nāma.

However, when many have arrived, lodging should be given in order after having the resident monks get up. If one monastic compound each is sufficient, one monastic compound each should be given. In that case, the fire-hall, long hall, circular hall, pavilions, and so on, all belong to that monk. If this is not sufficient, a portion of a multi-storied building should be given. If the multi-storied buildings are insufficient, a portion of a cell should be given. If the cells are insufficient, a portion of a sleeping area should be given. If the sleeping areas are insufficient, a bed-space should be given. If a bed-space is insufficient, a stool-space should be given. However, a monk should not be allocated a mere standing space, for this is not called a lodging. But when a stool-space is insufficient, one bed-space or one stool-space should be given to three persons, with the words: 'Venerable sirs, rest in turn.' For it is not possible to dwell in the open all night in the cold season. The senior elder, having rested in the first watch, should leave and say to the second elder: 'Friend, enter here.' If the senior elder is heavy with sleep and does not know the time, one should clear one's throat, knock on the door, and say: 'Venerable sir, the time has come; the cold is afflicting.' He must then leave and give the space; he is not allowed to refuse. The second elder also, having rested during the middle watch, should give it to the other in the same way as before. If he is heavy with sleep, he should be roused in the way that was stated. Thus, for one night, one bed-space should be given to three. In Jambudīpa, however, some monks, thinking, 'A lodging—be it a bed-space, a stool-space, or whatever little there is—is suitable for one and unsuitable for another,' take lodging daily, whether guests arrive or not. This is called the taking of lodging during the seasons.

219. Vassāvāse pana atthi āgantukavattaṃ, atthi āvāsikavattaṃ. Āgantukena tāva sakaṭṭhānaṃ muñcitvā aññattha gantvā vasitukāmena vassūpanāyikadivasameva tattha na gantabbaṃ. Vasanaṭṭhānaṃ vā hi tatra sambādhaṃ bhaveyya, bhikkhācāro vā na sampajjeyya, tena na phāsukaṃ vihareyya, tasmā “idāni māsamattena vassūpanāyikā bhavissatī”ti taṃ vihāraṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Tattha māsamattaṃ vasanto sace uddesatthiko, uddesasampattiṃ sallakkhetvā, sace kammaṭṭhāniko, kammaṭṭhānasappāyataṃ sallakkhetvā, sace paccayatthiko, paccayalābhaṃ sallakkhetvā antovasse sukhaṃ vasissati. Sakaṭṭhānato ca tattha gacchantena na gocaragāmo ghaṭṭetabbo. Na tattha manussā vattabbā “tumhe nissāya salākabhattādīni vā yāgukhajjakādīni vā vassāvāsikaṃ vā natthi, ayaṃ cetiyassa parikkhāro, ayaṃ uposathāgārassa, idaṃ tāḷañceva sūci ca, sampaṭicchatha tumhākaṃ vihāra”nti. Senāsanaṃ pana jaggitvā dārubhaṇḍamattikābhaṇḍāni paṭisāmetvā gamikavattaṃ pūretvā gantabbaṃ.

219. Regarding the rains-residence, there are duties for incoming monks and duties for resident monks. First, an incoming monk who wishes to leave his own place and go to dwell elsewhere should not go there on the very day of entering the rains-residence. For the dwelling place there might be crowded, or the alms-round might not be successful, and thus he would not dwell comfortably. Therefore, thinking, 'Now, in about a month, the rains-residence will begin,' he should enter that monastery. Dwelling there for about a month, if he is one who seeks instruction, he should consider the availability of instruction; if he is a meditation practitioner, he should consider the suitability for meditation; if he seeks requisites, he should consider the gain of requisites—then he will dwell happily during the rains. And when going there from his own place, he should not cause a disturbance in the alms-resort village. The people there should not be told, 'Because of you, there are no ticket-meals, gruel and snacks, or rains-residence cloth. This is a requisite of the cetiya; this is a key and a needle. Accept your monastery.' Instead, having taken care of the lodging, having put away the wooden and clay articles, and having fulfilled the duties of a departing monk, he should go.

Evaṃ gacchantenapi daharehi pattacīvarabhaṇḍikāyo ukkhipāpetvā telanāḷikattaradaṇḍādīni gāhetvā chattaṃ paggayha attānaṃ dassentena gāmadvāreneva na gantabbaṃ, paṭicchannena aṭavimaggena gantabbaṃ. Aṭavimagge asati gumbādīni maddantena na gantabbaṃ, gamikavattaṃ pana pūretvā vitakkaṃ chinditvā suddhacittena gamanavatteneva gantabbaṃ. Sace pana gāmadvārena maggo hoti, gacchantañca naṃ saparivāraṃ disvā manussā “amhākaṃ thero viyā”ti upadhāvitvā “kuhiṃ, bhante, sabbaparikkhāre gahetvā gacchathā”ti vadanti, tesu ce eko evaṃ vadati “vassūpanāyikakālo nāmāyaṃ, yattha antovassenibaddhabhikkhācāro bhaṇḍapaṭicchādanañca labbhati, tattha bhikkhū gacchantī”ti, tassa [M 0.0285] ce sutvā te manussā “bhante, imasmimpi gāme jano [V 0.0265] bhuñjati ceva nivāseti ca, mā aññattha gacchathā”ti vatvā mittāmacce pakkositvā sabbe sammantayitvā vihāre nibaddhavattañca salākabhattādīni ca vassāvāsikañca ṭhapetvā “idheva, bhante, vasathā”ti yācanti, sabbesaṃ sādituṃ vaṭṭati. Sabbañcetaṃ kappiyañceva anavajjañca. Kurundiyaṃ pana “kuhiṃ gacchathāti vutte ‘asukaṭṭhāna’nti vatvā ‘kasmā tattha gacchathā’ti vutte ‘kāraṇaṃ ācikkhitabba’”nti vuttaṃ. Ubhayampi panetaṃ suddhacittattāva anavajjaṃ. Idaṃ āgantukavattaṃ nāma.

Thus, even when traveling, a monk should not go precisely through the village gate, having caused young monks to carry the bundles of bowl and robes, having taken an oil tube, a walking staff, and so on, and having raised an umbrella, thereby showing himself. He should go by a concealed forest path. If there is no forest path, he should not go by trampling on shrubs and so on. Rather, having fulfilled the duties of a traveler and having cut off wrong thought, he should go with a pure mind, precisely in accordance with the conduct for traveling. However, if the path is through the village gate, and people, seeing him going with his retinue, run up thinking, 'He is like our Elder!' and say, 'Venerable sir, where are you going, having taken all these requisites?' And if one among them says thus: 'This is the time for entering the Rains-residence. Monks go to a place where, during the Rains-residence, a constant alms-round and robes for covering the body are obtained.' Then, having heard his words, those people might say, 'Venerable sir, in this village too, the people both eat and clothe themselves; do not go elsewhere!' Then, having summoned friends and companions, and having all consulted together, and having established in the monastery a fixed duty, ticket-food and so on, and the Rains-residence robe, they might request, 'Venerable sir, please dwell right here!' It is allowable to accept from all of them. And all this is both allowable and blameless. In the Kurundī, however, it is said: 'When asked, "Where are you going?", one should say, "To such-and-such a place." When asked, "Why are you going there?", the reason should be told.' But both of these are blameless only because of the purity of mind. This is called the conduct for an incoming monk.

Idaṃ pana āvāsikavattaṃ. Paṭikacceva hi āvāsikehi vihāro jaggitabbo, khaṇḍaphullapaṭisaṅkharaṇaparibhaṇḍāni kātabbāni, rattiṭṭhānadivāṭṭhānavaccakuṭipassāvaṭṭhānāni padhānagharavihāramaggoti imāni sabbāni paṭijaggitabbāni. Cetiye sudhākammaṃ muṇḍavedikāya telamakkhanaṃ mañcapīṭhajaggananti idampi sabbaṃ kātabbaṃ “vassaṃ vasitukāmā āgantvā uddesaparipucchākammaṭṭhānānuyogādīni karontā sukhaṃ vasissantī”ti. Kataparikammehi āsāḷhījuṇhapañcamito paṭṭhāya vassāvāsikaṃ pucchitabbaṃ. Kattha pucchitabbaṃ? Yato pakatiyā labbhati. Yehi pana na dinnapubbaṃ, te pucchituṃ na vaṭṭati. Kasmā pucchitabbaṃ? Kadāci hi manussā denti, kadāci dubbhikkhādīhi upaddutā na denti, tattha ye na dassanti, te apucchitvā vassāvāsike gāhite gāhitabhikkhūnaṃ lābhantarāyo hoti, tasmā pucchitvāva gāhetabbaṃ.

This, however, is the duty of residents. Indeed, the monastery should be cared for by the residents beforehand; the work of repairing what is broken and dilapidated and all related duties should be performed. The places for night use and day use, latrines, urinals, the meditation hall, and the monastery path—all these should be cared for. Plastering the cetiya, oiling the low railing of its platform, and cleaning the beds and chairs—all this, too, should be done so that 'monks wishing to spend the rains, having come, may dwell comfortably while engaging in recitation, questioning, and application to meditation subjects.' Those who have completed the preparations should inquire about the rains-residence offering, starting from the fifth day of the waxing moon of Āsāḷhī. From whom should it be asked? From the one from whom it is customarily received. However, it is not proper to ask those who have not given before. Why should it be asked? For sometimes people give, and sometimes, afflicted by famine and so forth, they do not give. In such a case, if the rains-residence offering is accepted without asking those who will not give, there is an obstruction to the gains for the monks who have accepted. Therefore, it should be accepted only after asking.

Pucchantena “tumhākaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ gāhaṇakālo upakaṭṭho”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace vadanti “bhante, imaṃ saṃvaccharaṃ chātakādīhi upaddutamha, na sakkoma dātu”nti vā “yaṃ pubbe dema, tato ūnataraṃ dassāmā”ti vā “idāni kappāso sulabho, yaṃ pubbe dema, tato bahutaraṃ dassāmā”ti vā, taṃ sallakkhetvā tadanurūpena nayena tesaṃ senāsane bhikkhūnaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ gāhetabbaṃ. Sace manussā vadanti “yassa amhākaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ pāpuṇāti, so temāsaṃ pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetu, vihāramaggaṃ jaggatu, cetiyaṅgaṇabodhiyaṅgaṇāni jaggatu, bodhirukkhe udakaṃ āsiñcatū”ti, yassa taṃ pāpuṇāti, tassa ācikkhitabbaṃ. Yo pana gāmo paṭikkamma yojanadviyojanantare hoti, tatra ce kulāni upanikkhepaṃ [M 0.0286] ṭhapetvā pahāre vassāvāsikaṃ dentiyeva, tāni kulāni āpucchitvāpi tesaṃ senāsane vattaṃ katvā vasantassa vassāvāsitaṃ gāhetabbaṃ. Sace pana tesaṃ senāsane paṃsukūliko vasati, āgatañca taṃ disvā “tumhākaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ demā”ti vadanti, tena saṅghassa ācikkhitabbaṃ. Sace tāni kulāni saṅghassa dātuṃ na icchanti, “tumhākaṃyeva demā”ti vadanti, sabhāgo bhikkhu “vattaṃ katvā gaṇhāhī”ti [V 0.0266] vattabbo. Paṃsukūlikassa panetaṃ na vaṭṭati. Iti saddhādeyyadāyakamanussā pucchitabbā.

By one who is asking, it should be said thus: 'The time for accepting your rains-residence robe has approached.' If they say, 'Venerable sir, this year we are afflicted by famine and so forth; we are not able to give,' or, 'We will give less than what we gave before,' or, 'Now cotton is easy to obtain; we will give much more than what we gave before,' then, having noted that speech, the rains-residence robe should be accepted by the bhikkhus in their dwelling place in a manner appropriate to that. If the people say, 'Whichever bhikkhu receives our rains-residence robe, let him provide drinking water for the three months, let him maintain the monastery path, let him maintain the cetiya grounds and the Bodhi grounds, and let him pour water on the Bodhi tree,' then it should be told to him who receives it. However, if a village is one or two yojanas distant from the monastery, and if families there, having placed a deposit, give the rains-residence robe at the appointed time, then even without asking those families, the rains-residence robe should be accepted by a bhikkhu who is dwelling there, after he has performed the duties in their dwelling place. But if a rag-robe-wearing bhikkhu dwells in their dwelling place, and seeing him who has come, they say, 'We will give you the rains-residence robe,' it should be told to the Saṅgha by him. If those families do not wish to give to the Saṅgha and say, 'We will give only to you,' a fellow bhikkhu should be told, 'Having performed the duties, take it.' But for a rag-robe-wearing bhikkhu, this is not allowable. Thus, in the aforesaid manner, the people who are donors of faith-offerings should be asked.

Tatruppāde pana kappiyakārakā pucchitabbā. Kathaṃ pucchitabbā? Kiṃ, āvuso, saṅghassa bhaṇḍapaṭicchādanaṃ bhavissatīti? Sace vadanti “bhavissati, bhante, ekekassa navahatthasāṭakaṃ dassāma, vassāvāsikaṃ gāhethā”ti, gāhetabbaṃ. Sacepi vadanti “sāṭakā natthi, vatthu pana atthi, gāhetha, bhante”ti, vatthumhi santepi gāhetuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Kappiyakārakānañhi hatthe “kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ paribhuñjathā”ti dinnavatthuto yaṃ yaṃ kappiyaṃ, sabbaṃ paribhuñjituṃ anuññātaṃ. Yaṃ panettha piṇḍapātatthāya gilānapaccayatthāya ca uddissa dinnaṃ, taṃ cīvare upanāmentehi saṅghasuṭṭhutāya apaloketvā upanāmetabbaṃ, senāsanatthāya pana uddissa dinnaṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ hoti. Cīvaravaseneva pana catupaccayavasena vā dinnaṃ cīvare upanāmentānaṃ apalokanakammakiccaṃ natthi. Apalokanakammaṃ karontehi ca puggalavaseneva kātabbaṃ, saṅghavasena na kātabbaṃ. Jātarūparajatavasenapi āmakadhaññavasena vā apalokanakammaṃ na vaṭṭati, kappiyabhaṇḍavasena cīvarataṇḍulādivaseneva ca vaṭṭati. Taṃ pana evaṃ kattabbaṃ “idāni subhikkhaṃ sulabhapiṇḍaṃ, bhikkhū cīvarena kilamanti, ettakaṃ nāma taṇḍulabhāgaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvaraṃ kātuṃ ruccatī”ti, “gilānapaccayo sulabho, gilāno vā natthi, ettakaṃ nāma taṇḍulabhāgaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvaraṃ kātuṃ ruccatī”ti.

But regarding requisites that have arisen there, the stewards should be asked. How should they be asked? 'Friends, will there be cloth for the Saṅgha's covering?' If they say, 'There will be, venerable sir. We will give each one a nine-cubit cloth; please accept the rains-residence robe,' it should be accepted. Even if they say, 'There are no cloths, but there are provisions; please accept them, venerable sir,' it is still proper to accept, even when there are provisions. For, whatever is given into the hands of the stewards with the words, 'Use the allowable goods,' all of that which is allowable is permitted to be used. Whatever has been given here, designated for alms-food and for requisites for the sick, when converting it to robes, it should be done after announcing it for the well-being of the Saṅgha. But what has been given designated for lodging is heavy goods. However, for those converting what was given by way of robes or by way of the four requisites into robes, there is no duty of making an announcement. And when making an announcement, it should be done on an individual basis; it should not be done on behalf of the Saṅgha. An announcement is not allowable by way of gold and silver or by way of raw grain; it is allowable by way of allowable goods, such as robes, rice, and so on. It should be done thus: 'Now it is a time of abundance and alms-food is easy to obtain; the monks are in difficulty regarding robes. Does it please the venerable ones to use this portion of rice to make robes for the monks?' Or: 'Requisites for the sick are easy to obtain, or there is no one who is sick. Does it please the venerable ones to use this portion of rice to make robes for the monks?'

Evaṃ cīvarapaccayaṃ sallakkhetvā senāsanassa kāle ghosite sannipatite saṅghe senāsanaggāhako sammannitabbo. Sammannantena ca dve sammannitabbāti vuttaṃ. Evañhi navako vuḍḍhassa, vuḍḍho ca navakassa gāhessatīti. Mahante pana mahāvihārasadise vihāre tayo cattāro janā sammannitabbā. Kurundiyaṃ pana “aṭṭhapi soḷasapi jane sammannituṃ [M 0.0287] vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tesaṃ sammuti kammavācāyapi apalokanenapi vaṭṭatiyeva. Tehi sammatehi bhikkhūhi senāsanaṃ sallakkhetabbaṃ. Cetiyagharaṃ bodhigharaṃ āsanagharaṃ sammuñjaniaṭṭo dāruaṭṭo vaccakuṭi iṭṭhakasālā vaḍḍhakisālā dvārakoṭṭhako pānīyamāḷo maggo pokkharaṇīti etāni hi asenāsanāni, vihāro aḍḍhayogo pāsādo hammiyaṃ guhā maṇḍapo rukkhamūlaṃ veḷugumboti imāni senāsanāni, tāni gāhetabbāni.

Thus, having considered the robe-requisite, when the time for lodgings is announced and the Saṅgha has assembled, a lodging-assigner should be appointed. It has been said that two should be appointed. For in this way the junior will assign to the senior, and the senior to the junior. However, in a large monastery similar to the Mahāvihāra, three or four persons should be appointed. In the Kurundī commentary, however, it is said, 'It is permissible to appoint even eight or sixteen persons.' Their appointment is valid by a formal act as well as by an announcement. By these appointed monks, the lodging should be considered for allocation. A shrine house, a Bodhi-tree house, a sitting hall, a place for brooms, a wood store, a toilet, a brick hall, a workshop, a gatehouse, a water pavilion, a path, a pond—these indeed are not lodgings. A dwelling, a lean-to, a multi-storied building, a long-halled building, a cave, a pavilion, the foot of a tree, a bamboo grove—these are lodgings. These are to be assigned.

220. Gāhentena ca “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṃ bhikkhū gaṇetuṃ, bhikkhū gaṇetvā seyyā gaṇetuṃ, seyyā gaṇetvā seyyaggena gāhetu”nti(cūḷava. 318) ādivacanato paṭhamaṃ vihāre [V 0.0267] bhikkhū gaṇetvā mañcaṭṭhānāni gaṇetabbāni, tato ekekaṃ mañcaṭṭhānaṃ ekekassa bhikkhuno gāhetabbaṃ. Sace mañcaṭṭhānāni atirekāni honti, vihāraggena gāhetabbaṃ. Sace vihārāpi atirekā honti, pariveṇaggena gāhetabbaṃ. Pariveṇesupi atirekesu puna aparopi bhāgo dātabbo. Atimandesu hi bhikkhūsu ekekassa bhikkhuno dve tīṇi pariveṇāni dātabbāni. Gahite pana dutiyabhāge añño bhikkhu āgacchati, na attano aruciyā so bhāgo tassa dātabbo. Sace pana yena gahito, so attano ruciyā taṃ dutiyabhāgaṃ vā paṭhamabhāgaṃ vā deti, vaṭṭati.

220. When assigning, according to the words beginning, 'Monks, I allow you first to count the monks; having counted the monks, to count the sleeping places; having counted the sleeping places, to assign them by the best sleeping place,' one should first count the monks in the monastery and then count the bed spaces. Then, each bed space should be assigned to each monk. If there are extra bed spaces, they should be assigned as the monastery's portion. If there are also extra dwellings, they should be assigned as the surrounding area's portion. If there are also extra surrounding areas, another portion should be given again. Indeed, when the monks are very few, two or three surrounding areas may be given to each monk. However, after a second portion has been taken, if another monk arrives, that portion is not to be given to him on account of his own displeasure. But if the one who took it gives that second portion or the first portion of his own accord, it is permissible.

“Na, bhikkhave, nissīme ṭhitassa senāsanaṃ gāhetabbaṃ, yo gāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 318) vacanato upacārasīdhato bahi ṭhitassa na gāhetabbaṃ, antoupacārasīmāya pana dūre ṭhitassapi labbhatiyeva.

“Monks, a lodging should not be assigned to one standing outside the boundary. Whoever would assign it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.” According to this statement, a lodging should not be assigned to one standing outside the proximity boundary, but it is indeed allowable for one standing far inside the proximity boundary.

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānassa patirūpaṃ seyyaṃ dātu”nti (cūḷava. 316) vacanato yo (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 316) kāsasāsabhagandarātisārādīhi gilāno hoti, kheḷamallakavaccakapālādīni ṭhapetabbāni honti, kuṭṭhī vā hoti, senāsanaṃ dūseti, evarūpassa heṭṭhāpāsādapaṇṇasālādīsu aññataraṃ ekamantaṃ senāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ. Yasmiṃ vasante senāsanaṃ na dussati, tassa varaseyyāpi dātabbāva. Yopi sinehapānavirecananatthukammādīsu yaṃ kiñci [M 0.0288] bhesajjaṃ karoti, sabbo so gilānoyeva. Tassapi sallakkhetvā patirūpaṃ senāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ.

“Monks, I allow a suitable lodging to be given to the sick.” According to this, if a monk is sick with cough, asthma, fistulas, dysentery, and so forth, and requires spittoons, chamber pots, and the like to be set out, or if he is a leper and soils the lodging—for such a person, a separate lodging should be given in a lower story of a building, a leaf hut, or similar, in a secluded place. For a sick person who does not soil the lodging while dwelling there, even the best lodging should indeed be given. Whoever undergoes any medical treatment, such as drinking oil, purgatives, or nasal treatments, is considered sick. For him also, after considering his condition, a suitable lodging should be given.

“Na, bhikkhave, ekena dve paṭibāhetabbā, yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 319) vacanato ekena dve senāsanāni na gahetabbāni. Sacepi gaṇheyya, pacchimena gahaṇena purimaggahaṇaṃ paṭippassambhati. Gahaṇena hi gahaṇaṃ paṭippassambhati, gahaṇena ālayo paṭippassambhati, ālayena gahaṇaṃ paṭippassambhati, ālayena ālayo paṭippassambhati. Kathaṃ? Idhekacco (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 319) vassūpanāyikadivase ekasmiṃ vihāre senāsanaṃ gahetvā sāmantavihāraṃ gantvā tatrāpi gaṇhāti, tassa iminā gahaṇena purimaggahaṇaṃ paṭippassambhati. Aparo “idha vasissāmī”ti ālayamattaṃ katvā sāmantavihāraṃ gantvā tattha senāsanaṃ gaṇhāti, tassa iminā gahaṇeneva purimo ālayo paṭippassambhati. Eko “idha vasissāmī”ti senāsanaṃ vā gahetvā ālayaṃ vā katvā sāmantavihāraṃ gantvā “idheva dāni vasissāmī”ti ālayaṃ karoti, iccassa ālayena vā gahaṇaṃ, ālayena vā ālayo [V 0.0268] paṭippassambhati, sabbattha pacchime gahaṇe vā ālaye vā tiṭṭhati. Yo pana ekasmiṃ vihāre senāsanaṃ gahetvā “aññasmiṃ vihāre vasissāmī”ti gacchati, tassa upacārasīmātikkame senāsanaggāho paṭippassambhati. Yadi pana “tattha phāsu bhavissati, vasissāmi, no ce, āgamissāmī”ti gantvā aphāsukabhāvaṃ ñatvā pacchā vā gacchati, vaṭṭati.

“Bhikkhus, two lodgings are not to be reserved by one bhikkhu. Whoever should reserve them, commits an offense of wrong-doing.” According to this statement, two lodgings are not to be taken by one. Even if one should take them, the earlier taking is annulled by the later taking. For indeed, a taking is annulled by a taking, an attachment is annulled by a taking, a taking is annulled by an attachment, and an attachment is annulled by an attachment. How? Here, on the day of entering the Rains, a certain bhikkhu, having taken a lodging in one monastery, goes to a neighboring monastery and takes one there also. For him, by this later taking, the earlier taking is annulled. Another, having made a mere attachment with the thought, “I will stay here,” goes to a neighboring monastery and takes a lodging there. For him, by this very taking, the earlier attachment is annulled. A certain one, having either taken a lodging or made an attachment with the thought, “I will stay here,” goes to a neighboring monastery and makes an attachment with the thought, “Now I will stay right here.” For this one, either the earlier taking is annulled by the later attachment, or the earlier attachment is annulled by the later attachment. In all cases, the claim stands on the last taking or attachment. Furthermore, as for one who, having taken a lodging in one monastery, goes with the thought, “I will stay in another monastery,” for him, upon crossing the boundary of the precincts, the taking of the lodging is annulled. If, however, having gone with the thought, “If it is comfortable there, I will stay; if not, I will return,” and having realized the state of discomfort, one then returns, it is permissible.

Senāsanaggāhakena ca senāsanaṃ gāhetvā vassāvāsikaṃ gāhetabbaṃ.
