Gāhentena sace saṅghiko ca saddhādeyyo cāti dve cīvarapaccayā honti, tesu yaṃ bhikkhū paṭhamaṃ gahituṃ icchanti, taṃ gahetvā tassa ṭhitikato paṭṭhāya itaro gāhetabbo. “Sace bhikkhūnaṃ appatāya pariveṇaggena senāsane gāhiyamāne ekaṃ pariveṇaṃ mahālābhaṃ hoti, dasa vā dvādasa vā cīvarāni labhanti, taṃ vijaṭetvā aññesu alābhakesu āvāsesu pakkhipitvā aññesampi bhikkhūnaṃ gāhetabba”nti mahāsumatthero āha. Mahāpadumatthero panāha “na evaṃ [M 0.0289] kātabbaṃ. Manussā hi attano āvāsapaṭijagganatthāya paccayaṃ denti, tasmā aññehi bhikkhūhi tattha pavisitabba”nti.

And the lodging-assigner, having assigned the lodgings, should then assign the rains-residence robes. When assigning, if there are two kinds of robe-requisites, namely, that belonging to the Sangha and that which is a faith-donation, among these, whichever robe-requisite the bhikkhus wish to take first, having assigned that one, and beginning from the one who has received it, the other should be assigned. The Elder Mahāsuma said: “If, due to there being few bhikkhus, when lodgings are being assigned by precinct, one precinct becomes very profitable—they receive ten or twelve robes—that profit should be set apart and, having been distributed among other residences with little gain, should be assigned to other bhikkhus as well.” But the Elder Mahāpaduma said: “It should not be done so. For people give requisites for the purpose of maintaining their own residence; therefore, other bhikkhus should enter there.”

221. Sace panettha mahāthero paṭikkosati “mā, āvuso, evaṃ gāhetha, bhagavato anusiṭṭhiṃ karotha. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pariveṇaggena gāhetu”nti (cūḷava. 318). Tassa paṭikkosanāya aṭṭhatvā “bhante, bhikkhū bahū, paccayo mando, saṅgahaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti saññāpetvā gāhetabbameva. Gāhentena ca sammatena bhikkhunā mahātherassa santikaṃ gantvā evaṃ vattabbaṃ “bhante, tumhākaṃ senāsanaṃ pāpuṇāti, paccayaṃ dhārethā”ti. Asukakulassa paccayo asukasenāsanañca mayhaṃ pāpuṇāti, āvusoti. Pāpuṇāti bhante, gaṇhatha nanti. Gaṇhāmi, āvusoti. Gahitaṃ hoti. “Sace pana ‘gahitaṃ vo, bhante’ti vutte ‘gahitaṃ me’ti vā, ‘gaṇhissatha, bhante’ti vutte ‘gaṇhissāmī’ti vā vadati, aggahitaṃ hotī”ti mahāsumatthero āha. Mahāpadumatthero panāha “atītānāgatavacanaṃ vā hotu vattamānavacanaṃ vā, satuppādamattaṃ ālayakaraṇamattameva cettha pamāṇaṃ, tasmā gahitameva hotī”ti.

221. If a senior elder here objects, saying, “Friends, do not assign in this way; act according to the Blessed One’s instruction. For this was said by the Blessed One: ‘Bhikkhus, I allow assigning by precinct,’” then, not heeding his objection, having persuaded him by saying, “Venerable sir, the bhikkhus are many and the requisites are few; it is proper to make a collection,” the assignment should indeed be made. And the appointed bhikkhu, having gone to the senior elder, should speak thus: “Venerable sir, a lodging falls to you; please accept the requisite.” If the elder asks, “Friend, does the requisite from such-and-such family and such-and-such lodging fall to me?” the appointed bhikkhu should reply, “Venerable sir, it does fall to you. Please take it.” If the elder says, “Friend, I take it,” it is considered taken. The Elder Mahāsuma, however, said: “If, when asked, ‘Venerable sir, has it been taken by you?’ he replies, ‘It has been taken by me’; or when asked, ‘Venerable sir, will you take it?’ he replies, ‘I will take it,’ it is not considered taken.” But the Elder Mahāpaduma said: “Be it a statement in the past or future tense, or a statement in the present tense, the mere arising of mindfulness and the mere act of making an attachment are the standard here. Therefore, it is indeed considered taken.”

Yopi paṃsukūliko bhikkhu senāsanaṃ gahetvā paccayaṃ vissajjeti, ayampi na aññasmiṃ āvāse pakkhipitabbo, tasmiṃyeva pariveṇe aggisālāya vā dīghasālāya vā rukkhamūle vā aññassa gāhetuṃ vaṭṭati. Paṃsukūliko “vasāmī”ti senāsanaṃ jaggissati, itaro “paccayaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti evaṃ dvīhi kāraṇehi senāsanaṃ sujaggitataraṃ bhavissati. Mahāpaccariyaṃ [V 0.0269] pana vuttaṃ “paṃsukūlike vāsatthāya senāsanaṃ gaṇhante senāsanaggāhakena vattabbaṃ, ‘bhante idha paccayo atthi, so kiṃ kātabbo’ti. Tena ‘heṭṭhā aññaṃ gāhāpehī’ti vattabbo. Sace pana kiñci avatvāva vasati, vuṭṭhavassassa ca pādamūle ṭhapetvā sāṭakaṃ denti, vaṭṭati. Atha ‘vassāvāsikaṃ demā’ti vadanti, tasmiṃ senāsane vassaṃvuṭṭhabhikkhūnaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti. Yesaṃ pana senāsanaṃ natthi, kevalaṃ paccayameva denti, tesaṃ paccayaṃ avassāvāsikasenāsane gāhetuṃ vaṭṭati. Manussā thūpaṃ katvā vassāvāsikaṃ gāhāpenti. Thūpo nāma [M 0.0290] asenāsanaṃ, tassa samīpe rukkhe vā maṇḍape vā upanibandhitvā gāhetabbaṃ. Tena bhikkhunā cetiyaṃ jaggitabbaṃ. Bodhirukkhabodhigharaāsanagharasammuñjaniaṭṭadāruaṭṭavaccakuṭidvārakoṭṭhakapānīyakuṭipānīyamāḷakadantakaṭṭhamāḷakesupi eseva nayo. Bhojanasālā pana senāsanameva, tasmā taṃ ekassa vā bahūnaṃ vā paricchinditvā gāhetuṃ vaṭṭatīti sabbamidaṃ vitthārena mahāpaccariyaṃ vuttaṃ.

If a rag-robe-wearing bhikkhu, having taken a lodging, should relinquish the requisite, this requisite should not be placed in another monastery. It is allowable for it to be assigned to another in that very precinct, in the fire hall, or in the long hall, or at the foot of a tree. The rag-robe-wearing bhikkhu will look after the lodging, thinking, 'I will reside here'; the other will be concerned with the requisite, thinking, 'I will take it.' Thus, for these two reasons, the lodging will be especially well looked after. However, in the Mahāpaccarī it is said: 'When a rag-robe-wearing bhikkhu is taking a lodging for the sake of residence, the lodging-assigner should say, "Venerable sir, there is a requisite here; what should be done with it?" He should then say, "Have another take it below." But if he resides without saying anything, and after he has completed the Rains-residence, they give a cloth, placing it at his feet, it is allowable. Then, if they say, "We give the Rains-residence requisite," it belongs to the bhikkhus who have completed the Rains in that lodging.' For those donors who have no lodging, but give only a requisite, it is allowable for their requisite to be assigned in a lodging not designated for the Rains-residence. People, having made a thūpa of offerings, have the Rains-residence requisite assigned. A thūpa, by definition, is not a lodging; it should be assigned by associating it with a nearby tree or pavilion. That bhikkhu should look after the cetiya. This same principle applies also to a Bodhi tree, a Bodhi-house, an assembly hall, a stand for brooms, a stand for wood, a latrine, a gatehouse, a water-hut, a stand for water pots, and a stand for tooth-sticks. A dining hall, however, is indeed a lodging; therefore, it is allowable for it to be assigned to one or many after having been demarcated. All this is said in detail in the Mahāpaccarī.

Senāsanaggāhakena pana pāṭipadaaruṇato paṭṭhāya yāva puna aruṇaṃ na bhijjati, tāva gāhetabbaṃ. Idañhi senāsanaggāhassa khettaṃ. Sace pātova gābhite senāsane añño vitakkacāriko bhikkhu āgantvā senāsanaṃ yācati, “gahitaṃ, bhante, senāsanaṃ, vassūpagato saṅgho, ramaṇīyo vihāro, rukkhamūlādīsu yattha icchatha, tattha vasathā”ti vattabbo. Pacchimavassūpanāyikadivase pana sace kālaṃ ghosetvā sannipatite saṅghe koci dasahatthaṃ vatthaṃ āharitvā vassāvāsikaṃ deti, āgantuko ce bhikkhu saṅghatthero hoti, tassa dātabbaṃ. Navako ce hoti, sammatena bhikkhunā saṅghatthero vattabbo “sace, bhante, icchatha, paṭhamabhāgaṃ muñcitvā idaṃ vatthaṃ gaṇhathā”ti, amuñcantassa na dātabbaṃ. Sace pana pubbe gāhitaṃ muñcitvā gaṇhāti, dātabbaṃ. Eteneva upāyena dutiyattherato paṭṭhāya parivattetvā pattaṭṭhāneva āgantukassa dātabbaṃ. Sace pana paṭhamavassūpagatā dve tīṇi cattāri pañca vā vatthāni alatthuṃ, laddhaṃ laddhaṃ eteneva upāyena vissajjāpetvā yāva āgantukassa samakaṃ hoti, tāva dātabbaṃ. Tena samake laddhe avasiṭṭho anubhāgo therāsane dātabbo. Paccuppanne lābhe sati ṭhitikāya gāhetuṃ katikaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati.

The monk appointed to take charge of lodgings, however, should take possession from the dawn of the first day after the full moon for as long as the next dawn does not break. This indeed is the sphere for the taking of lodgings. If, early in the morning, after a lodging has been taken, another monk who wanders about with much thought arrives and requests a lodging, he should be told: 'Venerable Sir, the lodgings have been taken, the Saṅgha has entered the rains-residence, the monastery is pleasant; dwell wherever you wish, at the foot of a tree or elsewhere.' On the day of the later rains-residence observance, however, if, after the time has been announced and the Saṅgha has assembled, someone brings a ten-cubit cloth and gives it as a rains-residence cloth, and if the visiting monk is the Saṅgha elder, it should be given to him. If he is a junior, the Saṅgha elder should be told by an appointed monk: 'Venerable Sir, if you wish, relinquish the first share and take this cloth.' To him who does not relinquish it, it should not be given. But if, having relinquished what was previously taken, he takes it, it should be given. By this same method, starting from the second elder, it should be rotated and given to the visitor when his turn arrives. If, however, those who entered the first rains-residence obtained two, three, four, or five cloths, whatever was received should, by this same method, be caused to be relinquished and given until the visitor's share is equal. When an equal share has been received by him, the remaining portion should be given to the elder's seat. When there is a present gain, it is allowable to make an agreement to take it according to a fixed rule.

Sace dubbhikkhaṃ hoti, dvīsupi vassūpanāyikāsu vassūpagatā bhikkhū bhikkhāya kilamantā “āvuso, idha vasantā sabbeva kilamāma, sādhu vata dve bhāgā homa, yesaṃ ñātipavāritaṭṭhānāni atthi, te tattha vasitvā pavāraṇāya āgantvā attano pattaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ gaṇhantū”ti vadanti, tesu ye tattha vasitvā pavāraṇāya āgacchanti, tesaṃ apaloketvā [V 0.0270] vassāvāsikaṃ dātabbaṃ. Sādiyantāpi hi teneva vassāvāsikassa sāmino, khīyantāpi ca āvāsikā neva adātuṃ labhanti. Kurundiyaṃ pana vuttaṃ “katikavattaṃ kātabbaṃ ‘sabbesaṃ no idha yāgubhattaṃ [M 0.0291] nappahoti, sabhāgaṭṭhāne vasitvā āgacchatha, tumhākaṃ pattaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ labhissathā’ti. Tañce eko paṭibāhati, supaṭibāhitaṃ. No ce paṭibāhati, katikā sukatā. Pacchā tesaṃ tattha vasitvā āgatānaṃ apaloketvā dātabbaṃ, apalokanakāle paṭibāhituṃ na labbhatī”ti. Punapi vuttaṃ “sace vassūpagatesu ekaccānaṃ vassāvāsike apāpuṇante bhikkhū katikaṃ karonti ‘chinnavassānaṃ vassāvāsikañca idāni uppajjanakavassāvāsikañca imesaṃ dātuṃ ruccatī’ti, evaṃ katikāya katāya gāhitasadisameva hoti, uppannuppannaṃ tesameva dātabba”nti. Temāsaṃ pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā vihāramaggacetiyaṅgaṇabodhiyaṅgaṇāni jaggitvā bodhirukkhe udakaṃ siñcitvā pakkantopi vibbhantopi vassāvāsikaṃ labhatiyeva. Bhatiniviṭṭhañhi tena kataṃ, saṅghikaṃ pana apalokanakammaṃ katvā gāhitaṃ antovasse vibbhantopi labhateva, paccayavasena gāhitaṃ pana na labhatīti vadanti.

If there is a famine, and the monks who have entered the rains-residence during both the earlier and later rains-residences are exhausted from seeking alms-food, they may say: 'Friends, staying here we are all exhausted. It would be good indeed if we become two groups: those monks who have places of relatives or invitation should stay in that place, and having come on the day of Pavāraṇā, let them receive the rains-residence gift that is due to them.' Among them, for those who, having stayed in that place, come on the day of Pavāraṇā, the rains-residence gift should be given after informing the Saṅgha. For even though they consent, those monks are not the owners of the rains-residence gift; and even if the resident monks are displeased, they cannot refuse to give it. However, in the Kurundī commentary it is said: 'A formal agreement should be made thus: "Rice-gruel and food are not sufficient here for all of us; having stayed in a suitable place, you should come back, and you will receive the rains-residence gift that is due to you." If one monk objects to that formal agreement, it is well objected. If he does not object, the agreement is well made. Later, it should be given to those who, having stayed there, have returned, after informing the Saṅgha; at the time of informing, it is not allowable to object.' Furthermore, it is said: 'If, among the monks who have entered the rains-residence, while the rains-residence gift has not yet arrived for some, the monks make an agreement thus: "It is agreeable to give both the rains-residence gift of those whose rains-residence is broken and the rains-residence gift that is to arise now to these monks whose rains-residence is broken," when the agreement has been made thus, it is just as if it has been received; whatever arises should be given to those very monks.' Even if one, having provided drinking water for three months, having maintained the monastery path, the stupa courtyard, and the Bodhi tree courtyard, and having watered the Bodhi tree, has then departed or disrobed, one certainly receives the rains-residence gift. For a service rendered for payment has been done by him. However, as for a Saṅghika item received after performing the act of informing, one certainly receives it even if one disrobes during the rains-residence; but as for a rains-residence gift received by means of requisites, they say that one does not receive it.

Sace vuṭṭhavasso disaṃgamiko bhikkhu āvāsikassa hatthato kiñcideva kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ gahetvā “asukakule mayhaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ pattaṃ, taṃ gaṇhathā”ti vatvā gataṭṭhāne vibbhamati, vassāvāsikaṃ saṅghikaṃ hoti. Sace pana manusse sammukhā sampaṭicchāpetvā gacchati, labhati. “Idaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ amhākaṃ senāsane vutthabhikkhuno demā”ti vutte yassa gāhitaṃ, tasseva hoti. Sace pana senāsanasāmikassa piyakamyatāya puttadhītādayo bahūni vatthāni āharitvā “amhākaṃ senāsane demā”ti denti, tattha vassūpagatassa ekameva vatthaṃ dātabbaṃ, sesāni saṅghikāni honti. Vassāvāsikaṭhitikāya gāhetabbāni, ṭhitikāya asati therāsanato paṭṭhāya gāhetabbāni. Senāsane vassūpagataṃ bhikkhuṃ nissāya uppannena cittappasādena bahūni vatthāni āharitvā “senāsanassa demā”ti dinnesupi eseva nayo. Sace pana pādamūle ṭhapetvā “etassa bhikkhuno demā”ti vadanti, tasseva honti.

If a bhikkhu who has completed the rains-residence, desiring to go to another region, takes a suitable article from the hand of a resident bhikkhu and says, 'My rains-residence gift has been received at such-and-such a family; you should take it,' and then disrobes in the place he has gone to, the rains-residence gift becomes the property of the Saṅgha. But if he departs after having caused the donors to acknowledge it in his presence, he receives it. When it is said, 'We give this rains-residence gift to the bhikkhu who has resided in our dwelling,' it belongs to that very bhikkhu for whom it was accepted. But if, out of a desire to please the owner of the dwelling, sons, daughters, and others bring many robes and give them, saying, 'We give these in our dwelling,' then only one robe is to be given to the one who has entered the rains-residence there; the remaining ones become the property of the Saṅgha. They are to be accepted according to the established procedure for rains-residence gifts. If there is no established procedure, they are to be accepted beginning from the elder's seat. Even when many robes are brought due to faith that has arisen on account of a bhikkhu who has entered the rains-residence in a dwelling, and are given with the words, 'We give to the dwelling,' this same principle applies. But if, having placed them at his feet, they say, 'We give to this bhikkhu,' they belong to that bhikkhu alone.

Ekassa gehe dve vassāvāsikāni, paṭhamabhāgo sāmaṇerassa gāhito hoti, dutiyo therāsane. So ekaṃ dasahatthaṃ, ekaṃ aṭṭhahatthaṃ sāṭakaṃ peseti “vassāvāsikaṃ pattabhikkhūnaṃ dethā”ti, vicinitvā varabhāgaṃ sāmaṇerassa datvā anubhāgo therāsane dātabbo[M 0.0292]. Sace pana ubhopi gharaṃ netvā bhojetvā sayameva pādamūle ṭhapeti, yaṃ yassa dinnaṃ, tadeva tassa hoti. Ito paraṃ mahāpaccariyaṃ āgatanayo hoti – ekassa ghare daharasāmaṇerassa vassāvāsikaṃ pāpuṇāti, so ce pucchati “amhākaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ kassa patta”nti, “sāmaṇerassā”ti avatvā [V 0.0271] “dānakāle jānissasī”ti vatvā dānadivase ekaṃ mahātheraṃ pesetvā nīharāpetabbaṃ. Sace yassa vassāvāsikaṃ pattaṃ, so vibbhamati vā kālaṃ vā karoti, manussā ce pucchanti “kassa amhākaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ patta”nti, tesaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Sace te vadanti “tumhākaṃ demā”ti, tassa bhikkhuno pāpuṇāti. Atha saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā denti, saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā pāpuṇāti. Sace vassūpagatā suddhapaṃsukūlikāyeva honti, ānetvā dinnaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ senāsanaparikkhāraṃ vā katvā ṭhapetabbaṃ, bimbohanādīni vā kātabbānīti.

In a donor's house, there are two rains-residence requisites: the first share is assigned to the novice, the second is assigned at the elder's seat. The donor sends one ten-cubit cloth and one eight-cubit cloth, saying, 'Give the rains-residence requisite to the monks who have obtained it.' Having chosen, the better share should be given to the novice, and the lesser share should be given at the elder's seat. If, however, having taken both monks to the house and fed them, the donor himself places the cloths at their feet, whichever cloth is given to whichever person, that very cloth belongs to that person. Hereafter, the method that has come in the Mahāpaccarī is as follows: In a certain house, the rains-residence requisite falls to a young novice. If that donor asks, 'To whom has our rains-residence requisite fallen?', without saying, 'It has fallen to the novice,' one should say, 'You will know at the time of the offering.' On the day of the offering, having sent a great elder, it should be caused to be brought out. If the one to whom the rains-residence requisite has fallen disrobes or passes away, and the people ask, 'To whom has our rains-residence requisite fallen?', it should be told to them as it truly is. If they say, 'We give it to you,' it falls to that monk. Or if they give it to the Saṅgha or to a group, it falls to the Saṅgha or to the group. If the monks who have entered the rains-residence are exclusively practitioners of the refuse-rag robe, the rains-residence requisite that has been brought and given should be kept after being made into a requisite for the lodging, or things such as pillows should be made from it.

Ayaṃ tāva antovasse vassūpanāyikadivasavasena

This, for now, is by way of the day of entering the rains-residence, within the rains-residence period.

Senāsanaggāhakathā.

The Discourse on the Acceptance of Lodgings.

222. Ayamaparopi utukāle antarāmuttako nāma senāsanaggāho veditabbo. Divasavasena hi tividho senāsanaggāho purimako pacchimako antarāmuttakoti. Vuttañhetaṃ –

222. This other acceptance of lodgings, named Antarāmuttaka, which occurs in the proper season, should be understood. Indeed, by way of the day, the acceptance of lodgings is of three kinds: the earlier, the later, and the intermediate. For this was said:

“Tayome, bhikkhave, senāsanaggāhā, purimako pacchimako antarāmuttako. Aparajjugatāya āsāḷhiyā purimako gāhetabbo, māsagatāya āsāḷhiyā pacchimako gāhetabbo, aparajjugatāya pavāraṇāya āyatiṃ vassāvāsatthāya antarāmuttako gāhetabbo”ti (mahāva. 318).

“Monks, there are these three assignments of lodgings: the first, the last, and the intermediate. On the day after the full moon of Āsāḷha has passed, the first is to be taken. When a month has passed since the full moon of Āsāḷha, the last is to be taken. On the day after the Pavāraṇā has passed, the intermediate is to be taken for the purpose of the rains-residence in the future.”

Etesu (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318) tīsu senāsanaggāhesu purimako pacchimako cāti ime dve gāhā thāvarā, antarāmuttako pana senāsanapaṭijagganatthaṃ bhagavatā anuññāto. Tathā hi ekasmiṃ vihāre mahālābhaṃ senāsanaṃ hoti, senāsanasāmikā vassūpagataṃ bhikkhuṃ sabbapaccayehi sakkaccaṃ upaṭṭhahitvā pavāretvā gamanakāle bahuṃ samaṇaparikkhāraṃ denti, mahātherā dūratova āgantvā vassūpanāyikadivase taṃ [M 0.0293] gahetvā phāsuṃ vasitvā vuṭṭhavassā lābhaṃ gaṇhitvā pakkamanti. Āvāsikā “mayaṃ etthuppannaṃ lābhaṃ na labhāma, niccaṃ āgantukamahātherāva labhanti, teyeva naṃ āgantvā paṭijaggissantī”ti palujjantampi na olokenti. Bhagavā tassa paṭijagganatthaṃ “aparajjugatāya pavāraṇāya āyatiṃ vassāvāsatthāya antarāmuttako gāhetabbo”ti āha.

Among these three assignments of lodgings, the first and the last are permanent, but the intermediate was permitted by the Blessed One for the purpose of maintaining the lodging. For indeed, in a certain monastery, there is a lodging with great gain. The patrons of the lodging respectfully attend to a monk who has entered the rains-residence with all requisites, invite him at the Pavāraṇā, and at the time of his departure, give abundant monastic supplies. Senior monks come from afar and, on the day of entering the rains-residence, take that lodging, dwell comfortably, and after completing the rains, take the gain and depart. The resident monks, thinking, ‘We do not obtain the gain that arises here; visiting senior monks always obtain it. Let them be the ones to come and maintain it,’ do not look after the lodging even when it is falling into ruin. The Blessed One, for the purpose of maintaining that lodging, said: ‘On the day after the Pavāraṇā has passed, the intermediate is to be taken for the purpose of the rains-residence in the future.’”

Taṃ gāhentena saṅghatthero vattabbo “bhante, antarāmuttakasenāsanaṃ gaṇhathā”ti. Sace gaṇhāti[V 0.0272], dātabbaṃ. No ce, eteneva upāyena anutheraṃ ādiṃ katvā yo gaṇhāti, tassa antamaso sāmaṇerassapi dātabbaṃ. Tena taṃ senāsanaṃ aṭṭha māse paṭijaggitabbaṃ, chadanabhittibhūmīsu yaṃ kiñci khaṇḍaṃ vā phullaṃ vā hoti, taṃ sabbaṃ paṭisaṅkharitabbaṃ. Uddesaparipucchādīhi divasaṃ khepetvā rattiṃ tattha vasituṃ vaṭṭati, rattiṃ pariveṇe vasitvā tattha divasaṃ khepetumpi vaṭṭati, rattindivaṃ tattheva vasitumpi vaṭṭati, utukāle āgatānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ na paṭibāhitabbaṃ. Vassūpanāyikadivase pana sampatte sace saṅghatthero “mayhaṃ idaṃ pana senāsanaṃ dethā”ti vadati, na labhati. “Bhante, idaṃ antarāmuttakaṃ gahetvā ekena bhikkhunā paṭijaggita”nti vatvā na dātabbaṃ, aṭṭha māse paṭijaggitabhikkhusseva gāhitaṃ hoti. Yasmiṃ pana senāsane ekasaṃvacchare dvikkhattuṃ paccaye denti chamāsaccayena chamāsaccayena, taṃ antarāmuttakaṃ na gāhetabbaṃ. Yasmiṃ vā tikkhattuṃ denti catumāsaccayena catumāsaccayena, yasmiṃ vā catukkhattuṃ denti temāsaccayena temāsaccayena, taṃ antarāmuttakaṃ na gāhetabbaṃ. Paccayeneva hi taṃ paṭijagganaṃ labhissati. Yasmiṃ pana ekasaṃvacchare sakideva bahū paccaye denti, etaṃ antarāmuttakaṃ gāhetabbanti.

The monk who is taking it should tell the Saṅghatthera: 'Venerable Sir, please take the intermediate lodging.' If he takes it, it should be given. If not, then by this same method, starting with the next senior monk, it should be given to whichever monk takes it, even to a novice at the least. That lodging should be maintained by that monk for eight months. In the roof, walls, and floor, whatever is broken or cracked, all of it should be repaired. Having spent the day with recitation, questioning, and so forth, it is allowable to dwell there at night. Having dwelt in the monastic compound at night, it is also allowable to spend the day there. It is also allowable to dwell there day and night. Elders who have come during the season should not be prevented. However, when the day for entering the Rains-residence arrives, if the Saṅghatthera says, 'Give this lodging to me,' he does not get it. Having said, 'Venerable Sir, this lodging was taken as an intermediate one and has been maintained by a monk,' it should not be given. It is possessed by the very monk who maintained it for eight months. But a lodging for which requisites are provided twice in one year, every six months, should not be taken as an intermediate one. Nor should one for which they are provided three times, every four months, or four times, every three months. For its maintenance will surely be obtained through the requisites. But a lodging for which many requisites are provided just once in a year may be taken as an intermediate one.

223. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, akataṃ vā vihāraṃ vippakataṃ vā navakammaṃ dātuṃ, khuddake vihāre kammaṃ oloketvā chappañcavassikaṃ navakammaṃ dātuṃ, aḍḍhayoge kammaṃ oloketvā sattaṭṭhavassikaṃ navakammaṃ dātuṃ, mahallake vihāre pāsāde vā kammaṃ oloketvā dasadvādasavassikaṃ navakammaṃ dātu”nti (cūḷava. 323) vacanato akataṃ vippakataṃ vā senāsanaṃ ekassa bhikkhuno apalokanena vā kammavācāya vā sāvetvā navakammaṃ [M 0.0294] katvā vasituṃ yathāvuttakālaparicchedavasena dātabbaṃ. Navakammiko bhikkhu antovasse taṃ āvāsaṃ labhati, utukāle paṭibāhituṃ na labhati. Laddhanavakammena pana bhikkhunā vāsipharasunikhādanādīni gahetvā sayaṃ na kātabbaṃ, katākataṃ jānitabbaṃ. Sace so āvāso jīrati, āvāsasāmikassa vā tassa vaṃse uppannassa vā kassaci kathetabbaṃ “āvāso te nassati, jaggatha etaṃ āvāsa”nti. Sace so na sakkoti, bhikkhūhi ñātīhi vā upaṭṭhākehi vā samādāpetvā jaggitabbo. Sace tepi na sakkonti, saṅghikena paccayena jaggitabbo, tasmimpi asati ekaṃ āvāsaṃ vissajjetvā avasesā jaggitabbā, bahū vissajjetvā ekaṃ saṇṭhapetumpi vaṭṭatiyeva.

223. “I allow, monks, that new work be given for a dwelling that is unbuilt or incomplete. For a small dwelling, after inspecting the work, new work may be given for five or six years. For a medium dwelling, after inspecting the work, new work may be given for seven or eight years. For a large dwelling or a mansion, after inspecting the work, new work may be given for ten or twelve years.” In accordance with this, an unbuilt or incomplete lodging should be given to one monk, after informing him either by consultation or by a formal motion, to reside there after completing the new work according to the aforementioned time limits. A monk undertaking new work who obtains that dwelling within the rainy season cannot be turned away during that season. However, a monk who has received the new work should not personally take up an adze, axe, chisel, and so on; he should know what has been done and what has not been done. If that dwelling deteriorates, the owner of the dwelling or someone born in his lineage should be told, “Your dwelling is perishing; take care of this dwelling.” If he is unable to do so, it should be maintained by having the monks, their relatives, or their supporters undertake it. If they too are unable, it should be maintained with Saṅgha property. When that is also not available, having given up one dwelling, the remaining ones should be maintained. It is also permissible to establish one after giving up many.

Dubbhikkhe bhikkhūsu pakkantesu sabbe āvāsā nassanti, tasmā ekaṃ vā dve vā tayo vā [V 0.0273] āvāse vissajjetvā tato yāgubhattacīvarādīni paribhuñjantehi sesāvāsā jaggitabbāyeva.

During a time of famine, when monks have departed, all dwellings are ruined. Therefore, having relinquished one, two, or three dwellings, and while consuming the rice-gruel, food, robes, and so on obtained from the proceeds, the remaining dwellings must indeed be maintained.

Kurundiyaṃ pana vuttaṃ “saṅghike paccaye asati eko bhikkhu ‘tuyhaṃ ekamañcaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā jaggāhī’ti vattabbo. Sace bahutaraṃ icchati, tibhāgaṃ vā upaḍḍhabhāgaṃ vā datvāpi jaggāpetabbaṃ. Atha thambhamattamevettha avasiṭṭhaṃ, bahukammaṃ kātabbanti na icchati, ‘tuyhaṃ puggalikameva katvā jaggāhī’ti dātabbaṃ. Evampi hi ‘saṅghassa bhaṇḍakaṭhapanaṭṭhānañca navakānañca vasanaṭṭhānaṃ labhissatī’ti jaggāpetabbo. Evaṃ jaggito pana tasmiṃ jīvante puggaliko hoti, mate saṅghikova. Sace saddhivihārikānaṃ dātukāmo hoti, kammaṃ oloketvā tibhāgaṃ vā upaḍḍhaṃ vā puggalikaṃ katvā jaggāpetabbo. Evañhi saddhivihārikānaṃ dātuṃ labhati. Evaṃ jagganake pana asati ekaṃ āvāsaṃ vissajjetvātiādinā nayena jaggāpetabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Idampi ca aññaṃ tattheva vuttaṃ.

But in the Kurundī, it is said: 'When there are no properties belonging to the Saṅgha, a monk should be told, “Take a place for one bed and maintain it.” If he desires more, a third part or a half part should be given, and he should be made to maintain it. Now, if only a pillar remains there and he does not desire it, thinking, “Much work is to be done,” it should be given to him with the words, “Make it your personal property and maintain it.” For even in this way, he should be made to maintain it with the thought that, “The Saṅgha will obtain a place for storing requisites and a dwelling place for new monks.” A monastery maintained in this way is his personal property while he is living; when he is dead, it becomes the Saṅgha's. If he wishes to give it to his co-residents, the work should be reviewed, and having made a third part or a half part personal property, the co-resident should be made to maintain it. For in this way, he is able to give it to his co-residents. But when there is no one to maintain it in this way, it should be caused to be maintained by the method beginning with, “having given up one monastery…”' This other saying was also stated in that very same place.

Dve bhikkhū saṅghikabhūmiṃ gahetvā sodhetvā saṅghikasenāsanaṃ karonti, yena sā bhūmi paṭhamaṃ gahitā, so sāmī. Ubhopi puggalikaṃ karonti, soyeva sāmī. So saṅghikaṃ karoti, itaro puggalikaṃ karoti, aññaṃ ce bahu senāsanaṭṭhānaṃ atthi, puggalikaṃ karontopi na vāretabbo. Aññasmiṃ pana tādise patirūpe ṭhāne asati [M 0.0295] taṃ paṭibāhitvā saṅghikaṃ karonteneva kātabbaṃ. Yaṃ pana tassa tattha vayakammaṃ kataṃ, taṃ dātabbaṃ. Sace pana katāvāse vā āvāsakaraṇaṭṭhāne vā chāyūpagaphalūpagā rukkhā honti, apaloketvā hāretabbā. Puggalikā ce honti, sāmikā āpucchitabbā. No ce denti, yāvatatiyakaṃ āpucchitvā “rukkhaagghanakamūlaṃ dassāmā”ti hāretabbā.

Two monks, having taken and cleared land belonging to the Saṅgha, build a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha; the monk by whom that land was first taken is the owner. If both make it personal property, that very same one is the owner. If that one makes it the Saṅgha's property and the other makes it personal property, and if there is other land for many dwellings, the one making it personal property should not be prevented. But when there is no other such suitable place, that monk should be prevented, and it must be built by the one who is making it property of the Saṅgha. Whatever work was done there by that monk should be paid for. Furthermore, if in a completed monastery or in a place for building a monastery there are trees that provide shade or fruit, they should be removed after informing the Saṅgha. If they are personal property, the owners should be asked. If they do not give permission, after asking up to the third time, they should be removed with the words, “We will give the value of the trees.”

224. Yo pana saṅghikaṃ vallimattampi aggahetvā āharimena upakaraṇena saṅghikāya bhūmiyā puggalikavihāraṃ kāreti, upaḍḍhaṃ saṅghikaṃ hoti, upaḍḍhaṃ puggalikaṃ. Pāsādo ce hoti, heṭṭhāpāsādo saṅghiko, upari puggaliko. Sace yo heṭṭhāpāsādaṃ icchati, heṭṭhāpāsādaṃ tassa hoti. Atha heṭṭhā ca upari ca icchati, ubhayattha upaḍḍhaṃ labhati. Dve senāsanāni kāreti, ekaṃ saṅghikaṃ, ekaṃ puggalikaṃ. Sace vihāre uṭṭhitena dabbasambhārena kāreti, tibhāgaṃ labhati. Sace akataṭṭhāne cayaṃ vā pamukhaṃ vā karoti bahikuṭṭe, upaḍḍhaṃ saṅghassa, upaḍḍhaṃ tassa. Atha mahantaṃ visamaṃ pūretvā apade padaṃ dassetvā kataṃ hoti, anissaro tattha saṅgho.

224. If a bhikkhu, without taking anything belonging to the Saṅgha, even as much as a vine, causes a personal dwelling to be built on Saṅgha land with materials brought in from elsewhere, half is of the Saṅgha, and half is personal. If it is a multi-storied building, the lower story is of the Saṅgha, and the upper is personal. If a bhikkhu desires the lower story, the lower story is for him. If, however, he desires both the lower and the upper, he obtains half in both places. If he causes two dwellings to be built, one is of the Saṅgha, and one is personal. If he causes it to be built with materials that have arisen in the monastery, he obtains a third part. If, in an undeveloped place, he makes a terrace or a porch on an outer wall, half is for the Saṅgha, and half is for him. If, however, it is made after filling in a large, uneven area and indicating a site where there was no site, the Saṅgha has no ownership there.

Sace [V 0.0274] bhikkhu saṅghikavihārato gopānasiādīni gahetvā aññasmiṃ saṅghikāvāse yojeti, suyojitāni. Puggalikāvāse yojentehi pana mūlaṃ vā dātabbaṃ, paṭipākatikaṃ vā kātabbaṃ. Chaḍḍitavihārato mañcapīṭhādīni theyyacittena gaṇhanto uddhāreyeva bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbo. “Puna āvāsikakāle dassāmī”ti gahetvā saṅghikaparibhogena paribhuñjantassa naṭṭhaṃ sunaṭṭhaṃ, jiṇṇaṃ sujiṇṇaṃ. Arogaṃ ce, pākatikaṃ kātabbaṃ, puggalikaparibhogena paribhuñjantassa naṭṭhaṃ vā jiṇṇaṃ vā gīvā hoti. Tato dvāravātapānādīni saṅghikāvāse vā puggalikāvāse vā yojitāni, paṭidātabbāniyeva. Sace koci saṅghiko vihāro undriyati, yaṃ tattha mañcapīṭhādikaṃ, taṃ guttatthāya aññatra harituṃ vaṭṭati. Tasmā aññatra haritvā saṅghikaparibhogena paribhuñjantassa naṭṭhaṃ sunaṭṭhaṃ, jiṇṇaṃ sujiṇṇaṃ. Sace arogaṃ, tasmiṃ vihāre paṭisaṅkhate puna pākatikaṃ kātabbaṃ. Puggalikaparibhogena paribhuñjato naṭṭhaṃ vā jiṇṇaṃ vā gīvā hoti, tasmiṃ paṭisaṅkhate dātabbameva. Ayaṃ senāsanaggāhakathā.

If a bhikkhu takes rafters and so forth from a dilapidated Saṅgha monastery and installs them in another Saṅgha residence, they are well-installed. However, if they are installed in a personal residence, either the price must be given, or a replacement must be provided. If a bhikkhu takes beds, chairs, and so forth from an abandoned monastery with the intention to steal, he should be made to pay the value of the goods from the very moment of lifting them. If one takes an item with the thought, 'I will give it back when residents come to live here again,' and uses it for the Saṅgha's use, should it be lost, it is well lost; should it be worn out, it is well worn out. If it is undamaged, it should be restored to its original state. For one who uses it for personal use, if it is lost or worn out, it becomes a debt. Doors, windows, and so forth from that residence, if installed in either a Saṅgha residence or a personal residence, must certainly be returned. If a Saṅgha monastery is dilapidated, whatever beds, chairs, and so forth are there, it is allowable to carry them elsewhere for the sake of safekeeping. Therefore, for one who, having carried them elsewhere, uses them for the Saṅgha's use, should they be lost, they are well lost; should they be worn out, they are well worn out. If they are undamaged, when that monastery has been repaired, they should be restored to their original state. For one who uses them for personal use, should they be lost or worn out, it becomes a debt; when that monastery has been repaired, they must certainly be given back. This is the discussion concerning the taking of lodgings.

225. Ayaṃ [M 0.0296] panettha catupaccayasādhāraṇakathā (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 325 pakkhikabhattādikathā) – sammatena appamattakavissajjakena bhikkhunā cīvarakammaṃ karontassa “sūciṃ dehī”ti vadato ekā dīghā, ekā rassāti dve sūciyo dātabbā. “Avibhattaṃ saṅghikabhaṇḍa”nti pucchitabbakiccaṃ natthi. Pipphalatthikassa eko pipphalako, kantāraṃ paṭipajjitukāmassa upāhanayugaḷaṃ, kāyabandhanatthikassa kāyabandhanaṃ, “aṃsabaddhako me jiṇṇo”ti āgatassa aṃsabaddhako, parissāvanatthikassa parissāvanaṃ dātabbaṃ, dhammakaraṇatthikassa dhammakaraṇo. Sace paṭṭako na hoti, dhammakaraṇo paṭṭakena saddhiṃ dātabbo. “Āgantukapattaṃ āropessāmī”ti yācantassa kusiyā ca aḍḍhakusiyā ca pahonakaṃ dātabbaṃ. “Maṇḍalaṃ nappahotī”ti āgatassa maṇḍalaṃ ekaṃ dātabbaṃ, aḍḍhamaṇḍalāni dve dātabbāni, dve maṇḍalāni yācantassa na dātabbāni. Anuvātaparibhaṇḍatthikassa ekassa cīvarassa pahonakaṃ dātabbaṃ, sappinavanītādiatthikassa gilānassa ekaṃ bhesajjaṃ nāḷimattaṃ katvā tato tatiyakoṭṭhāso dātabbo. Evaṃ tīṇi divasāni datvā nāḷiyā paripuṇṇāya catutthadivasato paṭṭhāya saṅghaṃ āpucchitvā dātabbaṃ, guḷapiṇḍepi ekadivasaṃ tatiyabhāgo dātabbo. Evaṃ tīhi divasehi niṭṭhite piṇḍe tato paraṃ saṅghaṃ āpucchitvā dātabbaṃ. Sammannitvā ṭhapitayāgubhājakādīhi ca bhājanīyaṭṭhānaṃ āgatamanussānaṃ anāpucchitvāva upaḍḍhabhāgo dātabbo. Asammatehi pana apaloketvā dātabboti.

225. Furthermore, this is the general discourse herein on the four requisites. A monk appointed as a distributor of minor items should give two needles—one long and one short—to a monk who is doing robe-work and says, 'Give me a needle.' There is no need to ask, 'Is this Saṅgha property not yet divided?' To one who needs a small knife, a small knife should be given. To one who wishes to travel through a wilderness, a pair of sandals should be given. To one who needs a waistband, a waistband should be given. To one who comes saying, 'My shoulder strap is worn out,' a shoulder strap should be given. To one who needs a water strainer, a water strainer should be given. To one who needs a water pot with a strainer, a water pot with a strainer should be given. If there is no cloth, the water pot with a strainer should be given together with a cloth. To one who requests, saying 'I will fit a stand for a newcomer's bowl,' sufficient material for a long stand-piece and a short stand-piece should be given. To one who comes saying, 'The circular mat is not sufficient,' one circular mat should be given; two half-mats should be given. To one who asks for two circular mats, they should not be given. To one who needs a border for a robe, sufficient for one robe should be given. For a sick person who needs ghee, fresh butter, and so forth, one medicine should be prepared in the amount of a nāḷi, and then a third portion of that should be given. After giving in this way for three days, when the nāḷi measure is complete, from the fourth day onward, it should be given after asking the Saṅgha. In the case of a lump of jaggery also, a third portion should be given for one day. Thus, when the lump is finished in three days, from then on, it should be given after asking the Saṅgha. Those appointed as distributors of gruel and so forth should give half a portion without asking to people who come to the place of distribution. However, those not appointed should give after informing the Saṅgha.

Saṅghassa santakaṃ sammatena vā āṇattehi vā ārāmikādīhi dīyamānaṃ, gihīnañca santakaṃ [V 0.0275] sāmikena vā āṇattena vā dīyamānaṃ “aparassa bhāgaṃ dehī”ti asantaṃ puggalaṃ vatvā gaṇhato bhaṇḍādeyyaṃ. Aññena dīyamānaṃ gaṇhanto bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbo. Asammatena vā anāṇattena vā dīyamāne “aparampi bhāgaṃ dehī”ti vatvā vā kūṭavassāni gaṇetvā vā gaṇhanto uddhāreyeva bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbo. Itarehi dīyamānaṃ evaṃ gaṇhato bhaṇḍādeyyaṃ sāmikena pana “imassa dehī”ti dāpitaṃ vā sayaṃ dinnaṃ vā sudinnanti ayaṃ sabbaṭṭhakathāvinicchayato sāro.

Regarding property belonging to the Saṅgha being given by one who is appointed, or by those instructed such as monastery attendants, and property belonging to laypeople being given by the owner or by one who is instructed: for one who takes it by speaking of a non-existent person, saying, 'Give a portion to another,' it is an unlawful taking of goods. One who takes what is being given by another (unauthorized person) should be made to pay the value of the goods. When it is being given by one who is not appointed or not instructed, one who takes it by saying, 'Give another portion as well,' or by calculating with fraudulent seniority, should be made to pay the value of the goods from the very moment of lifting them. For one who takes in this way what is being given by these others (the appointed and instructed), it is an unlawful taking of goods. However, if it was caused to be given by the owner, saying, 'Give to this one,' or was given by the owner himself, it is well-given. This is the essence from the decisions in all the commentaries.

Piṇḍāya [M 0.0297] paviṭṭhassapi odanapaṭivīso antoupacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitasseva gahetuṃ vaṭṭati. Yadi pana dāyakā “bahiupacārasīmaṭṭhānampi, bhante, gaṇhatha, āgantvā paribhuñjissantī”ti vadanti, evaṃ antogāmaṭṭhānampi gahetuṃ vaṭṭati.

Even for one who has entered for alms, it is allowable to take a share of rice only while standing within the boundary of the precincts. However, if the donors say, 'Venerable sirs, take also the share of those standing outside the boundary of the precincts; having returned, they will consume it,' in that case, it is allowable to take also the share of those standing inside the village.

Pāḷiṃ aṭṭhakathañceva, oloketvā vicakkhaṇo;

Saṅghike paccaye evaṃ, appamattova bhājayeti.

A wise person, having looked into the Pāḷi and the Commentary, should thus, being heedful, distribute the requisites belonging to the Saṅgha.

Iti pāḷimuttakavinayavinicchayasaṅgahe sabbākārato

Thus, in the Compendium of Vinaya Decisions beyond the Pāḷi, in all aspects...

Catupaccayabhājanīyavinicchayakathā samattā.

The discourse on the decision concerning the distribution of the four requisites is completed.

29. Kathinatthāravinicchayakathā

29. 29. The Discourse on the Decision Concerning the Spreading of the Kaṭhina

226. Kathinanti [V 0.0276] ettha (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) pana kathinaṃ attharituṃ ke labhanti, ke na labhanti? Gaṇanavasena tāva pacchimakoṭiyā pañca janā labhanti, uddhaṃ satasahassampi, pañcannaṃ heṭṭhā na labhanti. Vuṭṭhavassavasena purimikāya vassaṃ upagantvā paṭhamapavāraṇāya pavāritā labhanti. Chinnavassā vā pacchimikāya upagatā vā na labhanti. “Aññasmiṃ vihāre vuṭṭhavassāpi na labhantī”ti mahāpaccariyaṃ vuttaṃ. Purimikāya upagatānaṃ pana sabbe gaṇapūrakā honti, ānisaṃsaṃ na labhanti, ānisaṃso itaresaṃyeva hoti. Sace purimikāya upagatā cattāro vā honti tayo vā dve vā eko vā, itare gaṇapūrake katvā kathinaṃ attharitabbaṃ. Atha cattāro bhikkhū upagatā, eko paripuṇṇavasso sāmaṇero, so ce pacchimikāya upasampajjati, gaṇapūrako ceva hoti ānisaṃsañca labhati. Tayo bhikkhū dve sāmaṇerā, dve bhikkhū tayo sāmaṇerā, eko bhikkhu cattāro sāmaṇerāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Sace purimikāya upagatā kathinatthārakusalā na honti, atthārakusalā khandhakabhāṇakattherā pariyesitvā ānetabbā. Kammavācaṃ sāvetvā kathinaṃ attharāpetvā dānañca bhuñjitvā gamissanti, ānisaṃso pana itaresaṃyeva hoti.

226. Here, regarding the Kathina: who are eligible to spread the Kathina, and who are not? In terms of number, at the lowest limit five persons are eligible, even up to a hundred thousand; below five, they are not eligible. In terms of having spent the rains, those who, having entered the rains-residence in the first period and performed the first Pavāraṇā, are eligible. Those who have broken the rains-residence, or entered in the later period, are not eligible. “Even those who have spent the rains-residence in another monastery are not eligible,” it is stated in the Mahāpaccarī. However, all the others may serve as quorum-fillers for those who entered in the first period, but they do not receive the benefits; the benefits belong only to those who entered in the first period. If those who entered in the first period are four, or three, or two, or one, then, having made the others quorum-fillers, the Kathina should be spread. But if four monks have entered, and there is one novice who has completed a full rains-residence, if he receives higher ordination in the later period, he is both a quorum-filler and receives the benefits. Three monks, two novices; two monks, three novices; one monk, four novices—in this case too, the same method applies. If those who entered in the first period are not skilled in spreading the Kathina, then Theras who are skilled in spreading it and are reciters of the Khandhaka should be sought and brought. Having had the formal act (kammavācā) announced, having had the Kathina spread, and having partaken of the alms-offering, they will depart; the benefits, however, belong only to the others.

Kathinaṃ [M 0.0298] kena dinnaṃ vaṭṭati? Yena kenaci devena vā manussena vā pañcannaṃ vā sahadhammikānaṃ aññatarena dinnaṃ vaṭṭati. Kathinadāyakassa vattaṃ atthi, sace so taṃ ajānanto pucchati – “bhante, kathaṃ kathinaṃ dātabba”nti, tassa evaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ “tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññatarappahonakaṃ sūriyuggamanasamaye vatthaṃ ‘kathinacīvaraṃ demā’ti dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Tassa parikammatthaṃ ettakā nāma sūciyo, ettakaṃ suttaṃ, ettakaṃ rajanaṃ, parikammaṃ karontānaṃ ettakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yāgubhattañca dātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti.

By whom should the Kathina be given? It is proper if given by any deva or human, or by any one of the five co-religionists. There is a duty for the Kathina donor; if he, not knowing it, asks, “Venerable Sir, how should the Kathina be given?” he should be instructed thus: “At sunrise, it is proper to give a cloth sufficient for any one of the three robes, saying, ‘We give the Kathina robe.’ For its preparation, it is proper to give so many needles, so much thread, so much dye, and gruel and food to so many bhikkhus who are undertaking the preparation.”

Kathinatthārakenapi dhammena samena uppannaṃ kathinaṃ attharantena vattaṃ jānitabbaṃ. Tantavāyagehato hi ābhatasantāneneva khalimakkhitasāṭako na vaṭṭati, malīnasāṭakopi na vaṭṭati, tasmā kathinatthārasāṭakaṃ labhitvā suṭṭhu dhovitvā sūciādīni cīvarakammūpakaraṇāni sajjetvā bahūhi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ tadaheva sibbitvā niṭṭhitasūcikammaṃ rajitvā kappabinduṃ datvā kathinaṃ attharitabbaṃ. Sace tasmiṃ anatthateyeva aññaṃ kathinasāṭakaṃ āharati, aññāni ca [V 0.0277] bahūni kathinānisaṃsavatthāni deti, yo ānisaṃsaṃ bahuṃ deti, tassa santakena attharitabbaṃ. Itaro tathā tathā ovaditvā saññāpetabbo.

A bhikkhu who spreads the Kathina should also know the duty regarding a Kathina cloth that has been obtained in accordance with the Dhamma and with equity. For a cloth brought straight from the weaver's house, smeared with paste, is not proper; nor is a soiled cloth proper. Therefore, having obtained a Kathina-spreading cloth, it should be thoroughly washed, and the robe-making implements, such as needles, should be prepared. Then, on that very day, together with many bhikkhus, it should be sewn, the needlework completed, dyed, marked with the kappabindu, and the Kathina spread. If, before it is spread, another person brings another Kathina cloth and also gives many other accessory cloths, the Kathina should be spread with the cloth belonging to the one who gives many accessory cloths. The first donor should be advised in such and such a way and made to understand.

Kathinaṃ pana kena attharitabbaṃ? Yassa saṅgho kathinacīvaraṃ deti. Saṅghena pana kassa dātabbaṃ? Yo jiṇṇacīvaro hoti. Sace bahū jiṇṇacīvarā, vuḍḍhassa dātabbaṃ. Vuḍḍhesupi yo mahāpariso tadaheva cīvaraṃ katvā attharituṃ sakkoti, tassa dātabbaṃ. Sace vuḍḍho na sakkoti, navakataro sakkoti, tassa dātabbaṃ. Apica saṅghena mahātherassa saṅgahaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, tasmā “tumhe, bhante, gaṇhatha, mayaṃ katvā dassāmā”ti vattabbaṃ. Tīsu cīvaresu yaṃ jiṇṇaṃ hoti, tadatthāya dātabbaṃ. Pakatiyā dupaṭṭacīvarassa dupaṭṭatthāyeva dātabbaṃ. Sacepissa ekapaṭṭacīvaraṃ ghanaṃ hoti, kathinasāṭakā ca pelavā, sāruppatthāya dupaṭṭappahonakameva dātabbaṃ, “ahaṃ alabhanto ekapaṭṭaṃ pārupāmī”ti vadantassapi dupaṭṭaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Yo pana lobhapakatiko hoti, tassa na dātabbaṃ. Tenapi “kathinaṃ attharitvā pacchā visibbitvā dve cīvarāni karissāmī”ti na gahetabbaṃ. Yassa pana dīyati, tassa –

But by whom should the Kathina be spread? By the bhikkhu to whom the Sangha gives the Kathina-robe. But to whom should it be given by the Sangha? To a bhikkhu whose robe is worn out. If there are many whose robes are worn out, it should be given to the senior. Among the seniors, it should be given to the one who has a large retinue and is able to make and spread the robe on that very day. If the senior is not able, but a more junior one is able, it should be given to that more junior one. Moreover, it is proper for the Sangha to show support to the great elder; therefore, it should be said, 'Venerable Sir, please accept it; we will make it and give it.' It should be given for the purpose of whichever of the three robes is worn out. For one who by nature wears a double-layered robe, it should be given only for the purpose of a double-layered robe. Even if his single-layered robe is thick and the kathina cloth is thin, for the purpose of suitability, only enough for completing a double-layered robe should be given. It is proper to give a double-layered robe even to one who says, 'Not receiving it, I will wear a single-layered one.' But it should not be given to a bhikkhu who is of a greedy nature. Nor should it be accepted by him thinking, 'Having spread the Kathina, I will afterwards un-stitch it and make two robes.' But to the bhikkhu to whom it is given—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, idaṃ saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppannaṃ, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dadeyya kathinaṃ attharituṃ, esā ñatti.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This kathina-cloth has arisen for the Sangha. If the proper time has come for the Sangha, the Sangha should give this kathina-cloth to the bhikkhu of such-and-such a name for spreading the Kathina. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu [M 0.0299] me, bhante, saṅgho, idaṃ saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppannaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno deti kathinaṃ attharituṃ, yassāyasmato khamati imassa kathinadussassa itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dānaṃ kathinaṃ attharituṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This kathina-cloth has arisen for the Sangha. The Sangha gives this kathina-cloth to the bhikkhu of such-and-such a name for spreading the Kathina. Whichever venerable one approves of the giving of this kathina-cloth to the bhikkhu of such-and-such a name for spreading the Kathina, he should be silent. Whomever does not approve, he should speak.

“Dinnaṃ idaṃ saṅghena kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno kathinaṃ attharituṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti (mahāva. 307) –

“This kathina-cloth has been given by the Sangha to the bhikkhu of such-and-such a name for spreading the Kathina. The Sangha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I bear this in mind.”

Evaṃ dutiyakammavācāya dātabbaṃ.

Thus, it should be given by a formal act with the motion second.

Evaṃ dinne pana kathine sace taṃ kathinadussaṃ niṭṭhitaparikammameva hoti, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce niṭṭhitaparikammaṃ hoti, “ahaṃ thero”ti vā “bahussuto”ti vā ekenapi akātuṃ na labbhati[V 0.0278], sabbeheva sannipatitvā dhovanasibbanarajanāni niṭṭhāpetabbāni. Idañhi kathinavattaṃ nāma buddhappasatthaṃ. Atīte padumuttaropi bhagavā kathinavattaṃ akāsi. Tassa kira aggasāvako sujātatthero nāma kathinaṃ gaṇhi. Taṃ satthā aṭṭhasaṭṭhiyā bhikkhusatasahassehi saddhiṃ nisīditvā akāsi.

But when the Kathina has been given in this way, if that Kathina cloth is already fully prepared, that is skillful. If it is not fully prepared, no one—whether saying, ‘I am a senior,’ or, ‘I am learned’—is allowed to abstain from the work; all must gather together to complete the washing, sewing, and dyeing. For this duty concerning the Kathina is praised by the Buddhas. In the past, the Blessed One Padumuttara also performed the Kathina duty. It is said that his chief disciple, the Elder named Sujāta, received the Kathina. The Teacher performed it, having sat down together with 6,800,000 bhikkhus.

Katapariyositaṃ pana kathinaṃ gahetvā atthārakena bhikkhunā sace saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharitukāmo hoti, porāṇikā saṅghāṭi paccuddharitabbā, navā saṅghāṭi adhiṭṭhātabbā, “imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”ti vācā bhinditabbā. Sace uttarāsaṅgena kathinaṃ attharitukāmo hoti, porāṇako uttarāsaṅgo paccuddharitabbo, navo uttarāsaṅgo adhiṭṭhātabbo, “iminā uttarāsaṅgena kathinaṃ attharāmī”ti vācā bhinditabbā. Sace antaravāsakena kathinaṃ attharitukāmo hoti, porāṇako antaravāsako paccuddharitabbo, navo antaravāsako adhiṭṭhātabbo, “iminā antaravāsakena kathinaṃ attharāmī”ti vācā bhinditabbā.

But, having taken the finished Kathina cloth, if the bhikkhu who is the spreader wishes to spread the Kathina with the outer robe, the old outer robe should be disowned, the new outer robe should be determined, and the words, ‘I spread the Kathina with this outer robe,’ should be uttered. If he wishes to spread the Kathina with the upper robe, the old upper robe should be disowned, the new upper robe should be determined, and the words, ‘I spread the Kathina with this upper robe,’ should be uttered. If he wishes to spread the Kathina with the lower robe, the old lower robe should be disowned, the new lower robe should be determined, and the words, ‘I spread the Kathina with this lower robe,’ should be uttered.

Tena (pari. 413) kathinatthārakena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo “atthataṃ, bhante, saṅghassa kathinaṃ, dhammiko kathinatthāro, anumodathā”ti. Tehi anumodakehi [M 0.0300] bhikkhūhi ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo “atthataṃ, āvuso, saṅghassa kathinaṃ, dhammiko kathinatthāro, anumodāmā”ti. Tena kathinatthārakena bhikkhunā sambahule bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo “atthataṃ, bhante, saṅghassa kathinaṃ, dhammiko kathinatthāro, anumodathā”ti. Tehi anumodakehi bhikkhūhi ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo “atthataṃ, āvuso, saṅghassa kathinaṃ, dhammiko kathinatthāro, anumodāmā”ti. Tena kathinatthārakena bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo “atthataṃ, āvuso, saṅghassa kathinaṃ, dhammiko kathinatthāro, anumodāhī”ti. Tena anumodakena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo “atthataṃ, āvuso, saṅghassa kathinaṃ, dhammiko kathinatthāro, anumodāmī”ti. Evaṃ sabbesaṃ atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ parivāre “dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ atthārakassa ca anumodakassa cā”ti (pari. 403). Punapi vuttaṃ “na saṅgho kathinaṃ attharati, na gaṇo kathinaṃ attharati, puggalo kathinaṃ attharati, saṅghassa anumodanāya gaṇassa anumodanāya puggalassa attharāya saṅghassa [V 0.0279] atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, gaṇassa atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, puggalassa atthataṃ hoti kathina”nti (pari. 414).

The monk who spreads the Kathina should approach the Sangha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, raise his joined palms, and say: "Venerables, the Sangha’s Kathina is spread. The spreading of the Kathina is lawful. Please rejoice." Those rejoicing monks should arrange their upper robes over one shoulder, raise their joined palms, and say: "Friend, the Sangha’s Kathina is spread. The spreading of the Kathina is lawful. We rejoice." The monk who spreads the Kathina should approach several monks, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, raise his joined palms, and say: "Venerables, the Sangha’s Kathina is spread. The spreading of the Kathina is lawful. Please rejoice." Those rejoicing monks should arrange their upper robes over one shoulder, raise their joined palms, and say: "Friend, the Sangha’s Kathina is spread. The spreading of the Kathina is lawful. We rejoice." The monk who spreads the Kathina should approach a single monk, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, raise his joined palms, and say: "Friend, the Sangha’s Kathina is spread. The spreading of the Kathina is lawful. Please rejoice." That rejoicing monk should arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, raise his joined palms, and say: "Friend, the Sangha’s Kathina is spread. The spreading of the Kathina is lawful. I rejoice." In this way, the Kathina is spread for all. And this was stated in the Parivāra: "The Kathina is spread for two individuals: the one who spreads it and the one who rejoices." Furthermore, it is said: "The Sangha does not spread the Kathina, nor does a group spread the Kathina; an individual spreads the Kathina. Through the Sangha’s rejoicing, through the group’s rejoicing, and through the individual’s spreading, the Kathina is spread for the Sangha, the Kathina is spread for the group, and the Kathina is spread for the individual."

Evaṃ atthate pana kathine sace kathinacīvarena saddhiṃ ābhataṃ ānisaṃsaṃ dāyakā “yena amhākaṃ kathinaṃ gahitaṃ, tasseva demā”ti denti, bhikkhusaṅgho anissaro. Atha avicāretvāva datvā gacchanti, bhikkhusaṅgho issaro. Tasmā sace kathinatthārakassa sesacīvarānipi dubbalāni honti, saṅghena apaloketvā tesampi atthāya vatthāni dātabbāni, kammavācā pana ekāyeva vaṭṭati. Avasesakathinānisaṃse balavavatthāni vassāvāsikaṭhitikāya dātabbāni, ṭhitikāya abhāve therāsanato paṭṭhāya dātabbāni, garubhaṇḍaṃ na bhājetabbaṃ. Sace pana ekasīmāya bahū vihārā honti, sabbehi bhikkhūhi sannipātāpetvā ekattha kathinaṃ attharitabbaṃ, visuṃ visuṃ attharituṃ na vaṭṭati.

Thus, when the Kathina has been spread, if donors, bringing accompanying requisites together with the Kathina robe, give them saying, 'We give only to the one by whom our Kathina was accepted,' the Bhikkhu-Saṅgha has no authority. However, if they give without specifying and then depart, the Bhikkhu-Saṅgha has authority. Therefore, if the other robes of the monk who spread the Kathina are also worn out, the Saṅgha, after making an announcement, should give cloths for the sake of those robes as well; however, only a single formal motion is allowable. The remaining durable cloths among the Kathina's accompanying requisites should be distributed according to the order of the rains-residence; in the absence of such an order, they should be distributed starting from the senior-most monk. Heavy articles should not be divided. Furthermore, if there are many monasteries within a single boundary, all the bhikkhus should be made to assemble, and the Kathina should be spread in one place; it is not allowable to spread it separately.

“Atthatakathinānaṃ [M 0.0301] vo, bhikkhave, pañca kappissanti, anāmantacāro asamādānacāro gaṇabhojanaṃ yāvadatthacīvaraṃ yo ca tattha cīvaruppādo. So nesaṃ bhavissatī”ti (mahāva. 306) vacanato atthatakathinānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anāmantacārādayo pana pañcānisaṃsā labbhanti. Tattha anāmantacāroti anāmantetvā caraṇaṃ, yāva kathinaṃ na uddharīyati, tāva cārittasikkhāpadena anāpattīti vuttaṃ hoti. Asamādānacāroti cīvaraṃ asamādāya caraṇaṃ, cīvaravippavāsoti attho. Gaṇabhojananti gaṇabhojanasikkhāpadena anāpatti vuttā. Yāvadatthacīvaranti yāvatā cīvarena attho, tāvatakaṃ anadhiṭṭhitaṃ avikappitaṃ vaṭṭatīti attho. Yo ca tattha cīvaruppādoti tattha kathinatthatasīmāya matakacīvaraṃ vā hotu saṅghaṃ uddissa dinnaṃ vā saṅghikena tatruppādena ābhataṃ vā, yena kenaci ākārena yaṃ saṅghikaṃ cīvaraṃ uppajjati, taṃ tesaṃ bhavissatīti attho.

Because of the statement: 'Bhikkhus, for you who have spread the Kathina, five things will be allowable: going about without taking leave, going about without the three robes, group meals, as many robes as are needed, and whatever robe-material arises there, that will be for them' (Mahāvagga 306), the five advantages, beginning with 'going about without taking leave,' are obtained by the bhikkhus who have spread the Kathina. Therein, 'going about without taking leave' means going about without informing; as long as the Kathina is not withdrawn, it is said that there is no offense under the training rule on conduct. 'Going about without the three robes' means going about without taking the robes; the meaning is that separation from one's robes is allowable. 'Group meals' means that no offense is stated under the training rule on group meals. 'As many robes as are needed' means that as many robes as are required are allowable, even if undetermined and not made into shared property; this is the meaning. 'And whatever robe-material arises there' means that within that boundary where the Kathina was spread, whether it be the robe of a deceased bhikkhu, or a robe given with the Saṅgha as the intended recipient, or a robe brought with income belonging to the Saṅgha that arose there—whatever robe belonging to the Saṅgha arises in any way, that will be for them; this is the meaning.

Iti pāḷimuttakavinayavinicchayasaṅgahe

Thus, in the Compilation of Vinaya Judgments outside the Pāḷi Canon,

Kathinatthāravinicchayakathā samattā.

The discourse on the decision regarding the spreading of the Kathina is concluded.

30. Garubhaṇḍavinicchayakathā

30. The Discourse on the Decision Regarding Heavy Articles

227. Garubhaṇḍānīti [V 0.0280] ettha “pañcimāni, bhikkhave, avissajjiyāni na vissajjetabbāni saṅghena vā gaṇena vā puggalena vā, vissajjitānipi avissajjitāni honti, yo vissajjeyya, āpatti thullaccayassā”tiādinā (cūḷava. 321) nayena dassitāni ārāmo ārāmavatthu, vihāro vihāravatthu, mañco pīṭhaṃ bhisi bimbohanaṃ, lohakumbhī lohabhāṇakaṃ lohavārako lohakaṭāhaṃ vāsi pharasu kuṭhārī kudālo nikhādanaṃ, valli veḷu muñjaṃ pabbajaṃ tiṇaṃ mattikā dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍanti imāni pañca garubhaṇḍāni nāma.

227. Herein, the heavy articles are shown by the method beginning with: “Bhikkhus, these five things are not to be relinquished; they should not be relinquished by the Saṅgha, by a group, or by an individual. Even if relinquished, they are not [considered] relinquished. Whoever should relinquish them commits an offense of grave transgression.” These five [groups of] things are called heavy articles, namely: a park, park land; a dwelling, dwelling land; a couch, a chair, a mattress, a pillow; a bronze pot, a large bronze vessel, a bronze water pot, a bronze cauldron, an adze, an axe, a hatchet, a spade, a chisel; a creeper, bamboo, muñja grass, pabbaja grass, ordinary grass, clay, wooden articles, and earthenware articles.

Tattha (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 321) ārāmo nāma pupphārāmo vā phalārāmo vā. Ārāmavatthu nāma tesaṃyeva ārāmānaṃ atthāya paricchinditvā ṭhapitokāso, tesu vā ārāmesu vinaṭṭhesu tesaṃ porāṇakabhūmibhāgo. Vihāro [M 0.0302] nāma yaṃ kiñci pāsādādi senāsanaṃ. Vihāravatthu nāma tassa patiṭṭhānokāso. Mañco nāma masārako bundikābaddho kuḷīrapādako āhaccapādakoti imesaṃ catunnaṃ mañcānaṃ aññataro. Pīṭhaṃ nāma masārakādīnaṃyeva catunnaṃ pīṭhānaṃ aññataraṃ. Bhisi nāma uṇṇabhisiādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ aññatarā. Bimbohanaṃ nāma rukkhatūlalatātūlapoṭakītūlānaṃ aññataraṃ. Lohakumbhī nāma kāḷalohena vā tambalohena vā yena kenaci lohena katakumbhī. Lohabhāṇakādīsupi eseva nayo. Ettha pana bhāṇakanti arañjaro vuccati. Vārakoti ghaṭo. Kaṭāhaṃ kaṭāhameva. Vāsiādīsu valliādīsu ca duviññeyyaṃ nāma natthi. Pañcāti ca rāsivasena vuttaṃ, sarūpavasena panetāni pañcavīsatividhāni honti. Vuttañhetaṃ –

Herein, 'park' refers to a flower park or a fruit park. 'Park land' refers to the space demarcated and set aside for those very parks, or, if those parks are destroyed, the ancient portion of their land. 'Dwelling' refers to any lodging such as a storied building, etc. 'Dwelling land' refers to its foundation site. 'Couch' refers to any one of these four types of couches: masāraka, bundikābaddha, kuḷīrapādaka, or āhaccapādaka. 'Chair' refers to any one of the four types of chairs, such as the masāraka, etc. 'Mattress' refers to any one of the five types, such as a wool-stuffed mattress, etc. 'Pillow' refers to any one [stuffed with] tree-cotton, creeper-cotton, or pōṭakī-cotton. 'Bronze pot' refers to a pot made of any metal, whether black bronze or red bronze (copper). The same method applies to 'bronze vessel,' etc. Here, however, 'bhāṇaka' is called an 'arañjara.' 'Vāraka' is a 'ghaṭa' (water pot). A 'kaṭāha' is simply a cauldron. Regarding 'adze,' etc., and 'creeper,' etc., there is nothing difficult to understand. The term 'five' is stated by way of groups, but in terms of their individual forms, these are of twenty-five kinds. For it is said:

“Dvisaṅgahāni dve honti, tatiyaṃ catusaṅgahaṃ;

Catutthaṃ navakoṭṭhāsaṃ, pañcamaṃ aṭṭhabhedanaṃ.

Two are grouped as two, the third as fourfold; the fourth has nine sections, the fifth has an eightfold division.

“Iti pañcahi rāsīhi, pañcanimmalalocano;

Pañcavīsavidhaṃ nātho, garubhaṇḍaṃ pakāsayī”ti.

Thus, with five classes, the Lord, endowed with the five stainless eyes, declared the twenty-five kinds of heavy articles.

Tatrāyaṃ [V 0.0281] vinicchayakathā – idañhi sabbampi garubhaṇḍaṃ senāsanakkhandhake “avissajjiya”nti vuttaṃ, kīṭāgirivatthusmiṃ “avebhaṅgiya”nti dassitaṃ, parivāre pana –

Herein is the discourse on the determination: Indeed, all these heavy articles are said to be 'not to be relinquished' in the Senāsanakkhandhaka, and shown to be 'not to be divided' in the story of Kīṭāgiri; but in the Parivāra—

“Avissajjiyaṃ avebhaṅgiyaṃ,

Pañca vuttā mahesinā;

Vissajjentassa paribhuñjantassa anāpatti,

Pañhāmesā kusalehi cintitā”ti. (pari. 479) –

'Not to be relinquished, not to be divided—five have been spoken of by the Great Sage. For one who relinquishes or makes use of them, there is no offense. This is a question considered by the skillful.'

Āgataṃ. Tasmā mūlacchejjavasena avissajjiyañca avebhaṅgiyañca, parivattanavasena pana vissajjentassa paribhuñjantassa ca anāpattīti evamettha adhippāyo veditabbo.

It is so stated. Therefore, by way of permanent disposal, they are both not to be relinquished and not to be divided; but by way of exchange, for one who relinquishes and for one who makes use of them, there is no offense—thus should the meaning here be understood.

228. Tatrāyaṃ anupubbikathā – idaṃ tāva pañcavidhampi cīvarapiṇḍapātabhesajjatthāya upanetuṃ na vaṭṭati, thāvarena ca thāvaraṃ, garubhaṇḍena ca garubhaṇḍaṃ parivattetuṃ vaṭṭati. Thāvare pana khettaṃ vatthu taḷākaṃ mātikāti evarūpaṃ [M 0.0303] bhikkhusaṅghassa vicāretuṃ vā sampaṭicchituṃ vā adhivāsetuṃ vā na vaṭṭati, kappiyakārakeheva vicāritato kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ vaṭṭati. Ārāmena pana ārāmaṃ ārāmavatthuṃ vihāraṃ vihāravatthunti imāni cattāripi parivattetuṃ vaṭṭati.

228. Herein is the discourse in due order: Firstly, it is not allowable to apply these five kinds of heavy articles for the purpose of robes, alms-food, or medicine. It is, however, allowable to exchange immovable property for immovable property, and heavy articles for heavy articles. But concerning immovable property—such as a field, a site, a reservoir, or a water-channel—it is not allowable for the Saṅgha of bhikkhus to manage, accept, or consent to such things. An allowable item is permissible only after it has been managed by allowable stewards. It is, however, allowable to exchange these four: a park for a park, a park site for a park site, a dwelling for a dwelling, and a dwelling site for a dwelling site.

Tatrāyaṃ parivattananayo – saṅghassa nāḷikerārāmo dūre hoti, kappiyakārakā bahutaraṃ khādanti, yampi na khādanti, tato sakaṭavetanaṃ datvā appameva āharanti, aññesaṃ pana tassa ārāmassa avidūre gāmavāsīnaṃ manussānaṃ vihārassa samīpe ārāmo hoti, te saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā sakena ārāmena taṃ ārāmaṃ yācanti, saṅghena “ruccati saṅghassā”ti apaloketvā sampaṭicchitabbo. Sacepi bhikkhūnaṃ rukkhasahassaṃ hoti, manussānaṃ pañca satāni, “tumhākaṃ ārāmo khuddako”ti na vattabbaṃ. Kiñcāpi hi ayaṃ khuddako, atha kho itarato bahutaraṃ āyaṃ deti. Sacepi samakameva deti, evampi icchiticchitakkhaṇe paribhuñjituṃ sakkāti gahetabbameva. Sace pana manussānaṃ bahutarā rukkhā honti, “nanu tumhākaṃ bahutarā rukkhā”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace “atirekaṃ amhākaṃ puññaṃ hotu, saṅghassa demā”ti vadanti, jānāpetvā sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭati. Bhikkhūnaṃ rukkhā phaladhārino, manussānaṃ rukkhā na tāva phalaṃ gaṇhanti, kiñcāpi na gaṇhanti, “na cirena gaṇhissantī”ti sampaṭicchitabbameva. Manussānaṃ rukkhā phaladhārino, bhikkhūnaṃ rukkhā na tāva phalaṃ gaṇhanti, “nanu tumhākaṃ rukkhā phaladhārino”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace “gaṇhatha, bhante, amhākaṃ puññaṃ bhavissatī”ti [V 0.0282] denti, jānāpetvā sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭati. Evaṃ ārāmena ārāmo parivattetabbo. Eteneva nayena ārāmavatthupi vihāropi vihāravatthupi ārāmena parivattetabbaṃ, ārāmavatthunā ca mahantena vā khuddakena vā ārāmaārāmavatthuvihāravihāravatthūni.

In this matter, this is the method of exchange: The Saṅgha's coconut grove is far away, the stewards consume a great deal, and of what they do not consume, they bring back only a little after paying the cart fare. However, other people, villagers living not far from that grove, have a grove near the monastery. They approach the Saṅgha and request that grove in exchange for their own. After seeking approval with the formula, 'It is agreeable to the Saṅgha,' it should be accepted by the Saṅgha. Even if the bhikkhus have a thousand trees and the people have five hundred, it should not be said, 'Your grove is small.' For although this one is small, it yields much more revenue than the other. Even if it yields the same, it should still be taken, thinking, 'It can be used whenever desired.' But if the people have more trees, it should be said, 'Do you not have more trees?' If they say, 'Let the excess be for our merit; we give it to the Saṅgha,' it is proper to accept after informing the Saṅgha. If the bhikkhus’ trees are fruit-bearing, but the people’s trees do not yet bear fruit—even if they do not—it should still be accepted, thinking, 'They will bear fruit before long.' If the people’s trees are fruit-bearing, but the bhikkhus’ trees do not yet bear fruit, it should be said, 'Are not your trees fruit-bearing?' If they say, 'Venerable sirs, please take it; it will be for our merit,' it is proper to accept after informing the Saṅgha. In this way, a grove should be exchanged for a grove. By this same method, grove-land, a monastery, or monastery-land should be exchanged for a grove; and with grove-land, groves, grove-lands, monasteries, and monastery-lands, whether large or small, should be exchanged.

Kathaṃ vihārena vihāro parivattetabbo? Saṅghassa antogāme gehaṃ hoti, manussānaṃ vihāramajjhe pāsādo hoti, ubhopi agghena samakā, sace manussā tena pāsādena taṃ gehaṃ yācanti, sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭati. Bhikkhūnaṃ ce mahagghataraṃ gehaṃ hoti, “mahagghataraṃ amhākaṃ geha”nti vutte ca “kiñcāpi mahagghataraṃ pabbajitānaṃ asāruppaṃ, na [M 0.0304] sakkā tattha pabbajitehi vasituṃ, idaṃ pana sāruppaṃ, gaṇhathā”ti vadanti, evampi sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭati. Sace pana manussānaṃ mahagghaṃ hoti, “nanu tumhākaṃ gehaṃ mahaggha”nti vattabbaṃ. “Hotu, bhante, amhākaṃ puññaṃ bhavissati, gaṇhathā”ti vutte pana sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭati. Evampi vihārena vihāro parivattetabbo. Eteneva nayena vihāravatthupi ārāmopi ārāmavatthupi vihārena parivattetabbaṃ, vihāravatthunā ca mahagghena vā appagghena vā vihāravihāravatthuārāmaārāmavatthūni. Evaṃ thāvarena thāvaraparivattanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

How should a dwelling be exchanged for a dwelling? If the Saṅgha has a house within the village, and laypeople have a mansion in the middle of the monastery, and both are of equal value, if the laypeople ask for that house in exchange for the mansion, it is proper to accept. If the bhikkhus’ house is more valuable, and when it is said, “Our house is more valuable,” if the laypeople say, “Although it is more valuable, it is unsuitable for renunciants; renunciants cannot live there. But this is suitable, please take it,” then it is also proper to accept. But if the laypeople’s mansion is more valuable, it should be said, “Is not your mansion more valuable?” If they say, “Venerable sirs, let it be; it will be merit for us; please take it,” then it is proper to accept. In this way, a dwelling should be exchanged for a dwelling. By this same method, dwelling-land, a grove, or grove-land should be exchanged for a dwelling; and with dwelling-land, dwellings, dwelling-land, groves, and grove-land, whether of greater or lesser value, should be exchanged. Thus, the exchange of one immovable property for another should be understood.

Garubhaṇḍena garubhaṇḍaparivattane pana mañcapīṭhaṃ mahantaṃ vā hotu khuddakaṃ vā, antamaso caturaṅgulapādakaṃ gāmadārakehi paṃsvāgārakesu kīḷantehi katampi saṅghassa dinnakālato paṭṭhāya garubhaṇḍaṃ hoti. Sacepi rājarājamahāmattādayo ekappahāreneva mañcasataṃ vā mañcasahassaṃ vā denti, sabbe kappiyamañcā sampaṭicchitabbā, sampaṭicchitvā “vuḍḍhapaṭipāṭiyā saṅghikaparibhogena paribhuñjathā”ti dātabbā, puggalikavasena na dātabbā. Atirekamañce bhaṇḍāgārādīsu paññapetvā pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitumpi vaṭṭati. Bahisīmāya “saṅghassa demā”ti dinnamañco saṅghattherassa vasanaṭṭhāne dātabbo. Tattha ce bahū mañcā honti, mañcena kammaṃ natthi. Yassa vasanaṭṭhāne kammaṃ atthi, tattha “saṅghikaparibhogena paribhuñjathā”ti dātabbo. Mahagghena satagghanakena vā sahassagghanakena vā mañcena aññaṃ mañcasataṃ labhati, parivattetvā gahetabbaṃ. Na kevalaṃ mañcena mañcoyeva, ārāmaārāmavatthuvihāravihāravatthupīṭhabhisibimbohanānipi parivattetuṃ vaṭṭanti. Esa nayo pīṭhabhisibimbohanesupi. Etesu pana akappiyaṃ na paribhuñjitabbaṃ, kappiyaṃ saṅghikaparibhogena paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Akappiyaṃ vā mahagghaṃ kappiyaṃ vā parivattetvā vuttavatthūni gahetabbāni. Agarubhaṇḍupagaṃ pana bhisibimbohanaṃ nāma natthi.

Now, in exchanging one heavy article for another: whether a bed or a bench, be it large or small, even one with four-finger-breadth legs made by village children playing in dust-heaps, from the time it is given to the Saṅgha, it becomes a heavy article. Even if kings, royal ministers, and so forth, donate a hundred or a thousand beds at once, all allowable beds should be accepted. Having accepted them, they should be given with the instruction, 'Use them as communal property of the Saṅgha, according to seniority,' and they should not be given for individual use. It is permissible to place excess beds in storerooms and so forth, and to place bowls and robes on them. A bed given outside the boundary with the words, 'We give this to the Saṅgha,' should be given to the dwelling place of the Saṅgha's elder. If there are many beds there and there is no use for a bed, it should be given to a dwelling place where there is a use for one, with the instruction, 'Use it as communal property of the Saṅgha.' If for an expensive bed, one worth a hundred or a thousand, one obtains another hundred beds, they should be accepted through exchange. Not only may a bed be exchanged for a bed, but it is also permissible to exchange it for groves, grove-lands, monasteries, monastery-lands, benches, mattresses, and pillows. This same principle applies to benches, mattresses, and pillows. However, among these, what is unallowable should not be used; what is allowable should be used as communal property of the Saṅgha. Having exchanged an unallowable article, or a valuable allowable article, the aforementioned items should be acquired. Furthermore, there is no such thing as a mattress or pillow that is not included among heavy articles.

229. Lohakumbhī lohabhāṇakaṃ lohakaṭāhanti imāni tīṇi mahantāni vā hontu khuddakāni [V 0.0283] vā, antamaso pasatamattaudakagaṇhanakānipi garubhaṇḍāniyeva. Lohavārako pana kāḷalohatambalohavaṭṭalohakaṃsalohānaṃ yena kenaci kato sīhaḷadīpe pādagaṇhanako bhājetabbo. Pādo ca nāma magadhanāḷiyā pañcanāḷimattaṃ gaṇhāti[M 0.0305], tato atirekagaṇhanako garubhaṇḍaṃ. Imāni tāva pāḷiyaṃ āgatāni lohabhājanāni. Pāḷiyaṃ pana anāgatāni bhiṅgārapaṭiggahauḷauṅkadabbikaṭacchupātitaṭṭakasarakasamuggaaṅgārakapalladhūmakaṭacchuādīni khuddakāni vā mahantāni vā sabbāni garubhaṇḍāni. Patto ayathālakaṃ tambalohathālakanti imāni pana bhājanīyāni. Kaṃsalohavaṭṭalohabhājanavikati saṅghikaparibhogena vā gihivikaṭā vā vaṭṭati, puggalikaparibhogena na vaṭṭati. Kaṃsalohādibhājanaṃ saṅghassa dinnampi hi pārihāriyaṃ na vaṭṭati, gihivikaṭanīhāreneva paribhuñjitabbanti mahāpaccariyaṃ vuttaṃ.

229. Bronze or copper pots, large bronze or copper vessels, and bronze or copper pans—these three, whether they be large or small, even if they only hold a measure of a handful of water, are indeed heavy articles. However, a bronze or copper water-pot made of any of these—black bronze, red copper, bluish bronze, or white bronze (bell-metal)—which, in the island of Sīhaḷa, holds a pāda, is to be divided. A pāda, by the Magadhan nāḷi measure, holds five nāḷi; a vessel that holds more than that is a heavy article. These, so far, are the bronze or copper vessels that have come down in the Pāḷi. However, those not come down in the Pāḷi—such as water-pots, spittoons, water-pipes, spoons, ladles, bowls, plates, small cups, caskets, charcoal pans, incense ladles, and so forth—whether they be small or large, all are heavy articles. However, an alms-bowl, an iron plate, and a copper plate—these are to be divided. A special vessel made of white bronze (bell-metal) or bluish bronze may be used as Sangha property or as laypeoples' property, but it is not allowable for personal use. Indeed, even if a vessel of white bronze (bell-metal) or the like is given to the Sangha, it is not allowable to be carried about as a personal requisite. It should be used only in the manner of laypeoples' property being handled by them. Thus it is said in the Mahāpaccarī.

Ṭhapetvā pana bhājanavikatiṃ aññasmimpi kappiyalohabhaṇḍe añjanī añjanisalākā kaṇṇamalaharaṇī sūci paṇṇasūci khuddako pipphalako khuddakaṃ ārakaṇṭakaṃ kuñcikā tāḷaṃ kattarayaṭṭhi vedhako natthudānaṃ bhiṇḍivālo lohakūṭo lohakutti lohaguḷo lohapiṇḍi lohacakkalikaṃ aññampi vippakatalohabhaṇḍaṃ bhājanīyaṃ. Dhūmanettaphāladīparukkhadīpakapallakaolambakadīpaitthipurisatiracchānagatarūpakāni pana aññāni vā bhitticchadanakavāṭādīsu upanetabbāni antamaso lohakhilakaṃ upādāya sabbāni lohabhaṇḍāni garubhaṇḍāniyeva honti, attanā laddhānipi pariharitvā puggalikaparibhogena na paribhuñjitabbāni, saṅghikaparibhogena vā gihivikaṭāni vā vaṭṭanti. Tipubhaṇḍepi eseva nayo. Khīrapāsāṇamayāni taṭṭakasarakādīni garubhaṇḍāniyeva.

But setting aside various kinds of vessels, among other allowable metal goods are: an ointment box, an ointment stick, an ear-wax scraper, a needle, a stylus, a small knife, a small thorn-remover, a key, a lock, a walking stick, an awl, a nasal medicine applicator, a fork, an iron hammer, iron rust, an iron rod, an iron lump, an iron hoop, and any other unfinished iron goods; these are to be distributed. However, items such as a pipe for inhaling smoke, a ploughshare, a lamp stand, a lamp dish, a hanging lamp, images of women, men, or animals, or other such images to be affixed to walls, roofs, doors, and so on—up to and including an iron stake—all these iron goods are indeed heavy goods. Even if acquired personally, they are not to be carried about and used for personal enjoyment; they are allowable for the Sangha's use or as laypeople's property. For goods made of tin, this is the same method. Items made of soapstone, such as platters, drinking cups, and so forth, are indeed heavy goods.

Ghaṭako pana telabhājanaṃ vā pādagaṇhanakato atirekameva garubhaṇḍaṃ. Suvaṇṇarajatahārakūṭajātiphalikabhājanāni gihivikaṭānipi na vaṭṭanti, pageva saṅghikaparibhogena vā puggalikaparibhogena vā. Senāsanaparibhoge pana āmāsampi anāmāsampi sabbaṃ vaṭṭati.

A small pot or an oil vessel, however, is a heavy good only if it is larger than what holds a pāda. Vessels of gold, silver, jewels, or genuine crystal, even if they are laypeople's property, are not allowable; what then needs to be said of them for the Sangha's use or for personal use? However, in the use of a lodging, everything is allowable, whether it may be handled or not.

Vāsiādīsu yāya vāsiyā ṭhapetvā dantakaṭṭhacchedanaṃ vā ucchutacchanaṃ vā aññaṃ mahākammaṃ kātuṃ na sakkā, ayaṃ bhājanīyā. Tato mahantatarā yena kenaci ākārena katā vāsi garubhaṇḍameva. Pharasu pana antamaso vejjānaṃ sirāvedhanapharasupi garubhaṇḍameva. Kuṭhāriyaṃ pharasusadisoyeva vinicchayo. Yā pana āvudhasaṅkhepena katā, ayaṃ anāmāsā. Kudālo antamaso caturaṅgulamattopi garubhaṇḍameva. Nikhādanaṃ caturassamukhaṃ vā hotu doṇimukhaṃ vā vaṅkaṃ vā ujukaṃ vā, antamaso [M 0.0306] sammuñjanīdaṇḍakavedhanampi daṇḍabaddhaṃ ce, garubhaṇḍameva. Sammuñjanīdaṇḍakhaṇanakaṃ [V 0.0284] pana adaṇḍakaṃ phalamattameva. Yaṃ sakkā sipāṭikāya pakkhipitvā pariharituṃ, taṃ bhājanīyaṃ. Sikharampi nikhādaneneva saṅgahitaṃ. Yehi manussehi vihāre vāsiādīni dinnāni honti, te ce ghare daḍḍhe vā corehi vā vilutte “detha no, bhante, upakaraṇe, puna pākatike karissāmā”ti vadanti, dātabbā. Sace āharanti, na vāretabbā, anāharantāpi na codetabbā.
