For a shameless person, even if learned, due to reverence for gain, falsifies the sacred text, expounds what is not Dhamma and not Vinaya as the Teacher's Dispensation, and causes great harm to the Dispensation, even creating schisms in the Sangha or disputes in the Sangha. But a conscientious person, scrupulous and eager to train, does not falsify the sacred text even for the sake of life. They expound only the Dhamma and Vinaya, treating the Teacher’s Dispensation with reverence and establishing it. Thus, in the past, the great elders declared three times: 'In the future, the conscientious will protect it, the conscientious will protect it, the conscientious will protect it!' In this way, one who is conscientious, not abandoning or deviating from the Vinaya, through this sense of moral shame alone, stands firmly established in the Vinaya—well-established indeed.

Asaṃhīroti saṃhīro nāma yo pāḷiyaṃ vā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vā heṭṭhato vā uparito vā padapaṭipāṭiyā vā pucchiyamāno vitthunati vipphandati santiṭṭhituṃ na sakkoti, yaṃ yaṃ parena vuccati, taṃ taṃ anujānāti, sakavādaṃ chaḍḍetvā paravādaṃ gaṇhāti. Yo pana pāḷiyaṃ vā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vā heṭṭhupariyena vā padapaṭipāṭiyā vā pucchiyamāno na vitthunati na vipphandati, ekekalomaṃ saṇḍāsena gaṇhanto viya “evaṃ mayaṃ vadāma, evaṃ no ācariyā vadantī”ti vissajjeti, yamhi pāḷi ca pāḷivinicchayo ca suvaṇṇabhājane pakkhittasīhavasā viya parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ agacchanto tiṭṭhati, ayaṃ vuccati “asaṃhīro”ti.

Regarding 'unwavering': One called 'wavering' is a person who, when questioned on the Pāḷi or the commentary, from an earlier or later point, or on the sequence of words, becomes distressed and trembles, is unable to stand firm, agrees to whatever is said by another, and having abandoned their own view, adopts the other's view. But one who, when questioned on the Pāḷi or the commentary, from an earlier or later point, or on the sequence of words, does not become distressed or tremble, but answers—like one grasping each single hair with tongs—saying, 'Thus we say; thus our teachers say'; in whom the Pāḷi and the analysis of the Pāḷi stand without going to destruction or exhaustion, like lion's fat placed in a golden vessel—this one is called 'unwavering'.

Ācariyaparamparā kho panassa suggahitā hotīti theraparamparā vaṃsaparamparā assa suṭṭhu gahitā hoti. Sumanasikatāti suṭṭhu manasikatā, āvajjitamatte ujjalitapadīpo viya hoti. Sūpadhāritāti suṭṭhu upadhāritā pubbāparānusandhito atthato kāraṇato ca upadhāritā[M 0.0324]. Attanomatiṃ pahāya ācariyasuddhiyā vattā hoti, “mayhaṃ ācariyo asukācariyassa santike uggaṇhi, so asukassā”ti evaṃ sabbaṃ ācariyaparamparaṃ theravādaṅgaṃ haritvā yāva upālitthero sammāsambuddhassa santike uggaṇhīti pāpetvā ṭhapeti, tatopi āharitvā upālitthero sammāsambuddhassa santike uggaṇhi, dāsakatthero attano upajjhāyassa upālittherassa, soṇatthero attano upajjhāyassa dāsakattherassa, siggavatthero attano upajjhāyassa soṇattherassa, moggaliputtatissatthero attano upajjhāyassa siggavattherassa caṇḍavajjittherassa cāti evaṃ sabbaṃ ācariyaparamparaṃ theravādaṅgaṃ āharitvā attano ācariyaṃ pāpetvā ṭhapeti. Evaṃ uggahitā hi ācariyaparamparā suggahitā hoti. Evaṃ asakkontena pana avassaṃ dve tayo parivaṭṭā uggahetabbā. Sabbapacchimena hi nayena yathā ācariyo ācariyācariyo ca pāḷiñca paripucchañca vadanti, tathā ñātuṃ vaṭṭati.

‘The lineage of teachers is well grasped by him’ means that the succession of elders and the succession of lineage is well grasped by him. ‘Well attended to’ means thoroughly borne in mind; it is like a lamp that flares up the moment one reflects. ‘Well retained’ means well remembered, having been retained by connecting the preceding and subsequent, and by way of the meaning and the reason. Abandoning his own opinion, he speaks with the purity of the teacher: “My teacher learned from such-and-such a teacher, who learned from such-and-such a one,” thus tracing the entire lineage of teachers, a component of the Theravāda, back to the Elder Upāli, who learned in the presence of the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. From there, bringing it forward: the Elder Upāli learned in the presence of the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One; the Elder Dāsaka learned from his preceptor, the Elder Upāli; the Elder Soṇa learned from his preceptor, the Elder Dāsaka; the Elder Siggava learned from his preceptor, the Elder Soṇa; and the Elder Moggaliputtatissa learned from his preceptors, the Elder Siggava and the Elder Caṇḍavajji. Thus, bringing forth the entire lineage of teachers, a component of the Theravāda, he establishes it up to his own teacher. Indeed, a lineage of teachers learned in this way is well-grasped. However, one who is unable to do so must learn at least two or three successions. For by the most basic method, it is proper to know how the teacher and the teacher’s teacher recite the Pāḷi and the inquiry.

Imehi ca pana tīhi lakkhaṇehi samannāgatena vinayadharena vatthuvinicchayatthaṃ sannipatite saṅghe otiṇṇe vatthusmiṃ codakena ca cuditakena ca vutte vattabbe sahasā avinicchinitvāva cha ṭhānāni oloketabbāni. Katamāni cha? Vatthu oloketabbaṃ, mātikā oloketabbā, padabhājanīyaṃ oloketabbaṃ, tikaparicchedo oloketabbo, antarāpatti oloketabbā, anāpatti oloketabbāti.

Furthermore, a Vinaya-holder endowed with these three characteristics, when the Saṅgha is assembled to decide a matter, when the matter has come up, and when what should be said has been said by both the accuser and the accused, should look into six points without deciding hastily. What six? The matter (vatthu) should be looked into, the matrix (mātikā) should be looked into, the word-analysis (padabhājanīya) should be looked into, the threefold division (tikapariccheda) should be looked into, the intermediate offense (antarāpatti) should be looked into, and the non-offense (anāpatti) should be looked into.

Vatthuṃ [V 0.0301] olokentopi hi “tiṇena vā paṇṇena vā paṭicchādetvā āgantabbaṃ, na tveva naggena āgantabbaṃ, yo āgaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (pārā. 517) evaṃ ekaccaṃ āpattiṃ passati, so taṃ suttaṃ ānetvā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamessati.

Indeed, when examining the story, he sees a certain offense, thus: ‘One should come having covered oneself with grass or with leaves, but one should certainly not come naked. Whoever should come thus, there is an offense of wrong-doing.’ He, having brought that text, will settle that legal case.

Mātikaṃ olokentopi “sampajānamusāvāde pācittiya”ntiādinā (pāci. 3) nayena pañcannaṃ āpattīnaṃ aññataraṃ āpattiṃ passati, so taṃ suttaṃ ānetvā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamessati.

When examining the Mātikā, by the method beginning with, ‘In the case of intentional lying, there is a pācittiya offense,’ he sees one or another of the five offenses. He, having brought that text, will settle that legal case.

Padabhājanīyaṃ olokentopi “akkhayite sarīre methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevati, āpatti pārājikassa. Yebhuyyena khayite sarīre methunaṃ dhammaṃ [M 0.0325] paṭisevati, āpatti thullaccayassā”tiādinā (pārā. 59 atthato samānaṃ) nayena sattannaṃ āpattīnaṃ aññataraṃ āpattiṃ passati, so padabhājanīyato suttaṃ ānetvā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamessati.

When examining the Padabhājanīya, by the method beginning with, ‘If he engages in sexual intercourse with an undecayed body, there is an offense of pārājika. If he engages in sexual intercourse with a mostly decayed body, there is an offense of thullaccaya,’ he sees one or another of the seven offenses. He, having brought the text from the Padabhājanīya, will settle that legal case.

Tikaparicchedaṃ olokentopi tikasaṅghādisesaṃ vā tikapācittiyaṃ vā tikadukkaṭaṃ vā aññataraṃ vā āpattiṃ tikaparicchede passati, so tato suttaṃ ānetvā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamessati.

When examining the threefold classification, he sees in the threefold classification either a threefold saṅghādisesa, or a threefold pācittiya, or a threefold dukkaṭa, or some other offense. He, having brought the text from there, will settle that legal case.

Antarāpattiṃ olokentopi “paṭilātaṃ ukkhipati, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (pāci. 355) evaṃ yā sikkhāpadantaresu antarāpatti hoti, taṃ passati, so taṃ suttaṃ ānetvā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamessati.

When examining the intermediate offenses, he sees that intermediate offense which occurs between the training rules, thus: ‘He lifts up a folded robe; there is an offense of wrong-doing.’ He, having brought that text, will settle that legal case.

Anāpattiṃ olokentopi “anāpatti bhikkhu asādiyantassa, atheyyacittassa, na maraṇādhippāyassa, anullapanādhippāyassa, na mocanādhippāyassa asañcicca asatiyā ajānantassā”ti (pārā. 72, 136, 180, 225, 263 thokaṃ thokaṃ visadisaṃ) evaṃ tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sikkhāpade niddiṭṭhaṃ anāpattiṃ passati, so taṃ suttaṃ ānetvā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamessati.

When examining the non-offenses, he sees the non-offense pointed out in various training rules, thus: ‘There is no offense for a monk who does not consent, who is not of a thieving mind, who does not intend death, who does not intend to induce someone to speak, who does not intend to release someone from the Order, who acts unintentionally, unmindfully, or unknowingly.’ He, having brought that text, will settle that legal case.

Yo hi bhikkhu catubbidhavinayakovido tilakkhaṇasampanno imāni cha ṭhānāni oloketvā adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamessati, tassa vinicchayo appaṭivattiyo buddhena sayaṃ nisīditvā vinicchitasadiso hoti. Taṃ ce evaṃ vinicchayakusalaṃ bhikkhuṃ koci katasikkhāpadavītikkamo [V 0.0302] bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā attano kukkuccaṃ puccheyya, tena sādhukaṃ sallakkhetvā sace anāpatti hoti, “anāpattī”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace pana āpatti hoti, sā desanāgāminī ce, “desanāgāminī”ti vattabbaṃ. Vuṭṭhānagāminī ce, “vuṭṭhānagāminī”ti vattabbaṃ. Athassa pārājikacchāyā dissati, “pārājikāpattī”ti na vattabbaṃ. Kasmā? Methunadhammavītikkamo hi uttarimanussadhammavītikkamo ca oḷāriko, adinnādānamanaussaviggahavītikkamā pana sukhumā cittalahukā. Te sukhumeneva āpajjati, sukhumena rakkhati, tasmā visesena taṃvatthukaṃ kukkuccaṃ pucchiyamāno “āpattī”ti avatvā sacassa ācariyo dharati, tato tena so bhikkhu “amhākaṃ ācariyaṃ pucchā”ti pesetabbo. Sace so [M 0.0326] puna āgantvā “tumhākaṃ ācariyo suttato nayato oloketvā ‘satekiccho’ti maṃ āhā”ti vadati, tato tena so “sādhu suṭṭhu yaṃ ācariyo bhaṇati, taṃ karohī”ti vattabbo. Atha panassa ācariyo natthi, saddhiṃ uggahitatthero pana atthi, tassa santikaṃ pesetabbo “amhehi saha uggahitatthero gaṇapāmokkho, taṃ gantvā pucchā”ti. Tenapi “satekiccho”ti vinicchite “sādhu suṭṭhu tassa vacanaṃ karohī”ti vattabbo. Atha tassa saddhiṃ uggahitattheropi natthi, antevāsiko paṇḍito atthi, tassa santikaṃ pesetabbo “asukadaharaṃ gantvā pucchā”ti. Tenapi “satekiccho”ti vinicchite “sādhu suṭṭhu tassa vacanaṃ karohī”ti vattabbo. Atha daharassapi pārājikacchāyāva upaṭṭhāti, tenapi “pārājikosī”ti na vattabbo. Dullabho hi buddhuppādo, tato dullabhatarā pabbajjā ca upasampadā ca. Evaṃ pana vattabbo “vivittaṃ okāsaṃ sammajjitvā divāvihāraṃ nisīditvā sīlāni visodhetvā dvattiṃsākāraṃ tāva manasikarohī”ti. Sace tassa arogaṃ sīlaṃ, kammaṭṭhānaṃ ghaṭayati, saṅkhārā pākaṭā hutvā upaṭṭhahanti, upacārappanāppattaṃ viya cittaṃ ekaggaṃ hoti, divasaṃ atikkantampi na jānāti, so divasātikkame upaṭṭhānaṃ āgato evaṃ vattabbo “kīdisā te cittappavattī”ti. Ārocitāya ca cittapavattiyā vattabbo “pabbajjā nāma cittavisuddhatthāya, appamatto samaṇadhammaṃ karohī”ti.

A monk who is skilled in the fourfold Vinaya, endowed with the three characteristics, and who examines these six factors will settle a legal issue. His judgment is irreversible, like a decision made by the Buddha himself after sitting down to adjudicate. If a monk skilled in such judgment is approached by another monk who has transgressed a training rule and asks about his own scruples, he should carefully consider it. If there is no offense, he should say, 'There is no offense.' If there is an offense, and it is one requiring confession, he should say, 'It requires confession.' If it is one requiring rehabilitation, he should say, 'It requires rehabilitation.' But if the shadow of an offense of defeat appears, he should not say, 'It is an offense of defeat.' Why? Because the transgression of sexual intercourse and the transgression of claiming superhuman attainments are gross, whereas the transgressions of taking what is not given and of killing a human being are subtle, arising from a fickle mind. One falls into them subtly and guards against them subtly. Therefore, when questioned specifically about such a matter, without declaring it an offense, if his teacher is alive, then that monk should be sent to him, saying, 'Ask our teacher.' If that monk returns and says, 'After examining the texts and the reasoning, our teacher told me, "It is remediable,"' then he should be told, 'Good, very well. Do what the teacher says.' But if he has no teacher, yet there is an elder with whom he has studied, he should be sent to him, saying, 'Go and ask the elder who is a prominent teacher in our community.' If that elder also decides, 'It is remediable,' he should be told, 'Good, very well. Do what he says.' If there is no such elder, but there is a wise resident pupil, he should be sent to him, saying, 'Go and ask that young monk.' If the pupil also decides, 'It is remediable,' he should be told, 'Good, very well. Do what he says.' But if even to the young monk the shadow of an offense of defeat appears, he should not say, 'You have committed an offense of defeat.' For the arising of a Buddha is rare, and even rarer are the going forth and the full admission. Instead, he should be told, 'Sweep a secluded spot, sit for the day-sojourn, purify your moral precepts, and for now, reflect on the thirty-two parts of the body.' If his moral precepts are sound, his meditation subject succeeds, his formations become clear and present themselves, and his mind becomes unified as if having attained access or absorption concentration, he may not even notice the passing of a day. When he comes to the assembly after the day has passed, he should be asked, 'What was the state of your mind?' After hearing the report of his mental state, he should be told, 'The going forth is for the purification of the mind. Be heedful and practice the duties of a recluse.'

Yassa pana sīlaṃ bhinnaṃ hoti, tassa kammaṭṭhānaṃ na ghaṭayati, patodābhitunnaṃ viya cittaṃ vikampati, vippaṭisāragginā ḍayhati, tattapāsāṇe nisinno viya taṅkhaṇeyeva vuṭṭhāti. So āgato “kā te cittapavattī”ti pucchitabbo. Ārocitāya cittapavattiyā “natthi loke raho nāma pāpakammaṃ pakubbato. Sabbapaṭhamañhi pāpaṃ karonto attanā jānāti. Athassa ārakkhadevatā paracittavidū samaṇabrāhmaṇā aññā ca devatā jānanti, tvaṃyeva dāni tava sotthiṃ [V 0.0303] pariyesāhī”ti vattabbo. Evaṃ katavītikkameneva bhikkhunā sayameva āgantvā ārocite paṭipajjitabbaṃ.

However, for one whose moral precepts are broken, the meditation subject does not succeed. His mind trembles as if struck with a goad, it burns with the fire of remorse, and he rises up at that very moment as if sitting on a hot stone. When he comes, he should be asked, 'What is the state of your mind?' When the state of his mind is reported, he should be told, 'For one who commits an evil deed, there is no such thing as a secret place in the world. Indeed, one who does evil first of all knows it himself. Then his guardian deity, recluses and brahmins who know the minds of others, and other deities know it. Now, you yourself must seek your own well-being.' This is how one should proceed when a monk who has committed a transgression comes of his own accord and reports it.

235. Idāni yā sā pubbe vuttappabhedā codanā, tassāyeva sampattivipattijānanatthaṃ ādimajjhapariyosānādīnaṃ vasena vinicchayo veditabbo[M 0.0327]. Seyyathidaṃ, codanāya ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Codanāya “ahaṃ taṃ vattukāmo, karotu me āyasmā okāsa”nti evaṃ okāsakammaṃ ādi. Otiṇṇena vatthunā codetvā sāretvā vinicchayo majjhe. Āpattiyaṃ vā anāpattiyaṃ vā patiṭṭhāpanena samatho pariyosānaṃ.

235. Now, regarding that accusation with its varieties mentioned previously, its deliberation should be understood by way of its beginning, middle, and end, in order to know its success or failure. That is to say: what is the beginning of an accusation, what is the middle, and what is the end? The beginning of an accusation is the act of requesting permission, thus: 'I wish to speak to you; may the venerable one grant me leave.' The middle is the deliberation, having accused and reminded based on the matter that has been brought forward. The end is the settlement by establishing whether there is an offense or no offense.

Codanāya kati mūlāni, kati vatthūni, kati bhūmiyo? Codanāya dve mūlāni samūlikā vā amūlikā vā. Tīṇi vatthūni diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ parisaṅkitaṃ. Pañca bhūmiyo kālena vakkhāmi, no akālena, bhūtena vakkhāmi, no abhūtena, saṇhena vakkhāmi, no pharusena, atthasaṃhitena vakkhāmi, no anatthasaṃhitena, mettacitto vakkhāmi, no dosantaroti. Imāya ca pana codanāya codakena puggalena “parisuddhakāyasamācāro nu khomhī”tiādinā (pari. 436) nayena upālipañcakesu vuttesu pannarasasu dhammesu patiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Cuditakena dvīsu dhammesu patiṭṭhātabbaṃ sacce ca akuppe cāti.

How many roots are there for an accusation, how many grounds, and how many bases? For an accusation, there are two roots: well-founded or unfounded. There are three grounds: seen, heard, or suspected. There are five bases: 'I will speak at the right time, not at the wrong time; I will speak truthfully, not falsely; I will speak gently, not harshly; I will speak beneficially, not unbeneficially; I will speak with a mind of loving-kindness, not with inner malice.' Moreover, in this accusation, the accusing person should be established in the fifteen qualities mentioned in the Upāli Pentads, beginning with, 'Am I pure in bodily conduct?' The accused person should be established in two qualities: in truth and in imperturbability.

Anuvijjakena (pari. 360) ca codako pucchitabbo “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ codesi, kimhi naṃ codesi, sīlavipattiyā codesi, ācāravipattiyā codesi, diṭṭhivipattiyā codesī”ti. So ce evaṃ vadeyya “sīlavipattiyā vā codemi, ācāravipattiyā vā codemi, diṭṭhivipattiyā vā codemī”ti. So evamassa vacanīyo “jānāsi panāyasmā sīlavipattiṃ, jānāsi ācāravipattiṃ, jānāsi diṭṭhivipatti”nti. So ce evaṃ vadeyya “jānāmi kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sīlavipattiṃ, jānāmi ācāravipattiṃ, jānāmi diṭṭhivipatti”nti. So evamassa vacanīyo “katamā panāvuso, sīlavipatti, katamā ācāravipatti, katamā diṭṭhivipattī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya “cattāri pārājikāni terasa saṅghādisesā, ayaṃ sīlavipatti. Thullaccayaṃ pācittiyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ dukkaṭaṃ dubbhāsitaṃ, ayaṃ ācāravipatti. Micchādiṭṭhi antaggāhikā diṭṭhi, ayaṃ diṭṭhivipattī”ti.

The examiner should ask the accuser: “Friend, regarding this monk whom you accuse, on what grounds do you accuse him? Do you accuse him for a corruption of virtue, for a corruption of conduct, or for a corruption of view?” If he should say, “I accuse him for a corruption of virtue, or for a corruption of conduct, or for a corruption of view,” he should be addressed thus: “Venerable one, do you know corruption of virtue, do you know corruption of conduct, do you know corruption of view?” If he should say, “Friend, I know corruption of virtue, I know corruption of conduct, and I know corruption of view,” he should be addressed thus: “Friend, what then is corruption of virtue? What is corruption of conduct? What is corruption of view?” If he should say, “The four Pārājikas and the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, this is corruption of virtue. Thullaccaya, Pācittiya, Pāṭidesanīya, Dukkaṭa, and Dubbhāsita, this is corruption of conduct. Wrong view and extremist view, this is corruption of view.”

So evamassa vacanīyo “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ codesi, diṭṭhena vā codesi, sutena vā codesi, parisaṅkāya vā codesī”ti[M 0.0328]. So ce evaṃ vadeyya “diṭṭhena vā [V 0.0304] codemi, sutena vā codemi, parisaṅkāya vā codemī”ti. So evamassa vacanīyo “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ diṭṭhena codesi, kiṃ te diṭṭhaṃ, kinti te diṭṭhaṃ, kadā te diṭṭhaṃ, kattha te diṭṭhaṃ, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, thullaccayaṃ pācittiyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ dukkaṭaṃ dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, kattha cāyaṃ bhikkhu ahosi, kattha ca tvaṃ karosi, kiñca tvaṃ karosi, kiṃ ayaṃ bhikkhu karotī”ti?

He should be addressed thus: “Friend, regarding this monk whom you accuse, do you accuse him based on what has been seen, based on what has been heard, or based on suspicion?” If he should say, “I accuse him based on what has been seen, or based on what has been heard, or based on suspicion,” he should be addressed thus: “Friend, regarding this monk whom you accuse based on what has been seen, what did you see? How did you see it? When did you see it? Where did you see it? Did you see him committing a Pārājika? Did you see him committing a Saṅghādisesa? Did you see him committing a Thullaccaya, a Pācittiya, a Pāṭidesanīya, a Dukkaṭa, or a Dubbhāsita? And where was this monk? And where were you? And what were you doing? And what was this monk doing?”

So ce evaṃ vadeyya “na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ diṭṭhena codemi, apica sutena codemī”ti. So evamassa vacanīyo “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ sutena codesi, kiṃ te sutaṃ, kinti te sutaṃ, kadā te sutaṃ, kattha te sutaṃ, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannoti sutaṃ, saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpannoti sutaṃ, thullaccayaṃ pācittiyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ dukkaṭaṃ dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannoti sutaṃ, bhikkhussa sutaṃ, bhikkhuniyā sutaṃ, sikkhamānāya sutaṃ, sāmaṇerassa sutaṃ, sāmaṇeriyā sutaṃ, upāsakassa sutaṃ, upāsikāya sutaṃ, rājūnaṃ sutaṃ, rājamahāmattānaṃ sutaṃ, titthiyānaṃ sutaṃ, titthiyasāvakānaṃ suta”nti.

If he should say thus: 'Friend, I do not indeed accuse this monk based on what has been seen, but rather I accuse him based on what has been heard,' he should be spoken to thus: 'Friend, regarding your accusing this monk based on what has been heard: what was heard by you? How was it heard by you? When was it heard by you? Where was it heard by you? Was it heard that he has committed a pārājika offense? Was it heard that he has committed a saṅghādisesa offense? Was it heard that he has committed a thullaccaya, pācittiya, pāṭidesanīya, dukkaṭa, or dubbhāsita offense? Was it heard from a monk? Was it heard from a nun? Was it heard from a female probationer? Was it heard from a male novice? Was it heard from a female novice? Was it heard from a male lay follower? Was it heard from a female lay follower? Was it heard from kings? Was it heard from royal ministers? Was it heard from heretics? Was it heard from the disciples of heretics?'

So ce evaṃ vadeyya “na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ sutena codemi, apica parisaṅkāya codemī”ti. So evamassa vacanīyo “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ parisaṅkāya codesi, kiṃ parisaṅkasi, kinti parisaṅkasi, kadā parisaṅkasi, kattha parisaṅkasi? Pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannoti parisaṅkasi, saṅghādisesaṃ thullaccayaṃ pācittiyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ dukkaṭaṃ dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannoti parisaṅkasi, bhikkhussa sutvā parisaṅkasi, bhikkhuniyā sutvā…pe… titthiyasāvakānaṃ sutvā parisaṅkasī”ti.

If he should say thus: 'Friend, I do not indeed accuse this monk based on what has been heard, but rather I accuse him based on suspicion,' he should be spoken to thus: 'Friend, regarding your accusing this monk based on suspicion: what do you suspect? How do you suspect? When do you suspect? Where do you suspect? Do you suspect that he has committed a pārājika offense? Do you suspect that he has committed a saṅghādisesa, thullaccaya, pācittiya, pāṭidesanīya, dukkaṭa, or dubbhāsita offense? Do you suspect after hearing from a monk? Do you suspect after hearing from a nun… or from the disciples of heretics?'

Diṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhena sameti, diṭṭhena saṃsandate diṭṭhaṃ;

Diṭṭhaṃ paṭicca na upeti, asuddhaparisaṅkito;

So puggalo paṭiññāya, kātabbo tenuposatho.

What is seen corresponds with what is seen; what is seen accords with what is seen. If, based on what is seen, he does not fall into an offense, he is one who is groundlessly suspected. The Uposatha should be performed with that person based on his admission.

Sutaṃ sutena sameti, sutena saṃsandate sutaṃ;

Sutaṃ paṭicca na upeti, asuddhaparisaṅkito;

So puggalo paṭiññāya, kātabbo tenuposatho.

What is heard corresponds with what is heard; what is heard accords with what is heard. If, based on what is heard, he does not fall into an offense, he is one who is groundlessly suspected. The Uposatha should be performed with that person based on his admission.

Mutaṃ [M 0.0329][V 0.0305] mutena sameti, mutena saṃsandate mutaṃ;

Mutaṃ paṭicca na upeti, asuddhaparisaṅkito;

So puggalo paṭiññāya, kātabbo tenuposatho.

What is sensed corresponds with what is sensed; what is sensed accords with what is sensed. If, based on what is sensed, he does not fall into an offense, he is one who is groundlessly suspected. The Uposatha should be performed with that person based on his admission.

Paṭiññā lajjīsu katā, alajjīsu evaṃ na vijjati;

Bahumpi alajjī bhāseyya, vattānusandhitena kārayeti. (pari. 359);

An admission is accepted from the conscientious; for the shameless, this is not the case. Though a shameless one might speak much, he should be made to act by means of an admission consistent with the code of conduct.

Apicettha saṅgāmāvacarena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamantena nīcacittena saṅgho upasaṅkamitabbo rajoharaṇasamena cittena, āsanakusalena bhavitabbaṃ nisajjakusalena, there bhikkhū anupakhajjantena nave bhikkhū āsanena appaṭibāhantena yathāpatirūpe āsane nisīditabbaṃ, anānākathikena bhavitabbaṃ atiracchānakathikena, sāmaṃ vā dhammo bhāsitabbo, paro vā ajjhesitabbo, ariyo vā tuṇhībhāvo nātimaññitabbo.

Furthermore, a monk who enters the battleground of disputes, when approaching the Saṅgha, should approach the Saṅgha with a humble mind, with a mind like a dust-removing cloth. He should be skilled in seating and skilled in sitting. Without encroaching upon the elder monks, and without barring the new monks from a seat, he should sit in a suitable seat. He should not be a speaker of various talks, nor a speaker of worldly talk. He should either speak the Dhamma himself or request another to do so. Or, noble silence should not be despised.

Saṅghena anumatena puggalena anuvijjakena anuvijjitukāmena na upajjhāyo pucchitabbo, na ācariyo pucchitabbo, na saddhivihāriko pucchitabbo, na antevāsiko pucchitabbo, na samānupajjhāyako pucchitabbo, na samānācariyako pucchitabbo, na jāti pucchitabbā, na nāmaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, na gottaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, na āgamo pucchitabbo, na kulapadeso pucchitabbo, na jātibhūmi pucchitabbā. Taṃ kiṃkāraṇā? Atrassa pemaṃ vā doso vā, peme vā sati dose vā chandāpi gaccheyya dosāpi gaccheyya mohāpi gaccheyya bhayāpi gaccheyyāti.

An investigator, authorized by the Saṅgha and wishing to investigate, should not question the preceptor, should not question the teacher, should not question the co-resident, should not question the resident pupil, should not question one with the same preceptor, nor one with the same teacher. Lineage should not be asked, name should not be asked, clan should not be asked, textual tradition should not be asked, family background should not be asked, nor should birthplace be asked. For what reason? Because in this matter, there might arise affection or aversion towards him. When there is affection or aversion, one might go astray through desire, go astray through aversion, go astray through delusion, or go astray through fear.

Saṅghena anumatena puggalena anuvijjakena anuvijjitukāmena saṅghagarukena bhavitabbaṃ, no puggalagarukena, saddhammagarukena bhavitabbaṃ, no āmisagarukena, atthavasikena bhavitabbaṃ, no parisakappikena, kālena anuvijjitabbaṃ, no akālena, bhūtena anuvijjitabbaṃ, no abhūtena, saṇhena anuvijjitabbaṃ, no pharusena, atthasaṃhitena anuvijjitabbaṃ, no anatthasaṃhitena, mettacittena anuvijjitabbaṃ, no dosantarena, na upakaṇṇakajappinā bhavitabbaṃ, na jimhaṃ pekkhitabbaṃ, na akkhi nikhaṇitabbaṃ, na bhamukaṃ ukkhipitabbaṃ, na sīsaṃ ukkhipitabbaṃ, na hatthavikāro kātabbo, na hatthamuddā dassetabbā.

The person authorized by the Sangha, being an investigator who wishes to investigate, should be respectful of the Sangha, not of individuals. One should be respectful of the true Dhamma, not of material rewards. One should decide by the meaning, not by conforming to the assembly. One should investigate at a proper time, not at an improper time. One should investigate with a true matter, not with an untrue matter. One should investigate gently, not harshly. One should investigate what is beneficial, not what is unbeneficial. One should investigate with a mind of loving-kindness, not with a mind of ill-will. One should not be one who whispers near the ear, nor look for faults, nor wink the eye, nor raise the eyebrow, nor raise the head, nor make distorted hand gestures, nor show a clenched fist.

Āsanakusalena [M 0.0330] bhavitabbaṃ nisajjakusalena, yugamattaṃ pekkhantena atthaṃ anuvidhiyantena sake [V 0.0306] āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na ca āsanā vuṭṭhātabbaṃ, na vītihātabbaṃ, na kummaggo sevitabbo, na bāhāvikkhepakaṃ bhaṇitabbaṃ, aturitena bhavitabbaṃ asāhasikena, acaṇḍikatena bhavitabbaṃ vacanakkhamena, mettacittena bhavitabbaṃ hitānukampinā, kāruṇikena bhavitabbaṃ hitaparisakkinā, asamphappalāpinā bhavitabbaṃ pariyantabhāṇinā, averavasikena bhavitabbaṃ anasuruttena, attā pariggahetabbo, paro pariggahetabbo, codako pariggahetabbo, cuditako pariggahetabbo, adhammacodako pariggahetabbo, adhammacuditako pariggahetabbo, dhammacodako pariggahetabbo, dhammacuditako pariggahetabbo, vuttaṃ ahāpentena avuttaṃ appakāsentena otiṇṇāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṃ uggahetvā paro paripucchitvā yathāpaṭiññāya kāretabbo, mando hāsetabbo, bhīru assāsetabbo, caṇḍo nisedhetabbo, asuci vibhāvetabbo, ujumaddavena na chandāgati gantabbā, na dosāgati gantabbā, na mohāgati gantabbā, na bhayāgati gantabbā, majjhattena bhavitabbaṃ dhammesu ca puggalesu ca, evañca pana anuvijjako anuvijjamāno satthu ceva sāsanakaro hoti, viññūnañca sabrahmacārīnaṃ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cāti.

One should be skilled in seating and skilled in sitting posture. One should sit in one's own seat, looking at a distance of a yoke's length and considering the decided meaning. One should not rise from the seat, nor should the decision be diminished. A wrong path should not be followed. One should not speak while flailing one's arms. One should be unhurried and not reckless. One should not be harsh but be patient with unpleasant speech. One should have a mind of loving-kindness, being compassionate for the welfare of others. One should be merciful, seeking the welfare of others. One should not speak frivolous talk but speak to the very end. One should not be under the sway of enemies and should not be contentious. Oneself should be examined; others should be examined; the accuser should be examined; the accused should be examined; the unrighteous accuser should be examined; the unrighteously accused should be examined; the righteous accuser should be examined; the righteously accused should be examined. Without diminishing what has been said and without revealing what has not been said, having carefully grasped the words and phrases that have come before the Saṅgha and having questioned others, one should cause them to act according to their acknowledgement. The dull person should be gladdened; the timid person should be reassured; the harsh person should be restrained; the impure one should be made clear. The upright person should be approached with gentleness. One should not follow the wrong course of desire, the wrong course of hatred, the wrong course of delusion, or the wrong course of fear. One should be impartial in matters of the Dhamma and towards individuals. Thus, the investigator, while investigating, becomes one who carries out the Teacher's Dispensation and is dear, agreeable, respected, and to be cultivated with loving-kindness by wise fellow-monks.

Iti pāḷimuttakavinayavinicchayasaṅgahe

Thus, in the Compendium of Vinaya Judgments Independent of the Pāḷi Canon,

Codanādivinicchayakathā samattā.

The Discourse on Judgments concerning Accusations and so forth is concluded.

32. Garukāpattivuṭṭhānavinicchayakathā

32. The Discourse on the Judgment concerning Rehabilitation from Grave Offenses

236. Garukāpattivuṭṭhānanti [V 0.0307] parivāsamānattādīhi vinayakammehi garukāpattito vuṭṭhānaṃ. Tattha (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) tividho parivāso paṭicchannaparivāso suddhantaparivāso samodhānaparivāsoti. Tesu paṭicchannaparivāso tāva yathāpaṭicchannāya āpattiyā dātabbo. Kassaci hi ekāhappaṭicchannā āpatti hoti, kassaci dvīhappaṭicchannā, kassaci ekāpatti hoti, kassaci dve tisso tatuttari vā. Tasmā paṭicchannaparivāsaṃ dentena [M 0.0331] paṭhamaṃ tāva paṭicchannabhāvo jānitabbo. Ayañhi āpatti nāma dasahākārehi paṭicchannā hoti.

236. Rehabilitation from a grave offense means emerging from a grave offense through disciplinary procedures such as probation and penance. Herein, probation is threefold: concealed probation, pure-end probation, and combined probation. Among these, concealed probation is to be given according to the offense as it was concealed. For some, an offense is concealed for one day; for some, for two days. For some, it is one offense; for some, there are two, three, or more than that. Therefore, when giving concealed probation, the fact of concealment must first be known. For this offense is concealed in ten ways.

Tatrāyaṃ mātikā – āpatti ca hoti āpattisaññī ca, pakatatto ca hoti pakatattasaññī ca, anantarāyiko ca hoti anantarāyikasaññī ca, pahu ca hoti pahusaññī ca, chādetukāmo ca hoti chādeti cāti. Tattha āpatti ca hoti āpattisaññī cāti yaṃ āpanno, sā āpattiyeva hoti, sopi ca tattha āpattisaññīyeva. Iti jānanto chādeti, channā hoti, atha panāyaṃ tattha anāpattisaññī, acchannā hoti. Anāpatti pana āpattisaññāyapi anāpattisaññāyapi chādentena acchāditāva hoti, lahukaṃ vā garukāti garukaṃ vā lahukāti chādeti, alajjipakkhe tiṭṭhati, āpatti pana acchannā hoti, garukaṃ lahukāti maññamāno deseti, neva desitā hoti, na channā, garukaṃ vā garukāti ñatvā chādeti, channā hoti, garukalahukabhāvaṃ na jānāti, āpattiṃ chādemīti chādeti, channāva hoti.

Herein, this is the matrix: there is an offense and one is percipient of it as an offense; one is in a normal state and is percipient of being in a normal state; one is without impediment and is percipient of being without impediment; one is able and is percipient of being able; one desires to conceal and does conceal it. Therein, 'there is an offense and one is percipient of it as an offense' means that what one has fallen into is indeed an offense, and one is also percipient of it as an offense. Knowing thus, if one conceals it, it is concealed. But if one is not percipient of it as an offense, it is not concealed. A non-offense, however, whether one conceals it with the perception of an offense or with the perception of a non-offense, is indeed not concealed. If one conceals a minor offense as major, or a major offense as minor, one stands on the side of the shameless; the offense, however, is not concealed. If, thinking a major offense is minor, one confesses it, it is neither confessed nor concealed. If, knowing a major offense as major, one conceals it, it is concealed. If one does not know the state of being major or minor, but conceals it thinking, 'I am concealing an offense,' it is indeed concealed.

Pakatattoti tividhaṃ ukkhepanīyakammaṃ akato. So ce pakatattasaññī hutvā chādeti, channā hoti. Atha “mayhaṃ saṅghena kammaṃ kata”nti apakatattasaññī hutvā chādeti, acchannā hoti. Apakatattena pana pakatattasaññinā vā apakatattasaññinā vā chāditāpi acchannāva hoti. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

A 'pakatatta' is a monk for whom the threefold act of suspension has not been performed. If he, perceiving himself to be a 'pakatatta', conceals it, it is concealed. But if, perceiving himself not to be a 'pakatatta' and thinking, "The Saṅgha has performed an act against me," he conceals it, it is not concealed. However, for one who is not a 'pakatatta', even if he conceals it while perceiving himself to be a 'pakatatta' or not perceiving himself to be a 'pakatatta', it remains unconcealed. And this has been stated:

“Āpajjati garukaṃ sāvasesaṃ,

Chādeti anādariyaṃ paṭicca;

Na [V 0.0308] bhikkhunī no ca phuseyya vajjaṃ,

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā”ti. (pari. 481) –

"He commits a grave offense with residue; he conceals it on account of disrespect. He is not a bhikkhunī, nor does he incur the fault. This is a question to be pondered by the skilled."

Ayañhi pañho ukkhittakena kathito.

For this question was explained by a suspended monk.

Anantarāyikoti yassa dasasu antarāyesu ekopi natthi, so ce anantarāyikasaññī hutvā chādeti, channā hoti. Sacepi so bhīrujātikatāya andhakāre amanussacaṇḍamigabhayena antarāyikasaññī hutvā chādeti, acchannāva hoti. Yassapi pabbatavihāre vasantassa kandaraṃ [M 0.0332] vā nadiṃ vā atikkamitvā ārocetabbaṃ hoti, antarāmagge ca caṇḍavāḷaamanussādibhayaṃ atthi, magge ajagarā nipajjanti, nadī pūrā hoti, etasmiṃ pana satiyeva antarāye antarāyikasaññī chādeti, acchannā hoti. Antarāyikassa pana antarāyikasaññāya chādayato acchannāva.

'Anantarāyika' is one for whom there is none of the ten obstacles. If he, perceiving there is no obstacle, conceals it, it is concealed. And if that monk, due to a fearful nature, perceives an obstacle out of fear of non-human beings and fierce animals in the darkness and conceals it, it remains unconcealed. Also, for one dwelling in a mountain monastery who must cross a ravine or a river to report it, and on the way there is danger from fierce beasts, non-human beings, and so on, or pythons lie on the path, or the river is flooded—if, while this obstacle is actually present, he perceives an obstacle and conceals it, it is not concealed. For one who has an obstacle, however, if he conceals it with the perception that there is an obstacle, it remains unconcealed.

Pahūti so sakkoti bhikkhuno santikaṃ gantuñceva ārocetuñca, so ce pahusaññī hutvā chādeti, channā hoti. Sacassa mukhe appamattako gaṇḍo vā hoti, hanukavāto vā vijjhati, danto vā rujjati, bhikkhā vā mandā laddhā hoti, tāvatakena pana neva vattuṃ na sakkoti, na gantuṃ, apica kho “na sakkomī”ti saññī hoti, ayaṃ pahu hutvā appahusaññī nāma. Iminā chāditāpi acchāditā. Appahunā pana vattuṃ vā gantuṃ vā asamatthena pahusaññinā vā appahusaññinā vā chāditā hoti, acchāditāva.

'Pahu' is one who is able to go to a monk and report it. If he, perceiving himself to be able, conceals it, it is concealed. If a small boil is on his mouth, or lockjaw afflicts him, or a tooth aches, or he has received little almsfood, and because of just that much he considers himself unable to speak or go, and indeed he perceives, 'I am not able'—this one, though being able, is called 'one who perceives himself to be unable.' Even if concealed by this one, it is not concealed. But for one who is unable, being incapable of speaking or going, if he conceals it with the perception of being able or with the perception of being unable, it remains unconcealed.

Chādetukāmo ca hoti chādeti cāti idaṃ uttānatthameva. Sace pana “chādessāmī”ti dhuranikkhepaṃ katvā purebhatte vā pacchābhatte vā paṭhamayāmādīsu vā lajjidhammaṃ okkamitvā antoaruṇeyeva āroceti, ayaṃ chādetukāmo na chādeti nāma. Yassa pana abhikkhuke ṭhāne vasantassa āpajjitvā sabhāgassa bhikkhuno āgamanaṃ āgamentassa, sabhāgassa santikaṃ vā gacchantassa aḍḍhamāsopi māsopi atikkamati, ayaṃ na chādetukāmo chādeti nāma, ayampi acchannāva hoti. Yo pana āpannamattova aggiṃ akkantapuriso viya sahasā pakkamitvā sabhāgaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā āvikaroti, ayaṃ na chādetukāmova na chādeti nāma. Sace pana sabhāgaṃ disvāpi “ayaṃ me upajjhāyo vā ācariyo vā”ti lajjāya nāroceti, channāva hoti āpatti. Upajjhāyādibhāvo hi idha appamāṇaṃ, averisabhāgamattameva pamāṇaṃ. Tasmā averisabhāgassa [V 0.0309] santike ārocetabbā. Yo pana visabhāgo hoti sutvā pakāsetukāmo, evarūpassa upajjhāyassapi santike na ārocetabbā.

The phrase 'He has the desire to conceal and he conceals' is of clear meaning. But if, thinking, 'I will conceal,' he lays aside the burden and, having entered a state of shamefulness, confesses just before dawn—whether before the meal, after the meal, or during the first watch of the night and so on—this is called 'desiring to conceal but not concealing.' For a monk who, living in a place without monks, commits an offense, if half a month or a month passes while he awaits the arrival of a suitable fellow monk or while going to the presence of a suitable fellow monk, this is called 'not desiring to conceal but concealing'; this offense is also considered unconcealed. But a monk who, just after committing an offense, departs in haste like a man who has stepped on a fire, goes to a place with suitable fellow monks, and makes it manifest—this is called 'neither desiring to conceal nor concealing.' If, however, even after seeing a suitable fellow monk, he does not confess out of shame, thinking, 'This is my preceptor or my teacher,' the offense remains concealed. For here, the status of being a preceptor or teacher is not the standard; the only standard is being a suitable, non-hostile fellow monk. Therefore, one should confess in the presence of a suitable, non-hostile fellow monk. But if a monk is unsuitable and desires to publicize the matter after hearing it, one should not confess in his presence, even if he is one's preceptor.

Tattha purebhattaṃ vā āpattiṃ āpanno hotu pacchābhattaṃ vā divā vā rattiṃ vā, yāva aruṇaṃ na uggacchati, tāva ārocetabbaṃ. Uddhaste [M 0.0333] aruṇe paṭicchannā hoti, paṭicchādanapaccayā ca dukkaṭaṃ āpajjati, sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ āpannassa pana santike āvikātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Sace āvikaroti, āpatti āvikatā hoti, dukkaṭā pana na muccati. Tasmā suddhassa santike āvikātabbā. Āvikaronto ca “tuyhaṃ santike ekaṃ āpattiṃ āvikaromī”ti vā “ācikkhāmī”ti vā ārocemī”ti vā “mama ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpannabhāvaṃ jānāhī”ti vā vadatu, “ekaṃ garukāpattiṃ āvikaromī”tiādinā vā nayena vadatu, sabbehipi ākārehi appaṭicchannāva hotīti kurundiyaṃ vuttaṃ. Sace pana “lahukāpattiṃ āvikaromī”tiādinā nayena vadati, paṭicchannāva hoti. Vatthuṃ āroceti, āpattiṃ āroceti, ubhayaṃ āroceti, tividhenapi ārocitāva hoti.

In this matter, whether one has committed an offense before the meal or after the meal, during the day or at night, it should be disclosed as long as dawn has not yet risen. When dawn has risen, it becomes concealed, and due to the condition of concealment, one incurs a dukkaṭa offense. However, it is not proper to disclose it in the presence of one who has committed a similar Saṅghādisesa offense. If one does disclose it, the offense is made known, but one is not freed from the dukkaṭa offense. Therefore, it should be disclosed in the presence of one who is pure from a similar offense. And when disclosing, one may say, “In your presence, I make known one offense,” or “I declare,” or “I announce,” or “Know that I have committed one offense,” or one may say by the method of, “I make known one grave offense,” and so on—by all these modes, it is indeed not concealed, thus it is said in the Kurundī. But if one says by the method of, “I make known a minor offense,” and so on, it is indeed concealed. One discloses the basis, one discloses the offense, one discloses both—even by these three ways, it is indeed disclosed.

237. Iti imāni dasa kāraṇāni upaparikkhitvā paṭicchannaparivāsaṃ dentena paṭhamameva paṭicchannabhāvo jānitabbo, tato paṭicchannadivase ca āpattiyo ca sallakkhetvā sace ekāhappaṭicchannā hoti, “ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchanna”nti evaṃ yācāpetvā khandhake (cūḷava. 98) āgatanayeneva kammavācaṃ vatvā parivāso dātabbo. Atha dvīhatīhādipaṭicchannā hoti, “dvīhappaṭicchannaṃ, tīhappaṭicchannaṃ, catūhappaṭicchannaṃ, pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ…pe… cuddasāhappaṭicchanna”nti evaṃ yāva cuddasadivasāni divasavasena yojanā kātabbā, pañcadasadivasapaṭicchannāya “pakkhapaṭicchanna”nti yojanā kātabbā. Tato yāva ekūnatiṃsatimo divaso, tāva “atirekapakkhapaṭicchanna”nti, tato “māsapaṭicchannaṃ, atirekamāsapaṭicchannaṃ, dvemāsapaṭicchannaṃ, atirekadvemāsapaṭicchannaṃ, temāsa…pe… atirekaekādasamāsapaṭicchanna”nti evaṃ yojanā kātabbā. Saṃvacchare puṇṇe “ekasaṃvaccharapaṭicchanna”nti, tato paraṃ “atirekasaṃvaccharaṃ, dvesaṃvacchara”nti evaṃ yāva “saṭṭhisaṃvaccharaṃ, atirekasaṭṭhisaṃvaccharapaṭicchanna”nti vā tato vā bhiyyopi vatvā yojanā kātabbā.

237. Thus, having examined these ten factors, when granting probation for concealment, one must first ascertain the fact of concealment. Then, having considered the days of concealment and the offenses, if it is a one-day concealment, one should have him request, saying, “Venerable sir, I have committed one offense—a deliberate emission of semen, concealed for one day.” Having thus had him request, the probation should be granted by reciting the formal motion according to the method found in the Khandhaka. If it is a concealment of two days, three days, or so on, the phrasing should be applied according to the number of days up to fourteen days, thus: “concealed for two days,” “concealed for three days,” … up to “concealed for fourteen days.” For a fifteen-day concealment, the phrasing should be “concealed for a half-month.” Beyond that, up to the twenty-ninth day, it should be phrased as “concealed for more than a half-month.” Then, the phrasing should be applied thus: “concealed for a month,” “concealed for more than a month,” “concealed for two months,” “concealed for more than two months,” … up to “concealed for more than eleven months.” When a full year is completed, it should be phrased as “concealed for one year.” Beyond that, “concealed for more than a year,” “concealed for two years,” up to “concealed for sixty years,” “concealed for more than sixty years,” or even more—the phrasing should be applied accordingly.

Sace pana dve tisso tatuttari vā āpattiyo honti, yathā “ekaṃ āpatti”nti vuttaṃ, evaṃ “dve āpattiyo, tisso āpattiyo”ti vattabbaṃ. Tato paraṃ pana sataṃ vā hotu sahassaṃ vā[V 0.0310], “sambahulā”ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Nānāvatthukāsupi “ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā [M 0.0334] āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ, ekaṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ, ekaṃ duṭṭhullavācaṃ, ekaṃ attakāmaṃ, ekaṃ sañcarittaṃ, ekāhappaṭicchannāyo”ti evaṃ gaṇanavasena vā “ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ nānāvatthukā ekāhappaṭicchannāyo”ti evaṃ vatthukittanavasena vā “ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannāyo”ti evaṃ nāmamattavasena vā yojanā kātabbā. Tattha nāmaṃ duvidhaṃ sajātisādhāraṇaṃ sabbasādhāraṇañca. Tattha saṅghādisesoti sajātisādhāraṇaṃ. Āpattīti sabbasādhāraṇaṃ. Tasmā “sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannāyo”ti evaṃ sabbasādhāraṇanāmavasenapi vaṭṭati. Idañhi parivāsādivinayakammaṃ vatthuvasena gottavasena nāmavasena āpattivasena ca kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

If, however, there are two or three offenses, or more than that, then just as it was said 'one offense,' so too it should be said, 'two offenses, three offenses.' Beyond that, however, whether there be a hundred or a thousand, it is proper to say 'numerous.' Even for offenses with various grounds, the phrasing should be made either by way of enumeration, thus: 'Venerable sir, I have committed numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses: one of emission of semen, one of bodily contact, one of lewd speech, one of serving for one's own desire, one of acting as a go-between, concealed for one day'; or by way of stating the grounds, thus: 'Venerable sir, I have committed numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses with various grounds, concealed for one day'; or by way of the name only, thus: 'Venerable sir, I have committed numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for one day.' Therein, the name is twofold: that which is common to its own class and that which is common to all. Therein, 'Saṅghādisesa' is common to its own class. 'Offense' is common to all. Therefore, it is also proper to say, by way of the name common to all, thus: 'I have committed numerous offenses, concealed for one day.' Indeed, this disciplinary act, such as probation and so forth, is certainly proper to perform based on the ground, the class, the name, and the offense.

Tattha sukkavissaṭṭhīti vatthu ceva gottañca. Saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca. Tattha “sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ kāyasaṃsagga”ntiādinā vacanenapi “nānāvatthukāyo”ti vacanenapi vatthu ceva gottañca gahitaṃ hoti. “Saṅghādiseso”ti vacanenapi “āpattiyo”ti vacanenapi nāmañceva āpatti ca gahitā hoti. Tasmā etesu yassa kassaci vasena kammavācā kātabbā. Idha pana sabbāpattīnaṃ sādhāraṇavasena sambahulanayeneva ca sabbattha kammavācaṃ yojetvā dassayissāma. Ekañhi āpattiṃ āpajjitvā “sambahulā”ti vinayakammaṃ karontassapi vuṭṭhāti ekaṃ vinā sambahulānaṃ abhāvato. Sambahulā pana āpajjitvā “ekaṃ āpajji”nti karontassa na vuṭṭhāti, tasmā sambahulanayeneva yojayissāma. Seyyathidaṃ – paṭicchannaparivāsaṃ dentena sace ekāhappaṭicchannā āpatti hoti.

Therein, 'emission of semen' is both the ground and the class. 'Saṅghādisesa' is both the name and the offense. Therein, by the statement beginning with 'emission of semen, bodily contact,' and by the statement 'of various grounds,' both the ground and the class are taken. By the statement 'Saṅghādisesa' and by the statement 'offenses,' both the name and the offense are taken. Therefore, among these, the formal act should be performed by way of any one of them whatsoever. Here, however, we will show the application of the formal act in all cases by way of what is common to all offenses and by the method of 'numerous.' Indeed, even for one who, having committed a single offense, performs the disciplinary act saying 'numerous,' there is rehabilitation, because without one, there are no 'numerous.' But for one who, having committed numerous offenses, performs the act saying 'I have committed one,' there is no rehabilitation. Therefore, we will apply it only by the method of 'numerous.' As follows: if, when granting concealed probation, there is an offense concealed for one day.

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yācāmi. Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, dutiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yācāmi. Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannāyo[M 0.0335], tatiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yācāmīti –

“Venerable sirs, I have committed numerous offenses concealed for one day; I, venerable sirs, ask the Saṅgha for one day's probation for numerous offenses concealed for one day. Venerable sirs, I have committed numerous offenses concealed for one day; for a second time, venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha for one day's probation for numerous offenses concealed for one day. Venerable sirs, I have committed numerous offenses concealed for one day; for a third time, venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha for one day's probation for numerous offenses concealed for one day.”

Evaṃ tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having had him request thus three times—

“Suṇātu [V 0.0311] me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed numerous offenses concealed for one day. He asks the Saṅgha for a one-day probation for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant to the monk, named so-and-so, a one-day probation for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed numerous offenses concealed for one day. He asks the Saṅgha for a one-day probation for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. The Saṅgha grants to the monk, named so-and-so, a one-day probation for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. Whichever venerable one agrees with the granting of a one-day probation for numerous offenses concealed for one day to the monk named so-and-so, he should remain silent. Whomever does not agree, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“For a second time I speak on this matter… For a third time I speak on this matter…

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāso, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

“A one-day probation for numerous offenses concealed for one day has been granted by the Saṅgha to the monk named so-and-so. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I hold this.”

Evaṃ yo yo āpanno hoti, tassa tassa nāmaṃ gahetvā kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus, for each and every monk who has committed an offense, the formal act should be performed by taking the name of each one.

Kammavācāpariyosāne ca tena bhikkhunā māḷakasīmāyameva “parivāsaṃ samādiyāmi, vattaṃ samādiyāmī”ti vattaṃ samādātabbaṃ, samādiyitvā tattheva saṅghassa ārocetabbaṃ. Ārocentena ca –

And at the conclusion of the formal act, the duties should be undertaken by that monk within the hall-boundary itself, saying, 'I undertake probation, I undertake the duties.' Having undertaken them, he should announce it to the Saṅgha right there. And when announcing, he should say:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ [M 0.0336] ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasāmi, vediyāmahaṃ, bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti –

“Venerable sirs, I have committed numerous offenses concealed for one day. I requested the Saṅgha for a one-day probation for numerous offenses concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted me a one-day probation for numerous offenses concealed for one day. I am undergoing probation. I make it known, venerable sirs; may the Saṅgha remember me as one who makes it known.”

Evaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Imañca atthaṃ gahetvā yāya kāyaci vācāya ārocetuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

Thus it should be announced. And having grasped this meaning, it is certainly proper to announce it in any language whatsoever.

Ārocetvā [V 0.0312] (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) sace nikkhipitukāmo hoti, “parivāsaṃ nikkhipāmi, vattaṃ nikkhipāmī”ti nikkhipitabbaṃ. Ekapadenapi cettha nikkhitto hoti parivāso, dvīhi pana sunikkhittoyeva. Samādānepi eseva nayo. Nikkhittakālato paṭṭhāya pakatattaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati. Māḷakato bhikkhūsu nikkhantesu ekassapi santike nikkhipituṃ vaṭṭati, māḷakato nikkhamitvā satiṃ paṭilabhantena sahagacchantassa santike nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace sopi pakkanto, aññassa yassa māḷake nārocitaṃ, tassa ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ. Ārocentena ca avasāne “vediyatīti maṃ āyasmā dhāretū”ti vattabbaṃ. Dvinnaṃ ārocentena “āyasmantā dhārentū”ti, tiṇṇaṃ ārocentena “āyasmanto dhārentū”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace appabhikkhuko vihāro hoti, sabhāgā bhikkhū vasanti, vattaṃ anikkhipitvā vihāreyeva rattipariggaho kātabbo. Atha na sakkā sodhetuṃ, vuttanayeneva vattaṃ nikkhipitvā paccūsasamaye ekena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepato, aparikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānato dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā mahāmaggato okkamma gumbena vā vatiyā vā paṭicchannaṭṭhāne nisīditabbaṃ, antoaruṇeyeva vuttanayena vattaṃ samādiyitvā ārocetabbaṃ. Ārocentena sace navakataro hoti, “āvuso”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace vuḍḍhataro, “bhante”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace añño koci bhikkhu kenacideva karaṇīyena taṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchati, sace esa taṃ passati, saddaṃ vāssa suṇāti, ārocetabbaṃ, anārocentassa ratticchedo ceva vattabhedo ca. Atha dvādasahatthaṃ upacāraṃ okkamitvā ajānantasseva gacchati, ratticchedo hotiyeva, vattabhedo pana natthi, uggate aruṇe vattaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace so bhikkhu kenacideva karaṇīyena pakkanto hoti, yaṃ aññaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ passati, tassa ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ. Vihāraṃ gantvāpi yaṃ paṭhamaṃ passati, tassa ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ. Ayaṃ nikkhittavattassa parihāro.

Having announced, if one wishes to set aside the probation, it should be set aside by saying, 'I set aside the probation, I set aside the observance.' Here, the probation is set aside even with a single phrase, but with two phrases, it is well set aside. This is also the method when undertaking it. From the time it is set aside, one stands in the state of a normal monk. When the monks have departed from the sīmā, it is allowable to set it aside in the presence of even one monk. Having departed from the sīmā, a monk who regains mindfulness should set it aside in the presence of a monk accompanying him. If that monk has also departed, one should announce it to another monk who was not informed within the sīmā and then set it aside. And when announcing, at the end, one should say: 'May the venerable one bear in mind that this is being made known.' When announcing to two, one should say: 'May the venerable ones bear in mind.' When announcing to three, one should say: 'May the venerable ones bear in mind.' If it is a monastery with few monks and monks of a similar standing reside there, the counting of the nights should be done right in the monastery without setting aside the observance. Then, if it is not possible to purify, having set aside the observance by the method already stated, at the time of early dawn, together with one monk, one should sit in a concealed place, such as by a bush or a fence, having gone beyond two clod-throws from the enclosure of an enclosed monastery, or from the place suitable for an enclosure of an unenclosed monastery, and having stepped off the main road. Then, within the dawn period, having undertaken the observance by the method stated, it should be announced. When announcing, if the other is more junior, one should say, 'Friend.' If more senior, one should say, 'Venerable sir.' If some other monk comes to that place for some reason, and if this one sees him or hears his sound, it should be announced. For one who does not announce, there is a breaking of the night and a breach of the observance. Then, if he departs without one's knowledge after having entered the twelve-cubit precinct, the breaking of the night certainly occurs, but there is no breach of the observance. When dawn has arisen, the observance should be set aside. If that monk has departed for some reason, one should announce to whichever other monk one sees first of all and set it aside. Even having gone to the monastery, one should announce to whomever one sees first and set it aside. This is the procedure for one who has set aside the observance.

238. Evaṃ [M 0.0337] yattakāni divasāni āpatti paṭicchannā hoti, tattakāni tato adhikatarāni vā kukkuccavinodanatthāya parivasitvā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā vattaṃ samādiyitvā mānattaṃ yācitabbaṃ. Ayañhi vatte samādinne eva mānattāraho hoti nikkhittavattena parivutthattā. Anikkhittavattassa pana puna samādānakiccaṃ natthi. So hi paṭicchannadivasātikkameneva mānattāraho hoti, tasmā tassa mānattaṃ dātabbameva. Taṃ dentena –

238. Thus, for as many days as an offense was concealed, for that many days or for more, having undergone probation for the purpose of dispelling remorse, having approached the Sangha, and having undertaken the observance, mānatta should be requested. For this bhikkhu, having undergone probation with the observance set aside, is worthy of mānatta only when the observance has been undertaken. But for one who has not set aside the observance, there is no duty of undertaking it again. For that one is worthy of mānatta simply by the passing of the days of concealment; therefore, mānatta should indeed be given to him. When giving it—

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ [V 0.0313] āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ, bhante, parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmi. Ahaṃ, bhante…pe… sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso, dutiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmi. Ahaṃ, bhante…pe… sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso, tatiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmī”ti –

“Venerable sir, I have committed several offenses, concealed for one day. I, that one, requested the Sangha for a one-day probation for those several offenses concealed for one day. The Sangha granted me a one-day probation for those several offenses concealed for one day. Venerable sir, I, that one, having lived through the probation, request the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several offenses concealed for one day. Venerable sir… I, that one, having lived through the probation, for a second time, venerable sir, request the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several offenses concealed for one day. Venerable sir… I, that one, having lived through the probation, for a third time, venerable sir, request the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several offenses concealed for one day.”

Evaṃ tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having had him request thus three times—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed several offenses, concealed for one day. He requested the Sangha for a one-day probation for those several offenses, concealed for one day. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a one-day probation for those several offenses, concealed for one day. Having lived through the probation, he now requests the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several offenses, concealed for one day. If it is agreeable to the Sangha, may the Sangha grant the monk named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for those several offenses, concealed for one day. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ [M 0.0338] sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed several offenses, concealed for one day. He requested the Sangha for a one-day probation for those several offenses, concealed for one day. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a one-day probation for those several offenses, concealed for one day. Having lived through the probation, he now requests the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several offenses, concealed for one day. The Sangha grants the monk named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for those several offenses, concealed for one day. To whichever venerable one the granting of a six-night mānatta to the monk named so-and-so for these several offenses concealed for one day is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time, I state this matter... and so forth... For a third time, I state this matter... and so forth...

“Dinnaṃ saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

A six-night mānatta for several offenses concealed for one day has been granted by the Sangha to the monk named so-and-so. This is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

Evaṃ [V 0.0314] kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus the formal act announcement should be made.

Kammavācāpariyosāne ca tena bhikkhunā māḷakasīmāyameva “mānattaṃ samādiyāmi, vattaṃ samādiyāmī”ti vattaṃ samādātabbaṃ, samādiyitvā tattheva saṅghassa ārocetabbaṃ. Ārocentena ca –

And at the conclusion of the formal act, that monk should undertake the observance right within the sīmā of the assembly hall, saying, "I undertake mānatta, I undertake the observance." Having undertaken it, he should inform the Sangha right there. And when informing, he should say:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ mānattaṃ carāmi, vediyāmahaṃ bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti –

Venerable sirs, I have committed several offenses concealed for one day. I requested the Sangha for a one-day probation for those several offenses concealed for one day. The Sangha granted me a one-day probation for those several offenses concealed for one day. Having completed the probation, I requested the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several offenses concealed for one day. The Sangha granted me a six-night mānatta for those several offenses concealed for one day. I am now observing mānatta. I am making it known, venerable sirs; may the Sangha remember me as one who is making it known.

Evaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Imañca pana atthaṃ gahetvā yāya kāyaci vācāya ārocetuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

It should be announced thus. However, having grasped this meaning, it is indeed proper to announce it in any wording whatsoever.

Ārocetvā [M 0.0339] sace nikkhipitukāmo hoti, “mānattaṃ nikkhipāmi, vattaṃ nikkhipāmī”ti saṅghamajjhe nikkhipitabbaṃ. Māḷakato bhikkhūsu nikkhantesu ekassapi santike nikkhipituṃ vaṭṭati. Māḷakato nikkhamitvā satiṃ paṭilabhantena sahagacchantassa santike nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace sopi pakkanto, aññassa yassa māḷake nārocitaṃ, tassa ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ. Ārocentena pana avasāne “vediyatīti maṃ āyasmā dhāretū”ti vattabbaṃ. Dvinnaṃ ārocentena “āyasmantā dhārentū”ti, tiṇṇaṃ ārocentena “āyasmanto dhārentū”ti vattabbaṃ. Nikkhittakālato paṭṭhāya pakatattaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati. Sace appabhikkhuko vihāro hoti, sabhāgā bhikkhū vasanti, vattaṃ anikkhipitvā antovihāreyeva rattiyo gaṇetabbā. Atha na sakkā sodhetuṃ, vuttanayeneva vattaṃ nikkhipitvā paccūsasamaye catūhi pañcahi vā bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepato, aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānato dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā mahāmaggato okkamma gumbena vā vatiyā vā paṭicchannaṭṭhāne nisīditabbaṃ, antoaruṇeyeva vuttanayena vattaṃ samādiyitvā ārocetabbaṃ. Sace añño koci bhikkhu kenacideva karaṇīyena taṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchati, sace esa taṃ passati, saddaṃ vāssa suṇāti, ārocetabbaṃ. Anārocentassa ratticchedo ceva vattabhedo ca, atha dvādasahatthaṃ upacāraṃ okkamitvā ajānantasseva gacchati, ratticchedo hoti eva, vattabhedo [V 0.0315] pana natthi. Ārocitakālato paṭṭhāya ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ ṭhapetvā sesehi sati karaṇīye gantumpi vaṭṭati, aruṇe uṭṭhite tassa bhikkhussa santike vattaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace sopi kenaci kammena pure aruṇeyeva gacchati, aññaṃ vihārato nikkhantaṃ vā āgantukaṃ vā yaṃ paṭhamaṃ passati, tassa santike ārocetvā vattaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Ayañca yasmā gaṇassa ārocetvā bhikkhūnañca atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāva vasi, tenassa ūne gaṇe caraṇadoso vā vippavāso vā na hoti. Sace na kañci passati, vihāraṃ gantvāpi yaṃ paṭhamaṃ passati, tassa ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ. Ayaṃ nikkhittavattassa parihāro.

Having informed, if he wishes to relinquish the observance, he should relinquish it in the midst of the Sangha, saying, 'I relinquish the mānatta, I relinquish the observance.' If the monks have departed from the assembly hall, it is allowable to relinquish it in the presence of even one monk. Having departed from the assembly hall, a monk who has regained mindfulness should relinquish it in the presence of a monk accompanying him. If that one has also departed, it should be relinquished after having informed another who was not informed in the assembly hall. When informing, at the end, one should say, 'May the venerable one remember me as one who is making it known.' When informing two, one should say, 'May the venerable ones remember,' and when informing three, 'May the venerable ones remember.' From the time of relinquishment, he stands in the position of an ordinary monk. If the monastery has few monks and suitable monks reside there, the nights should be counted within the monastery itself without relinquishing the observance. But if it is not possible to purify, having relinquished the observance in the manner stated, at dawn, together with four or five monks, one should sit in a concealed place, having gone beyond two clod-throws from the enclosure of a monastery that has a surrounding wall, or from a place suitable for an enclosure for one that does not have a surrounding wall, having left the main road, concealed by a bush or a fence. Then, just before dawn, having undertaken the observance in the manner stated, he should inform. If some other monk comes to that place for any reason, if this one sees him or hears his voice, he should inform him. For one who does not inform, there is both a break in the nights and a breach of the observance. But if another monk enters the twelve-cubit precinct and departs without this one's knowledge, there is indeed a break in the nights, but there is no breach of the observance. Starting from the time of informing, having left one monk, it is allowable for the remaining monks to go if there is business. When dawn has arisen, the observance should be relinquished in the presence of that monk. If that monk also departs just before dawn for some business, the observance should be relinquished in the presence of whomever he sees first, whether one leaving the monastery or a newcomer, after having informed him. And since this one dwelt having informed the group and having noted the presence of the monks, for him there is no fault of practicing with an incomplete quorum or of dwelling in separation. If he sees no one, even after going to the monastery, he should relinquish the observance after having informed the first one he sees. This is the procedure for one who has relinquished the observance.

239. Evaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ akhaṇḍaṃ caritvā yattha siyā vīsatigaṇo bhikkhusaṅgho, tattha so bhikkhu abbhetabbo. Abbhentehi ca paṭhamaṃ [M 0.0340] abbhānāraho kātabbo. Ayañhi nikkhittavattattā pakatattaṭṭhāne ṭhito, pakatattassa ca abbhānaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, tasmā vattaṃ samādāpetabbo, vatte samādinne abbhānāraho hoti. Tenapi vattaṃ samādiyitvā ārocetvā abbhānaṃ yācitabbaṃ. Anikkhittavattassa puna vattasamādānakiccaṃ natthi. So hi chārattātikkameneva abbhānāraho hoti, tasmā so abbhetabbo. Abbhentena ca –

239. Having thus practiced the mānatta for six nights without interruption, wherever there is a Sangha of twenty bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should be reinstated there. And by those reinstating, he should first be made worthy of reinstatement. For this one, because of having relinquished the observance, stands in the position of a normal bhikkhu, and it is not proper to perform reinstatement for a normal bhikkhu. Therefore, he should be made to undertake the observance. When the observance has been undertaken, he becomes worthy of reinstatement. By him also, having undertaken the observance and announced it, reinstatement should be requested. For one who has not relinquished the observance, there is no further duty of undertaking the observance. For he becomes worthy of reinstatement merely by the passing of the six nights. Therefore, he should be reinstated. And the one requesting reinstatement should say—

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ, bhante, ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmi. Ahaṃ, bhante…pe… sohaṃ ciṇṇamānatto dutiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmi. Ahaṃ, bhante…pe… sohaṃ ciṇṇamānatto tatiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sirs, I committed several offenses concealed for one day. I requested the Sangha for a one-day probation for those several offenses concealed for one day. The Sangha granted me a one-day probation for those several offenses concealed for one day. Having completed the probation, I requested the Sangha for the mānatta of six nights for those several offenses concealed for one day. The Sangha granted me the mānatta of six nights for those several offenses concealed for one day. Venerable sirs, having completed the mānatta, I request the Sangha for reinstatement. Venerable sirs… and so forth… having completed the mānatta, for a second time, venerable sirs, I request the Sangha for reinstatement. Venerable sirs… and so forth… having completed the mānatta, for a third time, venerable sirs, I request the Sangha for reinstatement.

Evaṃ tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having had him request thus three times—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ [V 0.0316] ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable Sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, has committed several offenses concealed for one day. He requested the Sangha for a one-day probation for those several offenses concealed for one day. The Sangha granted this bhikkhu, named so-and-so, a one-day probation for those several offenses concealed for one day. Having completed the probation, he requested the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several offenses concealed for one day. The Sangha granted this bhikkhu, named so-and-so, a six-night mānatta for those several offenses concealed for one day. Having completed the mānatta, he requests the Sangha for reinstatement. If it is agreeable to the Sangha, the Sangha should reinstate the bhikkhu, named so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ [M 0.0341] sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno abbhānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable Sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, has committed several offenses concealed for one day. He requested the Sangha for a one-day probation for those several offenses concealed for one day. The Sangha granted the bhikkhu named so-and-so a one-day probation for those several offenses concealed for one day. Having completed the probation, he requested the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several offenses concealed for one day. The Sangha granted the bhikkhu named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for those several offenses concealed for one day. Having completed the mānatta, he requests the Sangha for reinstatement. The Sangha reinstates the bhikkhu named so-and-so. If it is agreeable to the venerable ones that the bhikkhu named so-and-so be reinstated, let them remain silent. If it is not agreeable to anyone, let them speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For the second time, I declare this matter...and so forth...For the third time, I declare this matter...and so forth.

“Abbhito saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The bhikkhu named so-and-so has been reinstated by the Sangha. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore they are silent. Thus I hold it.

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

The formal act should be performed thus.

Evaṃ tāva ekāhappaṭicchannāya āpattiyā paṭicchannaparivāso mānattadānaṃ abbhānañca veditabbaṃ. Imināva nayena dvīhādipaṭicchannāsupi tadanurūpā kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus, first, for an offense concealed for one day, the probation for a concealed offense, the granting of mānatta, and reinstatement should be understood. By this very method, for offenses concealed for two days and so on, the corresponding formal act should be performed.

240. Sace pana appaṭicchannā āpatti hoti, parivāsaṃ adatvā mānattameva datvā ciṇṇamānatto abbhetabbo. Kathaṃ? Mānattaṃ dentena tāva –

240. However, if the offense is unconcealed, without giving probation, only mānatta should be given, and having completed mānatta, he should be reinstated. How? By the one giving mānatta, first—

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmi. Ahaṃ, bhante…pe… dutiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmi. Ahaṃ[V 0.0317], bhante…pe… tatiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable Sirs, I have committed several unconcealed offenses. I, therefore, Venerable Sirs, request the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several unconcealed offenses. Venerable Sirs...and so forth...For the second time, Venerable Sirs, I request the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several unconcealed offenses. Venerable Sirs...and so forth...For the third time, Venerable Sirs, I request the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several unconcealed offenses.

Tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having had him request three times—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ [M 0.0342] āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.
