Venerable Sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has committed several unconcealed offenses. He requests the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several unconcealed offenses. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should give this bhikkhu named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for those several unconcealed offenses. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable Sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This bhikkhu, named so-and-so, has committed several unconcealed offenses. He requests the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several unconcealed offenses. The Sangha gives a six-night mānatta to the bhikkhu, named so-and-so, for those several unconcealed offenses. To whichever venerable one the giving of a six-night mānatta to the bhikkhu, named so-and-so, for those several unconcealed offenses is agreeable, let him be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, let him speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For the second time, I declare this matter...and so forth...For the third time, I declare this matter...and so forth.

“Dinnaṃ saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The Sangha has granted a six-night mānatta to the bhikkhu named so-and-so for those several unconcealed offenses. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus should the formal act be performed.

Kammavācāpariyosāne ca vattasamādānaṃ vattanikkhepo mānattacaraṇañca sabbaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Ārocentena pana –

At the conclusion of the formal act, the undertaking of the duties, the laying aside of the duties, and the practice of mānatta should all be understood in the manner stated. But by the one informing—

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ [V 0.0318] āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ mānattaṃ carāmi, vediyāmahaṃ, bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti –

Venerable Sirs, I have committed several unconcealed offenses. I requested the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those several unconcealed offenses. The Sangha granted me a six-night mānatta for those several unconcealed offenses. I am now practicing the mānatta. I am to be recognized, Venerable Sirs; let the Sangha hold me as one to be recognized.

Evaṃ ārocetabbaṃ.

Thus should it be announced.

Ekassa dvinnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ vā ārocentena paṭicchannamānatte vuttanayeneva ārocetabbaṃ. Ciṇṇamānatto ca yattha siyā vīsatigaṇo bhikkhusaṅgho, tattha so abbhetabbo. Abbhentena ca –

When informing one, two, or three, it should be announced in the same way as stated for concealed mānatta. And having completed the mānatta, wherever there is a Sangha of twenty bhikkhus, he should be reinstated there. And by the one seeking reinstatement—

“Ahaṃ[M 0.0343], bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmi. Ahaṃ, bhante…pe… sohaṃ ciṇṇamānatto dutiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmi. Ahaṃ, bhante…pe… sohaṃ ciṇṇamānatto tatiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sir, I have committed numerous unconcealed offenses. I requested the Sangha for six nights' penance for those numerous unconcealed offenses. The Sangha granted me six nights' penance for those numerous unconcealed offenses. Having completed the penance, I now request the Sangha for reinstatement. Venerable sir, … I, having completed the penance, for a second time, venerable sir, request the Sangha for reinstatement. Venerable sir, … I, having completed the penance, for a third time, venerable sir, request the Sangha for reinstatement.

Evaṃ tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having had him request thus three times—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed numerous unconcealed offenses. He requested the Sangha for six nights' penance for those numerous unconcealed offenses. The Sangha granted six nights' penance to the monk, named so-and-so, for those numerous unconcealed offenses. Having completed the penance, he now requests the Sangha for reinstatement. If it is agreeable to the Sangha, may the Sangha reinstate the monk, named so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno abbhānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed numerous unconcealed offenses. He requested the Sangha for six nights' penance for those numerous unconcealed offenses. The Sangha granted six nights' penance to the monk, named so-and-so, for those numerous unconcealed offenses. Having completed the penance, he now requests the Sangha for reinstatement. The Sangha reinstates the monk named so-and-so. If the reinstatement of the monk named so-and-so is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent. If anyone does not approve, let him speak.

“Dutiyampi [V 0.0319] etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time I speak on this matter… For a third time I speak on this matter…

Abbhito saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The monk named so-and-so has been reinstated by the Sangha. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

Evaṃ kammavācaṃ vatvā abbhetabbo. Evaṃ appaṭicchannāya āpattiyā vuṭṭhānaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Having recited the formal act in this way, he should be reinstated. Thus should reinstatement from an unconcealed offense be understood.

241. Sace [M 0.0344] kassaci ekāpatti paṭicchannā hoti, ekā appaṭicchannā, tassa paṭicchannāya āpattiyā parivāsaṃ datvā parivutthaparivāsassa mānattaṃ dentena appaṭicchannāpattiṃ paṭicchannāpattiyā samodhānetvāpi dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Kathaṃ? Sace paṭicchannāpatti ekāhappaṭicchannā hoti –

241. If a certain monk has one offense concealed and one unconcealed, having given him probation for the concealed offense, when giving penance to one who has completed the probation, it is permissible to also give it by combining the unconcealed offense with the concealed offense. How? If the concealed offense is concealed for a single day—

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso, ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sirs, I have committed numerous offenses concealed for one day. I requested the Sangha for a one-day probation for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. The Sangha granted me a one-day probation for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. I have completed the probation. Venerable sirs, I have committed numerous unconcealed offenses. Therefore, venerable sirs, I request the Sangha for six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed.

Tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having had him request three times—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed numerous offenses concealed for one day. He requested the Sangha for a one-day probation for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. The Sangha granted a one-day probation to the monk, named so-and-so, for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. He has completed the probation. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed numerous unconcealed offenses. He requests the Sangha for six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. If it is agreeable to the Sangha, may the Sangha grant six nights' penance to the monk, named so-and-so, for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu [V 0.0320] me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo [M 0.0345] āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed numerous offenses concealed for one day. He requested the Sangha for a one-day probation for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. The Sangha granted a one-day probation to the monk, named so-and-so, for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. He has completed the probation. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed numerous unconcealed offenses. He requests the Sangha for six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. The Sangha grants six nights' penance to the monk, named so-and-so, for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. If the granting of six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed, to the monk named so-and-so, is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent. If anyone does not approve, let him speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time I speak on this matter… For a third time I speak on this matter…

“Dinnaṃ saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The Sangha has granted six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed, to the monk named so-and-so. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus should the formal act be performed.

Kammavācāpariyosāne ca vattasamādānādi sabbaṃ vuttanayameva. Ārocentena pana –

And at the conclusion of the formal act, everything, beginning with the undertaking of the duties, is just as has been stated. But by the one announcing—

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso, ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ mānattaṃ carāmi, vediyāmahaṃ, bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti –

Venerable sir, I have committed numerous offenses concealed for a single day. I requested the Saṅgha for a one-day parivāsa for those numerous offenses concealed for a single day. The Saṅgha granted me a one-day parivāsa for those numerous offenses concealed for a single day. Having lived out the parivāsa, venerable sir, I have committed numerous unconcealed offenses. I, venerable sir, requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. The Saṅgha granted me a six-night mānatta for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. I am now practicing the mānatta. I am known, venerable sir; let the Saṅgha hold me as known.

Evaṃ [V 0.0321] ārocetabbaṃ.

Thus should it be announced.

Samādinnamānattena ca anūnaṃ katvā vuttanayena chārattaṃ mānattaṃ caritabbaṃ. Ciṇṇamānatto ca yattha siyā vīsatigaṇo bhikkhusaṅgho, tattha so abbhetabbo. Abbhentena ca –

And having undertaken the mānatta, the six-night mānatta should be practiced without deficiency in the manner stated. And a monk who has completed the mānatta, wherever there is a Saṅgha of twenty monks, should be reinstated there. And by the one being reinstated:

“Ahaṃ[M 0.0346], bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso, ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ, bhante, ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sir, I have committed numerous offenses concealed for a single day. I requested the Saṅgha for a one-day parivāsa for those numerous offenses concealed for a single day. The Saṅgha granted me a one-day parivāsa for those numerous offenses concealed for a single day. Having lived out the parivāsa, venerable sir, I committed numerous unconcealed offenses. I, venerable sir, requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. The Saṅgha granted me a six-night mānatta for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. Now, venerable sir, having completed the mānatta, I request the Saṅgha for reinstatement.

Evaṃ tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having had him request thus three times—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannāñca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed numerous offenses, concealed for one day. He requested the Saṅgha for a one-day parivāsa for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so a one-day parivāsa for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. Having lived out the parivāsa, this monk named so-and-so has committed numerous unconcealed offenses. He requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. Having observed the mānatta, he requests rehabilitation from the Saṅgha. If it is acceptable to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should rehabilitate the monk named so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji ekāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ ekāhappaṭicchannānaṃ ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso, ayaṃ itthannāmo [V 0.0322] bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ [M 0.0347] mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno abbhānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed numerous offenses concealed for one day. He requested the Saṅgha for a one-day parivāsa for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so a one-day parivāsa for those numerous offenses concealed for one day. Having lived out the parivāsa, this monk named so-and-so committed numerous unconcealed offenses. He requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. Having observed the mānatta, he requests rehabilitation from the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha rehabilitates the monk named so-and-so. The venerable one who approves of the rehabilitation of the monk named so-and-so should remain silent; the one who does not approve should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For the second time, I say this matter… For the third time, I say this matter…

“Abbhito saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The monk named so-and-so has been reinstated by the Saṅgha. It is pleasing to the Saṅgha, therefore they are silent. Thus I hold it.

Evaṃ kammavācaṃ katvā abbhetabbo.

Having performed the formal act in this way, he should be reinstated.

Paṭicchannaparivāsakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on probation for concealed offenses is concluded.

242. Suddhantaparivāso samodhānaparivāsoti dve avasesā. Tattha (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) suddhantaparivāso duvidho cūḷasuddhanto mahāsuddhantoti. Duvidhopi cesa rattiparicchedaṃ sakalaṃ vā ekaccaṃ vā ajānantassa ca assarantassa ca tattha vematikassa ca dātabbo. Āpattipariyantaṃ pana “ettakā ahaṃ āpattiyo āpanno”ti jānātu vā mā vā, akāraṇametaṃ, tattha yo upasampadato paṭṭhāya anulomakkamena vā ārocitadivasato paṭṭhāya paṭilomakkamena vā “asukañca asukañca divasaṃ vā pakkhaṃ vā māsaṃ vā saṃvaccharaṃ vā tava suddhabhāvaṃ jānāsī”ti pucchiyamāno “āma, bhante, jānāmi, ettakaṃ nāma kālaṃ ahaṃ suddho”ti vadati, tassa dinno suddhantaparivāso cūḷasuddhantoti vuccati.

242. The probation-until-purity and the combined-probation are the two remaining. Herein, the probation-until-purity is of two kinds: the minor probation-until-purity and the major probation-until-purity. And both of these should be given to one who does not know the limit of nights, whether all or some, and to one who cannot remember it or is doubtful about it. However, regarding the extent of the offenses, whether he knows or does not know, “I have committed so many offenses,” this is not a factor. Therein, when a monk—starting from the day of his higher ordination in forward order or starting from the day of confession in reverse order—is asked, “Do you know your state of purity on such and such a day, or fortnight, or month, or year?” and he replies, “Yes, venerable sir, I know; for such and such a period of time I was pure,” the probation-until-purity given to him is called the minor probation-until-purity.

Taṃ gahetvā parivasantena yattakaṃ kālaṃ attano suddhiṃ jānāti, tattakaṃ apanetvā avasesaṃ māsaṃ vā dvemāsaṃ vā parivasitabbaṃ. Sace “māsamattaṃ asuddhomhī”ti sallakkhetvā aggahesi, parivasanto ca puna aññaṃ māsaṃ sarati, tampi māsaṃ parivasitabbameva, puna parivāsadānakiccaṃ natthi. Atha “dvemāsaṃ asuddhomhī”ti sallakkhetvā aggahesi, parivasanto ca “māsamattamevāhaṃ asuddhomhī”ti sanniṭṭhānaṃ karoti, māsameva parivasitabbaṃ, puna parivāsadānakiccaṃ [V 0.0323] natthi. Ayañhi suddhantaparivāso nāma uddhampi [M 0.0348] ārohati, heṭṭhāpi orohati. Idamassa lakkhaṇaṃ. Aññasmiṃ pana āpattivuṭṭhāne idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ – yo appaṭicchannaṃ āpattiṃ “paṭicchannā”ti vinayakammaṃ karoti, tassāpatti vuṭṭhāti. Yo paṭicchannaṃ “appaṭicchannā”ti vinayakammaṃ karoti, tassa na vuṭṭhāti. Acirapaṭicchannaṃ “cirapaṭicchannā”ti karontassapi vuṭṭhāti, cirapaṭicchannaṃ “acirapaṭicchannā”ti karontassa na vuṭṭhāti. Ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā “sambahulā”ti karontassa vuṭṭhāti ekaṃ vinā sambahulānaṃ abhāvato. Sambahulā pana āpajjitvā “ekaṃ āpajji”nti karontassa na vuṭṭhāti.

Having undertaken it, one who is undergoing probation should deduct whatever period of time he knows himself to be pure and observe probation for the remaining month or two months. If, having reflected, ‘I was impure for about a month,’ he undertook it, and while undergoing probation he again remembers another month, he must observe probation for that month too; there is no need to grant probation again. But if, having reflected, ‘I was impure for two months,’ he undertook it, and while undergoing probation he concludes, ‘I was impure for only about a month,’ he must observe probation for only a month; there is no need to grant probation again. For this probation until purity ascends and also descends. This is its characteristic. But in other cases of emerging from an offense, this is the characteristic: if a bhikkhu performs a formal act of the Vinaya for an unconcealed offense as if it were ‘concealed,’ he emerges from that offense. If a bhikkhu performs a formal act of the Vinaya for a concealed offense as if it were ‘unconcealed,’ he does not emerge from it. For one who performs the act for a recently concealed offense as if it were ‘long-concealed,’ he also emerges from the offense. For one who performs the act for a long-concealed offense as if it were ‘recently concealed,’ he does not emerge from it. For one who, having committed a single offense, performs the act as if for ‘many,’ he emerges from the offense, because without one, there cannot be many. But for one who, having committed many offenses, performs the act as if ‘I committed one,’ he does not emerge from the offense.

Yo pana yathāvuttena anulomapaṭilomanayena pucchiyamānopi rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti nassarati, vematiko vā hoti, tassa dinno suddhantaparivāso mahāsuddhantoti vuccati. Taṃ gahetvā gahitadivasato paṭṭhāya yāva upasampadadivaso, tāva rattiyo gaṇetvā parivasitabbaṃ, ayaṃ uddhaṃ nārohati, heṭṭhā pana orohati. Tasmā sace parivasanto rattiparicchede sanniṭṭhānaṃ karoti “māso vā saṃvaccharo vā mayhaṃ āpannassā”ti, māsaṃ vā saṃvaccharaṃ vā parivasitabbaṃ.

Whatever bhikkhu, even when questioned according to the aforesaid method of direct and reverse sequence, does not know the extent of the nights, does not remember, or is uncertain, the probation until purity given to him is called the ‘great probation until purity.’ Having undertaken that, starting from the day it was undertaken, he should observe probation for as many nights as there are up to the day of his higher ordination, having counted them. This does not ascend, but it descends. Therefore, if while undergoing probation he makes a determination regarding the extent of the nights, thinking, ‘For me who has committed the offense, it has been a month or a year,’ he should observe probation for a month or a year.

Parivāsayācanadānalakkhaṇaṃ panettha evaṃ veditabbaṃ – tena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo –

Herein, the procedure for requesting and granting probation should be known thus: That bhikkhu should approach the Sangha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, sit in a squatting position, raise his joined palms, and should speak thus:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ, āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, rattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yācāmī”ti.

“Venerable sirs, I have committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses. I do not know the extent of the offenses, I do not know the extent of the nights; I do not remember the extent of the offenses, I do not remember the extent of the nights; I am uncertain about the extent of the offenses, I am uncertain about the extent of the nights. I, therefore, request from the Sangha probation until purity for those offenses.”

Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo.

He should request a second time. He should request a third time.

Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

The Sangha should be informed by a competent and able bhikkhu:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo [V 0.0324] āpajji, āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ [M 0.0349] yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses. He does not know the extent of the offenses, he does not know the extent of the nights; he does not remember the extent of the offenses, he does not remember the extent of the nights; he is uncertain about the extent of the offenses, he is uncertain about the extent of the nights. He requests from the Sangha probation until purity for those offenses. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should grant probation until purity for those offenses to the bhikkhu named so-and-so. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji, āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses. He does not know the extent of the offenses, he does not know the extent of the nights; he does not remember the extent of the offenses, he does not remember the extent of the nights; he is uncertain about the extent of the offenses, he is uncertain about the extent of the nights. He requests the Sangha for probation until purity for these offenses. The Sangha grants probation until purity for these offenses to the bhikkhu named so-and-so. To whichever venerable one the granting of probation until purity for these offenses to the bhikkhu named so-and-so is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“For a second time I state this matter… and so on. For a third time I state this matter… and so on.”

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ. Suddhantaparivāso, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

“Probation until purity for those offenses has been granted by the Sangha to the bhikkhu named so-and-so. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I bear this in mind.”

Evaṃ suddhantaparivāso dātabbo.

Thus is probation until purity to be granted.

Kammavācāpariyosāne vattasamādānādi sabbaṃ vuttanayameva. Ārocentena pana –

At the conclusion of the formal act, the undertaking of the observances and so forth is all as previously stated. When making the announcement, however, one should say:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ, āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, rattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasāmi, vediyāmahaṃ, bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti ārocetabbaṃ.

“Venerable sir, I have committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses. I do not know the extent of the offenses, I do not know the extent of the nights; I do not remember the extent of the offenses, I do not remember the extent of the nights; I am uncertain about the extent of the offenses, I am uncertain about the extent of the nights. Therefore, venerable sir, I requested the Sangha for probation until purity for those offenses. The Sangha granted me probation until purity for those offenses. I am now undergoing probation. I am making this known, venerable sir; may the Sangha bear me in mind as one who is making this known.”

Ekassa [V 0.0325] dvinnaṃ vā tiṇṇaṃ vā ārocanaṃ vuttanayameva. Parivutthaparivāsassa mānattaṃ dentena –

The announcement to one, two, or three bhikkhus is as previously stated. When granting mānatta to one who has completed probation, one should say:

“Ahaṃ[M 0.0350], bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ, āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, rattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ, bhante, parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mārattaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sir, I have committed several Sanghādisesa offenses. I do not know the number of the offenses, I do not know the number of the nights; I do not remember the number of the offenses, I do not remember the number of the nights; I am uncertain about the number of the offenses, I am uncertain about the number of the nights. I, venerable sir, requested the Sangha for probation until purity for those offenses. The Sangha granted me probation until purity for those offenses. I, venerable sir, having completed probation, request the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those offenses.

Evaṃ tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having had him make the request three times—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji, āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed several Sanghādisesa offenses. He does not know the number of the offenses, he does not know the number of the nights; he does not remember the number of the offenses, he does not remember the number of the nights; he is uncertain about the number of the offenses, he is uncertain about the number of the nights. He requested the Sangha for probation until purity for those offenses. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so probation until purity for those offenses. He, having completed probation, requests the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those offenses. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should grant the monk named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for those offenses. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji, āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed several Sanghādisesa offenses. He does not know the number of the offenses, he does not know the number of the nights; he does not remember the number of the offenses, he does not remember the number of the nights; he is uncertain about the number of the offenses, he is uncertain about the number of the nights. He requested the Sangha for probation until purity for those offenses. The Sangha granted probation until purity for those offenses to the monk named so-and-so. Having completed probation, he requests the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those offenses. The Sangha grants a six-night mānatta for those offenses to the monk named so-and-so. To whichever venerable one the granting of a six-night mānatta for those offenses to the monk named so-and-so is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time I state this matter... For a third time I state this matter...

“Dinnaṃ [M 0.0351][V 0.0326] saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

A six-night mānatta has been granted by the Sangha to the monk named so-and-so for those offenses. The Sangha approves of it, therefore it is silent. Thus do I understand it.

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus is the formal motion to be made.

Kammavācāpariyosāne mānattasamādānādi sabbaṃ vuttanayameva. Ārocentena pana –

At the conclusion of the formal motion, the undertaking of mānatta and so forth is all as stated before. However, when making the announcement, one should say:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ, āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, rattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ mānattaṃ carāmi, vediyāmahaṃ, bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti –

Venerable sirs, I have committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses. I do not know the number of the offenses, I do not know the number of the nights; I do not remember the number of the offenses, I do not remember the number of the nights; I am uncertain about the number of the offenses, I am uncertain about the number of the nights. I requested the Saṅgha for probation until purity for those offenses. The Saṅgha granted me probation until purity for those offenses. Having lived out that probation, I requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for those offenses. The Saṅgha granted me a six-night mānatta for those offenses. I am observing mānatta. I inform you, venerable sirs; may the Saṅgha remember me as one who informs.

Evaṃ ārocetabbaṃ.

It should be announced thus.

Ciṇṇamānatto ca yattha siyā vīsatigaṇo bhikkhusaṅgho, tattha so bhikkhu abbhetabbo. Abbhentena ca –

And when he has completed mānatta, where there is a Saṅgha of twenty bhikkhus, that bhikkhu is to be reinstated there. And by the one reinstating—

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ, āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, rattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ bhante ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sirs, I have committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses. I do not know the number of the offenses, I do not know the number of the nights; I do not remember the number of the offenses, I do not remember the number of the nights; I am uncertain about the number of the offenses, I am uncertain about the number of the nights. I requested the Saṅgha for probation until purity for those offenses. The Saṅgha granted me probation until purity for those offenses. Having lived out that probation, I requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for those offenses. The Saṅgha granted me a six-night mānatta for those offenses. Venerable sirs, having completed mānatta, I request the Saṅgha for reinstatement.

Evaṃ [M 0.0352] tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having had him request three times—

“Suṇātu me[V 0.0327], bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji, āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed several Sanghādisesa offenses; he does not know the number of the offenses, he does not know the number of the nights; he does not remember the number of the offenses, he does not remember the number of the nights; he is uncertain about the number of the offenses, he is uncertain about the number of the nights. He requested the Sangha for probation until purity for those offenses. The Sangha granted probation until purity for those offenses to the monk named so-and-so. Having completed probation, he requested the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for those offenses. The Sangha granted a six-night mānatta for those offenses to the monk named so-and-so. Having completed mānatta, he requests the Sangha for reinstatement. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should reinstate the monk named so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji, āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno abbhānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed several Sanghādisesa offenses; he does not know the limit of the offenses, he does not know the limit of the nights; he does not remember the limit of the offenses, he does not remember the limit of the nights; he is uncertain about the limit of the offenses, he is uncertain about the limit of the nights. He requested the Sangha for probation until purity for these offenses. The Sangha granted probation until purity for these offenses to the monk named so-and-so. Having completed probation, he requested the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for these offenses. The Sangha granted a six-night mānatta for these offenses to the monk named so-and-so. Having completed mānatta, he requests the Sangha for reinstatement. The Sangha reinstates the monk named so-and-so. If any venerable one approves of the reinstatement of the monk named so-and-so, he should remain silent. If anyone disapproves, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time I state this matter… For a third time I state this matter…

“Abbhito saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The monk named so-and-so has been reinstated by the Sangha. The Sangha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.

Evaṃ kammavācaṃ katvā abbhetabbo.

Having performed the formal act in this way, he should be reinstated.

Suddhantaparivāsakathā niṭṭhitā.

The section on probation until purity is concluded.

243. Samodhānaparivāso [M 0.0353] pana tividho hoti – odhānasamodhāno agghasamodhāno missakasamodhānoti. Tattha (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) odhānasamodhāno nāma antarāpattiṃ āpajjitvā [V 0.0328] paṭicchādentassa parivutthadivase odhunitvā makkhetvā purimāya āpattiyā mūladivasaparicchede pacchā āpannaṃ āpattiṃ samodahitvā dātabbaparivāso vuccati.

243. Now, probation by combination is of three kinds: combination by concealment, combination by value, and mixed combination. Among these, combination by concealment is said to be the probation that is to be given to one who, having committed and concealed an offense during the period of his penance, by shaking off and invalidating the days already served, and combining the offense committed afterwards with the root-day period of the former offense.

Ayaṃ panettha vinicchayo – yo paṭicchannāya āpattiyā parivāsaṃ gahetvā parivasanto vā mānattāraho vā mānattaṃ caranto vā abbhānāraho vā anikkhittavatto aññaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā purimāya āpattiyā samā vā ūnatarā vā rattiyo paṭicchādeti, tassa mūlāyapaṭikassanena te parivutthadivase ca mānattaciṇṇadivase ca sabbe odhunitvā adivase katvā pacchā āpannāpattiṃ mūlaāpattiyaṃ samodhāya parivāso dātabbo. Tena sace mūlāpatti pakkhapaṭicchannā, antarāpatti ūnakapakkhapaṭicchannā, puna pakkhameva parivāso parivasitabbo. Athāpi antarāpatti pakkhapaṭicchannāva, pakkhameva parivasitabbaṃ. Etenupāyena yāva saṭṭhivassapaṭicchannā mūlāpatti, tāva vinicchayo veditabbo. Saṭṭhivassānipi parivasitvā mānattāraho hutvāpi hi ekadivasaṃ antarāpattiṃ paṭicchādetvā puna saṭṭhivassāni parivāsāraho hoti. Evaṃ mānattacārikamānattārahakālepi āpannāya āpattiyā mūlāyapaṭikassane kate mānattaciṇṇadivasāpi parivāsavutthadivasāpi sabbe makkhitāva honti. Sace pana nikkhittavatto āpajjati, mūlāyapaṭikassanāraho nāma na hoti. Kasmā? Yasmā na so parivasanto āpanno, pakatattaṭṭhāne ṭhito āpanno, tasmā tassā āpattiyā visuṃ mānattaṃ caritabbaṃ. Sace paṭicchannā hoti, parivāsopi vasitabbo.

Here is the ruling in this matter: If any bhikkhu—having undertaken probation for a concealed offense, and while undergoing that probation, or while worthy of mānatta, or while observing mānatta, or while worthy of rehabilitation, not having laid down the observance—falls into another offense and conceals it for a number of nights equal to or less than the former offense, for him, by means of being sent back to the beginning, all those days served on probation and days of mānatta observed are to be shaken off and made non-days; probation should then be given by combining the later-committed offense with the original offense. In that case, if the original offense was concealed for a fortnight and the intermediate offense was concealed for less than a fortnight, probation for a fortnight must be undergone again. Moreover, if the intermediate offense was also concealed for a fortnight, a fortnight must be undergone. By this method, the ruling should be understood up to an original offense concealed for sixty years. Indeed, even after having undergone probation for sixty years and having become worthy of mānatta, if one conceals an intermediate offense for even one day, one again becomes worthy of probation for sixty years. Likewise, at the time of observing mānatta or being worthy of mānatta, when being sent back to the beginning is done for an offense that has been committed, all the days of mānatta observed and the days served on probation become obliterated. But if one who has laid down the observance commits an offense, he is not one called worthy of being sent back to the beginning. Why? Because he did not commit the offense while undergoing probation; he committed it while standing in the state of a normal bhikkhu. Therefore, for that offense, mānatta must be observed separately. If it is concealed, probation must also be undergone.

“Sace pana antarāpatti mūlāpattito atirekapaṭicchannā hoti, tattha kiṃ kātabba”nti vutte mahāsumatthero āha “atekiccho ayaṃ puggalo, atekiccho nāma āvikārāpetvā vissajjetabbo”ti. Mahāpadumatthero panāha “kasmā atekiccho nāma, nanu ayaṃ samuccayakkhandhako nāma buddhānaṃ ṭhitakālasadiso, āpatti nāma paṭicchannā vā hotu appaṭicchannā vā samakaūnataraatirekapaṭicchannā vā, vinayadharassa kammavācaṃ yojetuṃ samatthabhāvoyevettha pamāṇaṃ, tasmā yā atirekapaṭicchannā [M 0.0354] hoti, taṃ mūlāpattiṃ katvā tattha itaraṃ samodhāya parivāso dātabbo”ti. Ayaṃ odhānasamodhāno nāma.

“But if the intermediate offense is concealed for a longer period than the root offense, what should be done in that case?” When this was said, the Elder Mahāsuma said: “This person is incurable; one who is called ‘incurable’ should be dismissed after having been made to reveal it.” But the Elder Mahāpaduma said: “Why should he be called ‘incurable’? Is not this section on accumulation like the time when the Buddhas were present? Whether an offense be concealed or unconcealed, or concealed for an equal, lesser, or greater period, the measure here is merely the ability of the Vinaya master to formulate the formal act. Therefore, whichever offense is concealed for a longer period, having made that the root offense and having combined the other with it, probation should be given.” This is called combination by concealment.

Taṃ dentena paṭhamaṃ mūlāya paṭikassitvā pacchā parivāso dātabbo. Sace koci bhikkhu pakkhapaṭicchannāya āpattiyā parivasanto antarā anikkhittavattova puna pañcāhappaṭicchannaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, tena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo –

When giving it, one should first send him back to the beginning, and afterwards probation should be given. If any monk, while undergoing probation for an offense concealed for a fortnight, without having relinquished his observance, again commits an offense concealed for five days, that monk should approach the Sangha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior monks, sit down on his heels, raise his joined palms, and speak thus:

“Ahaṃ[V 0.0329], bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācāmī”ti.

“Venerable sirs, I have committed several offenses concealed for a fortnight. I requested the Sangha for a fortnight’s probation for those several offenses concealed for a fortnight, and the Sangha granted me a fortnight’s probation for those several offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, I committed several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. Venerable sirs, I request the Sangha for a sending-back to the beginning for those several intermediate offenses concealed for five days.”

Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo.

He should request a second time. He should request a third time.

Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

A competent and able bhikkhu should inform the Sangha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikasseyya, esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. This monk named so-and-so has committed several offenses concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Saṅgha for a fortnight’s probation for those several offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so a fortnight’s probation for those several offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, he committed several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. He now requests the Saṅgha for drawing back to the root for those several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. If it is agreeable to the Saṅgha, may the Saṅgha draw the monk named so-and-so back to the root for those several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ [M 0.0355] pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanā, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. This monk named so-and-so has committed several offenses concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Saṅgha for a fortnight’s probation for those several offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so a fortnight’s probation for those several offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, he committed several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. He now requests the Saṅgha for drawing back to the root for those several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. The Saṅgha is drawing the monk named so-and-so back to the root for those several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. Let the venerable ones who approve of drawing the monk named so-and-so back to the root for those several intermediate offenses concealed for five days remain silent. Let those who disapprove speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“For a second time I state this matter… For a third time I state this matter…”

“Paṭikassito [V 0.0330] saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanā, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

“The monk named so-and-so has been drawn back to the root by the Saṅgha for those several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

Evaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanā kātabbā.

Thus should the drawing back to the root be performed.

Evañca samodhānaparivāso dātabbo. Tena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā…pe… evamassa vacanīyo –

And the combined probation should be given in this way. That monk should approach the Saṅgha and… he should say this:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ, taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācāmī”ti.

“Venerable sirs, I committed several offenses concealed for a fortnight. I requested the Saṅgha for a fortnight's probation for those several offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Saṅgha granted me a fortnight's probation for those several offenses concealed for a fortnight. While on probation, I committed several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. I requested the Saṅgha for drawing back to the root for those several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. The Saṅgha drew me back to the root for those several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. Venerable sirs, I now request the Saṅgha for combined probation for the several intermediate offenses concealed for five days, together with the former offenses.”

Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo.

He should request a second time. He should request a third time.

Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

An experienced and competent bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ [M 0.0356] āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati[V 0.0331], yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. This monk named so-and-so committed several offenses concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Saṅgha for a fortnight's probation for those several offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so a fortnight's probation for those several offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, he committed several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. He requested the Saṅgha for drawing back to the root for those several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. The Saṅgha drew the monk named so-and-so back to the root for those several intermediate offenses concealed for five days. He now requests the Saṅgha for a combined probation for the several intermediate offenses concealed for five days, together with the former offenses. If it is agreeable to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha may grant the monk named so-and-so a combined probation for the several intermediate offenses concealed for five days, together with the former offenses. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While on probation, he committed numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim. He requested the Sangha for reinstatement to the root for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim. The Sangha reinstated the monk named so-and-so to the root for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim. He now requests the Sangha for combined probation for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim, along with the earlier offenses. The Sangha grants the monk named so-and-so combined probation for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim, along with the earlier offenses. If the granting of combined probation to the monk named so-and-so for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim, along with the earlier offenses, is agreeable to the venerable ones, they should remain silent. If it is not agreeable, they should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For the second time, I state this matter… For the third time, I state this matter…

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāso[M 0.0357], khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The Sangha has granted combined probation to the monk named so-and-so for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim, along with the earlier offenses. This is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I understand it.

Evaṃ samodhānaparivāso dātabbo.

Thus should combined probation be granted.

Kammavācāpariyosāne ca vattasamādānādi sabbaṃ pubbe vuttanayameva. Ārocentena pana –

At the conclusion of the formal act, the undertaking of duties, and so forth, all is to be done just as previously described. However, for the one announcing:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasanto antarā [V 0.0332] sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ, taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasāmi, vediyāmahaṃ, bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti –

Venerable sir, I committed numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. I requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted me a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, I committed numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim. I requested the Sangha for reinstatement to the root for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim. The Sangha reinstated me to the root for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim. I then requested the Sangha for combined probation for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim, along with the earlier offenses. The Sangha granted me combined probation for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim, along with the earlier offenses. I am now undergoing probation. I acknowledge it, venerable sir; may the Sangha bear in mind that I acknowledge it.

Evaṃ ārocetabbaṃ.

Thus should it be announced.

Parivutthaparivāsassa mānattaṃ dentena –

When granting the six-night period of penance to one who has completed probation:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ, taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho antarā [M 0.0358] sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ, bhante, parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sir, I committed numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. I requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted me a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, I committed numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim. I requested the Sangha for reinstatement to the root for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim. The Sangha reinstated me to the root for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim. I requested the Sangha for combined probation for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim, together with the earlier offenses. The Sangha granted me combined probation for those numerous offenses concealed for five days in the interim, together with the earlier offenses. Venerable sir, having completed probation, I request the Sangha for a six-night penance for those numerous offenses.

Evaṃ tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

After having him request this three times—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ [V 0.0333] mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk named so-and-so committed numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While on probation, he committed in the interim numerous offenses concealed for five days. He requested the Sangha for reinstatement to the root for the numerous offenses committed in the interim and concealed for five days. The Sangha reinstated the monk named so-and-so to the root for the numerous offenses committed in the interim and concealed for five days. He requested the Sangha for a combined probation for the numerous offenses committed in the interim and concealed for five days, together with the earlier offenses. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a combined probation for the numerous offenses committed in the interim and concealed for five days, together with the earlier offenses. Having completed the probation, he requests the Sangha for a six-night period of penance for the numerous offenses. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha may grant the monk named so-and-so a six-night period of penance for the numerous offenses committed in the interim. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so saṅghaṃ antarā [M 0.0359] sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Saṅgha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While on probation, he committed numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. He requested the Saṅgha to relegate him to the beginning for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. The Saṅgha relegated the monk named so-and-so to the beginning for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. He then requested the Saṅgha for combined probation for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days, along with the earlier offenses. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so combined probation for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days, along with the earlier offenses. Having completed his probation, he now requests the Saṅgha for six-night penance for those numerous offenses. The Saṅgha grants the six-night penance to the monk named so-and-so for those numerous offenses. If it is agreeable to the venerable ones to grant the six-night penance to the monk named so-and-so for those numerous offenses, let them remain silent. If anyone disapproves, let them speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

A second time I state this matter… and so on… A third time I state this matter… and so on.

“Dinnaṃ saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The six-night penance for numerous offenses has been granted by the Saṅgha to the monk named so-and-so. The Saṅgha is agreeable; therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus should the formal act be performed.

Kammavācāpariyosāne ca mānattasamādānādi sabbaṃ vuttanayameva. Ārocentena pana –

At the conclusion of the formal act, the undertaking of the penance, and so forth, is all according to the method already stated. However, the one who announces should—

“Ahaṃ[V 0.0334], bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ, taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi[M 0.0360], sohaṃ mānattaṃ carāmi, vediyāmahaṃ bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti –

Venerable sirs, I have committed numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. I requested the Saṅgha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Saṅgha granted me a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, I committed numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. I requested the Saṅgha to relegate me to the beginning for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. The Saṅgha relegated me to the beginning for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. I requested the Saṅgha for combined probation for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days, along with the earlier offenses. The Saṅgha granted me combined probation for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days, along with the earlier offenses. Having completed my probation, I requested the Saṅgha for six-night penance for those numerous offenses. The Saṅgha granted me six-night penance for those numerous offenses. I am undergoing the penance. I am undergoing it, venerable sirs; may the Saṅgha hold me as one who is undergoing it.

Evaṃ ārocetabbaṃ.

Thus should it be announced.

Ciṇṇamānattaṃ abbhentena ca –

And by one who has completed the penance and is to be rehabilitated:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ, taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ, bhante, ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sirs, I have committed numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. I requested the Saṅgha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Saṅgha granted me a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While on probation, I committed numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. I requested the Saṅgha to relegate me to the beginning for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. The Saṅgha relegated me to the beginning for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. I requested the Saṅgha for combined probation for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days, along with the earlier offenses. The Saṅgha granted me combined probation for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days, along with the earlier offenses. Having completed the probation, I requested the Saṅgha for six-night penance for those numerous offenses. The Saṅgha granted me six-night penance for those numerous offenses. Venerable sirs, having completed the penance, I request the Saṅgha for rehabilitation.

Evaṃ [V 0.0335] tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Thus, having had him request three times—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so saṅghaṃ [M 0.0361] antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for the numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a fortnight's probation for the numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While on probation, he committed numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. He requested the Sangha for relegation to the beginning for the numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. The Sangha relegated the monk named so-and-so to the beginning for the numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. He requested the Sangha for a combined probation for the numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days, together with the earlier offenses. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a combined probation for the numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days, together with the earlier offenses. Having completed the probation, he requested the Sangha for a six-night penance for the numerous offenses. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a six-night penance for the numerous offenses. Having completed the penance, he requests the Sangha for rehabilitation. If it is the right time for the Sangha, the Sangha should rehabilitate the monk named so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pañcāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pañcāhappaṭicchannānaṃ purimāsu āpattīsu samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno abbhānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk so-and-so has committed numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted this monk so-and-so a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While on probation, he committed numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. He requested the Sangha for relegation to the beginning for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. The Sangha relegated the monk so-and-so to the beginning for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days. He requested the Sangha for combined probation for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days together with the previous offenses. The Sangha granted this monk so-and-so combined probation for those numerous intervening offenses concealed for five days together with the previous offenses. Having completed probation, he requested the Sangha for the six-night penance for those numerous offenses. The Sangha granted this monk so-and-so the six-night penance for those numerous offenses. Having completed the penance, he requests the Sangha for rehabilitation. The Sangha rehabilitates the monk so-and-so. If the rehabilitation of the monk so-and-so is agreeable to the venerable ones, let them be silent. Whoever does not agree, let them speak.

“Dutiyampi [V 0.0336] etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

A second time I speak of this matter… and so on… A third time I speak of this matter… and so on…

“Abbhito saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The monk so-and-so has been rehabilitated by the Sangha. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold it.

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus should the formal act be performed.

Sace [M 0.0362] mānattāraho vā mānattaṃ caranto vā abbhānāraho vā anikkhittavatto antarāpattiṃ āpajjitvā paṭicchādeti, vuttanayeneva purimāpattiyā antarāpattiyā ca divasaparicchedaṃ sallakkhetvā tadanurūpāya kammavācāya mūlāya paṭikassitvā parivāsaṃ datvā parivutthaparivāsassa mānattaṃ datvā ciṇṇamānatto abbhetabbo. Sace pana paṭicchannāya āpattiyā parivasanto antarāpattiṃ āpajjitvā na paṭicchādeti, tassa mūlāyapaṭikassanāyeva kātabbā, puna parivāsadānakiccaṃ natthi.
