Mūlāyapaṭikassanena pana parivutthadivasānaṃ makkhitattā puna ādito paṭṭhāya parivasitabbaṃ. Parivutthaparivāsassa ca mūlāpattiyā antarāpattiṃ samodhānetvā mānattaṃ dātabbaṃ, ciṇṇamānatto ca abbhetabbo. Kathaṃ? Mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ karontena tāva sace mūlāpatti pakkhapaṭicchannā hoti,

If a monk deserving of penance, or undergoing penance, or deserving of rehabilitation, or not having abandoned his observance, commits an intervening offense and conceals it, he should be dealt with in the manner stated: by determining the period for both the earlier offense and the intervening offense, then being relegated to the beginning with the appropriate formal act, given probation, and after completing probation, given penance. Once he has completed penance, he should be rehabilitated. However, if while undergoing probation for a concealed offense, he commits an intervening offense and does not conceal it, he should only be relegated to the beginning; there is no need to give probation again. But because the days of probation already completed are nullified by being relegated to the beginning, probation must be undertaken anew from the start. After completing probation, penance should be given by combining the intervening offense with the original offense, and having completed penance, he should be rehabilitated. How? When relegating him to the beginning, if the original offense was concealed for a fortnight,

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ antarāsambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācāmī”ti –

“Venerable sirs, I have committed numerous offenses that were concealed for a fortnight. I requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight, and the Sangha granted me a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, I committed numerous unconcealed intervening offenses. Therefore, venerable sirs, I request the Sangha for relegation to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed intervening offenses.”

Tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

After causing him to request three times—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ [V 0.0337] mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikasseyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed numerous offenses that were concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a fortnight's probation for the numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, he committed numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. He requests the Sangha for a drawing back to the root for those numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. If it is agreeable to the Sangha, the Sangha should draw back to the root the monk named so-and-so for those numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu [M 0.0363] me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanā, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed numerous offenses that were concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a fortnight's probation for the numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, he committed numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. He requests the Sangha for a drawing back to the root for those numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. The Sangha draws back to the root the monk named so-and-so for those numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. To whichever venerable one the drawing back to the root of the monk named so-and-so for those numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time I speak on this matter... For a third time I speak on this matter...

“Paṭikassito saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu, antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassanā khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The monk named so-and-so has been drawn back to the root by the Sangha for the numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. The drawing back to the root is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus the formal act should be performed.

Evaṃ mūlāya paṭikassitena puna ādito paṭṭhāya parivasitabbaṃ. Parivasantena ca –

Having been drawn back to the root in this way, probation must be undertaken anew from the beginning. And while undergoing probation:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ paṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ, taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ [V 0.0338] appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, sohaṃ parivasāmi, vediyāmahaṃ, bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti –

Venerable sirs, I committed numerous offenses that were concealed for a fortnight. I requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted me a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, I committed numerous concealed intermediate offenses. I requested the Sangha for a drawing back to the root for those numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. The Sangha drew me back to the root for those numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. I am now undergoing probation. I acknowledge it, venerable sirs; may the Sangha remember me as one who acknowledges it.

Ārocetabbaṃ.

It should be announced.

Parivutthaparivāsassa [M 0.0364] mānattaṃ dentena –

When giving penance to one who has completed probation:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ, taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, sohaṃ, bhante, parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sirs, I committed numerous offenses that were concealed for a fortnight. I requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted me a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, I committed numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. I requested the Sangha for a drawing back to the root for those numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. The Sangha drew me back to the root for those numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. Venerable sirs, having completed probation, I request the Sangha for six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed.

Tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

After having him request three times:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, taṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed numerous offenses that were concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a fortnight's probation for the numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, he committed numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. He requested the Sangha for a drawing back to the root for those numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. The Sangha drew him back to the root for those numerous unconcealed intermediate offenses. Having completed probation, he requests the Sangha for six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. If it is agreeable to the Sangha, the Sangha should grant the monk named so-and-so six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji [V 0.0339] pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā [M 0.0365] āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, taṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed numerous offenses that were concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a fortnight's probation for the numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, he committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the interim. He requested the Sangha for relegation to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha relegated him to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. Now, having completed probation, he requests the Sangha for six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. The Sangha grants the monk named so-and-so six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. If granting six nights' penance to the monk named so-and-so for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed, is agreeable to the venerable ones, let them remain silent. If anyone does not approve, let them speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

I state this matter a second time… I state this matter a third time…

“Dinnaṃ saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The Sangha has granted six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed, to the monk named so-and-so. The Sangha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus should the formal motion be made.

Kammavācāpariyosāne mānattasamādānādi sabbaṃ vuttanayameva. Ārocentena pana –

At the conclusion of the formal motion, the undertaking of penance and all other procedures are as previously described. The monk should then announce:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ, taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ [M 0.0366][V 0.0340] adāsi, sohaṃ mānattaṃ carāmi, vediyāmahaṃ bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti –

Venerable sirs, I have committed numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. I requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted me a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While observing probation, I committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the interim. I requested the Sangha for relegation to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha relegated me to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. Having completed the probation, I requested the Sangha for six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. The Sangha granted me six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. I am observing penance. I declare this, venerable sirs. May the Sangha remember me as one who declares.

Evaṃ ārocetabbaṃ.

Thus should it be announced.

Ciṇṇamānattaṃ abbhentena ca –

And by one who has completed the penance and is seeking rehabilitation:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ, taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ apaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ bhante ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sirs, I have committed numerous offenses that were concealed for a fortnight. I requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted me a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While observing probation, I committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the interim. I requested the Sangha for relegation to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha relegated me to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. Having completed the probation, I requested the Sangha for six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. The Sangha granted me six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. Venerable sirs, having completed the penance, I request the Sangha for reinstatement.

Tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having caused him to request three times:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, taṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi[M 0.0367], so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, committed numerous offenses that were concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Sangha for a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted the monk, named so-and-so, a fortnight's probation for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While undergoing probation, he committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the interim. He requested the Sangha for relegation to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha relegated him to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. Having lived out the probation, he requested the Sangha for six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. The Sangha granted the monk, named so-and-so, six nights' penance for those numerous offenses, both concealed and unconcealed. Having completed the penance, he requests the Sangha for reinstatement. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should reinstate the monk named so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu [V 0.0341] me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji pakkhapaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ pakkhapaṭicchannānaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivasanto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, taṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ paṭicchannānañca appaṭicchannānañca chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno abbhānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed numerous offenses that were concealed for a fortnight. He requested the Sangha for a fortnight's parivāsa for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a fortnight's parivāsa for those numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight. While on parivāsa, he committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the meantime. He requested the Sangha for relegation to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the meantime. The Sangha relegated him to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the meantime. Having completed the parivāsa, he requested the Sangha for the six-night mānatta for those numerous concealed and unconcealed offenses. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so the six-night mānatta for those numerous concealed and unconcealed offenses. Having completed the mānatta, he requests the Sangha for reinstatement. The Sangha reinstates the monk named so-and-so. To whichever venerable one the reinstatement of the monk named so-and-so is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

A second time I speak on this matter… A third time I speak on this matter…

“Abbhito saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The monk named so-and-so has been reinstated by the Sangha. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I bear this in mind.

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus should the formal act be performed.

Imināva nayena mānattārahamānattacārikaabbhānārahakālesupi antarāpattiṃ āpajjitvā appaṭicchādentassa mūlāyapaṭikassanameva katvā mūlāpattiyā antarāpattiṃ samodhānetvā mānattaṃ datvā ciṇṇamānattassa abbhānaṃ kātabbaṃ. Ettha pana “sohaṃ parivasanto”ti āgataṭṭhāne “sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso mānattāraho”ti vā “sohaṃ mānattaṃ caranto”ti vā “sohaṃ ciṇṇamānatto abbhānāraho”ti vā vattabbaṃ.

In this same way, even at the times of being deserving of mānatta, undergoing mānatta, or deserving of reinstatement, if one commits an intermediate offense and does not conceal it, having been relegated to the beginning and having the intermediate offense combined with the root offense, mānatta should be given. After the mānatta has been completed, reinstatement should be performed. Here, in the place where it is said, 'I, while undergoing parivāsa…,' it should be said, 'I, having completed parivāsa, am deserving of mānatta,' or 'I, while undergoing mānatta…,' or 'I, having completed mānatta, am deserving of reinstatement.'

Sace [M 0.0368] pana appaṭicchannāya āpattiyā mānattaṃ caranto antarāpattiṃ āpajjitvā na paṭicchādeti, so mūlāya paṭikassitvā antarāpattiyā puna mānattaṃ datvā ciṇṇamānatto abbhetabbo. Kathaṃ? Mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ karontena tāva –

However, if, while undergoing mānatta for an unconcealed offense, one commits an intervening offense and does not conceal it, one should be relegated to the beginning, be given mānatta again, and then, having completed the mānatta, be reinstated. How? When performing the relegation to the beginning, one should say:

“Ahaṃ[V 0.0342], bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ mānattaṃ caranto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sirs, I committed numerous unconcealed offenses. For these numerous unconcealed offenses, I requested the Sangha for a six-night mānatta. The Sangha granted me a six-night mānatta for these numerous unconcealed offenses. While undergoing that mānatta, I committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the interim. Venerable sirs, I now request the Sangha for relegation to the beginning on account of these numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim.

Tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having caused him to request three times:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so mānattaṃ caranto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikasseyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed numerous unconcealed offenses. He requested the Sangha for a six-night mānatta for these numerous unconcealed offenses. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for these numerous unconcealed offenses. While undergoing mānatta, he committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the interim. He now requests the Sangha for relegation to the beginning for these numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. If it is suitable for the Sangha, the Sangha should relegate the monk named so-and-so to the beginning for these numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so mānattaṃ caranto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ [M 0.0369] āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanā, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed numerous unconcealed offenses. He requested the Sangha for six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses. The Sangha granted the monk named so-and-so six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses. While undergoing mānatta, he committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the interim. He requests the Sangha for relegation to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha relegates the monk named so-and-so to the beginning for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. To whichever venerable one the relegation to the beginning for the monk named so-and-so for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim is agreeable, he should remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time I state this matter… For a third time I state this matter…

“Paṭikassito saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu, antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ [V 0.0343] mūlāyapaṭikassanā khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The monk named so-and-so has been relegated by the Sangha. The relegation to the beginning for the numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I bear this in mind.

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus the formal act should be performed.

Evaṃ mūlāya paṭikassitvā mānattaṃ dentena –

Having thus relegated him to the beginning, when granting mānatta:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ mānattaṃ caranto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ, taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sir, I have committed numerous unconcealed offenses. I requested the Sangha for six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses. The Sangha granted me six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses. While undergoing mānatta, I committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the interim. I then requested the Sangha for revocation to the root for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha revoked me to the root for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. Now, venerable sir, I request the Sangha for six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim.

Tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having made him request three times:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so mānattaṃ caranto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, taṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ [M 0.0370] mūlāya paṭikassi, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed numerous unconcealed offenses. He requested the Sangha for six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses. The Sangha granted six-night mānatta to the monk, named so-and-so, for those numerous unconcealed offenses. While undergoing mānatta, he committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the interim. He requested the Sangha for revocation to the root for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha revoked him to the root for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. He requests the Sangha for six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. If it is timely for the Sangha, the Sangha should grant six-night mānatta to the monk, named so-and-so, for the numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ [V 0.0344] mānattaṃ adāsi, so mānattaṃ caranto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, taṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, has committed numerous unconcealed offenses. He requested the Sangha for six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses. The Sangha granted the monk, named so-and-so, six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses. While undergoing mānatta, he committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the interim. He requested the Sangha for revocation to the root for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha revoked him to the root for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. He requests the Sangha for six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha grants six-night mānatta to the monk, named so-and-so, for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. To whichever venerable one the granting of six-night mānatta to the monk, named so-and-so, for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim is agreeable, let him remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, let him speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time I state this matter… For a third time I state this matter…

“Dinnaṃ saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

Six-night mānatta has been granted by the Sangha to the monk named so-and-so for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. It is agreeable to the Sangha; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I hold it.

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

Thus should the formal act be performed.

Kammavācāpariyosāne mānattasamādānādi sabbaṃ vuttanayameva. Ārocentena pana –

At the conclusion of the formal act, the undertaking of mānatta and so forth is all in the manner already described. But by one who is announcing:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ mānattaṃ [M 0.0371] caranto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ mānattaṃ carāmi, vediyāmahaṃ, bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti –

Venerable sir, I committed numerous unconcealed offenses. I requested the Sangha for six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses. The Sangha granted me six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses. While undergoing mānatta, I committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the interim. I requested the Sangha for six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha revoked me to the root for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. I then requested the Sangha for six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha granted me six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. I am undergoing mānatta. I am to be acknowledged, venerable sir; may the Sangha remember me as one to be acknowledged.

Evaṃ ārocetabbaṃ.

Thus should it be announced.

Ciṇṇamānattaṃ [V 0.0345] abbhentena ca –

And by one who has completed mānatta and is fit for rehabilitation:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ mānattaṃ caranto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ appaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāciṃ, taṃ maṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ, bhante, ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmī”ti –

Venerable sir, I committed numerous unconcealed offenses. I requested the Sangha for six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses. The Sangha granted me six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses. While undergoing mānatta, I committed numerous unconcealed offenses in the interim. I requested the Sangha for revocation to the root for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha revoked me to the root for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. I then requested the Sangha for six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Sangha granted me six-night mānatta for those numerous unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. Venerable sir, having completed mānatta, I request the Sangha for rehabilitation.

Tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having made him request three times:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so mānattaṃ caranto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so [M 0.0372] saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ yāci, taṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed several unconcealed offenses. He requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for the several unconcealed offenses. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for the several unconcealed offenses. While undergoing mānatta, he committed several unconcealed offenses in the interim. He requested the Saṅgha for a sending back to the beginning for the several unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Saṅgha sent him back to the beginning for the several unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. He requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for the several unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for the several unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. Having completed the mānatta, he requests rehabilitation from the Saṅgha. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should rehabilitate the monk named so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so mānattaṃ caranto antarā sambahulā āpattiyo āpajji appaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanaṃ [V 0.0346] yāci, taṃ saṅgho antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāya paṭikassi, so saṅghaṃ antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno abbhānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk named so-and-so has committed several unconcealed offenses. He requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for the several unconcealed offenses. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for the several unconcealed offenses. While undergoing mānatta, he committed several unconcealed offenses in the interim. He requested the Saṅgha for a sending back to the beginning for the several unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Saṅgha sent him back to the beginning for the several unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. He requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for the several unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. The Saṅgha granted the monk named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for the several unconcealed offenses committed in the interim. Having completed the mānatta, he requests rehabilitation from the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha rehabilitates the monk named so-and-so. If the rehabilitation of the monk named so-and-so is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent. If it is not agreeable, let him speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time I state this matter... For a third time I state this matter...

“Abbhito saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

The monk named so-and-so has been rehabilitated by the Saṅgha. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.

Evaṃ kammavācaṃ katvā abbhetabbo.

Having performed the formal act in this way, he is to be rehabilitated.

Abbhānārahakālepi antarāpattiṃ āpajjitvā appaṭicchādentassa imināva nayena mūlāyapaṭikassanā mānattadānaṃ abbhānañca veditabbaṃ. Kevalaṃ [M 0.0373] panettha “mānattaṃ caranto”ti avatvā “ciṇṇamānatto abbhānāraho”ti vattabbaṃ.

Even at the time when one is eligible for rehabilitation, for one who commits an offense in the interim and does not conceal it, the sending back to the beginning, the granting of mānatta, and rehabilitation should be understood in this very way. However, in this case, instead of saying 'undergoing mānatta,' it should be said 'having completed mānatta, is eligible for rehabilitation.'

Odhānasamodhānaparivāsakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on the probation for covering up and aggregating is concluded.

244. Agghasamodhāno (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) nāma sambahulāsu āpattīsu yā ekā vā dve vā tisso vā sambahulā vā āpattiyo sabbacirapaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhāya tāsaṃ rattiparicchedavasena avasesānaṃ ūnatarapaṭicchannānaṃ āpattīnaṃ parivāso dīyati, ayaṃ vuccati agghasamodhāno. Yassa pana sataṃ āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannā, aparampi sataṃ āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāti evaṃ dasakkhattuṃ katvā āpattisahassaṃ divasasataṃ paṭicchannaṃ hoti, tena kiṃ kātabbanti? Sabbā samodahitvā dasa divase parivasitabbaṃ. Evaṃ ekeneva dasāhena divasasatampi parivasitabbameva hoti. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

244. Aggregation by Valuation is this: Among many offenses, when one, two, three, or many offenses have been concealed for the longest time, probation is given for the remaining offenses concealed for a shorter period by aggregating them according to the valuation of those longest-concealed offenses, based on their reckoning of nights. This is called Aggregation by Valuation. But for a bhikkhu for whom a hundred offenses are concealed for ten days, and another hundred offenses are also concealed for ten days—and so on, having done this ten times, a thousand offenses are concealed for a hundred days—what is to be done by him? Having aggregated all of them, probation should be undertaken for ten days. Thus, by just one ten-day period, even a hundred days of probation are indeed to be undertaken. And this has been said:

“Dasasataṃ rattisataṃ, āpattiyo chādayitvāna;

Dasa rattiyo vasitvāna, mucceyya pārivāsiko”ti. (pari. 477);

“Having concealed a thousand offenses for a hundred nights, having dwelt for ten nights, the probationer would be released.”

Ayaṃ [V 0.0347] agghasamodhāno nāma.

This is called Aggregation by Valuation.

Tassa ārocanadānalakkhaṇaṃ evaṃ veditabbaṃ – sace kassaci bhikkhuno ekā āpatti ekāhappaṭicchannā hoti, ekā āpatti dvīhappaṭicchannā, ekā tīhapaṭicchannā, ekā catūhappaṭicchannā, ekā pañcāhappaṭicchannā, ekā chāhappaṭicchannā, ekā sattāhappaṭicchannā, ekā aṭṭhāhappaṭicchannā, ekā navāhappaṭicchannā, ekā dasāhappaṭicchannā hoti, tena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā…pe… evamassa vacanīyo –

The characteristic of its informing and granting is to be understood thus: If a certain bhikkhu has one offense concealed for one day, one offense concealed for two days, one for three days, one for four days, one for five days, one for six days, one for seven days, one for eight days, one for nine days, and one offense concealed for ten days, that bhikkhu, having approached the Saṅgha, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder... and so on... should speak as follows:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo sambahulā āpattiyo dvīhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācāmī”ti.

“Venerable sirs, I have committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses: several offenses concealed for one day, several offenses concealed for two days... and so on... several offenses concealed for ten days. Venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha for aggregated probation by valuation, based on those offenses which were concealed for ten days.”

Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo.

He should ask a second time. He should ask a third time.

Byattena [M 0.0374] bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

The Saṅgha is to be informed by an experienced and capable bhikkhu—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses, several offenses concealed for one day... several offenses concealed for ten days. He asks the Saṅgha for aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days. If it is agreeable to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant to the bhikkhu named so-and-so aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā [V 0.0348] āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses, several offenses concealed for one day... several offenses concealed for ten days. He asks the Saṅgha for aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days. The Saṅgha is giving aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days to the bhikkhu named so-and-so. If the giving of aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days to the bhikkhu named so-and-so is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, let him speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“For a second time I state this matter... For a third time I state this matter...”

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāso, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

“Aggregated probation by valuation has been granted by the Saṅgha to the bhikkhu named so-and-so for those offenses that were concealed for ten days. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

This is how the formal act is to be made.

Kammavācāpariyosāne vattasamādānādi sabbaṃ vuttanayameva. Ārocentena pana –

At the conclusion of the formal act, the undertaking of the observances, etc., all is to be done in the manner stated. But when announcing, one is to say:

“Ahaṃ[M 0.0375], bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasāmi, vediyāmahaṃ, bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti –

“Venerable Sir, I have committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses, several offenses concealed for one day… several offenses concealed for ten days. I requested the Saṅgha for aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days. The Saṅgha granted me aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days. I am undergoing probation. I declare, Venerable Sir. May the Saṅgha remember me as one who is declaring.”

Evaṃ ārocetabbaṃ.

Thus it is to be announced.

Parivutthaparivāsassa mānattaṃ dentena –

When granting mānatta to one who has completed probation:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ, bhante, parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācāmī”ti –

“Venerable Sir, I have committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses—several offenses concealed for one day… several offenses concealed for ten days. I requested the Saṅgha for aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days. The Saṅgha granted me aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days. Now, Venerable Sir, having completed the probation, I request the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for these offenses.”

Tikkhattuṃ [V 0.0349] yācāpetvā –

Having had him request three times—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ[M 0.0376], saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses—several offenses concealed for one day… several offenses concealed for ten days. He requested the Saṅgha for aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days. The Saṅgha granted this bhikkhu named so-and-so aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days. Having completed the probation, he requests the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for these offenses. If it is agreeable to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant this bhikkhu named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for these offenses. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ deti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu named so-and-so has committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses—several offenses concealed for one day… several offenses concealed for ten days. He requested the Saṅgha for aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days. The Saṅgha granted this bhikkhu named so-and-so aggregated probation by valuation for those offenses that were concealed for ten days. Having completed the probation, he requests the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for these offenses. The Saṅgha is giving this bhikkhu named so-and-so a six-night mānatta for these offenses. If the giving of a six-night mānatta to the bhikkhu named so-and-so for these offenses is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, let him speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“For a second time I state this matter… For a third time I state this matter…”

“Dinnaṃ saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

“A six-night mānatta has been granted by the Saṅgha to the bhikkhu named so-and-so for these offenses. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

Evaṃ kammavācā kātabbā.

This is how the formal act is to be made.

Kammavācāpariyosāne ca mānattasamādānādi sabbaṃ vuttanayameva. Ārocentena pana –

At the conclusion of the formal act, the undertaking of mānatta, etc., is all according to the method already described. However, the one who announces should—

“Ahaṃ[V 0.0350], bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa [M 0.0377] me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ mānattaṃ carāmi, vediyāmahaṃ, bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti ārocetabbaṃ.

It should be announced: 'Venerable sir, I have committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses—several offenses concealed for one day… several offenses concealed for ten days. I requested the Saṅgha for a probation by aggregation according to the gravest of those offenses, those which were concealed for ten days. The Saṅgha granted me a probation by aggregation according to the gravest of those offenses, those which were concealed for ten days. Having completed the probation, I requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for those offenses. The Saṅgha granted me a six-night mānatta for those offenses. I am undergoing mānatta. I make it known, venerable sir; may the Saṅgha remember me as one who is making it known.'

Ciṇṇamānatto abbhetabbo. Abbhentena ca –

Having completed the mānatta, he should be reinstated. And when seeking reinstatement, he should—

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ, bhante, ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācāmī”ti –

“Venerable sir, I have committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses—several offenses concealed for one day… several offenses concealed for ten days. I requested the Saṅgha for a probation by aggregation according to the gravest of those offenses, those which were concealed for ten days. The Saṅgha granted me a probation by aggregation according to the gravest of those offenses, those which were concealed for ten days. Having completed the probation, I requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for those offenses. The Saṅgha granted me a six-night mānatta for those offenses. Now, venerable sir, having completed the mānatta, I request the Saṅgha for reinstatement.”

Tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā –

Having had him request three times—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheyya, esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses—several offenses concealed for one day… several offenses concealed for ten days. He requested the Saṅgha for a probation by aggregation according to the gravest of those offenses, those which were concealed for ten days. The Saṅgha granted this monk, named so-and-so, a probation by aggregation according to the gravest of those offenses, those which were concealed for ten days. Having completed the probation, he requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for these offenses. The Saṅgha granted this monk, named so-and-so, a six-night mānatta for these offenses. Having completed the mānatta, he requests the Saṅgha for reinstatement. If it is agreeable to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should reinstate the monk, named so-and-so. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu [V 0.0351] me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji sambahulā āpattiyo [M 0.0378] ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, so saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāsaṃ adāsi, so parivutthaparivāso saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāci, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, so ciṇṇamānatto saṅghaṃ abbhānaṃ yācati, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ abbheti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno abbhānaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk, named so-and-so, committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses—several offenses concealed for one day… several offenses concealed for ten days. He requested the Saṅgha for a probation by aggregation according to the gravest of those offenses, those which were concealed for ten days. The Saṅgha granted this monk, named so-and-so, a probation by aggregation according to the gravest of those offenses, those which were concealed for ten days. Having completed the probation, he requested the Saṅgha for a six-night mānatta for these offenses. The Saṅgha granted this monk, named so-and-so, a six-night mānatta for these offenses. Having completed the mānatta, he requests the Saṅgha for reinstatement. The Saṅgha reinstates the monk, named so-and-so. If the reinstatement of the monk, named so-and-so, is agreeable to the venerable ones, let them be silent. If it is not agreeable to anyone, let them speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“For a second time I speak on this matter… for a third time I speak on this matter….”

“Abbhito saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

“The monk named so-and-so has been reinstated by the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

Evaṃ kammavācaṃ katvā abbhetabbo.

Having performed the formal act in this way, he should be reinstated.

Agghasamodhānaparivāsakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on probation by aggregation according to the gravest is concluded.

245. Missakasamodhāno (cuḷava. aṭṭha. 102) nāma – yo nānāvatthukā āpattiyo ekato katvā dīyati. Tatrāyaṃ nayo –

245. Mixed aggregation refers to that which is given having grouped together offenses of various grounds. Herein is the method:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ, ekaṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ, ekaṃ duṭṭhullavācaṃ, ekaṃ attakāmaṃ, ekaṃ sañcarittaṃ, ekaṃ kuṭikāraṃ, ekaṃ vihārakāraṃ, ekaṃ duṭṭhadosaṃ, ekaṃ aññabhāgiyaṃ, ekaṃ saṅghabhedakaṃ, ekaṃ saṅghabhedānuvattakaṃ, ekaṃ dubbacaṃ, ekaṃ kuladūsakaṃ, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācāmī”ti –

“Venerable sir, I have committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses: one emission of semen, one bodily contact, one coarse speech, one serving one's own lust, one acting as a go-between, one building a hut, one building a monastery, one malicious false accusation, one related to another faction, one causing schism in the Saṅgha, one following a schismatic, one being difficult to admonish, and one corrupting families. Venerable sir, I request the Saṅgha for combined probation for these offenses.”

Tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā tadanurūpāya kammavācāya parivāso dātabbo.

Having had him request three times, probation should be given by means of the appropriate formal act.

Ettha [V 0.0352] ca “saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji nānāvatthukāyo”tipi “saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji”itipi evaṃ pubbe vuttanayena vatthuvasenapi [M 0.0379] gottavasenapi nāmavasenapi āpattivasenapi yojetvā kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva, tasmā na idha visuṃ kammavācaṃ yojetvā dassayissāma pubbe sabbāpattisādhāraṇaṃ katvā yojetvā dassitāya eva kammavācāya nānāvatthukāhipi āpattīhi vuṭṭhānasambhavato sāyevettha kammavācā alanti.

And here, whether one says, “He has committed Saṅghādisesa offenses of various grounds,” or, “He has committed Saṅghādisesa offenses,” it is indeed proper to perform the formal act by the method previously stated, having formulated it according to the ground, the clan, the name, or the offense. Therefore, we will not formulate and show a separate formal act here. Since emergence from offenses of even various grounds is possible by that very formal act which was previously shown—having been formulated and made common to all offenses—that same formal act is sufficient here.

Missakasamodhānaparivāsakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on probation by mixed aggregation is concluded.

246. Sace koci bhikkhu parivasanto vibbhamati, sāmaṇero vā hoti, vibbhamantassa sāmaṇerassa ca parivāso na ruhati. So ce puna upasampajjati, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ, yo parivāso dinno, sudinno, yo parivuttho, suparivuttho, avaseso parivasitabbo. Sacepi mānattāraho mānattaṃ caranto abbhānāraho vā vibbhamati, sāmaṇero vā hoti, so ce puna upasampajjati, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ, yo parivāso dinno, sudinno, yo parivuttho, suparivuttho, yaṃ mānattaṃ dinnaṃ, sudinnaṃ, yaṃ mānattaṃ ciṇṇaṃ, taṃ suciṇṇaṃ, so bhikkhu abbhetabbo.

246. If any bhikkhu, while undergoing probation, disrobes or becomes a novice, the probation is not established for the one who has disrobed and for the novice. If he is ordained again, for him that same previous granting of probation stands: the probation that was given was well-given; the probation that was undergone was well-undergone; the remainder must be undergone. If also one deserving of penance while undergoing penance, or one deserving of rehabilitation, disrobes or becomes a novice, if he is ordained again, for him that same previous granting of probation stands: the probation that was given was well-given; the probation that was undergone was well-undergone; the penance that was given was well-given; the penance that was practiced was well-practiced; that bhikkhu is to be rehabilitated.

Sace koci bhikkhu parivasanto ummattako hoti khittacitto vedanāṭṭo, ummattakassa khittacittassa vedanāṭṭassa ca parivāso na ruhati. So ce puna anummattako hoti akhittacitto avedanāṭṭo, tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ, yo parivāso dinno, sudinno, yo parivuttho, suparivuttho, avaseso parivasitabbo. Mānattārahādīsupi eseva nayo.

If any bhikkhu, while undergoing probation, becomes insane, distracted in mind, or afflicted by pain, the probation is not established for one who is insane, for one who is distracted in mind, and for one who is afflicted by pain. If he again becomes sane, not distracted in mind, and not afflicted by pain, that same previous granting of probation stands: the probation that was given was well-given; the probation that was undergone was well-undergone; the remainder must be undergone. In the cases of those deserving of penance and so on, this is the same method.

Sace koci parivasanto ukkhittako hoti, ukkhittakassa parivāso na ruhati. Sace puna osārīyati, tassa tadeva purimaṃ parivāsadānaṃ, yo parivāso dinno, sudinno, yo parivuttho, suparivuttho, avaseso parivasitabbo. Mānattārahādīsupi eseva nayo.

If any bhikkhu, while undergoing probation, is suspended, the probation is not established for the suspended one. If he is reinstated again, for him that same previous granting of probation stands: the probation that was given was well-given; the probation that was undergone was well-undergone; the remainder must be undergone. In the cases of those deserving of penance and so on, this is the same method.

Sace kassaci bhikkhuno itthiliṅgaṃ pātubhavati, tassa sāyeva upajjhā, sāyeva upasampadā, puna upajjhā na gahetabbā, upasampadā ca na kātabbā, bhikkhuupasampadato pabhuti yāva vassagaṇanā, sāyeva vassagaṇanā[M 0.0380], na ito paṭṭhāya vassagaṇanā kātabbā. Appatirūpaṃ dānissā bhikkhūnaṃ majjhe vasituṃ, tasmā bhikkhunupassayaṃ gantvā bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ vasitabbaṃ. Yā desanāgāminiyo vā vuṭṭhānagāminiyo vā āpattiyo bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīhi [V 0.0353] sādhāraṇā, tāsaṃ bhikkhunīhi kātabbaṃ, vinayakammameva bhikkhunīnaṃ santike kātabbaṃ. Yā pana bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīhi asādhāraṇā sukkavissaṭṭhiādikā āpattiyo, tāhi āpattīhi anāpatti, liṅge parivatte tā āpattiyo vuṭṭhitāva honti, puna pakatiliṅge uppannepi tāhi āpattīhi tassa anāpattiyeva. Bhikkhuniyā purisaliṅge pātubhūtepi eseva nayo. Vuttañcetaṃ –

If the female characteristic appears in a bhikkhu, his preceptor remains the same, and his higher ordination remains the same. A new preceptor should not be taken, nor should a new higher ordination be performed. The seniority in years is counted from his higher ordination as a bhikkhu; the seniority should not be counted anew from this point. It is now improper for this person to live among the bhikkhus; therefore, she should go to a bhikkhunī's residence and live with the bhikkhunīs. As for those offenses requiring confession or rehabilitation that are common to bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs, the disciplinary procedure for them should be carried out in the presence of the bhikkhunīs. However, for those offenses not common to bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs, such as the emission of semen, there is no offense. When the characteristic has changed, those offenses are considered absolved. Even if the original characteristic reappears, there is still no offense regarding those matters. This same principle applies when the male characteristic appears in a bhikkhunī. And this was stated:

“Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno itthiliṅgaṃ pātubhūtaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi bhikkhave taṃyeva upajjhaṃ, taṃyeva upasampadaṃ, tāniyeva vassāni bhikkhunīhi saṅgamituṃ, yā āpattiyo bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīhi sādhāraṇā, tā āpattiyo bhikkhunīnaṃ santike vuṭṭhātuṃ. Yā āpattiyo bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīhi asādhāraṇā, tāhi āpattīhi anāpatti.

Now at that time, the female characteristic had appeared in a certain bhikkhu. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, I allow that same preceptor, that same higher ordination, and those same years of seniority. I allow her to associate with the bhikkhunīs. As for the offenses that are common to bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs, I allow her to be absolved of them in the presence of the bhikkhunīs. As for the offenses that are not common to bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs, for those offenses, there is no offense.'

“Tena kho pana samayena aññatarissā bhikkhuniyā purisaliṅgaṃ pātubhūtaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi bhikkhave taṃyeva upajjhaṃ, taṃyeva upasampadaṃ, tāniyeva vassāni bhikkhūhi saṅgamituṃ, yā āpattiyo bhikkhunīnaṃ bhikkhūhi sādhāraṇā, tā āpattiyo bhikkhūnaṃ santike vuṭṭhātuṃ. Yā āpattiyo bhikkhunīnaṃ bhikkhūhi asādhāraṇā, tāhi āpattīhi anāpattī”ti (pārā. 69).

At that time, the male characteristic had appeared in a certain bhikkhunī. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, I allow that same preceptor, that same ordination, and those same years of seniority. I allow association with the bhikkhus. Whatever offenses of bhikkhunīs are common with bhikkhus, I allow absolution from those offenses in the presence of the bhikkhus. Whatever offenses of bhikkhunīs are not common with bhikkhus, for those offenses, there is no offense.' (pārā. 69).

247. Ayaṃ panettha pāḷimuttakavinicchayo (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.69) – imesu dvīsu liṅgesu purisaliṅgaṃ uttamaṃ, itthiliṅgaṃ hīnaṃ, tasmā purisaliṅgaṃ balavaakusalena antaradhāyati, itthiliṅgaṃ dubbalakusalena patiṭṭhāti. Itthiliṅgaṃ pana antaradhāyantaṃ dubbalaakusalena antaradhāyati, purisaliṅgaṃ balavakusalena patiṭṭhāti. Evaṃ ubhayampi akusalena antaradhāyati, kusalena paṭilabbhati.

247. Herein, this is the ruling apart from the Pāli: Among these two genders, the male gender is superior, and the female gender is inferior. Therefore, the male gender disappears through strong unwholesome kamma, and the female gender is established through weak wholesome kamma. But the female gender, when disappearing, disappears through weak unwholesome kamma, and the male gender is established through strong wholesome kamma. Thus, both disappear through unwholesome kamma and are regained through wholesome kamma.

Tattha [M 0.0381] sace dvinnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ekato sajjhāyaṃ vā dhammasākacchaṃ vā katvā ekāgāre nipajjitvā niddaṃ okkantānaṃ ekassa itthiliṅgaṃ pātubhavati, ubhinnampi sahaseyyāpatti hoti. So ce paṭibujjhitvā attano vippakāraṃ disvā dukkhī dummano rattibhāgeyeva itarassa āroceyya, tena samassāsetabbo “hotu mā cintayittha, vaṭṭasseveso doso, sammāsambuddhena dvāraṃ dinnaṃ, bhikkhu vā hotu bhikkhunī vā, anāvaṭo dhammo, avārito saggamaggo”ti. Samassāsetvā evaṃ vattabbaṃ “tumhehi bhikkhunupassayaṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭati, atthi pana te kāci sandiṭṭhā [V 0.0354] bhikkhuniyo”ti. Sacassā honti tādisā bhikkhuniyo, “atthī”ti, no ce honti, “natthī”ti vatvā so bhikkhu vattabbo “mama saṅgahaṃ karotha, idāni maṃ paṭhamaṃ bhikkhunupassayaṃ nethā”ti. Tena bhikkhunā taṃ gahetvā tassā vā sandiṭṭhānaṃ attano vā sandiṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ santikaṃ gantabbaṃ. Gacchantena ca na ekakena gantabbaṃ, catūhi pañcahi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ jotikañca kattaradaṇḍakañca gahetvā saṃvidahanaṃ parimocetvā “mayaṃ asukaṃ nāma ṭhānaṃ gacchāmā”ti gantabbaṃ. Sace bahigāme dūre vihāro hoti, antarāmagge gāmantaranadīpārarattivippavāsagaṇaohīyanāpattīhi anāpatti. Bhikkhunupassayaṃ gantvā tā bhikkhuniyo vattabbā “asukaṃ nāma bhikkhuṃ jānāthā”ti? “Āma, ayyā”ti. Tassa itthiliṅgaṃ pātubhūtaṃ, saṅgahaṃ dānissā karothāti. Tā ce “sādhu ayyā, idāni mayampi sajjhāyissāma, dhammaṃ sossāma, gacchatha tumhe”ti vatvā saṅgahaṃ karonti, ārādhikā ca honti saṅgāhikā lajjiniyo, tā kopetvā aññattha na gantabbaṃ. Gacchati ce, gāmantaranadīpārarattivippavāsagaṇaohīyanāpattīhi na muccati.

In this case, if of two bhikkhus who, having recited together or discussed the Dhamma together, lie down in the same dwelling and fall asleep, the female sex appears in one of them, both incur the offense of lying down together. If that person, upon waking, sees their own transformation and is distressed and unhappy, they should inform the other during the night itself. The other should console them, saying, 'Let it be. Do not worry. This is only a fault of the cycle of existence. The Perfectly Self-Enlightened One has given a way. Whether one is a bhikkhu or a bhikkhunī, the Dhamma is not obstructed, the path to the heavenly realm is not barred.' After consoling them, he should say this: 'It is proper for you to go to the bhikkhunīs’ residence. Are there any bhikkhunīs known to you?' If there are such bhikkhunīs for her, she should say, 'There are.' If there are not, having said, 'There are not,' that bhikkhu should be told: 'Please provide assistance for me. Now, first take me to the bhikkhunīs' residence.' That bhikkhu should take her and go to the presence of bhikkhunīs known to her or to those known to himself. And while going, he should not go alone, but together with four or five bhikkhus, taking a torch and a walking stick. Having been exempted from the offense of making a prior arrangement, and having announced, 'We are going to such-and-such a place,' they should go. If the monastery is far away, outside the village, there is no offense on the way for traveling to another village, crossing a river, being separated at night, or being left behind by the group. Having gone to the bhikkhunīs’ residence, those bhikkhunīs should be asked, 'Do you know the bhikkhu named so-and-so?' When they say, 'Yes, venerable sirs,' they should be told, 'The female sex has appeared for that person. Now, please provide assistance for this bhikkhunī.' If they say, 'Very well, venerable sirs. Now we too will recite and listen to the Dhamma. You may go,' and they provide assistance, and are receptive, helpful, and conscientious, one should not anger them and go elsewhere. If one does go, one is not freed from the offenses of traveling to another village, crossing a river, being separated at night, or being left behind by the group.

Sace pana lajjiniyo honti, na saṅgāhikāyo, aññattha gantuṃ labbhati. Sacepi alajjiniyo honti, saṅgahaṃ pana karonti, tāpi pariccajitvā aññattha gantuṃ labbhati. Sace lajjiniyo ca saṅgāhikā ca, ñātikā na honti, āsannagāme pana aññā ñātikā honti paṭijagganikā, tāsampi santikaṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭatīti vadanti. Gantvā sace bhikkhubhāvepi nissayapaṭipanno, patirūpāya bhikkhuniyā santike nissayo gahetabbo, mātikā vā vinayo vā uggahito suggahito, puna uggaṇhanakāraṇaṃ natthi. Sace bhikkhubhāvepi parisāvacaro, tassa santikeyeva upasampannā [M 0.0382] sūpasampannā, aññassa santike nissayo gahetabbo. Pubbe taṃ nissāya vasantehipi aññassa santike nissayo gahetabbo. Paripuṇṇavassasāmaṇerenapi aññassa santike upajjhā gahetabbā.

If, however, they are conscientious but not supportive, it is allowable to go elsewhere. Even if they are not conscientious but are supportive, it is allowable to abandon them and go elsewhere. If they are conscientious and supportive but are not relatives, and in a nearby village there are other relatives who can look after her, they say it is permissible to go to them. Having gone, if, even in the state of being a bhikkhu, she had undertaken dependence, dependence should be taken with a suitable bhikkhunī. If the Mātikā or the Vinaya has been learned and is well-grasped, there is no reason to learn it again. If, even in the state of being a bhikkhu, he was a teacher with a following, those ordained in his presence are considered well-ordained; she, however, must take dependence with another. Even those who previously lived in dependence on him must take dependence with another. Even a sāmaṇera of full standing must take a preceptor from another.

Yaṃ panassa bhikkhubhāve adhiṭṭhitaṃ ticīvarañca patto ca, taṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahati, puna adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Saṅkaccikā ca udakasāṭikā ca gahetabbā. Yaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ vā atirekapatto vā vinayakammaṃ katvā ṭhapito hoti, tampi sabbaṃ vinayakammaṃ vijahati, puna kātabbaṃ. Paṭiggahitatelamadhuphāṇitādīnipi paṭiggahaṇaṃ vijahanti. Sace paṭiggahaṇato sattame divase liṅgaṃ parivattati, puna paṭiggahetvā sattāhaṃ vaṭṭati. Yaṃ pana bhikkhukāle aññassa bhikkhuno santakaṃ paṭiggahitaṃ, taṃ paṭiggahaṇaṃ na vijahati. Yampi ubhinnaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ avibhajitvā [V 0.0355] ṭhapitaṃ, taṃ pakatatto rakkhati. Yaṃ pana vibhattaṃ etasseva santakaṃ, taṃ paṭiggahaṇaṃ vijahati. Vuttañcetaṃ parivāre –

Whatever he has determined for his bhikkhu status—the three robes and the bowl—that determination is relinquished; it must be determined anew. A breast-band and a bathing cloth should be taken. Any extra robe or extra bowl that was set aside after a formal act of Vinaya—that entire formal act is relinquished; it must be done again. The acceptance of oil, honey, molasses, and the like is also relinquished. If the sex changes on the seventh day from its acceptance, it must be accepted again, and it is then allowable for seven days. However, what was accepted on behalf of another bhikkhu during his time as a bhikkhu—that acceptance is not relinquished. What was set aside as common property for both without being divided—the one in a normal state protects it. But what was divided and belongs to this one alone—that acceptance is relinquished. And this is stated in the Parivāra:

“Telaṃ madhu phāṇitañcāpi sappiṃ, sāmaṃ gahetvā nikkhipeyya;

Avītivatte sattāhe, sati paccaye paribhuñjantassa āpatti;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā”ti. (pari. 480);

“Oil, honey, molasses, and also ghee, having received them oneself, one should set them aside; for one who consumes them when there is a reason, before seven days have passed, there is an offense. This question has been considered by the wise.”

Idañhi liṅgaparivattanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Paṭiggahaṇaṃ nāma liṅgaparivattanena, kālakiriyāya, sikkhāpaccakkhānena, hīnāyāvattanena, anupasampannassa dānena, anapekkhavissajjanena, acchinditvā gahaṇena ca vijahati. Tasmā sacepi harītakakhaṇḍampi paṭiggahetvā ṭhapitamatthi, sabbamassa paṭiggahaṇaṃ vijahati. Bhikkhuvihāre pana yaṃ kiñcissā santakaṃ paṭiggahetvā vā appaṭiggahetvā vā ṭhapitaṃ, sabbassa sāva issarā, āharāpetvā gahetabbaṃ. Yaṃ panettha thāvaraṃ tassā santakaṃ senāsanaṃ vā uparopakā vā, te yassicchati, tassa dātabbā. Terasasu sammutīsu yā bhikkhukāle laddhā sammuti, sabbā paṭippassambhati, purimikāya senāsanaggāho paṭippassambhati. Sace pacchimikāya senāsane gahite liṅgaṃ parivattati, bhikkhusaṅgho cassā uppannalābhaṃ dātukāmo hoti, apaloketvā dātabbo.

Indeed, this was said in reference to the change of gender. The state of having formally accepted an item is abandoned through a change of gender, through death, through renouncing the training, through returning to the lower life, through giving to one who is not fully ordained, through discarding without concern, and through its being taken after being snatched away. Therefore, even if a piece of myrobalan fruit has been formally received and set aside, for that person, the entire state of formal acceptance is abandoned. However, in the bhikkhu's monastery, whatever belonging of hers has been set aside, whether formally received or not formally received, she herself is the owner of it all; it should be taken after having it brought. Whatever immovable property belonging to her is here, such as a lodging or fruit-bearing trees, these should be given to whomever she wishes. Among the thirteen authorizations, whatever authorization was obtained during the time as a bhikkhu, all that authorization ceases. The taking of a lodging in the earlier rains-retreat ceases.
