If the gender changes after a lodging for the later rains-retreat has been taken, and the Saṅgha of bhikkhus wishes to give the accrued gain to her, it should be given after announcing it.

Sace bhikkhunīhi sādhāraṇāya paṭicchannāya āpattiyā parivasantassa liṅgaṃ parivattati, puna pakkhamānattameva dātabbaṃ. Sace mānattaṃ carantassa parivattati[M 0.0383], puna pakkhamānattameva dātabbaṃ. Sace ciṇṇamānattassa parivattati, bhikkhunīhi abbhānakammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Sace akusalavipāke parikkhīṇe pakkhamānattakāle punadeva liṅgaṃ parivattati, chārattaṃ mānattameva dātabbaṃ. Sace ciṇṇe pakkhamānatte parivattati, bhikkhūhi abbhānakammaṃ kātabbanti.

If, for one undergoing probation for a concealed offense common to bhikkhunīs, the gender changes, probation for half a month only should be given again. If it changes while one is undertaking mānatta, probation for half a month only should be given again. If it changes for one who has completed mānatta, the act of rehabilitation should be performed by the bhikkhunīs. If, when the result of unwholesome kamma is exhausted, the gender changes once again during the time of probation for half a month, mānatta for six nights only should be given. If it changes after the probation for half a month has been completed, the act of rehabilitation should be performed by the bhikkhus.

Bhikkhuniyā liṅgaparivattanepi vuttanayeneva sabbo vinicchayo veditabbo. Ayaṃ pana viseso – sace bhikkhunikāle āpannā sañcarittāpatti paṭicchannā hoti, parivāsadānaṃ natthi, chārattaṃ mānattameva dātabbaṃ. Sace pakkhamānattaṃ carantiyā liṅgaṃ parivattati, na tenattho, chārattaṃ mānattameva dātabbaṃ. Sace ciṇṇamānattāya parivattati, puna mānattaṃ adatvā bhikkhūhi abbhetabbo. Atha bhikkhūhi mānatte adinne puna liṅgaṃ parivattati, bhikkhunīhi pakkhamānattameva dātabbaṃ. Atha chārattaṃ mānattaṃ carantassa puna parivattati, pakkhamānattameva dātabbaṃ. Ciṇṇamānattassa pana liṅgaparivatte jāte bhikkhunīhi abbhānakammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Puna parivatte [V 0.0356] ca liṅge bhikkhunibhāve ṭhitāyapi yā āpattiyo pubbe paṭippassaddhā, tā suppaṭippassaddhā evāti.

In the case of a bhikkhunī's change of gender, the entire determination should be understood according to the method already stated. This, however, is the distinction: if a sañcaritta offense committed during the time as a bhikkhunī is concealed, the giving of parivāsa does not apply; mānatta for six nights only should be given. If the gender changes while she is undergoing pakkhamānatta, that is of no consequence; mānatta for six nights only should be given. If the gender changes after she has completed mānatta, he should be rehabilitated by the bhikkhus without mānatta being given again. Then, if the gender changes again before mānatta is given by the bhikkhus, pakkhamānatta only should be given by the bhikkhunīs. Then, if the gender changes again while he is undergoing mānatta for six nights, pakkhamānatta only should be given. For one who has completed mānatta, however, when a change of gender occurs, the act of rehabilitation should be performed by the bhikkhunīs. And should the gender change again, for one who was established in the state of a bhikkhunī, whatever offenses were previously settled are indeed well-settled.

248. Ito paraṃ pārivāsikādīnaṃ vattaṃ dassayissāma – pārivāsikena (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 76) bhikkhunā upajjhāyena hutvā na upasampādetabbaṃ, vattaṃ nikkhipitvā pana upasampādetuṃ vaṭṭati. Ācariyena hutvāpi kammavācā na sāvetabbā, aññasmiṃ asati vattaṃ nikkhipitvā sāvetuṃ vaṭṭati. Āgantukānaṃ nissayo na dātabbo. Yehipi pakatiyāva nissayo gahito, te vattabbā “ahaṃ vinayakammaṃ karomi, asukattherassa nāma santike nissayaṃ gaṇhatha, mayhaṃ vattaṃ mā karotha, mā maṃ gāmappavesanaṃ āpucchathā”ti. Sace evaṃ vuttepi karontiyeva, vāritakālato paṭṭhāya karontesupi anāpatti. Añño sāmaṇeropi na gahetabbo, upajjhaṃ datvā gahitasāmaṇeropi vattabbo “ahaṃ vinayakammaṃ karomi, mayhaṃ vattaṃ mā karotha, mā maṃ gāmappavesanaṃ āpucchathā”ti. Sace evaṃ vuttepi karontiyeva, vāritakālato paṭṭhāya karontesupi anāpatti. Na bhikkhunovādakasammuti sāditabbā, sammatenapi bhikkhuniyo na ovaditabbā, tasmā bhikkhusaṅghassa vattabbaṃ “bhante, ahaṃ vinayakammaṃ karomi, bhikkhunovādakaṃ [M 0.0384] jānāthā”ti. Paṭibalassa vā bhikkhussa bhāro kātabbo. Āgatā bhikkhuniyo “saṅghassa santikaṃ gacchatha, saṅgho vo ovādadāyakaṃ jānissatī”ti vā “ahaṃ vinayakammaṃ karomi, asukabhikkhussa nāma santikaṃ gacchatha, so vo ovādaṃ dassatī”ti vā vattabbā.

248. Hereafter, we will explain the duties of those undergoing probation and others. A bhikkhu on probation should not confer the higher ordination by acting as a preceptor; however, having suspended the observances, it is permissible to confer the higher ordination. Even when acting as an ācariya, he should not recite the formal act (kammavācā); if no one else is available, having suspended the observances, it is permissible to recite it. Dependence should not be given to visiting monks. Even those who have already taken dependence should be told: 'I am undergoing a disciplinary action. Take dependence from the elder named so-and-so. Do not perform duties for me, and do not ask my permission to enter the village.' If, even after being told this, they continue to do so, there is no offense for him from the time they were forbidden. Another novice should not be accepted. A novice who has already been accepted by him as preceptor should also be told: 'I am undergoing a disciplinary action. Do not perform duties for me, and do not ask my permission to enter the village.' If, even after being told this, they continue to do so, there is no offense for him from the time they were forbidden. The appointment as an instructor of bhikkhunīs is not to be accepted. Even one who has been appointed should say to the Sangha of bhikkhus: 'Venerable sirs, I am undergoing a disciplinary action; please designate an instructor for the bhikkhunīs.' Or, the responsibility should be given to a capable bhikkhu. Bhikkhunīs who have come should be told: 'Go to the Sangha of bhikkhus; the Sangha will designate an instructor for you,' or 'I am undergoing a disciplinary action. Go to the bhikkhu named so-and-so; he will give you instruction.'

Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena parivāso dinno hoti, sā āpatti na āpajjitabbā, aññā vā tādisikā tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarā, kammaṃ na garahitabbaṃ, kammikā na garahitabbā, na pakatattassa bhikkhuno uposatho ṭhapetabbo, na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā, palibodhatthāya vā pakkosanatthāya vā savacanīyaṃ na kātabbaṃ. Palibodhatthāya hi karonto “ahaṃ āyasmantaṃ imasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ savacanīyaṃ karomi, imamhā āvāsā parampi mā pakkama, yāva na taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ hotī”ti evaṃ karoti, pakkosanatthāya karonto “ahaṃ taṃ savacanīyaṃ karomi, ehi mayā saddhiṃ vinayadharānaṃ sammukhībhāvaṃ gacchāhī”ti evaṃ karoti, tadubhayampi na kātabbaṃ. Vihāre jeṭṭhakaṭṭhānaṃ na kātabbaṃ, pātimokkhuddesakena vā dhammajjhesakena vā na bhavitabbaṃ, napi terasasu sammutīsu ekasammutivasenapi issariyakammaṃ kātabbaṃ, “karotu me āyasmā okāsaṃ, ahaṃ taṃ vattukāmo”ti evaṃ pakatattassa okāso na kāretabbo, vatthunā vā āpattiyā vā na codetabbo, “ayaṃ te doso”ti na sāretabbo, bhikkhūhi aññamaññaṃ yojetvā [V 0.0357] kalaho na kāretabbo, saṅghattherena hutvā pakatattassa bhikkhuno purato na gantabbaṃ na nisīditabbaṃ, dvādasahatthaṃ upacāraṃ muñcitvā ekakeneva gantabbañceva nisīditabbañca, yo hoti saṅghassa āsanapariyanto seyyāpariyanto vihārapariyanto, so tassa dātabbo.

The offense for which the Sangha has granted probation should not be committed, nor any other similar offense, nor one that is more serious. The formal act should not be criticized, nor the bhikkhus who performed it. He should not suspend the Uposatha of a bhikkhu in a normal state, nor should he suspend the Pavāraṇā. A formal declaration of censure should not be made for the purpose of obstruction or for summoning. For one doing so for the purpose of obstruction acts thus: 'I declare the venerable one censurable in this matter. Do not depart from this residence to another as long as that legal issue is not settled.' One doing so for the purpose of summoning acts thus: 'I declare you censurable. Come, go with me into the presence of the experts in the Vinaya.' Neither of these should be done. The position of seniority in the monastery should not be assumed. One should not be a reciter of the Pātimokkha or one who invites a Dhamma discourse. Nor should an act of authority be performed by the power of even one appointment among the thirteen appointments. One should not have a bhikkhu in a normal state grant permission by saying, 'May the venerable one grant me permission; I wish to speak to you.' He should not accuse a bhikkhu in a normal state based on a matter or an offense. He should not remind one by saying, 'This is your fault.' A quarrel should not be caused by inciting bhikkhus against one another. Being the elder of the Sangha, he should not walk or sit in front of a bhikkhu in a normal state. He should walk and sit alone, leaving a perimeter of twelve cubits. Whatever is the last seat, the last lodging, and the last dwelling of the Sangha, that should be given to him.

Tattha āsanapariyanto nāma bhattaggādīsu saṅghanavakāsanaṃ, svassa dātabbo, tattha nisīditabbaṃ. Seyyāpariyanto nāma seyyānaṃ pariyanto sabbalāmakaṃ mañcapīṭhaṃ. Ayañhi vassaggena attano pattaṭṭhāne seyyaṃ gahetuṃ na labhati, sabbabhikkhūhi vicinitvā gahitāvasesā maṅgulagūthabharitā vettalatādivinaddhā lāmakaseyyāvassa dātabbā. Yathā ca seyyā, evaṃ vasanaāvāsopi vassaggena attano pattaṭṭhāne tassa na vaṭṭati, sabbabhikkhūhi vicinitvā gahitāvasesā pana rajohatabhūmi jatukamūsikabharitā [M 0.0385] paṇṇasālā assa dātabbā. Sace pakatattā sabbe rukkhamūlikā abbhokāsikā ca honti, channaṃ na upenti, sabbepi etehi vissaṭṭhāvāsā nāma honti, tesu yaṃ icchati, taṃ labhati.

Among these, 'the limit of seating' is the seat of the most junior monk in places such as the dining hall; that should be given to him, and he should sit there. 'The limit of bedding' is the very last of the beddings, the most inferior couch or chair. Indeed, this monk does not get to take bedding in the place that falls to him by seniority; only the inferior bedding remaining after all the monks have chosen and taken—one that is filled with bedbug droppings and bound with things such as rattan vines—should be given to him. And just as with the bedding, so too the dwelling place that falls to him by seniority is not allowable for him; but a leaf-hut remaining after all the monks have chosen and taken—one with a dust-covered floor, filled with bats and mice—should be given to him. If all the monks in good standing are tree-root dwellers and open-air dwellers, and do not enter a roofed dwelling, then all dwellings are called 'dwellings abandoned' by these monks. Among those, he obtains whichever one he desires.

Vassūpanāyikadivase paccayaṃ ekapasse ṭhatvā vassaggena gaṇhituṃ labhati, senāsanaṃ na labhati, nibaddhavassāvāsikaṃ senāsanaṃ gaṇhitu kāmena vattaṃ nikkhipitvā gahetabbaṃ. Ñātipavāritaṭṭhāne “ettake bhikkhū gahetvā āgacchathā”ti nimantitena “bhante, asukaṃ nāma kulaṃ bhikkhū nimantesi, etha, tattha gacchāmā”ti evaṃ saṃvidhāya bhikkhūnaṃ puresamaṇena vā pacchāsamaṇena vā hutvā kulāni na upasaṅkamitabbāni, “bhante, asukasmiṃ nāma gāme manussā bhikkhūnaṃ āgamanaṃ icchanti, sādhu vatassa, sace tesaṃ saṅgahaṃ kareyyāthā”ti evaṃ panassa vinayapariyāyena kathetuṃ vaṭṭati. Āgatāgatānaṃ ārocetuṃ harāyamānena āraññikadhutaṅgaṃ na samādātabbaṃ. Yenapi pakatiyā samādinnaṃ, tena dutiyaṃ bhikkhuṃ gahetvā araññe aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpetabbaṃ, na ekakena vatthabbaṃ. Tathā bhattaggādīsu āsanapariyante nisajjāya harāyamānena piṇḍapātikadhutaṅgampi na samādātabbaṃ. Yo pana pakatiyāva piṇḍapātiko, tassa paṭisedho natthi, na ca tappaccayā piṇḍapāto nīharāpetabbo “mā maṃ jāniṃsū”ti. Nīhaṭabhatto hutvā vihāreyeva nisīditvā bhuñjanto “rattiyo gaṇayissāmi, gacchato me bhikkhuṃ disvā anārocentassa ratticchedo siyā”ti iminā kāraṇena piṇḍapāto na nīharāpetabbo, “mā maṃ ekabhikkhupi jānātū”ti ca iminā ajjhāsayena vihāre sāmaṇerehi pacāpetvā bhuñjitumpi na labhati, gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisitabbameva. Gilānassa pana navakammaācariyupajjhāyakiccādipasutassa vā vihāreyeva acchituṃ vaṭṭati.

On the day of entering the Rains-residence, one is allowed to receive requisites for the Rains-residence by standing to one side according to seniority, but one does not receive a dwelling. One who wishes to take up a fixed Rains-residence dwelling should take it after laying aside one's duties. In a place where one is invited by relatives with the words, 'Take so many monks and come,' one should not, having become a leading or a following monk for the other monks, approach families by arranging it thus: 'Venerable sirs, such-and-such a family has invited the monks; come, let us go there.' However, it is proper for one to speak by way of the Vinaya, saying, 'Venerable sirs, in such-and-such a village, the people desire the coming of the monks. It would indeed be good if you would extend your support to them.' The forest-dweller's ascetic practice should not be undertaken by one who is ashamed to announce to monks as they arrive. And by one who has ordinarily undertaken it, he should cause the dawn to arise in the forest after taking a second monk; one should not dwell alone. Similarly, the alms-food-eater's ascetic practice should also not be undertaken by one who is ashamed of sitting at the end of the seats in a refectory and so on. But for one who is by nature an alms-food-eater, there is no prohibition. And on account of that probation, alms-food should not be caused to be brought out with the thought, 'Lest they know me.' Alms-food should not be caused to be brought out for this reason: 'Having had the meal brought, I will sit and eat right in the monastery and thus count the nights; for if I, while going about, see a monk and do not announce my status, there would be an interruption of my nights.' And with this intention, 'Let not even a single monk know me,' one is not allowed to have novices cook in the monastery and eat. One must indeed enter the village for alms-food. However, for one who is sick, or for one engaged in new construction work or the duties of a teacher, preceptor, and so on, it is permissible to stay right in the monastery.

Sacepi [V 0.0358] gāme anekasatā bhikkhū vicaranti, na sakkā hoti ārocetuṃ, gāmakāvāsaṃ gantvā sabhāgaṭṭhāne vasituṃ vaṭṭati. Yasmā “pārivāsikena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā āgantukena ārocetabbaṃ, āgantukassa ārocetabbaṃ, uposathe ārocetabbaṃ, pavāraṇāya ārocetabbaṃ, sace gilāno hoti, dūtenapi ārocetabba”nti (cūḷava. 76) vuttaṃ[M 0.0386], tasmā kañci vihāraṃ gatena āgantukena tattha bhikkhūnaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Sace sabbe ekaṭṭhāne ṭhite passati, ekaṭṭhāne ṭhiteneva ārocetabbaṃ. Atha rukkhamūlādīsu visuṃ ṭhitā honti, tattha tattha gantvā ārocetabbaṃ, sañcicca anārocentassa ratticchedo ca hoti, vattabhede ca dukkaṭaṃ. Atha vicinanto ekacce na passati, ratticchedova hoti, na vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ.

Even if hundreds of monks are wandering in a village and it is not possible to inform them, it is proper to go to a small village monastery and stay in a suitable place. Because it is said: 'O monks, a monk on probation who is a newcomer should inform; a newcomer should be informed; one should inform on the Uposatha; one should inform on the Pavāraṇā; if one is sick, one should inform even by a messenger' (Cūḷavagga 76). Therefore, a newcomer monk on probation who has gone to any monastery should inform the monks there. If he sees all of them staying in one place, he should inform them while staying in that one place. But if they are staying separately at the foot of trees and so on, he should go to each and every place and inform them. For one who intentionally does not inform, there is an interruption of the night and a dukkaṭa offense for the breach of duty. But if, while searching, he does not see some of them, there is only an interruption of the night, and not a dukkaṭa offense for the breach of duty.

Āgantukassapi attano vasanavihāraṃ āgatassa ekassa vā bahūnaṃ vā vuttanayeneva ārocetabbaṃ, ratticchedavattabhedāpi cettha vuttanayeneva veditabbā. Sace āgantukā muhuttaṃ vissamitvā vā avissamitvā eva vā vihāramajjhena gacchanti, tesampi ārocetabbaṃ. Sace tassa ajānantasseva gacchanti, ayañca gatakāle jānāti, gantvā ārocetabbaṃ, sampāpuṇituṃ vā sāvetuṃ vā asakkontassa ratticchedova hoti, na vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ. Yepi antovihāraṃ appavisitvā upacārasīmaṃ okkamitvā gacchanti, ayañca nesaṃ chattasaddaṃ vā ukkāsitasaddaṃ vā khipitasaddaṃ vā sutvā āgantukabhāvaṃ jānāti, gantvā ārocetabbaṃ, gatakāle jānantenapi anubandhitvā ārocetabbameva, sampāpuṇituṃ asakkontassa ratticchedova hoti, na vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ. Yopi rattiṃ āgantvā rattiṃyeva gacchati, sopissa ratticchedaṃ karoti, aññātattā pana vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ natthi. Sace ajānitvāva abbhānaṃ karoti, akatameva hotīti kurundiyaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmā adhikā rattiyo gahetvā kātabbaṃ. Ayaṃ apaṇṇakapaṭipadā.

It should be announced in the manner already stated to an incoming bhikkhu who has arrived at one's own dwelling monastery, whether to one or to many. Here, the interruption of the night and breaches of duty should also be understood in the manner already stated. If incoming bhikkhus, having rested for a moment or without having rested at all, go through the middle of the monastery, it should be announced to them also. If they go while that resident bhikkhu does not know, and this one comes to know after they have gone, he should go and announce it. For one who is unable to reach them or make them hear, only an interruption of the night occurs; there is no dukkaṭa offense for the breach of duty. For those bhikkhus also who, without entering the monastery, go after having stepped into the precincts—if this one, having heard the sound of their umbrella, the sound of them clearing their throat, or the sound of them sneezing, knows them to be incoming bhikkhus—he should go and announce it. Even for one who comes to know after they have gone, he should follow and indeed announce it. For one who is unable to reach them, only an interruption of the night occurs; there is no dukkaṭa offense for the breach of duty. An incoming bhikkhu who arrives at night and leaves that same night also causes an interruption of this one's night. However, because of not being known, there is no dukkaṭa offense for the breach of duty. If he performs the rehabilitation without knowing, it is as if not done; thus it is said in the Kurundī. Therefore, it should be done by taking additional nights. This is the unerring practice.

Nadīādīsu nāvāya gacchantampi paratīre ṭhitampi ākāse gacchantampi pabbatatalaaraññādīsu dūre ṭhitampi bhikkhuṃ disvā sace “bhikkhū”ti vavatthānaṃ atthi, nāvādīhi gantvā vā mahāsaddaṃ katvā vā vegena anubandhitvā vā ārocetabbaṃ, anārocentassa ratticchedo ceva vattabhede dukkaṭañca. Sace vāyamantopi sampāpuṇituṃ vā sāvetuṃ vā na sakkoti, ratticchedova hoti, na vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ. Saṅghasenābhayatthero pana visayāvisayena katheti “visaye kira anārocentassa ratticchedo ceva vattabhede dukkaṭañca hoti, avisaye pana ubhayampi natthī”ti. Karavīkatissatthero “samaṇo ayanti vavatthānameva pamāṇaṃ. Sacepi avisayo hoti, vattabhede dukkaṭameva natthi, ratticchedo pana hotiyevā”ti āha.

Having seen a bhikkhu—whether going by boat in a river or the like, standing on the other shore, going through the sky, or standing far away on a mountain top, in a forest, or the like—if there is the recognition, 'This is a bhikkhu,' it should be announced by going by boat or other means, by making a loud sound, or by following quickly. For one who does not announce it, there is an interruption of the night and a dukkaṭa offense for a breach of duty. If, even while striving, one is not able to reach him or make him hear, there is only an interruption of the night; there is no dukkaṭa offense for a breach of duty. The Elder Saṅghasenābhaya, however, speaks in terms of what is within range and what is not: 'It is said that for one who does not announce it when it is within range, there is both an interruption of the night and a dukkaṭa offense for a breach of duty. But when it is not within range, neither occurs.' The Elder Karavīkatissa said: 'The recognition alone, "This is a recluse," is the standard. Even if it is not within range, there is no dukkaṭa offense for a breach of duty, but the interruption of the night certainly occurs.'

Uposathadivase [M 0.0387][V 0.0359] “uposathaṃ sampāpuṇissāmā”ti āgantukā bhikkhū āgacchanti, iddhiyā gacchantāpi uposathabhāvaṃ ñatvā otaritvā uposathaṃ karonti, tasmā āgantukasodhanatthaṃ uposathadivasepi ārocetabbaṃ. Pavāraṇāyapi eseva nayo. Gantuṃ asamatthena gilānena bhikkhuṃ pesetvā ārocāpetabbaṃ, anupasampannaṃ pesetuṃ na vaṭṭati.

On the Uposatha day, visiting bhikkhus arrive thinking, 'We will attend the Uposatha.' Even those traveling by psychic power, upon knowing it is the Uposatha day, descend and perform the Uposatha. Therefore, for the purpose of clearing the visiting bhikkhus, it should also be announced on the Uposatha day. This same principle applies to the Pavāraṇā. A sick bhikkhu who is unable to go should have it announced by sending a bhikkhu; it is not allowable to send one who is not fully ordained.

Na pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā abhikkhuko nānāsaṃvāsakehi vā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo aññatra pakatattena aññatra antarāyā. Yattha hi ekopi bhikkhu natthi, tattha na vasitabbaṃ. Na hi tattha vuttharattiyo gaṇanūpikā honti. Dasavidhe antarāye pana sacepi rattiyo gaṇanūpikā na honti, antarāyato parimuccanatthāya gantabbameva. Tena vuttaṃ “aññatra antarāyā”ti. Nānāsaṃvāsakehi saddhiṃ vinayakammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, tesaṃ anārocanepi ratticchedo natthi, abhikkhukāvāsasadisameva hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “nānāsaṃvāsakehi vā sabhikkhuko”ti.

A bhikkhu under probation should not go from a residence with bhikkhus or from a non-residence to a residence or non-residence that is without bhikkhus, or to a residence or non-residence that has bhikkhus of a different communion, unless accompanied by a bhikkhu of normal standing or unless there is an obstacle. Indeed, where there is not even a single bhikkhu, one should not stay there, for there are no bhikkhus there who can count the nights spent. However, in the case of the ten kinds of obstacles, even if there are no bhikkhus who can count the nights, one must indeed go in order to be freed from the obstacle. Therefore, it is said, 'unless there is an obstacle.' It is not proper to perform a formal act of the Vinaya together with those of a different communion; even without informing them, there is no interruption of the nights. It is just like a residence without bhikkhus. Therefore, it is said, 'or [a residence] with bhikkhus of a different communion.'

Na pārivāsikena bhikkhunā pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ. Tattha āvāso nāma vasanatthāya katasenāsanaṃ. Anāvāso nāma cetiyagharaṃ bodhigharaṃ sammuñjanīaṭṭako dāruaṭṭako pānīyamāḷo vaccakuṭi dvārakoṭṭhakoti evamādi. “Etesu yattha katthaci ekacchanne chadanato udakapatanaṭṭhānaparicchinne okāse ukkhittakova vasituṃ na labhati, pārivāsiko pana antoāvāseyeva na labhatī”ti mahāpaccariyaṃ vuttaṃ. Mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ avisesena “udakapātena vārita”nti vuttaṃ. Kurundiyaṃ pana “etesu ettakesu pañcavaṇṇacchadanabaddhaṭṭhānesu pārivāsikassa ca ukkhittakassa ca pakatattena saddhiṃ udakapātena vārita”nti vuttaṃ. Tasmā nānūpacārepi ekacchanne na vaṭṭati. Sace panettha tadahupasampannepi pakatatte paṭhamaṃ pavisitvā nipannepi saṭṭhivassikopi pārivāsiko pacchā pavisitvā jānanto nipajjati, ratticchedo ceva vattabhede dukkaṭañca, ajānantassa ratticchedova, na vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ. Sace pana tasmiṃ nisinne pacchā pakatatto [M 0.0388] pavisitvā nipajjati, pārivāsiko ca jānāti, ratticchedo ceva vattabhede dukkaṭañca. No ce jānāti, ratticchedova, na vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ.

A bhikkhu on probation should not stay under the same roof with a bhikkhu of normal standing, whether in a residence or a non-residence. Here, a residence means a lodging made for dwelling. A non-residence means a shrine room, a Bodhi-tree shrine, a platform for brooms, a platform for wood, a water pavilion, a toilet, a gate-house, and so forth. According to the Mahāpaccarī, 'In any of these places where, under a single roof, the area is defined by the dripping of water from the roof, a bhikkhu under suspension is not allowed to stay. However, a bhikkhu on probation is not allowed inside the residence itself.' The Mahā-aṭṭhakathā states generally, 'Prohibited by the dripping of water.' The Kurundī, however, states, 'In these places roofed with five kinds of materials, it is prohibited by the dripping of water for both the probationer and the one under suspension to be with a bhikkhu of normal standing.' Therefore, even if in different precincts, it is not permissible under a single roof. If, herein, even if a bhikkhu of normal standing who was ordained that very day enters first and lies down, and later a sixty-vassa bhikkhu on probation enters knowingly and lies down, there is an interruption of his nights and an offense of wrong-doing for breaking the observance. If he does so unknowingly, only his nights are interrupted; there is no offense of wrong-doing for breaking the observance. If, however, while the probationer is sitting there, a bhikkhu of normal standing enters afterward and lies down, and the probationer knows, there is an interruption of his nights and an offense of wrong-doing for breaking the observance. If he does not know, only his nights are interrupted; there is no offense of wrong-doing for breaking the observance.

Pārivāsikena bhikkhunā pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ tadahupasampannampi disvā āsanā vuṭṭhātabbaṃ, vuṭṭhāya ca “ahaṃ iminā sukhanisinno vuṭṭhāpito”ti parammukhenapi na gantabbaṃ, “idaṃ ācariya āsanaṃ, ettha nisīdathā”ti evaṃ pakatatto bhikkhu āsanena nimantetabboyeva. Navakena [V 0.0360] pana “mahātheraṃ obaddhaṃ karomī”ti pārivāsikattherassa santikaṃ na gantabbaṃ. Pārivāsikena pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ na ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ, na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ, dvādasahatthaṃ pana upacāraṃ muñcitvā nisīdituṃ vaṭṭati. Pārivāsikena bhikkhunā pakatattena saddhiṃ na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ. Ettha pana akataparicchedāya bhūmiyā caṅkamante paricchedaṃ katvā vālukaṃ ākiritvā ālambanaṃ yojetvā katacaṅkame nīcepi na caṅkamitabbaṃ, ko pana vādo iṭṭhakacayena sampanne vedikāparikkhitte. Sace pana pākāraparikkhitto hoti, dvārakoṭṭhakayutto pabbatantaravanantaragumbantaresu vā suppaṭicchanno, tādise caṅkame caṅkamituṃ vaṭṭati, appaṭicchannepi upacāraṃ muñcitvā vaṭṭati.

A bhikkhu under probation, upon seeing a bhikkhu of normal standing—even one ordained that same day—should rise from his seat. Having risen, he should not pass by even with his back turned, thinking, 'I was made to rise by this one while I was sitting comfortably.' Instead, the bhikkhu of normal standing should indeed be invited to the seat with the words, 'Venerable sir, this is a seat, please sit here.' A junior bhikkhu, however, should not approach a senior bhikkhu under probation with the thought, 'I will cause trouble for the elder.' A bhikkhu under probation should not sit on the same seat with a bhikkhu of normal standing, nor sit on a high seat when the other is sitting on a low one, nor sit on a seat when the other is sitting on the ground. However, it is permissible to sit after leaving a surrounding space of twelve cubits. A bhikkhu under probation should not walk on the same walking path with a bhikkhu of normal standing, nor walk on a high walking path when the other is walking on a low one, nor walk on a walking path when the other is walking on the ground. Here, when a bhikkhu of normal standing is walking on unbounded ground, a probationer should not walk even on a low walking path that has been prepared by marking a boundary, scattering sand, and setting up a support—what then is to be said of one complete with brickwork and surrounded by a railing? However, if the walking path is enclosed by a wall, fitted with a gatehouse, or is well-concealed in the midst of mountains, forests, or thickets, it is permissible to walk on such a path. Even in an unconcealed place, it is permissible after leaving the surrounding space.

Pārivāsikena bhikkhunā pārivāsikavuḍḍhatarena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena mānattārahena mānattacārikena abbhānārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ. Ettha pana sace vuḍḍhatare pārivāsike paṭhamaṃ nipanne itaro jānanto pacchā nipajjati, ratticchedo cassa hoti, vattabhede ca dukkaṭaṃ. Vuḍḍhatarassa pana ratticchedova, na vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ. Ajānitvā nipajjati, dvinnampi vattabhedo natthi, ratticchedo pana hoti. Atha navakapārivāsike paṭhamaṃ nipanne vuḍḍhataro pacchā nipajjati, navako ca jānāti, ratti cassa chijjati, vattabhede ca dukkaṭaṃ hoti. Vuḍḍhatarassa ratticchedova, na vattabhedo. No ce jānāti, dvinnampi vattabhedo natthi, ratticchedo pana hoti. Sace apacchāpurimaṃ nipajjanti, vuḍḍhatarassa ratticchedova, itarassa vattabhedopīti kurundiyaṃ vuttaṃ.

A bhikkhu on probation should not live under one roof—whether in a residence or a non-residence—with a more senior bhikkhu on probation, a bhikkhu deserving to be sent back to the beginning, a bhikkhu deserving penance, a bhikkhu undergoing penance, or a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation. Here, if the more senior bhikkhu on probation lies down first and the other, knowing, lies down afterward, his nights are interrupted, and there is an offense of wrong-doing for the breach of observance. For the more senior one, however, only his nights are interrupted; there is no offense of wrong-doing for the breach of observance. If one lies down without knowing, for both there is no breach of observance, but their nights are interrupted. Then, if a junior bhikkhu on probation lies down first and the more senior one lies down afterward, and the junior knows, his nights are interrupted, and he commits an offense of wrong-doing for the breach of observance. For the more senior one, only his nights are interrupted; there is no breach of observance. If he does not know, for both there is no breach of observance, but their nights are interrupted. If they lie down without one preceding the other, for the more senior one, only his nights are interrupted; for the other, his nights are interrupted and there is also a breach of observance—so it is said in the Kurundī.

Dve [M 0.0389] pārivāsikā samavassā, eko paṭhamaṃ nipanno, eko jānantova pacchā nipajjati, ratti cassa chijjati, vattabhede ca dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ nipannassa ratticchedova, na vattabhedo. Sace pacchā nipajjantopi na jānāti, dvinnampi vattabhedo natthi, ratticchedo pana hoti. Sace dvepi apacchāpurimaṃ nipajjanti, dvinnampi ratticchedoyeva, na vattabhedo. Sace hi dve pārivāsikā ekato vaseyyuṃ, te aññamaññassa ajjhācāraṃ ñatvā agāravā vā vippaṭisārino vā hutvā taṃ vā āpattiṃ āpajjeyyuṃ tato pāpiṭṭhataraṃ vā, vibbhameyyuṃ vā, tasmā nesaṃ sahaseyyā sabbapakārena paṭikkhittā. Mūlāyapaṭikassanārahādayo cettha pārivāsikānaṃ pakatattaṭṭhāne ṭhitāti veditabbā. Tasmā pārivāsikena bhikkhunā mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena [V 0.0361] mānattārahena mānattacārikena abbhānārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ na ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ, na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na chamāya nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāya caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ.

Two probationers of the same seniority: if one lies down first, and the other, knowing, lies down afterward, his nights are interrupted, and there is an offense of wrong-doing for the breach of observance. For the one who lies down first, only his nights are interrupted; there is no breach of observance. If the one lying down afterward does not know, there is no breach of observance for either, but their nights are interrupted. If both lie down without one preceding the other, only their nights are interrupted for both; there is no breach of observance. For if two probationers were to live together, knowing each other’s misconduct, being disrespectful or regretful, they might commit that offense or something worse, or they might disrobe. Therefore, their sleeping together in the same lodging is prohibited in every way. Here, those deserving to be sent back to the beginning, etc., should be understood as standing in the position of bhikkhus of normal standing in relation to probationers. Therefore, a bhikkhu on probation should not sit on the same seat with a bhikkhu deserving to be sent back to the beginning, a bhikkhu deserving penance, a bhikkhu undergoing penance, or a bhikkhu deserving rehabilitation; nor sit on a high seat while the other sits on a low one; nor sit on a seat while the other sits on the ground. He should not walk on the same cloister walk, nor walk on a high cloister walk while the other walks on a low one, nor walk on a cloister walk while the other walks on the ground.

“Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sāditabbaṃ pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ āsanābhihāro seyyābhihāro pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ, yo sādiyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 75) vacanato pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ṭhapetvā navakataraṃ pārivāsikaṃ avasesānaṃ antamaso mūlāyapaṭikassanārahādīnampi abhivādanādiṃ sādiyantassa dukkaṭaṃ, saddhivihārikānampi sādiyantassa dukkaṭameva. Tasmā te vattabbā “ahaṃ vinayakammaṃ karomi, mayhaṃ vattaṃ mā karotha, mā maṃ gāmappavesanaṃ āpucchathā”ti. Sace saddhāpabbajitā kulaputtā “tumhe, bhante, tumhākaṃ vinayakammaṃ karothā”ti vatvā vattaṃ karonti, gāmappavesanampi āpucchantiyeva, vāritakālato paṭṭhāya anāpatti.

“Monks, a bhikkhu on probation should not accept from bhikkhus of normal standing the following: bowing, rising to greet, raising the joined palms, respectful conduct, the offering of a seat, the offering of a bed, foot-water, a footstool, a foot-wiping potsherd, the receiving of bowl and robe, or attending to the back during bathing. Whoever should accept them, incurs an offense of wrong-doing.” According to this, excepting a more junior probationer, for a probationer who accepts bowing and so forth from the remaining monks—even from those deserving of being sent back to the beginning, etc.—it is a wrong-doing. For one who accepts these services even from his co-residents, it is indeed a wrong-doing. Therefore, they should be told: “I am undergoing a Vinaya procedure; do not perform duties for me; do not ask my permission to enter the village.” If sons of good family who have gone forth out of faith, having said, “Venerable sir, you may perform your Vinaya procedure,” perform the duties and indeed ask permission for village entry, from the time they have been forbidden, there is no offense.

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pārivāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ mithū yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ āsanābhihāraṃ seyyābhihāraṃ pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ nahāne piṭṭhiparikamma”nti [M 0.0390] (cūḷava. 75) vacanato pana pārivāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ aññamaññaṃ yo yo vuḍḍho, tena tena navakatarassa abhivādanādiṃ sādituṃ vaṭṭati.

“Monks, I allow for bhikkhus on probation among one another, according to seniority: bowing, rising to greet, raising the joined palms, respectful conduct, the offering of a seat, the offering of a bed, foot-water, a footstool, a foot-wiping potsherd, the receiving of bowl and robe, and attending to the back during bathing.” According to this, among bhikkhus on probation, whichever one is elder is permitted to accept bowing and so forth from one who is more junior.

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pārivāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pañca yathāvuḍḍhaṃ uposathaṃ pavāraṇaṃ vassikasāṭikaṃ oṇojanaṃ bhatta”nti (cūḷava. 75) vacanato imāni uposathādīni pañca pakatattehipi saddhiṃ vuḍḍhapaṭipāṭiyā kātuṃ vaṭṭati, tasmā (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 75) pātimokkhe uddissamāne hatthapāse nisīdituṃ vaṭṭati. Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana “pāḷiyā anisīditvā pāḷiṃ vihāya hatthapāsaṃ amuñcantena nisīditabba”nti vuttaṃ. Pārisuddhiuposathe kariyamāne saṅghanavakaṭṭhāne nisīditvā tattheva nisinnena attano pāḷiyā pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo. Pavāraṇāyapi saṅghanavakaṭṭhāne nisīditvā tattheva nisinnena attano pāḷiyā pavāretabbaṃ. Saṅghena ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā bhājiyamānaṃ vassikasāṭikampi attano pattaṭṭhāne gahetuṃ vaṭṭati.

“I allow, monks, for bhikkhus on probation five things according to seniority: the Uposatha, the Pavāraṇā, the rainy-season robe, the distribution, and the meal.” According to this, it is permissible to perform these five things, beginning with the Uposatha, together with bhikkhus of normal standing in order of seniority. Therefore, when the Pātimokkha is being recited, it is permissible to sit within arm's reach. However, in the Mahāpaccariya it is said: “Without sitting in the line of seniority, having left the line, one should sit without letting go of arm's reach.” When the purification Uposatha is being performed, having sat in the place of the most junior monk of the Sangha, and while seated right there, the purification Uposatha should be performed according to one's own turn in seniority. For the Pavāraṇā also, having sat in the place of the most junior monk of the Sangha, and while seated right there, one should perform the Pavāraṇā according to one's own turn. When the Sangha, having struck the bell, is distributing the rainy-season robe, it is also permissible to receive it at the place where one's turn comes.

Oṇojananti [V 0.0362] vissajjanaṃ vuccati. Sace hi pārivāsikassa dve tīṇi uddesabhattādīni pāpuṇanti, aññā cassa puggalikabhattapaccāsā hoti, tāni paṭipāṭiyā gahetvā “bhante, heṭṭhā gāhetha, ajja mayhaṃ bhattapaccāsā atthi, sveva gaṇhissāmī”ti vatvā vissajjetabbāni. Evaṃ tāni punadivasesu gaṇhituṃ labhati. “Punadivase sabbapaṭhamaṃ tassa dātabba”nti kurundiyaṃ vuttaṃ. Yadi pana na gaṇhāti na vissajjeti, punadivase na labhati. Idaṃ oṇojanaṃ nāma pārivāsikasseva odissa anuññātaṃ. Kasmā? Tassa hi saṅghanavakaṭṭhāne nisinnassa bhattagge yāgukhajjakādīni pāpuṇanti vā na vā, tasmā “so bhikkhāhārena mā kilamitthā”ti idamassa saṅgahakaraṇatthāya odissa anuññātaṃ.

‘Oṇojana’ is called relinquishment. Indeed, if a probationer monk receives two or three designated meals and so forth, and he also has an expectation of a personal meal, having received them in order, he should relinquish them, saying: ‘Venerable sirs, let those below take this. Today I have an expectation of a meal; I will take it tomorrow.’ In this way, he is able to receive their equivalent on subsequent days. In the Kurundī it is said: ‘On the next day, it should be given to him first of all.’ But if he neither receives nor relinquishes it, he does not get it on the next day. This, called oṇojana, was allowed specifically for the probationer alone. Why? Because for that probationer monk sitting in the place of the most junior monk of the Sangha, gruel, hard food, and so forth may or may not reach him in the refectory. Therefore, so that ‘that monk may not become weary on account of alms-food,’ this relinquishment was allowed specifically for him for the purpose of giving him support.

Bhattanti āgatāgatehi vuḍḍhapaṭipāṭiyā gahetvā gantabbaṃ vihāre saṅghassa catussālabhattaṃ. Etaṃ yathāvuḍḍhaṃ labhati, pāḷiyā pana gantuṃ vā ṭhātuṃ vā na labhati, tasmā pāḷito osakkitvā hatthapāse ṭhitena hatthaṃ pasāretvā yathā seno nipatitvā gaṇhāti, evaṃ gaṇhitabbaṃ. Ārāmikasamaṇuddesehi āharāpetuṃ na labhati. Sace sayameva āharanti, vaṭṭati. Rañño mahāpeḷabhattepi eseva nayo. Catussālabhatte pana sace oṇojanaṃ kattukāmo hoti, attano atthāya ukkhitte [M 0.0391] piṇḍe “ajja me bhattaṃ atthi, sveva gaṇhissāmī”ti vattabbaṃ. “Punadivase dve piṇḍe labhatī”ti mahāpaccariyaṃ vuttaṃ. Uddesabhattādīnipi pāḷito osakkitvāva gahetabbāni, yattha pana nisīdāpetvā parivisanti, tattha sāmaṇerānaṃ jeṭṭhakena, bhikkhūnaṃ saṅghanavakena hutvā nisīditabbaṃ. Idaṃ pārivāsikavattaṃ.

By 'meal' is meant the Sangha's meal in the four-gabled hall at the monastery, which is to be approached and taken by those who have come, in order of seniority. This is obtained according to seniority, but it is not permissible to go or stand in the line. Therefore, having stepped back from the line, one should stand within arm's reach, extend the hand, and take it just as a hawk swoops down to seize. It is not permissible to have it brought by monastery attendants or novices. If they bring it of their own accord, it is permissible. This same method applies to the king's great basket-meal. However, in the case of the meal in the four-gabled hall, if one wishes to make a relinquishment, when the alms-food has been lifted up for oneself, one should say, 'Today I have food; I will receive it only tomorrow.' In the Mahāpaccariya it is said, 'On the next day, he receives two portions of alms-food.' Designated meals and so forth should also be received only after stepping back from the line. But in a place where they serve after having one seated, the probationer should sit, having become the most senior of the novices and the most junior of the monks. This is the observance for the probationer.

Mūlāyapaṭikassanārahānaṃ mānattārahānaṃ mānattacārikānaṃ abbhānārahānañca idameva vattanti veditabbaṃ. Mānattacārikassa vatte pana “devasikaṃ ārocetabba”nti viseso. Ratticchedesu ca “tayo kho, upāli, pārivāsikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā, sahavāso vippavāso anārocanā”ti (cūḷava. 83) vacanato yvāyaṃ “pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne”tiādinā nayena vutto sahavāso, yo ca ekasseva vāso, yā cāyaṃ āgantukādīnaṃ anārocanā, etesu tīsu ekenapi kāraṇena pārivāsikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedo hoti.

It should be understood that this very observance applies to those deserving of being sent back to the root, those deserving of penance, those undergoing penance, and those deserving of reinstatement. In the observance for one undergoing penance, however, there is this special rule: 'It must be reported daily.' And regarding the interruptions of nights, according to the passage, 'Upāli, there are three interruptions of nights for a probationer monk: co-residence, separate residence, and non-reporting.' Co-residence is that which is spoken of by the method beginning 'with a regular monk under one roof...'; separate residence is the residence of one alone; and non-reporting is the non-reporting to incoming monks and so forth. In these three cases, by even one of these reasons, a probationer monk has an interruption of nights.

Mānattacārikassa pana “cattāro kho, upāli, mānattacārikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā, sahavāso, vippavāso, anārocanā, ūne gaṇe caraṇa”nti vacanato imesu catūsu kāraṇesu ekenapi [V 0.0363] ratticchedo hoti. Gaṇoti cettha cattāro vā atirekā vā. Tasmā sacepi tīhi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ vasati, ratticchedo hotiyeva.

However, for a monk undergoing penance, according to the statement, 'O Upāli, there are four interruptions of nights for a monk undergoing penance: co-residence, separate residence, not announcing the observance, and practicing in an incomplete group,' by even one of these four reasons an interruption of nights occurs. And here, 'group' means four or more monks. Therefore, even if he dwells with three monks, an interruption of nights certainly occurs.

Iti pāḷimuttakavinayavinicchayasaṅgahe

Thus in the Compendium of Vinaya Decisions Independent of the Pāḷi Text.

Garukāpattivuṭṭhānavinicchayakathā samattā.

The Discussion on Decisions Regarding Rising from Serious Offenses is concluded.

33. Kammākammavinicchayakathā

33. The Discussion on Decisions Concerning Kamma and Akamma

249. Kammākammanti [V 0.0364] ettha (pari. 482-484) pana kammāni cattāri – apalokanakammaṃ ñattikammaṃ ñattidutiyakammaṃ ñatticatutthakammanti. Imāni cattāri kammāni katihākārehi vipajjanti? Pañcahākārehi vipajjanti – vatthuto vā ñattito vā anussāvanato vā sīmato vā parisato vā.

249. Now, here concerning kamma and akamma, there are four kinds of kamma: the act of seeking consent (apalokanakamma), the act of making a motion (ñattikamma), the act of making a motion with one announcement (ñattidutiyakamma), and the act of making a motion with three announcements (ñatticatutthakamma). In how many ways do these four acts fail? They fail in five ways: on account of the basis (vatthu), on account of the motion (ñatti), on account of the announcement (anussāvana), on account of the boundary (sīmā), or on account of the assembly (parisā).

Kathaṃ [M 0.0392] vatthuto kammāni vipajjanti? Sammukhākaraṇīyaṃ kammaṃ asammukhā karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Paṭipucchākaraṇīyaṃ kammaṃ apaṭipucchā karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Paṭiññāya karaṇīyaṃ kammaṃ apaṭiññāya karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Sativinayārahassa amūḷhavinayaṃ deti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Amūḷhavinayārahassa tassa pāpiyasikakammaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Tassa pāpiyasikakammārahassa tajjanīyakammaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Tajjanīyakammārahassa niyassakammaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Niyassakammārahassa pabbājanīyakammaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Pabbājanīyakammārahassa paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Paṭisāraṇīyakammārahassa ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Ukkhepanīyakammārahassa parivāsaṃ deti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Parivāsārahassa mūlāya paṭikassati, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Mūlāyapaṭikassanārahassa mānattaṃ deti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Mānattārahaṃ abbheti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Abbhānārahaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Anuposathe uposathaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Apavāraṇāya pavāreti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Paṇḍakaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Theyyasaṃvāsakaṃ, titthiyapakkantakaṃ, tiracchānagataṃ, mātughātakaṃ, pitughātakaṃ, arahantaghātakaṃ, bhikkhunidūsakaṃ, saṅghabhedakaṃ, lohituppādakaṃ, ubhatobyañjanakaṃ, ūnavīsativassaṃ puggalaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Evaṃ vatthuto kammāni vipajjanti.

How do acts fail on account of the basis (vatthu)? When an act that should be done face to face is done not face to face, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. When an act that should be done with questioning is done without questioning, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. When an act that should be done with acknowledgement is done without acknowledgement, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Giving a verdict of innocence (amūḷhavinaya) to one deserving a verdict reached through mindfulness (sativinaya), it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Imposing a heavier penalty (tassapāpiyasikakamma) on one deserving a verdict of innocence, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Imposing censure (tajjanīyakamma) on one deserving a heavier penalty, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Imposing dependence (niyassakamma) on one deserving censure, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Imposing banishment (pabbājanīyakamma) on one deserving dependence, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Imposing an act of reconciliation (paṭisāraṇīyakamma) on one deserving banishment, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Imposing suspension (ukkhepanīyakamma) on one deserving an act of reconciliation, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Granting probation (parivāsa) to one deserving suspension, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Reinstating to the beginning (mūlāya paṭikassati) one deserving probation, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Granting penance (mānatta) to one deserving to be reinstated to the beginning, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Rehabilitating (abbheti) one deserving penance, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Ordaining one who is worthy of rehabilitation, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Holding the Uposatha on a non-Uposatha day, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Performing the Pavāraṇā when it is not the time for Pavāraṇā, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. Ordaining a eunuch (paṇḍaka), a thief-in-disguise-of-a-monk (theyyasaṃvāsaka), one who has gone over to another sect (titthiyapakkantaka), an animal in human form (tiracchānagata), a matricide (mātughātaka), a patricide (pitughātaka), a killer of an Arahant (arahantaghātaka), a violator of a bhikkhunī (bhikkhunidūsaka), a schismatic (saṅghabhedaka), one who has wounded a Buddha (lohituppādaka), a hermaphrodite (ubhatobyañjanaka), or a person under twenty years of age, it is an unlawful act, failed on account of the basis. In this way, acts fail on account of the basis.

Kathaṃ ñattito kammāni vipajjanti? Pañcahākārehi ñattito kammāni vipajjanti – vatthuṃ na parāmasati, saṅghaṃ na parāmasati, puggalaṃ na parāmasati, ñattiṃ na parāmasati, pacchā vā ñattiṃ ṭhapeti. Imehi pañcahākārehi ñattito kammāni vipajjanti.

How do acts fail on account of the motion (ñatti)? Acts fail on account of the motion in five ways: by not referring to the basis, by not referring to the Saṅgha, by not referring to the individual, by not referring to the motion, or by presenting the motion afterward. In these five ways, acts fail on account of the motion.

Kathaṃ [V 0.0365] anussāvanato kammāni vipajjanti? Pañcahākārehi anussāvanato kammāni vipajjanti – vatthuṃ na parāmasati, saṅghaṃ na parāmasati, puggalaṃ na parāmasati, sāvanaṃ hāpeti, akāle vā sāveti. Imehi pañcahākārehi anussāvanato kammāni vipajjanti.

How do acts fail on account of the announcement (anussāvana)? Acts fail on account of the announcement in five ways: by not referring to the basis, by not referring to the Saṅgha, by not referring to the individual, by omitting the announcement, or by announcing at the wrong time. In these five ways, acts fail on account of the announcement.

Kathaṃ sīmato kammāni vipajjanti? Ekādasahi ākārehi sīmato kammāni vipajjanti – atikhuddakaṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, atimahatiṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, khaṇḍanimittaṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, chāyānimittaṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, animittaṃ sīmaṃ [M 0.0393] sammannati, bahisīme ṭhito sīmaṃ sammannati, nadiyā sīmaṃ sammannati, samudde sīmaṃ sammannati, jātassare sīmaṃ sammannati, sīmāya sīmaṃ sambhindati, sīmāya sīmaṃ ajjhottharati. Imehi ekādasahi ākārehi sīmato kammāni vipajjanti.

How do acts fail on account of the boundary (sīmā)? Acts fail on account of the boundary in eleven ways: by designating a boundary that is too small; by designating a boundary that is too large; by designating a boundary with broken markers; by designating a boundary with a shadow as a marker; by designating a boundary without markers; by designating a boundary while standing outside of it; by designating a boundary in a river; by designating a boundary in the ocean; by designating a boundary in a natural lake; by connecting a boundary with another boundary; or by overlapping a boundary with another boundary. In these eleven ways, acts fail on account of the boundary.

Kathaṃ parisato kammāni vipajjanti? Dvādasahi ākārehi parisato kammāni vipajjanti – catuvaggakaraṇīye kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te anāgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti, catuvaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti, catuvaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti.

How do acts fail on account of the assembly (parisā)? Acts fail on account of the assembly in twelve ways. In an act to be done by a quorum of four: when the bhikkhus eligible for the act have not arrived, the consent of those entitled to give it has not been brought, and those present object. In an act to be done by a quorum of four: when the bhikkhus eligible for the act have arrived, but the consent of those entitled to give it has not been brought, and those present object. In an act to be done by a quorum of four: when the bhikkhus eligible for the act have arrived and the consent of those entitled to give it has been brought, yet those present object.

Pañcavaggakaraṇe kamme…pe… dasavaggakaraṇe kamme…pe… vīsativaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te anāgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti, vīsativaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti, vīsativaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti. Imehi dvādasahi ākārehi parisato kammāni vipajjanti.

In an act to be performed by a quorum of five… and so on… in an act to be performed by a quorum of ten… and so on… in an act to be performed by a quorum of twenty: when the bhikkhus eligible for the act have not arrived, the consent of those entitled to give it has not been brought, and those present object. In an act to be performed by a quorum of twenty: when the bhikkhus eligible for the act have arrived, but the consent of those entitled to give it has not been brought, and those present object. In an act to be performed by a quorum of twenty: when the bhikkhus eligible for the act have arrived and the consent of those entitled to give it has been brought, yet those present object. In these twelve ways, acts fail on account of the assembly.

Catuvaggakaraṇe kamme cattāro bhikkhū pakatattā kammappattā, avasesā pakatattā chandārahā. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, so neva kammappatto nāpi chandāraho, apica kammāraho. Pañcavaggakaraṇe kamme pañca bhikkhū pakatattā kammappattā, avasesā pakatattā chandārahā. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, so neva kammappatto nāpi chandāraho, apica kammāraho[V 0.0366]. Dasavaggakaraṇe kamme dasa bhikkhū pakatattā kammappattā, avasesā pakatattā chandārahā. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, so neva kammappatto nāpi chandāraho, apica kammāraho. Vīsativaggakaraṇe kamme vīsati bhikkhū pakatattā kammappattā, avasesā [M 0.0394] pakatattā chandārahā. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, so neva kammappatto nāpi chandāraho, apica kammāraho.

In an act to be performed by a group of four, four monks, being qualified, are eligible for the act; the remaining qualified monks are eligible to give their consent. The one for whom the Saṅgha performs the act is neither eligible for the act nor eligible to give consent, but is indeed subject to the act. In an act to be performed by a group of five, five monks, being qualified, are eligible for the act; the remaining qualified monks are eligible to give their consent. The one for whom the Saṅgha performs the act is neither eligible for the act nor eligible to give consent, but is indeed subject to the act. In an act to be performed by a group of ten, ten monks, being qualified, are eligible for the act; the remaining qualified monks are eligible to give their consent. The one for whom the Saṅgha performs the act is neither eligible for the act nor eligible to give consent, but is indeed subject to the act. In an act to be performed by a group of twenty, twenty monks, being qualified, are eligible for the act; the remaining qualified monks are eligible to give their consent. The one for whom the Saṅgha performs the act is neither eligible for the act nor eligible to give consent, but is indeed subject to the act.

250. Apalokanakammaṃ kati ṭhānāni gacchati? Ñattikammaṃ, ñattidutiyakammaṃ, ñatticatutthakammaṃ kati ṭhānāni gacchati? Apalokanakammaṃ pañca ṭhānāni gacchati. Ñattikammaṃ nava ṭhānāni gacchati. Ñattidutiyakammaṃ satta ṭhānāni gacchati. Ñatticatutthakammaṃ satta ṭhānāni gacchati.

250. To how many instances does the act of announcement apply? To how many instances do the act by motion, the act with motion as the second, and the act with motion as the fourth apply? The act of announcement applies to five instances. The act by motion applies to nine instances. The act with motion as the second applies to seven instances. The act with motion as the fourth applies to seven instances.

Apalokanakammaṃ katamāni pañca ṭhānāni gacchati? Osāraṇaṃ nissāraṇaṃ bhaṇḍukammaṃ brahmadaṇḍaṃ kammalakkhaṇaññeva pañcamaṃ. Apalokanakammaṃ imāni pañca ṭhānāni gacchati.

To which five instances does the act of announcement apply? Reinstatement, expulsion, the act of shaving the head, the Brahma-penalty, and fifth, an act that is merely a characteristic of an act. The act of announcement applies to these five instances.

Ñattikammaṃ katamāni nava ṭhānāni gacchati? Osāraṇaṃ nissāraṇaṃ uposathaṃ pavāraṇaṃ sammutiṃ dānaṃ paṭiggahaṇaṃ paccukkaḍḍhanaṃ kammalakkhaṇaññeva navamaṃ. Ñattikammaṃ imāni nava ṭhānāni gacchati.

To which nine instances does the act by motion apply? Inclusion, sending forth, the Uposatha, the Pavāraṇā, designation, giving, acceptance of an offense, revocation of the Pavāraṇā, and ninth, an act that is merely a characteristic of an act. The act by motion applies to these nine instances.

Ñattidutiyakammaṃ katamāni satta ṭhānāni gacchati? Osāraṇaṃ nissāraṇaṃ sammutiṃ dānaṃ uddharaṇaṃ desanaṃ kammalakkhaṇaññeva sattamaṃ. Ñattidutiyakammaṃ imāni satta ṭhānāni gacchati.

To which seven instances does the act with motion as the second apply? Reinstatement, expulsion, designation, giving, withdrawal, announcing a site, and seventh, an act that is merely a characteristic of an act. The act with motion as the second applies to these seven instances.

Ñatticatutthakammaṃ katamāni satta ṭhānāni gacchati? Osāraṇaṃ nissāraṇaṃ sammutiṃ dānaṃ niggahaṃ samanubhāsanaṃ kammalakkhaṇaññeva sattamaṃ. Ñatticatutthakammaṃ imāni satta ṭhānāni gacchati. Ayaṃ tāva pāḷinayo.

To which seven instances does the act with motion as the fourth apply? Reinstatement, expulsion, designation, giving, censure, formal admonition, and seventh, an act that is merely a characteristic of an act. The act with motion as the fourth applies to these seven instances. This, for now, is the method according to the Pāli.

251. Ayaṃ panettha ādito paṭṭhāya vinicchayakathā (pari. aṭṭha. 482) – apalokanakammaṃ nāma sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghaṃ sodhetvā chandārahānaṃ chandaṃ āharitvā samaggassa saṅghassa anumatiyā tikkhattuṃ sāvetvā kattabbakammaṃ. Ñattikammaṃ nāma vuttanayeneva samaggassa saṅghassa anumatiyā ekāya ñattiyā kattabbakammaṃ. Ñattidutiyakammaṃ nāma vuttanayeneva samaggassa saṅghassa anumatiyā ekāya ñattiyā ekāya ca anussāvanāyāti evaṃ ñattidutiyāya anussāvanāya [V 0.0367] kattabbakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthakammaṃ nāma vuttanayeneva samaggassa saṅghassa anumatiyā ekāya ñattiyā tīhi ca anussāvanāhīti evaṃ ñatticatutthāhi tīhi anussāvanāhi kattabbakammaṃ.

251. Herein, from the beginning, is the discourse on the determination. The act of announcement is an act to be done after having purified the Sangha present in the boundary, having brought the consent of those worthy of giving consent, and having announced it three times with the approval of the united Sangha. The act by motion is an act to be done with the approval of the united Sangha by means of a single motion, in the manner already stated. The act with motion as the second is an act to be done with the approval of the united Sangha by means of a single motion and a single proclamation, in the manner already stated—thus, an act to be done by a proclamation having the motion as its second part. The act with motion as the fourth is an act to be done with the approval of the united Sangha by means of a single motion and three proclamations, in the manner already stated—thus, an act to be done by three proclamations having the motion as their fourth part.

Tatra [M 0.0395] apalokanakammaṃ apaloketvāva kātabbaṃ, ñattikammādivasena na kātabbaṃ. Ñattikammampi ekaṃ ñattiṃ ṭhapetvāva kātabbaṃ, apalokanakammādivasena na kātabbaṃ. Ñattidutiyakammaṃ pana apaloketvā kātabbampi akātabbampi atthi. Tattha sīmāsammuti sīmāsamūhanaṃ kathinadānaṃ kathinuddhāro kuṭivatthudesanā vihāravatthudesanāti imāni chakammāni garukāni apaloketvā kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, ñattidutiyakammavācaṃ sāvetvāva kātabbāni. Avasesā terasa sammutiyo senāsanaggāhakamatakacīvaradānādisammutiyo cāti etāni lahukakammāni, apaloketvāpi kātuṃ vaṭṭanti, ñattikammañatticatutthakammavasena pana na kātabbameva. “Ñatticatutthakammavasena kayiramānaṃ daḷhataraṃ hoti, tasmā kātabba”nti ekacce vadanti. Evaṃ pana sati kammasaṅkaro hoti, tasmā na kātabbanti paṭikkhittameva. Sace pana akkharaparihīnaṃ vā padaparihīnaṃ vā duruttapadaṃ vā hoti, tassa sodhanatthaṃ punappunaṃ vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Idaṃ akuppakammassa daḷhīkammaṃ hoti, kuppakamme kammaṃ hutvā tiṭṭhati. Ñatticatutthakammaṃ ñattiñca tisso ca kammavācāyo sāvetvāva kātabbaṃ, apalokanakammādivasena na kātabbaṃ.

Therein, the act of announcement should be done only by announcement; it should not be done by means of an act by motion or other acts. The act by motion, too, should be done by establishing only one motion; it should not be done by means of an act of announcement or other acts. However, there are cases where the act with motion as the second should be done by announcement and cases where it should not be done by announcement. Among these, these six weighty acts—the designation of a boundary, the removal of a boundary, the granting of the kathina, the withdrawal of the kathina, the declaration of a hut site, and the declaration of a monastery site—should not be done by announcement; they must be done by having announced the formal declaration with motion as the second. The remaining thirteen designations, and designations such as the appointment of a distributor of lodgings and the giving of a deceased monk's robes—these are lighter acts; they may be done even by announcement. However, they should not be done by means of an act by motion or an act with motion as the fourth. Some say, 'If it is done by means of an act with motion as the fourth, it becomes stronger, therefore it should be done.' But if this were the case, there would be a mixing of acts, and therefore it has been rejected. However, if there is a deficiency in letters, or a deficiency in words, or an ill-spoken word, it is permissible to repeat it for the sake of correction. This is the strengthening of an unshakeable act; in a shakeable act, the act stands as performed. The act with motion as the fourth must be done by having announced the motion and the three formal declarations; it should not be done by means of an act of announcement or other acts.

Sammukhākaraṇīyaṃ kammaṃ asammukhā karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammanti ettha pana atthi kammaṃ sammukhākaraṇīyaṃ, atthi kammaṃ asammukhākaraṇīyaṃ. Tattha asammukhākaraṇīyaṃ nāma dūtenūpasampadā, pattanikkujjanaṃ, pattukkujjanaṃ, ummattakassa bhikkhuno ummattakasammuti, sekkhānaṃ kulānaṃ sekkhasammuti, channassa bhikkhuno brahmadaṇḍo, devadattassa pakāsanīyakammaṃ, apasādanīyaṃ dassentassa bhikkhuno bhikkhunisaṅghena kātabbaṃ avandiyakammanti aṭṭhavidhaṃ hoti. Idaṃ aṭṭhavidhampi kammaṃ asammukhā kataṃ sukataṃ hoti akuppaṃ, sesāni sabbakammāni sammukhā eva kātabbāni. Saṅghasammukhatā dhammasammukhatā vinayasammukhatā puggalasammukhatāti imaṃ catubbidhaṃ sammukhāvinayaṃ upanetvāva kātabbāni. Evaṃ katāni hi sukatāni honti, evaṃ akatāni panetāni imaṃ sammukhāvinayasaṅkhātaṃ vatthuṃ vinā katattā vatthuvipannāni nāma honti. Tena vuttaṃ “sammukhākaraṇīyaṃ kammaṃ asammukhā karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakamma”nti. Paṭipucchākaraṇīyādīsupi paṭipucchādikaraṇameva vatthu, taṃ vatthuṃ vinā katattā tesampi vatthuvipannatā veditabbā. Apica ūnavīsativassaṃ vā antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannapubbaṃ vā ekādasasu [M 0.0396][V 0.0368] vā abhabbapuggalesu aññataraṃ upasampādentassapi vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ hoti. Ayaṃ vatthuto kammavipattiyaṃ vinicchayo.

“A legal act that should be performed in the presence is done in absence—this is a defective basis, an unlawful act.” Herein, however, there are acts to be done in the presence and acts to be done in absence. Among these, an act to be done in absence is of eight kinds: ordination by messenger, turning the almsbowl upside down, turning the almsbowl upright, the designation of an insane monk as insane, the designation of trainee families as trainees, the imposing of the Brahma-penalty on the monk Channa, the proclamation act against Devadatta, and the act of non-veneration to be performed by the community of nuns against a monk who shows a feature inspiring disrespect. These eight kinds of acts, when done in absence, are well-done and irreversible. All other acts must be done only in the presence. They must be done only after having brought about this fourfold presence-Vinaya: the presence of the Sangha, the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, and the presence of the individual. For acts done in this way are well-done, whereas those not done in this way are called ‘defective in basis’ because they are done without this basis, which is called the ‘presence-Vinaya’. Therefore it is said: “A legal act that should be performed in the presence is done in absence—this is a defective basis, an unlawful act.” Also in the case of acts to be done by interrogation and so forth, the very act of interrogation and so forth is the basis; because they are done without that basis, their defectiveness in basis should be understood. Moreover, ordaining someone under twenty years of age, or someone who has previously committed an ultimate offense, or any of the eleven disqualified individuals also results in an unlawful act that is defective in basis. This is the determination regarding the failure of an act in terms of its basis.

Ñattito vipattiyaṃ pana vatthuṃ na parāmasatīti yassa upasampadādikammaṃ karoti, taṃ na parāmasati, tassa nāmaṃ na gaṇhāti. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ dhammarakkhito āyasmato buddharakkhitassa upasampadāpekkho”ti vattabbe “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, āyasmato buddharakkhitassa upasampadāpekkho”ti vadati. Evaṃ vatthuṃ na parāmasati.

In the case of failure by way of the motion, as for 'one does not refer to the subject matter': one does not refer to that person for whom one performs the act of ordination, etc.; one does not state his name. When it should be said, 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This Dhammarakkhita is the ordination candidate of the venerable Buddharakkhita,' one says, 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The ordination candidate of the venerable Buddharakkhita.' In this way, one does not refer to the subject matter.

Saṅghaṃ na parāmasatīti saṅghassa nāmaṃ na gaṇhāti. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ dhammarakkhito”ti vattabbe “suṇātu me, bhante, ayaṃ dhammarakkhito”ti vadati. Evaṃ saṅghaṃ na parāmasati.

As for 'one does not refer to the Sangha': one does not state the name of the Sangha. When it should be said, 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This is Dhammarakkhita,' one says, 'Venerable sirs, may you hear me. This is Dhammarakkhita.' In this way, one does not refer to the Sangha.

Puggalaṃ na parāmasatīti yo upasampadāpekkhassa upajjhāyo, taṃ na parāmasati, tassa nāmaṃ na gaṇhāti. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ dhammarakkhito āyasmato buddharakkhitassa upasampadāpekkho”ti vattabbe “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ dhammarakkhito upasampadāpekkho”ti vadati. Evaṃ puggalaṃ na parāmasati.

As for 'one does not refer to the person': one does not refer to him who is the preceptor of the ordination candidate; one does not state his name. When it should be said, 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This Dhammarakkhita is the ordination candidate of the venerable Buddharakkhita,' one says, 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This Dhammarakkhita is an ordination candidate.' In this way, one does not refer to the person.

Ñattiṃ na parāmasatīti sabbena sabbaṃ ñattiṃ na parāmasati, ñattidutiyakamme ñattiṃ aṭṭhapetvā dvikkhattuṃ kammavācāya eva anussāvanakammaṃ karoti, ñatticatutthakammepi ñattiṃ aṭṭhapetvā catukkhattuṃ kammavācāya eva anussāvanakammaṃ karoti. Evaṃ ñattiṃ na parāmasati.

As for 'one does not refer to the motion': one does not refer to the motion at all. In an act with a motion and one proclamation, having set aside the motion, one performs the act of announcement only by the formal declaration twice. And also in an act with a motion and three proclamations, having set aside the motion, one performs the act of announcement only by the formal declaration four times. In this way, one does not refer to the motion.

Pacchā vā ñattiṃ ṭhapetīti paṭhamaṃ kammavācāya anussāvanakammaṃ katvā “esā ñattī”ti vatvā “khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti vadati. Evaṃ pacchā ñattiṃ ṭhapeti. Iti imehi pañcahākārehi ñattito kammāni vipajjanti.

As for 'or one places the motion afterwards': first, having performed the act of announcement by the formal declaration and having said, 'This is the motion,' one says, 'It is approved by the Sangha, therefore it is silent; thus do I hold this.' In this way, one places the motion afterwards. Thus, by these five modes, acts are vitiated by way of the motion.

Anussāvanato vipattiyaṃ pana vatthuādīni tāva vuttanayeneva veditabbāni. Evaṃ pana nesaṃ aparāmasanaṃ hoti – “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho”ti paṭhamānussāvanāya vā “dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi. Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho”ti dutiyatatiyānussāvanāsu vā “ayaṃ dhammarakkhito āyasmato buddharakkhitassa upasampadāpekkho”ti vattabbe “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, āyasmato buddharakkhitassā”ti vadanto [V 0.0369] vatthuṃ na parāmasati nāma. “Suṇātu [M 0.0397] me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ dhammarakkhito”ti vattabbe “suṇātu me, bhante, ayaṃ dhammarakkhito”ti vadanto saṅghaṃ na parāmasati nāma. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ dhammarakkhito āyasmato buddharakkhitassā”ti vattabbe “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ dhammarakkhito upasampadāpekkho”ti vadanto puggalaṃ na parāmasati nāma.

Regarding failure by way of the announcement, the subject matter and so forth should, for now, be understood in the manner already stated. However, their non-reference is as follows: when, in the first announcement, or in the second and third announcements where one says, 'A second time I speak on this matter... a third time I speak on this matter. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me,' it should be said, 'this Dhammarakkhita is the ordination candidate of the venerable Buddharakkhita,' one who instead says, 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me... of the venerable Buddharakkhita,' is called one who does not refer to the subject matter. When it should be said, 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This is Dhammarakkhita,' one who instead says, 'Venerable sirs, may you hear me. This is Dhammarakkhita,' is called one who does not refer to the Sangha. When it should be said, 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me, this Dhammarakkhita is the ordination candidate of the venerable Buddharakkhita,' one who instead says, 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me, this Dhammarakkhita is an ordination candidate,' is called one who does not refer to the individual.

Sāvanaṃ hāpetīti sabbena sabbaṃ kammavācāya anussāvanaṃ na karoti, ñattidutiyakamme dvikkhattuṃ ñattimeva ṭhapeti, ñatticatutthakamme catukkhattuṃ ñattimeva ṭhapeti. Evaṃ sāvanaṃ hāpeti. Yopi ñattidutiyakamme ekaṃ ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā ekaṃ kammavācaṃ anussāvento akkharaṃ vā chaḍḍeti, padaṃ vā duruttaṃ karoti, ayampi sāvanaṃ hāpetiyeva. Ñatticatutthakamme pana ekaṃ ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā sakimeva vā dvikkhattuṃ vā kammavācāya anussāvanaṃ karontopi akkharaṃ vā padaṃ vā chaḍḍentopi duruttaṃ karontopi anussāvanaṃ hāpetiyevāti veditabbo.

'He omits the announcement' means: he does not perform the announcement by the formal proclamation at all. In an act of a motion and one proclamation, he sets forth only the motion twice. In an act of a motion and three proclamations, he sets forth only the motion four times. In this way, he omits the announcement. Moreover, a bhikkhu who, in an act of a motion and one proclamation, having set forth the motion once and while reciting the one formal proclamation, drops a syllable or mispronounces a word—this bhikkhu too surely omits the announcement. In an act of a motion and three proclamations, however, it should be understood that one surely omits the announcement even when, having set forth the motion once, one performs the announcement by the formal proclamation only once or twice; or when one drops a syllable or a word; or when one mispronounces.

252. “Duruttaṃ karotī”ti ettha pana ayaṃ vinicchayo. Yo hi aññasmiṃ akkhare vattabbe aññaṃ vadati, ayaṃ duruttaṃ karoti nāma. Tasmā kammavācaṃ karontena bhikkhunā yvāyaṃ –

252. Here, however, concerning 'he speaks incorrectly,' this is the determination. For whoever, when one syllable should be uttered, utters another, this one is said to speak incorrectly. Therefore, by a bhikkhu performing the formal act of proclamation—

“Sithilaṃ dhanitañca dīgharassaṃ, garukaṃ lahukañca niggahitaṃ;

Sambandhaṃ vavatthitaṃ vimuttaṃ, dasadhā byañjanabuddhiyā pabhedo”ti. –

“Lax and tense, long and short, heavy and light, and the niggahita; connected, separated, and released—thus are the ten divisions of the understanding of articulation.”

Vutto, ayaṃ suṭṭhu upalakkhetabbo. Ettha hi sithilaṃ nāma pañcasu vaggesu paṭhamatatiyaṃ. Dhanitaṃ nāma tesveva dutiyacatutthaṃ. Dīghanti dīghena kālena vattabbaākārādi. Rassanti tato upaḍḍhakālena vattabbaakārādi. Garukanti dīghameva, yaṃ vā “āyasmato buddharakkhitattherassa yassa nakkhamatī”ti evaṃ saṃyogaparaṃ katvā vuccati. Lahukanti rassameva, yaṃ vā “āyasmato buddharakkhitattherassa yassa na khamatī”ti evaṃ asaṃyogaparaṃ katvā vuccati. Niggahitanti yaṃ karaṇāni niggahetvā avissajjetvā avivaṭena mukhena sānunāsikaṃ katvā vattabbaṃ. Sambandhanti yaṃ parapadena sambandhitvā “tuṇhissā”ti vā “tuṇhassā”ti vā vuccati. Vavatthitanti yaṃ parapadena asambandhaṃ katvā vicchinditvā “tuṇhī assā”ti vā “tuṇha assā”ti vā vuccati. Vimuttanti yaṃ karaṇāni aniggahetvā vissajjetvā vivaṭena mukhena anunāsikaṃ akatvā vuccati.

This, which has been stated, should be well noted. Here, 'lax' refers to the first and third consonants of the five classes. 'Tense' refers to the second and fourth of those same classes. 'Long' means vowels such as 'ā' that should be uttered with a long duration. 'Short' means vowels such as 'a' that should be uttered for half that duration. 'Heavy' refers to a long vowel, or that which is uttered by making it followed by a conjunct consonant, as in 'āyasmato buddharakkhitattherassa yassa nakkhamatī.' 'Light' refers to a short vowel, or that which is uttered by making it not followed by a conjunct consonant, as in 'āyasmato buddharakkhitattherassa yassa na khamatī.' 'Niggahita' refers to that which should be uttered by restraining the articulators, not releasing them, making it nasal with a not-fully-opened mouth. 'Connected' refers to that which, being connected to a following word, is uttered as 'tuṇhissā' or 'tuṇhassā.' 'Separated' refers to that which, being disconnected from a following word and broken off, is uttered as 'tuṇhī assā' or 'tuṇha assā.' 'Released' refers to that which is uttered by not restraining the articulators, releasing them, and not making it nasal, with an open mouth.

Tattha [M 0.0398][V 0.0370] “suṇātu me”ti vattabbe ta-kārassa tha-kāraṃ katvā “suṇāthu me”ti vacanaṃ sithilassa dhanitakaraṇaṃ nāma, tathā “pattakallaṃ esā ñattī”ti vattabbe “patthakallaṃ esā ñatthī”tiādivacanaṃ. “Bhante saṅgho”ti vattabbe bha-kāragha-kārānaṃ ba-kāraga-kāre katvā “bante saṃgo”ti vacanaṃ dhanitassa sithilakaraṇaṃ nāma. “Suṇātu me”ti vivaṭena mukhena vattabbe pana “suṇaṃtu me”ti vā “esā ñattī”ti vattabbe “esaṃ ñattī”ti vā avivaṭena mukhena ananunāsikaṃ katvā vacanaṃ vimuttassa niggahitavacanaṃ nāma. “Pattakalla”nti avivaṭena mukhena anunāsikaṃ katvā vattabbe “pattakallā”ti vivaṭena mukhena anunāsikaṃ akatvā vacanaṃ niggahitassa vimuttavacanaṃ nāma. Iti sithile kattabbe dhanitaṃ, dhanite kattabbe sithilaṃ, vimutte kattabbe niggahitaṃ, niggahite kattabbe vimuttanti imāni cattāri byañjanāni antokammavācāya kammaṃ dūsenti. Evaṃ vadanto hi aññasmiṃ akkhare vattabbe aññaṃ vadati, duruttaṃ karotīti vuccati.

Therein, when 'suṇātu me' should be uttered, uttering 'suṇāthu me' by changing the letter 'ta' to 'tha' is called making a lax consonant tense. Similarly, when 'pattakallaṃ esā ñattī' should be uttered, there is the utterance 'patthakallaṃ esā ñatthī' and so on. When 'Bhante saṅgho' should be uttered, uttering 'bante saṃgo' by changing the letters 'bha' and 'gha' to 'ba' and 'ga' is called making a tense consonant lax. However, when 'suṇātu me' should be uttered with an open mouth, but is instead uttered as 'suṇaṃtu me,' or when 'esā ñattī' should be uttered, but is instead uttered as 'esaṃ ñattī' with a not-fully-opened mouth, making it nasal, this is called the utterance of a constrained sound for a released sound. When 'pattakallaṃ' should be uttered with a not-fully-opened mouth, making it nasal, but is instead uttered as 'pattakallā' with an open mouth, not making it nasal, this is called the utterance of a released sound for a constrained sound. Thus: a tense utterance when a lax one should be made; a lax utterance when a tense one should be made; a constrained utterance when a released one should be made; and a released utterance when a constrained one should be made—these four types of articulation within the formal act of proclamation vitiate the formal act. For one who speaks thus, when one letter should be uttered, he utters another; he is said to speak incorrectly.

Itaresu pana dīgharassādīsu chasu byañjanesu dīghaṭṭhāne dīghameva, rassaṭṭhāne rassamevāti evaṃ yathāṭhāne taṃ tadeva akkharaṃ bhāsantena anukkamāgataṃ paveṇiṃ avināsentena kammavācā kātabbā. Sace pana evaṃ akatvā dīghe vattabbe rassaṃ, rasse vā vattabbe dīghaṃ vadati, tathā garuke vattabbe lahukaṃ, lahuke vā vattabbe garukaṃ vadati, sambandhe vā pana vattabbe vavatthitaṃ, vavatthite vā vattabbe sambandhaṃ vadati, evaṃ vuttepi kammavācā na kuppati. Imāni hi cha byañjanāni kammaṃ na kopenti. Yaṃ pana suttantikattherā “da-kāro ta-kāramāpajjati, ta-kāro da-kāramāpajjati, ca-kāro ja-kāramāpajjati, ja-kāro ca-kāramāpajjati, ya-kāro ka-kāramāpajjati, ka-kāro ya-kāramāpajjati, tasmā da-kārādīsu vattabbesu ta-kārādivacanaṃ na virujjhatī”ti vadanti, taṃ kammavācaṃ patvā na vaṭṭati. Tasmā vinayadharena neva da-kāro ta-kāro kātabbo…pe… na ka-kāro ya-kāro. Yathāpāḷiyā niruttiṃ sodhetvā dasavidhāya byañjananiruttiyā vuttadose pariharantena kammavācā kātabbā. Itarathā hi sāvanaṃ hāpeti nāma.

However, regarding the other six types of articulation, such as long and short, the formal act of proclamation should be performed by uttering that very syllable in its proper place—only the long sound where a long sound is due, and only the short sound where a short sound is due—without destroying the continuous tradition that has come down in sequence. However, if one does not do so—if, where a long sound should be uttered, one utters a short sound, or where a short sound should be uttered, one utters a long sound; or where a heavy sound should be uttered, one utters a light sound, or where a light sound should be uttered, one utters a heavy sound; or where a connected sound should be uttered, one utters a separated sound, or where a separated sound should be uttered, one utters a connected sound—even if uttered thus, the formal act of proclamation is not vitiated. For these six types of articulation do not vitiate the formal act. But the elders learned in the Suttas say: 'The sound 'da' becomes the sound 'ta,' the sound 'ta' becomes the sound 'da,' the sound 'ca' becomes the sound 'ja,' the sound 'ja' becomes the sound 'ca,' the sound 'ya' becomes the sound 'ka,' the sound 'ka' becomes the sound 'ya.'
