Therefore, when 'da' and similar sounds should be uttered, uttering 'ta' and similar sounds instead is not contrary.' This, however, is not valid when it comes to the formal act of proclamation. Therefore, a bearer of the Vinaya should not make the sound 'da' into 'ta'… nor 'ka' into 'ya.' The formal act of proclamation should be performed by purifying the pronunciation according to the Pāli, avoiding the faults mentioned in the tenfold classification of articulation. Otherwise, it is indeed called impairing the announcement.

Akāle vā sāvetīti sāvanāya akāle anokāse ñattiṃ aṭṭhapetvā paṭhamaṃyeva anussāvanakammaṃ katvā pacchā ñattiṃ ṭhapeti. Iti imehi pañcahākārehi anussāvanato kammāni vipajjanti.

Or, 'he announces at an improper time' means that, for the announcement, at an improper time and on an improper occasion, without having set forth the motion, he performs the act of announcement first and then sets forth the motion afterward. Thus, by these five modes, formal acts are vitiated by way of the announcement.

253. Sīmato [M 0.0399] vipattiyaṃ pana atikhuddakasīmā nāma yā ekavīsati bhikkhū na gaṇhāti[V 0.0371]. Kurundiyaṃ pana “yattha ekavīsati bhikkhū nisīdituṃ na sakkontī”ti vuttaṃ. Tasmā yā evarūpā sīmā, ayaṃ sammatāpi asammatā gāmakhettasadisāva hoti, tattha kataṃ kammaṃ kuppati. Esa nayo sesasīmāsupi. Ettha pana atimahatī nāma yā kesaggamattenapi tiyojanaṃ atikkamitvā sammatā hoti. Khaṇḍanimittā nāma aghaṭitanimittā vuccati. Puratthimāya disāya nimittaṃ kittetvā anukkameneva dakkhiṇāya pacchimāya uttarāya disāya kittetvā puna puratthimāya disāya pubbakittitaṃ nimittaṃ paṭikittetvā ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭati, evaṃ akhaṇḍanimittā hoti. Sace pana anukkamena āharitvā uttarāya disāya nimittaṃ kittetvā tattheva ṭhapeti, khaṇḍanimittā hoti. Aparāpi khaṇḍanimittā nāma yā animittupagaṃ tacasārarukkhaṃ vā khāṇukaṃ vā paṃsupuñjaṃ vā vālukapuñjaṃ vā aññataraṃ antarā ekaṃ nimittaṃ katvā sammatā hoti. Chāyānimittā nāma yā pabbatacchāyādīnaṃ yaṃ kiñci chāyaṃ nimittaṃ katvā sammatā hoti. Animittā nāma yā sabbena sabbaṃ nimittāni akittetvā sammatā hoti. Bahisīme ṭhito sīmaṃ sammannati nāma nimittāni kittetvā nimittānaṃ bahi ṭhito sammannati. Nadiyā samudde jātassare sīmaṃ sammannatīti etesu nadīādīsu yaṃ sammannati, sā evaṃ sammatāpi “sabbā, bhikkhave, nadī asīmā, sabbo samuddo asīmo, sabbo jātassaro asīmo”ti (mahāva. 147) vacanato asammatāva hoti. Sīmāya sīmaṃ sambhindatīti attano sīmāya paresaṃ sīmaṃ sambhindati. Sīmāya sīmaṃ ajjhottharatīti attano sīmāya paresaṃ sīmaṃ ajjhottharati. Tattha yathā sambhedo ca ajjhottharaṇañca hoti, taṃ sabbaṃ sīmākathāyaṃ vuttameva. Iti imā ekādasapi sīmā asīmā gāmakhettasadisā eva, tāsu nisīditvā kataṃ kammaṃ kuppati. Tena vuttaṃ “imehi ekādasahi ākārehi sīmato kammāni vipajjantī”ti.

253. Regarding invalidation on account of the boundary, an 'excessively small boundary' is one that does not accommodate twenty-one bhikkhus. In the Kurundī, however, it is said: 'where twenty-one bhikkhus are not able to sit.' Therefore, such a boundary, even if designated, is considered undesignated and is just like a village-area; a formal act performed therein is invalid. This principle applies to the other boundaries as well. Here, however, an 'excessively large boundary' is one that is designated extending beyond three yojanas, even by a hair's breadth. A 'boundary with broken markers' is called a boundary with unconnected markers. Having announced the marker in the eastern direction, and then having announced the markers in sequence in the southern, western, and northern directions, it is proper to again announce the previously announced marker in the eastern direction and establish it; thus, it becomes a boundary with unbroken markers. But if, having brought them in sequence, one announces the marker in the northern direction and establishes it right there, it becomes a boundary with broken markers. Furthermore, another 'boundary with broken markers' is one that is designated by making an unsuitable object—such as a tree with its heartwood on the outside, a stump, a pile of earth, or a pile of sand—an intermediate marker. A 'boundary with a shadow marker' is one that is designated by making any shadow, such as that of a mountain, a marker. A 'markerless boundary' is one that is designated without announcing any markers whatsoever. 'To designate a boundary while standing outside the boundary' means that having announced the markers, one designates it while standing outside the markers. 'To designate a boundary in a river, the ocean, or a natural lake': a boundary that one designates in these places, such as a river, even if so designated, is indeed an undesignated boundary because of the statement: 'Bhikkhus, every river is a non-boundary, every ocean is a non-boundary, every natural lake is a non-boundary.' 'To join a boundary with a boundary' means to join one's own boundary with the boundary of others. 'To cover a boundary with a boundary' means to cover the boundary of others with one's own boundary. How the joining and covering occur in that regard has all been stated in the 'Discussion on Boundaries'. Thus, these eleven are also non-boundaries, just like a village-area. A formal act performed while sitting within them is invalid. Therefore it is said: 'For these eleven reasons, formal acts are invalidated on account of the boundary.'

Parisato kammavipattiyaṃ pana kiñci anuttānaṃ nāma natthi. Yampi tattha kammappattachandārahalakkhaṇaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā, tampi parato “cattāro bhikkhū pakatattā kammappattā”tiādinā nayena vuttameva. Tattha pakatattā kammappattāti catuvaggakaraṇe kamme cattāro pakatattā anukkhittā anissāritā [M 0.0400] parisuddhasīlā cattāro bhikkhū kammappattā kammassa arahā anucchavikā sāmino. Na tehi vinā taṃ kammaṃ karīyati, na tesaṃ chando vā pārisuddhi vā eti, avasesā pana sacepi sahassamattā honti, sace samānasaṃvāsakā sabbe chandārahāva honti, chandapārisuddhiṃ datvā āgacchantu vā mā vā, kammaṃ pana tiṭṭhati. Yassa pana saṅgho parivāsādikammaṃ karoti, so neva kammappatto nāpi chandāraho, apica yasmā [V 0.0372] taṃ puggalaṃ vatthuṃ katvā saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, tasmā kammārahoti vuccati. Sesakammesupi eseva nayo.

However, in the case of an invalidation of an act due to the assembly, there is nothing that is called 'not evident.' Even if the characteristic of being qualified for the act and worthy of consent were to be spoken of there, that too has already been stated later by the method beginning with, 'Four bhikkhus, being of proper status, are qualified for the act.' Here, 'being of proper status, qualified for the act' means that in an act requiring a quorum of four, four bhikkhus who are of proper status—not suspended, not banished, of pure morality—are qualified for the act, deserving of the act, suitable, and authoritative. Without them, that act cannot be performed; neither their consent nor their attestation of purity is obtained. As for the rest, even if they number a thousand, if they are of the same communion, they are all worthy of consent; having given their consent and attestation of purity, whether they come or not, the act still stands. But for one upon whom the Saṅgha imposes a parivāsa act or similar act, he is neither qualified for the act nor worthy of giving consent; moreover, because the Saṅgha performs the act with that person as the object, he is called 'worthy of the act.' This is the same method in the remaining acts as well.

254. Apalokanakammaṃ katamāni pañca ṭhānāni gacchati, osāraṇaṃ nissāraṇaṃ bhaṇḍukammaṃ brahmadaṇḍaṃ kammalakkhaṇaññeva pañcamanti ettha “osāraṇaṃ nissāraṇa”nti padasiliṭṭhatāyetaṃ vuttaṃ, paṭhamaṃ pana nissāraṇā hoti, pacchā osāraṇā. Tattha yā sā kaṇṭakassa sāmaṇerassa daṇḍakammanāsanā, sā nissāraṇāti veditabbā. Tasmā etarahi sacepi sāmaṇero buddhassa vā dhammassa vā saṅghassa vā avaṇṇaṃ bhaṇati, akappiyaṃ “kappiya”nti dīpeti, micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato, so yāvatatiyaṃ nivāretvā taṃ laddhiṃ vissajjāpetabbo. No ce vissajjeti, saṅghaṃ sannipātetvā “vissajjehī”ti vattabbo. No ce vissajjeti, byattena bhikkhunā apalokanakammaṃ katvā nissāretabbo. Evañca pana kammaṃ kātabbaṃ –

254. In what five instances is an act of announcement applicable? Reinstatement, banishment, an act against a corruptor of families, the higher penalty, and the fifth is simply the characteristic of the act. Here, 'reinstatement, banishment' is stated for the sake of euphony, but first comes banishment, then reinstatement. Therein, the disciplinary act of expulsion against the novice Kaṇṭaka should be known as banishment. Therefore, nowadays, if a novice speaks disparagingly of the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Saṅgha, declares the improper as 'proper,' holds wrong views, or is possessed of an extremist view, he should be dissuaded up to the third time to abandon that doctrine. If he does not abandon it, the Saṅgha should be assembled and he should be told, 'Abandon it.' If he still does not abandon it, he should be banished by a competent bhikkhu after the act of announcement has been performed. And the act should be performed thus:–

“Saṅghaṃ, bhante, pucchāmi ‘ayaṃ itthannāmo sāmaṇero buddhassa dhammassa saṅghassa avaṇṇavādī micchādiṭṭhiko, yaṃ aññe sāmaṇerā labhanti dirattatirattaṃ bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ sahaseyyaṃ, tassā alābhāya nissāraṇā ruccati saṅghassā’ti. Dutiyampi. Tatiyampi bhante saṅghaṃ pucchāmi ‘ayaṃ itthannāmo sāmaṇero…pe… ruccati saṅghassā’ti, cara pire vinassā”ti.

“Venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha: ‘This novice named so-and-so speaks dispraise of the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha, and is of wrong view. Does the Saṅgha approve of his banishment, so that he may not obtain the sharing of lodging with the bhikkhus for two or three nights that other novices obtain?’ A second time… A third time, venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha: ‘This novice named so-and-so… does the Saṅgha approve?’ ‘Go, you wretch; perish!’”

So aparena samayena “ahaṃ, bhante, bālatāya añāṇatāya alakkhikatāya evaṃ akāsiṃ, svāhaṃ saṅghaṃ khamāpemī”ti khamāpento yāvatatiyaṃ yācāpetvā apalokanakammeneva osāretabbo, evañca pana osāretabbo. Saṅghamajjhe byattena bhikkhunā saṅghassa anumatiyā sāvetabbaṃ –

At a later time, when that novice asks for forgiveness, saying, ‘Venerable sirs, I acted thus through foolishness, ignorance, and wretchedness. I ask the Saṅgha for forgiveness,’ he should be made to request up to the third time and then be reinstated by the act of announcement alone. And he should be reinstated thus: In the midst of the Saṅgha, a competent bhikkhu should announce it with the consent of the Saṅgha:

“Saṅghaṃ[M 0.0401], bhante, pucchāmi ‘ayaṃ itthannāmo sāmaṇero buddhassa dhammassa saṅghassa avaṇṇavādī micchādiṭṭhiko, yaṃ aññe sāmaṇerā labhanti dirattatirattaṃ bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ sahaseyyaṃ, tassā alābhāya nissārito, svāyaṃ idāni sorato nivātavutti lajjidhammaṃ okkanto hirottappe patiṭṭhito katadaṇḍakammo accayaṃ deseti, imassa sāmaṇerassa yathā pure kāyasambhogasāmaggidānaṃ ruccati saṅghassā’”ti.

Venerable Sirs, I ask the Sangha: ‘This novice named so-and-so, who speaks dispraise of the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha, and is of wrong view, was expelled so that he would not obtain the sharing of lodging with the bhikkhus for two or three nights that other novices obtain. This very novice is now well-behaved, of humble conduct, has entered upon the state of conscientiousness, is established in moral shame and moral dread, is one for whom the penalty-act has been carried out, and confesses his transgression. Is the granting to this novice of communion in bodily association, as before, agreeable to the Sangha?’”

Evaṃ [V 0.0373] tikkhattuṃ vattabbaṃ. Evaṃ apalokanakammaṃ osāraṇañca nissāraṇañca gacchati. Bhaṇḍukammaṃ pabbajjāvinicchayakathāya vuttameva.

This should be said three times. Thus the act of announcement applies to both reinstatement and expulsion. The act of shaving is as stated in the discourse on the decision of ordination.

Brahmadaṇḍo pana na kevalaṃ channasseva paññatto, yo aññopi bhikkhu mukharo hoti, bhikkhū duruttavacanehi ghaṭṭento khuṃsento vambhento viharati, tassapi dātabbo, evañca pana dātabbo. Saṅghamajjhe byattena bhikkhunā saṅghassa anumatiyā sāvetabbaṃ –

The brahma-penalty, however, was not laid down for Channa alone. It should also be given to any other bhikkhu who is sharp-tongued, who dwells harassing, reviling, and disparaging the bhikkhus with ill-spoken words. And it should be given thus: In the midst of the Sangha, it should be announced by a competent bhikkhu with the consent of the Sangha:

“Bhante, itthannāmo bhikkhu mukharo, bhikkhū duruttavacanehi ghaṭṭento khuṃsento vambhento viharati, so bhikkhu yaṃ iccheyya, taṃ vadeyya, bhikkhūhi itthannāmo bhikkhu neva vattabbo, na ovaditabbo na anusāsitabbo, saṅghaṃ, bhante, pucchāmi ‘itthannāmassa bhikkhuno brahmadaṇḍassa dānaṃ ruccati saṅghassā’ti. Dutiyampi pucchāmi…pe… tatiyampi pucchāmi ‘itthannāmassa bhikkhuno brahmadaṇḍassa dānaṃ ruccati saṅghassā’”ti.

Venerable Sirs, the bhikkhu named so-and-so is abusive of speech; he lives harassing, reviling, and disparaging the bhikkhus with harsh words. That bhikkhu may say whatever he wishes. The bhikkhus should neither speak to, nor admonish, nor instruct the bhikkhu named so-and-so. Venerable Sirs, I ask the Sangha: 'Is the giving of the brahma-penalty to the bhikkhu named so-and-so agreeable to the Sangha?' A second time I ask... A third time I ask: 'Is the giving of the brahma-penalty to the bhikkhu named so-and-so agreeable to the Sangha?'

Tassa aparena samayena sammā vattitvā khamāpentassa brahmadaṇḍo paṭippassambhetabbo, evañca pana paṭippassambhetabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā saṅghamajjhe sāvetabbaṃ –

At a later time, if that bhikkhu behaves properly and asks for forgiveness, the brahma-penalty should be revoked. And it should be revoked thus: A competent bhikkhu should make an announcement in the midst of the Sangha:

“Bhante, bhikkhusaṅgho asukassa bhikkhuno brahmadaṇḍaṃ adāsi, so bhikkhu sorato nivātavutti lajjidhammaṃ okkanto hirottappe patiṭṭhito paṭisaṅkhā āyatiṃ saṃvare tiṭṭhati, saṅghaṃ, bhante, pucchāmi ‘tassa bhikkhuno brahmadaṇḍassa paṭippassaddhi ruccati saṅghassā’”ti.

“Venerable Sirs, the Sangha of bhikkhus imposed the brahma-penalty on a certain bhikkhu. That bhikkhu is now well-behaved, of humble conduct, has adopted the state of conscientiousness, is established in moral shame and moral dread, and through reflection abides in future restraint. Venerable Sirs, I ask the Sangha: ‘Is the remission of the brahma-penalty for that bhikkhu agreeable to the Sangha?’”

Evaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ vatvā apalokanakammeneva brahmadaṇḍo paṭippassambhetabboti.

Having spoken thus up to a third time, the brahma-penalty should be remitted by means of an act of announcement only.

Kammalakkhaṇaññeva [M 0.0402] pañcamanti yaṃ taṃ bhagavatā bhikkhunikkhandhake –

The fifth is the characteristic of the formal act itself, as stated by the Blessed One in the Bhikkhunīkhandhaka:

“Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo kaddamodakena osiñcanti ‘appeva nāma amhesu sārajjeyyu’nti, kāyaṃ vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ dassenti, ūruṃ vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ dassenti, aṅgajātaṃ vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ dassenti. Bhikkhuniyo obhāsenti, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ sampayojenti ‘appeva nāma amhesu sārajjeyyu’”nti (cūḷava. 411) –

“At that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus splashed the bhikkhunīs with muddy water, thinking, ‘Perhaps they might become infatuated with us.’ They exposed their bodies to the bhikkhunīs, they exposed their thighs to the bhikkhunīs, they exposed their private parts to the bhikkhunīs. They taunted the bhikkhunīs; they associated with the bhikkhunīs, thinking, ‘Perhaps they might become infatuated with us.’”

Imesu [V 0.0374] vatthūsu yesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dukkaṭaṃ paññapetvā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tassa bhikkhuno daṇḍakammaṃ kātu”nti vatvā “kiṃ nu kho daṇḍakammaṃ kātabba”nti saṃsaye uppanne “avandiyo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhunisaṅghena kātabbo”ti evaṃ avandiyakammaṃ anuññātaṃ, taṃ kammalakkhaṇaññeva pañcamaṃ, imassa apalokanakammassa ṭhānaṃ hoti. Tassa hi kammaññeva lakkhaṇaṃ, na osāraṇādīni, tasmā kammalakkhaṇanti vuccati. Tassa karaṇaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā saddhiṃ vitthārato dassayissāma. Bhikkhunupassaye sannipatitassa bhikkhunisaṅghassa anumatiyā byattāya bhikkhuniyā sāvetabbaṃ –

In these matters, for those bhikkhus for whom a dukkaṭa offense has been laid down, and after saying, “Bhikkhus, I allow a penalty-act to be performed for that bhikkhu,” when a doubt has arisen, “What penalty-act should be performed?”—the act of making unworthy of veneration was permitted thus: “Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should be made unworthy of veneration by the Sangha of bhikkhunīs.” That very characteristic of the act is the fifth basis for this act of announcement. For its characteristic is the act itself, not reinstatement and so forth; therefore, it is called 'the characteristic of the act.' We will show its performance in detail, together with its revocation. In the bhikkhunīs' residence, with the consent of the assembled Sangha of bhikkhunīs, it should be announced by a competent bhikkhunī:

“Ayye, asuko nāma ayyo bhikkhunīnaṃ apāsādikaṃ dasseti, etassa ayyassa avandiyakaraṇaṃ ruccatī”ti bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ pucchāmi. ‘Ayye, asuko nāma ayyo bhikkhunīnaṃ apāsādikaṃ dasseti, etassa ayyassa avandiyakaraṇaṃ ruccatī’ti dutiyampi. Tatiyampi bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ pucchāmī”ti.

“Venerable ladies, I ask the Sangha of bhikkhunīs: ‘The venerable one named so-and-so shows what is uninspiring to the bhikkhunīs. Is making this venerable one unworthy of veneration agreeable to the Sangha of bhikkhunīs?’ A second time I ask. A third time I ask the Sangha of bhikkhunīs.”

Evaṃ tikkhattuṃ sāvetvā apalokanakammena avandiyakammaṃ kātabbaṃ.

Having thus announced it three times, the act of making unworthy of veneration should be performed by means of an act of announcement.

Tato paṭṭhāya so bhikkhu bhikkhunīhi na vanditabbo. Sace avandiyamāno hirottappaṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvā sammā vattati, tena bhikkhuniyo khamāpetabbā. Khamāpentana bhikkhunupassayaṃ agantvā vihāreyeva saṅghaṃ vā gaṇaṃ vā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ vā upasaṅkamitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā “ahaṃ, bhante, paṭisaṅkhā āyatiṃ saṃvare tiṭṭhāmi, na puna apāsādikaṃ dassessāmi, bhikkhunisaṅgho mayhaṃ khamatū”ti khamāpetabbaṃ. Tena saṅghena vā gaṇena vā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ pesetvā ekabhikkhunā vā sayameva gantvā bhikkhuniyo vattabbā “ayaṃ bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā āyatiṃ saṃvare [M 0.0403] ṭhito, iminā accayaṃ desetvā bhikkhunisaṅgho khamāpito, bhikkhunisaṅgho imaṃ bhikkhuṃ vandiyaṃ karotū”ti. So vandiyo kātabbo, evañca pana kātabbo. Bhikkhunupassaye sannipatitassa bhikkhunisaṅghassa anumatiyā byattāya bhikkhuniyā sāvetabbaṃ –

From that time onward, that bhikkhu is not to be venerated by the bhikkhunīs. If, not being venerated, he establishes moral shame and moral dread and conducts himself well, he should ask the bhikkhunīs for forgiveness. When asking for forgiveness, without going to the bhikkhunīs' residence, he should approach the Sangha, a group, or a single bhikkhu right there in the monastery. Sitting in the squatting posture and raising his joined palms, he should ask for forgiveness thus: 'Venerable Sirs, having reflected, I will stand in future restraint; I will not again show what is uninspiring. May the Sangha of bhikkhunīs forgive me.' That Sangha or group should send a bhikkhu, or that single bhikkhu should go himself, to tell the bhikkhunīs: 'This bhikkhu, having reflected, is established in future restraint. Having confessed his transgression, he has asked the Sangha of bhikkhunīs for forgiveness. May the Sangha of bhikkhunīs make this bhikkhu worthy of veneration.' He is to be made worthy of veneration, and this is how he is to be made so. In the bhikkhunīs' residence, with the consent of the assembled Sangha of bhikkhunīs, an announcement is to be made by a competent bhikkhunī:

“Ayye, asuko nāma ayyo bhikkhunīnaṃ apāsādikaṃ dassetīti bhikkhunisaṅghena avandiyo kato, so lajjidhammaṃ okkamitvā paṭisaṅkhā āyatiṃ saṃvare ṭhito, accayaṃ desetvā bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ khamāpesi, tassa ayyassa vandiyakaraṇaṃ ruccatīti bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ pucchāmī”ti –

“Venerable Ladies, the venerable one named so-and-so was made not worthy of veneration by the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs for showing what is displeasing to the bhikkhunīs. Having entered upon the state of shame, he, through reflection, is established in future restraint; having confessed his transgression, he has asked the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs for forgiveness. Does the making of that venerable one worthy of veneration find approval with the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs? I ask the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.”

Tikkhattuṃ [V 0.0375] vattabbaṃ. Evaṃ apalokanakammeneva vandiyo kātabbo.

It is to be said three times. Thus, he is to be made worthy of veneration by means of a motion by announcement only.

255. Ayaṃ panettha pāḷimuttakopi kammalakkhaṇavinicchayo (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496). Idañhi kammalakkhaṇaṃ nāma bhikkhunisaṅghamūlakaṃ paññattaṃ, bhikkhusaṅghassapi panetaṃ labbhatiyeva. Yañhi bhikkhusaṅgho salākabhattauposathaggesu ca apalokanakammaṃ karoti, etampi kammalakkhaṇameva. Acchinnacīvarajiṇṇacīvaranaṭṭhacīvarānañhi saṅghaṃ sannipātetvā byattena bhikkhunā yāvatatiyaṃ sāvetvā apalokanakammaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Appamattakavissajjakena pana cīvaraṃ karontassa paccayabhājanīyakathāyaṃ vuttappabhedāni sūciādīni anapaloketvāpi dātabbāni. Tesaṃ dāne soyeva issaro, tato atirekaṃ dentena apaloketvā dātabbaṃ. Tato hi atirekadāne saṅgho sāmī. Gilānabhesajjampi tattha vuttappakāraṃ sayameva dātabbaṃ, atirekaṃ icchantassa apaloketvā dātabbaṃ. Yopi ca dubbalo vā chinniriyāpatho vā pacchinnabhikkhācārapatho vā mahāgilāno, tassa mahāvāsesu tatruppādato devasikaṃ nāḷi vā upaḍḍhanāḷi vā, ekadivasaṃyeva vā pañca vā dasa vā taṇḍulanāḷiyo dentena apalokanakammaṃ katvāva dātabbā. Pesalassa bhikkhuno tatruppādato iṇapalibodhampi bahussutassa saṅghabhāranittharakassa bhikkhuno anuṭṭhāpanīyasenāsanampi saṅghakiccaṃ karontānaṃ kappiyakārakādīnaṃ bhattavetanampi apalokanakammena dātuṃ vaṭṭati.

255. Here also is a determination of the characteristics of formal acts from outside the Pāḷi canon. Although this so-called characteristic of a formal act was laid down with the community of bhikkhunīs as its basis, it is indeed also applicable to the community of bhikkhus. For instance, when the community of bhikkhus performs a motion by announcement regarding food by ticket or in the Uposatha hall, this too is a characteristic of a formal act. When robes are to be given to bhikkhus whose robes have been stolen, are worn-out, or are lost, it is allowable to do so after assembling the Saṅgha, and after a competent bhikkhu has made an announcement three times and performed the motion by announcement. However, a bhikkhu who dispenses small amounts may give items such as needles—of the kinds mentioned in the discourse on the distribution of requisites—to a bhikkhu who is making a robe, even without a motion by announcement. In the giving of these, he alone is the master. But if giving more than that, one should do so after a motion by announcement. For in giving more than that, the Saṅgha is the owner. Medicines for the sick should also be given by oneself in the manner described there, but if a sick person desires more, it should be given after a motion by announcement. Furthermore, for a bhikkhu who is weak, whose posture is impaired, whose alms-round is cut off, or who is gravely ill, one who wishes to give a daily measure or half-measure of rice, or even five or ten measures of rice for a single day, from what is produced in the great monasteries, should give it only after having performed a motion by announcement. For a virtuous bhikkhu, it is permissible to clear a debt from what is produced there; for a learned bhikkhu who carries out the burdens of the Saṅgha, to give a lodging from which he is not to be displaced; and for stewards and others who perform the Saṅgha’s duties, to give food and wages—all by means of a motion by announcement.

Catupaccayavasena [M 0.0404] dinnatatruppādato saṅghikaṃ āvāsaṃ jaggāpetuṃ vaṭṭati, “ayaṃ bhikkhu issaravatāya vicāretī”ti kathāpacchindanatthaṃ pana salākaggādīsu vā antarasannipāte vā saṅghaṃ āpucchitvāva jaggāpetabbo. Cīvarapiṇḍapātatthāya odissa dinnatatruppādatopi apaloketvā āvāso jaggāpetabbo, anapaloketvāpi vaṭṭati, “sūro vatāyaṃ bhikkhu cīvarapiṇḍapātatthāya odissa dinnato āvāsaṃ jaggāpetī”ti evaṃ uppannakathāpacchedanatthaṃ pana apalokanakammameva katvā jaggāpetabbo.

From the revenue arising from that which was given by means of the four requisites, it is allowable to have a Saṅgha dwelling maintained. However, for the purpose of cutting off talk such as, ‘This bhikkhu administers with the authority of a master,’ it should be maintained only after having consulted the Saṅgha, whether at the place for distributing lots or at an intermediate assembly. From the revenue arising from that which was given specifically for the purpose of robes and alms-food, the dwelling should also be maintained after a motion by announcement. It is also allowable without a motion by announcement. However, for the purpose of cutting off talk that has arisen, such as, ‘Indeed, this bhikkhu is bold; he has the dwelling maintained from that which was given specifically for the purpose of robes and alms-food,’ it should be maintained only after having performed the motion by announcement.

Cetiye chattaṃ vā vedikaṃ vā bodhigharaṃ vā āsanagharaṃ vā akataṃ vā karontena jiṇṇaṃ vā paṭisaṅkharontena sudhākammaṃ vā karontena manusse samādapetvā kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace kārako natthi, cetiyassa upanikkhepato kāretabbaṃ. Upanikkhepepi asati apalokanakammaṃ katvā tatruppādato kāretabbaṃ, saṅghikenapi apaloketvā cetiyakiccaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Cetiyassa santakena apaloketvāpi saṅghikakiccaṃ na vaṭṭati, tāvakālikaṃ pana gahetvā paṭipākatikaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Cetiye sudhākammādīni karontehi pana bhikkhācārato vā saṅghato vā yāpanamattaṃ alabhantehi cetiyasantakato yāpanamattaṃ [V 0.0376] gahetvā paribhuñjantehi vattaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, “vattaṃ karomā”ti macchamaṃsādīhi saṅghabhattaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati.

At a cetiya, it is allowable to have a parasol, a railing, a Bodhi-tree enclosure, or a sitting hall made, or a dilapidated one repaired, or plasterwork done, after having encouraged the people. If there is no one to do the work, it should be caused to be done from the cetiya's deposit. If there is no deposit, after performing a motion by announcement, it should be caused to be done from the revenue arising there. It is also allowable to perform the cetiya's duties with Saṅgha property after a motion by announcement. With the cetiya's property, even after a motion by announcement, it is not allowable to perform the Saṅgha's duties. However, it is allowable to take it as a temporary loan and then restore it. But for those doing plasterwork and other such tasks at the cetiya, if they do not receive enough for sustenance from the alms-round or from the Saṅgha, it is allowable for them to perform their duties while taking and consuming enough for sustenance from the cetiya's property. It is not allowable to prepare a Saṅgha meal with fish, meat, and so on, saying, ‘We are performing the duties.’

Ye vihāre ropitā phalarukkhā saṅghena pariggahitā honti, jagganakammaṃ labhanti. Yesaṃ phalāni ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā bhājetvā paribhuñjanti, tesu apalokanakammaṃ na kātabbaṃ. Ye pana apariggahitā, tesu apalokanakammaṃ kātabbaṃ, taṃ pana salākaggayāgaggabhattaggaantarasaaāpātesupi kātuṃ vaṭṭati, uposathagge pana vaṭṭatiyeva. Tattha hi anāgatānampi chandapārisuddhi āharīyati, tasmā taṃ suvisodhitaṃ hoti. Evañca pana kātabbaṃ, byattena bhikkhunā bhikkhusaṅghassa anumatiyā sāvetabbaṃ –

The fruit trees planted in the monastery which are taken possession of by the Saṅgha receive tending. For those whose fruits are distributed and consumed after striking the bell, a motion by announcement is not to be made. However, for those not taken possession of, a motion by announcement must be made. That may be done even in the ticket-food hall, the ticket-gruel hall, the meal hall, and in intermediate assemblies, but in the Uposatha hall, it is certainly proper. For there, the consent and purity of even those not present are brought forth; therefore, that place is well-purified. And it should be done thus: a competent bhikkhu should make the announcement with the approval of the Saṅgha of bhikkhus—

“Bhante, yaṃ imasmiṃ vihāre antosīmāya saṅghasantakaṃ mūlatacapattaaṅkurapupphaphalakhādanīyādi atthi, taṃ sabbaṃ āgatāgatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yathāsukhaṃ paribhuñjituṃ ruccatīti saṅghaṃ pucchāmī”ti –

“Venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha: Does it find approval that whatever belongs to the Saṅgha within the boundary of this monastery—such as roots, bark, leaves, sprouts, flowers, fruits, and edibles—be consumed at their pleasure by all bhikkhus who come?”

Tikkhattuṃ pucchitabbaṃ.

It should be asked three times.

Catūhi [M 0.0405] pañcahi bhikkhūhi kataṃ sukatameva. Yasmimpi vihāre dve tayo janā vasanti, tehi nisīditvā katampi saṅghena katasadisameva. Yasmiṃ pana eko bhikkhu hoti, tena bhikkhunā uposathadivase pubbakaraṇapubbakiccaṃ katvā nisinnena katampi katikavattaṃ saṅghena katasadisameva hoti. Karontena pana phalavārena kātumpi cattāro māse cha māse ekasaṃvaccharanti evaṃ paricchinditvāpi aparicchinditvāpi kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Paricchinne yathāparicchedaṃ paribhuñjitvā puna kātabbaṃ. Aparicchinne yāva rukkhā dharanti, tāva vaṭṭati. Yepi tesaṃ rukkhānaṃ bījehi aññe rukkhā ropitā honti, tesampi sā eva katikā.

An act performed by four or five bhikkhus is indeed well-performed. Even in a monastery where two or three persons reside, an act performed by them after having sat down is equivalent to it being performed by the Saṅgha. But in a monastery where there is only one bhikkhu, the agreement made by that bhikkhu, having sat down after performing the preliminary duties and tasks on the Uposatha day, is also equivalent to it being made by the Saṅgha. When performing this act, it is proper to do so by the fruit season; it is also proper to do so for four months, six months, or one year, either by specifying a time limit or by not specifying one. If a limit is specified, after consuming according to the specification, the act must be performed again. If no limit is specified, it is valid for as long as the trees live. Even for other trees planted from the seeds of those trees, that very same agreement applies.

Sace pana aññasmiṃ vihāre ropitā honti, tesaṃ yattha ropitā, tasmiṃyeva vihāre saṅgho sāmī. Yepi aññato bījāni āharitvā purimavihāre pacchā ropitā, tesu aññā katikā kātabbā, katikāya katāya puggalikaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhanti, yathāsukhaṃ phalādīni paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭanti. Sace panettha taṃ taṃ okāsaṃ parikkhipitvā pariveṇāni katvā jagganti, tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ puggalikaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhanti, aññe paribhuñjituṃ na labhanti. Tehi pana saṅghassa [V 0.0377] dasamabhāgaṃ datvā paribhuñjitabbāni. Yopi majjhevihāre rukkhaṃ sākhāhi parivāretvā rakkhati, tassapi eseva nayo.

If, however, they are planted in another monastery, the Saṅgha is the owner in that very monastery where they are planted. And for trees that are later planted in the former monastery with seeds brought from elsewhere, another agreement should be made for them. When the agreement has been made, they stand as individual property, and it is permissible to enjoy the fruits and so on as they please. If, however, in this monastery, having enclosed this or that space and made compounds, they tend them, they stand as the individual property of those monks, and other monks do not get to enjoy them. However, they are to be enjoyed by those monks after giving a tenth part to the Saṅgha. This very same rule also applies to a monk who surrounds a tree in the middle of the monastery with branches and protects it.

Porāṇakavihāraṃ gatassa sambhāvanīyabhikkhuno “thero āgato”ti phalāphalaṃ āharanti, sace tattha mūle sabbapariyattidharo bahussutabhikkhu vihāsi, “addhā ettha dīghā katikā katā bhavissatī”ti nikkukkuccena paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Vihāre phalāphalaṃ piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati, dhutaṅgaṃ na kopeti. Sāmaṇerā attano ācariyupajjhāyānaṃ bahūni phalāni denti, aññe bhikkhū alabhantā khiyyanti, khiyyanamattameva taṃ hoti. Sace dubbhikkhaṃ hoti, ekaṃ panasarukkhaṃ nissāya saṭṭhipi janā jīvanti, tādise kāle sabbesaṃ saṅgahakaraṇatthāya bhājetvā khāditabbaṃ. Ayaṃ sāmīci. Yāva pana katikavattaṃ na paṭippassambhati, tāva tehi khāyitaṃ sukhāyitameva. Kadā pana katikavattaṃ paṭippassambhati? Yadā samaggo saṅgho sannipatitvā “ito paṭṭhāya bhājetvā khādantū”ti sāvebhi, ekabhikkhuke pana vihāre etena sāvitepi purimakatikā paṭippassambhatiyeva[M 0.0406]. Sace paṭippassaddhāya katikāya sāmaṇerā neva rukkhato pātenti, na bhūmito gahetvā bhikkhūnaṃ denti, patitaphalāni pādehi paharantā vicaranti, tesaṃ dasamabhāgato paṭṭhāya yāva upaḍḍhaphalabhāgena phātikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Addhā phātikammalobhena āharitvā dassenti, puna subhikkhe jāte kappiyakārakesu āgantvā sākhāparivārādīni katvā rukkhe rakkhantesu sāmaṇerānaṃ phātikammaṃ na kātabbaṃ, bhājetvā paribhuñjitabbaṃ.

When a respected monk goes to a monastery with an old agreement, they bring various fruits, saying, 'The elder has arrived.' If, in that monastery, a learned monk who has mastered all the scriptures has previously resided, one should partake without scruple, thinking, 'Surely, a long-standing agreement must have been made here.' Various fruits in the monastery are allowable even for those who undertake the ascetic practice of an alms-goer; it does not break the ascetic practice. Novices give many fruits to their own teachers and preceptors. Other monks, not receiving any, complain; that is merely a complaint. If there is a famine, and even sixty people can live by depending on a single jackfruit tree, in such a time, it should be divided and eaten for the sake of supporting all. This is proper conduct. However, as long as the agreement has not ceased, what is eaten by them is indeed well-eaten. Now, when does the agreement cease? When the complete Saṅgha, having assembled, announces, 'From now on, let them divide and eat,' then it ceases. However, in a monastery with a single monk, even when it is announced by this monk, the former agreement indeed ceases. If, after the agreement has ceased, the novices neither knock fruits down from the tree, nor pick them up from the ground and give them to the monks, but walk about kicking the fallen fruits with their feet, a transaction for growth should be made for them, starting from a tenth part up to a share of half the fruit. Surely, out of desire for the gain from the transaction, they will bring and give them. Again, when there is an abundance of food, and suitable attendants, having come and done things like fencing with branches and so on, are guarding the trees, a transaction for growth should not be made for the novices; it should be divided and partaken of.

“Vihāre phalāphalaṃ atthī”ti sāmantagāmehi manussā gilānānaṃ vā gabbhinīnaṃ vā atthāya āgantvā “ekaṃ nāḷikeraṃ detha, ambaṃ detha, labujaṃ dethā”ti yācanti, dātabbaṃ, na dātabbanti? Dātabbaṃ. Adīyamāne hi te domanassikā honti. Dentena pana saṅghaṃ sannipātetvā yāvatatiyaṃ sāvetvā apalokanakammaṃ katvāva dātabbaṃ, katikavattaṃ vā katvā ṭhapetabbaṃ, evañca pana kātabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā saṅghassa anumatiyā sāvetabbaṃ –

People from the surrounding villages, thinking, 'There are fruits in the monastery,' come for the sake of the sick or pregnant women and ask, 'Give a coconut, give a mango, give a breadfruit.' Should it be given or not? It should be given. For if it is not given, they become displeased. However, one who wishes to give should do so only after having assembled the Saṅgha, announced it up to the third time, and performed the act of announcement. Or, a formal agreement should be made and established. And this is how it should be done: It should be announced by a competent monk with the consent of the Saṅgha:

“Sāmantagāmehi manussā āgantvā gilānādīnaṃ atthāya phalāphalaṃ yācanti, dve nāḷikerāni dve tālaphalāni dve panasāni pañca ambāni pañca kadaliphalāni gaṇhantānaṃ anivāraṇaṃ, asukarukkhato ca asukarukkhato ca phalaṃ gaṇhantānaṃ anivāraṇaṃ ruccati bhikkhusaṅghassā”ti –

'People from the surrounding villages come and ask for fruits for the sake of the sick and others. Is it agreeable to the Saṅgha of monks that there be no prevention for those who take two coconuts, two palmyra fruits, two jackfruits, five mangoes, and five bananas, and for those who take fruit from such-and-such a tree and from such-and-such a tree?'

Tikkhattuṃ vattabbaṃ. Tato paṭṭhāya gilānādīnaṃ nāmaṃ gahetvā yācantā “gaṇhathā”ti na vattabbā[V 0.0378], vattaṃ pana ācikkhitabbaṃ “nāḷikerādīni iminā nāma paricchedena gaṇhantānaṃ asukarukkhato ca asukarukkhato ca phalaṃ gaṇhantānaṃ anivāraṇaṃ kata”nti. Anuvicaritvā pana “ayaṃ madhuraphalo ambo, ito gaṇhathā”tipi na vattabbā.

It should be said three times. From then on, to those who come asking, having mentioned the name of the sick and others, one should not say, 'Take.' Rather, the formal agreement should be explained: 'Non-prevention has been made for those taking coconuts and so on by this specified limit, and for those taking fruit from such-and-such a tree and from such-and-such a tree.' Furthermore, having followed them around, one should also not say, 'This mango has sweet fruit; take from this tree.'

Phalabhājanakāle pana āgatānaṃ sammatena upaḍḍhabhāgo dātabbo, asammatena apaloketvā dātabbaṃ. Khīṇaparibbayo vā maggagamiyasatthavāho vā añño vā issaro āgantvā yācati, apaloketvāva dātabbaṃ, balakkārena gahetvā khādanto na vāretabbo. Kuddho hi so rukkhepi chindeyya, aññampi anatthaṃ kareyya. Puggalikapariveṇaṃ āgantvā gilānassa nāmena yācanto “amhehi chāyādīnaṃ atthāya [M 0.0407] ropitaṃ, sace atthi, tumhe jānāthā”ti vattabbo. Yadi pana phalabharitāva rukkhā honti, kaṇṭake bandhitvā phalavārena gaṇhanti, apaccāsīsantena hutvā dātabbaṃ, balakkārena gaṇhanto na vāretabbo. Pubbe vuttamevettha kāraṇaṃ.

But at the time of distributing fruit, half a share should be given to those who have arrived by an appointed monk; by an unappointed one, it should be given after informing the Saṅgha. If one whose provisions are exhausted, or a caravan leader traveling a road, or another lord comes and asks, it should be given only after informing the Saṅgha. One who takes by force and eats should not be stopped. For if angered, he might even cut down the trees or cause other harm. To one who comes to a private monastic compound and asks in the name of a sick person, it should be said: 'It was planted by us for the sake of shade and so on. If there is any, you yourselves know.' But if the trees are laden with fruit, and they take their turn of fruit by tying thorns, it should be given without expecting anything in return. One who takes by force should not be stopped. The reason herein is just as has been stated before.

Saṅghassa phalārāmo hoti, paṭijagganaṃ na labhati. Sace taṃ koci vattasīsena jaggati, saṅghasseva hoti. Athāpi kassaci paṭibalassa bhikkhuno “imaṃ sappurisa jaggitvā dehī”ti saṅgho bhāraṃ karoti, so ce vattasīsena jaggati, evampi saṅghasseva hoti. Phātikammaṃ paccāsīsantassa pana tatiyabhāgena vā upaḍḍhabhāgena vā phātikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. “Bhāriyaṃ kamma”nti vatvā ettakena anicchanto pana “sabbaṃ taveva santakaṃ katvā mūlabhāgaṃ dasamabhāgamattaṃ datvā jaggāhī”tipi vattabbo, garubhaṇḍattā pana na mūlacchejjavasena dātabbaṃ. So mūlabhāgaṃ datvā khādanto akatāvāsaṃ vā katvā katāvāsaṃ vā jaggitvā nissitakānaṃ ārāmaṃ niyyāteti, tehipi mūlabhāgo dātabbova.

The Sangha has a fruit-grove; it does not get a caretaker. If someone tends to it on the basis of duty, it belongs to the Sangha alone. Furthermore, if the Sangha assigns the duty to some capable monk, saying, 'Good man, tend to this and give its yield,' and if he tends to it on the basis of duty, even so, it belongs to the Sangha alone. But for one who expects payment for the work, payment should be made with a third part or with a half part. But if he is unwilling for that much, saying, 'The work is heavy,' he may also be told: 'Having made it all your own property, tend to it, giving about a tenth part as the original share.' However, because it is heavy property, it should not be given in a way that cuts off the root. That monk, having given the original share and consuming the produce, having built an unbuilt dwelling or having maintained a built one, hands over the grove to his dependents. By them too, the original share must be given.

Yadā pana bhikkhū sayaṃ jaggituṃ pahonti, atha tesaṃ jaggituṃ na dātabbaṃ, jaggitakāle pana na vāretabbā, jagganakāleyeva vāretabbā. “Bahu tumhehi khāyitaṃ, idāni mā jaggittha, bhikkhusaṅghoyeva jaggissatī”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace pana neva vattasīsena jagganto atthi, na phātikammena, na saṅgho jaggituṃ pahoti, eko anāpucchitvāva jaggitvā phātikammaṃ vaḍḍhetvā paccāsīsati, apalokanakammena phātikammaṃ vaḍḍhetvāva dātabbaṃ. Iti imaṃ sabbampi kammalakkhaṇameva hoti. Apalokanakammaṃ imāni pañca ṭhānāni gacchati.

However, when the bhikkhus are able to tend the property themselves, then it should not be given to others to tend. But when it has been tended and is fruitful, they should not be prevented; they should be prevented only at the very time of tending. It should be said: 'Much has been consumed by you. Now, do not tend. The community of bhikkhus itself will tend.' But if there is no one tending on the basis of duty, nor by taking payment for the work, and the Sangha is not able to tend, and if one bhikkhu, without asking permission, tends the property and, having improved it, expects payment, this should be given only after having increased the payment by means of an act of announcement. Thus, all this is indeed a characteristic of a formal act. The act of announcement applies to these five cases.

256. Ñattikammaṭṭhānabhede pana (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496) –

256. In the classification of the grounds for a formal act with a motion, however:

“Suṇātu [V 0.0379] me, bhante, saṅgho, itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho, anusiṭṭho so mayā, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, itthannāmo āgaccheyya, ‘āgacchāhī’ti vattabbo”ti –

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This so-and-so is the candidate for higher ordination of the venerable so-and-so. He has been instructed by me. If it is suitable for the Sangha, so-and-so should come. He should be told, ‘Come.’”

Evaṃ upasampadāpekkhassa osāraṇā osāraṇā nāma.

Thus, the summoning of a candidate for higher ordination is called ‘summoning’ (osāraṇā).

“Suṇantu [M 0.0408] me āyasmantā, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu dhammakathiko, imassa neva suttaṃ āgacchati, no suttavibhaṅgo, so atthaṃ asallakkhetvā byañjanacchāyāya atthaṃ paṭibāhati, yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā avasesā imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasameyyāmā”ti –

“Venerable sirs, listen to me. This bhikkhu, so-and-so, is a Dhamma preacher, but he knows neither the Sutta nor the Sutta Vibhaṅga. Without considering the meaning, he rejects the meaning by the shadow of the letter. If it is suitable for the venerable sirs, having made this bhikkhu, so-and-so, rise from his seat, let us, the remaining ones, settle this legal issue.”

Evaṃ ubbāhikavinicchaye dhammakathikassa bhikkhuno nissāraṇā nissāraṇā nāma.

Thus, in a legal decision by removal, the removal of a Dhamma-preaching bhikkhu is called ‘removal’ (nissāraṇā).

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ajjuposatho pannaraso, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho uposathaṃ kareyyā”ti –

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. Today is the Uposatha, the fifteenth day. If it is suitable for the Sangha, let the Sangha perform the Uposatha.”

Evaṃ uposathakammavasena ṭhapitā ñatti uposatho nāma.

Thus, a motion established by way of the Uposatha formal act is called ‘Uposatha’.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ajja pavāraṇā pannarasī, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho pavāreyyā”ti –

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. Today is the Pavāraṇā, the fifteenth day. If it is suitable for the Sangha, let the Sangha perform the Pavāraṇā.”

Evaṃ pavāraṇakammavasena ṭhapitā ñatti pavāraṇā nāma.

Thus, a motion established by way of the Pavāraṇā formal act is called ‘Pavāraṇā’.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmaṃ anusāseyya”nti, “yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, itthannāmo itthannāmaṃ anusāseyyā”ti, “yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmaṃ antarāyike dhamme puccheyya”nti, “yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, itthannāmo itthannāmaṃ antarāyike dhamme puccheyyā”ti, “yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmaṃ vinayaṃ puccheyya”nti, “yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, itthannāmo itthannāmaṃ vinayaṃ puccheyyā”ti, “yadi [V 0.0380] saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmena vinayaṃ puṭṭho vissajjeyya”nti, “yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, itthannāmo itthannāmena vinayaṃ puṭṭho vissajjeyyā”ti –

“Venerable Sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This so-and-so is the candidate for higher ordination of the venerable so-and-so. If it seems fit to the Sangha, I would instruct so-and-so.” “If it seems fit to the Sangha, so-and-so would instruct so-and-so.” “If it seems fit to the Sangha, I would question so-and-so about the obstructive factors.” “If it seems fit to the Sangha, so-and-so would question so-and-so about the obstructive factors.” “If it seems fit to the Sangha, I would question so-and-so about the Vinaya.” “If it seems fit to the Sangha, so-and-so would question so-and-so about the Vinaya.” “If it seems fit to the Sangha, I would answer when questioned about the Vinaya by so-and-so.” “If it seems fit to the Sangha, so-and-so would answer when questioned about the Vinaya by so-and-so.”

Evaṃ attānaṃ vā paraṃ vā sammannituṃ ṭhapitā ñatti sammuti nāma.

Thus, a motion established for appointing oneself or another is called 'authorization' (sammuti).

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, idaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno nissaggiyaṃ saṅghassa nissaṭṭhaṃ, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dadeyyā”ti, “yadāyasmantānaṃ [M 0.0409] pattakallaṃ, āyasmantā imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dadeyyu”nti –

“Venerable Sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This robe of the monk named so-and-so is to be forfeited and relinquished to the Sangha. If it seems fit to the Sangha, the Sangha should give this robe to the monk named so-and-so.” “If it seems fit to the venerable ones, the venerable ones should give this robe to the monk named so-and-so.”

Evaṃ nissaṭṭhacīvarapattādīnaṃ dānaṃ dānaṃ nāma.

Thus, the giving of relinquished robes, bowls, and so forth, is called 'giving' (dāna).

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu āpattiṃ sarati vivarati uttāniṃ karoti deseti, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno āpattiṃ paṭiggaṇheyya”nti, “yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno āpattiṃ paṭiggaṇheyya”nti, tena vattabbo “passasī”ti. Āma, passāmīti. “Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsī”ti –

“Venerable Sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This monk, so-and-so by name, remembers, reveals, lays open, and confesses an offense. If it seems fit to the Sangha, I would accept the offense from the monk, so-and-so by name.” “If it seems fit to the venerable ones, I would accept the offense from the monk, so-and-so by name.” He should be asked: 'Do you see it?' 'Yes, I see it.' 'You should restrain yourself in the future.'

Evaṃ āpattipaṭiggaho paṭiggaho nāma.

Thus, the acceptance of an offense is called 'acceptance' (paṭiggaha).

“Suṇantu me āyasmantā āvāsikā, yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, idāni uposathaṃ kareyyāma, pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyyāma, āgame kāḷe pavāreyyāmā”ti.

“May the venerable resident monks listen to me. If it is the proper time for the venerable sirs, let us now perform the Uposatha, recite the Pātimokkha, and perform the Pavāraṇā at the coming time.”

Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā taṃ kāḷaṃ anuvaseyyuṃ, āvāsikena bhikkhunā byattena paṭibalena āvāsikā bhikkhū ñāpetabbā –

If, monks, those monks are quarrelsome, disputatious, contentious, makers of chatter, and creators of legal issues in the Sangha, and should they stay for that time, a resident monk who is competent and capable should inform the resident monks:

“Suṇantu me āyasmantā āvāsikā, yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, idāni uposathaṃ kareyyāma, pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyyāma, āgame juṇhe pavāreyyāmā”ti –

May the venerable resident monks listen to me. If it is the proper time for the venerable sirs, let us now perform the Uposatha, recite the Pātimokkha, and perform the Pavāraṇā at the coming full moon.

Evaṃ [V 0.0381] katā pavāraṇāpaccukkaḍḍhanā paccukkaḍḍhanā nāma.

Thus, the withdrawal of the Pavāraṇā, once made, is called 'withdrawal'.

Sabbeheva ekajjhaṃ sannipatitabbaṃ, sannipatitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

All should gather together in one place. Having gathered, a competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Sangha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ, sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvatteyya, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho [M 0.0410] imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ tiṇavatthārakena vūpasameyya ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyutta”nti –

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. We, living in quarrel, contention, and dispute, have often engaged in unmonk-like and unseemly conduct and have uttered much that is out of place. If we were to have each other dealt with in accordance with these offenses, the case might lead to harshness, bitterness, and division. If it seems fit to the Sangha, let the Sangha settle this case by covering it over as with grass, setting aside grave offenses and those connected with laypeople.

Evaṃ tiṇavatthārakasamathena katvā sabbapaṭhamā sabbasaṅgāhikañatti kammalakkhaṇaṃ nāma.

Thus, the very first motion that encompasses all, made by the settlement of covering over with grass, is called a characteristic of a formal act.

Tathā tato parā ekekasmiṃ pakkhe ekekaṃ katvā dve ñattiyo. Iti yathāvuttappabhedaṃ osāraṇaṃ nissāraṇaṃ…pe… kammalakkhaṇaññeva navamanti ñattikammaṃ imāni nava ṭhānāni gacchati.

Similarly, after that, two motions, one made for each faction, are also a characteristic of a formal act. Thus, with the distinctions as described—inclusion, exclusion, and so on—the ninth is indeed a characteristic of a formal act. In this way, a motion-as-formal-act pertains to these nine instances.

257. Ñattidutiyakammaṭṭhānabhede (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496) pana vaḍḍhassa licchavino pattanikkujjanavasena khandhake vuttā nissāraṇā, tasseva pattukkujjanavasena khandhake vuttā osāraṇā ca veditabbā. Vuttañhetaṃ (cūḷava. 265-266) –

257. However, in the section on the formal act with a motion as the second part, the exclusion of Vaḍḍha the Licchavi by way of overturning the bowl, spoken of in the Khandhaka, and also the inclusion of that same person by way of turning the bowl upright, spoken of in the Khandhaka, are to be understood. For this was said:

“Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa upāsakassa patto nikkujjitabbo. Bhikkhūnaṃ alābhāya parisakkati, bhikkhūnaṃ anatthāya parisakkati, bhikkhūnaṃ avāsāya parisakkati, bhikkhū akkosati paribhāsati, bhikkhū bhikkhūhi bhedeti, buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi aṭṭhahi aṅgehi samannāgatassa upāsakassa pattaṃ nikkujjituṃ.

‘Monks, the bowl of a lay follower who is endowed with eight factors should be overturned. He strives for the non-gain of monks, he strives for the harm of monks, he strives for the non-residence of monks, he insults and reviles monks, he causes monks to be divided from monks, he speaks dispraise of the Buddha, he speaks dispraise of the Dhamma, he speaks dispraise of the Sangha. I allow, monks, the bowl of a lay follower endowed with these eight factors to be overturned.

Evañca pana bhikkhave nikkujjitabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

‘And it should be overturned in this way, monks. The Sangha is to be informed by a competent and capable monk:

“Suṇātu [V 0.0382] me, bhante, saṅgho, vaḍḍho licchavī āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattaṃ nikkujjeyya, asambhogaṃ saṅghena kareyya, esā ñatti.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. Vaḍḍha the Licchavi accuses the venerable Dabba Mallaputta of a groundless corruption of virtue. If it is timely for the Sangha, the Sangha should overturn the bowl for Vaḍḍha the Licchavi and should make him to be of non-communion with the Sangha. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, vaḍḍho licchavī āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, saṅgho vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattaṃ nikkujjati, asambhogaṃ saṅghena karoti, yassāyasmato khamati vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattassa nikkujjanā asambhogaṃ [M 0.0411] saṅghena karaṇaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. Vaḍḍha the Licchavi accuses the venerable Dabba Mallaputta of a groundless corruption of virtue. The Sangha overturns the bowl for Vaḍḍha the Licchavi and makes him to be of non-communion with the Sangha. If the overturning of the bowl for Vaḍḍha the Licchavi and the making him to be of non-communion with the Sangha is agreeable to any venerable one, he should remain silent. Whomever does not approve, he should speak.

“Nikkujjito saṅghena vaḍḍhassa licchavissa patto asambhogo saṅghena, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

‘The bowl for Vaḍḍha the Licchavi has been overturned by the Sangha; he has been made to be of non-communion by the Sangha. This is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this matter.’

Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatassa upāsakassa patto ukkujjitabbo. Na bhikkhūnaṃ alābhāya parisakkati, na bhikkhūnaṃ anatthāya parisakkati…pe… na saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi aṭṭhahi aṅgehi samannāgatassa upāsakassa pattaṃ ukkujjituṃ.

‘Monks, the bowl should be reinstated for a lay follower possessed of eight qualities. He does not strive for the bhikkhus’ loss, he does not strive for the bhikkhus’ harm… he does not speak dispraise of the Sangha. Monks, I allow the reinstatement of the bowl for a lay follower possessed of these eight qualities.’

Evañca pana, bhikkhave, ukkujjitabbo. Tena, bhikkhave, vaḍḍhena licchavinā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo –

‘And in this way, monks, it should be reinstated. Then, monks, Vaḍḍha the Licchavi should approach the Sangha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the bhikkhus, sit on his haunches, raise his joined hands in salutation, and say this:’

“Saṅghena me, bhante, patto nikkujjito, asambhogomhi saṅghena, sohaṃ, bhante, sammā vattāmi, lomaṃ pātemi, netthāraṃ vattāmi, saṅghaṃ pattukkujjanaṃ yācāmī”ti.

‘Venerable sirs, the Sangha has overturned my bowl; I am excluded from the Sangha's communion. Now, venerable sirs, I conduct myself rightly, I humble myself, I conduct myself for rehabilitation. I ask the Sangha for the reinstatement of my bowl.’

Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo.

He should ask a second time. He should ask a third time.

Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

A competent and able bhikkhu should inform the Sangha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, saṅghena vaḍḍhassa licchavissa patto nikkujjito, asambhogo [V 0.0383] saṅghena, so sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, saṅghaṃ pattukkujjanaṃ yācati, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattaṃ ukkujjeyya, sambhogaṃ saṅghena kareyya, esā ñatti.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Sangha listen to me. The Sangha overturned Vaḍḍha the Licchavi’s bowl, and he is excluded from the Sangha's communion. Now he conducts himself rightly, he humbles himself, he conducts himself for rehabilitation, and he asks the Sangha for the reinstatement of his bowl. If it is agreeable to the Sangha, the Sangha should reinstate the bowl of Vaḍḍha the Licchavi and bring him into communion with the Sangha. This is the motion.’

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, saṅghena vaḍḍhassa licchavissa patto nikkujjito, asambhogo saṅghena, so sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, saṅghaṃ pattukkujjanaṃ yācati, saṅgho vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattaṃ ukkujjati, sambhogaṃ saṅghena karoti, yassāyasmato khamati vaḍḍhassa licchavissa pattassa ukkujjanā [M 0.0412] sambhogaṃ saṅghena karaṇaṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Sangha listen to me. The Sangha has overturned the bowl of Vaḍḍha the Licchavi, and he is excluded from the Sangha's communion. Now he conducts himself rightly, he humbles himself, he conducts himself for rehabilitation, and he asks the Sangha for the reinstatement of his bowl. The Sangha reinstates the bowl of Vaḍḍha the Licchavi and brings him into communion with the Sangha. If it is agreeable to any venerable one that the bowl of Vaḍḍha the Licchavi be reinstated and that he be brought into communion with the Sangha, let him be silent. If anyone does not approve, let him speak.’

“Ukkujjito saṅghena vaḍḍhassa licchavissa patto sambhogo saṅghena, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

‘The Sangha has reinstated the bowl of Vaḍḍha the Licchavi, and he is included in the Sangha's communion. The Sangha approves of it, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.’

Ettha (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 265) ca aṭṭhasu aṅgesu ekakenapi aṅgena samannāgatassa pattanikkujjanakammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, antosīmāya vā nissīmaṃ gantvā nadīādīsu vā nikkujjituṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Evaṃ nikkujjite pana patte tassa gehe koci deyyadhammo na gahetabbo, “asukassa gehe bhikkhaṃ mā gaṇhitthā”ti aññavihāresupi pesetabbaṃ. Ukkujjanakāle pana yāvatatiyaṃ yācāpetvā hatthapāsaṃ vijahāpetvā ñattidutiyakammena ukkujjitabbo.

Here, it is permissible to perform the act of overturning the bowl for a lay supporter possessed of even one of the eight factors. It is permissible to overturn it within the boundary or by going outside the boundary to rivers and so forth. Once the bowl has been overturned in this way, no gift should be accepted in his house. A message should also be sent to other monasteries: 'Do not accept alms in such-and-such a person's house.' At the time of righting the bowl, after having him ask up to the third time and having him withdraw from arm's reach, it should be righted by a motion with one following announcement.

Sīmāsammuti, ticīvarena avippavāsasammuti, santhatasammuti, bhattuddesakasenāsanaggāhāpakabhaṇḍāgāriyacīvarapaṭiggāhakacīvarabhājakayāgubhājakakhajjabhājakaphalabhājakaappamattakavissajjakasāṭiyaggāhāpakapattaggāhāpakaārāmikapesakasāmaṇerapesakasammutīti etāsaṃ sammutīnaṃ vasena sammuti veditabbā. Kathinacīvaradānamatakacīvaradānavasena dānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Kathinuddhāravasena uddhāro veditabbo. Kuṭivatthuvihāravatthudesanāvasena desanā veditabbā. Yā pana tiṇavatthārakasamathe sabbasaṅgāhikañattiñca ekekasmiṃ pakkhe ekekañattiñcāti tisso ñattiyo ṭhapetvā puna ekekasmiṃ pakkhe ekekāti dve ñattidutiyakammavācā vuttā, tāsaṃ vasena kammalakkhaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Iti ñattidutiyakammaṃ imāni satta ṭhānāni gacchati.

Authorization is to be understood by way of these authorizations: authorization for boundaries; authorization for not being separated from the three robes; authorization for a spread; authorization of a meal-assigner, a lodging-assigner, a treasurer, a robe-receiver, a robe-distributor, a gruel-distributor, a hard-food-distributor, a fruit-distributor, a disposer of minor items, a cloth-receiver, a bowl-receiver, a director of monastery attendants, and a director of novices. Giving is to be understood by way of the giving of the Kathina robe and the giving of a deceased monk's robe. Withdrawal is to be known by way of the withdrawal of the Kathina. Declaration is to be understood by way of the declaration of a site for a hut and a site for a monastery. But as for the legal procedure of covering over with grass, having set aside the three motions—the all-inclusive motion and one motion for each side—again two acts of a motion with one following announcement, one for each side, have been stated. By way of these, the characteristic of a formal act is to be known. Thus, an act of a motion with one following announcement applies to these seven instances.

258. Ñatticatutthakammaṭṭhānabhede [V 0.0384] pana tajjanīyakammādīnaṃ sattannaṃ kammānaṃ vasena nissāraṇā, tesaṃyeva ca kammānaṃ paṭippassambhanavasena osāraṇā veditabbā. Bhikkhunovādakasammutivasena sammuti veditabbā. Parivāsadānamānattadānavasena dānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Mūlāyapaṭikassanakammavasena niggaho veditabbo. Ukkhittānuvattikā, aṭṭha yāvatatiyakā, ariṭṭho, caṇḍakāḷī ca imete yāvatatiyakāti imāsaṃ ekādasannaṃ samanubhāsanānaṃ vasena samanubhāsanā veditabbā. Upasampadakammaabbhānakammavasena kammalakkhaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Iti ñatticatutthakammaṃ imāni satta [M 0.0413] ṭhānāni gacchati. Evaṃ kammāni ca kammavipatti ca tesaṃ kammānaṃ kārakasaṅghaparicchedo ca vipattivirahitānaṃ kammānaṃ ṭhānabhedagamanañca veditabbaṃ.

258. However, in the classification of the instances of a formal act consisting of a motion and three announcements, expulsion should be known by way of the seven formal acts beginning with the act of censure. And reinstatement should be known by way of the calming of those same formal acts. Authorization should be known by way of the authorization of an exhorter of bhikkhunīs. Giving should be known by way of the giving of probation and the giving of penance. Suppression should be known by way of the formal act of sending back to the origin. Admonition should be known by way of these eleven admonitions: the bhikkhunī who follows one who has been suspended, the eight yāvatatiyaka cases, Ariṭṭha, and Caṇḍakāḷī—these are the yāvatatiyaka cases. The characteristic of a formal act should be known by way of the formal act of higher ordination and the formal act of rehabilitation. Thus, the formal act consisting of a motion and three announcements applies to these seven instances. In this way, formal acts, the failure of formal acts, the delimitation of the Sangha that performs those formal acts, and the application to the different instances of formal acts that are free from failure should be known.

Iti pāḷimuttakavinayavinicchayasaṅgahe

Thus, in the Compilation of Vinaya Determinations Independent of the Canon,

Kammākammavinicchayakathā samattā.

The Discourse on the Determination of Formal Acts and Non-Formal Acts is concluded.

Pakiṇṇakakaṇḍamātikā

The Matrix for the Miscellaneous Section

Gaṇabhojaṃ [V 0.0385] paramparaṃ, nāpucchā paṃsukūlakaṃ;

Acchinnaṃ paṭibhānañca, vippakatauddisanaṃ.

Group meals, successive meals, not asking permission, rag-robes; an uncut robe, intricate figures, making one get up while eating, and a place for teaching.

Tivassantaṃ dīghāsanaṃ, gilānupaṭṭhavaṇṇanaṃ;

Attapātamanavekkhaṃ, silāpavijjhalimpanaṃ.

Seating according to seniority, a long seat, attending to the sick, and praising death; taking one's own life, not inspecting a seat, rolling stones, and setting fires.

Micchādiṭṭhigopadānaṃ, dhammikārakkhuccārādi;

Nhānaghaṃsaṃ paṇḍakādi, dīghakesādyādāsādi.

Wrong view, giving to a guardian, a righteous request, and excrement, etc.; rubbing while bathing, eunuchs, etc., long hair, etc., and mirrors, etc.

Naccādaṅgachedaniddhi, patto sabbapaṃsukūlaṃ;

Parissāvanaṃ naggo ca, pupphagandhaāsittakaṃ.

Dancing, etc., cutting off a limb, psychic power, the bowl, and all rag-robes; a water strainer, a naked person, and things strewn with flowers and scents.

Maḷorikekabhājanaṃ, celapaṭi pādaghaṃsī;

Bījanī chattanakhādi, kāyabandhanivāsanaṃ.

A bowl-stand, a single vessel, a cloth mat, and a foot-rubber; a whisk, an umbrella, fingernails, etc., a waistband, and an under-robe.

Kājaharaṃ dantakaṭṭhaṃ, rukkhāroho chandāropo;

Lokāyataṃ khipitako, lasuṇaṃ nakkamitabbaṃ.

Carrying with a shoulder-pole, a tooth-stick, climbing a tree, and showing partiality; worldly lore, sneezing, garlic, and what should not be trodden upon.

Avandiyo tūlabhisi, bimbohanaāsandādi;

Uccāsanamahāsanaṃ, cīvaraadhammokāso.

One not to be venerated, a cotton mattress, a pillow, a couch, etc.; a high seat, a grand seat, and a place unsuitable for a robe according to the rule.

Saddhādeyyaṃ santuttaraṃ, nikkhepo satthakammādi;

Nahāpito dasabhāgo, pātheyyaṃ mahāpadeso;

Ānisaṃsoti mātikā.

That which is given in faith, an under-robe and upper-robe, laying down, the act of using a weapon, etc.; a barber, a tenth part, provisions for a journey, the great standards, and the benefits. Thus is the matrix.

34. Pakiṇṇakavinicchayakathā

34. The Discourse on Miscellaneous Determinations

1. Idāni [M 0.0414][V 0.0386] pakiṇṇakakathā ca veditabbā. “Gaṇabhojane aññatra samayā pācittiya”nti (pāci. 217) vuttaṃ gaṇabhojanaṃ (pāci. aṭṭha. 217-218) dvīhi ākārehi pasavati viññattito vā nimantanato vā. Kathaṃ viññattito pasavati? Cattāro bhikkhū ekato ṭhitā vā nisinnā vā upāsakaṃ disvā “amhākaṃ catunnampi bhattaṃ dehī”ti vā viññāpeyyuṃ, pāṭekkaṃ vā passitvā “mayhaṃ dehi, mayhaṃ dehī”ti evaṃ ekato vā nānāto vā viññāpetvā ekato vā gacchantu nānāto vā, bhattaṃ gahetvāpi ekato vā bhuñjantu nānāto vā. Sace ekato gaṇhanti, gaṇabhojanaṃ hoti, sabbesaṃ āpatti. Paṭiggahaṇameva hettha pamāṇaṃ. Evaṃ viññattito pasavati.

1. Now, the discourse on miscellaneous topics should also be understood. It has been said: 'In a group meal, except for the proper occasion, there is a pācittiya offense.' A group meal arises in two ways: by way of request or by way of invitation. How does it arise by way of request? Four monks, standing or sitting together, having seen a lay follower, might request, 'Give a meal to the four of us,' or, having seen him individually, might request, 'Give to me, give to me.' Having thus requested either together or separately—whether they go together or separately, or having received the meal, whether they eat together or separately—if they receive it together, it is a group meal, and there is an offense for all. Herein, the receiving itself is the standard. Thus it arises by way of request.

Kathaṃ nimantanato pasavati? Cattāro bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā “tumhe, bhante, odanena nimantemi, odanaṃ me gaṇhatha ākaṅkhatha oloketha adhivāsetha paṭimānethā”ti evaṃ yena kenaci vevacanena vā bhāsantarena vā pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ nāmaṃ gahetvā nimanteti. Evaṃ ekato nimantitā paricchinnakālavasena ajjatanāya vā svātanāya vā ekato gacchanti, ekato gaṇhanti, ekato bhuñjanti, gaṇabhojanaṃ hoti, sabbesaṃ āpatti. Ekato nimantitā ekato vā nānāto vā gacchanti, ekato gaṇhanti, ekato vā nānāto vā bhuñjanti, āpattiyeva. Ekato nimantitā ekato vā nānāto vā gacchanti, nānāto gaṇhanti, ekato vā nānāto vā bhuñjanti, anāpatti. Cattāri pariveṇāni vā vihāre vā gantvā nānāto nimantitā, ekaṭṭhāne ṭhitesuyeva vā eko puttena eko pitarāti evampi nānāto nimantitā ekato vā nānāto vā gacchantu, ekato vā nānāto vā bhuñjantu, sace ekato gaṇhanti, gaṇabhojanaṃ hoti, sabbesaṃ āpatti. Evaṃ tāva nimantanato pasavati.

How does it arise by way of invitation? Having approached four bhikkhus, one invites them, saying: 'Venerable sirs, I invite you with rice. Please accept my rice, desire it, look upon it, consent to it, and esteem it.' Thus, having taken the name of one of the five kinds of foods, one invites with any synonym or with another language. In this way, bhikkhus invited together for a limited time—whether for today or for tomorrow—if they go together, receive together, and eat together, it is a group meal; for all, there is an offense. Bhikkhus invited together, if they go together or separately, receive together, and eat together or separately, there is indeed an offense. Bhikkhus invited together, if they go together or separately, receive separately, and eat together or separately, there is no offense. If, having gone to four cells or monasteries, they are invited separately, or if—even while they are standing in one place—one is invited by a son and another by a father, thus they are invited separately, let them go together or separately, and let them eat together or separately; if they receive together, it is a group meal, and for all there is an offense. Thus far, it arises by way of invitation.

Tasmā sace koci saṅghabhattaṃ kattukāmena nimantanatthāya pesito vihāraṃ āgamma “bhante, sve amhākaṃ ghare bhikkhaṃ gaṇhathā”ti avatvā “bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vā “saṅghabhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vā “saṅgho bhattaṃ gaṇhatū”ti vā vadati, bhattuddesakena paṇḍitena bhavitabbaṃ. Nimantanikā [M 0.0415] gaṇabhojanato, piṇḍapātikā ca dhutaṅgabhedato mocetabbā. Kathaṃ? Evaṃ tāva vattabbaṃ “sve na sakkā upāsakā”ti. Punadivase, bhanteti. Punadivasepi na sakkāti. Evaṃ [V 0.0387] yāva aḍḍhamāsampi haritvā puna vattabbo “kiṃ tvaṃ avacā”ti. Sace punapi “saṅghabhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadati, tato “imaṃ tāva upāsaka pupphaṃ kappiyaṃ karohi, imaṃ tiṇa”nti evaṃ vikkhepaṃ katvā puna “tvaṃ kiṃ kathayitthā”ti pucchitabbo. Sace punapi tatheva vadati, “āvuso, tvaṃ piṇḍapātike vā mahallakatthere vā na lacchasi, sāmaṇere lacchasī”ti vattabbo. “Nanu, bhante, asukasmiṃ asukasmiñca gāme bhadante bhojesuṃ, ahaṃ kasmā na labhāmī”ti ca vutte te nimantituṃ jānanti, tvaṃ na jānāsīti. Te kathaṃ nimantesuṃ, bhanteti? Te evamāhaṃsu “amhākaṃ, bhante, bhikkhaṃ gaṇhathā”ti. Sace sopi tatheva vadati, vaṭṭati.

Therefore, if someone, wishing to offer a meal to the Sangha, is sent to invite them, comes to the monastery, and instead of saying, 'Venerable sirs, tomorrow at our house, please accept almsfood,' says, 'Please accept a meal,' or 'Please accept a meal for the Sangha,' or 'May the Sangha accept a meal,' the meal-distributing monk should be wise. Monks who delight in invitations should be freed from the offense of a group meal, and alms-round-goers from the breaking of the ascetic practice. How so? First, it should be said, 'Lay follower, tomorrow is not possible.' When he says, 'Venerable sir, the next day?' it should be said, 'On the next day also, it is not possible.' Having postponed it thus for as long as half a month, he should be asked again, 'What did you say?' If he again says, 'Please accept a meal for the Sangha,' then, after creating a diversion thus, 'Lay follower, first make this flower allowable, and this grass,' he should be asked again, 'What did you say?' If he again speaks in that same way, it should be said, 'Friend, you will not get the alms-round-goers or the great elder monks; you will get only novices.' And when it is said, 'But, venerable sir, in such-and-such a village and in such-and-such a village they fed the venerable ones, did they not? Why do I not get them?' it should be said, 'Those people know how to invite; you do not know.' When he asks, 'Venerable sir, how did those people invite?' it should be said, 'They said thus: "Venerable sirs, please accept our almsfood."' If he also speaks in that same manner, it is allowable.

Atha punapi “bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadati, “na dāni tvaṃ, āvuso, bahū bhikkhū lacchasi, tayo eva, āvuso, lacchasī”ti vattabbo. “Nanu, bhante, amukasmiñca amukasmiñca gāme sakalaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ bhojesuṃ, ahaṃ kasmā na labhāmī”ti. “Tvaṃ nimantituṃ na jānāsī”ti. Te kathaṃ nimantesuṃ, bhanteti? Te evamāhaṃsu “amhākaṃ, bhante, bhikkhaṃ gaṇhathā”ti. Sace sopi tatheva “bhikkhaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadati, vaṭṭati. Atha punapi “bhattamevā”ti vadati, tato vattabbo – “gaccha tvaṃ, natthamhākaṃ tava bhattenattho, nibaddhagocaro esa amhākaṃ, mayamettha piṇḍāya carissāmā”ti. Taṃ “caratha, bhante”ti vatvā āgataṃ pucchanti “kiṃ bho laddhā bhikkhū”ti? Kiṃ etena, bahu ettha vattabbaṃ, therā “sve piṇḍāya carissāmā”ti āhaṃsu, mā dāni tumhe pamajjitthāti. Dutiyadivase cetiyavattaṃ katvā ṭhitabhikkhū saṅghattherena vattabbā “āvuso, dhuragāme saṅghabhattaṃ, apaṇḍitamanusso pana agamāsi, gacchāma, dhuragāme piṇḍāya carissāmā”ti. Bhikkhūhi therassa vacanaṃ kātabbaṃ, na dubbacehi bhavitabbaṃ, gāmadvāre aṭṭhatvāva piṇḍāya caritabbaṃ, tesu pattāni gahetvā nisīdāpetvā bhojentesu bhuñjitabbaṃ.

If again he says, 'Take the meal,' it should be said, 'Friend, you will not get many monks now; you will get only three, friend.' If he says, 'Venerable Sir, did they not feed the entire community of monks in such and such a village and in such and such a village? Why do I not get them?' The reply is, 'You do not know how to invite.' 'How did those people invite, Venerable Sir?' 'Those people said thus: "Venerable Sirs, accept our almsfood."' If that inviter also says in the same way, 'Accept the almsfood,' it is allowable. Or if he again says, 'Only the meal,' then it should be said: 'You go. We have no need for your meal. This is our regular alms-resort; we will go for alms here.' They ask the one who has returned after saying, 'Go, venerable sirs,' 'Well, sir, did you get the monks?' He replies, 'What is the use of this? There is much to be said here. The elders said, "Tomorrow we will go for alms." Now, do not you all be heedless.' On the second day, the monks standing there after having performed the duties at the cetiya should be told by the elder of the Sangha: 'Friends, in the regular alms-village there is a meal for the Sangha, but an unwise person went. Let us go; we will go for alms in the regular alms-village.' The monks should follow the elder's word and not be difficult to admonish. Without waiting at the village gate, they should go for alms. When those people, having taken their bowls and had them seated, are feeding them, they should eat.

Sace āsanasālāya bhattaṃ ṭhapetvā rathikāsu āhiṇḍantā ārocenti “āsanasālāyaṃ, bhante, bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti, na vaṭṭati. Atha pana “bhattaṃ ādāya tattha tattha gantvā bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadanti, paṭikacceva [M 0.0416] vā vihāraṃ atiharitvā patirūpe ṭhāne ṭhapetvā āgatāgatānaṃ denti, ayaṃ abhihaṭabhikkhā nāma vaṭṭati. Sace pana bhattasālāya dānaṃ sajjetvā taṃ taṃ pariveṇaṃ pahiṇanti “bhattasālāya bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti, vaṭṭati. Ye pana manussā piṇḍacārike bhikkhū disvā āsanasālaṃ sammajjitvā tattha nisīdāpetvā bhojenti, na te paṭikkhipitabbā. Ye pana gāme bhikkhaṃ alabhitvā gāmato nikkhamante bhikkhū disvā [V 0.0388] “bhante, bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadanti, te paṭikkhipitabbā, na nivattitabbaṃ. Sace “nivattatha, bhante, bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadanti, “nivattathā”ti vuttapade nivattituṃ vaṭṭati. “Nivattatha, bhante, ghare bhattaṃ kataṃ, gāme bhattaṃ kata”nti vadanti, gehe ca gāme ca bhattaṃ nāma yassa kassaci hoti, nivattituṃ vaṭṭati. “Nivattatha bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti sambandhaṃ katvā vadanti, nivattituṃ na vaṭṭati. Āsanasālāto piṇḍāya carituṃ nikkhamante disvā “nisīdatha, bhante, bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vuttepi eseva nayo.

If, having placed food in the rest-house, they wander the streets announcing, 'Venerable sirs, receive food in the rest-house,' it is not allowable. But if they say, 'Having taken the food, go to various places and receive it,' or if beforehand they bring it to the monastery and, having placed it in a suitable place, give it to all who come, this is called 'brought almsfood' and is allowable. If, however, they prepare an offering in the meal hall and send word to each dwelling, saying, 'Receive food in the meal hall,' it is allowable. Those people who, seeing monks going for alms, sweep the rest-house, have them sit there, and offer them food—they should not be refused. But those people who, seeing monks who are leaving the village after not receiving alms therein, say, 'Venerable sirs, receive food'—they should be refused; one should not turn back. If they say, 'Turn back, venerable sirs, receive food,' in the phrase where 'turn back' is said, it is allowable to turn back. If they say, 'Turn back, venerable sirs, food is prepared in the house; food is prepared in the village'—since in a house and in a village food is something that belongs to anyone, it is allowable to turn back. If they say, 'Turn back, receive food,' making a connection between the phrases, it is not allowable to turn back. Even when, seeing monks setting out from the rest-house to wander for alms, they say, 'Sit down, venerable sirs, receive food,' this is the same rule.

“Aññatra samayā”ti vacanato gilānasamayo cīvaradānasamayo cīvarakārasamayo addhānagamanasamayo nāvābhiruhanasamayo mahāsamayo samaṇabhattasamayoti etesu sattasu samayesu aññatarasmiṃ anāpatti. Tasmā yathā mahācammassa parato maṃsaṃ dissati, evaṃ antamaso pādāpi phālitā honti, vālikāya vā sakkharāya vā pahaṭamatte dukkhaṃ uppādenti, na sakkā ca hoti antogāme piṇḍāya carituṃ, īdise gelaññe gilānasamayoti bhuñjitabbaṃ, na lesakappiyaṃ kātabbaṃ.

Because it is said, 'Except at the proper time,' there is no offense on any one of these seven occasions: the time of illness, the time of giving robes, the time of making robes, the time of going on a long journey, the time of embarking on a boat, the time of a great assembly, and the time of a meal for ascetics. Therefore, just as when the thick skin of the sole is split, the flesh is seen from the outside, so too, even if the feet are merely cracked, or if they produce pain by mere contact with sand or gravel, and one is unable to go for alms within the village—in such an illness, one should partake, thinking, 'It is the time of illness.' Pretending to be ill should not be done.

Cīvaradānasamayo nāma anatthate kathine vassānassa pacchimo māso, atthate kathine pañcamāsā. Etthantare “cīvaradānasamayo”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ. Cīvare kariyamāne cīvarakārasamayoti bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yadā hi sāṭakañca suttañca labhitvā cīvaraṃ karonti, ayaṃ cīvarakārasamayo nāma, visuṃ cīvarakārasamayo nāma natthi, tasmā yo tattha cīvare kattabbaṃ yaṃ kiñci kammaṃ karoti, mahāpaccariyañhi “antamaso sūcivedhako”tipi vuttaṃ. Tena “cīvarakārasamayo”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ. Kurundiyaṃ pana vitthāreneva vuttaṃ “yo cīvaraṃ vicāreti chindati, moghasuttakaṃ ṭhapeti, āgantukapattaṃ ṭhapeti, paccāgataṃ sibbeti, āgantukapattaṃ bandhati, anuvātaṃ chindati [M 0.0417] ghaṭeti āropeti, tattha paccāgataṃ sibbeti, suttaṃ karoti valeti, pipphalikaṃ niseti, parivattanaṃ karoti, sabbopi cīvaraṃ karotiyevāti vuccati. Yo pana samīpe nisinno jātakaṃ vā dhammapadaṃ vā katheti, ayaṃ na cīvarakārako, etaṃ ṭhapetvā sesānaṃ gaṇabhojane anāpattī”ti.

The time for giving robes, namely, when the Kathina has not been spread, is the last month of the rains retreat; when the Kathina has been spread, it is five months. During this interval, one should partake, thinking, 'It is the time for giving robes.' When a robe is being made, one should partake, thinking, 'It is the time of robe-making.' For when, having obtained cloth and thread, they make a robe, this is called 'the time of robe-making'; there is no separate 'time of robe-making.' Therefore, any monk who does any work that should be done on the robe—for in the Mahāpaccarī it is said, 'Even one who threads a needle'—that monk should partake, thinking, 'It is the time of robe-making.' In the Kurundī, however, it is stated in detail: 'A monk who examines a robe, cuts it, sets a basting thread, sets a reinforcing patch, sews a hem, attaches a reinforcing patch, cuts, joins, and applies the border strip; and therein sews a hem, makes and twists thread, sharpens a small knife, and turns the knife—all this is said to be "indeed making a robe." But a monk who, sitting nearby, relates the Jātaka or the Dhammapada, is not a robe-maker. Excluding this monk, for the rest there is no offense in a group meal.'

Addhānagamanasamaye antamaso aḍḍhayojanaṃ gantukāmenapi “aḍḍhayojanaṃ gacchissāmī”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ, gacchantena bhuñjitabbaṃ, gatena ekadivasaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ.

At the time of traveling a distance, even by one who desires to go at least half a yojana, one should partake thinking, 'I will go half a yojana.' While going, one may partake. Having arrived, one may partake for one day only.
